title: Fact Check: Biden DID NOT behave inappropriately with child, viral pic is photoshopped
content:
This picture is edited. The original image shows Biden touching a child's t-shirt during his visit to the Capitol Child Development Center in Hartford, Connecticut in October 2021.
Ever since his run for the 2020 presidential election, US President Joe Biden has faced a barrage of accusations of behaving inappropriately with children . One among them is a photo that shows Biden kneeling in front of a boy, with his hands close to the boy's pants. The archived versions of similar posts  can be seen here and here . AFWA's investigation found that the viral photo was digitally altered. AFWA probe A reverse search of the viral image led us to the original photo uploaded to the website of the Associated Press  in 2021.  As per the AP, the photograph was from Biden's visit to the Capitol Child Development Center in Hartford, Connecticut on October 15, 2021. We noticed multiple similarities between this photo and the viral one. Every person standing in the background appears to be in the same position in both photos. The significant difference between the two images is the positioning of Biden's hands and the point at which the boy stood. The boy in the original photo was cut out and moved up, so as to place his shirt over Biden's hand. In fact, Biden's right hand was also cut out. Although it was done so badly, a part of it is still visible if you look closely. At the same time, the other boy standing behind the boy talking to Biden was completely photoshopped out. If you compare the fence and the road in that part of the photos, you can see blurriness in the viral photo there. A video from the moment where Bident interacts with the child is available on YouTube. Nowhere in this video, can the US President be seen behaving inappropriately with the boy. Biden has been accused by some adult women of acting inappropriately with them. However, there is no evidence of the US President being sexually inappropriate with children. It is hence clear that the image in question is morphed and does not show Biden touching a young child inappropriately. Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Jan 1, 2023 07:10 IST

title: Fact Check: 2011 Japan tsunami video FALSELY shared as from Indonesia
content:
The video in circulation is not from Indonesia, but is CCTV footage from the Japan tsunami in 2011.
A terrifying video viral on social media supposedly shows a tsunami in Indonesia. One person wrote, while sharing this video on Twitter, "Few seconds before Tsunami & when it hits." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found no link between the viral clip and Indonesia. The original video shows the 2011 tsunami in Japan. AFWA Probe
A reverse image search revealed that the video has been popular for years. A YouTube video uploaded in 2014 purports to show the 2011 tsunami in Japan.
A further YouTube search revealed another video posted on April 11, 2013. The video was shared with the note "This tsunami footage was recorded on CCTV cameras that were placed along Route 45 in Iwate Prefecture. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport, and Tourism (MLIT) published it in the sped-up form because the original videos were in very low frame rate." This video contained the viral clip.
The video's description mentioned Ozawa in Yamada. The Japanese text at the bottom of the video also specified the location. Yamada is a region in northeast Japan .Â
We then searched the area on Google Maps  and found several similarities between the original video and the area visible in Google Street View.  Signal lines on the road and the building on the right are similar. Given below is a comparison.
The area was rebuilt after the tsunami. The latest satellite image available on Google Earth shows this.
The video was also previously fact-checked by AFP when a tsunami hit Indonesia in 2018.
Thus, we were able to conclude that this video is not from Indonesia at all.
(With Inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jan 1, 2023 07:11 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of goons thrashing cop is from 2020, falsely shared as recent incident in Bihar
content:
The incident happened in 2020 during the NDA rule in the state.
The hooch tragedy in Bihar that killed almost 70 people has created political turmoil in the state. Amid this, many shared a violent video  on social media that shows a policeman being beaten up by a group of people. Those sharing the video on Twitter claimed, "Liquor mafias thrashed the policemen. How did the Mahagathbandhan government make this Bihar?" On December 28, 2022, the same video was shared by the Bihar BJP's Twitter account . The archived versions of these posts can be seen here  and here .Â
AFWA's investigation found the video was old. In September 2020, a Bihar policeman was assaulted, allegedly by liquor mafia goons. Locals secretly recorded this on video. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of a keyframe of the viral video led us to the various news reports which contained the same video. On September 6, 2020, the viral video was shared by Zee News  in a news report. On September 8, 2020, the same video was also shared by the Navbharat Times . Per the reports, on September 5, 2020, a group of liquor mafia goons allegedly attacked ASI Ashutosh Kumar of the Jakkanpur police station in Patna.
AFWA contacted Rajesh Kumar Jha, India Today's Correspondent from Patna to get more information about the viral clip. Jha confirmed that the incident happened in Patna in 2020 as described in news reports. He also added that after the incident, the police arrested several suspects. On September 6, 2020, the viral video was uploaded to the official YouTube channel of News18 Bihar Jharkhand with the same information.
Per a news report , in 2017, Nitish Kumar ended his alliance with Mahagathbandhan and returned to the NDA. He became Chief Minister of Bihar for the sixth time with the support of the BJP. In the 2020 Assembly Election, Nitish Kumar retained his place as CM of Bihar for the seventh time. In August 2022, he returned to the Mahagathbandhan. So, when this incident happened, Bihar's was being governed by the NDA. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jan 1, 2023 07:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of truck knocking over welcome sign is NOT from India, its from Turkey
content:
This video is not from India. The incident took place in Kefeli, a small village in Turkey.
A video making the rounds on social media shows an overloaded truck, that while crossing the road, uprooted a signboard and dragged it along with it. Within seconds, the truck driver realized that the board has been removed and is stuck atop the vehicle. The driver then reversed, got rid of the sign, and continued on its way.
Social media users claim that this incident was from India. IPS Rupin Sharma shared the video writing, "#MeraBharatMahaan. This can happen only in India." Archives of such posts can be found here , and here .
AFWA found that this incident did not take place in India but in Kefeli, a village in Turkey. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a video  shared on Dailymotion on December 15. It matched the viral video in all aspects. The caption of the video, written in Turkish, said: "An event like a movie in Mersin. This is how the truck changed the way of the village with one move."Â
With the help of keywords, we found another report  on the incident that stated that this video was shot in Kefeli, a small village in the Tarsus district of the Mersin province in Turkey. The report further mentioned that the truck was loaded with wood.Â
The same video was also tweeted  by "Yeni Safak", a Turkish daily, and another Turkish media outlet  namely "Haber 7" around the same time.
On December 14, the truck displaced a sign  mounted at the entrance of the neighbourhood that said: "Welcome to Kefeli neighbourhood".Â
We also found the CCTV footage of this incident shared on Facebook by Efsane Kamyonlar, a video creator based in Turkey. The video has garnered more than six million views at the time of writing this report.
The neighbourhood headman Gurlesin Gungor  reportedly came to know about the incident after other drivers and workers were unable to find their way to the village because of the welcome sign was tilted at a 90 degrees angle, leading people to a different direction altogether.Â
Güngör also reportedly reached out to the truck driver Seydi Sevindi, who went back to the neighbourhood and had the sign moved to its original place two days after the incident.Â
A video report on the incident by "Halk TV" shows the neighbourhood as well as the signboard that was displaced by the truck.
Thus, we concluded that the video of a truck knocking a signboard out of its place in a small Turkish village became fodder for misleading claims about India.Â
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Jan 1, 2023 10:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Deer covered in snow rescued months ago resurfaces amid US winter storms
content:
This video is neither recent nor from the US storm. It was shot in Kazakhstan, a central-Asian country, and dates back to February 2021.
The deadly winter storm that struck the US in the run-up to the festive season . The death toll of this historic blizzard has, so far, crossed 60  as heavy snowfall, freezing winds, and a sudden drop in temperature wreaked havoc in the US.
Amid this, a video  making the rounds on social media shows a deer standing still in the middle of a road as if frozen amid the heavy snow. One person helped the deer get rid of the snow encasing its muzzle, and ran away after the impromptu rescue operation. Many claimed that this incident showed the harsh effect of the US Cold wave.
A Twitter user sharing the video  wrote, "This extremely cold weather across many parts of the USA & Canada has been extremely harsh for people & wildlife. This crazy footage shows two walkers who spotted a deer with its mouth, eyes & ears completely frozen over. The brilliant effort to help! Stay safe everyone." Archives of such posts can be found here , and here .
AFWA found that this video is neither recent nor from the US storm. It was shot in Kazakhstan, a central-Asian country, and dates back to February 2021.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram reel  from December 2021. The reel featured the same viral clip, but its title read, "Frozen deer @ -56 degree saved by locals in Kazakhstan." Russia state-affiliated media RT also tweeted  this video of the deer covered in snow on March 4, 2021. This confirmed that the video is definitely not from the ongoing US winter storm. Deer with frozen face rescued by locals in #Kazakhstan Follow us on Telegram https://t.co/KywEoFgfNA pic.twitter.com/VwQcFbliDw — RT (@RT_com) March 4, 2021 Further, we found the same video shared by the YouTube channel of "Press TV", a news channel based in Austria. Posted  in March 2021, the video description stated that two Kazakhstan residents, Abylaikhan Kuandyk and Nurzhan Makayev, found a roe deer on a road on February 25, 2021. Roe deer is a species of deer well-adapted to cold environments. Apart from this, the footage was credited to "Nurjan Makaev, Ruptly." Further, we found the same clip shared on Ruptly   as from the Kostanay region in Kazakhstan.
Deer with frozen face rescued by locals in #Kazakhstan Follow us on Telegram https://t.co/KywEoFgfNA pic.twitter.com/VwQcFbliDw — RT (@RT_com) March 4, 2021
Further, we found the same video shared by the YouTube channel of "Press TV", a news channel based in Austria. Posted  in March 2021, the video description stated that two Kazakhstan residents, Abylaikhan Kuandyk and Nurzhan Makayev, found a roe deer on a road on February 25, 2021. Roe deer is a species of deer well-adapted to cold environments. Apart from this, the footage was credited to "Nurjan Makaev, Ruptly." Further, we found the same clip shared on Ruptly   as from the Kostanay region in Kazakhstan.
Several other YouTube channels  also shared the same clip  with the same information along with news reports . Also, the two brothers were hailed on social media  for their heroic deed.
SDP Noticias, a media outlet based in Mexico, reported  the incident in March 2021 stating that the incident took place in Kazakhstan, where two brothers from the Denisov district who were heading home when they saw the deer on the side of the road and decided to help. The report consisted of a four-minute-long video of the incident.
Further, we found an article  by KST News that interviewed the two brothers from Kostanay. "It was a shame that other drivers also saw a wandering animal, but drove past. In such cases, you need to stop and try to help," one of the brothers told KST News. The report also shared a photo of the brothers along with the deer rescued by them.
India Today and GNT also shared this video erroneously as recent but later deleted it. Thus, we concluded that the video of men  rescuing a seemingly frozen deer is not from the US.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jan 1, 2023 12:18 IST

title: Fact Check: These photos are NOT from Vande Bharat Express that was pelted with stones in Bengal
content:
Although Vande Bharat was hit by stones on January 2 evening, these images are from the Howrah-Purulia Express that has hit by stones on January 1, 2023.
Days after the inaugural journey of the first Vande Bharat Express in West Bengal on December 30, 2022, the train made the headlines after it was attacked with stones on the evening of January 2. Following this, many on social media shared photos taken  inside an air-conditioned train compartment, claiming them to be from the Vande Bharat Express. For instance, a Twitter handle named Asansol BJP District Organisation shared a set of two images featuring a man with a bandage on his face and seats covered in blood and shattered glasses. The tweet read: "Stone pelted on Vande Bharat train in West Bengal. The train was inaugurated on 30 Dec by Hon'ble PM @narendramodi ji. Is this the reply to Jai Shri Ram, CM @MamataOfficial? Shame!"  Stone pelted on Vande Bharat train in West Bengal. The train was inaugurated on 30 Dec by Hon'ble PM @narendramodi ji. Is this the reply to Jai Shri Ram, CM @MamataOfficial ? Shame! pic.twitter.com/o7X74zemFx — Asansol BJP District Organization (@AsansolBjpDist) January 2, 2023  Many also shared a photo where the window of an AC chair car can be seen shattered, with seats covered in glass and blood. "As per eyewitness @RuprajSengupta, the C13 coach of #VandeBharatExpress was damaged due to stone pelting at Kumarganj [KMRJ], Maldah, WB in the evening yesterday while returning from New Jalpaiguri Junction [NJP], proving my point that we need to kick out internal enemies first," the tweet read. Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .  As per eyewitness @RuprajSengupta , the C13 coach of #VandeBharatExpress was damaged due to stone pelting at Kumarganj [KMRJ], Maldah, WB in the evening yesterday while returning from New Jalpaiguri Junction [NJP], proving my point that we need to kick out internal enemies first. pic.twitter.com/Ep8HjqYywZ — ব্রাহ্মণ উবাচ | ब्राह्मण उवाच | Brahmin Said 🇮🇳 (@BrahmanUvacha) January 2, 2023 Bengal BJP President Dr Sukanata Majumdar shared these photos and criticised Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee but later deleted the tweet. Times Now also published a report on the incident while featuring the same photo of the bloodstained seat. AFWA's probe found that these images are unrelated to the recent Vande Bharat stone-pelting incident. AFWA Probe When we searched keywords related to the recent stone-pelting incident, reports from ABP News and TV9 Bangla suggested that no passengers were harmed. Reportedly, a glass door of a compartment was shattered. They also mentioned that the incident took place near Samsi, in the Malda district of West Bengal. A reverse image search of the viral images took us to a Facebook post by Pranabesh Sen , an office executive at the West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (WBSEDCL). Sen shared these images while penning his horrifying experience of stone-pelting while returning to his native district of Bankura from Howrah in the 12827 Howrah-Purulia Superfast Express. Notably, Sen shared these images on January 1, 2023, a day before the Vande Bharat stone-pelting incident, making it clear that the images were unrelated to that. In his Facebook post, Sen noted that the incident happened on the first day of the new year near the Panshkura town of the East Medinipur district in West Bengal around 5:48 pm. He also noted that the coach number he was in was D3 and the seat number of an injured passenger was 73. We also found the seat arrangement and colour of the newly inaugurated HWH-NJP Vande Bharat Express in a video shared by AajTak Bangla . A comparison between the seats of the Premium and Executive classes of the Vande Bharat and the viral photos made it clear that the latter were not from the Vande Bharat Express at all. AFWA also reached out to Sen, who said: "I remember the exact time when it happened because I was taking a call. Just when the train was near Panshkura junction, the person who was sitting in the window side was struck by a stone and the window shattered and fell on him. His face was injured, his teeth broke and there was blood over his face. The person was in severe pain." He said that the injured passenger was taken to the hospital by the station master at the Kharagpur Junction, adding that he did not see any Railway Protection Force personnel following the incident and that no one approached him to report what happened. Sen also shared the original photographs with AFWA. Upon examining the Exif data , we found that these photos were taken on January 1, near the Panshkura Station. The photos were shot at 5:53 pm, nearly five minutes after the stone hit the window. Moreover, the newly inaugurated Vande Bharat Express runs from Howrah to the New Jalpaiguri Junction  via Barddhaman, Bolpur, and Malda Town. On the other hand, the Purulia express leaves from Howrah and takes the southeastern route  via Kharagpur, which is in a completely different direction. The Panshkura Station does not fall in the Vande Bharat Express route. Thus, it is safe to conclude that the images making rounds are not from the Vande Bharat Express but from the Howrah-Purulia Express and were shot a day before the December 2 stone-pelting incident. title: Fact Check: No, Rohit Sharma DID NOT donate blood to Rishabh Pant after accident, viral photo is old
content:
Claims of Rohit Sharma immediately rushing to the hospital to donate his blood to Pant are not true. The photo of Sharma being shared is not recent, but more than six years old.
Indian cricketer Rishabh Pant suffered a near-fatal accident when driving to his home in Roorkee on December 30, last year. Pant has been undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Dehradun. Now, on social media, a photo of Indian captain Rohit Sharma lying in a hospital bed is making the rounds.
Those sharing Sharma's photo claimed that he met the injured Pant to donate blood . "He met Pant to donate the blood in emergency as doctors said they needed a person with same blood group immediately, Rohit Sharma the definition of Leader and Saviour," read one such tweet. The archived versions of such claims can be seen here , here and here .
AFWA's investigation found that the news of Rohit Sharma rushing to donate blood to Pant is not true. The photo of the Indian skipper going viral is also not recent, but more than six years old.
When we reverse-searched the viral image of Sharma lying on a hospital bed, it led us to a tweet by him from November 11, 2016. The tweet read: "All went well. Thank you for your good wishes. Can't wait to be back at it." This picture was reportedly taken after Sharma underwent surgery in London to treat a thigh injury that he sustained during the final ODI against New Zealand in 2016. This proved that the photo was old. All went well. Thank you for your good wishes. Can't wait to be back at it 🏃🏻 pic.twitter.com/llKqRtc3LJ — Rohit Sharma (@ImRo45) November 11, 2016 Next, we searched on the internet using keywords from the viral tweet. We have found no news reports of Sharma rushing to the hospital to donate his blood to Pant. Upon investigating further, we found news reports of Sharma enjoying a family vacation with his wife Ritika Sajdeh and daughter Samaira in the Maldives in the run-up to New Year's Eve. Sharma is not part of the three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka that began on January 3 but will return to lead the Men In Blue in the ODIs.
All went well. Thank you for your good wishes. Can't wait to be back at it 🏃🏻 pic.twitter.com/llKqRtc3LJ — Rohit Sharma (@ImRo45) November 11, 2016
Next, we searched on the internet using keywords from the viral tweet. We have found no news reports of Sharma rushing to the hospital to donate his blood to Pant. Upon investigating further, we found news reports of Sharma enjoying a family vacation with his wife Ritika Sajdeh and daughter Samaira in the Maldives in the run-up to New Year's Eve. Sharma is not part of the three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka that began on January 3 but will return to lead the Men In Blue in the ODIs.
Sharma and his wife also shared photos on Instagram from their recent Maldives trip. This hinted that Sharma might not have been in India at all when the Indian wicket-keeper and batsman met with an accident in Roorkee.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Rohit Sharma (@rohitsharma45)     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Ritika Sajdeh (@ritssajdeh)
A post shared by Rohit Sharma (@rohitsharma45)
A post shared by Ritika Sajdeh (@ritssajdeh)
To get to the bottom of this, AFWA spoke to senior sports journalist Vikrant Gupta of Sports Tak. Gupta confirmed that no such development had happened so far. However, Gupta also informed us that Sharma was in touch with Rishabh Pant's doctors from the Maldives. Several media reports have also suggested the same.Â
Thus, it is evident that the claims of Sharma immediately rushing to the hospital to donate his blood to Pant are untrue. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Jan 3, 2023 20:44 IST

title: Fact Check: Cristiano Ronaldo DID NOT say 'Inshallah' during Insta Live video after Saudi club signing
content:
This video is from October 2020, when he played for Juventas. During a live, Ronaldo declared his support for Russian mixed martial arts performer Khabib Nurmagomedov and said this.
After a disappointing run in the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar and his November ouster from Manchester United, Portuguese star footballer Cristiano Ronaldo is on his way to making a fresh start with Al Nassr, a Saudi Arabian club . Reportedly, the deal was sealed on the last day of 2022.Â
Following the signing, a clip  allegedly from an Instagram Live by Ronaldo has started making rounds on social media. In it, he said, "Inshallah," a phrase popularly used by Muslims to refer to the "Almighty's will", before laughing. Those sharing this video claimed that Ronaldo said this after joining Al Nassr. The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA's investigation found that the video is more than two years old and unrelated to Al Nassr signing Ronaldo.Â
A reverse image search of the keyframes from the viral clip led us to an Instagram post from October 19, 2020. It featured a longer version of the same video and five times Ballon d'Or winner can be heard saying, "of course, of course, Khabib's going to win, my brother," before saying, "Inshallah."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by . (@pathtooparadise)
A post shared by . (@pathtooparadise)
The caption of this post read: "Cristiano Ronaldo saying Inshallah to Khabibs victory next week against Gaethje. We pray to Allah that he guides him to the straight path, the path of Islam. We pray to the almighty to save us from the fire of hell." Given that the clip was shared as early as October 2020, it is evident that the video was unrelated to Ronaldo joining Al Nassr. In October 2020, the former Real Madrid star was a part of the Italian football giant Juventas. He returned to Manchester United  in August 2021, and his contract there was terminated  days after the 2022 FIFA World Cup kicked off following a controversial interview with Piers Morgan. We searched using relevant keywords and found a Mirror UK report from October 2020 about the video. It said that Ronaldo had extended his support for Khabib Nurmagomedov, a former mixed martial art performer from Russia ahead of his battle against Justin Gaethje. The Sun also reported the same around the same time, making the context of the video clear. So, while we could not pinpoint the exact date when Ronaldo said this during an Instagram Live, we are more than sure that it has nothing to do with him joining Al Nassr. Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Jan 4, 2023 17:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Amazing timelapse of snow burying a neighbourhood is years old, not from recent US storm
content:
This is an old video and has been on the internet since 2016 at least. As per older videos, this incident may have been from the US state of Virginia.
In the last week of December 2022, a blizzard left 39 people dead across New York's Erie County . Buffalo city, the seat of Erie County, was the most affected by prolonged whiteout conditions and power outages.
Among the many, many photos and videos of the storm shared on social media is a timelapse video of an area gradually getting buried under snow over a span of two days that is going viral. "Buffalo, NY - 48 hour timelapse of Blizzard in 60 seconds," read the caption to one such video . The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here , here  and here .Â
AFWA found that the video is at least seven years old and not related to the recent blizzard in Buffalo, New York. AFWA PROBEÂ
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to the same shared on Reddit  about four years ago. The caption to the video read, "Time lapse of a blizzard that dropped 31 inches of snow in 48 hours!". The Reddit post had no other information about the video.Â
A subsequent search using relevant keywords led us to the same video uploaded to a YouTube channel "Worse Than Chiggers" on January 25, 2016. Per its description, the video was from the winter storm Jonas that hit northern Virginia in the US between January 22 and 24, 2016. The channel also claimed the video was shot by the person running it from their front porch in northern Virginia.   We also found the same video in a Daily Mail  report published on January 27, 2016. Per the report as well, the video was from Virginia. We were not able to independently verify the location of the video. However, it is clear that the clip is old and not related to the recent blizzard in Buffalo, New York. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Jan 4, 2023 22:22 IST

title: Fact Check: PM Modi did not announce slashing fuel prices, 2016 video shared with misleading claim
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi did not make any such announcement. This video is from December 3, 2016, shot during Modi's Parivartan Rally in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. There he focused on issues like demonetisation and corruption.
A video that's being shared by many online shows Prime Minister Narendra Modi's rally. Alongside Modi, Uttar Pradesh Deputy-Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, and Bharatiya Janata Party leader OP Mathur can be seen in the video. Those sharing it, claimed in Hindi, "Prime Minister Narendra Modi suddenly announces cut on petrol prices."
AFWA's investigation however found that Modi did not make any such announcement. Also, this video is old. AFWA Probe
At the 3.39 second mark on that video, we spotted some clues. "Parivartan Maha Rally", and "Mission 300+" banners in Hindi can be seen in that video.
We then ran a keyword search on Facebook and Youtube and which led us to the original video. On December 3, 2016, the same video was shared by the BJP's official Facebook Page , with the title, "LIVE: PM Shri Narendra Modi addressing Parivartan Rally in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh". We also found the same video on PM Modi's official YouTube channel with a similar title.Â
In the speech, PM Modi did not say anything about slashing fuel prices. Rather, he focused on other issues like demonetisation, corruption, mobile banking, Digital India, and various welfare schemes, among other things.
On November 8, 2016, Modi announced the demonetisation  of Rs 1,000 and Rs 500 notes. While addressing the crowd at the Parivartan Rally , the PM said, "Shouldn't I fight corruption? Is fighting corruption a crime? Why are some people calling me a wrongdoer for fighting corruption." He spoke about issues like black money , corruption , and poverty .
On December 3, 2016, the Times of India published a report on how PM Modi encouraged people to use mobile banking from a Moradabad rally. On that same day, India Today shared a video report titled, "I am fighting this war for you, what will those accusing me do? I am a fakir. I will walk away with my little belongings: PM Narendra Modi in Moradabad rally". Media reports, however, did not say anything about the speech focusing on slashing fuel prices.Â
Thus, it's clear that this video was shared with a misleading claim. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Jan 5, 2023 15:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Ronaldo's goal falsely shared as debut score for Al-Nassr
content:
Ronaldo is yet to make his debut for his new club. The viral clip was taken from the match that was played between Juventus and Udinese in 2021.
Star footballer Cristiano Ronaldo joined the Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr in the early hours of December 31, 2022. Ronaldo, 37, signed a two-and-a-half-year, $75 million per year contract with the club . "History in the making. This is a signing that will not only inspire our club to achieve even greater success but inspire our league, our nation and future generations, boys and girls to be the best version of themselves." Al-Nassr announced after his signing . History in the making. History in the making. Welcome @Cristiano to your new home @AlNassrFC pic.twitter.com/oan7nu8NWC — AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) December 30, 2022
Following this, a video of Ronaldo scoring a goal was shared by many online , with people claiming that this was his first goal for Al-Nassr.Â
The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .  AFWA PROBE
AFWA found that the claim in the viral video is misleading. He has yet to make his debut for the club. The actual video was from the 2021-22 Italian Series A match  between the Italian football clubs Juventus and Udinese.
Under the viral tweet, we saw many responses pointing out that this video was not Ronaldo's first goal for the Saudi club, but from a match that took place between Juventus and Udinese in 2021. We then reverse-searched screengrabs from the video, and that led us to a video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Serie A. The video was titled "Udinese 2-2 Juventus | Udinese pull off comeback to surprise Juve! Serie A 2021/22." At the 2.43-minute mark , one can see the footage used in the viral clip. Ronaldo is yet to make his debut for Al-Nassr reportedly because he's currently serving a suspension for smashing an Everton fan's phone . The ban will end on January 21, 2023. Thus, it is clear that the video being shared is misleading. (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Jan 5, 2023 22:51 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Haldwani, these visuals of railway track encroachments are from Kolkata
content:
This video is old and from West Bengal. Another similar photo being shared with the same claim is also from Kolkata.
For the thousands who faced homelessness in Uttarakhand's Haldwani, the Supreme Court decision to pause an eviction drive on railway land on December 5 came as a shot to the arm. "There cannot be uprooting of 50,000 people overnight… It's a human issue, some workable solution needs to be found," the Supreme Court said, stopping the Uttarakhand High Court order that had cleared the eviction of the people.
On the day of this hearing, '#HaldwaniEncroachment' became one of the top trends on Twitter. The hashtag featured visuals of alleged encroachment on railway lands in Haldwani.
One such video  of massive encroachment on railway tracks is being widely shared on Twitter and Facebook. Shot from what feels like a moving train, the video shows people drying clothes, bathing, and even selling vegetables on railway tracks.Â
A Twitter user shared the video with the caption, "See How closely the #Railways land is encroached in #Haldwani. Clearly can be seen that this illegal settlement. Politicians who r responsible for this, sd also be punished. How these people migrated here must be looked n sent back to their native home."
Bharatiya Janata Party leader Priti Gandhi also shared a photo  showing encroachment on railway tracks, claiming it to be from Haldwani. "This is what the Supreme Court has legitimised today," she wrote alongside the image. The archived version of this post can be seen here .
AFWA found that both the viral video and image are old and from West Bengal's Kolkata. Who shot the video?
In the viral video, one can see two posters of Mamata Bannerjee. This gave us a clue that the video might have been from West Bengal.
A quick reverse search of the keyframes led us to a four-minute-long YouTube video from January 13, 2017. The viral clip was a part of this video. As per its description, it was shot in Kolkata.
The yellow taxi and Bengal MEMU train
In the longer video, we found more clues to conclude that it was from West Bengal. At one part, we noticed yellow taxis.
 Towards the end of the same video, a train can be seen approaching. One can see the word "Eastern" and the number "63007" written on it. While the word "eastern" indicates that this train is a part of "Eastern Railways", the number belongs to the Katwa-Rampurhat MEMU train . MEMU trains serve short- and medium-distance routes in India. Both these indicate that the place seen in this video cannot be Haldwani.
In this video, one can also see "Tolly Nalah" written on a yellow board. Tolly Nallah or Tolly Canal is a stream located in Kolkata.
This YouTube channel on which the video was shared belongs to Sukamal Chakraborty, a teacher and a vlogger. AFWA contacted Chakraborty, who confirmed that he had shot it around six years ago when he had just begun vlogging. "I shot this video while travelling in a train which was going from Ballygunge to Budge Budge," he added. What is the source of the image?
Using reverse search, we found the railway track encroachment photo shared by Priti Gandhi on the Getty Images website . As per the information given here, this photo was shot on December 12, 2013, in a Kolkata slum.
To sum it up, old visuals of encroachment on railway tracks in Kolkata are being passed off as from Haldwani. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jan 6, 2023 09:05 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of crowd at seer's funeral procession FASELY shared as Chandrababu Naidu rally
content:
This video is from the funeral procession of Siddeshwar Swami, the seer of the Jnanayogashrama who died on January 3, 2023, in Karnataka's Vijayapura district.
Former Andhra Pradesh chief minister and Telugu Desam Party president N Chandrababu Naidu has been holding a series of political rallies across the state in preparation for the 2024 Assembly Elections in the state. Naidu's rallies gained national attention after 11 people died in two different incidents of stampedes during his roadshows. High tension prevailed in Naidu's native constituency Kuppam in Chittoor district on January 4 after Andhra Pradesh police prevented the TDP supremo from participating in a road show there. Police reportedly resorted to mild lathi-charge and seized Naida's campaign vehicle. Following this, he resumed the roadshow on foot. Following this, several people on social media have shared a video  of a massive rally  with the claim that it was from Naidu's roadshow in Kuppam. "Grand welcome to #NaraChandrababuNaidu kuppam people," read the caption to one such video. The archived versions of a similar post  can be seen here . AFWA's investigation, however, found that the video is from the funeral procession of Siddeshwar Swami, a seer from Sri Jnanayogashrama in Karnataka. It is not related to Naidu's political rally. AFWA probe We noticed a few people on social media pointing out that the video was from Siddeshwar Swami's antim yatra or funeral procession. As per media reports , Siddeshwar Swami, a prominent Lingayat seer from Jnanayogashrama died on January 3 in the Vijayapura district of Karnataka. The same video was tweeted by a person on January 4. As per this tweet, the video was from Siddeshwar Swami's funeral procession. कर्नाटकातील विजयपूर येथील सिद्धेश्वर स्वामी यांचे काल स्वर्गरोहण झाले सुमारे वीस लाख भक्त जमले होते एक दैदिप्यमान सोहळा pic.twitter.com/KMsoU8V2r2 — राष्ट्रभक्त काका (@gajanan137) January 4, 2023 We then shared the video with Kannada daily Vartha Bharati's district reporter from Vijayapura, Asif Hussain. The journalist confirmed to us that the video is from Mahatma Gandhi Circle in Vijayapura. Speaking to AFWA, Hussain said, "Lakhs of people had gathered to pay their respect to the seer. His mortal remains was brought in a procession from Sainik School ground to Jnanayogashrama where the last rites were performed. The procession passed through the Mahatma Gandhi Circle, the same place that's seen in the viral video." We also compared the video with the Street View of the Mahatma Gandhi Circle on Google Maps. We were able to identify the central library building which can be seen at the end of the road throughout the video. We also geolocated a commercial building that appeared around 30 seconds into the video.  It is hence clear that the video in question is from the funeral procession of a seer from Karnataka. It has nothing to do with the road shows organised by Naidu in Andhra Pradesh. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jan 6, 2023 15:41 IST

title: Fact Check: This dangerous leopard attack video is not from Dehradun but Jorhat in Assam
content:
The incident happened in Assam's Jorhat. Many people were injured by the same leopard before it was caught by the authorities.
Recently, a leopard and its cubs were spotted at the Forest Research Institute in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. As per news reports , after that, the area was sealed off and visitors' entry was stopped. Authorities also reportedly issued strict orders for residents. Meanwhile, a video allegedly showing the same leopard has been shared widely.Â
In the video , a leopard can be seen jumping onto a moving car. The animal then ran away and disappeared. A person shared it on Facebook and wrote, "FRI Dehradun. Plz be careful. Leopard's frequent attack in FRI. FRI sealed for 15 days."Â
Many others shared the same video and claimed it happened in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. The archived version of the video can be seen here .Â
News outlets like Jagran and Bharat 24 also reported the same. The archived versions of such reports can be seen here and here .Â
AFWA's investigation, however, found that the video was not from Dehradun. The incident took place at the Lahdoigarh police post in the Jorhat district of Assam. AFWA PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to the various news reports containing the same video. On December 28, 2022, Zee News published the news with a headline, "The dreaded 'leopard' attacked a moving vehicle in Assam's Jorhat." Per the report, a leopard attacked a moving car in Assam's Jorhat. On December 27, the same video has been uploaded to the official YouTube channels of CNN-News18 and India Today with the same claim. Other leading news outlets like the Economic Times , NDTV , FirstPost , Mirror Now also reported the same. Purna Bikash Bora, India Today's correspondent from Jorhat, confirmed the same and added that the leopard injured three members of a family in a residential area. Moushumi Bora, Parismita Bora and Jiten Bora were seriously wounded. Meanwhile, the leopard also attacked the Forest Department team. Two jawans from the department were injured. Later, the animal was caught by the officers. AFWA also contacted a Dehradun divisional forest officer called Nitishmani Tripathi, who confirmed that no such leopard attack had happened there recently. Thus, it is clear that the viral leopard attack video is from Assam's Jorhat, not from Dehradun, Uttarakhand. Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 6, 2023 17:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of ISRO rocket launch WRONGLY shared as 'sunrise' at midnight in India
content:
This video shows the launch of ISRO's GSLV MK3 rocket at midnight in Andhra Pradesh.
A video making the rounds on social media supposedly shows "sunrise at midnight" in India. The video appears to show that night sky that, all of a sudden, illuminates with a burst of orange. A sun-like circular object lights up the night sky resembling a sunrise. The video also shows a huge number of spectators recording the event, who stand up and clap.
Social media users claimed that this video showed a sunrise at midnight somewhere in India. An archive of a similar tweet can be found here .Â
AFWA found that this video does not show a sunrise but a rocket launch at Andhra Pradesh's Sriharikota. AFWA PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Reddit post that contained an extended version of the viral clip. The full video, shared a month ago, first shows the bright source of light appearing amid the darkness, and then rising further up in the sky. The video was titled, "Midnight Sunrise in Sriharikota. ISRO launched 36 broadband satellites on the GSLVMK3 rocket."
The Indian Space Research Organisation launched its heaviest rocket, Launch Vehicle Mark 3 (LVM3 or GSLV Mark 3) on October 23, 2022. The rocket took off from the second launch pad of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR, Sriharikota at 12:07 am. The launch marked the first dedicated commercial launch for NewSpace India Limited in partnership with a UK-based firm OneWeb, successfully launching 36 broadband communication satellites.
With the help of relevant keywords, we found several verified Twitter handles that shared the extended version of the viral video of the rocket launch. Sunrise at midnight 🌞 @isro launched 36 broadband satellites in one rocket. #GSLVMK3 from #Sriharikota 🚀 proud moment for #India 👏👏👍🇮🇳 @ZUBI_26 @PMOIndia pic.twitter.com/mMW0CjcLaX — Rishi Suri (@rishi_suri) December 2, 2022
Sunrise at midnight 🌞 @isro launched 36 broadband satellites in one rocket. #GSLVMK3 from #Sriharikota 🚀 proud moment for #India 👏👏👍🇮🇳 @ZUBI_26 @PMOIndia pic.twitter.com/mMW0CjcLaX — Rishi Suri (@rishi_suri) December 2, 2022
We also found another video of the launch shared by Sidharth MP, a Chennai-based reporter with WION. In this video, a sight similar to the viral video can be seen unfolding behind the reporter.Â
AFWA shared the viral video with him to confirm if it was from the same event. Sidharth told us that this video is indeed from the same launch as there were no other recent night launches. He further added that the video was shot from the viewers' gallery at the launch.
With the help of a keyword search, we found a YouTube video  shared by a person who witnessed the rocket launch on October 23, 2022. Upon reaching out to him, Griffin Steve confirmed that the viral clip is from the ISRO rocket launch itself. A comparison of the video of the launch shared by him on YouTube and keyframes of the viral video confirms that the latter was indeed from the same event.
The GSLV MK3 was reportedly the heaviest rocket in use by the Indian Space Research Organisation, that ferried its heaviest payload into space — 36 satellites weighing a total of 5,796 kilos.Â
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jan 6, 2023 22:45 IST

title: Fact Check: UFO in Pakistan? Nope, it's just streetlight in dense fog - and some Photoshop
content:
This photo shows a street light in Lahore during a densely fogged evening in Lahore, Pakistan. The UFO was edited into the photo.
Every now and then, we come across half-baked stories about unidentified flying objects, also known as UFOs, being spotted in various corners of the world. Why should Pakistan be any different? Just days after we entered 2022, many shared a photo of a supposed UFO, spotted in Lahore, Pakistan.Â
A Twitter user sharing the photo wrote, "UFO spotted in Lahore, Received this image. Around #earthquake a friend messaged me he says he has seen a UFO at the time to earthquake. This picture is of yesterday night.. Source is legit." Earthquake tremors were felt in Lahore and several cities on the Pakistani side of Punjab on January 4, 2023. The epicentre of the 4.1 magnitude quake was recorded 34 km west of Lahore and 12 km west of Sheikhupura.
The archived versions of similar claims can be seen here , here , here .
AFWA found that the viral photo of a UFO was edited. The photo of a street light in Lahore was edited to make it look like a UFO.Â
A reverse image search of the viral photo led us to a similar image, but without any UFOs visible in it. A Twitter user, Asad, posted this photo on January 3. As per the photo's caption, "Smog/Fog in Lahore at 5:57 PM, Today." An archived version of this tweet can be seen here . Smog/Fog in Lahore at 5:57 PM, Today. pic.twitter.com/CwK4jSnKko — Asad (@asadfacts) January 3, 2023
Smog/Fog in Lahore at 5:57 PM, Today. pic.twitter.com/CwK4jSnKko — Asad (@asadfacts) January 3, 2023
To get to the bottom of the matter, AFWA contacted Asad. When we asked him about the details of this photo, Asad said that the photo was taken by him with his Samsung Galaxy A53 phone. He said that this photo was taken at Abdullah Haroon Road, Lake City, Lahore, at 5:57 pm on January 3. He further added he had no idea why people are using the photo he has taken to show UFOs in Pakistan.
Here is the comparison between the viral picture with the original one.Â
He also mailed us the original version of the photo. We then extracted the photo's Exif data and came to know that the photo was taken on January 3, 2023, at 6:01 pm. The time, date, and name of the mobile manufacturer further confirmed the details provided by him.
We then searched the internet to find news about UFOs spotted in Lahore, Pakistan. We found no such news reports which could confirm the claim.
Thus, it is clear that the viral tweet of a UFO spotted in Lahore is untrue. The picture is edited.
(Written by Ashish Kumar and Vikas Bhadauria)

title: Fact Check: Old pic from Cambodia FALSELY shared to show the bad conditions of Indian schools
content:
This photo is not from India at all. It's from Cambodia.
A heart-wrenching photo of children in tattered clothes studying in a derelict classroom has gone viral on social media . Those sharing the photo claimed it was from India. A Twitter user  posted wrote, "Mr. Prime Minister, what sort of India are you creating in which children do not even have clothes to cover their bodies." Samajwadi Party leader IP Singh too shared the photo, stating it to be from India. However, he later deleted it. The archived version of his post can be seen here . AFWA found that the viral image is not from India but from Cambodia. ALSO READ | Fact Check: This dangerous leopard attack video is not from Dehradun but Jorhat in Assam AFWA PROBE Using reverse search, we found the viral picture in a blog named ' sabbayphoto.blogspot.com '. As per the blog, this photo was shot in the Kratie province of Cambodia. The blog also contained other photos from the same classroom. We also found that many Facebook users  had shared this image along with a few other similar ones with captions in the Khmer language, the official language of Cambodia. Some  had also mentioned that  that the image in question was taken in the Sambour district of the Kratie province in Cambodia. We also found this image in a March 2015 article published in the Cambodian news website Post Khmer . This article was written by one Thou Veasna, a resident of the Ratanakiri province of Cambodia.  Earlier in 2020, this image went viral as the photo of a school in Indonesia. At the time, the Indonesian fact-checking website turnbackhoax.id  had debunked it. (With inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Jan 9, 2023 14:38 IST

title: Fact Check: DOCTORED image of Rahul Gandhi having alcohol and chicken during Bharat Jodo Yatra viral
content:
This is a doctored image. The original photo featured Rahul Gandhi with a cup of either tea or coffee and plates of dry fruits. It was supposedly shot in a dhaba near Karnal, Haryana.
The Congress party's Bharat Jodo Yatra led by Rahul Gandhi is approaching its last lap as it moves towards Kashmir. As the Yatra moved through Haryana, a photo  of the former Congress party president made the rounds on social media. The photo showed Rahul Gandhi eating. Among the many things on the table in front of Gandhi was a plate of what looked like chicken drumsticks and a glass of alcohol. The photograph was supposedly taken in during the Yatra. This image was shared by many with captions taking sarcastic digs at the Congress leader like: "The ascetic, absorbed in penance." तपस्वी, तपस्या में लीन है ।। pic.twitter.com/6ABYuTrIws — कुँवर निर्विकार सिंह (@NirvikarRana) January 9, 2023 AFWA's investigation found this image was doctored. The original photo does not feature either alcohol or meat in it. AFWA Probe A reverse image search of the viral image took us to a tweet by a verified Twitter user named Gurpreet Garry Walia, who identifies himself as a journalist in his bio. This image showed Gandhi with a glass of what looked like either tea or coffee in front of him and plates of dry fruit. खाने की तस्वीर को ज़ूम करके देख रहे होंगे अंधभक्त की कोई गलती मिल जाए , सहमत हो मित्रो 😂 pic.twitter.com/c2HFkWAuuu — Gurpreet Garry Walia (@_garrywalia) January 8, 2023 This tweet from January 8 read: "Bhakts must be zooming into the image to check if they can find any flaws in it." Comparing both images made it clear that a glass of alcohol and a plate of chicken was later added digitally to the original one. When searching with relevant keywords, we came across a Times Now report published on January 9, decoding Gandhi's diet through this Yatra. This report also featured a tweet by journalist Paranjoy Guha Thakurta who shared the same image of Rahul Gandhi shot inside a cafe. Per Guha Thakurta's tweet from January 7, he met Gandhi when the Yatra crossed Punjab. Thakurta mentioned that they met while Gandhi was eating at a dhaba a few kilometres away from Haryana's Karnal. It was sheer coincidence: travelling to Punjab this morning, I crossed the Bharat Jodo Yatra. With some difficulty and a scuffle, I was able to meet Rahul Gandhi while he was eating at a dhaba a few kms from Karnal. We discussed politics, economics and India's richest men.. 1/2 pic.twitter.com/yg4394bFfT — ParanjoyGuhaThakurta (@paranjoygt) January 7, 2023 Whether Rahul Gandhi eats meat or drinks alcohol is beyond the scope of this story. However, it is more than clear that the image that has gone viral was photoshopped. Published By: Admin Published On: Jan 9, 2023 15:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Putin WASN'T reading Imran Khan's book, viral pic is photoshopped!
content:
This image is doctored. The original image dates back to June 14, 2016, and shows Putin reading a different book.
A photo of Russian President Vladimir Putin reading a book that features former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan on its cover has been shared widely on social media. Another book on the table can also be seen featuring Khan on its cover.Â
The book Putin appears to be reading is " Pakistan: A Personal History ", Khan's 2011 memoir. The book on the table appears to be " Let There Be Justice: The Political Journey of Imran Khan ," BJ Sadiq's 2017 biography of the cricketer-turned-politician. Putin Studying Imran Khan pic.twitter.com/iIfKJB5QZ0 — Imran-Riaz-ᏞꫀꪇꫀꪀᎴ  (@ImranRiazLegend) January 6, 2023
Putin Studying Imran Khan pic.twitter.com/iIfKJB5QZ0 — Imran-Riaz-ᏞꫀꪇꫀꪀᎴ  (@ImranRiazLegend) January 6, 2023
Supporters of Khan shared the photo ( https://bit.ly/3Iv8lJ3 ) with Urdu captions like: "The world reads Imran Khan and we are very lucky to have a leader like him." An archived version of such a post can be seen here . عمران خان Ú©Ùˆ دنیا پڑھتی ہے اور ہم بہت خوش نصیب ہیں کہ ہمیں عمران خان جیسا لیڈر ملا شکر الحمداللہ رب العالمین pic.twitter.com/oVebHLkav6 — ماہ نور ملک (@Mahnoor2662) January 6, 2023
عمران خان Ú©Ùˆ دنیا پڑھتی ہے اور ہم بہت خوش نصیب ہیں کہ ہمیں عمران خان جیسا لیڈر ملا شکر الحمداللہ رب العالمین pic.twitter.com/oVebHLkav6 — ماہ نور ملک (@Mahnoor2662) January 6, 2023
 AFWA's probe has found that the viral image was doctored.
A simple reverse image search of the viral image led us to the original one uploaded to the stock photo website Alamy . Uploaded on June 14, 2016, this photo showed Putin holding a book with a brown cover. Per Alamy's description, it showed Putin reviewing a book during a meeting with President of the Russian Academy of Sciences Vladimir Fortov and Director of the Federal Agency for Scientific Organisations Mikhail Kotyukov at the Kremlin.Â
A comparison between this photo and the viral one made it clear that the covers of Khan's memoir and biography were photoshopped into the 2016 photo.Â
We tried to identify the book Putin was reading in the photo. Google translated the cover to "Report". We could also see 2015 written on the brown cover. However, we weren't able to find what he was reading. The book to his side, however, was one we could identify. It was "Matter Under Extreme Conditions: Classification of States" by Vladimir E Fortov.
Thus, we concluded that Putin was not reading about Imran Khan. At least in this photo. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 9, 2023 18:16 IST

title: Fact Check: No 'AI Super Soldiers' yet! This robot fighter was created using VFX
content:
This robot in the video was created using VFX. The robot's stunts were performed by an actor.
Are robotic soldiers a reality now? A video  widely shared on social media purportedly shows an "AI super soldier" training. The video features a humanoid robot armed with a gun. The men training the robot appear to manhandle it on several occasions. A person shared this video  writing, "Designing robots capable of independently deciding to use deadly force against a human being should not be legal. I mean if they catch you doing this, you should be locked up for no less than five years. This is more dangerous than 95% of what we lock people up for." Another person  wrote, "You see where this is going? Those that control the droids will control us. They should be focussing on creating robots to help us advance, not to destroy humans." Archives of similar posts can be found here , and here . AFWA found that this video was created with the help of VFX and the "AI Super Soldier" in it is just an actor. AFWA Probe  A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video  shared on Twitter on October 28, 2019. In the responses to the tweet, one person shared a small portion of the clip highlighting the shadow of the robot, which surprisingly did not match its structure. The shadow, appearing to be that of an armed human, can be seen marked in red below. Fake ! pic.twitter.com/Xbs4CfciX9 — Killing Joke 🇸🇳🏆🌟 (@Fovsman) October 29, 2019 Further searches led us to an extended version of the viral video shared on Aparat, an Iranian video-sharing platform. This four-minute-long video featured more scenes from the supposed training, along with the viral clip. This video, however, started with an intro clip featuring an Apple computer with "Corridor Digital" written on it.  With the help of this clue, we found the YouTube channel  of Corridor Digital, an American production studio based in Los Angeles, known for creating viral online short-form videos. With the help of keywords, we found the same video  of the AI robot shared on its YouTube channel in October 2019. The video carried a disclaimer that read, "This video is a comedic parody and is not owned, endorsed, created by, or associated with the Boston Dynamics company." Boston Dynamics is an American engineering and robotics design company that was founded in 1992. It has been owned by the Hyundai Motor Group since December 2020. Further, we found another video  shared by Corridor Digital around the same time showing how the video was created using VFX. As it turns out, the "Super Soldier" was nothing but an actor, who was later replaced by a computer-generated robot. At the end of the video, one of the crew members said that it took around two months to create the video. Moreover, the same channel has created more such VFX videos  featuring a similar robot being knocked around by its trainers in a different setting. Earlier, we debunked such VFX creations being mistaken for real incidents, which can be found here , and here . (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Jan 9, 2023 19:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Brazil Police shoot ex-Prez Bolsonaro's son's plane? Thrilling chase video is from 2011
content:
The video is from 2011 and is not related to former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro or his family members. It shows Brazilian federal police chasing and stopping alleged smugglers.
On January 8, supporters of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro stormed into and vandalised the Congress, the Supreme Court, and the Presidential Palace. Hours after the invasion, security forces managed to retake the three buildings. Reportedly , Brazil's current President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered strict action against the rioters. Police arrested more than 300 people over the attacks.Â
Following this, a dramatic video  of a car chasing a plane on a dirt runway has been shared by many. A man in the car appears to shoot at the plane with an automatic weapon, damaging its wings and preventing it from flying away.Â
Sharing this clip , Twitter users claimed, "This is not a movie, this is Brazilian Police crashing into Jair Bolsonaro's eldest son, Flávio Bolsonaro, private plane as he attempts to flee the country. This comes as a response to the former Brazilian President's role in attempting to overturn their democratic election." The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .
Flavio Bolsonaro  is the eldest son of Jair Bolsonaro. He is also a lawyer and a politician.
AFWA's investigation found that the video has been on the internet since as early as 2011 and is not related to the former Brazilian President or his family members.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to various news reports. On November 4, 2011, India Today reported that this video showed how four men were arrested in a dramatic chase after a Brazilian police car crashed into their aircraft shattering its wings.Â
On November 2, 2011, the same video has been shared by Brazilian news outlet Estadao's YouTube channel with similar details. Around the same time, the Daily Mail reported the same , adding that this chase was conducted by the Brazilian Federal Police in the Ribeirao Preto municipality.
On December 1, 2015, Mirror reported that in the incident, five smugglers were arrested and Federal police seized 114 laptops as well as stolen printers and surveillance technology.
Thus, it is clear that the video has nothing to do with the recent anti-democratic rioting in Brazil and definitely does not show Jair Bolsonaro's son's plane being shot by the police. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 9, 2023 20:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Photo of man in exotic headgear is from 2021, NOT recent insurrection in Brazil capital
content:
Both photos date back to September 2021. While these demonstrations were also carried out by Bolsonaro supporters, they are not from the recent rioting in the Brazilian capital.
Supporters of the former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro stormed the Congress, the Supreme Court, and the Presidential Palace in Brasilia on January 8 after months of protests alleging election fraud. This comes around a week after Bolsonaro's rival, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva was sworn in as the 39th President of Brazil.Â
Bolsonaro has constantly denied his defeat in the elections stoking anti-democratic sentiments in his far-right followers. However, following the insurrection, reminiscent of the January 2021 attack on the US Capitol in Washington DC, he denied any role in encouraging the rioters on Twitter . Â
Meanwhile, two images have gone viral with these events in the backdrop. The first is an image of a man with yellow and green body paint wearing a horned and feathered headgear. The second is the photograph of the American conspiracy theorist Jake Angeli, also known as the QAnon Shaman, who had participated in the attack on the US Capitol building on January 6, 2021.Â
A Twitter user  shared these photos with the caption, "This Brazil protest going on must be CIA work behind the scenes. One picture is from the Jan 6th protests at the US capital and the other is from today in Brazil. You would think they would make it look less obvious." The archived version of this post can be seen here.Â
Another image that has been widely shared shows a sea of people in a large area. A Twitter user shared this image with the caption, "A Massive Crowd Scene from Sundays Election Protest in Brazil." The archived version of this post can be seen here. AFWA found that both the viral images are from 2021 and thus are not related to the recent demonstrations in Brazil.Â
AFWA found that both the viral images are from 2021 and thus are not related to the recent demonstrations in Brazil.Â
Using reverse search, we found this the first image of the headgeared man in a September 7, 2021, report published in the Brazilian news website Brasil de Fato . Per this report, it was from Sao Paulo, Brazil. The photo was credited to photographer Guilherme Gandolfi. Atos pró-Bolsonaro | Em São Paulo, manifestante se vestiu como o "homem dos chifres" na invasão do Capitólio, quando apoiadores de Trump organizaram manifestação golpista para questionar o resultado das eleições nos EUA. Foto: Guilherme Gandolfi @guifrodu pic.twitter.com/Z4o8cVwB1V — Brasil de Fato (@brasildefato) September 7, 2021
Gandolfi, a professional photographer based in Sao Paulo, shared this photo on his Twitter on January 9 and wrote in Portuguese that he was the one who shot it in the Avenida Paulista avenue of Sao Paulo on September 7, 2021, during a protest called by Bolsonaro. Resposta do a foto que fiz na av Paulista em 7 de setembro de 2021 em protesto convocado por Bolsonaro O capitólio BR foi planejado e deixaram acontecer pic.twitter.com/LxxVY9MLnX — Guilherme Gandolfi 📸 (@guifrodu) January 8, 2023
