In September 2021, multiple Brazilian websites  had carried this image in their reports. As per these reports, the man with yellow-green body paint participated in a demonstration on Brazilian Independence Day. His look was reportedly inspired by the aforementioned American conspiracy theorist Jake Angeli. A reverse search of the photo of the sea of protestors image led us to a September 7, 2021, report  published in a Brazilian news website. As per the report, this photo was the aerial view of a demonstration in Brazil in favour of Bolsonaro. Many other  Brazilian news websites  had also carried the same image in their September 2021 reports.  All these reports stated that this image was taken in Brazil's capital Brasilia where thousands of people had gathered to show their support for Bolsonaro on September 7, 2021.   The visuals of the recent Brazil riots can be seen in this New York Times report. Thus, we concluded that both images were from 2021 and unrelated to the recent riots.  Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 9, 2023 22:02 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of crowd gathered at Brazil's National Congress is NOT from recent riots
content:
This video has been on the internet since as early as September 2022. Thousands of far-right Brazilian protesters attacked multiple government buildings on January 8. But this video does not show that.
Echoing the January 2021 invasion of the United States Capitol by Donald Trump's supporters, on January 8, thousands of supporters of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro stormed  the country's Congress, Presidential Palace, and Supreme Court. Last year, after losing the elections to his leftist rival Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Bolsonaro challenged the election. Lula took office as President of Brazil on January 1.
Among many images and videos from the rampage circulating on social media is an 18-second video  that shows thousands of people gathered at a huge ground. As per those sharing it, the video  shows people who refused to accept Bolsonaro's election defeat and gathered to invade the Congress and the Presidential Palace.Â
AFWA found that the video has been on the internet since before Brazil's 2022 presidential elections. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to the same video shared by multiple people  on Twitter in September 2022. As per a few of these tweets, the video was from Brazil's 200th independence day celebration held on September 7. O TSE proibiu o presidente @jairbolsonaro de usar imagens do 7 de setembro em propagandas eleitorais. Vamos compartilhar pra avisar que está proibido, em? A onda verde e amarelo é GIGANTE! 🇧🇷💚 pic.twitter.com/1HCCijupSd — Carla Zambelli (@Zambelli2210) September 11, 2022
O TSE proibiu o presidente @jairbolsonaro de usar imagens do 7 de setembro em propagandas eleitorais. Vamos compartilhar pra avisar que está proibido, em? A onda verde e amarelo é GIGANTE! 🇧🇷💚 pic.twitter.com/1HCCijupSd — Carla Zambelli (@Zambelli2210) September 11, 2022
We also found a similar video uploaded to Twitter on September 7. Prevejo pânico na redação da globo e no comitê anti-Bolsonaro do DataFolha: #7desetembro pic.twitter.com/oAEcLnJkei — Flavio Bolsonaro #B22 (@FlavioBolsonaro) September 7, 2022
Prevejo pânico na redação da globo e no comitê anti-Bolsonaro do DataFolha: #7desetembro pic.twitter.com/oAEcLnJkei — Flavio Bolsonaro #B22 (@FlavioBolsonaro) September 7, 2022
Using Google Maps, we were also able to confirm the viral video is from Brazil's National Congress.Â
In September, Bolsonaro and Lula were busy campaigning for the presidential elections. Bolsonaro was reportedly accused of using the independence anniversary on September 7, 2022, for his election campaign. Multiple videos  of Bolsonaro addressing a large crowd in front of the National Congress were uploaded by people on Facebook on September 7.
Since the oldest version of the video we could find is from September, it is clear that the crowd gathered was not protesting against Lula's election win.Â
General elections  were held in Brazil in October 2022. Lula received the majority of the votes in the second round that was held on October 30, 2022, and became the president-elect of Brazil for a third term. Protests broke out in many states of Brazil as supporters of Bolsonaro refused to recognise Bolsonaro's defeat and alleged election fraud.Â
Backers of Bolsonaro on January 8 broke through police cordons and overran Brazil's three branches of power. The incident in fact triggered an international outcry with world leaders condemning the attack. As per reports , police arrested over 400 in the matter.Â
So, while we could not ascertain whether the viral video was shot on September 7, 2022, it is clear that it is at least three months old and not related to the January 8 riots. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 9, 2023 22:35 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show recent Indonesia earthquake 'caught on camera'
content:
This video shows tremors caused by an earthquake in Taiwan in September 2022.
Indonesia was rattled by a 7.7 magnitude earthquake in the early hours of January 10. The epicentre of this earthquake was 427 kilometres south of the Indonesian island of Ambon at a depth of 95 kilometres. Following this, a video allegedly showing the tremors has gone viral on social media.Â
The video shows four people standing in a forest clearing when the ground starts shaking vigorously, causing one of them to fall. Those sharing  the video claimed it showed the recent earthquake in Indonesia.Â
News Nation journalist Rahul Sisodia shared this video on Twitter  with the caption, "A powerful 7.7-magnitude #earthquake in #Indonesia was caught on camera." The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
Times Now Navbharat also used this video in its report about the recent Indonesian earthquake. An archived version can be seen here .Â
AFWA found that this video shows tremors that were felt in Taiwan in September 2022. Â
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a Yahoo News report from September 19, 2022. Per this report, this video was first shared by the 'Zhuoxi Township Mountaineering Association' on Facebook. Zhuoxi Township is a mountain indigenous township in Hualien County, Taiwan. Reportedly, when the earthquake occurred, the members of the mountaineering group were at an altitude of 1,000 metres.Â
Using a keyword search, we found that the Zhuoxi Township Mountaineering Association had posted this video on Facebook  on September 18, 2022. The association stated that when this earthquake hit, its members were working on a flora and fauna course on Zhuoxi Mountain.Â
Taiwanese and Chinese news portals like Setn.com , Ftvnews.com.tw , and Ettoday.net  also reported on this video in September 2022. Â
According to a New York Post report , a 6.8 magnitude earthquake hit Taiwan on September 18, 2022. Its epicentre was Taitung County and it followed a 6.4 magnitude earthquake on September 17, 2022.  As per Taiwan News , at least one person died and 146 were injured because of the earthquake.
It is also worth noting that the earthquake in Indonesia occurred at 2.47 am local time. In the viral video, daylight is clearly visible, something that would not be the case at close to three in the morning.Â
Thus, to sum up, a video of a 2022 earthquake in Taiwan was shared as footage from the recent quake in Indonesia. Â Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 10, 2023 17:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Railway cleaning upgrade under BJP regime? Both photos from 2020
content:
Both these images are shot in 2020. The first image is from Howrah station and was shot on May 11, 2020. The second image was shot at Asansol Junction on August 13, 2020.
A lot has been said about the modernisation of the Indian Railways after the Narendra Modi-led Bharatiya Janata Party government took over in 2014. In that context, a postcard being widely shared on social media features two images of railway stations. Both depict workers cleaning a platform but using different equipment.Â
While the first image shows several workers cleaning a platform with mops, the second shows a worker cleaning a railway platform with what looks like a motorised industrial scrubber-dryer.
The former was labelled "Before" and the latter was labelled "After". And the words, "This is Acche Din," were written at the bottom, to supposedly illustrate the technological upgrades that happened under the BJP-led Centre.
AFWA's investigation found that both images were from 2020.
A reverse search of the first image from the postcard led us to a Mint report from May 12, 2020. The article was about a clarification by the Ministry of Home Affairs for railway passengers. This report featured the same image and credited it to Reuters.  Subsequent refined searches led us to the original photo shared by the stock photo website Alamy . Per the details provided in Alamy, this photo was shot at the Howrah railway station on May 11, 2020, a day before rail services in India partially resumed after a nearly seven-week lockdown to slow the spread of Covid-19. Per reports, train services resumed on May 12, 2020, after the government decided to lift the strict lockdown. When we ran a reverse search of the second image, we found it in a tweet by the official account of Eastern Railway. Per the tweet, this photo was from Asansol Junction in West Bengal, shot on August 13, 2020. "Intensive cleaning of station platform, station adjacent area and track at Asansol on 13.8.2020 on the occasion of observance of 'Swachhta Saptah' from 10 to 16 August, 2020," read the tweet. Intensive cleaning of station platform, station adjacent area and track at Asansol on 13.8.2020 on the occasion of observance of 'Swachhta Saptah' from 10 to 16 August, 2020. pic.twitter.com/eBm7Gwv1Nu — Eastern Railway (@EasternRailway) August 13, 2020 Therefore, it is clear that both images are not only from the BJP regime in the Centre, but also from the same year.\ Also Read | 2 hotels among unsafe structures to be demolished in 'sinking' Joshimath tomorrow Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 10, 2023 20:14 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of elephant attacking van is NOT from Kerala, but from Sri Lanka
content:
This video is from the Monaragala district of Sri Lanka where an elephant attacked a van in search of food.
Just a day after the forest authority captured an elephant in Kerala's Wayanad on January 9, a video of an elephant wreaking havoc in the middle of a road started making the rounds on social media. The video featured a tusker, wandering on a road, allegedly somewhere near a forest area in Kerala.Â
A few seconds into the video, a van could be seen approaching the elephant. People could be seen throwing something from the inside of the van at the giant. The elephant then attacked the van and attempted to overturn it.  Scared, the people started escaping the vehicle while the elephant continued to attack. As more people arrived, the elephant retreated to the forest.Â
This video was shared by Porinju Veliyath, an investor and fund manager, who wrote , "Wild animals in Kerala are confused. Shrinking natural habitat. Shortage of food." Another person who shared the video wrote, "We Indians don't even wait for fellow humans to cross the road, why will we wait for an animal."
Zee News, on the other hand, shared the same video on January 9 , reporting it to be from Palamaneru road in Andhra Pradesh's Chittoor. Archives of such posts can be found here  and here .
AFWA found that this video is not from Kerala, or from India at all. This video is from Sri Lanka.
 A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared on the YouTube channel of Lankasri News, a Sri Lankan news website. In this video, "Holiday Sri Lanka" can be seen written on the back of the van being attacked by the tusker.Â
We found other extended versions  of this video showing multiple vehicles passing by , offering food to the elephant that later attacked a van carrying men, women, and even small kids. These videos, too, mentioned this was from Sri Lanka. This suggested that the video might not be from Kerala after all.Â
 Further, we found a news report  featuring the same video. The report said the incident that took place in Sri Lanka, where an elephant attacked a van full of people in search of food. The incident took place in Monaragala, a town located in the Monaragala district of the Uva Province. Another report  mentioned that the incident took place on January 1, 2023, adding that it happened on a road leading to the Yala National Park , a huge area of forest, grassland, and lagoons bordering the Indian Ocean, in southeastern Sri Lanka. Situated in the Uva province, Yala is the second largest national park in the country and home to wildlife such as leopards, elephants, and crocodiles, as well as hundreds of bird species.
The people attacked in the incident were reportedly  trying to feed the elephant. No one was injured in the incident. Following the attack , the Department of Wildlife and Conservation Director General reportedly instructed his officials to arrest those who fed wild animals, particularly elephants. Moreover, the Yala Forest Site Officers were deployed to drive away wild elephants straying on the Buttala-Kataragama road to prevent such accidents.Â
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 10, 2023 20:29 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOESN'T show Russia testing vacuum bombs amid ongoing invasion of Ukraine
content:
This video has been on the internet since as early as December 2019. Russia's invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022.
Since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, countless videos and images unrelated to the war have circulated online. Adding to this list is the dramatic video of a bomb blast recently tweeted by a verified Twitter account that goes by the name " Terror Alarm ". As per the tweet, the video shows Russia testing ODAB-500 vacuum bombs. Several other social media accounts also claimed that the video is from the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.Â
AFWA's investigation, however, found that the video has been on the internet since as early as December 2019. At that time, it was claimed to be from Syria. AFWA Probe
Thermobaric weapons or vacuum bombs are controversial because they are far more powerful than most conventional weapons of similar size and have a terrible impact on anyone caught in their blast radius. The Ukrainian government and human rights groups have reportedly accused Russia of using thermobaric weapons in Ukraine.Â
However, to confirm whether the viral video is related to the Russia-Ukraine war, we reverse-searched its keyframes. This led us to the same video uploaded to a YouTube channel on December 12, 2019. As per this channel, the video showed the use of ODAB-500 vacuum bombs in Syria.Â
In the initial months of 2020, the same video was shared by multiple people on Facebook , who also claimed the video to be from the civil war in Syria. Â
Paste: https://fb.watch/hZ9WEvOnxo/Â
We also found multiple media reports about the use of Russian-made thermobaric weapons in Syria's civil war. According to a report published by British charity Action on Armed Violence (AOAV) in 2013, the thermobaric weapon is one of the 12 deadliest conventional weapons used in the Syrian war.
This video was earlier fact-checked by BBC in 2022. We couldn't ascertain the exact location of the viral video. However, it is clearly old and has been on the internet since before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Also Read |Â Fact Check: Video of elephant attacking van is NOT from Kerala, but from Sri Lanka Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Jan 10, 2023 23:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Arma 3 strikes again! Video game footage falsely shared as Brazil protestors shooting govt plane
content:
This is not from Brazil, or for that matter, even real. This footage is from the video game Arma 3.
Brazilian security forces detained about 1,500 people after supporters of former president Jair Bolsonaro stormed government buildings in Brasilia on January 8. Following the insurrection attempt, footage allegedly showing demonstrators in Brazil firing at a government plane with improvised anti-aircraft guns has gone viral on social media.Â
A Twitter user shared this video and wrote, "Escalation in #Brazil as protestors fire on government plane with improvised anti-aircraft guns. As you can see these home-built weapons are very inaccurate, which poses a danger to other civilians." The archived version of this claim can be seen here .Â
While many doubted the authenticity of this claim, some believed it to be a genuine video from Brazil . Some also claimed that this video was not from Brazil but from Mexico .Â
AFWA found that the viral video is from a video game.Â
We noticed that many people wrote words like "Arma" and "video game" while commenting on the viral video. Â
 We subsequently ran a keyword search on YouTube. This led us to a three-minute-long video on the channel "Compared Comparison". The visuals seen in the viral video can be seen here at the 1.39-minute mark. On comparing the visuals of the viral video with this one, we noticed several similarities between them. In the caption of this video, it was mentioned that this was a simulation created in Arma 3, an open-world, realism-based, military tactical shooting video game developed and published by Bohemia Interactive, a Czech video game developer. The person running the YouTube channel "Compared Comparison" is based in Austria and has stated in the "About" section that he creates modern cinematic military films using Arma 3 and DCS (Digital Combat Simulator). Earlier, videos from Arma 3 were passed off as real war footage in the backdrop of the Armenia-Azerbaijan war , the Israel-Palestine conflict and the Russia-Ukraine war . . AFWA debunked many such claims. Thus, it's clear that a video game simulation has been shared as protesters in Brazil firing at a government aircraft.  Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jan 11, 2023 18:11 IST

title: Fact Check: This scary photo is not from Joshimath - in fact, it's not even from India
content:
This photo does not show Joshimath. It shows the 2018 Llusco landslide that occurred in the Cusco region of Peru.
Joshimath, a pilgrimage town and the winter seat of the Badrinath, has lately made headlines for all the wrong reasons. A place that would otherwise see tourists at this time of the year now has buildings marked with red 'X' marks amid the land subsidence tragedy. Water gushing from under the ground and cracks in establishments has become a common sight in the panic-stricken city.Â
In fact, Joshimath and its surrounding areas have reportedly been sinking at the rate of 6.5 cm per year. With almost 700 buildings now marked unsafe in the holy town of Joshimath, more than 80 families so far have had to shift to safer locations away from their homes in the bone-chilling Uttarakhand winter. Locals reportedly blame the nearby Tapovan project of the National Thermal Power Corporation or NTPC, saying it has aggravated the situation.
As this crisis continued, a postcard about Joshimath that was widely shared on social media , featured a photo of land broken into numerous blocks. Scary giant cracks and fissures were visible in the aerial shot. The postcard said: "600 families of Uttarakhand's sinking Joshimath to be shifted to safer locations, plea in SC to declare it 'National Disaster'. Construction works around hills halted, PMO takes charge." Â AFWA found that the photo does not show the sinking Joshimath, but a 2018 landslide in Peru, a South American nation. AFWA PROBE A reverse search of the photo in question led us to a YouTube video titled "5 biggest landslides in all history." The video shared on August 8, 2022, featured the viral photo while talking about the 1970 Ancash earthquake, the most catastrophic natural disaster in the history of Peru. Additionally, they credited the photo to the Ministry of Defense of Peru. This suggested that the photo was not from Joshimath, or probably India at all. We also found the same photo shared by a blog post written by Philip S. Prince , a faculty member at Virginia Tech, an American university. The blog used a sand model to explain the 2018 Llusco landslide that occurred outside of Cusco, Peru. It further mentioned that the landslide destroyed the village of Lutto Kututo.Â
AFWA found that the photo does not show the sinking Joshimath, but a 2018 landslide in Peru, a South American nation.
A reverse search of the photo in question led us to a YouTube video titled "5 biggest landslides in all history." The video shared on August 8, 2022, featured the viral photo while talking about the 1970 Ancash earthquake, the most catastrophic natural disaster in the history of Peru. Additionally, they credited the photo to the Ministry of Defense of Peru. This suggested that the photo was not from Joshimath, or probably India at all.
We also found the same photo shared by a blog post written by Philip S. Prince , a faculty member at Virginia Tech, an American university. The blog used a sand model to explain the 2018 Llusco landslide that occurred outside of Cusco, Peru. It further mentioned that the landslide destroyed the village of Lutto Kututo.Â
Further, searches led us to a blog by AGU Blogosphere, a network of blogs hosted by the American Geophysical Union, the world's largest organisation of Earth and space scientists. The blog post from March 15, 2018, stated that a dramatic landslide at Llusco in the Cusco region of Peru destroyed a hundred houses and led to the government declaring an emergency . Â
The landslide, which reportedly covered an area of about 30 hectares, was caused by high pore water pressures.Â
We also found the viral photo tweeted by the official handle of the Ministry of Defense of Peru on March 16, 2018. The caption in Spanish read: "Minister of Defense, Jorge Kisic, together with the regional governor of Cusco, @EdwinLiconaGRC, carries out an inspection overflight in the area affected by landslides in the district of Llusco, Cusco." Ministro de Defensa, Jorge Kisic, junto con el gobernador regional de Cusco, @EdwinLiconaGRC , realiza sobrevuelo de inspección en zona afectada por desplazamiento de tierra en el distrito de Llusco, #Cusco . pic.twitter.com/U7b1TXzgNC — Mindef Perú (@MindefPeru) March 15, 2018
Ministro de Defensa, Jorge Kisic, junto con el gobernador regional de Cusco, @EdwinLiconaGRC , realiza sobrevuelo de inspección en zona afectada por desplazamiento de tierra en el distrito de Llusco, #Cusco . pic.twitter.com/U7b1TXzgNC — Mindef Perú (@MindefPeru) March 15, 2018
We also found a drone video of the landslide-affected region shot in March 2018 by Fameco Producciones, a film production studio based in Peru. The area filled with cracks and fissures resembled those in the viral photo.
Thus, it became clear that this photo showed a 2018 natural disaster in Peru, and not the ongoing crisis in Joshimath, Uttarakhand.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 11, 2023 21:35 IST

title: Fact Check: No need to be nostalgic! This ISN'T what Pan Am's economy class looked like in the 60s
content:
This is a mock-up interior of Boeing's 747 and not actually from Pan Am's 747. Moreover, the 747 first entered into service with Pan Am on January 22, 1970, and not the 1960s.
Pan American World Airways, also famously known as "Pan Am",  was a premier international air carrier of the United States for much of the 20th century. It was the first airline to operate Boeing's 747, the world's first commercial wide-body jumbo jet aircraft in the 1970s. At one point, Pan Am was operating 25 Boeing 747s. Almost 31 years ago on December 4, 1991, Pan Am flew its final flight and filed for bankruptcy.
A Facebook post now going viral purportedly shows what the economy class seating on a luxurious Pan Am 747 Flight in the 1960s looked like. And it's everything that economy class isn't anymore: wide comfortable seats, ample legroom, and a lot of space to breathe.
AFWA probed the claim and found that it is not a photograph of the economy class in a Pan Am flight. Rather it is a full-scale mock-up layout of the interior of a plane designed for the Boeing 747.  AFWA Probe
A reverse search of the photo led us to an array of media reports and photographs. Among them was a photo on Imgur credited to a man called Joseph Stutter. According to the photo's caption, it was a "Boeing 747's interior mock-up".
Subsequent searches led us to a report by Hoax Or Fact , according to which, this interior model never materialised into a real flight. It added that this was designed by Joe Stutter to demonstrate what the flight could look like. Another similar report by Huffpost , affirmed that the image only depicted the future vision of Boeing's 747 economy seating by engineer Joe Sutter, Boeing's lead designer on the 747 and author of "747: Creating the World's First Jumbo Jet and Other Adventures from a Life in Aviation".Â
On further probe, we also came across a YouTube video that manifestly revealed the interiors of the first 747 Pan Am flight in detail.Â
Pat Nixon, then First Lady of the United States christened Pan Am's first 747 as "Clipper Young America"  at Dulles International Airport (later Washington Dulles International Airport). Moreover, the 747 first entered into service with Pan Am on January 22, 1970, and not the 1960s.Â
Thus, it is clear that this is just a mock-up interior of Boeing's 747 and not from Pan Am's 747 fleet which was in service. The vision of 747's designer Joseph Stutter could never taste the sky.
More than 50 years later, many airlines are still flying modern and refurbished models of 747s in their fleets. Boeing rolled out its final 747 on December 6, last year.Â
(Written by Vikas Bhadauria) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 12, 2023 21:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi paused aarti at Brahma Sarovar, but it was not for a photoshoot
content:
This video was clipped to remove context. Rahul Gandhi was repeating the actions of the temple men who performed the aarti. After every three rounds, they paused for some time and Rahul Gandhi did the same.
Critics and detractors of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi often question his "Hinduness". On multiple instances, especially recently during his Bharat Jodo Yatra, photos and videos from Gandhi's temple visits have been used to claim his religiosity is mere performance. A recent example of this is a video of Rahul Gandhi performing aarti . Those sharing the video, which had ANI's logo on it, accused the Gandhi scion of pausing aarti to pose for a photo. In the video, Rahul Gandhi can be seen doing just that: pausing for a bit and then resuming once a photographer arrives. AFWA's investigation, however, found that the video in question has taken out of context. The pause, as seen in the video, is part of the ritual. AFWA probe Using relevant keywords, we found a longer version of the same video tweeted by ANI on January 8, 2023. Per this tweet, the video was from Rahul Gandhi's visit to Brahma Sarovar in Haryana's Kurukshetra during his Bharat Jodo Yatra. #WATCH | Congress MP Rahul Gandhi performs aarti at Brahma Sarovar in Kurukshetra, Haryana. pic.twitter.com/Mt9kNyrDHL — ANI (@ANI) January 8, 2023 In this longer version, one can see a few men standing in front of Rahul Gandhi and performing aarti along with him. The men could be seen pausing after oscillating the aarti lamp thrice and the Congress MP did the same. The official YouTube channel of the Indian National Congress also shared a longer video of Rahul Gandhi performing the aarti at Kurukshetra on January 8. To get to the bottom of this, AFWA spoke to Pandit Balram Gautam, the director of Parashakti Ved Pathshala, who conducted the special puja for Rahul Gandhi in Kurukshetra. The priest said, "Rahul Gandhi was repeating after the other Brahmins who were performing the aarti. He didn't stop for a photoshoot. After every three rounds, the Brahmins stopped the aarti on each side and Rahul Gandhi was doing the same. Aarati of this similar form is performed everywhere. We had also performed a special puja for Rahul Gandhi on the day." We were also able to find several other videos from Brahma Sarovar where aarti was performed in a similar fashion. Rahul Gandhi's visit to Brahma Sarovar on the 114th day of the Bharat Jodo Yatra was widely reported by media organisations. It is hence clear that a short video of Rahul Gandhi performing aarti at Brahma Sarovar was taken out of context and shared with misleading claims. Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: Jan 12, 2023 22:00 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show Chinese soldier beating Uyghur Muslim man for possessing Quran
content:
This video is from Indonesia, not from China. It shows a suspected pickpocket being assaulted in May 2017.
China's alleged mistreatment of Uyghurs , a mostly Muslim ethnic minority from the northwestern region of Xinjiang, has been internationally reported for years now. The United States has gone so far as to call it genocide and later, the United Nations noted that China's policies "may constitute international crimes, in particular crimes against humanity."Â
China, on the other hand, has denied all allegations of human rights abuses , insisting that the crackdown in Xinjiang was necessary to prevent terrorism and root out Islamist extremism, adding that camps were an effective tool for re-educating inmates in its fight against terrorism.
Now, a video purportedly showing a Chinese soldier beating an Uyghur man for possessing a copy of the Quran has been shared widely. The horrific video shows two men in military uniforms and a third man clad only in underwear in a room. One of the military men mercilessly whipped the mostly-naked man, who let out bloodcurdling screams all throughout.
Those sharing the video claimed , "This is a Chinese officer beating a Muslim Uyghur for having a copy of the Quran in his house! Everyone send this out so the world knows what is happening in East Turkistan."
AFWA's investigation found that the video is actually from 2017 and shows an Indonesian soldier assaulting a suspected thief.Â
Using relevant keywords and a reverse image search, we found that the video was quite viral in Indonesia in May 2017. According to a May 2017 report published in Tribun Jateng , the incident occurred at the Depok Baru Station in Jakarta on May 13, 2017.Â
Reportedly, the man being whipped was a suspected pickpocket. After the video went viral, the officer seen whipping the man was dismissed. A report published on May 24, 2017, in Tribune Medan also said the same . This proved that the video was neither from China nor recent.Â
In fact, it's been previously debunked. On January 3, 2019, China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lijian Zhao wrote on Twitter, "Fake news! Not Chinese language!! Not even Chinese police uniform!!! This is sheer propaganda against China, trying to sabotage relations between China & muslim countryies. There's no 'East Turkistan' in China. title: Fact Check: This is not the 'first ever snowfall' in Haryana village, it's a 2020 hailstorm video
content:
This video is more than two years old. And instead of snowfall, this video shows the aftermath of a hailstorm there.
North Indians have been battling bone-chilling cold weather since the beginning of the new year. Reportedly, January 2023 could go down in the books as the coldest for the region , and a weather expert has predicted that temperatures may even be as low as -4 degrees Celsius between January 14 and 19.
Amid this, a video of a car driving on what looks like a snow-covered road has gone viral. Those sharing the video claimed it was from the Barwala village of Haryana, as evidenced by a green signboard with "Barwala" written in English and Hindi in the video.Â
A Twitter user shared the video and wrote, "Neither #HIMACHAL nor #KASHMIR. First time in History Snowfall is seen in BARWALA village of #Haryana". The archived version of this post can be seen here .
AFWA found that the viral video is neither recent nor does it show snow.
We noticed that many people responded to the viral tweets, saying that the video showed the aftermath of hailstorms and not snowfall. We also noticed that the video contained the watermark "Fb.com/hrroadwaysfans". Subsequently, we looked for the Facebook page @hrroadwaysfans, and found that it had shared the same video on December 27, 2022. Using keyword search, we found a longer and much older version of the viral video. A YouTube channel shared it on March 14, 2020, with the title: "Barwala by pass # hailstorm #full rain fall barwala news". In the longer version of the video, a building with "JD Jindal Hospital" written on it could be seen. We looked for "JD Jindal Hospital" on Google maps and found a hospital with the same name in Hisar, Haryana. Hisar is less than 40 km away from Barwala village. On comparing photos of the hospital on Google Maps with the screenshots of the viral video, one can easily conclude it's the same building. Using Google Street View, we were able to geolocate the place seen in the viral video. AFWA spoke to Dr Surender Kumar, the owner of JD Jindal Hospital, who told us that he had never heard about snowfall in the area and that the viral video could probably have been related to a hailstorm. India Today's Hisar correspondent Praveen Kumar also said that to the best of his knowledge, Hisar had never witnessed snowfall, adding that the viral video could have been from a hailstorm. This year, so far, there have been no hailstorms in the area. Thus, it's clear that an old video showing the aftermath of a hailstorm in Haryana is being falsely shared as a recent video of snowfall there.  Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 13, 2023 19:23 IST

title: Fact Check: These protestors chanting 'Azaadi' has NOTHING to do with Pak-Baloch issue
content:
This video does not show Baloch nationalists asking for freedom from Pakistan, but a student protest in Pakistan against the Taliban's ban on the education of Afghan women.
Baloch separatists have been fighting for control of their land for a long time now, maintaining that they have been economically marginalised by the Pakistani government. Videos of protests and demonstrations often surface on social media showing Baloch activists demanding recognition of their sovereignty and rights.Â
The year 2022 was particularly dreadful for Balochistan as the Pakistan army reportedly tortured 187 people, forcibly disappeared 629, and extrajudicially killed 195 according to an annual report released by Paank , a human rights organisation of the Baloch National Movement.Â
Amid this, a video making the rounds on social media supposedly shows people from Balochistan demanding freedom from Pakistan. The video shows a woman, along with several other people, clapping hands and chanting "Azaadi".Â
A person shared this video  writing, "We demand azadi, Free Balochistan from the occupation of the Pak Army, and an end to barbarism. This is the voice of the Balochs, and we'll not allow Pakistan to abuse our rights any longer." Another wrote , "The voice of freedom from oppressed Balochis is reverberating in not only in Islamabad but also in the freedom loving world. And the free world is shouting 'azaadi' for you. Free Balochistan." Archives of such posts can be found here , here , and here .
AFWA found that this video shows a protest in Pakistan against the ban on the education of women in Afghanistan and not a call for secession from the nation. Â AFWA Probe Â
A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video took us to the same video tweeted  on January 1 by Habib Khan, founder of the non-governmental organisation Afghan Peace Watch (APW). According to his tweet, the video showed Pashtun students in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa demonstrating in support of Afghan women.Â
Further, we found an extended version of the video tweeted by Muhammad Faheem, a journalist based in Peshawar. His caption in Urdu stated that the video showed a student protest at the University of Peshawar against the ban on education and work for women in Afghanistan. Peshawar is the capital of the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. آزادی آزادی آزادی افغانستان میں لڑکیوں Ú©Û' تعلیم حاصل کرنے اور کام کرنے پر پابندی کیخلاف جامعہ پشاور میں طلباء Ùˆ طالبات کا احتجاج pic.twitter.com/QfcMRsokGO — Muhammad Faheem (@MeFaheem) December 26, 2022

Using this clue, we found Pakistani  and Afghani media outlets  reporting that this video was a protest at the University of Peshawar in response to the Taliban's closure of universities for Afghani women.Â
BBC Pashto on December 26, 2022 , also covered this protest and shared videos from different angles. The protestors, in this video, could be seen holding placards that said, "Ban Taliban", and, "Let Afghan Girls Learn."Â
While sharing the video on Twitter, Hum News, a Pakistani Urdu news channel, tagged Jamaima Afridi. We headed over to the profile  and found that she was the woman seen in the video. Afridi is a journalist and a women's rights activist based in Peshawar.
Afridi also tweeted the viral video, along with another video  from this protest, writing: "Today I organised a protest against the ban on women's access to education, movement, and work in Afghanistan. Thus, it is clear that a video of students protesting the Taliban's ban on the education of women, and not Baloch nationalists demanding freedom from Pakistan.Â
