title: Fact check: This 'strange object' DIDN'T cause Turkey earthquake, 2022 Kazakhstan rocket launch clip viral
content:
This video is neither recent nor from Turkey or Syria. It shows a common optical effect caused by a 2022 rocket launch in Kazakhstan.
Conspiracy theories around large-scale disasters are hardly a new phenomenon. If some on social media are to be believed, the deadly earthquakes in Turkey on February 6 were preceded by sightings of something strange in the night sky — perhaps a hint at something other than a natural phenomenon at play. People shared videos of a jellyfish-like pattern of lights in the sky that was allegedly seen right before the quakes. While many shared  the video, wondering what this phenomenon was, others presented more specific theories. For example, a Twitter user wrote : "That is the CIA death ray in action. They use it to initiate a shift the earths tectonic plates via an ultra low frequency phase shift induced plasma burst (sic)." Archives of similar posts can be found here  and here . AFWA found that this video shows a 2022 rocket launch — that too not in Turkey or Syria but in Kazakhstan. AFWA Probe A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared on September 25, 2022, on TGStat, a Russian firm that provides metrics about Telegram channels. Under the video, the text in Kyrgyz read: "Balkash. Saturday." Balkhash is a lake in southeastern Kazakhstan. Using this clue, we found the same video shared by another Twitter user around the same time. The caption mentioned the location of the video as Baikonur Cosmodrome in southern Kazakhstan. Baikonur Cosmodrome - Southern Kazakhstan 06/10/2022 pic.twitter.com/MQsUIJdvE3 — Catasach (@catasach369) October 7, 2022 Further, we found a report ( ) from "Kazinform", a news agency based in Kazakhstan, about citizens of the central-Asian country sharing photos and videos of a rocket launch in Baikonur. While the report did not contain the viral clip, the videos and photos in it bore a striking resemblance to the video in question. On September 21, 2022, NASA launched the Soyuz-2.1a rocket with the Soyuz MS-22 manned spacecraft from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. The crew, which consisted of two Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Prokopiev and Dmitry Petelin with NASA astronaut Francisco Rubio, reached the International Space Station (ISS) in three hours . The launch was broadcasted by news outlets  as well as Roscosmos  and NASA. After the launch, an optical effect called "Space Jellyfish" was reportedly observed in the Kazakh sky during the separation of the stages of the Soyuz launch vehicle. Apart from Kazakhstan, people living in Novosibirsk, a city in Russia, also captured  similar photos of the launch in September 2022. A "Space Jellyfish" or a "Rocket Jellyfish" is a rocket launch-related phenomenon caused by sunlight reflecting off the high-altitude plume gases emitted by a rocket during twilight. Similar sightings have been reported earlier as well. (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Feb 10, 2023 18:50 IST

title: No, Modi didn't inflate number of tap water beneficiaries by 3cr overnight. Clipped video shared
content:
The second clip of the PM's speech in Rajya Sabha was clipped out the context. In his speech, Modi mentioned that there were three crore households with tap water connections before the BJP came to power, and conclude the total number was 11 crore.
On February 8 and 9, Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered speeches in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, replying to the debate on the Motion of Thanks to the President's Speech. Following this, a video containing a section from each speech began making rounds on social media. People alleged, while sharing this video, that the PM inflated the number of tap water beneficiaries in his Rajya Sabha speech. The first clip was from the February 8 Lok Sabha speech where the prime minister said, "After 75 years of our independence, now eight crore families are getting tap water connection." In the second clip from the February 9 Rajya Sabha speech, PM Modi could be heard saying, "Now, 11 crore families are getting water through a tap connection." PM मोदी के फेंकने का नमूना देखिए। • कल लोकसभा में बताया कि नल जल योजना के लाभार्थी '𝟴 करोड़' हैं। • आज राज्यसभा में बताया कि नल जल योजना के लाभार्थी '𝟭𝟭 करोड़' हैं। महज 21 घंटे में '𝟯 करोड़' लाभार्थी बढ़ गए। ये कौन सा जादू है? pic.twitter.com/VJw2KewoVJ — Congress (@INCIndia) February 9, 2023 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The video  was shared on Twitter by the official account of the Indian National Congress. The tweet called out the PM's supposed penchant for exaggerating, and questioned how the number went from eight crore to 11 crore in a matter of 21 hours. The tweet read: "See an example of how PM Modi bluffs. Yesterday in Lok Sabha, he said that the number of beneficiaries of the water mission was eight crore. Today in Rajya Sabha, he said the number of beneficiaries was 11 crore. The number of beneficiaries increased by three crore within 21 hours. What kind of magic is this?"  Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel  and senior Congress leader Digvijaya Singh  among others shared the same video. बस इतनी ही तेजी से उनके मित्र की संपत्ति बढ़ती गयी। pic.twitter.com/lK18dkniJL — Bhupesh Baghel (@bhupeshbaghel) February 9, 2023 The archived versions of these tweets can be seen here  and here . AFWA's investigation found that the video of the PM's address in Rajya Sabha was clipped out of context. AFWA Probe We found PM Modi's Lok Sabha address on the YouTube channel of Sansad TV. The part about tap water connections appeared around the 57 minutes and 30 seconds mark. In the speech, PM Modi addressed Speaker Om Birla and said, "Aazadi ke 75 saal beet gaye. Aath crore parivaron ko aaj naal se jal mila hain. Wo maataein tumhare jhutth ko kaise sweekar karengi? Tumhari galtiyon ko, gaaliyon ko, kaise sweekar karengi?" (Seventy-five years of independence have passed. Now eight crore families have received water from taps. How will those mothers accept your lies? How will they accept your mistakes and abuses?) The part where Modi speaks about the tap water connection in Lok Sabha can be seen below. Did PM Modi increase the number of beneficiaries by three crore during his speech in the Rajya Sabha the next day? Let's find out. We found the complete video of PM Modi's address in Rajya Sabha uploaded to Sansad TV's YouTube channel on February 9. Here, around the 13 minutes and 13 seconds mark, the PM spoke about the water supply mission. He said, "Aazadi ke pehle se abb tak, hum sarkar mein aaye tab tak, sirf teen crore gharon tak nal se jal milta tha. Aadarniya Sabhapati Ji, pichle teen-char saal mein, aaj, 11 crore logon ko nal se jal mil raha hain." (Before India's independence, up till the time we came to power, only three crore houses used to receive water from taps. Respected chairman sir, in the last three to four years, today, 11 crore people are getting water from taps.) After watching the original video, it becomes clear that the first part of PM Modi's statement in the Rajya Sabha, where he stated the number of tap water connection users before the Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power, was clipped out from the viral video. So, while the prime minister mentioned eight crore tap connections in Lok Sabha as the achievement of his government, he included the number of tap connections provided before his tenure in Rajya Sabha, taking the number to 11 crore. To verify the official numbers of beneficiaries, we visited the website of the Jal Jeevan Mission  and came across the latest numbers as of February 10, 2023. Per the information there, a total of 7,90,23,796 tap water connections, about nine lakh 76 thousand short of touching eight crore, have been provided since the launch of the Jal Jeevan Mission on August 15, 2019. This estimate was mentioned by PM Modi in his Lok Sabha speech on February 8, 2023. The total number of households with tap water connections before and after the launch of this mission was also featured in the dashboard of this website. The number was more than three crore 20 lakh before August 15, 2019, and now it stands at more than 11 crore 13 lakh — covering 57.45 per cent of the targeted households that will be served with a tap water connection. Therefore, it is safe to conclude that a clipped video was shared to make it look like PM Modi inflated the number of tap water beneficiaries by three crore overnight. advertisement   Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Feb 11, 2023 18:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Mahua Moitra DIDN'T assault cop after 'unparliamentary language' row, this clip is from 2018
content:
This video is from August 2018 when Moitra got in a scuffle with a cop at an airport in Silchar, Assam.
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra recently drew flak for using an expletive during the Motion of Thanks on the President's Address in the Lok Sabha on February 7. Following her speech, in which she attacked the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party over the Adani-Hindenburg row, angry exchanges between the BJP and TMC members escalated to the use of "unparliamentary language" by Moitra. Moitra, however, has refused to apologise for her remark, which has now been expunged from the records. Following this, a video showing Moitra in a scuffle with a lady police officer started making the rounds on social media. Those sharing it claimed that this incident took place after her controversial parliamentary speech. Archives of these posts can be found here  and here . AFWA found that the video of Moitra manhandling a lady cop is from a five-year-old incident. AFWA Probe A keyword search on Google about a scuffle between the TMC MP and a police officer led us to a tweet from the ANI News  from August 2018, carrying the 11-second-long clip in question. The caption stated that the video showed Moitra assaulting a lady constable who tried to restrain her after TMC leaders were stopped at Silchar Airport in Assam. It further stated that the police constable sustained injuries during this scuffle. #WATCH : TMC's Mahua Moitra seen assaulting lady constable who tried to restrain Mahua Moitra after TMC leaders were stopped at Silchar Airport. Constable received injuries. #NRCAssam pic.twitter.com/FJjNQ77ngO — ANI (@ANI) August 2, 2018 According to another report  from the time, Moitra was part of an eight-member delegation sent by the TMC on a two-day visit. They were there to assess the situation in Assam and campaign against the final draft of the National Register of Citizenship, which reportedly  left out over 40 lakh names. The delegation, however, was stopped by security forces at the airport on August 2, 2018. They were reportedly prohibited from visiting people or addressing any gathering as Section 144 under the CrPC was imposed in the district. Following this, TMC members engaged in a scuffle with police officials and the viral video of Moitra tackling a female cop shows that. India Today interviewed Moitra post the incident, which can be seen below. Mahua Moitra, who was in TMC team in Sichar, speaks to India Today, said the delegation was confined illegally by Assam police. Listen in. Full video of #NewsToday - https://t.co/LAwkWgZdzr pic.twitter.com/gK64irYYkF — IndiaToday (@IndiaToday) August 3, 2018 Two Assam police women constables were reportedly injured in this incident, one of whom lodged an FIR against TMC supremo and West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Moitra. The TMC delegation, on the other hand, lodged a police complaint against the then Assam CM Sarbananda Sonowal, alleging "manhandling" and "illegal detention" by Assam Police officials. Thus, it's clear that a video showing a five-year-old incident is being falsely shared as recent in the backdrop of Moitra's recent parliamentary controversy. (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Feb 13, 2023 15:53 IST

title: Fact Check: This futuristic 'transparent smartphone' is literally just a piece of glass and some VFX
content:
This video does not show a real device. It's a piece of glass made to look like a smartphone using VFX.
A visual element that has been a staple of sci-fi movies and shows is that in the nebulous distant future, everything from monitors to TVs to hand-held devices is transparent. Tech companies have tried to capitalise on the futurists' love for this sort of elegant minimalism.Â
However, transparency in hand-held, as of now, is limited to see-through back panels. Though not for long, if some social media posts are to be taken seriously, a see-through smartphone may be making its way to the markets soon.
A video making the rounds on social media shows a person holding a smartphone as transparent as glass. As the person surfs through the settings and icons in the menu, his fingers can be seen holding the phone from the back. Not only that, the person then puts this smartphone on a wireless charger — just as transparent as the smartphone it is charging.
People shared the video of this phone , writing: "This is a transparent smartphone design. Coming soon in our market." While some admired the device's beauty , others replied to the tweet with their theories on how this futuristic phone was made. Archives of such posts can be seen here , here , and here .Â
AFWA found that this transparent smartphone is indeed too good to be true. The video, in fact, does not show a smartphone at all but a piece of glass and some VFX. AFWA PROBE
A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video led us to the website of AE Tips and Tricks which lists tutorials shared by different YouTube channels and designers for Adobe After Effects, a VFX and motion graphics software. On the website, we found a video tutorial for creating a transparent phone, shared by VFX Studio Koliba in April 2019. Before the tutorial began, the video showed a person using a see-through smartphone. This was the same as the viral clip.Â
Following that, a behind-the-scenes clip revealed that the person in the video was holding a piece of glass shaped like a smartphone with curved edges. Later, this glass became the "Transparent Smartphone" with the help of After Effects. This YouTube channel has, similarly, shared video tutorials for making different devices like TV, and a Smart Bracelet transparent. Not just that, the channel also has tutorials for making mind-boggling videos of a man pouring juice from a smartphone or bringing objects from a TV screen into reality.
Sadly, a smartphone as see-through as the one in the viral video does not exist as of yet. However, the concept of transparent phones is not new in itself. LG GD900, a slider phone equipped with a see-through keyboard, is considered the world's first transparent phone that was launched in 2009. Subsequently, companies came up with transparent displays, and prototypes of see-through phones .
In 2018, Chinese smartphone manufacturer Xiaomi announced its first "transparent" smartphone with a see-through back panel, but it wasn't received well by the public .Â
Most recently, the British technology startup, Nothing, released the much-hyped transparent phone — the Nothing Phone. Meanwhile, companies like Samsung and LG have also patented technology needed to make transparent smartphones. However, the existing concepts and devices are nowhere near the transparent phone shown in the viral video.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Feb 13, 2023 15:53 IST

title: Fact Check: This picturesque cricket stadium is NOT in Pakistan, it's just concept art
content:
Although there is a cricket stadium in this exact spot in Gwadar, Pakistan, the stadium in the viral photo was concept art designed by a Mumbai architecture firm.
A photo of a cricket stadium surrounded by towering cliffs has been making the rounds on social media lately. Those sharing it claimed that this stadium was in Balochistan, Pakistan. The most attractive cricket stadium of #Balochistan ," #Pakistan " one should visit and see the natural beauty of Gawader pic.twitter.com/5NPtw28nQy — sulmanbaloch (@sulmanb17963407) February 13, 2023 One such tweet read, "The most attractive cricket stadium of Balochistan, Pakistan one should visit and see the natural beauty of Gawader." Gawader or Gwadar is a port city located on the southwestern coast of Balochistan. The archived version of such a post can be seen here . Another person shared the photo and wrote: "The Gwadar #cricket stadium in Balochistan, Pakistan, has one of the most stunning backdrops in the world. Why not #PSL2023 matches here at #Gwadar." The PSL or the Pakistan Super League is a professional Twenty20 cricket league. AFWA found that this is not a real stadium. It's concept art designed by a Mumbai-based architecture firm. While there is a cricket stadium in Gwadar, it does not look anything like the viral photo. AFWA Probe We ran the photo through Google Lens, which led us to a website  for "Modern Green Structures and Architecture." Titled: "Prem Nath - Prem Nath & Associates," one of the pages on this website featured the same stadium. However, we noticed that in this photo, the stadium was not surrounded by cliffs. The photo of the stadium was accompanied by text that detailed the aim and ambition to build a sports stadium that meets "international standards and grandeur in scale, size and facilities." Subsequently, we searched for "Prem Nath & Associates". According to its website, it is a "Bombay-based complete design organisation established in 1967 having professional practice in architecture and interior designing and offering engineering services all over India for 50+ years." We also found the same design on the firm's website . The original model depicted a modern-looking cricket stadium with helipads and gardens besides. AFWA reached out to Prem Nath & Associates, who informed us via email that "this image of a stadium was designed by Ar. Prem Nath. The email added that the firm hadn't worked on any project in Pakistan and that this photo was "illegally shared" by certain Twitter users. This proved that the photo did not show the Gwadar cricket stadium. We then looked for photos of the stadium in question and came across a Facebook post shared by the International Cricket Council on January 31, 2021. We also found photos of the stadium in the Pakistani daily, Dawn . And judging by the photos, the location of the stadium is exactly where the viral photo depicts it. However, the stadium itself looked nothing like the one in the viral photo. We searched for news reports to check if any renovation work in this stadium was underway. We found none. Thus, it is clear that concept art for a cricket stadium was falsely shared as a real cricket stadium from Pakistan's Balochistan. Published By: Nandini Singh Published On: Feb 13, 2023 20:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Chinese spy balloons — here's how we deflated these false claims
content:
This video is a simulation made using a video game. It does not show actual US forces shooting down a surveillance balloon.
Since the first week of February, the US Air Force has shot down a Chinese "spy" balloon and three smaller objects in American airspace . The United States Department of Defense has alleged the incident was part of an extensive Chinese global surveillance program. China has, meanwhile, maintained that the "spy" balloon was a scientific vessel, and nothing more.
Social media has since seen a deluge of photos and videos of alleged "spy" balloons and unidentified flying objects in the US. One such video , seemingly shot from inside a moving vehicle, shows a disc-shaped object in the sky. Another video shows a fighter aircraft launching a missile at an object in the sky that promptly explodes.
AFWA found that the first video was old and unrelated to alleged spy balloons. And the second video was not real at all. So, let's look at how we came to these conclusions. UFO? NOT REALLYÂ
With the help of a reverse search, we found the first video (with the disc-like object in the sky) shared on Twitter and YouTube in 2020 . The caption to one such video read: "New Jersey UFO sighting". We noticed that while responding to tweets sharing this video, many people pointed out that the object seen in the clip was a blimp . New Jersey UFO sighting pic.twitter.com/NKLvXMaJdd — Paradigm Shift ☀️ (@ParadigmShiftss) September 20, 2020
New Jersey UFO sighting pic.twitter.com/NKLvXMaJdd — Paradigm Shift ☀️ (@ParadigmShiftss) September 20, 2020
We also found the same video in many news reports from 2020 . As per these reports , the flying object seen in the sky was a blimp belonging to Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company. A representative of Goodyear confirmed to Insider that the company flew a blimp in New York City and northern New Jersey to capture aerial footage of a National Football League match on September 14, 2020, at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey's East Rutherford.
Thus, it became clear that this video had nothing to do with the recent spate of alleged surveillance objects in American airspace. JET SET GOÂ
The video of the jets appeared animated and not real. A keyword search on YouTube led us to multiple simulation videos that depicted the shooting of the Chinese "spy" balloon by the US. A longer version of the now-viral video was uploaded to a gaming YouTube channel called "Growling Sidewinder" on February 5. Around 45 seconds into this video, we observed the viral clip.Â
The title of the video noted that the combat flight simulation game "Digital Combat Simulator" was used to make the video. The description of the video also listed the hardware and software used in the creation of this simulation.
This channel also featured many other simulations of aerial combat.Â
It is hence clear that while this video does show a Chinese "spy" balloon being shot, it's not real at all. Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Feb 13, 2023 21:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Don't get misled, you still can't drive a 15-year-old car in Delhi-NCR
content:
The ban on diesel cars older than ten years and petrol cars older than 15 is still very much in effect in the NCR.
If you live in the National Capital Region of India and own a ten-year-old diesel car, or a 15-year-old petrol car, a "government notification" being widely shared on social media must have caught your attention. It suggests that it's still not the end of the road for your car. You can still use it after paying a fee.Â
Don't get misled, this is not correct.
The message is going viral right from WhatsApp to Twitter and Facebook . Articles on Zee News , 24ExpressNews , and " Ghamasan " also seem to affirm this information.Â
These posts claim that the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has revoked  its order to ban ten-year-old diesel cars and 15-year-old petrol cars. All you have to do is pay Rs. 5,000 to renew your car's registration certificate.Â
An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that the ban on diesel cars older than ten years and petrol cars older than 15 is still very much in effect in the NCR. There is no change, no reprieve has been given. The government notification that's being shared pertains to a different issue regarding the sale and purchase of used cars.
NGT's old car rules are still in place
According to the Delhi Transport Department's website diesel cars older than ten years and petrol and CNG cars older than 15 years are still not allowed on road. In fact, this rule applies to government vehicles as well.Â
This ban was put in place by the National Green Tribunal, a statutory body, to curb pollution. As per news reports , it's estimated that the number of such vehicles in the capital exceeded 54 lakhs by February 2.Â
We spoke to Siyaram Verma, the assistant regional transport officer for the Gautam Budh Nagar district, who also confirmed that there had been no orders to lift the ban on these old vehicles. Verma said that the government notification being shared on social media is about a different matter, adding that it has no mention of ten- or 15-year-old vehicles.Â
The chairman of the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations of India Research & Academy Vinkesh Gulati, also tweeted that the ban was still effective, and that the media was also "getting entangled in misconstrued information". #Beware NGT has 𝐧𝐨𝐭 allowed >10yrs Diesel & >15 yrs Petrol to be renewed in NCR. The ban is still effective. #media is also getting entangled in misconstrued information! #Whatsapp #WhatsappForward pic.twitter.com/fLj5mIBfNi — Vinkesh Gulati 🇮🇳 (@VinkeshGulati) February 13, 2023 What is the viral notification all about?
#Beware NGT has 𝐧𝐨𝐭 allowed >10yrs Diesel & >15 yrs Petrol to be renewed in NCR. The ban is still effective. #media is also getting entangled in misconstrued information! #Whatsapp #WhatsappForward pic.twitter.com/fLj5mIBfNi — Vinkesh Gulati 🇮🇳 (@VinkeshGulati) February 13, 2023
The government notification going viral was issued in December last year. It elaborates rules for dealers or companies involved in the sale of second-hand vehicles. So far there was a grey area about the ownership of cars when they are in the process of sale through such dealers. This loophole was also being used to sell stolen cars. The rules were made to fix these loopholes.
According to the notification, such dealers will now be certified and will also be accountable for the cars till the old car is duly transferred in the name of the new owner.
The official Twitter account of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways also clarified about these rumours. A fake news is in circulation in Social Media claiming that MoRTH has issued a notification lifting ban imposed by Hon'ble NGT on vehicles (10 year old for diesel and 15 year old for petrol) in Delhi NCR.
— MORTHINDIA (@MORTHIndia) February 13, 2023
A fake news is in circulation in Social Media claiming that MoRTH has issued a notification lifting ban imposed by Hon'ble NGT on vehicles (10 year old for diesel and 15 year old for petrol) in Delhi NCR.
— MORTHINDIA (@MORTHIndia) February 13, 2023
So what's the deal with the Rs. 5,000 fees?
The NGT order to ban the aforementioned 10-15 year old cars does not apply to the whole country uniformly. There are many smaller cities where such old cars can still be re-registered and used. For example, in 33 districts in Uttar Pradesh, 20 districts in Bihar, and 26 districts in Maharashtra, vehicles older than ten to15 years are permitted for another 5 years .Â
Earlier, the re-registration fee was Rs. 600. Starting April 2022, however, this fee was hiked up to Rs. 5,000 . Â Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Feb 14, 2023 14:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Chinese 'spy' balloon wreckage? Nope, this video is at least 6 years old!
content:
This video has been on the internet since July 2017 and has nothing to do with the spy balloon incident.
A suspected Chinese "spy" balloon was shot down by the US airforce  in Early February. This was followed by at least three similar incidents . On social media, people have been sharing photos and videos of the balloon in question. Many of these, however, have nothing to do with the incident at all. One such is a video of the wreckage of what looks like an artificial satellite with a damaged balloon attached to it. This video shows the wreckage, nearly six to seven feet in length, inside a forest area. First video of the downed Chinese Spy Balloon!! #ChineseSpyBalloon #ChinaSpyBalloon #Balloon #spyballoon pic.twitter.com/hvCjOywj5w — James Bennett 🇺🇲 (@Sire_Bennett) February 4, 2023 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story People sharing the clip claimed that this was the first video of the alleged Chinese "spy" balloon that was shot down. Some of these clips also contained the text, "What our US apparently doesn't want us to see about what the Chinese Spy Balloons look like up close." Archived versions of these tweets can be seen here  and here . Thoughts / information on this video ? pic.twitter.com/kj9CZ0U3yp — Matt Baker (@slave_2_liberty) February 13, 2023 AFWA's investigation found that this video is almost six years old! AFWA Probe When we searched for news reports regarding the suspected Chinese "spy" balloon, we found a BBC article  quoting US government officials stating that the debris from the balloon was recovered from the Atlantic ocean. This raised doubts about the authenticity of the viral video.  As we reverse-searched keyframes from the viral clip, it led us to the same video shared by an Instagram account  on September 4, 2021. The post's caption read: "Balloon Satellite Falls 'from orbit', did not feature further details about this incident. This made it clear that the object had nothing to do with the recent Chinese "spy" balloon whatsoever.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by mystery_his_story (@mystery_his_story) Since the Instagram post did not mention any details about the video, we started surfing the replies to one of the tweets. There, we noticed several people  pointing out that the people in this video were speaking in Brazilian Portuguese and that the video was from Brazil. Subsequent refined searches led us to the same video uploaded to a YouTube channel on July 1, 2017. The description of this video read, "Balloon satellite crashes in Brazil." Additional searches led us to a website named Metabunk.org that investigates conspiracy theories. An article from July 1, 2017 , showed that a piece of paper glued to the back of the wreckage had the words "CONTACT PROJECT LOON RECOVERY TEAM" written on it. The article mentioned that a satellite had landed on May 15, 2017, but refrained from revealing its location. Subsequently, we searched for news reports in English and Portuguese from around that time to confirm this but found none. However, we came across multiple news reports that noted similar crashes of balloon "satellites" that were a part of project Loon. Similar incidents include ones that occurred in December 2017 in Keyna , in March 2017 in Brazil ,  in January 2017 in Panama , in April 2016 in Chile , in February 2016 in Sri Lanka , and in September 2015 in Los Angeles . What is Project Loon? In 2013, Google's parent organisation Alphabet announced Project Loon, planning to provide internet connectivity to rural and remote regions using high-altitude balloons. However, this project proved to be a failure and it was called off in January 2021. A detailed report on the project can be read here . So, while we were unable to pinpoint when and where the viral clip was shot, it is abundantly clear that it is not related to the "spy" balloon row.   Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Feb 14, 2023 19:26 IST

title: Fact Check: No aliens in Poland! This clip shows a rocket launch in South Korea
content:
This video is from December 30, 2022, and shows the test launch of a rocket in South Korea.
In the aftermath of three unidentified flying objects and a Chinese "spy" balloon being shot down by the US Air force in February, a similar incident was also allegedly witnessed in Poland. A video that's been widely shared online shows a trail of white and red smoke snaking behind a bright white light in the night sky.Â
"Now in Poland… the Air Force shot down a 'UFO'," read one such tweet . Archives of such posts can be seen here , here , and here . 🚨Now in Poland… the Air Force shot down a "UFO" 👽🛸🍿🥤😎🎬 pic.twitter.com/62KMTvY9ac — vegastar (@vegastarr) February 13, 2023
🚨Now in Poland… the Air Force shot down a "UFO" 👽🛸🍿🥤😎🎬 pic.twitter.com/62KMTvY9ac — vegastar (@vegastarr) February 13, 2023
AFWA found that the video shows the test launch of a rocket in South Korea.Â
We noticed that several people responded to the viral posts on Twitter and pointed out that the clip was from South Korea. Some also pointed out that in the video, people could be heard speaking in Korean.Â
A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to the same clip uploaded to a Korean YouTube channel on December 30, 2022. The title of the video in Korean read: "Unidentified aircraft found in the skies across the country."
A further search with relevant keywords led us to similar videos shared by several people from South Korea on December 30 and 31, 2022. While some claimed  the video showed a UFO, others said it was a South Korean missile test.  한국에 UFOê°€? 세계가 놀란 갑작스런 고체연료 로켓 발사 시험 VIDEO: South Korea's missile test causes UFO scare https://t.co/WeSNBJQZlU pic.twitter.com/qwO9ZtFvO3 — Ki Chul, Hwang (@conpaper) December 31, 2022 We also found similar videos and images in multiple media reports  from December 2022. As per these reports , these videos showed a solid-fueled rocket that was test-fired by South Korea on December 30, 2022. According to South Korea's Defense Ministry, the rocket launch was part of its efforts to build a space-based surveillance capability. The general public was not notified about the launch, and this reportedly triggered a UFO scare.  We compared the viral video with one of the photos from the launch shared by the Associated Press . The pattern of the white and red trail seen in the viral video is almost the same as that in the photo. A comparison of the two can be seen below. We were not able to independently verify the exact location of the viral video. According to media reports from South Korea , the rocket was spotted in the night sky in several areas including Seoul and parts of the Gangwon, Gyeonggi, and South Chungcheong provinces. Thus, it's clear that this video does not show a UFO being shot down in Poland. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Feb 15, 2023 14:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of 2022 Puerto Rico hurricane FALSELY shared as recent Cyclone Gabrielle in New Zealand
content:
This video shows Hurricane Fiona which struck Puerto Rico in September 2022.
At least four people have reportedly died  during the recent Cyclone Gabrielle in New Zealand. Though the cyclone has subsided now, it has left thousands of people displaced. According to a February 15 report by Deutsche Welle , the New Zealand police have been unable to contact over 1,400 people. The island country had to declare a state of emergency after the cyclone caused widespread flooding and landslides. Amid this, a video of a storm allegedly from a recent cyclone has been shared widely on social media. It shows strong winds almost uprooting a tree as debris flies around. The archived version of this post can be seen here . Malayalam news websites like Manorama Online and " TheFourthNews.in " used this video in their recent reports on Cyclone Gabrielle. AFWA found that the viral video is an old video and from Puerto Rico, not New Zealand. AFWA Probe We noticed that many people responded to the viral Twitter post saying that the video was not from New Zealand. A quick reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a tweet by Brett Adair, a meteorologist from Alabama, US, from September 19, 2022. He had shared several videos supposedly showing Hurricane Fiona in action. He stated that these videos were filmed west of Ponce in Puerto Rico. The viral video was part of this. Just west of Ponce, #PuertoRico in #Hurricane #Fiona - @NWSSanJuan @LiveStormsMedia @NHC_Atlantic pic.twitter.com/b8PRxJ2UXw — Brett Adair (@AlaStormTracker) September 18, 2022 Using this clue, we ran a keyword search and found a screenshot of this video in a Yahoo report from September 19, 2022. As per this report, it showed Hurricane Fiona wreaked havoc in Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic in September 2022. At least 25 people were killed in Puerto Rico because of the hurricane. It caused heavy rainfall, mudslides, floods, and large-scale power disruption. The Weather Channel and AccuWeather also used the viral video in their reports related to hurricane Fiona at the time. Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with the recent cyclone in New Zealand. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Feb 15, 2023 15:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Vertical fighter jet stunts at Aero India 2023? Nope, this Dubai clip shows a toy plane
content:
This video shows a radio-controlled miniature jet in Dubai. It has no links to Aero India 2023.
The 14th edition of Aero India 2023  i s currently taking place at the Yelahanka Air Force Station in Bengaluru. Ever since its inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on February 13, videos and photos of various aerial formations being showcased at the five-day biennial aerospace exhibition have dominated social media in India.Â
A video  allegedly shot at the event, shows an aircraft hovering  vertically, with its nose pointed towards the sky. The archived versions of such posts can be seen here  and here .
AFWA found that while similar manoeuvres  have been witnessed at Aero India 2023  this video is neither recent nor from India. It shows a radio-controlled aircraft in Dubai. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared  on February 9 on Twitter. The tweet stated that it showed a Russian pilot flying the Sukhoi SU-35 aircraft. This suggested that the viral video was shot before the India aero show began. Russian pilot at a flight demonstration. Aircraft type - Sukhoi SU-35 Maximum speed: 2,778 km/h Autonomy: 3,600 km Length: 22 m Weight: 18,400 kg Unit cost: 40,000,000$–65,000,000$ Builders: Sukhoi, KnAAPO pic.twitter.com/FbHR08u7hT — ALICIA 🍊🍊🍊 (@ALICIA56483057) February 9, 2023
Russian pilot at a flight demonstration. Aircraft type - Sukhoi SU-35 Maximum speed: 2,778 km/h Autonomy: 3,600 km Length: 22 m Weight: 18,400 kg Unit cost: 40,000,000$–65,000,000$ Builders: Sukhoi, KnAAPO pic.twitter.com/FbHR08u7hT — ALICIA 🍊🍊🍊 (@ALICIA56483057) February 9, 2023
Further searches led us to other social media posts  containing the same video  that also identified the aircraft  as a Russian SU-35 fighter jet. However, we noticed that a few people  had replied to these tweets pointing out that the aircraft in the video was a remote-controlled miniature and not the actual jet. This is definitely model aeroplane (dimensions by eye, rotational velocity). Accord to Wiki, mass of empty Su-35 is 19000kg = 186,4 kN and 2 motors with maximal thrust 86,3 kN (each). So mass > thrust (even without fuel) => ...
— BikeWander (@Bike_Wander) February 8, 2023 With the help of this clue, we searched for videos of remote-controlled miniatures of the jet and found a video  shared in May 2021 on a YouTube channel named "Supercar Blondie". The description of the video stated that it showed a radio-controlled fighter jet race held in a secluded area in Dubai. We noticed that the colour and design of one of these radio-controlled aircraft resembled the one in the viral video. Alexandra Mary Hirschi, known online as "Supercar Blondie", is a vlogger based in Dubai. In the video, Hirschi said that the miniature jet was a one-to-four-scale replica of a fighter plane. The owner of the jet, Mansour, added that it was a Sukhoi 30 model jet, fitted with canards while the other one was a Sukhoi 27. These RC aircraft cost about USD 30,000 and can go as fast as 500 kmph. A comparison between the model plane and the aircraft in the viral video can be seen below. While this YouTube video did not contain the viral clip, other radio-controlled jets could be seen flying with their nose pointed towards the sky. Additionally, the pilots seen in the video were from the "Sky Hub RC" — a radio-controlled fighter jet club  based in Dubai. advertisement The website mentioned that these radio-controlled races take place at Al Lisaili RC Flying Field in Dubai. We compared photos of this location available on Google Maps  with the viral video and found many similarities.  AFWA also spoke to Ludovic Bonnan, an RC pilot instructor and drone operator who is a member of the Sky Hub RC club. He said that the viral video was shot during the United Arab Emirates National Day celebrations at the Dubai RC Club on December 2. Subsequently, we found a video  of the UAE National Day 2022 celebration in which a man could be seen demonstrating a miniature jet at the same location. We noticed that his t-shirt contained the logo of Performance Aircraft Unlimited  or PAU, a Florida-based company that manufactures RC aeroplanes. This same t-shirt was also visible in the viral video. advertisement We also spoke to Mustafa, the owner of Gonzo Hobbies — a shop that sells these aircraft in UAE and GCC countries. He also confirmed to AFWA that the viral video shows a miniature SU-30 that his shop imported for a customer. It's noteworthy that Russian companies  are displaying their defence systems at Aero India 2023 . However, this video has nothing to do with the Indian aero exhibition. title: Fact Check: Video of high school student threatening teacher with gun is NOT from the US, it's from France
content:
The video is neither recent nor from the US. It is more than four years old and from Creteil, France.
A video of a teenager threatening his teacher with a gun in a classroom has shocked the internet. On social media, people claimed that the video was from the US and criticised President Joe Biden's government. On Twitter, one person shared the video  and wrote, "This is clearly Biden's America brought to you by alt-left extremist being elected into power." Another person tweeted , "I see so many videos of students disrespecting teachers and now a gun. The US is out of control. They behave like animals." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The archived versions of such claims can be seen here , here  and here . AFWA found that the video is more than four years old and from France, not the US. AFWA Probe A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to various news  reports from October 2018, which contained this video. As per the BBC , the video was initially distributed on Snapchat and was from a school in Créteil, a commune in the southeastern suburbs of Paris. The incident was filmed and uploaded to social media by one of the gun-wielding teen's classmates. According to a France 24 report , it was a fake gun. The teen admitted to pointing the imitation gun at the teacher but said it was meant "as a joke" and was unaware he was being filmed. He was reportedly angry that the teacher marked him down as absent when he had been merely late for class.  We then looked on YouTube and found the same video shared by The Sun, on October 22, 2018. As per the video's description, the teen faced prison time for the "joke" after the teacher in the clip reported the schoolboy for "violent threats with a weapon," which can earn the offender up to five years in prison. Thus, it's clear that the viral video is neither recent nor from the US. It is more than four years old and from Creteil, France. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Feb 17, 2023 17:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Apocalyptic video of dead fish is NOT from chemical spill after train crash in Ohio, US
content:
This video is from the coast of Laguna del Plata in Santa Fe, Argentina. Reportedly, these fish died as a result of the drop in the oxygen level in their natural habitat.
A train accident in the US, which has been compared to both, the Bhopal gas tragedy and the Chernobyl disaster, has been widely discussed on social media. On February 3, a train heading from Pennsylvania to Illinois derailed in the village of East Palestine in Ohio, releasing the hazardous material it was carrying into the air and the ground. Despite reassurances from government officials that the area's air and water quality remains safe, and there was no large-scale contamination, there have been reports  of residents allegedly experiencing nausea, headaches, and animals falling sick in the accident's aftermath. Many on social media have been raising concerns about the toxic chemical spill. Among such posts was a video  of thousands of dead fish that had washed up to a shore. People claimed that this video  was from Ohio and showed the consequences of the accident. The archived versions of such posts can be seen here , here and here . AFWA found that the video is from the coast of Laguna del Plata in Santa Fe, Argentina — not the US. AFWA Probe Using reverse image search, we found the same video uploaded to multiple YouTube channels  as early as January 22, 2023. This confirmed that the video predates the train derailment in Ohio. As per these channels, the video was from Laguna del Plata in Argentina's Santa Fe province. A further search with relevant keywords led us to multiple media reports  in Spanish that had used the same video and screenshots from it. According to these reports  as well, the video was from the coast of Laguna del Plata in Argentina. Per the reports , thousands of dead fish appeared on the shore of Laguna del Plata on January 21. Reportedly, the fish died because the oxygen level in the water dropped due to high temperatures and lack of rainfall. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Similar videos and images from Laguna del Plata were shared on Facebook by people from Santa Fe during the last week of January. Reportedly, the Ohio Department of Natural Resources  said that the chemical spill resulting from the derailment killed around 3,500 small fish across different streams in Ohio. It is, however, clear that the video in question is from Argentina, and it predates the Ohio incident. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Feb 17, 2023 21:01 IST

title: Fact Check: These square clouds were NOT seen in US skies after Chinese 'spy' balloon incident!
content:
This video has no links to the Chinese "spy" balloon and is at least five years old.
After Chinese "spy" balloons, weird clouds  have now allegedly been spotted in the US. A video  of a perfectly rectangular cloud allegedly observed in the US after the China "spy" balloon incident has been widely shared. Archives of such posts can be found here  and here .
AFWA found that the video of the mysterious clouds is not recent but from 2018.Â
A keyword search on Google about rectangular clouds led us to a news report from March 2018 about such sightings, sparking speculations about the US Air Force controlling the weather. The article carried a screengrab from the viral video. This meant that the viral video is not recent.Â
Around that time, this weather phenomenon  sparked speculations about the infamous High-Frequency Active Auroral Research Programme (HAARP) programme. Meteorologists, on the other hand, theorised that these clouds could have been formed by water vapour that came out of the engine of an aeroplane .Â
Interestingly, this wasn't the only square cloud spotted by people. We found a report  from around the same time carrying several photos of square clouds or "flying carpets", spotted in different parts of the UK and the US. This report too contained a screenshot from the viral video. The report noted that the cloud in the viral video was spotted above Tucson, a city in Arizona. Â
In 2014, NASA astronaut G Reid Wiseman tweeted a photo he reportedly took from the International Space Station, of square clouds running into volcanoes in Kamchatka, eastern Russia. Odd square cloud runs into Kamchatka's volcano field. pic.twitter.com/aNObWv3knR — Reid Wiseman (@astro_reid) June 12, 2014
Odd square cloud runs into Kamchatka's volcano field. pic.twitter.com/aNObWv3knR — Reid Wiseman (@astro_reid) June 12, 2014
AFWA showed the viral video to Dr. Abhilash S, an associate professor at Cochin University of Science and Technology, said that while such cloud formations are not very common, they occasionally occur because of reasons that could be natural or man-made, or sometimes even both.Â
"One possible reason can be air fronts, where two distinct air masses with contrasting temperature and density can cause lifting of air parcels and subsequent cloud formation. Another possibility would be large-standing atmospheric waves aligning the clouds in a straight line", he stated.Â
He added that Cloud Seeding experiments can also cause such weather phenomena. Cloud seeding is a type of weather modification that aims to change the amount or type of precipitation that falls from clouds by dispersing substances like silver iodide, potassium iodide, and dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) into the air using aircraft.Â
So, while we could not independently verify the location of this video, it is evident that it is at least five years older than the Chinese "spy" balloon incident.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Vani Mehrotra Published On: Feb 20, 2023 15:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Not extremists, Dhaka University admin removed Tagore statue from premises
content:
The statue was removed by the Dhaka University administration. A member of the students' union confirmed that no extremists were involved.
While barbed fences divide India and Bangladesh, veneration and love of Rabindra Nath Tagore unite both countries. The Nobel laureate is not only a cultural symbol for Bengalis but also a national icon for Indians and Bangladeshis, as his literary works were adopted as national anthems by both nations. Bangladesh's national anthem "Amar Shonar Bangla" was penned by Tagore.
But it would seem that Tagore's legacy in Bangladesh is under attack. A Twitter user shared two photos of a vandalised statue of Tagore, claiming that "extremists have defaced the sculpture of Rabindranath Tagore," at TSC, Dhaka University.Â
The first photo shows a statue of Tagore whose mouth is taped-up, holding a book with a large nail piercing through it. The second photo shows the dismantled head of the sculpture. The archived version of the tweet can be seen here.Â
AFWA's investigation found that the statue was removed by the administration of Dhaka University itself. THE CONTROVERSIAL STATUE
A group of students of Dhaka University's Faculty of Fine Arts designed and erected a sculpture of Tagore on February 14, in a symbolic protest against "censorship" and "stifling freedom of speech" in Bangladesh. This reportedly included this year's "Ekushey Book Fair" not allowing a stall for Adarsh Publications.Â
The statue, which was composed of thermocol (polystyrene), bamboo, and pages taken from old books, was installed next to the Raju Memorial Sculpture outside the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) in the university. The 19.5 feet tall statue's key features were a nail piercing through Tagore's collection of poems, "Gitanjali", and a tape shutting the mouth of the poet.Â
Reportedly, the statue was removed on February 16. Following this, the students put up a banner at the same place reading: "Rabindranath has disappeared!" Later, students recovered vandalised pieces of Tagore's statue, among which was the defaced and severed head seen in the viral photo.
A keyword search on Google led us to multiple media reports which contained these pictures. Speaking to New Age Bangladesh, Shimul Kumbhakar, the president of the university's unit of Bangladesh Students' Union said that they came to know from eyewitnesses that the sculpture of Rabindranath was removed by the university's proctorial team early on February 16 morning, adding, "But the proctor told us that he did not know anything about that."
The university administration, after an initial denial, conceded that the protesting sculpture was removed by them as it disrupted aesthetic beauty. A Daiji World report quoted university proctor AKM Golam Rabbani saying, "The university has a policy of placing sculptures on the campus. The sculpture (of Tagore) was placed without informing the university administration. Therefore, the administration removed it."Â
AFWA spoke to Kumbhakar, who confirmed that it was the university administration who had removed the sculpture. Kumbhkar verified that the viral photo of the vandalised Tagore statue was authentic and said that the proctor was responsible for removing the sculpture and that possibly during this process it had gotten damaged.
Kumbhkar also confirmed to us that no extremists were involved in the incident and there was no religious angle to it. Students later managed to find several pieces of the statute and attempted to build it again. Kumbhkar told AFWA that the statue has been placed again in the same place.
Thus, it is amply clear that the sculpture of Tagore at Dhaka University wasn't dismantled by extremists.
(Written by: Vikas Bhadauria) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Feb 20, 2023 20:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Photo of bleeding Afghani activist FALSELY shared as domestic violence victim in Pak
content:
This photo is neither recent nor from Pakistan. It shows Afghani activist Nargis Sadat, who was assaulted by members of the Taliban in Kabul in September 2021.
In Pakistan, violence against women and girls — including rape, murder, acid attacks, domestic violence, and forced and child marriage — is widespread, noted Human Rights Watch's World Report 2023 . A recent alleged gangrape  of a woman in Islamabad has enraged women's rights activists and has sparked furious protests across the country. Now, a photo of a bleeding woman is being shared widely on social media, with claims like, "Horrible state of women in Pakistan where a Husband in Lahore attacked her wife with a knife just because he did not like the food she cooked - he slit her cheek open." The archived version of the tweet can be found here . AFWA found that the woman in the picture is an Afghani women's rights activist who was assaulted by Taliban members during a protest march. AFWA Probe Using a reverse image search, we found the photo of the woman with the head injury in several media reports. A report on India.com  said the woman was Nargis Saddat, an Afghani women's rights activist and a participant in a protest that took place in Kabul on September 4, 2021. The Taliban prevented the demonstrators from marching towards the presidential palace by resorting to firing shots into the air and beating protestors with rifle butts. We also came across a report by CBS News  that contained the same photo. Its caption read: "An image from a video sent to CBS News by Afghan women's rights activist Nargis Sadat shows her bleeding from her head after Taliban members attacked her during a protest in Kabul in September 2021." The report noted that Hoda Khamosh, who organised the protests in the capital, said that it was the Taliban's announcement of an all-male interim cabinet that sparked the protests. She also said the Taliban beat one of her colleagues, Nargis Sadat, during one of the demonstrations. The reverse search also led us to a video of Sadat shot after the protest from which the viral image was extracted. Steve Hanke, a professor of applied economics at the Johns Hopkins University in the US tweeted  on September 5, 2021. In the tweet, he wrote: "Narges Sadat was brutally beaten by the Taliban in Kabul after Saturday's women's rights protest was broken up by tear gas & gunfire. Sadat yelled out 'We've given a lot of blood. But we're not afraid' as she retreated from the march." Thus, it's clear that the viral image is neither recent nor from Pakistan. (Written by Vikas Bhadauria) ALSO READ | Fact Check: Not extremists, Dhaka University admin removed Tagore statue from premises Published By: Rajeev Singh Published On: Feb 20, 2023 22:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of girl ziplining across river to attend school is NOT from India
content:
This video is not from India but from Colombia. It was recorded in the village of Puerto Mosquito in June 2022.
We've all probably heard tales from our grandparents about how in the days of yore, they had to scale mountains and cross rivers to go to school. Whether or not those stories were exaggerations, a video that is now viral appears to demonstrate that this might be the case for some even today. Brave Girls risk their lives for Education 😮👇 I request to Modiji Do Sumthing ...If our Girl read like this, how will they move forward? #thursdaymorning #MadgaonExpress #NoraFatehi #PetrolDieselPrice #TejRan #NikkiYadav #SidNaaz pic.twitter.com/jBVYgmo3bT — Ayesha (@Ayesha86627087) February 16, 2023
Brave Girls risk their lives for Education 😮👇 I request to Modiji Do Sumthing ...If our Girl read like this, how will they move forward? #thursdaymorning #MadgaonExpress #NoraFatehi #PetrolDieselPrice #TejRan #NikkiYadav #SidNaaz pic.twitter.com/jBVYgmo3bT — Ayesha (@Ayesha86627087) February 16, 2023
In the video , a girl in a school uniform crosses a turbulent stream using a makeshift zipline. Those sharing the video appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to look into the matter and help make things easier for the girl and others like her.Â
The video was shared on Facebook as well. The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found that the video is not from India at all — it's from a village in Colombia in South America.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Times of India  report from November 2022. The report, however, did not mention where the video was shot. In the ToI report, however, we found a tweet that shared the clip along with the Spanish text: "He who does not study is because he does not want to." Los Uribistas dicen que el que no estudia es porque no quiere Y esta es la realidad: pic.twitter.com/3zKVvgTjA2 — Memes Universidad Nacional (@nacional_memes) November 1, 2022 When we searched for Spanish keywords related to the video, came across another tweet  in Spanish that was shared on June 15, 2022, with the "Magdalena" hashtag in its caption. Magdalena is a department in Colombia located in the northern part of the country. It also mentioned that the video was shot in the village of Puerto Mosquito near the city of Santa Marta, where students needed to cross the Gaira River using makeshift ziplines to attend school. It also mentioned that the video was shot in the village of Puerto Mosquito near the city of Santa Marta, where students needed to cross the Gaira River using makeshift ziplines to attend school. A subsequent search with keywords in Spanish led us to multiple news reports from Colombia that reported on this video. One such article  published on June 15, 2022, also noted that the video was captured in the village of Puerto Mosquito, northeast of the city of Santa Marta. Reportedly , this dangerous practice became a routine affair for a group of students from the Narakajmanta community. The report also quoted the education secretary of Santa Marta, Antonio Peralta, who reacted to this video and stated, "It is a delicate situation and we assume it responsibly, and we are going to see how lines of action are drawn up for them. Actions must be taken on time." Another news report  quoted a local leader who said that this had been their situation since 2008 and several people had even lost their lives trying to cross the river similarly. Thus, it is more than clear that a video from Colombia was falsely shared as Indian. title: Fact Check: This video doesn't show deep cracks caused by recent tremors in Turkey and Syria
content:
This video is from the Pinglu region in China and has nothing to do with the devastating quakes in Turkey and Syria.
Just two weeks after a series of quakes left thousands dead and millions homeless in Turkey and Syria, a 6.4-magnitude tremor struck the border region of the two countries on February 20. But did these deadly quakes leave a long crack on Earth's surface?Â
Several people on social media are now sharing aerial footage  of 300 km-long fissure that they claimed  appeared in the aftermath of the recent quakes in the Turkey-Syria region. Turkey Syria Earthquake Caused 300 km Long Crack in Earth's Crust #turkeyearthquake2023 #earthquake #TurkeySyriaEarthquake2023 Turkey-Syria pic.twitter.com/55PIDDmOax — Ankita Jain (@Ankita20200) February 20, 2023
Turkey Syria Earthquake Caused 300 km Long Crack in Earth's Crust #turkeyearthquake2023 #earthquake #TurkeySyriaEarthquake2023 Turkey-Syria pic.twitter.com/55PIDDmOax — Ankita Jain (@Ankita20200) February 20, 2023
AFWA found that the video in question is from China and is not related to the recent quakes in Turkey and Syria. AFWA PROBEÂ
As per media reports , the magnitude 7.8 and 7.5 earthquakes that hit Turkey and Syria on February 6 created two ruptures on land. According to researchers  from the UK's Centre for the Observation and Modelling of Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Tectonics (COMET), the longest of the two fissures stretches 300 kilometres northeast from the Mediterranean Sea's northeastern tip. However, is the viral video related to the recent earthquakes? A reverse search of the video led us to a longer version of the same clip shared by an Instagram account on December 6, 2021. This confirmed the video is old and not related to the recent tremors in Turkey and Syria.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by DJ Pashur (@djpashur) The video was also shared by several Chinese YouTube channels  in 2022. According to these channels, it was from Pinglu county in the southern Shanxi province of China. Using relevant keywords in the Chinese language, we searched and found satellite images of the viral video's location and its coordinates  uploaded by people on Zhihu, a Quora-like question-and-answer website based in China. Using the coordinates, we located the fissure on Google Maps . A comparison of the longer version of the viral video with the Google Earth view of the area helped us find multiple similarities between the two. This confirmed the video is indeed from Pinglu County. The oldest satellite view of the location available on Google Earth is from 1985. The crack can be spotted at the same position even in the earliest version. According to various travel blogs , the fissure is named after Zhou Cang, a fictional character in the 14th-century Chinese historical novel "Romance of the Three Kingdoms".  Also, as per these sites , this fissure is around 10 km long. We also found different videos  of the same fissure  on Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok.  It is hence clear that the video in question is old and has nothing to do with the quakes in Turkey or Syria. Published By: Rajeev Singh Published On: Feb 21, 2023 21:02 IST

title: Fact Check: This 'not-so-new' technology will not replace CT scans and x-rays, it was made using them
content:
This video shows an Anatomage Table that uses medical imaging tests to show a 3-D model of cadavers for virtual dissection.
Is there a new technology that has rendered x-rays and CT scans obsolete? If social media is to be believed, this table-like device can show live 3D scans of your body — Just like that!Â
This table, according to social media posts, not only shows clear three-dimensional images of your internal organs but also allows you to zoom in and rotate the images to get a better view. A modern medical miracle, it would seem.Â
Sharing a video of this device , a person tweeted: "C.T Scan, MRI, X'RAYS  will go off. New digital technology has arrived. Now doctors can see your body live on screen." Archives of these posts can be found here and here .Â
AFWA found that this video shows a virtual dissection table used to study anatomy, and it uses medical imaging tests like the ones mentioned above to create 3-D models.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video on Yandex led us to a video shared in March 2018 on the YouTube channel of NJ.com. The video shows a virtual dissection table being used at a school in New Jersey for human anatomy classes. The device, per the video, was called the Anatomage table and it looked very similar to the one in the viral clip. Using relevant keywords, we found another video demonstration of the Anatomage table on the YouTube channel of the Campbell College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences. In this video, the demonstrator said that the device used high-definition thin-slice CT imaging of real human cadavers that were fixed in a specialised gel solution to give these results. The table also allowed users to import medical images, like CT scans, for better viewing. A comparison between the table seen in the viral video and the Anatomage table can be seen below. Anatomage is a medical company based in San Jose, California, that has been developing equipment for the education, medical and dental industries since 2004. In a 2020 interview , Kris Thomson, the director of applications at Anatomage, said that the Anatomage table was designed to help with anatomy education and to review CT and MRI scans in the hospitals in a more interactive manner. Jason Malley, Senior Manager of Strategic Partnerships at Anatomage, told AFWA that this table cannot replace x-rays or CT/MRI scans because it uses these imaging technologies itself. He said that the specimens seen in this device were frozen and sliced, and MRI, CT and other imaging tools were used to photograph each slice. This helps create a 3-D model. advertisement Malley also said that "not anyone can just be scanned using this table." He said the table had four human specimens, aside from animal specimens. Malley said that over 3,000 tables had been sold around the world, primarily for training in anatomy and physiology. Thus, it's clear that this table is neither a "new" technology nor can it replace medical imaging tests like x-rays, MRI scans and CT scans.     (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Feb 22, 2023 21:05 IST

title: Fact Check: No acid rain in Ohio after train derailment, these photos are old and unrelated!
content:
These images are old. While the first one shows fake blisters, the second one shows rashes caused by hookworm.
Has the US state of Ohio witnessed incidents of people getting "burnt" because of acid rains following the derailment of a train carrying toxic chemicals? This is what some people on social media  have alleged. Two photos allegedly showing people who received "third-degree burns" because of acid rains following the East Palestine derailment have been shared widely online.
The images show a person's arm and foot covered in what looks like severe burns. A Twitter user  shared these images and wrote, "If you are in the states of Ohio or Pennsylvania, please do not go outside while it's raining! We're getting reports of third-degree burns from what is suspected to be from acid rain. STAY INDOORS!". The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA found that the viral photos are neither recent nor do they have any connection with acid rain. AFWA PROBEÂ
A reverse search of the first image led us to a Reddit post  from May 2, 2012, titled, "Volunteered to be a victim for training today, they did a decent job...[Fake blisters]." The person who shared the photo stated in the comments that the burn was actually made of rubber and pasted to his arm.  Â
They also said that they served in the Air Force, and such exercises involving fake injuries were often conducted to train the emergency response teams. They also shared a photo  of a colleague who had fake rubber blisters on their face.  On reverse searching the second photo, we found it in a July 2018 Fox News report  about intestinal parasites known as hookworms. The was attributed to Kelli Mulhollen Dumas a dentist from Memphis in Tennessee, US, who had shared this photo  along with a few others on July 21, 2018.Â
On reverse searching the second photo, we found it in a July 2018 Fox News report  about intestinal parasites known as hookworms. The was attributed to Kelli Mulhollen Dumas a dentist from Memphis in Tennessee, US, who had shared this photo  along with a few others on July 21, 2018.Â
She stated in her post that the image showed the foot of a person named Michael who was infected with hookworm. CAN ACID RAIN CAUSE BURNS?Â
Acid rain is caused by air pollution. Some gases (especially nitrogen oxides and sulphur dioxide) react with the tiny droplets of water in clouds to form sulphuric and nitric acids. The rain from these clouds is known as "acid rain".Â
However, acid rain  is never acidic enough to burn the skin. Even the strongest recorded acid rain was only about as acidic as lemon juice or vinegar. However, acid rain can cause  respiratory problems and heart diseases. HAS THERE BEEN ACID RAIN IN OHIO?Â
A train derailed in East Palestine, Ohio, on February 3, releasing toxic chemicals into the air. Since then, many residents have reported  headaches, nausea, burning eyes and sore throats. However, there have been no reports of acid rain  in the area so far.  Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Feb 23, 2023 17:10 IST

title: Fact Check: None of these viral videos is from the Feb 23 Tajikistan earthquake
content:
This video is from the devastating earthquake that hit Turkey on February 6. The video shows volunteers from Tajikistan participating in rescue work.
A series of earthquakes hit a remote region of Tajikistan, near its border with China, on February 23. The strongest of these temblors measured at magnitude 6.8.Â
Though no casualties or damage had been reported at the time of writing this story, people on social media were swift in sharing videos of alleged rescue operations and damaged buildings in the country. These, however, were all from other parts of the world.
In this article, we will debunk four such videos. TAJIKS TO THE RESCUE Get well soon Tajikistan 🇹🇯 God help you #Tacikistan #earthquake pic.twitter.com/3QIO9qNziM — KASİDE (@zakkumec) February 23, 2023

One such video featured a group of men rescuing a child from the debris of a collapsed building. A few of these men wore green jackets with "Tajikistan" written on the back.Â
