title: Fact Check: Nehru was not a real 'citizen' of London, long-debunked claim goes viral again!
content:
The Citizen of London is a ceremonial title and doesn't bestow any citizenship rights. Nehru did sign a declaration to be true to the Queen of England, but it was symbolic.
The first Prime Minister of independent India, Jawaharlal Nehru, has over the years become the subject of unfathomable gossip, fabricated history, and conspiracy theories. These claims are debunked time and again. And yet, they keep resurfacing to haunt our sensibilities.
One such rumour about Nehru being a citizen of London, the city, has found a new life again on social media. A 38-second long, black and white video has been widely shared on social media, which shows a man standing up to Nehru and saying, "It is my privilege as Chamberlain of this city to offer you both the right hand of fellowship and greet you, Mr. Nehru, as a citizen of London."
A social media user, while sharing the clip, tweeted in Hindi that Nehru accepted the citizenship of London and pledged his loyalty to the then Queen of England. The archived version of the tweet can be found here .
It's noteworthy that this very video had also gone viral with similar allegations in September last year, and it was debunked by many fact-checking organisations at the time.
AFWA found that Nehru was conferred with the honour of "Freedom of the City of London". It is a symbolic privilege and has no bearing on the citizenship of the honoured person.
We performed a keyword search for the video on the internet, which led to us a video uploaded on the youtube channel of " British Plathe ",  a U.K. newsreel archive company.
The video's title read" "London Honours Two Great Premiers (1956)". Its description noted, "Two great Prime Ministers, Mr Nehru of India and Mr Holland of New Zealand, received the freedom of the City of London at the Guildhall." It further said that Nehru was accompanied by his daughter Mrs. Indira Gandhi.Â
Keyword searches led us to the stock image website Alamy. It included archived image of Nehru receiving the honour. The image was accompanied by a brief description that reads, "Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the Indian Prime Minister, inspecting a guard of honour furnished by the 290 Field Regiment, RA, City of London TA, on his arrival at Guildhall to receive the Freedom of the City of London."Â
A report by the BBC noted that the ceremony took place at the Guildhall in the British capital on July 3, 1956. The report further outlined that the ceremony was witnessed by the British Prime Minister, Anthony Eden, and both the dignitaries took Freeman's oath to be true to the Queen and keep peace in the City.
Citizens are to read 'The Declaration of a Freeman'
The ceremony requires the individuals to read " The Declaration of a Freeman ".Â
The declaration, according to the website of the City of London, goes, "I do solemnly swear that I will be good and true to our Sovereign Lady Queen Elizabeth the Second; that I will be obedient to the Mayor of this City; that I will maintain the Franchises and Customs thereof, and will keep this City harmless, in that which in me is; that I will also keep the Queen's Peace in my own person; that I will know no Gatherings nor Conspiracies made against the Queen's Peace, but I will warn the Mayor thereof, or hinder it to my power; and that all these points and articles I will well and truly keep, according to the Laws and Customs of this City, to my power."
What is the 'Freedom of the City of London'?
The website of the City of London describes the honour as one of the oldest surviving traditional ceremonies still in existence today. It suggests that the honour was first presented in 1237.
It chronicles, "The medieval term 'freeman' meant someone who was not the property of a feudal lord but enjoyed privileges such as the right to earn money and own land. Town dwellers who were protected by the charter of their town or city were often free - hence the term 'freedom' of the City."
In the middle ages, the bedrock of the English economy was founded on the wool and animal trade. The honour served as an economically valuable privilege. It granted the freemen the right to herd sheep or any other animals over London Bridge to the Smithfield meat market, without having to pay the tolls on the animals brought into the city for sale.
Other rights and privileges included the right to vote in parliamentary elections, civic elections, and certain other legal immunities from being tried and imprisoned.
However, according to Ancestry , an American genealogy company, most of these privileges have become defunct for practical reasons. The Freedom of the City, the highest honour of the City of London Corporation, is granted only by a special resolution of the Court of Common Council to distinguish personalities.Â
Until 1996, Freedom of the City was only granted to British or Commonwealth citizens of good character over the age of 21. Recently, in 2019, the regional head of the State Bank of India's UK operations, Sanjiv Chadha, received the Freedom of the City of London.
Thus, the Citizen of London is a ceremonial title and doesn't bestow any citizenship rights. However, Nehru did sign the declaration to be true to the Queen, but it was very symbolic and didn't come with any real obligations to do so.
(Written by Vikas Bhadauria) Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Feb 24, 2023 20:03 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 video of Kamal Nath saying Congress needs '90% Muslim votes' viral as recent
content:
This video was circulated ahead of the Madhya Pradesh assembly elections in November 2018. It is not recent.
Madhya Pradesh Congress president Kamal Nath on February 13 met the controversial self-styled godman Dhirendra Shastri at Bageshwar Dham in the Chhatarpur district. Reportedly, the Congress leader prayed at the temple for the party's victory in the upcoming assembly elections.
On February 24, Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Prashant Patel Umrao tweeted a video of Nath purportedly saying that his party will be doomed if Muslims didn't vote for the party. Sharing the video, Umrao claimed that the statement was made by Nath after his visit to Bageshwar Dham.
Criticising Nath for supposed hypocrisy, Umrao wrote: "Kamal Nath has repeatedly exposed his chameleon-like nature. After making a show of praying at Shri Bageshwar Dham, his entire focus is now on Muslim votes." The archived version of the post can be seen here .
AFWA found that the video in question is more than four years old.
With the help of relevant keywords, we found the same video shared by multiple media organisations in November 2018. A longer version of the same video was uploaded to the YouTube channel of NDTV  on November 21, 2018. As per this report, the clip was released by the BJP a few weeks ahead of the MP assembly elections that took place on November 28, 2018. Several other media organisations including India Today  and ABP  carried the video at that time. In the video, Nath could be heard asking a group of people to study the polling percentage in Muslim-majority booths in previous elections in Madhya Pradesh and find out why all Muslims didn't come out to cast their votes.
In the video, Nath could be heard asking a group of people to study the polling percentage in Muslim-majority booths in previous elections in Madhya Pradesh and find out why all Muslims didn't come out to cast their votes.
"If at some booths the polling percentage is 60 per cent, we need to find out why there was a dip in voting… We need, not 80 per cent, but 90 per cent of Muslims to come out and vote... If 90 per cent Muslims don't vote for us, we could suffer a huge loss," Nath could be heard saying in the video.
As per news reports from that time, after the video went viral, the BJP accused Nath of seeking votes on religious grounds. The saffron party also urged the Election Commission to take action against Nath and the party. The Congress, on the other hand, asked what was wrong with the video and called the BJP's allegations a conspiracy to divide voters into communal lines.
We were not able to independently verify the authenticity of the viral video. It is, however, clear that the video is from 2018 and not recent as claimed by Umrao. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Feb 26, 2023 13:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Mysterious fireball landed before Turkey quakes? Nope, it's just an asteroid spotted over Europe
content:
This video shows an asteroid that lit up the skies over Western Europe on February 13.
Did a mysterious object that fell from the sky cause the devastating February earthquakes in Turkey? This is a conspiracy theory that's now being discussed on social media, alongside a video of an illuminated object falling from the sky . Allegedly, this video was recorded in the Hatay province of Turkey.
One Twitter user shared the viral video and wrote, "The mysterious fireball that fell just before the earthquake in Turkey". The archived version of this tweet  can be seen here .
Some also claimed that this video had something to do with the High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program (HAARP), a former US Military program. They claimed that the earthquake in Turkey was caused by HAARP.
AFWA found that this video shows an asteroid that was spotted in the skies over Western Europe on February 13.Â
Upon reverse searching keyframes from the viral video, we found that it was shared on the YouTube channel of USA Today on February 14. As per the description given there, it showed an asteroid that was spotted across the skies over Europe. Who shot this video? We noticed that USA Today has credited this video to a person with the username "@tymlaly76700". We also found that many others on social media  had also attributed the video to the same person on Twitter. We looked into the Twitter account of @tymlaly76700 and found that it belongs to a person called Kevin who claims to live in Le Havre, France. Kevin shared this video on Twitter  on February 13. Replying to a question, he said that he shot the video "by chance" while trying to show a shooting star to children. What is HAARP? High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program ( HAARP ) is a former US military program that used high-power, high-frequency transmitters to study the properties of the ionosphere. The Ionosphere is the boundary between the Earth's atmosphere and the vacuum of space. In 2015, HAARP's operation was transferred from the US Air Force to the University of Alaska Fairbanks. According to the official website of HAARP , it cannot control or manipulate the weather. advertisement We also found a roundup report for journalists published on the British website Science Media Center . In this report, multiple experts denied the possibility of the Turkey-Syria earthquakes being caused by HAARP. To sum it up, a totally unrelated video is being falsely shared as a mysterious fireball that fell on the Earth just before the devastating quakes in Turkey. title: Fact Check: NOT communal violence! This video doesn't show Muslim man attacking Hindu priest in Rajasthan
content:

title: Disturbing video of a Pak father cruelly beating his young son given false communal spin
content:
This video shows a father thrashing his son in Pakistan, who was arrested for the deed in 2022.
A shocking video making the rounds on social media features a man mercilessly thrashing and strangling a child in front of two other children. People who shared this video  alleged that the man was Muslim and assaulted the child of a Hindu neighbour, asking him to sing praises of "Allah".Â
(Content warning: graphic violence)
Many tagged  the Home Minister of India in their tweets, demanding strict action against the man. Archives of such posts can be found here  and here .Â
AFWA found that this incident is from Pakistan, and shows a man beating his son.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a tweet  by Irum Azeem Farooque, a former member of the Provincial Assembly of Pakistan. The tweet from July 2022 contained a screengrab from the viral video and stated that it showed a man from Orangi, Karachi. I can't post the vdo Bec of graphic post not allowed anymore on Twitter,this man from #Orangi #Karachi needs to be in jail and the kids to a safer place ASAP Plz tag to those who can be of any help to to locate the whereabouts of this man .I can share the vdo if required pic.twitter.com/lEtCudtRqR — Irum Azeem Farooque (@Irumf) July 8, 2022
I can't post the vdo Bec of graphic post not allowed anymore on Twitter,this man from #Orangi #Karachi needs to be in jail and the kids to a safer place ASAP Plz tag to those who can be of any help to to locate the whereabouts of this man .I can share the vdo if required pic.twitter.com/lEtCudtRqR — Irum Azeem Farooque (@Irumf) July 8, 2022
Using this clue, we ran a keyword search that led us to a report  by 24 News HD, a news website based in Lahore. The report from July 6, 2022, was about a father who thrashed his child for disturbing him while he was sleeping. The report also carried a screengrab from the viral video.
Further, we found another report  that stated that Ismail, a father of three, tortured his eight-year-old son in the Pakistan Bazaar area of Karachi. The man's wife Jamila said that he had physically abused her and their three children for 11 years. The man was reportedly  arrested by Orangi Town Police after the video of child abuse went viral. We searched the Karachi Police's Twitter account for information and found a tweet from July 6, 2022, about the arrest of Ismail Ould Ibrahim. It contained a photo of two police officers and Ismail with his face blurred out. Geo TV also reported  the incident stating that the name of the minor victim was Asad. Thus, it is more than clear that a video of a father thrashing his minor son in Pakistan was shared with a misleading communal spin. title: Fact Check: This video does not show Saudi Arabia's first snowfall in the last 100 years
content:
This video dates back to February 2021 and was recorded in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Per reports, Saudi Arabia witnessed the first snow in a hundred years in 2013.
What is the first thing that comes to mind when you think about Saudi Arabia? It's probably a two-way tie between deserts and swanky skyscrapers. Regardless, it's never snowfall. After all, it's a hot dry land. But if social media is to be believed, we might have to change these preconceived notions about the Arabian Peninsula nation. Many tweeted a video that purportedly shows camels resting during what looks like heavy snowfall and blizzards. They claimed that the video captured Saudi Arabia's first snowfall in a hundred years.  Meanwhile, in Saudi Arabia…. Snowfall for the first time in 100years. ❄️🐪❄️ pic.twitter.com/JgpLCueMb4 — strawberrygirl (@Strawberygirli) February 25, 2023 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story One such tweet  read: "Saudi Arabia: snow falls for the first time in almost 100 years! Haarp help for New World order." HAARP or High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program is a former US Military program that has been the subject of various conspiracy theories. An archived version of this video can be seen here . AFWA's investigation found that the video is from 2021, and snowfall in some parts of Saudi Arabia is not a rare phenomenon — rather. It's a regular one. AFWA PROBE  Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across a video  featuring the same clip of camels sitting in a snowy field around the one-minute mark. The video, however, was uploaded to YouTube on February 19, 2021, making it evident that it was not recent. The Russian caption of this video roughly translates to, "Wonder of nature in the desert 2021! Snowfall in Saudi Arabia Testament and predictions of Isaiah." Subsequently, a search with relevant keywords alongside the reverse search of the screengrab led us to a Khaleej Times report . Published on February 18, 2021, this report featured the same video and mentioned that the video was from Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Per this report, the locals of the adjoining mountain region of Tabuk experienced heavy snowfalls and blizzards in the early morning of February 18, 2021.  This video was first shared by Bandar Al-hawas , a nature photographer and weather observer, who tagged the location as the Al-Zahr mountains in northwest Saudi Arabia. Does Saudi Arabia experience snowfalls? While the Arabian Desert lies mostly in Saudi Arabia and covers most of the country, snowfall is not an uncommon phenomenon in this part of the world, at least in the last decade. As per a Mirror report  from December 2013, Saudi Arabia witnessed its first ever snow in a hundred years. Since then, snowfall during the winter in the Tubuk region has been a somewhat regular affair. The same happened in 2018 , 2019 , 2020  and 2022 . What is HAARP? HAARP  or the High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program was associated with the United States military. It uses high-power, high-frequency transmitters to study the ionosphere, an ionised layer of the Earth's upper atmosphere. After multiple conspiracy theories were flagged against HAARP alleging that the program is designed to control the weather, this program was decided to be shut down by the U.S. Airforce . Ownership of the facility was transferred to the University of Alaska Fairbanks  in 2015. Thus, it is safe to conclude that a two-year-old video from Saudi Arabia was falsely shared as the first snowfall in the country in a hundred years. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Feb 27, 2023 21:34 IST

title: Fact Check: The Russia-Ukraine war is NOT a hoax and these photos certainly DON'T prove anything
content:
The first photo shows a residential building in Ukraine that was struck by a Russian missile in February 2022. The second image is a photo of the same building after its renovation.
More than a year of warfare, the deaths of over 8,000 civilians, and the displacement of hundreds of thousands later, the conspiracy theory that the Russian invasion of Ukraine is a hoax, a false flag, continues to find takers. Despite extensive media documentation, first-person social media accounts, and intelligence reports, conspiracy theorists highlight innocuous details and present them as proof of a grand coverup.  A recent example of such "evidence" is a collage of two photos of the same skyscraper — one in ruins, and the other, completely intact. While this is similar to many such "before and after" war photos, the twist here is that the intact building is allegedly from February 2023 and the bombed one is from February 2022. This, supposedly, is proof that the war is "fake". ALSO READ | Fact Check: NOT communal violence! This video doesn't show Muslim man attacking Hindu priest in Rajasthan Of the many proponents of this idea was also Stew Peters , an American far-right media personality and conspiracy theorist. The archived versions of such posts can be seen here , here  and here . AFWA found that the highrise structure seen in the photographs was indeed hit by a Russian missile in February 2022. However, it was later restored. In fact, the collage was originally shared by the government of Ukraine. ALSO READ | Fact Check: This video does not show Saudi Arabia's first snowfall in the last 100 years THE DESTROYED TOWER With the help of a reverse search, we found the first image carried by several media organisations in 2022. Images and videos of the same building captured from different angles were also published in news reports. According to Reuters , this was a residential building near the Zhuliany Airport in Ukrainian capital Kyiv that was hit by a missile on February 26, 2022, the third day of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.  Photos and videos of emergency services at the scene, rescuing people from inside the building, have also been shared in various media reports.  The destroyed skyscraper was also recorded in a database maintained by the Netherlands-based investigative journalism group, Bellingcat . The database is a collection of incidents that have resulted in potential civilian harm since day one of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story THE 'AFTER' PHOTO A reverse search of the viral collage led us to the official Facebook page of the Ukrainian government which had incidentally shared the same set of photos on February 21 this year. It claimed to show the "before and after" images of the tower following its restoration. The post said, "In February 2022, the Russian missile hit a residential building on Lobanovskyi Avenue in Kyiv, a heartbreaking photo of which horrified the whole world and showed Russia's true intentions." ALSO READ | Fact Check: Mysterious fireball landed before Turkey quakes? Nope, it's just an asteroid spotted over Europe It added, "Almost one year later, the building is renovated. The damage of the house is no longer visible, but its scar is forever in our hearts. Let each new reconstruction heal our wounds and become a symbol of our unbreakable future." The Mayor of Kyiv, Vitali Klitschko shared on Facebook a video of him visiting the same building in December 2022. In it, he could be seen observing the restoration work.   A group of green buildings adjacent to the highrise can be seen behind Klitschko in one of the frames in this video. We found the same location on Google Street View, where all the buildings can be seen. A comparison between the Google Street View photo and the frame from the Klitschko video can be seen below.    It is hence clear that the building in question was actually destroyed by Russian forces and has since been restored. Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Mar 1, 2023 11:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Zelenskyy ask young Americans to go to war against Russia? Viral video clipped out of context
content:
This clip was clipped out of context. Zelenskyy was referring to the consequences of Ukraine losing the war.
A year of deaths and destruction has passed since Russia invaded Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Shortly before the one-year anniversary of the war, US President Joe Biden visited Kyiv. Now, a video of the Ukraine President, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , has been shared widely on social media with some shocking allegations. Listen to this POS…😤 Zelinsky: "Ukraine needs fresh young Americans to help fight on the ground war. The US will have to send their Son's & Daughter's... to WAR...and they will be DYING." pic.twitter.com/QEHRSF38di — Algernon (@rudeger11) February 28, 2023
Listen to this POS…😤 Zelinsky: "Ukraine needs fresh young Americans to help fight on the ground war. The US will have to send their Son's & Daughter's... to WAR...and they will be DYING." pic.twitter.com/QEHRSF38di — Algernon (@rudeger11) February 28, 2023
Those sharing the video said that Zelenskyy sought young Americans to help fight on the ground war. The short clip featured Zelenskyy speaking and the audio was that of a translator. The audio translation said: "The US will have to send their sons and daughters exactly the same way as we are sending our sons and daughters to war, and they will have to fight. Because it's NATO that we are talking about, and they will be dying. God forbid because it's a horrible thing." Â
The archived version of such a post can be seen here .Â
AFWA's investigation found that the viral part of Zelensky's speech was clipped out of context. He was referring to the consequences of Ukraine losing the war.Â
Upon searching online for the relevant quote, we found a report by the Russian state-controlled international news network RT from February 25, 2023. The headline read, "Zelensky threatens unsupportive Americans."
Per this report, Zelenskyy allegedly threatened Americans who were against the US's support for Ukraine. The report said that while responding to a journalist, Zelenskyy allegedly urged the United States during a press conference to keep supporting the nation and stressed that the US would lose its influence over the world if it stopped backing Kyiv.Â
But, did he seek fresh young Americans to help fight the war?
We searched again with relevant keywords and found the full video of the press conference on the YouTube channel of DW News on February 24. The part where Zelenskyy spoke about non-supportive Americans appears around one-and-a-half hours into it.Â
A reporter sought Zelenskyy's response to an opinion poll in the United States that suggested a growing number of Americans had started to believe that the US government had provided "too much" support to Ukraine.Â
As Zelenskyy began responding in his native language, the translator prompted his gratitude towards American officials for supporting them. He then criticised those opposing the "US-favour", saying: "I can tell them only one thing. If they do not change their opinion, if they do not understand us, if they do not support Ukraine, they will lose NATO. They will lose the clout of the United States, they will lose the leadership position they are enjoying in the world." Â
Zelenskyy added, "They will lose the support of the country with 40 million of the population (Ukraine) with millions of children. Are American children any different from ours? Who wants a third world war? Would anyone be willing to accept that risk? The US is never going to give up on the NATO member states. If Ukraine loses, Russia is going to enter the Baltic states and NATO member states, and then the US will have to send their sons and daughters exactly the same way we are sending our sons and daughters to war, and they will have to fight. Because it's NATO that we are talking about, and they will be dying. God forbid it because it's a horrible thing."Â
NATO or The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation is an intergovernmental military alliance between 30 member states — 28 European and two North American. Ukraine, while not a part of NATO, has received its support since the Russian invasion began. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg recently said that Ukraine will become a member in the "long term", but also stressed that the immediate issue at hand was Ukraine staying an independent nation from Russia.
Thus, watching the original press address by Zelenskyy makes it clear that he never sought young Americans to fight the war in Ukraine. On the contrary, he was expressing fears that America might have to face a similar situation if Ukraine lost the war against Russia. Â Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Mar 1, 2023 21:18 IST

title: Fact Check: This is not what rain looks like from the sky — it's a microburst
content:
The photo shows a microburst in Las Vegas, not rain. Microbursts are powerful, localised columns of wind.
Precipitation comes in various forms— drizzle, rain, mist, and showers. Quite often, they cause severe damage, and sometimes, may also be exposed to misinformation. A spectacular picture of what seems like a form of precipitation has been going viral and is being shared alongside questionable "general knowledge" trivia.
The image  shows a wind column gushing down from clouds to the ground, somewhat similar to a tornado in morphology at first sight. A turbine engine of an aeroplane is also visible in the bottom right corner of the image, indicating that the photo might have been clicked mid-air from inside a flight. The image contained the text: "Did you know? This is what rain looks like from an airplane."
AFWA found that this natural phenomenon is not rain, but actually a microburst, a type of storm. AFWA PROBE Â
A reverse search of the image led us to a report by The Washington Post . The report titled, "Airplane passenger captures amazing photo of wet microburst belting Las Vegas," contained the viral picture. The report stated that a storm rolled through Las Vegas, pelting the city with heavy rain and strong wind gusts.
It further explained that it showed a single storm that intensified as it moved east into Las Vegas, eventually creating a windy and wet microburst.
The report attributed the picture to a person named Paul Hurst and said that it was clicked during his flight to Las Vegas. We tracked down Paul Hurst on Facebook and found the viral image there . Matt's Weather Rapport, a blog by Vermont-based journalist and weather reporter Matt Sutkoski, also featured the image  with the caption, "Via the Las Vegas Review-Journal, an airplane passenger captured a wet microburst hitting Las Vegas this past July."
Thus it's clear that the photo does not show normal rain. WHAT ARE MICROBURSTS?Â
Microbursts, also called downbursts , are powerful, localised columns of wind that occur when cooled air drops from the base of a thunderstorm at incredible speeds and subsequently hit the ground, spreading out in all directions.
A single microburst can create wind speeds up to 100 miles per hour  and cause damage as severe as an F1 tornado, downing trees, and damaging structures. However, they are different from tornadoes as they are not cyclonic and they stay in one place.
(Written by Vikas Bhadauria) Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Mar 1, 2023 22:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Bangladeshi actress Nazifa Tushi did not convert to Hinduism, fake Twitter account spreads lies
content:
Nazifa Tushi, a Bangladeshi actress, told AFWA that she does not have a Twitter account. Nor has she converted to Hinduism.
A Bengali actress who allegedly "left Islam and adopted Sanatan Dharma", said she is not afraid of "fatwas" if social media posts are to be believed. Screenshots of tweets from the account of "Nazifa Tushi" proclaiming, "No fatwa can change my mind, Har Har Mahadev," and, "After leaving Islam, feeling blessed in Sanatan Dharma," have been making the rounds on social media alongside these claims. One of these tweets contained a photo of a woman and a child, both sporting "tilaks" on their foreheads.Â
We also found the tweets visible in the screenshots, from February 27, 2023 , and August 22, 2022 . The archived version of these tweets can be seen here and here .Â
But did she do or say any of these things? AFWA found that neither has Bangladeshi actress Nazifa Tushi converted to Hinduism nor does she own the Twitter account in question. Who is Nazifa Tushi?
Nazifa is a renowned Bangladeshi actress, recently seen in the famous Bangladeshi movie "Hawa" . Tushi was widely praised for her performance in the film.
We first searched for news related to Tushi converting to Hinduism. However, we found no news reports about this from either India or Bangladesh. To get to the bottom of this, AFWA contacted Tushi.Â
She categorically told us that she did not have a Twitter account. She provided us with links to her official social media accounts on Facebook and Instagram .Â
We also compared the photo of the woman sporting the "tilak" with photos from Tushi's social media accounts and found no resemblance.Â
We used Facecheck to find the person in the viral image. This led us to the Instagram account " bhakti_kids_cdm ". There, we noticed several posts featuring the same woman. The Instagram account, tagged in these posts, belonged to Gourangi Gandharvika Devi Dasi . On this account, we found the viral photo , shared on February 25.Â
Tushi also denied allegations of religious conversion. She told AFWA, "I belong to a Bangladeshi Muslim family, and have not converted to Hinduism." The mysterious Twitter account
Every Twitter account has a unique ID number that remains the same even if the account's handle has been changed. Using TweetBeaver , we found the Twitter ID number of the handle "@Nazifa_Tusi". Â
When we searched for the ID on Yandex, we found that the same Twitter account was earlier active as "@Mahadev_Bhakt9", "@Charanjit_99" (impersonating Charanjit Singh Channi, the former chief minister of Punjab), and "@Shubham9_IND" (impersonating IAS officer Shubham Kumar). The last one was caught spreading misinformation earlier and was investigated by Boom  in 2021 . We also found tweets in which a person had addressed "@Nazifa_Tusi" as "@Charanjit_99" and "@Shubham9_IND". We used Twitonomy to examine the account and found that it was created on November 30, 2014. When we checked on the Wayback Machine, we found that the earliest archived tweet from this account was from August 10, 2022 . Curiously, Twitonomy, which examines a maximum of up to 3,200 of a user's most recent tweets, found that the account had only tweeted 190 times since August 9, 2022. This implied that previous tweets from this account had likely been scrubbed. (With inputs from Shahidul Hasan Khokan in Bangladesh)  Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Mar 2, 2023 20:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of PM Modi's effigy being paraded in Punjab is at least 2 years old
content:
This video was shared on social media as early as December 2020, and was shot during a farmers' protest in Punjab's Lohian Khas.
The radical Sikh leader Amritpal Singh, dubbed by many as "Bhindranwale 2.0", recently hit headlines for storming the Ajnala police station with hundreds of his supporters. The following day, on February 24, the Punjab police released Singh's close aide Lovepreet Toofan, saying that he wasn't found guilty. In its aftermath, the Punjab Congress president warned of a mass protest if the Waris Punjab De leader wasn't arrested.
Amid all this, a video began making the rounds on social media featuring an effigy of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, hung upside-down with a crane, and several turban-clad men walking alongside. Those sharing the video claimed that this was from a recent protest in Punjab.
Ashok Swain, a professor and the HoD of the Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Uppsala University in Sweden, shared the video  and wrote, "Modi's effigy wrapped with the national flag is being paraded in Punjab. They sent a contingent of paramilitary forces to Delhi airport to arrest Pawan Khera, but the regime and media are silent about it." Archives of such posts can be found here , here , and here . AFWA found that this video shows a 2020 protest in Punjab against the three contentious farm laws that have now been repealed. AFWA Probe We noticed something was written on PM Modi's effigy. The text in Punjabi roughly translates to, "He wasn't shutting up so we hung him." Extracting this text using Google Lens, we searched for Facebook posts containing these keywords and found the same video shared back in December 2020.  Further searches with the same keywords on Twitter and Facebook led us to multiple posts carrying photos of an upside-down effigy, shared on and around December 8, 2020.Â
AFWA found that this video shows a 2020 protest in Punjab against the three contentious farm laws that have now been repealed.
We noticed something was written on PM Modi's effigy. The text in Punjabi roughly translates to, "He wasn't shutting up so we hung him." Extracting this text using Google Lens, we searched for Facebook posts containing these keywords and found the same video shared back in December 2020. Â
Further searches with the same keywords on Twitter and Facebook led us to multiple posts carrying photos of an upside-down effigy, shared on and around December 8, 2020.Â
A few of these posts also contained hashtags like "Take Back Farm Laws" and mentioned that this was from a protest by Punjab farmers. Using this clue, we looked for December 2020 news reports about protests by Punjab farmers during which effigies were burnt. This led us to a report by the Punjab Kesari that carried a photo featuring a crane carrying PM Modi's upside-down effigy, which was surrounded by a crowd. It looked similar to the one in the viral video. The report said that this photo was shot during a farmers' protest in Lohian Khas, a town in Punjab near Jalandhar.Â
Searching for "Lohian Khas" in Punjabi led us to a tweet from December 2020 containing a photo of a man holding an upside-down effigy of Modi that looked similar to the one in the viral video. We also found a different video from the same protest shared by Jagjit Singh Dhanju , a journalist from Punjab.Â
In this video, we noticed a few shops in the background. Using them as clues, we geolocated the street on Google Maps and found that it was from Lohian Khas.
We also contacted Dhanju, who confirmed that while he did not shoot the video, it was from a December 2020 farmers' protest in Lohian Khas.Â
So, while we could not confirm when the video was shot, it's clear that it is at least two years old.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena, with input from Ashish Kumar)

title: Fact Check: Americans are NOT being conscripted for Ukraine war, deepfake Biden video goes viral
content:
The alleged statement by Biden is from an AI-generated deepfake. No draft has been announced in the US.
The United States has so far provided nearly $32 billion in weapons to Ukraine to defend itself against the Russian invasion which has killed thousands and displaced millions. Washington is also expected to announce an additional $400 million military aid package for Kyiv. But is the US now going to escalate things further by actively entering the war? At least that's what many seem to believe President Joe Biden has said.Â
A post that's being widely shared on social media alleges that Biden announced a national draft for the Ukraine war.Â
The post was a screenshot of a tweet containing the text, "BREAKING: Biden calls for a national draft. Men and women are to be selected to fight in Ukraine."
It further quoted Biden saying, "The recommended way forward will be to invoke the Selective Service Act, as is my authority as president." The post also contained a photo of Biden making an address.Â
India Today, in its investigation, found that Biden had not called for a national draft. The alleged statement by Biden is from an AI-generated "deepfake" video.
In the US, military conscription, commonly known as the draft, has been employed by the federal government in six conflicts. On January 27, 1973, then-Defense Secretary Melvin Laird announced the end of the military draft, after 25 uninterrupted years of conscription, saying that the Armed Forces "henceforth will depend exclusively on volunteer soldiers, sailors, airmen and Marines." Since then, it has not been employed again.
But did Biden announce a new draft?
We couldn't find any credible media reports about Biden calling for a national draft. Had he made a similar statement, media organisations across the world would have reported it.
We then searched for the text written in the viral screenshot and found the same tweeted by an account called "ThePatriotOasis". The tweet contained a video of Biden where he could be heard speaking about invoking the Selective Service Act. One of the frames in this video matched the photo in the viral screenshot. This made it clear that the viral screenshot was likely of this tweet. BREAKING: Biden calls for a national draft. Men and women are to be selected to fight in Ukriane. BIDEN: "The recommended way forward will be to invoke the Selective Service Act, as is my authority as president," pic.twitter.com/vD6rkBB5Dm — ThePatriotOasis (@ThePatriotOasis) February 27, 2023
BREAKING: Biden calls for a national draft. Men and women are to be selected to fight in Ukriane. BIDEN: "The recommended way forward will be to invoke the Selective Service Act, as is my authority as president," pic.twitter.com/vD6rkBB5Dm — ThePatriotOasis (@ThePatriotOasis) February 27, 2023
In the video, Biden said, "The illegal Russian offensive has been swift, callous and brutal. It's barbaric. Putin's illegal occupation of Kyiv and the impending Chinese blockade of Taiwan has created a two-front national security crisis that requires more troops than the volunteer military can supply. I have received guidance from General Milly, chairman of the Joint Chiefs, that the recommended way forward will be to invoke the Selective Service Act, as is my authority as president."
He further said, "The first to be called in a sequence determined by national lottery will be men and women whose twentieth birthday falls during the calendar year 2023. Remember, you are not sending your sons and daughters to war, you're sending them to freedom. God bless our troops and god bless Ukraine."
But here's the kicker. Soon after Biden's speech, a man appears on the screen and clarifies that this was an AI-generated video. He said, "That was an AI…I don't want to say recreation, but maybe a pre-creation of President Biden, designed and scripted by our producers here for the show of what could happen if President Biden were to declare and activate the Selective Service Act, begin drafting 20-year-olds here in the United States."
ThePatriotOasis appeared to have taken the video from The Post Millennial, a far-right Canadian online news magazine. Sharing the same video on February 27, 2023, the official Twitter account of The Post Millennial wrote that it was an AI-generated video. The tweet said, "AI imagines what would happen if Biden declares and activates the Selective Service Act and begins drafting 20 years old to war". AI imagines what would happen if Biden declares and activates the Selective Service Act and begins drafting 20 years old to war pic.twitter.com/896Htrtteu — The Post Millennial (@TPostMillennial) February 27, 2023
AI imagines what would happen if Biden declares and activates the Selective Service Act and begins drafting 20 years old to war pic.twitter.com/896Htrtteu — The Post Millennial (@TPostMillennial) February 27, 2023
The man in the video who said it was created using AI was Jack Posobiec, a far-right political activist in the US. The video was from a show he hosts for  Turning Point USA, a conservative American nonprofit. He also tweeted  the video on February 27.Â
We were also able to find the original video that was altered to create the deepfake. Using reverse search, we found the original on the YouTube channel of the White House, shared on December 8, 2021. There, the US president was speaking about the Build Back Better Act.Â
Thus, it's clear that no draft has been announced in the US and that the post making the rounds shows an AI-generated deepfake of Biden. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Mar 3, 2023 18:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Honour-killing of DJ in Hyderabad over inter-caste marriage given a communal spin
content:
The deceased Devarakonda Harish and the girl Manisha, both belong to the Hindu community.
The Cyberabad police arrested ten accused in the alleged honour killing of 28-year-old DJ operator Devarakonda Harish Kumar  on March 5. Harish was stabbed to death on March 1, allegedly by his brother-in-law and his accomplices for marrying against the latter's family wishes. Meanwhile, a cryptic post is being circulated on social media, giving communal hues to the brutal honour killing. Some social media users claimed that Harish married a Muslim girl and was allegedly killed by her family members and some Muslim fanatics. While sharing an image of the youth, users wrote , "This is Harish from Telangana, who was stabbed to death by Muslim fanatics. Harish loved and married a Muslim girl. After this, the family members of Harish's Muslim wife stabbed Harish to death with knives. Do they want a Hindu daughter-in-law, not a Hindu son-in-law? #JusticeForHarish."  Others also echoed similar communal claims on social media . The archived versions of such posts can be seen here , here and here .  advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story AFWA's investigation found the claims to be false. The deceased Devarakonda Harish and the girl both belong to the Hindu community and there is no communal angle to it. AFWA Probe A keyword search on the internet led us to various news reports citing this as a suspected honour-killing case. On March 4, 2023, The News Minute  cited Harish as a Dalit man and belonging to the 'Mala' community, while Manisha belonging to 'Valmiki Mehtar'. The Indian Express  stated that the deceased was a Dalit, while the girl belonged to a backward community. On February 22, Harish eloped with Manisha, 25, to get married. Later, when her brother learned about their whereabouts, he hacked Harish to death. News reports by The Times of India , and The Siasat Daily labelled it as a case of 'honour-killing'. The names of the accused are as follows– B. Deendayal (main accused), Trimukhe Naresh, Potlacheruvu Venkatesh Goud, Kalibhavaniwale Rohith Singh, Band Venkat, Parwary Aniketh, Koyalkar Manish, Bure Sainath, Mathangi Rajendra Kumar, Gouti Navanitha. These news reports clearly suggest that Harish, Manisha, the main accused Deendayal and all his associates belong to the Hindu community.  To get to the bottom of the matter, AFWA reached out to the SHO of Petbasheerabad Police Station Gouri Prashanth. He divulged that both Harish and Manisha belong to the backward-class Hindu communities. Speaking to AFWA, Harish's sister Pravallika also confirmed that Harish belongs to a Scheduled Caste community, while his wife Manisha is from the Scheduled Tribe. We were not able to independently ascertain the caste of the girl. It is, however, clear that a case of honour killing was falsely shared with a communal angle to mislead people. (Inputs Sanjeeva Rao, India Today, Telangana) Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Mar 7, 2023 13:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Italian PM didn't refuse to shake hands with PM Modi, here's complete picture
content:
The image was taken when PM Modi offered a handshake to his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni, while she folded her hands in 'Namaste'. The confusion didn't last too long and Meloni immediately shook hands with the Indian Prime Minister.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni recently made her first state visit to India on March 2, 2023. Soon after she met Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Hyderabad House in Delhi, an image of both counterparts was shared widely on social media with some surprising claims.
If the claims of some of the social media users are to be believed, then the Italian prime minister shied away from Modi's plea for a handshake, rather she folded her hands in 'Namaste'.
The image is being widely shared with the claim that PM Modi's Italian counterpart refused to shake hands with him.Â
A user called Meloni's act an insult and wrote , "Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni refuses to shake hands with Narendra Modi. It seems she's giving back 'sanskaar' to a 'sanskaari'."Â
While sharing this image, several netizens, including Congress leader Alka Lamba , took a jibe against PM Modi. भारत का परिधान मंत्री - इटली की प्रधानमंत्री. अति संस्कारी. pic.twitter.com/NR19n5feUG — Alka Lamba (@LambaAlka) March 4, 2023
भारत का परिधान मंत्री - इटली की प्रधानमंत्री. अति संस्कारी. pic.twitter.com/NR19n5feUG — Alka Lamba (@LambaAlka) March 4, 2023
An archived version of the tweet can be seen here .
AFWA's investigation found the claims to be false. The picture was taken when Italian PM Meloni folded her hands while PM Modi offered his hands for a handshake. Seeing Modi offering his hand, Meloni immediately shook his hand.
A keyword search on the internet led us to various videos and news reports containing the same shot. On March 2, 2023, a video was uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Doordarshan National. In the video, Modi can be seen greeting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni at Rashtrapati Bhawan where she received a ceremonial welcome. At the end of the ceremony, PM Modi took her to the car to bid goodbye.
At the 7.42-second timestamp of that video , PM Modi can be seen offering a handshake to his Italian counterpart while Meloni folded her hands in 'Namaste'. This awkward moment, however, was over in the blink of an eye, as Meloni immediately shook hands with the Indian Prime Minister.
The same video was uploaded on various YouTube channels, including Sansad TV , PMO India , The Indian Express , and Midday India  on the same day. Â
As per the news, Italian PM Giorgia Meloni received a Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhawan. She was the Chief Guest at the 8th edition of the Raisina Dialogue held in New Delhi. The visuals of the event can be found on the YouTube channel of the news agency ANI.
Thus, the image misses the complete picture and was shared with a misleading claim. Â Â Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Mar 8, 2023 20:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Photos, videos of unrelated incidents passed off as Bihari migrants attacked in Tamil Nadu
content:
The man in this video is Prateek, a pre-university student who was killed during a brawl over car parking at a sports tournament in Karnataka's Bengaluru. He was not a migrant worker from Bihar.
For the past few days, social media have been witnessing a huge surge in posts about migrants from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh being under attack in Tamil Nadu.
To assuage the concerns of migrant workers, Tamil Nadu Director General of Police (DGP) Sylendra Babu warned that stringent action  will be initiated against those involved in causing fear-mongering and sharing misinformation. The state police booked OpIndia Chief Executive Rahul Roushan and its Editor-in-Chief Nupur J Sharma for allegedly spreading misinformation  on its portal.
Bharatiya Janata Party's Tamil Nadu chief K Annamalai, BJP spokesperson Prashant Umrao and an unnamed editor of the Dainik Bhaskar were also booked for sharing "false messages" on migrants being allegedly attacked in Tamil Nadu. Nonetheless, these troubling and misleading posts continue to proliferate and create panic.
In this article, we will debunk a few such claims going viral on social media.
Post 1: Video of a man lying in a pool of blood
The first post includes a video featuring a young man with blood all over his body. Lying on the ground, the man can be seen gasping for breath. Some social media users, while sharing the video, claimed that it shows a migrant worker from Bihar being attacked in Tamil Nadu.Â
Listening to the video, we noticed people in the background speaking in Kannada. To learn more details, we then shared the clip with a few journalists in Bengaluru who confirmed to us that it is from a recent incident in Doddabelavangala of Bengaluru where two boys were murdered over car parking.
Multiple media organisations  reported this incident on February 18. As per these reports , Bharath Kumar, an engineering graduate, and Prateek, a pre-university student, were stabbed to death during a brawl over car parking at a sports tournament at Bengaluru's Doddabelavangala on February 17.
However, none of these media reports used the viral video. To get to the bottom of it, we reached out to Harish M.N, Inspector of Doddabelavangala. Harish confirmed to us that the video is from Doddabelavangala.
Speaking to us, the Inspector clarified, "The boy seen in the video is Prateek who was killed during a fight in Doddabelavangala on February 17. Both the accused and victims involved in this case were from Karnataka."
Post 2: Photos of two injured men The second post that we are going to debunk carries a collage of two photos. The first photo is of a man in a blue shirt, trying to wrap his bleeding head with a piece of cloth. The second photo features a man in a pink shirt, lying down in a pool of blood. Sharing collage, the posts claimed it is from Tamil Nadu and show Tamilians assaulting Bihari migrants for speaking in Hindi. With the help of a reverse search, we found the same and other similar photos of the two men in multiple media reports . The reports  identified the man in the blue shirt as Manoj and the one in a pink shirt as Gokul. The latter was one of the accused involved in the murder of a 22-year-old youth near Saravanampatti in Coimbatore in December 2021. advertisement Reportedly, the two had arrived at the Coimbatore district court for the hearing of a case when a gang of unidentified men attacked them with machetes. Gokul suffered a cut on his neck and died on the spot. Manoj somehow managed to escape with injuries and was later admitted to the hospital. None of the reports mentioned the men being migrant workers. We then contacted V Balakrishnan, Coimbatore City Police Commissioner, for better clarity on the matter. Speaking to India Today's fact-check team, the Commissioner said, "Both Gokul and Manoj were locals from Coimbatore. They were not migrant workers as claimed in the social media posts. The incident resulted from a previous enmity between the two groups." India Today's Coimbatore bureau also confirmed that the two men were from Kavundampalayam in Coimbatore and studied together in school. Thus, visuals and graphics of old and unrelated incidents are being shared with false claims to instil fear in migrant workers living in Tamil Nadu. (With inputs from Sudhakar in Coimbatore) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Mar 9, 2023 13:04 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of  journalist 'grilling' Bill Gates over Covid vaccines is a 'deepfake'
content:
This video is a "Deepfake". The original interview did not have a heated argument like the one seen in the viral clip.
A video purportedly showing a grilling interview of Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates is doing the rounds on social media and features a journalist accusing Gates of stealing technology from others and also profiteering from COVID-19 vaccines. The interview abruptly ends with Gates calling it off after a feud.
Sharing this video, a social media user wrote , "Best interview I ever heard. This is not how the world works. So one person is going to define how world works. Billions of lives are at state and this person is making Billion Dollar profit. So much for philanthropy (sic)." Advocate Prashant Bhushan also shared the video taking a jibe at Bill Gates, which he later deleted.
Archives of this post and similar others can be found here , here , and here .
India Today, in its investigation, found that Bill Gates was indeed interviewed by the journalist seen in this video. However, the viral clip is an AI-generated "deepfake".Â
We noticed a logo present on the top-right corner of the viral clip that reads "730". Taking a clue, we performed a keyword search that led us to an interview of Bill Gates, published on January 31, 2023, on the YouTube channel  of "ABC News (Australian Broadcasting Corporation)". The journalist from the viral video can be seen interviewing Gates in this video and the backgrounds of the two videos have striking similarities. "7.30" is ABC's national flagship current affairs program  presented by journalist Sarah Ferguson.Â
In the interview, Ferguson discussed with Gates topics ranging from the looming threat of climate change to the origin of COVID-19 and related conspiracy theories. The billionaire philanthropist stated that he had complained to technology companies about COVID-19 conspiracy theories  about him being spread online. Further, he also opined on the future of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) revolution, Elon Musk purchasing Twitter and his philanthropic endeavours in the interview. Â
Ferguson also questioned Gates about his controversial relationship with Jeffrey Epstein - a powerful financier who pleaded guilty to two state prostitution charges. In 2018, Epstein was sentenced to 18 months in prison, where he reportedly killed himself in August 2019.Â
Gates regretted his association with Epstein and said, "I shouldn't have had dinners with him." Further, he added that there was no relationship between Epstein and the "Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation". While some reported that Gates was irritated by the line of questioning regarding Epstein. The conversation in the original interview was nowhere near that in the viral video.Â
A social media user replied to one of the tweets sharing the viral video and called it a "Deepfake".Â
He wrote that the viral video was created by a TikTok creator called bdti989, who posted it with the caption "How dangerous AI can be". He further elaborated that the creator had stated that he edited the ABC News interview using artificial intelligence. Â
Spelling out the details of the interview, another news report stated that presenter Sarah Ferguson grilled Gates, asking if he "regrets the relationship he maintained" with Epstein, going against his ex-wife Melinda Gates' advice. However, there was no mention of Ferguson accusing Gates of stealing Microsoft or profiteering from Covid-19 vaccines anywhere.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Mar 10, 2023 18:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Neither WEF has ordered govts to legalise marriage with animals, nor Spain has laws for it
content:
WEF has never made such claims and has no authority and also no intention to give orders to governments and other institutions or individuals on any subject.
Sexual acts with animals are criminalised in most countries in the world. They, however, may vary in terms of sanctioned penalties and acts that are punishable.
A viral tweet is again bringing new attention to the contentious subject. A post shared on Twitter  made a startling claim that the World Economic Forum (WEF) is allegedly pressing for the legalisation of sex and marriage with animals and Spain already has laws in place for it.
The tweet features an article by 'Newspunch', and reads, "WEF Says It's Time To Legalize Sex and Marriage With Animals To Promote Inclusion. (me: there's a lot of information on the internet that says Spain has legalized this)."
The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .Â
The article reads further, "WEF has ordered the mainstream media to begin pushing the narrative in other countries. Make no mistake, this isn't just about Spain. They want to roll this sickness out across the world."
AFWA found that this isn't true. Neither the WEF has proposed the legalisation of sex and marriage with animals, nor does Spain have laws in place legalising them.
We performed a keyword search on Google to look for media reports of the WEF recommending for the legalisation of sex and marriage with animals, and if it's already been done in Spain. However, the search didn't yield any news report hinting at the WEF or Spain taking such bizarre steps.
We were also unable to find any record of such a proposal on their social media accounts and official website. Moreover, any such announcement by the WEF would have made international headlines across countries.Â
AFWA reached out to WEF for their comment on the viral news. Â
Yann Zopf, head of media-public engagement at WEF, said, "This is a fake story that aims to discredit the important work that the World Economic Forum does on serious global challenges. The WEF has never made such claims and has no authority and no intention to give orders to governments and other institutions or individuals on any subject."
We again performed a keyword search to look for media reports about Spain having already legalised bestiality.
We came across a few news reports  that refuted Spain taking such a measure. The claim apparently emerges from the Spanish Congress's nod to the new animal welfare law.
In February 2023, the lower house of the Spanish Congress passed the legislation  aimed at amending the laws governing animal abuse. However, the law is yet to be passed as the Senate must approve the amendment before it becomes law.Â
Many far-right organisations in the European country and even Poland's Justice Minister Zbigniew Ziobro mocked  the new law and claimed that it attempts to decriminalise sex with animals if they suffer no injuries during the act.
As soon as the legislation was given a nod, rumours  started spreading on social media that the bill spearheaded by "far-left" Social Rights Minister Ione Belarra attempts to decriminalise bestiality.
The controversy revolves around the ambiguous language contained in the amendment to Spain's Criminal Code, if passed it will change the quantum of punishment for the abuse of animals.
The wording of one of the laws that punish "sexual exploitation" of animals has been changed to mean only those acts of a sexual nature would be punished that cause animal injury requiring treatment."
Simply, the proposed new law doesn't categorically legalise sexual exploitation of animals, but rather only those that come with a physical injury.  This particular ambiguous section of the law has been picked up in isolation and presented without complete context to make people believe that Spain has legalised bestiality.Â
According to Snopes ,  which debunked the viral claim in February 2023, "Spain's Social Rights Ministry have defended the new wording, as according to them the only existing legislation brought in 2015 penalised just the "sexual exploitation" of animals, which could be interpreted as being sexual exploitation for financial gain only."
Giving more clarity, the Ministry said, "All sexual acts with animals will be punishable. In the event that they produce injuries, they will be considered crimes; in the rest – less serious offences – they will be classified as abuse without visible signs of injury."
The law is not aimed at decriminalising bestiality, but could possibly hinder the judicial process for punishing offenders involved in the sexual exploitation of animals because of the ambiguity in the language used.
We also reached out to the Government of Spain asking for precise reasons for the amendment to the criminal law and its foreseen and unforeseen implications. The story will be updated as and when we receive a response. Â
Thus, both the claims–World Economic Forum proposing governments to amend their laws for legalising marriage and sex with animals, and Spain already having legalised it– are untrue.Â
(Inputs by Vikas Bhadauria) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Mar 10, 2023 19:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of passenger harassed by TTE falsely linked to migrants' condition in Tamil Nadu
content:
This video is from a train that runs between Patna and New Delhi. The incident is not related to Tamil Nadu.
The Tamil Nadu police have so far registered 11 cases and arrested three persons for spreading rumours that migrant workers were not safe or were under attack in the state. Disconcerting news about the safety of migrant workers in Tamil Nadu has been circulating on social media for the last few weeks. The Director General of Tamil Nadu Police said that the workers were called back by their families due to the panic created by miscreants.Â
Amid this chaos, on March 8, a Twitter account by the name of Sintu Tiwari shared a video where a Train Ticket Examiner (TTE) can be seen scolding and manhandling a young man for not possessing a ticket. He pulls the man's ears and tries striking him in the head. After reprimanding the passenger, TTE allegedly collected a fine from him. While sharing the video, it was claimed that the young man was a Bihari migrant trying to flee Tamil Nadu and was attacked for travelling without a ticket.Â
The archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today's fact check team found that the video does not show migrant workers fleeing Tamil Nadu. This video is from a train that runs between Patna and New Delhi. The train doesn't pass through any station in Tamil Nadu.
In the viral clip, a man can be heard saying "Sampoorna Kranti Express". We then performed a keyword search for the train. It runs between Rajendra Nagar in Patna and New Delhi .Â
We reached out to Birendra Kumar, the Chief Public Relations Officer of East Central Railway for his clarification on the viral claim. The officer confirmed to us that the video is from the Sampoorna Kranti Express and not related to Tamil Nadu.Â
Kumar said, "This incident occurred a few days back inside the Sampoorna Kranti Express, in the Danapur division. The TTE is under suspension pending enquiry for manhandling a passenger who was travelling without a ticket."
Danapur division comes under the East Central Railway headquartered in Bihar.Â
Responding to the viral post, the official Twitter handle of the Danapur railway division also clarified that the concerned TTE has been suspended for harassing a passenger inside the Sampoorna Kranti Express. Concerned TTE has been suspended with immediate effect.
— DRM/DNR (@DrmDnr) March 9, 2023
Concerned TTE has been suspended with immediate effect.
— DRM/DNR (@DrmDnr) March 9, 2023
Thus, it is clear that the video does not show Bihari migrant workers trying to flee Tamil Nadu. Over the past week, India Today's fact check team has debunked several false claims about Bihari or Hindi-speaking migrants being ill-treated in Tamil Nadu. Some of them can be seen here . Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Mar 10, 2023 21:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Former UK PM Liz Truss did not mock India for illiteracy
content:
There is no record of Truss making such a statement. This quote is made-up.
India hoped for better bilateral ties with the United Kingdom after Rishi Sunak became the latter's first Indian-origin Prime Minister. Hurting this euphoria, a purported statement by Sunak's predecessor, Liz Truss, is garnering a lot of attention on social media for not the right reasons. She is alleged to have mocked India's "illiterate leaders and spiritual preachers".
A postcard was shared by many social media users featuring an alleged quote by the former UK prime minister saying, "India is a country where people carefully listen to the speeches of illiterate leaders and religious preachers." The postcard features a photograph of Truss as well. ये कटाक्ष है या तारीफ ? pic.twitter.com/lKHBvkvTJD — Sameer saifi 🇮🇳 (@Intezar_saifii) March 8, 2023
ये कटाक्ष है या तारीफ ? pic.twitter.com/lKHBvkvTJD — Sameer saifi 🇮🇳 (@Intezar_saifii) March 8, 2023
The postcard was shared by many, including one Punjab Congress leader on Twitter with a cheeky caption asking, "is this sarcasm or praise?"
Several Facebook users also shared the postcard, while taking a dig at prime minister Narendra Modi.
An archived version of the tweet can be seen here .Â
AFWA found that the quote attributed to Truss is absolutely baseless. There is no record of the former UK PM making such a statement against India or its political leaders.
Before becoming the prime minister of the UK from the Conservative party for a short tenure, Truss held the chair of the UK's foreign secretary from 2021 to 2022.
Given that Truss is not only a former prime minister of one of the prominent European countries but also held key cabinets, it is obvious that such comments would have appeared in leading media outlets. However, several keyword searches on Truss and her remarks on India yielded no news that supports the postcard's claims.
Subsequently, we searched for Truss's statement regarding India and came across a recent report published on February 24, 2023. The report highlighted her response to the question about West's trustworthiness. She said, "This is where India has a huge role to play, being the world's biggest democracy. I don't think India is a follower, I think India is a leader. You are the world's biggest democracy."
During the same event, she also urged a relook at the UN Security Council and supported a greater role for India in the world body. She also stressed that the current structure is not working out. Â
A report by 'Mint' published on September 5, 2022– the day she was elected as the UK's prime minister– quoted Truss's early desire to wrap up a trade deal with India and promised to look at their visa system to make sure it attracts Indians. The trade deal, however, could not materialise as she resigned after 45 days of taking the oath, making her the shortest-serving prime minister ever in the UK's history.
As the foreign secretary of the UK, Truss also paid a visit to India amid the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. She restrained from drawing lines between New Delhi's ties with Moscow. On being questioned about what the UK thinks of India's decision to buy oil from Russia amid the sanctions of western countries, Truss responded, " She wants India to join sanctions against Russia but will not tell what to do."
It is noteworthy that India has abstained from voting against Russia in the United Nations Security Council resolution that condemned and rejected Russia's annexation of four Ukrainian regions, not once but several times .
We also came across a similar-looking postcard on the Twitter handle of 'Bolta Hindustan', with the same logo visible on the viral postcard. The original postcard from the official handle quoted Truss after she had resigned from the PM's chair in October. The quote read, "I could not fulfil the promises with which I came to power, that's why I have resigned." मैं जिन वादों के साथ सत्ता में आई थी उसे पूरा नहीं कर पाई इसलिए इस्तीफ़ा दे दिया : लिज़ ट्रस, UK पीएम pic.twitter.com/7rJSPb6k1n — Bolta Hindustan (@BoltaHindustan) October 20, 2022
मैं जिन वादों के साथ सत्ता में आई थी उसे पूरा नहीं कर पाई इसलिए इस्तीफ़ा दे दिया : लिज़ ट्रस, UK पीएम pic.twitter.com/7rJSPb6k1n — Bolta Hindustan (@BoltaHindustan) October 20, 2022
A comparison between both postcards makes it clear that the original text was replaced with the quote visible in the viral postcard.
Thus, it is clear that a made-up quote has been falsely attributed to Liz Truss. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: Mar 10, 2023 22:49 IST

title: Fact Check: This horrific helicopter crash DID NOT kill couple, wedding went ahead as planned
content:
This helicopter crash, which took place at a wedding in Brazil in 2018, did not claim any lives.
Bridal entry is one of the most awaited moments in any Indian wedding. Every wedding season, social media get flooded with videos of extravagant and dramatic bridal entries—from making quirky entries on cars, bikes  to even tractor rides . Not just that, even water and air charters are not spared.
A video of one such lavish entry is doing the rounds on social media these days, where it is claimed that a couple aboard the helicopter lost their lives in a horrific crash.
A person sharing the video on Twitter  wrote, "The bride and groom arriving and landing in a luxurious wedding helicopter, all dreams vanish in a moment. Parents watching their own children die helplessly, invited guests too.  Never be proud of wealth. See the fate of a luxurious marriage."
Archives of such posts can be found here  and here .
India Today found that this helicopter crash did not claim any lives and the couple, unharmed, went ahead with the nuptials. AFWA Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video on Yandex led us to a report  carrying a screengrab from the viral video. It stated that a shocking incident took place at a wedding in Brazil, where a helicopter carrying the bride for her big entry crashed before landing. It further mentioned that the bride and pilot managed to escape from the chopper and there were no casualties.
Further searches led us to a news report on the incident by the Mirror  from May 2018. It reported that the helicopter carrying the bride crashed in the middle of the wedding venue — a vineyard north of Sao Paulo, Brazil. The couple, however, decided to go ahead with the nuptials.
Estadao, a daily newspaper published in Sao Paulo, also shared the viral video stating that three people were injured in the accident. Helicóptero que levava noiva para festa de casamento cai e deixa três feridos em Vinhedo https://t.co/qH4zGbDkkS pic.twitter.com/wTm8O4MnRT — Estadão 🗞️ (@Estadao) May 5, 2018
Helicóptero que levava noiva para festa de casamento cai e deixa três feridos em Vinhedo https://t.co/qH4zGbDkkS pic.twitter.com/wTm8O4MnRT — Estadão 🗞️ (@Estadao) May 5, 2018
We also found a tweet about this helicopter crash on the official Twitter page of the Fire Department of the Military Police of Sao Paulo. There, too, no mention of any casualties was found. Tivemos uma ocorrência de queda de helicóptero seguido de incêndio pela R Viena, 300 – Vista Alegre / Vinhedo, 4 vtrs do 7º e 19º Grupamento de Bombeiros atenderam. Reporting this incident on May 5, 2018, a leading Brazilian news portal G1 stated that there were four people in the chopper — the pilot, a child, a photographer, and the bride. Three people suffered minor injuries while the bride was unharmed. The report also carried video footage of the couple continuing with the wedding ceremony post this accident.
While this grand wedding entrance did go through a huge hiccup, however, those aboard the chopper had a miraculous escape.

title: Fact Check: Video of Molotov cocktails being hurled is from Palestine, not from recent protests in Pakistan
content:
This video is from Palestine's Ramallah city. It is not related to clashes between Imran Khan supporters and Pakistan police.
Pakistan police withdrew from the Lahore residence of former Prime Minister Imran Khan on March 15, after failing to arrest him for corruption charges. This temporary relief  came after clashes between law enforcement and Khan's supporters outside his residence in Zaman Park, which lasted nearly 24 hours.Â
As Khan's residence remained a battleground for several hours, images and videos of the riots started to flood social media. Among them, is a video  that contains different clippings of men allegedly hurling Molotov cocktails at police cannons and jeeps. Those sharing the video claimed these were the supporters of  Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) attacking police. The archived versions  of similar posts   can be seen here , here , and here . Imran Khan zindabad عمران خان زندہ باد 😍🥰😘❤ #زمان_پارک_پُہنچو #عمران_خان_ہماری_ریڈ_لائن #عمران_خان_Ú©ÛŒ_جان_Ú©Ùˆ_خطرہ #عمران_خان_ضروری_ہے #عمران_تیرےجانثار_سب_تیار #zamanpark #ImranKhan #muradsaeed #imrankhanPTI #ImranKhanOurRedLine #ImranKhan #زمان_پارک_پُہنچو pic.twitter.com/VrIdAswZyh — Farhan Ali (@raofarhankhan) March 15, 2023

India Today found that the video is old and from Palestine, and not related to the recent political developments in Pakistan. AFWA PROBEÂ
The video in question contains a watermark that reads "Kareem Khamysa". We then searched for this name on Facebook and found multiple videos with the same watermark uploaded on the profile of Palestinian journalist Kareem Khamysa , According to Khamysa'a Facebook bio, he works with the Palestine Times.Â
While we couldn't trace the video in question to Khamysa's account, however, we found similar other videos of protestors throwing Molotov cocktails at Israeli forces.
We then reached out to Khamysa, who confirmed that all the clips seen in the video were shot by him in Ramallah city of Palestine. However, he couldn't confirm the exact date and time of the footage contained in the video.
We further did a reverse search of the video's keyframes with relevant keywords in Arabic and found one of the clips  shared on March 5, 2020, by the verified Facebook page of Palestine based media company "Alarabiya Palestine". According to the description, the video shows young men attacking Israeli forces in the Al-Tira neighbourhood in Ramallah.
The other clips seen in the viral video were uploaded to the YouTube channel "Omar N AbuRub" on January 23, 2022. All the clips, here also,  carried a watermark of Khamysa's name.Â
It's clear that the video in question is from Palestine, and not related to the recent protests by PTI supporters in Pakistan in wake of Imran Khan's impending arrest. Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Mar 16, 2023 16:59 IST

title: Fact Check: Old videos resurface after 7.1 quake strikes Kermadec Islands in New Zealand
content:
This video is from February 2023 and shows an earthquake-hit region in the southeastern Turkish province of Hatay.
A powerful earthquake of magnitude 7.1 struck the Kermadec Islands region , located north of New Zealand on March 16 morning. Shortly after, the US Tsunami Warning System issued a tsunami alert for nearby, uninhabited islands in a 300-km radius. The National Emergency Management Agency later said that there was no tsunami threat for New Zealand. Nonetheless, netizens took to social media, posting videos of earthquakes and floods claiming them to be from New Zealand. These, however, turned out to be from other parts of the world.Â
In this article, we will debunk four such videos. Video 1 Imagine what #earthquake can do. A strong #EarthquakePH of 7.1 Magnitude hits #NewZealand today. #Tsunami alerted in kermadac island. #turkeyearthquake2023 has taken thousand of lives with the same intensity. A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to a report by The Independent which had carried the same video. The second video purportedly shows an aerial view of the disaster that hit the region. Several buildings can be seen reduced to rubble in this footage.Â

The third video in question shows four people standing in a forest when the ground starts shaking vigorously, causing one of them to fall.Â

Zhuoxi Township is a mountain indigenous village in Hualien County, Taiwan. According to this Facebook post, when the earthquake occurred, the members of the mountaineering group were at an altitude of 1,000 metres.
Taiwanese and Chinese news portals also reported on this video in September 2022. As per the New York Post report, a 6.8 magnitude earthquake hit Taiwan on September 18, 2022. The fourth video features a few cars being swept away by gushing flood water. Several vehicles can also be seen stuck in the flood.Â
Using reverse image search, we found the same video shared by several social media users and media organisations from Turkey on March 15, 2023. 📌 ZINDÃŽ- Li Semsûr û Rihayê lehî rabûye "Li Rihayê dayîk û zaroka wî di bin avê de man û ji alîyê welatîyan ve hatin rizgarkirin" https://t.co/3WyFxJcrLW pic.twitter.com/Zhh1SPZoLX — Botan Times (@BotanTimes) March 15, 2023
