title: Fact Check: Old video passed off as footage of Cheetah helicopter crashing in Arunachal
content:
This is an old video circulating on the internet since 2022.
Two pilots were killed after an Army Aviation Cheetah helicopter, on an operational sortie, crashed near Bomdila in Arunachal Pradesh  on March 16, 2023. The accident reportedly claimed the lives of Pilot Lt Col VVB Reddy and co-pilot Major Jayanth A. Like most tragic accidents, this too invited its share of misinformation. A video  of a black tandem-rotor helicopter crashing into a river is going viral on social media with a claim that it shows the Cheetah helicopter that crashed in Arunachal Pradesh. ALSO READ | 2 pilots killed in Indian Army Cheetah helicopter crash in Arunachal Pradesh A social media user, while sharing the clip, tweeted , "Army's Cheetah Helicopter Crash, search operation to find pilots." The archived version of the viral post can be seen here . #BreakingNews Army's Cheetah Helicopter Crash, search operation to find pilots. #ArunachalPradesh #ArmyCheetah #HelicopterCrash #PilotCoPilot #earthquakes #Tsunami #CheetahHelicopter #BipinRawat pic.twitter.com/3MmdWM635m — Aashima Rai💯% FB (@AashimaRai4) March 16, 2023 India Today Fact Check found that the video has been on the internet since 2022, thus ruling out any links to the recent crash of the Indian Army's Cheetah helicopter. AFWA PROBE A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a post  on Facebook that shared the same video in August 2022. According to it, the video showed a Chinook helicopter crashing into the Salmon river claiming the lives of the two pilots. ALSO READ | Fact Check: Former UK PM Liz Truss did not mock India for illiteracy Another Twitter user shared  this video around the same time, writing, "Video footage of a Boeing CH-47D Chinook helicopter (N388RA), that crashed into the Salmon River on July 21, 2022, while fighting the Moose Fire in Idaho." Video footage of a Boeing CH-47D Chinook helicopter (N388RA) , that crashed into the Salmon River on July 21, 2022 while fighting the Moose Fire in Idaho. 📹 Cactus @psickokactus1 #helicopter #safety #aviation #avgeek pic.twitter.com/tPfT8n6Dad — FL360aero (@fl360aero) August 13, 2022 We then searched for news reports about the Chinook helicopter crash. According to the US News report , a firefighting helicopter with two people aboard crashed in Idaho on July 21, 2022. Another report  about this incident stated that ROTAK Helicopter Services, the company that owned this helicopter, confirmed that a CH-47D Series Chinook crashed while battling the massive Moose Fire near Salmon, Idaho. ALSO READ | Fact Check: Old videos resurface after 7.1 quake strikes Kermadec Islands in New Zealand A CLOSER LOOK AT THE HELICOPTERS We looked at a photo  of the Indian Army's Cheetah helicopter on the website of its manufacturer — Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. It can be seen that Cheetahs are leaner and have skis as their landing gear. Also, they do not have two rotors unlike the helicopter seen in the viral video. On the other hand,  a CH-47D Series Chinook that had crashed in 2022 in Idaho, has striking similarities with the chopper seen in viral video. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story GEOLOCATING THE CRASH Fireaviation.com , a website that publishes news and commentaries about wildlife fire and aerial firefighting, carried a 3-D map of the Moose Fire.   With the help of this fire map, we narrowed down the location of the crash on Google Earth to an area adjacent to the Indianola Ranger Station near Salmon River that can be seen here . Using NASA Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), we also confirmed that there was a fire in this area around July 21, 2022. We have also reached out to Rotakheli and Fireaviation for more information about this video. The article will be updated as and when their response is received. While we could not independently verify that the viral video is of a helicopter crash in Idaho, however, it is pretty evident that it is from a 2022 crash. ( Vikas Bhadauria, with inputs from Sanjana Saxena ) Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Mar 18, 2023 14:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Pakistan's ex-PM Imran Khan's supporter did NOT wave gun at his election rally
content:
An old photo of Imran Khan's supporter has been edited to insert a gun.
Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan was allowed by an Islamabad court to go back without his indictment in the Toshakhana case after he marked his attendance outside the court complex.
While 'Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf' (PTI) chairman Khan was on his way to Islamabad for the court hearing, the police broke into his home. Over 30 party workers were arrested.
ALSO READ |Â Imran to appear in court today, supporters gather near his house with batons and iron rods
Meanwhile, an outraging image of a man waving a gun from a vehicle has gone viral on social media. Some users while sharing the image claimed that the man is a PTI supporter, and that he carried a gun at an election rally led by Khan in March 2023.
Mubasher Lucman, a known Pakistani journalist and anchorperson, was one of the first to share the picture on March 8, the day Khan suspended his election rally in Lahore after Police went berserk on his supporters. While sharing the viral image, he tweeted, "PTI is a law-abiding party."
His tweet has gone viral and has been shared more than 2500 times.
The archived version of this tweet and other similar claims can be seen here  and here . We found that the photo has been digitally altered to add the gun. AFWA Probe We performed a reverse image search with relevant keywords to know the veracity of the photo. The search led to us the original photo, in high resolution, on Getty Images , a website that provides stock images. It was published on the platform on August 15, 2014. No gun could be seen in this photo. The description of the photo reads, "Supporters of Pakistani cricketer-turned-politician Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) or Movement for Justice arrive in Islamabad to take part in Azadi (Freedom) march on August 15, 2014." The original photo provided credit to the Turkish state news agency Anadolu. Thereafter, we again searched the internet for keywords like, "Azadi March", "Freedom March" and "Imran Khan". On August 15, 2014, Khan organised the " Azadi March ", a 370-km long journey, to press for the resignation of the then Pakistan's Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. ALSO READ | Fresh FIR against Imran Khan for clashes between police, supporters in Lahore Another news report by African news channel eNCA  about PTI supporters being allegedly fired upon by the government supporters, also carried the original photo but without a gun. Thus, the photo of a PTI supporter who had come to participate in a rally led by Khan in 2014, was digitally doctored to add a gun. Published By: Ritika Shah Published On: Mar 18, 2023 21:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Palestinian children in Israeli prison? No, this image is cropped
content:
This is a cropped photo. The original image shows Palestinian children waiting for food at a soup kitchen in the West Bank city of Hebron, Palestine.
Children have been one of the biggest victims in the surging Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Since the start of 2023, seven Palestinian children and one Israeli child were killed. Around 12,000 Palestinian children have been jailed by Israel since 2000, according to the human rights organisation, Addameer. As of December 2022, 150 Palestinian children  are languishing in Israeli prisons. Against this backdrop, a photo of a few children standing behind metallic bars  is being circulated on social media with the claim that it shows Palestinian children in an Israeli prison. The archived version of the post and similar posts can be seen here , here  and here . India Today's fact-check team found that the image in question is morphed. The original photo shows Palestinian children waiting for food at a soup kitchen in the West Bank city of Hebron, Palestine. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story AFWA Probe With the help of a reverse image search, we found a larger version of the image in question on the website of the European Pressphoto Agency  (EPA). In this version of the image, we can see an open end of the metallic structure behind which the children were standing. A girl can also be seen standing outside this structure with a green bucket in her hand.  The description provided with the image reads, "Palestinian children wait to receive food, donated by the Islamic endowment authority Islamic waqf, at a soup kitchen in the West Bank city of Hebron August 18, 2010. " The photo was credited to EPA photographer Abed Al Hashlamoun. Similar images of children standing in a queue at the same location were also posted by Reuters  around the same time. Per Reuters, the pictures were taken on August 12, 2010, the second day of the holy month of Ramadan. We also came across a different photo clicked from the other side of the metallic structure on the stock image site, Alamy . This photograph was taken during Ramadan time of 2013. In this photo as well, children can be seen waiting outside the metallic structure with their buckets. Thus, the image in question was cropped and circulated with misleading claims.  Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 22, 2023 17:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Half-human-half-pig hybrid doesn't exist, it's a silicone sculpture
content:
It is not a living creature but a model made of rubber and silicon by a famous Italian artist Laira Maganuco.
In Greek mythology, a "Chimera" is a monstrous fire-breathing hybrid creature, composed of different animal parts. It is usually depicted as a lion, with the head of a goat protruding from its back, and a tail that might end with a snake's head. However, in science, the term "Chimera" means an organism that contains cells from two different species. For years, Chimeras or hybrid animals have featured in fantasy novels and sci-fi films. Now, if we say that a pig has given birth to a human-like creature, would you believe it? advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Recently, photos of a 'pig-human baby' have gone viral on social media  and garnered around 33,000 likes and 600 shares. The viral post claims that a pig that looks like a human being was born. The caption to these photos reads, "Inexplicably, a creature that was half human and half pig was born, and its presence sent the villagers fleeing in terror." The photos created a buzz on the internet in 2018-2019 as well when social media posts  claiming that a pig delivered offspring resembling a human baby went viral.  AFWA found that these photos are a work of art by Italian sculptor Laira Maganuco, and not a living creature. AFWA PROBE A simple Google reverse image search led us to the actual source. The pictures were first posted by an Italian artist Laira Maganuco on her website . According to the website, Maganuco specialises in creating hyper-realistic sculptures. This image of a "hybrid baby-pig", too, is one of the products of her many artworks. The description provided with this image reads, "This piece is entirely hand sculpted and made of platinum silicone...Contains elements of great detail, to make the piece of art look even more realistic." This "hybrid baby-pig" is one of the examples of human-made art that is still available for sale on Maganuco's website. The product description can be seen below: We then searched for Maganuco's social media accounts. We found images of similar sculptures of mysterious-looking creatures on her Facebook  and Instagram  accounts, where she promotes her artwork. The sculpture is also available for sale on the creative goods retail site Etsy . To sum it up, a hyper-realistic silicone sculpture of half-human and half-pig is shared with a misleading claim that it's a living creature. ( Report by: Vikas Bhadauria ) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Mar 22, 2023 19:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Puppet dancing to 'Naatu Naatu'? Nope - Edited video goes viral
content:
This video is from 2017. The original video features the Spanish song 'Despacito'.
SS Rajamouli's grand cinematic spectacle "RRR", and its catchy song "Naatu Naatu" has won hearts in India and the world. It bagged a Golden Globe  and an Academy Award  for the best original song. And while fans have been trying their best to recreate the complicated dance steps from the song, if social media is to be believed, puppets aren't far behind either. Ok. One last tweet, I promise, about #NaatuNaatu But couldn't resist this one. Real evidence of it being a global phenomenon since it now has the whole world on its 'strings' 😊 pic.twitter.com/ex1bmf4Boh — anand mahindra (@anandmahindra) March 22, 2023 A video was shared by Anand Mahindra, chairman of the Mahindra group. It showed a woman making a puppet dance to the song in a street. He tweeted, "Ok. One last tweet, I promise, about #NaatuNaatu But couldn't resist this one. Real evidence of it being a global phenomenon since it now has the whole world on its 'strings'." An archived version of this tweet  can be seen here. Following that, several social media accounts also shared this clip on Twitter and Facebook. Ok. One last tweet, I promise, about #NaatuNaatu But couldn't resist this one. Real evidence of it being a global phenomenon since it now has the whole world on its 'strings' 😊 Anand Mohinder. pic.twitter.com/xcwrHSDjnk — Chandan Chowdhury (@imchowdhuri) March 23, 2023  News outlets like the Times of India, the Hindustan Times Telegu, Zee news, and several others featured the same clip in their reports while claiming the same. The archived versions of these can be seen here , here , and here . India Today's probe found that the video of the puppet dance is almost six years old, and originally did not feature "Naatu Naatu". The video's origins A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video led to us the same clip uploaded to a YouTube channel  on September 2, 2017. Being nearly six years old, it became clear that it could not have been related to "Naatu Naatu", which was first released in November 2021. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story This video, instead of the "RRR" song, featured a cover of the popular Spanish number " Despacito ". Subsequent searches led us to several articles on BuzzFeed  and Jacaranda FM  published in December 2017. Although neither of these reports confirmed the time or location of this video, they mentioned that this puppet dance was recorded with the tune of "Despacito". In these reports, we found the earliest version of the viral video uploaded to a YouTube channel named "Aleksandar Stevanovic" on August 21, 2017. This video was titled "Despacito Dancing Puppet!! Amazing."  Here, the original track of "Despacito" could be heard playing. The noise of people laughing and chattering around could also be heard here. Thus, it is more than evident that the original video is at least six years old and shows a puppet dancing to "Despacito", and not "Naatu Naatu".  Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 23, 2023 18:51 IST

title: Fact Check: This incredible luxury train is NOT Indian - it's Indonesian
content:
This video is from a train in Indonesia.
Trains like the Tejas Express, the Vande Bharat Express, and the Gatimaan Express have redefined train travel in India. And now, on social media on any given day, you are likely to come across videos and photos from these trains with commuters singing praises.Â
One such video of a luxury train with state-of-the-art facilities  has been widely shared with captions like: "In a major makeover NaMo & his team have shown a rapid improvement in the railway infrastructure & trains which earlier resembled a third-world country." But is this train Indian? India Today found that the video is from Indonesia. Identifying the train We noticed multiple signs on the train were in the Indonesian language, like Nomor (Number), Buka (Open), Tutup Pintu Kembali (Keep Door Closed), and Geser (Slide). These hinted that the video was not from India. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story  We also noticed a board with the word "INKA" on one of the walls of the train. INKA is an Indonesian state-owned railway vehicle manufacturer. The video also carried a watermark that said, "adeodatusdeo". A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to a TikTok account  of the same name that shared the same video on January 1. The video was geotagged to Malang, a city in the Indonesian province of East Java. As per its description, the video showed a Ka Gajayana luxury class train that operates between Malang and Jakarta in Indonesia. With the help of a relevant keyword search, we found images similar to that of the train seen in the viral video shared in a series of tweets by the Twitter account of Kereta Api Indonesia, the public railway operator of Indonesia. As per the tweets, this is a Luxury Train 2 launched on May 26, 2019. Seminggu kemarin banyak yang tag Railmin waktu naik Kereta Luxury 2 nih. Yuk, kalian bisa share pengalaman kalian di kolom komentar ya. #KAI121 #KeretaLuxury2 pic.twitter.com/9itXEv96EY — Kereta Api Indonesia (@KAI121) November 25, 2020 We also found media reports  about the launch of this train in 2019. As per the reports, KA Gajayana is a train that boasts facilities like minibars, entertainment units, and seats with 140-degree reclining capacity. The train runs on four routes. We also found several YouTube videos  featuring the interiors of the same train. A comparison between the screengrabs from one such YouTube video and the viral clip can be seen below. It is, hence, clear that the video in question is from Indonesia. It has nothing to do with the Indian Railways. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 23, 2023 19:17 IST

title: Fact Check: These astronauts DIDN'T remove their helmets on the Moon - This photo was taken on Earth
content:
The photo was clicked during a training session at the Kennedy Space Centre in Florida, and not on the Moon.
More than five decades since humans first set foot on the Moon, conspiracy theories about it being faked — created in a studio — still continue to follow this historic achievement. Over the years, people have presented a plethora of questionable evidence to bolster this claim. One such piece of " evidence " that's been widely shared recently is a picture of three men in spacesuits without their helmets on what appears to be the lunar surface. One of them can be seen sitting in a Lunar Roving vehicle that's used to traverse the lunar surface. At the bottom of the picture, the text reads, "So these guys on the Moon took a moment to take their helmets off this picture." The text implies, as usual, that the moon landing was fake because no one would be able to survive on the Moon without a helmet. The archived version of the tweet can be seen here . India Today's probe found that the viral image is of Apollo 16 astronauts. It was clicked by Charles M Duke Jr during a training exercise in a space centre in Florida. It isn't from the Moon. Earth, not Moon We performed a reverse image search and found the viral picture on the National Aeronautics and Space Administration's (NASA) official account on the photo-sharing website Flickr . The description of the photo reads, "Apollo 16 astronauts (left to right), Lunar Module Pilot Charles M Duke, Commander John W Young, and Command Module Pilot Thomas K Mattingly II during a training exercise in preparation for the Lunar Landing Mission. Date: February 6, 1972." The photo was clicked almost a month before the mission was launched. We also found the viral image on Wikimedia Commons, an online repository of the free-use image, sound, and other media files. The website  states that the image was catalogued by NASA's Kennedy Space Center. On further probe, we found another photo  from the training exercise at the Kennedy Space Center, which is located on Merritt Island, Florida. The US launched Apollo 11 on July 16, 1969, the first space mission to put people on the moon. Neil Armstrong became the first man to set foot on the moon, almost three years before this photo was taken. Thus, it's clear the photo is being used out of context. It was taken at a US space centre in Florida and not on the moon. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 23, 2023 22:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Did AAP MLA Balkar Sidhu criticise his own party? Viral clip is 7 years old
content:
The viral video is not recent. This clip of Sidhu is about 7 years old. At the time, he was joining the Congress party.
A video of Phul Balkar Sidhu, a famous Punjabi folk singer and the Aam Aadmi Party MLA from Rampura, allegedly denigrating his own party has been widely shared online. In the short clip, he can be heard saying, "They are saying we will clean Punjab with a broom, but the broom will disband on itself. It is my humble request to the people of Punjab, the AAP leaders from UP, Bihar, and Delhi want to control Punjab. If they win, things will become much worse in Punjab." Punjab AAP vs Delhi AAP … open now pic.twitter.com/6wf9u2zNK0 — ਅਦਨਾਨ ਅਲੀ ਖਾਨ ( عدنان علی خان ) (@AdnanAliKhan555) March 21, 2023 "Save Punjab from Aam Aadmi Party. AAP MLA Balkar Sidhu's appeal to Punjab" can be seen written in the video. Sharing the video, a Twitter user wrote, "Punjab AAP vs Delhi AAP, open now." An archived version of such a claim can be seen here . India Today found that the video in question is about seven years old. At the time, Sidhu was joining the Congress party. The video We noticed the "ABP Sanjha" logo in the video, hinting that this clip was aired by the Punjabi-language news channel owned by the ABP Group. Subsequent searches with relevant keywords led us to a longer version of the video on the official YouTube channel of ABP Sanjha. The video was shared on February 9, 2016, and was titled in Punjabi: "Balkar Sidhu attacks Aam Aadmi Party". The viral segment can be viewed between 2 minutes 44 seconds and 3 minutes 15 seconds. As per the information given in the video, the interview was taken just before Sidhu joined the Congress party. ABP Sanjha also shared this video on its Facebook  page on February 9, 2016. Sidhu's political career Sidhu was a member of the AAP earlier  and was even given a ticket to contest the 2014 Talwandi Sabo assembly by-polls. However, he was later replaced by another candidate, Baljinder Kaur. Subsequently, Sidhu decided to contest elections as an independent candidate and was expelled from the AAP. He joined the Congress party  in February 2016 in the presence of Captain Amarinder Singh, who was a member of Congress at the time. Five years later, he rejoined the Aam Aadmi Party  in 2021 and won from the Rampura Phul in the 2022 Punjab assembly elections. Thus, it's clear that the video is being shared out of context. These comments were made by Sidhu seven years ago, following his expulsion from the AAP, right when he was about to join the Congress party. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story  Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 24, 2023 17:34 IST

title: Fact Check: NO links to Covid-19 vaccine! This video of bus driver getting heart attack is from 2012
content:
This video is from a 2012 incident and has no links to Covid-19 vaccines.
"School bus driver suffers heart attack and 13-year-old gets behind the wheel and saves all children's lives," read a tweet containing a terrifying video of an incapacitated driver behind the wheels of a school bus. This video, which has been making the rounds on social media, shows a bus driver flailing his arms in his seat as one of the kids on the bus bravely manages to get hold of the wheel. While some praised the heroic instincts of the child, others blamed the Covid-19 vaccines for the accident. A person shared the video  writing, "It is dangerous to get on buses, trains and air planes post vaccine era." Another, taking a jab at vaccines , wrote, "Hopefully he was injected then he doesn't die of corona." Archives of similar posts  can be found here, here , and here . India Today, in its investigation, found that this video is more than a decade old, thus ruling out any links between the accident and the Covid-19 vaccines. Our Probe A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to its extended version  of the clip shared on the YouTube channel of the Associated Press. According to the date stamp present at the top of this footage, the accident took place on April 9, 2012. The video description stated that a seventh grader steered this school bus towards the side of the road after the driver lost consciousness in Washington, US. In the full video, the kid stops the bus with the help of another boy following which two adults board to help. The video also contained an interview of the boy, Jeremy Wuitschic, in which he explains how he turned off the ignition as the driver appeared to be having a seizure. We also found a report by the Guardian  about this accident. According to it, 13-year-old Jeremy got behind the wheels of a bus, carrying a dozen kids to school, after its driver experienced a heart attack. His classmate, Johnny Wood, also went on to help by giving the stricken driver chest compressions. The bus was pulling into Surprise Lake Middle School in Milton, about 30 miles south of Seattle. The driver, Ryan Callis, reportedly died at the hospital where he was rushed after collapsing . Several media outlets interviewed the " bus heroes " at the time regarding this accident . Thus, it's clear that the video of a 2012 accident is being shared as a recent incident to further the agenda against Covid-19 vaccines. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 24, 2023 20:47 IST

title: Fact Check: This incredible stack of stones standing atop each other is NOT a natural occurrence
content:
This video shows a rock formation made by Michael Grab, an artist based in Boulder Creek, Colorado.
Nature is bizarre and fascinating at times. A video of a stack of rocks  that has been making the rounds of social media appears to be an example of this trait. It consists of a huge unwieldy stone standing on its pointed edge atop two smaller ones in the middle of gushing water. While this is baffling enough, another stack of three circular stones can be seen balanced over it. Sharing the video, some credited the stack of stones to God , while others claimed that some sort of asceticism  was at play here. Archives of such posts  can be found here, here , and here . India Today, in its investigation, found that this video shows the work of Michael Grab, an artist based in Boulder Creek, Colorado in the US. Our Probe A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video on Yandex led us to a news report  from 2013, about a Colorado artist named Mike Grab. According to the report, Grab arranges stones in perfect balance to make astonishing stacks. The report also featured photos of several stacks of stones that looked similar to the one seen in the viral video. We noticed that a few of these photos were watermarked "GravityGlue.com". Using this, we found an Instagram account  named "gravityglue" which, per its bio, belongs to Michael Grab. Skimming through its posts, we found a photo  shared on August 19, 2019, featuring the same stack of rocks that could be seen in the viral video. The post was geotagged to Boulder, Colorado. According to the website of Gravity Glue , such stone formations are created using a skill called Rock Balancing. We also found a video of the process of creating a stone formation on Grab's Facebook page. One can see him stacking the stones on top of each other and adjusting them one by one. In another video, one can even see the stones toppling down  many times in the process. Thus, it's clear the rock formation seen in the viral video is just a temporary rock formation made by a stone balance artist. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 24, 2023 22:49 IST

title: Fact Check: These pictures of Fauci's arrest are AI-generated, technology still far from perfection
content:
These are not real images but are AI-generated.
Lately, there has been a surge in AI-generated images depicting fabricated scenes of the arrest of notable personalities. Pictures of Donald's arrest being arrested caused a massive stir online. This time pictures of the arrest of Anthony Fauci, the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, have taken the online world by storm. These AI-generated images show Fauci in various situations–from being carried away by the force, to being forcibly held. A Twitter user shared these images of imaginary scenes on social media and wrote, " Who wants to see it? ". While another user wrote, " Fauci Arrested in New York it looks like! DUH WINNING! #Trump2024 ." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The archived version of the tweet  can be seen here. We found that Fauci has not been arrested, and these images are generated online using AI tools. AFWA Probe When such a high-profile personality gets arrested, it's not very difficult to verify the event, as the news would surface all over social media and news portals as well. We used a keyword search to find news reports about Fauci's arrest, if at all it's been made. However, no results were returned. Flaws in AI-generated images AI is still in its nascent stage and is constantly advancing, that's why images generated using this technology are often replete with flaws. Having observed many AI-generated images before, we noticed a few anomalies in these pictures too. In the top left picture, the policeman holding Fauci has five fingers, apart from the thumb which isn't visible.  Similarly, in the upper right photo, the policewoman has a right hand wrongfully attached to her left arm. Then, we compared the faces of real Fauci and the ones visible in the AI-generated images. We found them to be considerably different. It's not very difficult to spot an AI image. All it takes is a little perseverance and eagle eyes.       Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Mar 25, 2023 22:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Neither police chase nor perfect timing, this video of car bouncing on trucks is CGI
content:
This is a computer-generated video made by a UK-based artist.
How often have you witnessed the police chasing a fugitive in a car on a busy road? Mostly in movies or video games, right? However, if some media reports are to be believed, something like this was recently caught on camera. A viral video shows a car somehow managing to escape the cops through sheer luck.
This nine-second-long clip shows a blue car rushing and then suddenly swerving left after noticing a police vehicle in front. Fortunately, it ends up on the other side of the subway by bouncing twice on a truck and a bus passing under it. Unbelievable. pic.twitter.com/O2rrzh3RZh — No Context Brits (@NoContextBrits) December 6, 2022
Unbelievable. pic.twitter.com/O2rrzh3RZh — No Context Brits (@NoContextBrits) December 6, 2022
A Twitter account called "No Context Brits" shared this video. It was then shared by Harsh Goenka, the chairman of the RPG group. He tweeted, "Perfect timing." An archived version of it can be seen here .Â
Following Goenka's tweet, news outlets like News24 f eatured the same clip in their report and claimed it was a scene from a Hollywood movie. NDTV Hindi, Zee news and several other outlets also featured this clip in reports. Archived versions of these reports can be seen here  and here .
India Today's investigation found that the video is several years old and is nothing but CGI (Computer-generated imagery).
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a verified Instagram account called "2ncs" . There, we came across the same clip shared on April 6, 2021.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by 2NCS (@2ncs)
The post's caption, however, did not contain any additional details about the video apart from licencing-related information, and hashtags like"3d" and "animation". This hinted that the video could have been made using CGI.
Furthermore, the Instagram account also contained several similar videos of supercars performing jaw-dropping stunts. For instance, a video from November 2022 showed a yellow Ferrari tied to a flying aeroplane in the middle of the sky.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by 2NCS (@2ncs)
We searched online for "2ncs" and this led us to the artist portfolio website Behance . In it, we found an artist page named "2ncs", mentioning it belonged to an automotive CGI artist. Some CGI works with supercars by the artist featured here as well. We also found a video on the YouTube channel "2NCS" that explained how they created these videos using CGI. This video showed a Ferrari passing under a moving truck. This made it apparent that the viral video was likely made using CGI. We searched further and found that this video had earlier been debunked as fake. On April 28, 2021, Snopes  also fact-checked the video here in question and mentioned that the person behind the 2Ncs account was a 23-year-old named Dionisis who lives in the United Kingdom. It stated that the artist used software programmes like Autodesk 3DS Max and Adobe After Effects to create the video. Thus, it is clear that a CGI video was falsely shared as a real incident by many on social media. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Mar 27, 2023 14:57 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Hindu groups in Karnataka protesting PM Modi, this video is from 2021 Shiv Sena march
content:
This video is from a 2021 protest held by Shiv Sena in the Hingoli district of Maharashtra against rising fuel prices
With assembly polls at the doorstep in Karnataka, prominent political figures have been making their way to the state to garner support from the voters. In the past two months, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has visited Karnataka on several occasions, inaugurating and laying foundation stones for numerous projects. A video that's been shared  widely recently shows a large group of men sporting saffron scarves and carrying flags, with some standing on a bullock cart. Per those sharing the video, these were Hindu groups in the poll-bound state protesting against the prime minister. In the footage, some men can be heard raising slogans against the Modi government. The archived version of such a post can be found here .   India Today's investigation found that the video is from a 2021 protest held by the Shiv Sena in Maharashtra. Our Probe Reverse searching the viral video's keyframes led us to a report published on February 5, 2021, by the Marathi daily Sakal . This report included a photograph from the same rally. According to the report, the photograph was taken during a bullock cart march on February 5, 2021. The march was organised by the Shiv Sena in the Hingoli district of Maharashtra to protest fuel price hikes. Shiv Sena MLA Santosh Bangar reportedly led the rally, which began at the party office and continued via the Indira Gandhi Chowk in Hingoli. Further, we found videos  of the rally on YouTube that were uploaded on February 5. These videos clearly show slogans being raised against the fuel price hike. Per reports, retail prices of automobile fuels  reached record highs across India in February 2021, leading to demonstrations in several parts of the country. According to an Outlook report , on February 5, Shiv Sena held protests in several parts of Maharashtra against the Centre over the fuel price hike. At the time, the Uddhav Thackeray-led Maha Vikas Aghadi government was in power in Maharashtra. In 2021, a photograph from the same rally was circulated, with people claiming that it showed Bajrang Dal members protesting farm laws and PM Modi in Uttar Pradesh. At the time, India Today reached out to MLA Bangar for clarification, and he confirmed that the picture was from a Shiv Sena rally organised by him . It is, hence, clear that the video in question is from an old protest held by the Shiv Sena in Maharashtra, and has nothing to do with poll-bound Karnataka. title: Fact Check: No, these burqa-clad students did not dance to 'Jai Shri Ram'
content:
The video is from Bangladesh and the girls in the video were dancing to a Bengali song called "Amar Monta Je Aj Elomelo".
A video  making the rounds on social media shows a group of burqa-clad students dancing vigorously to a song that contained the words "Jai Shri Ram". A girl in a red saree can also be seen dancing with them. Overlaid text in the video said: "When your dance teacher is a Kattar Hindu."Â
But were the girls in the video dancing to the tune of "Jai Shri Ram"? India Today's investigation found that the video was edited. The song was added to the original video. OUR PROBE Â
We ran a reverse image search of the video's keyframes on Google and found several uploads of the video. In all these uploads, a Bengali song could be heard in the background. The videos can be seen here  and here . Carrying our probe further, we observed something written in Bengali on the walls of a school-like structure. Using the Translate tool of Google Lens, we found it said, "Madaripur Girls' High School." Madaripur, a part of the Dhaka Division, is a district in central Bangladesh. We located the school on Google Maps and looked for the photos and videos geotagged with this location. We found several photos of the school walls that matched the ones visible in the viral video. Among these was also a screengrab of a Facebook post  by Billal Hosain Sagor containing the viral video. Next, we searched for Billal's profile on Facebook. We found the viral video on his timeline. It was shared by him on March 1, 2023. The video had received more than 548,000 likes, 44,000 comments and ten million views at the time of writing this article. The song heard in this video was the same as the one in other videos we found following the reverse image search. We then looked for the song using keyword searches and found that it was "Amar Monta Je Aj Elomelo" by SI Tutul. Subsequently, we found another video from the Madaripur Girls High School on YouTube that was uploaded on February 27, 2023, around the same time Billal had uploaded the viral video . In the video, some girls can be seen enacting a dance performance with the national flag of Bangladesh in their hands. The girls can be seen wearing the same red and green sarees visible in the viral video. The description of the video read: "Display of Madipur Girls High School, Annual Sports Day." Thus, while we could not ascertain the occasion of the video, we could verify that the video did not feature a song with "Jai Shri Ram" in it. (Written by Vikas Bhadauria) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Mar 28, 2023 22:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of car fuel tank exploding in Uzbekistan falsely shared as electric car blast in India
content:
This video shows the fuel tank of a car exploding in Uzbekistan's Samarkand.
A scary video  allegedly showing an electric car blowing up has been making the rounds on social media. In the video, within seconds of the blast, smoke can be seen billowing out of the trunk of the car. Additionally, a man trying to flee from the scene is knocked down by a red projectile.Â
One person shared the video  claiming that this incident took place in India. The tweet read, "Electric car blows off while charging. Such incidents (accidents) seem to be happening here and there - in India. Whatever it is, it appears that this technology will take some more time to be fully a commercial success." Archives of such posts can be seen here , here  and here .Â
India Today, in its investigation, found that this video is neither from India nor does it show an electric car. In fact, the red object that hit the man in the viral clip was the fuel tank of the car.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a tweet  from February 28, 2023, carrying an extended version of the viral clip. The datestamp on this camera footage read February 25, 2023. The tweet read, "In Samarkand (Uzbekistan), the balloon ricocheted and hit a gas station employee right in the head. The man died on the spot." In Samarkand (Uzbekistan), the balloon ricocheted and hit a gas station employee right in the head. The man died on the spot. #explosion #death #Uzbekistan #gasstation pic.twitter.com/kcnVcHZhC6 — eye (@Evgeniy91234) February 28, 2023
In Samarkand (Uzbekistan), the balloon ricocheted and hit a gas station employee right in the head. The man died on the spot. #explosion #death #Uzbekistan #gasstation pic.twitter.com/kcnVcHZhC6 — eye (@Evgeniy91234) February 28, 2023
Using this clue, we searched online and found a Turkish news report  carrying the viral footage of the accident. The report stated that the fuel tank of a car exploded while a man was refuelling his car at a gas station in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It added that a part of the tank that blew up claimed the life of a 42-year-old officer who was trying to escape. Another report  stated that a 1994 Nexia-3 car exploded at a gas station on Bedil street in Samarkand.Â
Several other  media outlets  reported   about this car blast  in Uzbekistan around that time. One such report   contained a message  from a telegram channel named "Samarqand viloyati FVB" — the emergency department of the Samarkand Region . This message carried photos of the destroyed car and the broken red cylinder along with the details of the accident.Â
Roughly translated to English, the message stated that on February 25, at 11:30 am, a worker died at a fuel station on M. Bedil street, Samarkand, while refuelling the gas cylinder of a Nexia 3 car manufactured in 2019. No other casualties were reported. The same information was also shared by the department on its Facebook page. Â
While incidents of electric cars catching fire  and exploding  have earlier been reported in different parts of India, the viral video does not depict that. (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Mar 31, 2023 21:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Not French protests! This photo shows Israeli demonstrations against Netanyahu govt
content:
This image shows people protesting against the judicial reforms in Israel.
Protests in France against the pension reforms  turning violent  has been widely reported. Protestors have clashed with the police, and videos and photos of law enforcement authorities teargassing crowds, and protestors setting garbage on fire have been shared all over social media. A photo now making the rounds shows an aerial view image of a street flooded with people. Allegedly, this showed the protests in France.  A Twitter user  shared the photo and wrote, "Protests in Paris, last night." The archived version of this claim can be seen here . advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today's investigation found that this photo is not from France at all. It's from Israel. THE PHOTO We noticed that a person replying to the tweet in question  pointed out that this image was from Israel. Reverse-searching the viral image with relevant keywords led us to a Reuters report  from March 5, 2023. The report containing the photo was about the recent protests in Israel against the government's plan to overhaul the judicial system. As per the information given in the article, the image was clicked by photographer Ilan Rosenberg in Tel Aviv on March 4, 2023. This image was also used in the reports by The Jerusalem Post  and US News . A series of protests and strikes began in Israel in early 2023 after Benjamin Netanyahu's government proposed a judicial overhaul that would limit the powers of the Supreme Court. These protests intensified after he fired his defence minister, who had spoken against this plan. On March 27, Netanyahu announced a delay in the judicial overhaul plan. However, despite this delay, the protests are still going on in the country. GEOLOCATING THE PROTEST SITE We were able to find the exact location seen in the viral image. We discovered that Reuters photographer Ilan Rosenberg had shared a photo from the protests on March 5 on his Facebook page . Upon comparing this image with the viral image, we could conclude that they were both shot at the same location. In the image posted on Rosenberg's Facebook page, we could see "Crown Plaza City Center" written on a tall building. Next, we attempted to see the satellite view of this building on Google maps. One of the towers of the Crown Plaza City Center looks triangular from the aerial view. This shape can be seen in the image posted on Rosenberg's Facebook page as well as in Google Maps' satellite view. Also, on the other side of the road, there is the Tel Aviv government complex building which is semi-circular on one side and flat on the other side. Thus, it became clear that an image related to the protests in Israel is being falsely shared as protests in France.  Published By: Raajnandini Mukherjee Published On: Mar 31, 2023 23:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Painting of Egyptian priest discovered in a tomb in Giza falsely linked to Hinduism
content:
This is a picture of a tomb in Egypt, where a wall painting of a priest, dating back over 4,300 years, was discovered. This painting of the priest has no relation with Hinduism whatsoever.
The great pyramids of Egypt are considered as one of the most architecturally mystifying constructions on the earth, considering the period they were erected. Now and then, rumours about pyramids and myths associated with them keep stealing the spotlight. The latest one to spread like a wildfire on social media claims that a Hindu temple was found under one of these pyramids.
An Instagram user shared a picture of an excavated site and wrote, "A Hindu Ancient temple was found under the pyramids, Egypt. There is a Hindu temple under the pyramids. Pyramids are built on the temple. There are many doors of Hindu temples under the pyramids. They are covered by the pyramids.....As many Shiva Lingas are underground, many Hindu temples are still underground. Total world is Sanatana. Sanatana dharma."
In the picture, a pyramid can also be seen in the background.
The archived version of one of the posts can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check team found that the viral image is not of a Hindu temple discovered under a pyramid, but an excavated site where a wall painting was discovered in the tomb of a priest, near the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt.
To get to the bottom of the truth, we conducted a reverse image search. It led us to a few media reports that contained the viral image.
According to Livescience , a portal that catalogues developments in science, space, technology and history, the viral photo was clicked by Maksim Lebedev, faculty member at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Russian Academy of Sciences, Department of History of the East. He led a team of researchers that discovered the wall painting, dating back over 4,300 years.Â
The painting was discovered in 2012 by a team from the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences, which has been excavating these tombs since 1996.
Per the report, the painting shows vivid scenes of life, including boats sailing south on the Nile river, a bird hunting trip in a marsh and a man named Perseneb who's shown with his wife and dog. The painting was discovered when the researchers began the restoration process of the tomb of Perseneb, who was a "priest" and "steward".
A report by nbcnews  states that tomb, located 1,000 feet (300 meters) east of the Great Pyramid of Giza, contains an offering room, central room and burial chamber.
The tomb is believed to date to the middle or late fifth dynasty (ca. 2450-2350 B.C.).Â
Livescience quoted Lebedev, "The "The full agricultural sequence relating to crops represents the most crucial event in the life of ancient Egyptian society."
Remarkably, religious places of ancient Egypt civilisation are so called temples and the religious figure who performed ceremonies are called priest.
We then reached out to Lebedev for his comments. The report will be updated as and when the response is received.
Thus, an old discovery of a wall painting of a priest–that lived in an ancient Egypt society–in a tomb in Egypt was presented with a fabricated claim that a Hindu temple was discovered under a pyramid.
(Report: Vikas Bhadauria) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Apr 3, 2023 14:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of mob pelting stones during Ram Navami in Vadodara falsely shared as violence in Howrah
content:
The video is not from West Bengal, but from Mandvi Bazar of Vadodara, Gujarat. It was shot on March 30, 2023.
Sporadic unrest and violence during Ram Navami has become a norm in the last few years. Like many other parts of the country, stone pelting and arson  were reported in Howrah, West Bengal, on March 30. Consequently, section 144 was imposed and a few delinquents were arrested.Â

Around the 13-second timestamp of the video, signage of a shop named "Paramount Parfums" can be seen.

title: Fact Check: Video of police dragging young men out of their homes is not related to Ram Navami
content:
This is a 2022 video from Hyderabad. The men were protesting against alleged remarks of suspended BJP MLA T Raja Singh on Prophet Muhammad.
The recent Ram Navami festivities in multiple states of India were marred by incidents of violence, and several people were arrested by police in connection with the clashes. A video of police arresting young men by dragging them out of their homes was circulated on social media in this context.Â
The video was shared with claims that it shows Gujarat police arresting Muslim men who allegedly pelted stones at a Ram Navami rally. The same video was also shared claiming to be related to the Ram Navami clashes in Maharashtra. An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
However, India Today's investigation found that the video is old and from Hyderabad. It has nothing to do with the clashes that erupted during Ram Navami celebrations on March 30, 2023.
The number plate of the police vehicle is visible in one part of the video, and the number written on it begins with "TS 09." After searching, it was found that this number was from Hyderabad Central.Â
Additionally, in this video, we can see the boards of two shops named "SHAFFAF" and "MASQUATI". We searched for these shops on Google Maps and found they were located in Zohra Colony in Hyderabad's Shalibanda area. Story behind the video With the help of reverse image search of the viral video's keyframes, a similar clip was found tweeted by NDTV on August 25, 2022. As per this tweet, the video was from a protest held against the alleged remarks of suspended BJP MLA T Raja Singh on the Prophet Muhammad. The demonstration was held at Shalibanda in Hyderabad on August 24, 2022. Telangana | Protestors gathered at Shalibanda in Hyderabad last night over alleged remarks of suspended BJP leader T Raja Singh on #ProphetMuhammad ; police used force to restrain them pic.twitter.com/Wjs1Epvvwb — NDTV (@ndtv) August 25, 2022 AajTak also used footage from the same video in its report about the protest. As per reports , on August 22, 2022 Raja Singh released a video allegedly making derogatory statements against the Prophet. Following this, large crowds gathered in various parts of the city demanding action against the BJP leader. Reportedly, the police brought the situation under control after a lathi charge. Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi had alleged that the cops used disproportionate force and barged into protestors' homes at midnight. advertisement It is hence clear that the video in question is old and from Hyderabad. It has nothing to do with the recent riots that broke out during Ram Navami celebrations.  In 2022, the same video was circulated with people claiming it to be from Uttar Pradesh. India Today fact checked it at that time. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Apr 3, 2023 20:59 IST

title: Fact Check: No violence reported in MP's Khargone, this video of stone pelting is from Howrah
content:
This video is not from Khargone, but from Howrah, West Bengal. This happened on the evening of March 30. No violence was reported in Khargone this year.
For the past few days, social media platforms have been flooded with distressing visuals of the violence that broke out during and after the Ram Navami celebration on March 30. Except for some scattered incidents of communal clashes and unrest in a few states, the celebration remained largely peaceful.
One such video of a mob pelting stones is doing rounds on social media. Those sharing the video claimed that it is from the violence that ensued in Khargone, Madhya Pradesh. Not to forget that last year Khargone witnessed a series of violence during the Ram Navami celebrations.
A social media user, while sharing the clip wrote , "70 terrorists stone pelters in Khargone Madhya Pradesh arrested in view of Violence on Ram Navami."Â
An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
AFWA's probe, however, revealed that the video is not from Madhya Pradesh but from the communal clashes that erupted in Howrah, West Bengal. AFWA ProbeÂ
Around the three-second timestamp of the viral video, a pair of Kolkata's iconic yellow cabs can be seen, hinting that the visuals are probably from somewhere near Kolkata. A reverse image search of the keyframes extracted from the viral video led us to West Bengal's BJP state president Dr Sukanta Majumder's tweet, which contained the same viral video. Yesterday's attack and arson on RamNavami processions in various locations in West Bengal is a direct result of CM Mamata Banerjee's provocative statements against organizers of #RamNavami . We can clearly see WB police standing with the rioters & watching silently. pic.twitter.com/ExpMaUHB5O — Dr. Sukanta Majumdar (@DrSukantaBJP) March 31, 2023 The tweet attributed the visuals to the alleged violence and arson during Ram Navami in West Bengal. However, it didn't pinpoint the exact location of the incident. On further probe, we found a news report by Lokmat Times published on April 1 , 2023. The report featured a screenshot from the viral video and stated that clashes broke out in Howrah, the adjoining district to Kolkata. Around the 56-second timestamp of the viral video, a shop with a signboard reading "Ghose's eye clinic" could be spotted. On running a keyword search for the shop on Google maps , we geolocated it to GT Road, Shibpur, in Howrah. The screengrabs from the viral video matched the images of the shop found on Google maps. Going further, we reached out to the "Ghose's eye clinic". A staff member, who does not want to be named, confirmed to AFWA that the violence indeed took place on the evening of March 30, when processions of Ram Navami were carried out. No violence in Khargone We, then, searched for news reports to confirm if any similar incident had occurred in Khargone, but didn't come across any. However, a couple of articles from ABP News  and Amar Ujala noted that a saffron flag was hoisted on a Dargah, following which a complaint was lodged by the police. Thereupon, we also spoke to AajTak's Khargone correspondent Umesh Revliya, who confirmed that no violence was reported. Rather, in a harmonious atmosphere, people from the Muslim community showered flowers when the Ram Navami procession was taken out. An article by Dainik Bhaskar also reported the same . Thus, it can be concluded beyond doubt that a video of violence during Ram Navami celebrations in Howrah, West Bengal, was falsely attributed to Khargone, Madhya Pradesh. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Apr 4, 2023 14:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video of women and child chased by stray dogs is from Odisha, not Hyderabad or Jammu
content:
