title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show NRIs campaigning against BJP ahead of Karnataka polls
content:
This video is from April 2021 and shows a grassroots platform against the saffron party that was formed during the 2021 West Bengal assembly elections.
With assembly elections in Karnataka just days away, have Non-Resident Indians also taken to campaigning abroad? If social media is to be believed, a group of NRIs have taken to campaign against the Bharatiya Janata Party, the incumbent party in Karnataka, and this has allegedly been captured on video . No Vote to BJP ❌ #KarnatakaElection2023 pic.twitter.com/X8wrcfcqql — Deepak Khatri (@Deepakkhatri812) April 23, 2023
No Vote to BJP ❌ #KarnatakaElection2023 pic.twitter.com/X8wrcfcqql — Deepak Khatri (@Deepakkhatri812) April 23, 2023
In the 45-second-long video ,  Indians from Germany, Finland, England, and several parts of the US could be seen holding a placard that read, "No Vote To BJP."Â
Several Congress leaders and social media users shared this video with the "KarnatakaElections2023" hashtag alongside texts like, "Across the globe, everyone says 'NO VOTE to BJP'." The archived versions of such posts can be seen here  and here .Â
India Today's investigation, however, found that the video is two-years-old and not at all related to the upcoming Karnataka assembly elections.Â
While looking closely at the "No Vote To BJP" placards, we noticed a line in Bangla penned underneath the English words that said, "There is no division in Bengal." This hinted at the possibility of the video being related to elections in West Bengal. A subsequent reverse image search of keyframes of the viral video with relevant keywords led us to the original video tweeted  by an account called "No Vote To BJP" on April 24, 2021. The tweet read: "Bengalis across the world saying 'No Vote To BJP'." This made it clear that the video was two years old and unrelated to the upcoming elections in Karnataka. Notably, the 2021 West Bengal assembly elections were held in eight phases — starting from March 27, followed by the announcement of the results on May 2. Thus, it is clear that the video was aimed at the Bengal polls and not any other state. Bengalis across the world saying "No Vote To BJP". #NoVoteToBJP pic.twitter.com/7vXwu6NOxL — No Vote To BJP (@No_Vote_To_BJP) April 24, 2021 THE 'NO VOTE TO BJP' CAMPAIGN According to an analysis by The Hindu , the "No Vote To BJP", a silent campaign before and during the West Bengal polls, helped the Trinamool Congress in a big way to derail the BJP's chances in the state. This campaign was carried out on a large scale on social media and in the streets of Bengal through billboards, posters and leaflets that featured only four words — "No Vote To BJP" — without mention of any other political party. A Times of India article  from April 19, 2021, covered the implementation of this silent campaign. The platform reportedly was set up by a group of political and civil rights activists. Its main talking points against the BJP included employment loss during the Covid-19 lockdown, tribal rights on forest land, CAA, and more. (With inputs from Ashish Kashyap) Published By: Rajeev Singh Published On: Apr 24, 2023 21:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of crowd vandalising BJP election van is NOT from poll-bound Karnataka
content:
This video from Telangana's Munugode assembly constituency shows an incident that happened in November 2022.
The Karnataka assembly election is scheduled for May 10, and the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party is pursuing an aggressive campaign in the state. Prominent leaders like Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and BJP President JP Nadda are all campaigning. But if the Congress party is to be believed, this star-powered campaign is not working, and the people of Karnataka are aggressively demonstrating their opposition to the BJP.Â
On Facebook and Twitter , the official accounts of the Karnataka Congress shared a video of a mob vandalising a BJP campaign vehicle. The accompanying text in Kannada said that "not only the BJP candidates, but even seeing the BJP's campaign vehicle, people are disgusted and outraged." The archived version of the posts can be seen here and here .
India Today, in its investigation, found that the video is neither recent nor from Karnataka.
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to the same video shared by a Twitter user  on November 1, 2022. As per this post, the video was from Telangana. A further search on Facebook with the help of keywords in Telugu led us to a  longer version of the video shared by a Facebook user on the same date. Per this post, the video showed an attack on the convoy of Huzurabad MLA Eetala Rajendar in the Munugode assembly constituency in the Nalgonda district of Telangana. Taking a cue from this we searched on Twitter using relevant keywords in Telugu and English and found different videos from the same incident shared by the official Twitter accounts of BJP Telangana , Union Minister and BJP leader G Kishan Reddy  and BJP leader Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy . As per these tweets, the attack happened during an election campaign ahead of the Munugode bypolls. The frustration & desperation of TRS over losing the Munugode By-poll is evident from the attack on Sr leader, @BJP4India National Executive Member & MLA Sh @Eatala_Rajender Garu & his wife in Munugode I strongly condemn the attack on Smt & Sh Rajender garu & our Karyakartas 1/2 pic.twitter.com/gKUaxL3Jkl — G Kishan Reddy (@kishanreddybjp) November 1, 2022 Several media organisations also reported the incident in 2022. As per reports , the incident allegedly started with stone-pelting at Rajender's convoy by unidentified persons in Palivela village in Munugode. The BJP accused members of Bharat Rashtra Samithi, formerly known as Telangana Rashtra Samithi, of the attack. The BRS, on the other hand, accused the BJP of attacking its workers who were on their way to attend a roadshow of the BRS working president KT Rama Rao. It is hence clear that the viral video is old and from Telangana. It has nothing to do with the upcoming elections in Karnataka. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Apr 25, 2023 14:56 IST

title: Fact Check: 15-all-out T20 match from 2022 went viral MULTIPLE times as 'yesterday's game' across 2023
content:
The match took place in December 2022. The Sydney Thunder was bowled out at 15 runs against the Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League 2022.
"Fifteen, all out," is an extraordinary cricketing feat, albeit embarrassing for the batting side. And a video showing that happening in a supposedly recent match has been making the rounds on social media.Â
A Twitter user on April 25, while sharing the viral clip of a Twenty20 match, wrote: "Can you believe this....? This took place yesterday at Melbourne, Australia, in a T20 match. Never before seen such a score. And game." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .
India Today, however, found that this was from a Big Bash League match in December 2022 — and therefore, not recent. Our Probe
First, we found that the viral clip had been shared with a similar claim multiple times, once on January 28 , then on April 19 , then April 20 , and finally on April 24 . This made it clear that this was not a recent match.
The video appeared to be a highlight of a cricket match played between teams sporting green and blue jerseys. The scorecard at the bottom of the screen suggested that the match was being played between Thunder and Strikers. A keyword search using these clues led us to many news reports on what was described as a record-setting match, but on the wrong side of the history. A report by Sportstar published on December 16, 2022, spelt out the details of this unusual cricket match. It noted that The Sydney Thunder was bowled out at 15 runs in a 140-run chase against the Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League 2022 in Melbourne, Australia. The Big Bash League is an Australian professional club Twenty20 cricket league, which was established in 2011 by Cricket Australia.
A keyword search using these clues led us to many news reports on what was described as a record-setting match, but on the wrong side of the history. A report by Sportstar published on December 16, 2022, spelt out the details of this unusual cricket match. It noted that The Sydney Thunder was bowled out at 15 runs in a 140-run chase against the Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League 2022 in Melbourne, Australia. The Big Bash League is an Australian professional club Twenty20 cricket league, which was established in 2011 by Cricket Australia.
The Cricketer described the unusual event as "Sydney Thunder made men's T20 history as they recorded the lowest score in the format's history." More news reports that expounded on the events of the match can be seen here and here .
We also found the complete highlight of the match on YouTube from which the viral video was clipped. The description of the video uploaded on December 16, 2022, noted,  "Defending an under-par 9-139, Strikers quicks Henry Thornton and Wes Agar obliterated the Thunder to 15 all out, the lowest ever score in the history of T20 cricket."Â
Sydney Thunder was bowled out for just 15 runs in merely 35 balls. The team snatched the title which was earlier held by Turkey for being the lowest scorers in men's T20 history. In 2019, Turkey was bowled out at 21 by the Czech Republic in 2019.
Thus, it's clear a video of a cricket match played in 2022 is being shared as a recent game. Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Apr 26, 2023 17:41 IST

title: Fact Check: Not storm-hit Tinsukia in Assam, this clip shows a powerful tornado in Myanmar
content:
The video does not show storm-hit Tinsukia. It shows a rare and powerful tornado that hit Naypyidaw, the capital of Myanmar.
A terrifying video supposedly showing the storm-hit Tinsukia district of Assam has been making the rounds on social media. In the video, the violent storm can be seen damaging houses and nearly uprooting trees. Archives of such posts can be found here and here .
On April 24, schools and colleges in Tinsukia were shut following severe thunderstorms and hailstorms that ravaged the district that weekend. At least two people reportedly died in the Doomdooma area of the district, around 37,200 people in 54 villages were affected by severe storms.
But does the viral video , show this deadly storm?
India Today, in its investigation, found that this video captured a powerful tornado, thousands of kilometres away in Myanmar.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to its extended version in a news report about the deadly tornado that hit central Myanmar. The video reportedly shows a tornado that hit Naypyitaw on April 21 this year. Naypyidaw, officially spelt Nay Pyi Taw, is the capital of Myanmar.
Per a news report by the Associated Press , a rare, big tornado tore through two villages near the capital city in central Myanmar, destroying more than 200 houses and claiming the lives of at least eight people.Â
Per a local charity organisation , the tornado hit the Aung Myin Kone and Tadau villages on Naypyitaw's southern outskirts at around 6:10 pm on April 21. Reportedly, more than a hundred people were transported to hospitals. Two Buddhist monasteries, a small clinic , and around 230 houses were reportedly destroyed by the tornado that blew for approximately 40 minutes.Â
 Several media outlets in Myanmar also shared the viral video of the tornado around the same time. Thus, it's clear that the viral video shows the destruction caused by a storm in Myanmar and not Assam's Tinsukia.
(Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Apr 26, 2023 17:57 IST

title: Fact Check: These six photos are from 2013, 2018, and 2019 — they DON'T show recent Dantewada Maoist attack
content:
These pictures are from various Maoist attacks which took place between 2013 and 2019 in different parts of Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, and Odisha.
On April 26, ten security personnel and a civilian driver returning from a counter-insurgency operation were killed when their vehicle was blown up by Maoists in Chhattisgarh's Dantewada. In its aftermath, several photos  allegedly from the site of the attack flooded social media .
A substantial number of these photos, however, were unrelated to the attack. In this article, India Today will fact-check six such photos making the rounds on Facebook and Twitter. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Photos from 2013 The first image shows security officials standing near a blast site while the second photo shows jawans carrying what appears to be a corpse on a stretcher. With the help of reverse image search and relevant keywords, we found the first picture published by the Associated Press . According to the AP, the image showed paramilitary troops standing near their damaged vehicle after Maoist insurgents bombed it in the Koraput district of Odisha on August 27, 2013. At least five people died and two others were wounded in the incident.
The first image shows security officials standing near a blast site while the second photo shows jawans carrying what appears to be a corpse on a stretcher.
With the help of reverse image search and relevant keywords, we found the first picture published by the Associated Press . According to the AP, the image showed paramilitary troops standing near their damaged vehicle after Maoist insurgents bombed it in the Koraput district of Odisha on August 27, 2013. At least five people died and two others were wounded in the incident.
We found the second photo in a Frontline report  from June 12, 2013. Per the report, the photo was from an attack in Chhattisgarh's Jheeram Ghati that took place on May 25, 2013. Twenty-seven people, including the state Congress president Nand Kumar Patel and policemen, were killed in the attack.
An India Today report  from 2014 also said the photograph was from the Jheeram Ghati case. While neither report mentioned the source of the photo, it clearly precedes the recent Dantewada attack by almost a decade. Photos from 2018
We found the third image showing a bombed vehicle in a report by The Telegraph published in 2018. According to this report , the third image of a shows a bus that was bombed by suspected Maoist insurgents in Chhattisgarh's Dantewada in November 2018. The Telegraph credited the image to ABP Live. The incident, where four civilians and a Central Industrial Security Force jawan were killed, took place a day before Prime Minister Narendra Modi's scheduled visit to the Jagdalpur district for an election campaign. The fourth picture of security officials inspecting the site of a blast was published by multiple media outlets including The Indian Express  and NDTV  in 2018. The photo was credited to the Press Trust of India. Per these reports, the photo was from the site of an IED or improvised explosive device blast in the Kistaram area of Chhattisgarh's Sukma district on March 13, 2018. We also found the same image on the PTI website . Photos from 2019 The fifth image showing scattered pieces of a bombed vehicle was shared by ANI on its Twitter account with similar other images on May 1, 2019. According to ANI, the image was from an IED blast by suspected Maoist insurgents in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra. The blast was executed on a police vehicle. Reportedly, 15 security men and a driver were killed in the incident. #UPDATE Maharashtra: 10 security personnel injured in an IED blast by naxals in Gadchiroli. The blast was executed by naxals on a police vehicle which was carrying 16 security personnel. pic.twitter.com/PXBJaqPuF1 — ANI (@ANI) May 1, 2019 advertisement The sixth and final image shows the mangled remains of a car. This image was used by The Indian Express and several other media organisations  in 2019. As per The Indian Express report , the photo was from a bomb blast by suspected Maoists in Chhattisgarh's Dantewada on April 9, 2019. The photo was credited to The India Express. Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Bheema Mandavi and five others, including police personnel, were killed in the attack. The victims were part of a convoy of BJP leaders who were involved in election campaigns for the Lok Sabha Elections 2019. Incidentally, a Mint report  on the attack contained a photo of the same mangled vehicle shot from a different angle. This photo was credited to the PTI. title: Fact Check: Photo of loco pilot holding umbrella inside engine is NOT from Kerala's first Vande Bharat
content:
Although leakage was reported in an AC vent in the Kasargod-Thiruvananthapuram Vande Bharat Express, the image is nearly six-years-old, and was shot inside a dead engine near Dhanbad, Jharkhand.
On April 25, PM Narendra Modi inaugurated India's 16th Vande Bharat Express, the Kasargod-Thiruvananthapuram Express in Kerala . The train's debut journey, however, faced some hitches — there were reports of water leakage on its first day  while it was parked at Kannur. Following this, many on social media shared a baffling photo of a loco pilot (train driver)  sitting inside a train's engine with an open umbrella in his hand. Allegedly, this was the loco pilot of Kerala's inaugural Vande Bharat journey using an umbrella to protect himself from the leaking water. One person tweeted, "Dear Narendra Modi please stop making things. Clearly you are utterly incapable to make anything right. 'VANDE BHARAT' on the 1st day of inauguration rainwater started leaking from the roof of VB in Kerala. A picture is worth a thousand words." Archived versions of such posts can be seen here  and here . Dear @narendramodi please stop making things. Clearly you are utterly incapable to make anything right. 🙄 "VANDE BHARAT" on the 1st day of inauguration rain water started leaking from the roof of VB in Kerala. A picture is worth a thousand words. #ModiFailsIndia pic.twitter.com/Vfsaq8qHYb — Hisamuddin Khan (@Hisamud47588796) April 27, 2023 A new technology in "VANDE BHARAT" under the leadership of Honourable PM Mudi. On the 1st day of inauguration, rainwater falls inside the train from the roof. Means even if you are inside train now you can enjoy outside nature. Thank you, H0rrible PM Mudiji... pic.twitter.com/2Khuyp5z4a — Брат (@B5001001101) April 27, 2023 India Today's investigation, however, found that the image in question is several years old and not related to Vande Bharat at all.  OUR PROBE A reverse image search of the viral photo led us to a video tweeted by journalist-activist Sucheta Dalal on August 9, 2017. This video featured the same loco pilot with an umbrella covering his head. Dalal tagged then-Railway Minister Suresh Prabhu and the Railway Ministry in that tweet. Railway safety? @sureshpprabhu and @RailMinIndia need to take a serious look without victimising whistleblower pic.twitter.com/Ue7rv0LwTP — Sucheta Dalal (@suchetadalal) August 9, 2017 In the video, a voice of a man, assumably, the assistant loco pilot can also be heard complaining about the poor working conditions. He appealed to viewers to widely share this video.  The first ever Vande Bharat Express, known earlier as "Train 18", was launched by PM Modi on February 15, 2019 , making it clear that the video can not be related to it. Where is the video from? An advanced search with a relevant time filter led us to news reports in The Indian Express  and India Times  featuring a similar image. Published on August 11, 2017, both mentioned that the video was captured near Dhanbad, Jharkhand. We also found an extended version of the same video uploaded to the YouTube channel of the Bengali news outlet Sangbad Pratidin. Around the 20 seconds timestamp of this video, the person behind the camera addresses the loco pilot as BK Mandal from Chandrapura, a town in Jharkhand's Bokaro district. We also noticed the station signage of "Bermo" at one minute 17-second timestamp of this video. The Bermo railway station  is in the Bokaro district of Jharkhand and falls under the Dhanbad railway division of the East-Central Railway zone. In subsequent searches, we also came across a tweet by the Ministry of Railways  responding to the viral video, clarifying that the engine was dead (non-working) and was being pulled by another engine in front, as seen in the video. We r really concerned,had enquired .The fact that it was dead(non working)engine hauled by another engine in the front,can be seen in video
— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia) August 9, 2017 What happened to Kerala's Vande Bharat? We looked at various news reports about the water leakage in Kerala's Vande Bharat Express. None of these reports contained any mention or images of the loco pilot sitting under an umbrella. Per reports in Asianet  and Mathrubhumi , the Kunnur district of Kerala witnessed heavy rains on April 25, the inaugural day of the Vande Bharat Express. That night, the leak was observed after the train arrived in Kannur from Kasaragod. Reportedly, the leak was found through the AC vent. The public relations officer of the Palakkad division, Devadhanam, confirmed to India Today that the leakage was in the AC vent and repair works were complete by April 26 morning. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Apr 27, 2023 18:28 IST

title: Fact Check: 'Desi' version of Hyperloop in Bengaluru? Find the truth behind the viral video here
content:
This video shows people dealing with traffic on a road undergoing pipeline construction in Thane, Maharashtra.
A video  making the rounds of social media shows people driving two-wheelers not on the road, but through a cylindrical structure by the side of it. Those sharing the video called this the " desi" version of a Hyperloop  — a futuristic mode of transportation that would theoretically allow passengers to travel in pods at over 700 miles an hour inside giant low-pressure tubes. India's first hyperloop opened at Bellandur !! 🤣🤣 #bengaluru pic.twitter.com/ejO2VPEIYZ — Dr. Karthikeyan Gokulachandran, IPS (@karthikeyangips) April 27, 2023 Sharing the video, many on social media platforms  claimed that this video is from Bengaluru's Bellandur. Archived versions of such posts can be found here  and here . India Today, in its investigation, however, found that this video shows people dealing with traffic on a road undergoing pipeline construction in Thane, Maharashtra. Our Probe A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report  about Mumbaikars finding an alternative to the Hyperloop. This report carried a screenshot from the video in question. According to the report dated April 27, 2023, bike riders in Thane passed through big pipes kept on the side of a road because of the traffic congestion. We then noticed a watermark on the viral video — "vishu_bhoir1111". Using this, we found an Instagram account with the same username  that belonged to Vishvajeet R. Bhoir. We found the viral video shared here, with the caption stating that it was shot on Bhiwandi-Kalyan road, Maharashtra.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Bhiwandi (@bhiwandicity) India Today reached out to Vishwajeet, who told us that he shot this video on April 20, 2023, in Thane, Maharashtra. He wanted to highlight the issue of daily traffic jams on Kalyan Shilphata Road near Desai village because of the ongoing pipeline construction work. "To avoid traffic, people in the area have resorted to travelling on the wrong side of the road through the huge pipes lying at the side," added Vishwajeet. He also shot another video from the same area and sent it to us along with its location which can be seen on Google Maps here . The Saamana e-newspaper  and local media outlet Lokmat Kalyan Dombivli  also shared the viral video, reporting about the traffic congestion. Thus, it is more than clear, that the viral video has nothing to do with Bengaluru. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Apr 30, 2023 17:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Did this man really walk on the water? Know the secret behind this miracle
content:
The video of a man walking on the water is not real, but a visual magic trick. There are a few ways this can be achieved.
The mythical superhuman task of "walking on water" has been a source of endless fascination since time immemorial. Many have tried to recreate this feat but with little success. But a strange video circulating on social media seems to suggest that someone may just have pulled it off. A Twitter user on April 28, 2023, while sharing the clip of a man visibly standing on the water in a swimming pool and then miraculously walking on the water , wrote, "The moment a man walked on water". The archived version of the tweet  can be seen here. India Today's investigation, however, found that this was a visual trick by Julius Dein, an internet celebrity who creates viral comedy and magic videos. Our Probe A reverse search of keyframes from the video led us to an Instagram account  with almost seven million followers. The account belonged to Julius Dein, a magician from London, UK, the man seen walking on water in the viral video. We also found the longer version  of the viral video, uploaded to his Instagram on May 25, 2021. We also found the same video on Dein's official Facebook account , posted on May 24, 2021. There, he wrote, "Magician Walks on Water!". The same video was also uploaded on his YouTube channel at the same time with the same title .     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Julius Dein (@juliusdein) Julius Dein  is a London-born magician. He has huge followers on Facebook , Instagram  and other social media platforms. title: Fact Check: Virat Kohli NOT banned in IPL 2023, misleading social media viral in anticipation
content:
He has not been banned yet. There are apprehensions that he may face a single-match ban if RCB continues to maintain a slow over-rate for the third match this season.
Has Virat Kohli, the Royal Challengers Bangalore stand-in skipper, been banned from the Indian Premier League 2023? Social media was recently flooded with claims suggesting just that. A postcard  going viral features a picture of Kohli alongside a stamp that says "banned". The postcard made in the breaking news format reads further, "Official news is yet to confirm what went wrong. Sources say Virat Kohli will miss..." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today's fact-check team, however, found that Kohli hasn't been banned yet. Merely apprehensions were made after his team maintained a slow over-rate for two matches. Our Probe If Kohli, the former captain of the Indian cricket team, were banned, it would have been all over the news. After attempting several rounds of keyword searches, we couldn't find any news suggesting the ban. We also checked the website and social media accounts of the Board of Control for Cricket in India. There too, we didn't find any mention or press release announcing a ban.
Has Virat Kohli, the Royal Challengers Bangalore stand-in skipper, been banned from the Indian Premier League 2023? Social media was recently flooded with claims suggesting just that.
A postcard  going viral features a picture of Kohli alongside a stamp that says "banned". The postcard made in the breaking news format reads further, "Official news is yet to confirm what went wrong. Sources say Virat Kohli will miss..."
India Today's fact-check team, however, found that Kohli hasn't been banned yet. Merely apprehensions were made after his team maintained a slow over-rate for two matches. Our Probe
If Kohli, the former captain of the Indian cricket team, were banned, it would have been all over the news. After attempting several rounds of keyword searches, we couldn't find any news suggesting the ban. We also checked the website and social media accounts of the Board of Control for Cricket in India. There too, we didn't find any mention or press release announcing a ban.
However, there were news reports  anticipating the punishment if the RCB continued with a slow pace of over. As per a Mint report , Kohli and the rest of the team received fines because of a slow over-rate (play extending 90 minutes) during the match against the Rajasthan Royals. The league fined the RCB captain Rs. 24 lakh, while each of the other team members received lesser fines. The Rules
According to The Times of India , IPL teams, while bowling, are expected to complete an inning in 90 minutes. Non-compliance with this is subject to fines. The captain of the side flouting this rule for the first time is fined Rs. 12 lakh.Â
When a team is found guilty of having maintained a slow over-rate for the second time in the same season, the captain is fined Rs. 24 lakh. The rest of the team is also fined (either Rs. 6 lakh or 25 per cent of their match fee, whichever is lesser). When a team is found guilty of having maintained a slow over rate for the third time in the same season, the captain is fined Rs. 30 lakh and handed a one-match ban. The rest of the team is penalised as well. But can Kohli get a ban? There is some uncertainty surrounding who would receive a one-match ban in the event of a slow over-rate by the RCB. Kohli was named the RCB's stand-in skipper for the game against the Punjab Kings in late April. Regular captain Faf du Plessis, according to Wisden , would bat but not field after sustaining an injury in his team's last match against Chennai Super Kings on April 17. advertisement Kohli, on April 26, said that the South African cricketer  might be back for the RCB's next game against the Lucknow Super Giants. "Faf will play the impact role again tonight. We are playing the same team as the last game. Hopefully, he will lead from the next game onwards but yeah tonight he will play the same role that he played in the last 2 games," Kohli said. Du Plessis, thus, may be punished for the transgression and not Kohli. We also spoke to Vikrant Gupta, the managing editor of Sports Tak, who said, "Virat will likely face a 'suspended ban' in case of dereliction for the third time. A suspended ban is different from an ordinary ban, in the sense that in the former case, the player can choose the match to serve the ban. It need not necessarily be the next match." Thus, it's clear that the postcard suggesting Virat Kohli getting banned in IPL is misleading. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: May 1, 2023 16:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Shocking video of man throwing goats from moving truck is NOT from Pakistan
content:
This incident happened in Maharashtra's Nashik. However, the exact date of the incident could not be determined.
A shocking video of a person throwing goats from a moving truck has been widely shared on social media. The video was captured by somebody driving behind the truck. After chucking several goats onto the road, the man could be seen climbing down to the bonnet of a car that had pulled up behind the truck. A person could be heard saying, "This is how they steal." Â
Those sharing it claimed it was from Pakistan and that the man in the video was stealing goats. A Twitter user wrote, "This video of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan clearly shows that Pakistan is a country of savages and there are a large number of savages who exist all over the world, especially in Western countries.
How can you understand that Pakistani Muslims can be human beings? Innocent goats." The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .Â
Some people also claimed that the video was from the Kanpur-Unnao highway and from Gujarat's Surat .Â
India Today found that the viral video was from Maharashtra's Nashik.Â
We noticed "Aurangabad" written on a green road sign visible in the viral video. These road signs are a common feature on Indian highways.  Â
We also noticed that reacting to a Twitter post which claims this video to be from the Kanpur-Lucknow highway, a person wrote that this incident happened in Maharashtra. Â
The Unnao Police also said in its response to the same tweet that this incident took place on Maharashtra's Igatpuri Ghoti road. Igatpuri is a town located in the Nashik district in Maharashtra, and Ghoti is a village in the same district. उपरोक्त वीडियो जनपद उन्नाव से संबन्धित न होकर महाराष्ट्र के इगतपुर घोटी रोड से संबन्धित है। कृपया बिना पुष्टि के भ्रामक पोस्ट न करें।

So, contacted India Today's Nashik correspondent Pravin Thakare, who confirmed that this video was indeed from Nashik. He also sent us an image from the same location. On comparing it with the viral video, we found many similarities. These included the green-coloured road sign, a small board with "PUC" written on it, and a triangular traffic sign. We were also able to geo-locate the exact location seen in the video. It can be seen below. Thakare also told us that this incident was not recent and had possibly happened a few months ago. Assistant Police Inspector Dilip Khedkar of the Ghoti police station told India Today that while he was aware of this incident, nobody had yet filed a complaint. He also could not pinpoint a date for the video. Thus, it's abundantly clear that the video is not from Pakistan at all. [Update: After this story was published, the Ghoti police registered an FIR against unknown persons for the goat theft seen in the video] Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: May 1, 2023 23:43 IST

title: Fact Check: These images are NOT from K-Pop star Moonbin's funeral
content:
These images were photoshopped to include Moonbin's photos. None of them are from the K-pop star's funeral.
On April 19, K-pop star Moonbin of the boyband ASTRO was found dead at his home in the Gangnam district of Seoul, South Korea, by his manager. According to the Gangnam police , authorities believe the 25-year-old died by suicide. However, no official cause of death was announced at the time of writing this.
Following Moonbin's death, fans across the globe expressed grief on social media. Among the many tweets and Facebook and Instagram posts about the pop star, were also some that allegedly contained photos from his funeral service.Â
One such post features five photos , one showing a funeral procession, and the others supposedly capturing people grieving Moonbin at his wake.Â
India Today found that these photos were not from Moonbin's funeral at all and that the K-pop star's photos were digitally added to them.
The first photo in the post shows a large procession on a road with a picture of Moonbin mounted on top of one of the cars. Several guards could also be seen marching along the road in the photo. With the help of a reverse image search, we found the original version of this photo on the website of the Associated Press . According to this site, the photo was shot during the funeral procession of former South Korean President Kim Dae-jung at the Seoul Plaza in Seoul on August 23, 2009. In the original image, it's a portrait of Kim Dae-jung mounted atop the car, not Moonbin. The second photo is that of a portrait of Moonbin on an altar, surrounded by bouquets of flowers. With the help of a reverse image search, we found that this photo was also edited. We found the original photo on Getty Images where it was credited to the Agence France-Presse. This photo featured a portrait of Kim Jong-hyun (known professionally as Jonghyun), the lead singer of the K-pop boy band SHINee, who reportedly died by suicide On December 18, 2017. The caption for the photo on Getty Images read, "The portrait of Kim Jong-hyun, a 27-year-old lead singer of the massively popular K-pop boyband SHINee, is seen on a mourning altar at a hospital in Seoul on December 19, 2017." The third and fourth photos show a grieving woman accompanied by South Korean singer Cha Eun-woo. In two of these photos, the woman can also be seen holding a portrait of Moonbin. We found that these photos were also edited and were actually from the funeral of Jonghyun. In the original photo, the woman was holding a portrait of Jonghyun, not Moonbin. The latter's photo was edited into these photos. We found original photos on Getty Images , published in 2017. The photos were credited to photographer Chung Sung-Jun. The caption to the images read, "Relatives weep during the funeral of Jonghyun of SHINee at the hospital on December 21, 2017, in Seoul, South Korea. The lead vocalist of the K-pop group was found dead, in what is believed to have been a suicide at his apartment on December 18." The fifth and final photo appears to show a woman hugging K-pop singer Cha Eun-woo. However, this photo was also digitally altered to include the singer's face. The original photo was published by Getty Images on July 2, 2010. advertisement The caption of the photo read, "South Korean actor So Ji-Sub weeps with relatives of late South Korean actor and singer Park Yong Ha during a funeral ceremony at Memorial Park on July 2, 2010, in Seongnam, South Korea. The Korean actor and singer was found dead in his home on June 30, 2010, after an apparent suicide attempt."  These photos were previously fact-checked by the AFP . As per reports , the family of Moonbin chose to keep his funeral private. It is hence clear that none of these images show the funeral ceremony of Moonbin. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: May 2, 2023 17:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Kamala Harris was NOT drunk! Edited video of US Vice President goes viral
content:
The audio in this clip was edited. It was taken from a clip shared by a supposed impersonator of Harris.
A viral video of United States Vice President Kamala Harris appears to show her delivering an incoherent, slurred speech. Many on social media shared the clip, mocking her and speculating if she was drunk during the event.Â
In the video, Harris is heard saying, "Today is today, and yesterday was today yesterday. Tomorrow will be today, tomorrow. So live today, so the future today will be as the past today, as it is tomorrow." The archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today found that the video in question was edited. The voice in the video is not of Harris but of an impersonator.
In the video in question, we noticed people holding placards that said the words "Reproductive Freedom". Taking cue from this, we ran a keyword search and found the original video shared by the Facebook page of a nonprofit organisation called NARAL Pro-Choice America on April 26. According to the page, the video was from a speech made by Harris at a reproductive rights rally held at Howard University in Washington DC on April 25.Â
At no point during this speech, did we hear Harris making the incomprehensible statement heard in the viral clip. Instead, the Vice President spoke about the importance of reproductive freedom. She also spoke about running for re-election alongside US President Joe Biden. The original video was also uploaded to the YouTube channel of the New York Post on April 26, 2023. In fact, the viral clip appeared to be an audio-edited version of the video shared by the New York Post. We also found the transcript of the Vice President's speech on the White House website. No sentence in this transcript matched the words in the viral video. We also noticed that in the original video, the text on Harris' podium read, "Fighting for Reproductive Freedom." However, in the viral video, the text on the podium read: "Ramble Rants Reproductive Freedom." Using this clue, we found that the edited video was shared by a Twitter account called "Ramble Rants" whose bio mentioned "MAGA", the election slogan popularised by former US President Donald Trump during the 2016 presidential elections. The account posted the edited video on April 29. The next day, the account clarified that the tweet was a meme and shared a video of a supposed Kamala Harris impersonator. The audio in that clip was the same as the viral video. Here's the @mommyrn88 impression I used for the meme 😂😂 😂 https://t.co/MoX4EXsyL9 — Ramble_Rants (@ramble_rants) April 30, 2023 It is hence clear that the viral video was edited and doesn't show a real speech made by the US Vice President. title: Fact Check: US Press Sec prioritises press conference over wife's death? 2008 satire video fools people
content:
This video is a work of fiction made by a satirical website called The Onion.
A video making the rounds on social media shows a US Deputy Press Secretary allegedly holding a press conference at the White House right after losing his wife to a tragic accident. Many on social media were stunned to see the man dodging questions from reporters about his dead wife to prioritise the US President's agenda and issues of national significance. An archived version of this post can be seen here . advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today, in its investigation, found that this video was made by The Onion, a satirical news website. It's not a real incident. Our Probe A keyword search for the supposed Deputy Press Secretary, Theodore Barrett, as mentioned in the viral video, fetched multiple articles stating that there isn't and was never a Deputy Press Secretary in the White House  by that name . Further searches led us to an extended version of the viral clip shared in March 2008 by The Onion. The Onion is a satirical news website based in Chicago that has more than 20 million followers across the world. Its satirical news reports are often taken seriously, and this has thus resulted in the creation of the subreddit " Ate The Onion ", which chronicles social media users who fall for obviously satirical headlines. We found several other videos of this "Theodore Barrett", a character created by The Onion, holding press conferences on its official YouTube channel. One video from December 2008 shows a press conference held by Barrett in a similar fashion - this time about the President's strategy to defeat a monster seen in Manhattan. Another showed him speaking gibberish while answering questions from reporters about the President's stance on the Medicare Reform Bill.  The Onion also created the character of Deputy Press Secretary Debra Browning, and here is a satirical news video featuring her. We noticed the reporters seen in this video are exactly the same people, sitting in the same order, and performing the same actions as seen in the viral clip. A comparison between the two can be seen below. Per the archives of the White House , in 2008, when George W Bush was the President of the United States, Dana Perino was the Press Secretary, and Tony Fratto, Scott Stanzel, and Gordon Johndroe did press briefings as Deputy Press Secretaries. Thus, it's clear that people fell for a 2008 satirical news report. (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: May 3, 2023 16:24 IST

If Pappu Yadav had been attacked0 following his remarks against Yogi Adityanath, it would have made the news. But, several rounds of searches with relevant keywords did not lead us to any such news report.
As the logo of The Quint Hindi was visible in the viral video, we searched its YouTube channel and found that this video was uploaded on September 6, 2018.Â
The video description mentioned that the then MP of Madhepura, Bihar, alleged that protestors attacked him during a Bharat Bandh organised by upper-caste communities. Thus, we could verify that this video was unrelated to his recent remarks on the UP CM.
 A subsequent search led us to several reports in ABP Live , Zee News  and Amar Ujala  about the alleged attack. Per them, it took place in Bihar's Muzaffarpur. Yadav's cavalcade was allegedly attacked in the Sadar area of the Khabra village in Muzaffarpur amid a Bharat Bandh called by several organisations against amendments in the SC and ST Act.Â
A Jagran report  from September 7, 2018, however, contradicted what Yadav claimed and quoted the police denying any such attack. It also examined videos from the spot and concluded that Yadav was lying.Â
Although we did not independently verify what actually happened in Muzaffarpur in September 2018, it is evident that the video is not recent and not from Prayagraj. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: May 3, 2023 21:33 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT the underwater wreckage of Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 that disappeared in 2014
content:
Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, which disappeared in 2014, remains untraced to date. These images show parts of an old aircraft that was deliberately sunk in the Red Sea for ecotourism purposes.
In 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 disappeared from the radar with 239 passengers and crew members on board while flying from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. At the time, then prime minister Najib Razak had announced that investigation and analysis concluded that the flight likely ended up in a remote part of the southern Indian Ocean.Â
An enduring mystery of our time, the disappearance of the flight has often been at the centre of conspiracy theories. Recently, photos of an abandoned plane underwater have been circulating on social media. Many have claimed that this was the wreckage of the missing Malaysian aircraft.Â
One such post reads , "Malaysia Airplane MH370 that disappeared 9 years ago has been found under ocean with no human skeleton. The plane had 239 passengers on board." The archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today, in its investigation, found that the images in question show parts of an old aircraft that was deliberately sunk off the coast of Jordan to create an artificial reef. Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 remains untraced to date.Â
First, we could not find any credible news reports which confirmed that Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 was found. The fight's disappearance caused shockwaves across the globe and the discovery of its wreckage would have made headlines everywhere.Â
With the help of a reverse image search and relevant keywords, we found an Instagram video that contained shots that matched the viral photos of the aircraft. The video was uploaded to the Instagram profile of Deep Blue Dive Center, a scuba-diving centre based in the Jordanian port city of Aqaba.
"Tristar Airplane Wreck Red Sea, Aqaba JO," read the caption of the video.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Deep Blue Dive Center (@deepbluedivecenter)
A post shared by Deep Blue Dive Center (@deepbluedivecenter)
According to the website of this scuba-diving company, the aircraft is an old Lockheed Martin L1011 TriStar that was intentionally sunk in the waters of the Red Sea next to the King Abdullah Reef dive site in Aqaba, Jordan.
The plane was a non-Jordanian commercial aircraft that had been out of service and remained parked at the King Hussein International Airport for several years. The Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority purchased the plane and sank it in the Red Sea's Gulf of Aqaba to create an artificial diving site.
CNN reported this in 2022. According to this article, the abandoned jet was sunk in 2019 to create an artificial reef to encourage marine life. The report added that having remained underwater for so long, the plane's wings now sheltered numerous soft corals and the fuselage was surrounded by huge sponges populated by a variety of sea life. We also found videos of this plane uploaded by many divers on YouTube. Â It is hence clear that the photos in circulation are of an aircraft that was intentionally sunk in the Red Sea for ecotourism and are not related to the Malaysian flight that went missing in 2014. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: May 3, 2023 22:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Fake screenshot of NDTV opinion poll predicting historic Congress victory in Karnataka goes viral
content:
This is a fake screenshot. NDTV has not published any such opinion poll.
With the Karnataka assembly elections right around the corner, the internet right now is flooded with opinion polls full of myriad projections about which party might rule the southern state. Members and supporters of the state's two major parties, the Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party, of course, have shared various opinion polls favouring each.Â
One post that's been widely shared in the midst of this is a screenshot of what is being touted as an opinion poll by NDTV. The NDTV Poll of Polls, the supposed opinion poll, predicted a "historic victory" for the Congress party, projecting the party's seat share would range between 131 and 142.
A Twitter user while sharing a screenshot of this purported opinion poll wrote, "BREAKING NOW - KARNATAKA ELECTIONS. Most Opinion Polls are unanimously predicting that in Karnataka, BJP is staring at their biggest defeat due to huge anti-incumbency against 40% Commission govt." The archived version of such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today found that the viral screenshot is fake and misleading. NDTV's Poll of Polls is, in fact, an exit poll, which is published once the election concludes.
A keyword search for NDTV's Poll of Polls for the Karnataka assembly elections in 2023 yielded no result. This raised doubts about the veracity of the screenshot.Â
We then ran a Twitter advanced search using relevant keywords combined with its Twitter handle @ndtv. Again, we failed to find any tweet announcing such an opinion poll for Karnataka. Next, we went through NDTV's recent tweets and found that the media organisation had clarified that the viral screenshot was fake.Â
The outlet, while sharing the viral screenshot with a warning label that said, "Fake", wrote in the tweet: "Fake Tweet Alert | False posts on NDTV Poll of Poll tracker for Karnataka, being widely circulated, are misleading. Watch this space for the real #PollOfExitPolls on May 10th evening."
That means, Poll of Polls, which was pitched as an opinion poll, is indeed an exit poll, which is yet to be announced.
The Election Commission, from time to time, issues notifications prohibiting the conducting of exit polls, and publishing the result of any exit poll during the period starting from the commencement of polls till half an hour after the closing of the poll.Â
Thus, it's clear that NDTV's opinion poll did not project a massive Congress victory in Karnataka. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 4, 2023 03:51 IST

title: Fact Check: No 'Love Jihad' — this Muslim man did not kill his wife for being Hindu, they are both Muslim
content:
While it is true that the man killed his wife, she was Muslim, not Hindu. This was confirmed by the woman's family and the Bihar police.
A video of a young man confessing to murdering his wife has gone viral on social media. The video is that of an interview, during which, he is asked why he did so. To this, the man can be seen saying killed his wife in reverence of "Khuda" or God. He said that he killed his wife after a year of marriage four days ago. He added that he did it because it was a matter of Islam's honour. He declared that he was not in love with his wife, rather he was in love with Islam. The words, "He killed his wife because she was a Hindu," appeared in the video as he confessed to his alleged crime. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The video ended with a montage of photos of women, who were all purported victims of "Love Jihad", a far-right conspiracy theory that alleges Muslim men lure Hindu women into marrying them and subsequently convert them to Islam. "How proudly he is saying that he K!lled [sic] his wife just because she was Hindu," said a tweet containing the video. At the time of writing this, the tweet had been retweeted by more than 2,800 people. The archived version of the tweet can be seen here . How proudly he is saying that he K!lled his wife just because she was Hindu Watch and share 👇 pic.twitter.com/0Z2LtYa0uu — Maarwadi🚩🚩 (@Marwadi99) May 2, 2023

He said that he killed his wife after a year of marriage four days ago. He added that he did it because it was a matter of Islam's honour. He declared that he was not in love with his wife, rather he was in love with Islam. The words, "He killed his wife because she was a Hindu," appeared in the video as he confessed to his alleged crime.Â
The video ended with a montage of photos of women, who were all purported victims of "Love Jihad", a far-right conspiracy theory that alleges Muslim men lure Hindu women into marrying them and subsequently convert them to Islam.
"How proudly he is saying that he K!lled [sic] his wife just because she was Hindu," said a tweet containing the video. India Today's investigation found the man did not kill his wife for being Hindu, as the victim was also Muslim.Â
According to the viral post, the man in the video said that he killed his wife because she was Hindu. However, nowhere in the video did he make such a statement.Â
Upon reviewing the video, we noticed the logo of "Insaaf 24" on the microphone used by the interviewer. When we checked the social media accounts of the channel, we found a longer version of the same interview shared on its Facebook page. In this video, the man accused of murder identified himself as Mahbub from the Bangra village in the Samastipur district of Bihar. In the extended interview as well, there was no mention of the wife being Hindu.Â
India Today then reached out to Avinash Kumar, the SHO of the Bangra police station. Dismissing the viral claim, the officer said that both the accused and the victim were Muslims. "The husband's name was Mahbub Alam and the wife was 22-year-old Yasmeen. Both were Muslims and they were married per Islamic rituals," the inspector said.
India Today then spoke to Yasmeen's mother, who confirmed that they are a Muslim family. According to her, Yasmeen was killed on April 14, and she was pregnant at the time of her death. The First Information Report  was also filed on the same date.Â
India Today also obtained a copy of Mahbub and Yasmeen's marriage certificate, as well as Yasmeen's Aadhaar card. In the marriage document, Yasmeen's name was mentioned as Yasmeen Khatoon, daughter of Gaffar Nawab. The Aadhaar card mentions only Yasmeen as her name. The murder In the viral video, Mahbub said that he killed his wife for the sake of Islam's honour. However, there have been conflicting testimonies in this regard. When India Today asked SHO Avinash Kumar about the motive behind the murder, he said that Mahbub was "fully mental". Kumar said that Mahbub had fatally beaten Yasmeen (though the postmortem report is yet to be presented) and in the aftermath, he was caught and restrained by his neighbours, who called the police. The SHO added that even according to the neighbours, Mahbub was mentally unstable. However, he also said that no psychiatric examination had yet been conducted. Pressed further about the motive, Kumar told India Today that Yasmeen's family had alleged that she was killed over dowry demands. And according to the FIR as well, police have registered a case against Mahbub and five of his family members for dowry death under Sections 304 (B) and 34 of the Indian Penal Code. Mahbub's family, per the SHO, is absconding. Yasmeen's family disputes the mental illness angle. Speaking to India Today, Yasmeen's father Abdul Gaffar Nadaf dismissed it and said that they would have never wedded their daughter to him had he been of unsound mind, further adding that they would not have let Yasmeen stay with him had they discovered this later. He also said that Mahbub had demanded an LCD TV, a motorcycle, an almirah, and Rs. 2 lakh in cash as part of the dowry, sometime before Yasmeen's murder. These allegations were also repeated by Yasmeen's mother Obila. Thus, it is clear that the man in the viral video did not murder his wife for being Hindu. Both the alleged murderer and the victim are Muslim. Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: May 4, 2023 20:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Alia Bhatt perform at Met Gala afterparty? 2017 video viral again with dubious claim
content:
This video shows Bhatt's performance at the 2017 IIFA Awards.
Bollywood actor Alia Bhatt made her grand Met Gala debut on May 1, 2023, at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York . She wore a white dress adorned with one lakh pearls designed by fashion designer Prabal Gurung, who attended the event along with her.Â
Following this event, a video featuring the "Gangubai Kathiawadi" actor made the rounds on social media. In it , Bhatt could be on stage, seen wearing a pink top and blue jeans, rapping the popular song "Kar Gayi Chull" from her 2016 film "Kapoor & Sons". Background dancers behind her were dressed in black and neon green. Sharing the video, one person tweeted, "Alia Bhatt performing at the Met Gala afterparty." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here.
India Today's investigation, however, found that the video is not related to the Met Gala at all. It shows Alia Bhatt's performance during the 2017 IIFA Awards ceremony. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the video led us to the verified Facebook page of the International Indian Film Academy or IIFA . We found a 54-second-long similar clip shared there on June 11, 2018, with the caption, "Alia Bhatt - IIFA 2017". In this video, Bhatt could be seen in the same attire with the same background dancers, grooving to various songs, including the one in the viral clip. However, in this video, she couldn't be heard rapping.Â
A further search led us to a video news story published on News18's Facebook page on January 5, 2023. We found the viral video there, with a caption that read, "Alia Bhatt Rapping at Old IIFA Awards Gets Brutally Roasted". The description of the video also stated that this was Bhatt's performance at the 2017 IIFA Awards.
Many media outlets like MensXP , iDiva also reported on this 2017 performance.
We found a video posted by the Metropolitan Museum of Art on Instagram. The caption on the post read, "Art imitating life or life imitating art? Did you know: During the Met Gala, guests are invited to explore the Costume Institute exhibition - this year that's 'Karl Lagerfeld: A Line of Beauty,' on view through July 15." In that video, Alia Bhatt can be seen checking out the exhibit along with designer Prabal Gurung.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by The Metropolitan Museum of Art (@metmuseum)
A post shared by The Metropolitan Museum of Art (@metmuseum)
It's been reported that Bhatt may have skipped the Met Gala Afterparty and returned to India . Apart from Bhatt, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Isha Ambani, and Natasha Poonawalla attended the prestigious event. However, we couldn't find any news reports on these celebrities performing at the Met Gala afterparty.
Thus, it is safe to conclude that the viral video is not Alia Bhatt's performance at the Met Gala afterparty. The video shows her performance at IIFA Awards 2017.  Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: May 4, 2023 22:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Old gunfire video passed off as Manipur violence amid riots in the NE state
content:
This video is old and has no connection with the ongoing violence in Manipur. It's been on the internet since as early as July 2020.
The Manipur government on May 4 issued a shoot-at-sight order in "extreme cases" to contain escalating violence in the state reportedly between tribals and the majority Meitei community. Fifty-five columns of the Army and Assam Rifles have also reportedly been deployed to contain widespread rioting. Amid this, a video showing three people continuously firing bullets at nighttime has gone viral on social media. Many people are linking this video to the ongoing clashes in Manipur. A Twitter user  shared the viral video and wrote, "Here is a video of Kuki people firing's shots at Meitei people. Is this what you guys called a peace rally and trying to be the victim". Violence erupted in Manipur after a tribal solidarity march was organised on May 3 by the All-Tribal Students' Union Manipur against the demand for inclusion of the Meitei community in the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category. While Meitei  is the predominant ethnic group in Manipur, Kuki is one of the biggest tribes in the state. Both Meitei and Kuki are accusing each other of violence. Prashant Anand, the coordinator to Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge also shared this video , linking it to the recent violence in Manipur. The archived version of both these claims can be seen here  and here . India Today found that the video has been present on the internet since as early as July 2020 and is not related to the current unrest in Manipur. Our Probe On reverse searching keyframes from the viral video, we found that the clip was shared on Twitter on April 29, 2023. Upon going through the profile of the person who shared it, we found that they regularly share videos of gunfire. Vou postar + videos assim no @lovearmasvideos toda semana, sigam lá tbm✌️ pic.twitter.com/wbL5lhZwmI — I Love Armas (@Ilovearmas_) April 28, 2023 We also found this video in an Instagram post  dated July 5, 2020. title: Fact Check: This tractor march was NOT in support of the wrestlers' protest in Jantar Mantar
content:
This video is from a 2021 march held by the Kerala Youth Congress in Pallakad in support of the farmers' protest.
A day after the Delhi Police clashed with protesting wrestlers at Jantar Mantar , people from various walks of life, including farmers, went to the protest site on May 4 to show support for the wrestlers. Indian professional wrestlers have been sitting in protest since April 23, demanding the arrest of Wrestling Federation of India president Brij Bhushan over sexual harassment charges. Members of Khap Panchayats, who were attempting to join the wrestlers' protest, were stopped by the police at the Singhu border. Bharatiya Kishan Union leader Abhimanyu Kohar and his supporters were reportedly detained by the police. Amid these developments, a video of a large tractor rally has been widely shared on social media. Allegedly, this was the farmers' rally on its way to Jantar Mantar in support of the protesting wrestlers. In the video, tricolour flags can be seen attached to the tractors. The video was shared by the Facebook page of the Delhi Pradesh Youth Congress . Deepak Khatri, a National Coordinator for social media for the Congress party also shared the video. While he later deleted it, his tweet was shared by several people including Prateek Singh , the Rajasthan state spokesperson for the grand old party. The archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here . India Today, in its investigation, found that the video shows a tractor rally held by the Kerala Youth Congress in support of the farmers' protest in 2021. Our Probe The logo of the Malayalam news channel Manorama News can be seen at the bottom left corner of the video, and the word "Rally" is written in Malayalam on a white poster fixed in front of several tractors, indicating that the video is from Kerala. A keyword search in Malayalam on Facebook led us to an extended version of the same video shared on the Facebook page of Manorama News on January 3, 2021. Per this post , the video was from a Kisan March held by Youth Congress workers in support of the farmers' protest that was happening in Delhi against the three farm laws at the time. In this version of the video, Kerala Congress MLAs Shafi Parambil and KS Sabarinadhan could be seen. A video from the rally was also shared by Sabarinadhan on January 2, 2021. "Youth Congress Kisan March," the MLA wrote while sharing the video . Parambil also shared a photo  from the rally on January 3, 2021, thanking the public for its solidarity towards the farmers' protest. Multiple media reports from Kerala that were published on March 3, 2021, also contained images  from the rally that resembled the video. Per these reports, the Jai Kisan March was organised by the Youth Congress State Committee in the Palakkad district of Kerala on January 2, 2021. Srinivas BV, the National President of the Indian Youth Congress inaugurated the concluding session of the March. Videos from the march  and the concluding session were also shared on the Facebook account of Srinivas BV.  In them, Congress leaders could be heard speaking in support of the farmers' protest. It is hence clear the viral video is from a 2021 rally held in support of the farmers' protest. It has nothing to do with the ongoing protest by Indian wrestlers in Jantar Mantar. (With inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: May 5, 2023 16:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of immigrants crossing Morocco-Spain border FALSELY shared as US refugee crisis
content:
This video is old and has no connection with the US-Mexico border whatsoever. The footage shows sub-Saharan immigrants scaling the Melilla border fence that runs between Spain and Morocco in March 2022.
Unsettling photos of the lifeless body of a 3-year-old Syrian refugee Aylan Kurdi lying face down on a Turkish beach still serve as a stark reminder of how the world continues to ignore the plight of refugees. Now, similar distressing visuals of a large number of people climbing and attempting to cross over a wired fence have gone viral. Many on social media are calling it a mass attempt to cross the US border, presumably from Mexico.
A Twitter user, while sharing the video that seems to have emerged from TikTok, wrote how the U.S. Border now resembled a scene from "The Walking Dead", the popular zombie apocalypse TV show. The archived version of such posts can be seen here and here . The U.S. Border looks like a scene from the walking dead... #TheMoreYouKnow #Thursday pic.twitter.com/cJACIWYpaK — ⚖️The Justice Team⚖️ (@LawDog323E) May 4, 2023
The U.S. Border looks like a scene from the walking dead... #TheMoreYouKnow #Thursday pic.twitter.com/cJACIWYpaK — ⚖️The Justice Team⚖️ (@LawDog323E) May 4, 2023
India Today's investigation found that the viral video is not from the US-Mexico border at all. The footage shows immigrants scaling the Melilla border fence that runs between Melilla, a Spanish city in North Africa, and Morocco in March 2022.
Upon carefully examining the viral video, we saw a security force patrolling the area. We looked for the insignia visible on the uniforms and found that these people were part of the Spanish police. This provided us with the necessary hint that the incident was possibly from somewhere in Spain. Then, we performed a reverse search of keyframes from the video, combined with relevant keywords. This led us to a report by El Periodico , a Spanish daily, published on March 2, 2022. The report carried an extended version of the viral video and reported that around 2,500 sub-Saharan immigrants participated in a mass attempt to cross over into Spanish territory.
Then, we performed a reverse search of keyframes from the video, combined with relevant keywords. This led us to a report by El Periodico , a Spanish daily, published on March 2, 2022. The report carried an extended version of the viral video and reported that around 2,500 sub-Saharan immigrants participated in a mass attempt to cross over into Spanish territory.
In the longer video, a large number of immigrants who successfully managed to cross into the Spanish city of Melilla could be seen breaking into joy on the streets. The report stated that 491 immigrants managed to cross the barbed fences that run between Spain and Morocco. Other media organisations also reported this. The report also featured a photo that showed just how massive this attempt was to break through to the other side. In the photo, a huge line of immigrants on the Moroccan side could be seen waiting for their turn to jump the fence.
The Melilla border fence is around 12 kilometres long and is one of the two borders that separate the European Union and Africa, the other being Ceuta, also a Spanish enclave.Â
We hovered along the road in front of the fence using Street View on Google Maps, which was available throughout the length of the border. The exercise helped us successfully geolocate the location seen in the viral clip. The relevant patches of the road can be seen here and here . We also compared various elements seen in the viral video with the Street View of the area. A comparison can be seen below. Thus, it's clear that an old video of a wave of migrants trying to scale the high border fence between Spain and Morocco is being falsely shared as a US border situation. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: May 5, 2023 19:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Looting in Manipur stores? This video has nothing to do with ongoing violence in the state
content:
This video has been on the internet since as early as February. According to media reports, it shows a thrift store in Lucena City, Philippines.
Violence broke out in Manipur on May 3 after the Naga and Kuki tribes organised a Tribal Solidarity March against the move to give Scheduled Tribe status to the majority Metei community. Reportedly, protesters vandalised and set ablaze hundreds of houses, churches, temples, and vehicles during the violence. As armed forces were rushed into the state, the Manipur DGP said that protestors looted arms and ammunition from 23 sensitive police stations in the Imphal Valley and other districts.
However, some viral posts on social media claimed that people were also looting shops amid the violent protests in Manipur. The Aam Aadmi Party's person in charge for North Eastern states, Rajesh Sharma, tweeted a video of a group of men thronging inside what appears like a clothing store and racing to loot the wares. "BJP is a failed govt in Manipur, its responsibility of govt to save property & lives of people? Shame on BJP," wrote Sharma.
The archived version of his post can be seen here .
India Today's investigation found that the video is old and has been on the internet since as early as February this year. According to media reports, it's from the Philippines.
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the same video was shared by Yahoo News on March 1. Per this report, the video was from a secondhand goods store in Lucena City in the Philippines. Reportedly, a crowd poured into the shop during a special sale on February 24.
A search on YouTube with relevant keywords led to the same video uploaded by Vice News  on March 3. Per this report, the video was from a kind of thrift store in Lucena City.
According to Vice News, the shop announced new arrivals on February 24, and following this, a large number of people camped outside the shop even before its doors opened. The report also quoted the owner of the shop, Mildred Garcia Bundialan, who said that though she was used to customers' excitement whenever new arrivals were announced, the wildly excited crowd who appeared outside her store on February 24 surprised her.
The video was also shared by media organisations from the Philippines with the same description . Some of these organisations credited the video to a Facebook account called Mildred Ukay Suki. This account shared the same video  on February 24.
In Mildred's post as well, the location of the video mentioned was Lucena City.
According to her Facebook bio, Mildred is the owner of a store called Ukay Suki. She also posted similar videos of frenzied customers at the same shop on more than one occasion.
It is hence clear that the video in question is old and likely from the Philippines, though we could not independently verify that. It is not related to the ongoing violence in Manipur. Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 5, 2023 22:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Prakash Raj tell people not to vote for Congress in Karnataka polls? Viral clip is from 2019
content:
The video has clipped out of context and has nothing to do with the upcoming Karnataka Assembly Elections.
In the run-up to the Karnataka Assembly election 2023, actor Prakash Raj and politician courted controversy after he shared a photo comparing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adolf Hitler. In its aftermath, a video of Raj attacking the Congress party has been widely shared on social media. In that video, the actor can be heard saying, "So don't waste your vote on Congress. I did not join any political party. I am an independent. I seriously take offence to this dirty politics stooping down by the Congress". Sharing the video , one person tweeted, "Dear Karnataka, Prakasha has asked you all to NOT waste your votes on Congress. He is offended by the dirty politics of Congress party. So please vote for BJP." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here . Another person tweeted the video and wrote , "Big message Came From @prakashraaj Ji," alongside the hashtag "KarnatakaAssemblyElection". One sarcastic tweet containing the video read , "Prakash Raj uncle campaigning for BJP He blocked me ..tell him he is also our campaigner". The archived versions of these tweets can be seen here  and here . India Today's investigation found that the video is not related to the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections at all. OUR PROBE On the Twitter account of the actor , we found the longer version of the viral video there, shared on April 17, 2019 . This made it clear that the tweet had nothing to do with the upcoming polls in Karnataka. His tweet read, "FAKE NEWS by CONGRESS. Look at the dirty politics of this party. SHAME ON CONGRESS HAVE SENT THE COMPLAINT TO ELECTION COMMISSION WITH PROOF. Please spread and share to counter DIRTY POLITICS." In that video, the actor alleged that Congress was spreading misinformation about him. He said, "Look at the dirty politics the congress is doing in Bangalore Central. A man who claims to be Rizwan's PA, his name is Mazhar Ahmed. I am an independent. I seriously take offence to this dirty politics stooping down by the Congress party and Rizwan. I have given an election complaint and please don't believe in such rumours". FAKE NEWS by CONGRESS.. look at the dirty politics of this party. SHAME ON CONGRESS.. HAVE SENT THE COMPLAINT TO ELECTION COMMISSION WITH PROOF ..please spread and share to counter DIRTY POLITICS pic.twitter.com/4hjAibE2vg — Prakash Raj (@prakashraaj) April 17, 2019 Media outlets like the Deccan Herald  and Jagran  reported on this at the time. Prakash Raj contested the 2019 Lok Sabha elections from the Bangalore Central seat , as an independent candidate and Rizwan Arshad was the Congress candidate. Thus, the full version of the viral video makes it clear that Prakash Raj spoke about misinformation being spread using his name and photo back in 2019 — and therefore nothing to do with the Assembly polls in Karnataka. Published By: Ritika Shah Published On: May 8, 2023 14:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of burqa-clad women fighting in Saudi FALSELY shared as Karnataka incident
content:
This video is more than five years old, and was reportedly shot in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia.
In India, brawls in the middle of a road are not a rare sight at all. But a group of women, all clad in burqas, fighting with each other is not something one sees every day. In a video that's been widely shared, the women could be seen fighting each other so aggressively that one of them even drops her child mid-brawl. #BreakingNews No.1 Video from Bengaluru WTF Aunty G Abdul wife What did this kid do to you 😒 Kill each other no issue but what's this kid fault ?? "Kerala Story"matty taylor #Coronation #KarnatakaAssemblyElection #IPL2023 pic.twitter.com/N9JPWljsvg — SNEHA TIWARI (@iam_tiwari) May 6, 2023 Many who shared this video  claimed that this video was from Bangalore, Karnataka. Its archived version can be seen here . India Today's investigation found that the video is from Saudi Arabia and is several years old. Our Probe Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across an extended version of the same video. This appeared to have been shot inside a car. Uploaded to YouTube on September 15, 2018, we noticed in this video multiple cars in transit that featured Urdu or Arabic letters on their number plates. Using this as a clue, we searched with some advanced keywords and found several news reports from 2018 that featured screenshots from the same video. Russian state-owned news agency Sputnik  published a report on September 12, 2018, stating that the incident took place in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh. This report, however, did not mention the exact date or location of the brawl  Subsequently, we found similar reports about this brawl published in the Daily Mail , the Mirror  and The Sun  around the same time. None of the reports, however, contained any other details about the video. So, while we could not independently verify where the video was shot, it is more than safe to conclude that it is not from Bengaluru. ALSO READ | Fact Check: Did Prakash Raj tell people not to vote for Congress in Karnataka polls?
