title: Fact Check: Did Andrew Tye quit IPL citing lack of healthcare in India? Old quote viral out of context
content:
These comments by Andrew Tye are two years old. Tye isn't part of the ongoing IPL season.
Has Australian cricketer Andrew Tye quit the Indian Premier League? Some social media posts seem to suggest so. One such post — a Reel featuring a photo of Tye  wearing the Rajasthan Royals jersey and Hindi text — claims that the fast bowler left the IPL midway and returned home, saying, "I don't understand how Indian companies and government can spend so much money on the IPL when people there need hospitals." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this incident is a couple of years old and Tye is not part of the ongoing IPL season at all. OUR PROBE
We searched for news reports regarding this but found nothing recent. However, we found reports from April 2021 that quoted the cricketer making a similar remark. A report in The Economic Times  from April 26, 2021, mentioned that Tye, who was playing for the Rajasthan Royals at the time, opted out from the tournament amid rising Covid-19 deaths in India.
It is also worth mentioning that a big chunk of IPL 2021 matches were held in the United Arab Emirates in the wake of the Covid-19 surge in India. Per this report, Tye was quoted saying, "Looking at it from an Indian point of view, how are these companies and franchises spending so much money, and the government, on the IPL when there's people not being able to get accepted into hospital?"
"If sport can continue and be one of those avenues to relieve stress or give a glimmer of hope that the world is OK and there is light at the end of the tunnel, I think it should go ahead," he added.Â
Per an NDTV report  from the time, Tye decided to leave as he feared getting "locked out" of his own country amid rising Covid-19 cases. IS TYE PART OF THIS IPL SEASON?
A subsequent search with keywords took us to an India Today report from December 23, 2022, that featured a list of unsold players at the mini-auction for IPL 2023. With a base price of Rs. 1 crore, Andrew Tye was mentioned in the list of unsold overseas players. He last played for the Lucknow Super Giants  in the IPL in 2022.Â
Thus, it is evident that the comments by the Australian cricketer are two years old and not related to the ongoing IPL season. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: May 9, 2023 15:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of J-K chopper crash survivors FALSELY shared as Rajasthan MiG-21 crash aftermath
content:
This video shows survivors of a May 4 chopper crash in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district.
A video  making the rounds on social media shows injured flight crew members in a mountainous terrain being tended to by civilians and military personnel. Allegedly, these were the survivors of the May 8 MiG-21 crash in Rajasthan's Hanumangarh. Three people died  in this incident after debris from the crashed jet fell on them.Â
Text in video read , "MIG-21 aircraft crashed in Suratgarh during training."
India Today's investigation found that this video shows the survivors of a recent helicopter crash in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district. OUR PROBE
We noticed that in the comments section of the Instagram post, some people pointed out that this place could not be Suratgrah in Rajasthan since the terrain there was not mountainous.Â
Another person wrote that this video was from the recent helicopter crash in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar. Subsequent searches online led us to the YouTube channel of Greater Kashmir that had shared an extended version of this video on May 4. The video was titled, "Residents come to rescue of pilots, technician after army chopper crash lands in Kishtwar."Â
Subsequent searches online led us to the YouTube channel of Greater Kashmir that had shared an extended version of this video on May 4. The video was titled, "Residents come to rescue of pilots, technician after army chopper crash lands in Kishtwar."Â
Screams could be heard in this version of the video. A water body could also be seen in it. Also, in this video, another person could be seen lying on the ground, apparently unconscious. Â
The Northern Command of the Indian Army tweeted  a screenshot from this video on May 6, 2023, and thanked the residents of the Machhna village in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district for helping in the rescue operation after an army chopper crashed there. As per the tweet, the area in the video was located near the banks of River Marua in Kishtwar.Â
India Today's Kishtwar correspondent Kuldeep Sharma also confirmed that this video was indeed from Kishtwar's Marwah tehsil.Â
Per media reports , an Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) crashed near Machhna village in Marwah tehsil of the Kishtwar district on May 4. Three people, including two pilots and one technician, lost their lives in this incident.Â
To sum it up, a video of a helicopter crash in Jammu and Kashmir is being falsely shared as a MiG-21 crash in Rajasthan. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: May 9, 2023 21:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Kejriwal DID NOT ask people to vote for Congress in Jalandhar by-poll, viral video is edited
content:
This video shot ahead of the 2017 Punjab Assembly polls was cut out of context.
A day before the May 10 by-election in Punjab's Jalandhar, a video of Delhi Chief Minister and Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal, allegedly soliciting votes for the Congress party, has been shared by some on social media. In the video, Kejriwal can be seen saying, "In this election, do not vote for the BJP or the Shiromani Akali Dal. All must vote for Congress."Â
Sharing the video , one person tweeted in Hindi, "National President of the Aam Aadmi Party and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal set an example for opposition unity. Despite his own party and chief minister in the state, he appealed to people to vote for Congress in the Jalandhar Lok Sabha by-election." The archived version of such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Fact Check's investigation found that the viral video is almost six years old and also doctored. The original video was shot by Kejriwal during the Punjab Assembly elections in 2017.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to Kejriwal's official Facebook page , which contained the extended version of the clip, shared on January 30, 2017, before the Punjab Assembly elections. The post read, "RSS and Akali Dal have started transferring their votes in favour of Congress".Â
In that video, Kejriwal said, "It is being reported for the past two days that Akali Dal and RSS men are going door-to-door and appealing to people that in this election do not vote for BJP or Shiromani Akali Dal. All must vote for Congress. RSS and Akali Dal have started shifting their votes in favour of Congress. Now it is apparent that they all are the same. They all have only one intention - they do not want the Aam Aadmi Party to win. Because they know that if the Aam Aadmi Party comes to power, then all the files will be opened. They will be in jail and all the corruption will be exposed."
This proved that the video being shared was cut out of context. On February 2, 2017, Kejriwal went live on his official Facebook page and clarified that he never appealed to anyone to vote for Congress, adding that a doctored clip was being shared.
While he did not share the link to this doctored video, his words suggest it was the same video that is being shared now. It's also noteworthy that the same clip went viral right before the Delhi Assembly polls in 2020  as well. India Today had debunked it at the time.
Thus, it is very clear that the viral video has been cut out of context and has nothing to do with Jalandhar's by-election. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: May 10, 2023 17:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of people ecstatic over 'Trump Guilty' newsflash at bar is a meme - not actual celebration
content:
A 2016 video of fans celebrating during a football match was digitally altered to add a newsflash reading "Trump Guilty".
A jury on May 9 found former US President Donald J Trump liable for sexually abusing and defaming journalist, author, and advice columnist E Jean Carroll and awarded her $5 million in damages. In the civil case, the federal jury found that Carroll had sufficiently proved that Trump sexually abused her in a New York department store in 1996. Following this, a video of people celebrating the verdict was widely shared online. As per the video and its accompanying claim, people at a bar erupted in joy as news of the verdict flashed on a large TV A Twitter user while sharing the viral video  wrote, "Meanwhile, down at the bar," alongside hashtags like "Trump is Guilty" and "Trump Is A Rapist". The archived version of this tweet can be seen here .  India Today, however, found that this video is from 2016 and shows football fans celebrating. The Trump newsflash was digitally added to it. Our Probe We performed a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video and came across several posts  containing the same clip of the full bar  erupting in celebration . However, in each clip , the scene playing on the TV was different. In fact, in one of the videos, "Avengers: Endgame" appeared to play on the TV. This made it clear that this video was a popular meme template. Subsequent searches led us to the entry for the "Happiness Comes From The Simple Things" meme on the KnowYourMeme website. According to it, the original video was first shared on June 16, 2016, by the YouTube channel Heart News West Country. It reportedly showed fans celebrating the English national team scoring against Wales in the 2016 Euro tournament. We also found another video  of the same scene shot from a different angle shared on June 17, 2016, on the YouTube channel of Bristol Sport. The video was titled "Ashton Gate Erupts For Euro 2016 England Game," and its description said, "Thousands of football fans filled Ashton Gate Stadium on Thursday afternoon for the England v Wales game." The CBS Sports  and Bristol City Football Club  websites also shared the viral video in their reports on June 16, 2016. The reports described the event as fans at the Sports Bar & Grill at Ashton Gate watching a live broadcast of the "England vs Wales" match during the Euro 2016 tournament. Thus, it's clear that the viral video is a meme. ALSO READ | Fact Check: Did Prakash Raj tell people not to vote for Congress in Karnataka polls? Viral clip is from 2019 ALSO READ | Fact Check: Looting in Manipur stores? This video has nothing to do with ongoing violence in the state Published By: Rajeev Singh Published On: May 10, 2023 21:42 IST

title: Fact Check: Photoshopped image of MS Dhoni touching Sachin Tendulkar's feet goes viral
content:
This image is doctored. The original image is from April 8 and was shot at Wankhede Stadium before the MI-CSK match.
A photo of Chennai Super Kings skipper Mahendra Singh Dhoni touching Mumbai Indian mentor Sachin Tendulkar's feet has been widely shared on social media. This allegedly happened during the recent Indian Premier League (IPL) match between two teams in Chennai's MA Chidambaram Stadium on May 6.Â
People who shared the photo praised Dhoni's upbringing and claimed that when Tendulkar came to the field during the match, Dhoni went ahead and touched his feet. One such tweet opined: "Let me tell you that both are billionaires. Such acts prove where humility and decency can take you no matter what. On the other hand, some such people get inflated with little position and money. There is only one life, it is up to us to decide how to live it."
Several YouTube videos that featured this photo in their thumbnails also claimed the same.Â
The archived versions of such posts can be seen here: ( https://web.archive.org/web/20230510102710/https://twitter.com/SampatOfficial/status/1656179599104147457 ) and ( https://web.archive.org/web/20230510110849/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4X6O30wYfgo ).
India Today's investigation found that this image was photoshopped. OUR PROBE
It's noteworthy that when Bollywood singer Arijit Singh touched Dhoni's feet during the opening ceremony of the IPL 2023, it made headlines all over. It's only natural that Dhoni touching Tendulkar's feet would have resulted in the same media frenzy. We, however, could not find a single news report that said that.
Subsequently, we reverse-searched the image on Google and that led us to a Navbharat Times report from April 8, 2023 , that featured a similar photo of the two cricketers.
In the photo, instead of bending over and touching his feet, Dhoni stood beside Tendulkar, who looked the same as he did in the viral photo. Reportedly, this photo was shot in Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium before the April 8 encounter between the Mumbai Indians and the Chennai Super Kings.
Subsequent searches led us to an April 8 tweet from the official IPL Twitter account that said: "Two Legends, One Frame." It contained the Navbharat Times photo. 2⃣ Legends. 1⃣ Frame 💙💛 #TATAIPL | #MIvCSK | @sachin_rt | @msdhoni pic.twitter.com/9pLrQh4hp6 — IndianPremierLeague (@IPL) April 8, 2023
2⃣ Legends. 1⃣ Frame 💙💛 #TATAIPL | #MIvCSK | @sachin_rt | @msdhoni pic.twitter.com/9pLrQh4hp6 — IndianPremierLeague (@IPL) April 8, 2023
Upon comparing the original image with the viral one, it became apparent that the photo of Dhoni bowing down was digitally added to the original image.
While we could not find where the photo of Dhoni bending down was taken from, it is safe to conclude that both, the photo and the claim alongside it, are misleading. Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: May 10, 2023 22:00 IST

title: Fact Check: This is an old video from Guatemala - NOT Pakistanis protesting Imran Khan's arrest
content:
This video is from 2021 and shows Honduran migrants clashing with Guatemalan security forces.
Protests intensified in various cities in Pakistan including Islamabad, Lahore, Karachi, and Rawalpindi following former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan's arrest on May 9 in connection with a corruption case. At least eight people were killed and around 300 injured during the protests at the time of writing this. Amid this, a video of security forces trying to stop a sea of people from moving forward was shared by many on social media. Allegedly, this video was from the recent Pakistan protests — it has been shared  with hashtags like "Pakistan Republic", "Pakistan Civil War", and "Imran Khan Arrested". A Twitter user shared this video and wrote, "Exclusive Footage from Kashmir Highway, Islamabad. Huge crowd came from KP, according to the ground reports". The archived version of this tweet can be seen here . India Today found that this video is neither recent nor related to the ongoing protests in Pakistan. It dates back to January 2021 when clashes erupted between Honduran migrants and Guatemalan security forces. Not Pakistan A quick reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to its longer version uploaded to the YouTube channel of The Telegraph on January 18, 2021. Per the video's description, it showed migrants from Honduras clashing with the Guatemalan police. The Daily Mail  and the Chinese state-run China Global Television Network  also reported this incident at the time and shared the video. According to Reuters , on January 17, 2021, Guatemala's security forces stopped around 8,000 migrants in the Guatemalan village of Vado Hondo, about 55 km from the borders of Honduras and El Salvador. These migrants, reportedly from Honduras, left their country in an attempt to escape poverty and violence. Per the report, Guatemalan security officers managed to stop the migrants from going beyond Vado Hondo. Geolocating the video We found other videos  of the incident  shot from different angles . We noticed that on one side of the road, there was a red wall and trees planted at equal gaps. On the other side of the road, there were hills. Towards the direction in which the security forces are standing, we noticed a white building near the road. As the crowd pushed the security forces back, we observed a green pole. We were able to find this location in the Vado Hondo village of Guatemala. All the elements listed above are visible in the Google Maps Street View of this location. A comparison between the news videos and Google Maps and Street View can be seen below  Thus, it's clear that an old video from Guatemala is being falsely shared as a recent protest in Pakistan. This video has nothing to do with ongoing violence in the state Published By: Adarsh T R Published On: May 11, 2023 15:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of burqa-clad smuggler from Andhra FALSELY shared with communal spin amid Karnataka polls
content:
This is a 2020 video from Andhra Pradesh's Kurnool district. The burqa-clad man in this video was caught smuggling liquor from Telangana.
On May 10, amid Assembly elections in Karnataka, many shared a video  of policemen asking a person to remove their burqa. Soon, it's revealed that under the veil was a man and not a woman. We then see the man squatting down with a bunch of other men. मुसलमान को बदनाम करने के लिये बुर्का पहन कर कर्नाटक में पथराव कर रहा था ये! भक्तों भाजपा के ख़िलाफ़ साज़िश मत कहना अभी भाजपा की सरकार ही है वहाँ! मोदी जी कपड़े से पहचानो! pic.twitter.com/x7dCOZsmI7 — Surendra Rajput ‏ (@ssrajputINC) May 10, 2023 Per many who shared the clip, this was from Karnataka. Tweets suggested, "He was pelting stones in Karnataka wearing a burqa to defame Muslims!" Several others shared the same clip  with similar claims in Hindi alongside hashtags like "Karnataka Assembly Election 2023". Archived versions of such posts can be seen here  and here . एक धर्म को बदनाम करने के लिए कितना गिरोगे,,पैसे के लिए कुछ भी करने वाले लोगों का एक समूह #कर्नाटक में बुर्का पहनकर पुलिस पर पथराव करते पकड़ा गया,, #KarnatakaAssemblyElection2023 pic.twitter.com/RzA5CbPwNy — Mαɳιʂԋ Kυɱαɾ αԃʋσƈαƚҽ 🇮🇳🇮🇳 (@manishkumarttp) May 10, 2023 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today's investigation found that the video is more than a couple of years old and not related to the 2023 Karnataka Assembly elections at all.  Our Probe Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip, we found an extended version of a similar video uploaded to the YouTube channel of ETV Andhra Pradesh  on August 8, 2020, making it clear that the video is not recent.  There, the caption mentioned that several people were arrested by the police in Andhra Pradesh's Kurnool district following the recovery of illegal liquor in transit. Per the video's description, the police recovered liquor bottles hidden inside their burqas. We also came across another fact-check story by India Today  from August 16, 2020, debunking the same video. At the time was falsely shared as a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh member getting arrested for waving the Pakistani flag while clad in a burqa, in order to defame Muslims. At the time, India Today had reached out to Kurnool SP Fakkeerappa Kaginelli and ASP (Special Enforcement Bureau) Gowthami Sali, who confirmed the case was related to smuggling NDPL (non-duty paid liquor) from Telangana to Andhra Pradesh. title: Fact Check: BJP leader caught with EVM in Karnataka? No, mob destroyed equipment found in poll officer's car
content:
The car seen in the viral video did not belong to a BJP leader. It was that of a polling officer who was also mahandled during the incident.
As Karnataka waits for election results, a video allegedly from the state has been widely shared online. It shows a car surrounded by an angry mob, some of whom could be seen destroying electronic voting machines (EVMs).
Sharing the video , one person tweeted, "Local people created a ruckus after EVM machine was found in BJP leader's car," along with the hashtag "Karnataka Elections". Others too shared the video with similar claims. The archived version of such tweets can be seen here , here , and here .
Gujarat Congress' Hitendra Pithadiya shared the video on Twitter and wrote in Hindi, "Locals created a ruckus after EVMs were found in a BJP leader's car!" Prashant Anand, the coordinator to Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, also shared the video and wrote in Hindi, "See, public outrage as soon as EVM found in BJP leader's car. People have become so disturbed by Modi's lies that they have taken a stand to remove the BJP. Looking like the 2024 trailer." The archived version of such posts can be seen here and here. India Today Fact Check's investigation found that the viral claims are misleading. The EVMs were not recovered from a Bharatiya Janata Party leader's car. Rather the car belonged to an on-duty polling officer. Our Probe A keyword search on the internet led us to an Outlook India news report from May 11, that said that in Karnataka's Vijayapura district on the day of the Assembly polls, residents of the Masabinala village allegedly stopped a poll-duty vehicle carrying electronic voting machines (EVMs), and manhandled an officer. Twenty-three people were arrested. Other media outlets also reported the same news.  We also found that in response to a similar viral tweet, the official Twitter account of the Deputy Commissioner of the Vijayapura district  wrote, "It is false. Actually. Reserve EVMs carried in sector officer vehicle was stopped by villagers and damaged the EVMs. Case has been registered ad 24 people have been arrested." After that, we found a press note on the official website of the Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka. Per the note, "Malappa Hanamantappa Yerajari, Revenue Sector Officer of Basavan Bagewadi Assembly along with other staff was carrying reserve EVMs & VVPATs from Basavana Bagewadi's strong room towards Masabinal in Car No: KA- 28/Z-2305. During this time, around 100-150 public stopped their vehicle near Venkatesh temple, Masabinal and abused them in filthy language and dragged them out of the car, assaulted them with stones with the intention to kill them, damaged their vehicle, EVMs & other polling materials." The Superintendent of Police in Vijayapura, HD Ananda Kumar also tweeted the same information, dismissing any BJP leader's involvement in this incident. Thus, it is safe to conclude that the car seen in the viral video did not belong to a BJP leader. (With inputs from Aishwarya Paliwal and Babu Tadlagi) Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: May 11, 2023 23:11 IST

title: Fact Check: UFO spotted hovering between mountains in Russia? Nope, it's just VFX
content:
This video was created by VFX artist Colton Kirkegaard using Unreal Engine 4.
An unidentified flying object hovering over the Russian island of Sakhalin was allegedly captured on video and that clip is now being shared on social media. The video allegedly captured from a Russian military helicopter shows a disc-like object can be seen flying over a mountainous area. A Twitter user  shared the video and wrote, "Russia's Sakhalin has a lot of undeveloped land, so UFO resource exploration is prosperous. A Russian military helicopter captured a UFO over Sakhalin, Russia." The archived version of this post can be seen here . India Today found that the viral video was created using visual effects by an artist called Colton Kirkegaard.  Our Probe Responding to the viral tweet , a person said that this video was created by a special effects artist called Colton Kirkegaard. We found Kirkegaard's Instagram account and there we found the viral video  shared on March 6, 2021. The video contained the watermark of his Tik Tok account "@coltonkirk.mov". We found this video on the TikTok account as well. The Instagram post's caption read: "I've been noticing this video I made has been making the rounds being shared online outside of my TikTok page as of late (zero credit given to me of course). Pretty proud of it though, just crossed the 1.1M views mark too! Also fully rendered in Unreal Engine 4." Unreal Engine 4  is an advanced real-time 3D creation tool. Kirkegaard  is a VFX artist based in Los Angeles, US, who has worked on feature films for studios like Disney, Sony, Universal/Amblin, Playtone, and Warner Bros. He often shares similar computer-generated videos of UFOs on Instagram. India Today has reached out to him and the story will be updated when he responds. Earlier, another video created by him had gone viral as a UFO sighted in Antarctica. At the time also, fact-checkers  had debunked the claim. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: May 12, 2023 16:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Bilawal Bhutto seen celebrating Imran Khan's arrest? No, this video is from 2022
content:
This video is from April 2022 when Imran Khan was ousted as prime minister.
Violent protests erupted in Pakistan following the arrest of former Prime Minister Imran Khan. At least eight people have died and hundreds have been injured so far. While Khan was granted bail  on May 12, in the immediate aftermath of the arrest, a video of Pakistan People's Party Chairman and Foreign Affairs Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari celebrating with his supporters went viral. In the video, PPP supporters could be heard sloganeering, and Zardari could be seen joining them. Allegedly, they were celebrating Khan's arrest. A Twitter user while sharing the viral video wrote,"Cabal of crooks having fun after Khan Saab' arrest… your days are doomed, soon or later we'll get back to you." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here : India Today's investigation found that the video from April 2022, and predates the current political crisis by a year. National Health Minister of Pakistan Abdul Qadir Patel and Zardari were then celebrating the ouster of Khan as prime minister. Our Probe We ran a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video and found a slightly older tweet containing the video. The tweet  from April 10, 2023, said in Urdu: "Moments of celebration from April 9, 2022, when my Chairman showed a fascist captain the way to the Pavilion." On April 9, 2022, Khan was ousted as Pakistan's prime minister after losing a no-confidence vote in Parliament, following long political impasse. We, then, found the viral video on the YouTube channel of PPP leader and current Health Minister Abdul Qadir Patel. The video was shared on April 8, 2022, when the no-trust motion was brought against Khan. Its description read, "Ragre pe ragra, Abdul Qadir Patel Celebrating With Chairman PPP Bilawal Bhutto Zardari." Thus, it's clear that an old video, which predates the current turbulent political crisis in Pakistan, was shared with a misleading claim. Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: May 12, 2023 18:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of women assaulting a man in Kerala shared with false communal spin
content:
This inThe man and the women beating him up are Christians.
Against the backdrop of "The Kerala Story" and the many controversies surrounding it, a video of a group of women thrashing a man has gone viral. Many social media users, while sharing the video, alleged that the man seen in the video was Muslim and that he had misbehaved with Hindu women, who consequently flogged him. Sharing the video , a Twitter user wrote, "In Kerala Hindu girls attacked a Muslim man for his obnoxious and shameful misbehaviour. The awakening has started in Kerala after #TheKeralaStoryMovie! Let's hope the fire rages on. This is the right way to stop Love jihad. Our girls must show their DURGA AVTAR." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here . India Today's investigation revealed that the video is old and the man and the women in the video are Christians. Our Probe We ran a reverse image search on keyframes from the viral video. It led us to news reports that contained screenshots from the viral clip. A report by News18 Malayalam , dated January 6, 2023, noted that it was a conflict between former and current members of a Kerala church. Members of the Thrissur Muriyad Emperor Emmanuel Mediation Centre reportedly assaulted former member Shaji who was travelling with his family in a car on January 6. We also came across a report by India Today Malayalam  that 11 of the 59 women who assaulted Shaji and his family were arrested. They were booked  under section 307 (attempt to murder) of the Indian Penal Code. Per the reports, Shaji, his wife Ashlyn, son Sajan, and relatives Edwin and Anwin were beaten up by them in Muriyad. The women accused Shaji's son of circulating a morphed nude photo of a female member of the church. According to News18 Malayalam, the police had confirmed the existence of obscene photos. However, no confirmation of Sajan spreading the photos was reported. Church authorities also reportedly registered the case against Shaji with the Aloor Police. A senior police officer there clarified to The Quint  that the man and the women were Christians, dismissing communal angles that were linked to the video back in January as well. Thus, it's clear that the viral claim of Hindu women thrashing a Muslim man for misbehaving is patently false. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: May 12, 2023 20:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Imran Khan motorcade shared as latest scene of his welcome following release
content:
This is an old video from March 2023, when Khan was leaving with his supporters after making a court appearance in the Toshakhana case.
Pakistan's ousted Prime Minister Imran Khan arrived at his Lahore residence  on Saturday, May 13, after being granted bail by the Islamabad High Court following the high drama and nationwide protests over his arrest on corruption charges. In its aftermath, several videos and pictures of the just-released Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf chief were shared on social media. Among them was a video  allegedly showing Khan's car moving through a sea of supporters and party workers. Pakistani journalist Jameel Farooqui while sharing the viral video wrote in Urdu, "After enduring shelling and fascism all day, a sea of workers on the Srinagar highway was there to welcome Imran Khan (Video Credit - Abdul Qadir)." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here . India Today's investigation found that the video is from March 2023 when Khan was leaving the judicial complex in Islamabad after marking his appearance in the Toshakhana case. The court had at the time cancelled the arrest warrants issued in the case. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Our Probe We noticed the watermark "AbdulQadriARY" on the top left corner of the video. The watermark appeared to be a social media handle. We searched and found that it belonged to Pakistani journalist Abdul Qadir on YouTube , Twitter , and Facebook . Scrolling through his Twitter account, we found the viral video shared there on March 18, 2023. We also found a few clips of the viral video on his YouTube account. The description of the YouTube video read, "Imran Khan dodges arrest after police show up at Islamabad court today." Using search filters on Google, we looked for more information on this. We came across a report by Al Jazeera  published on March 18, 2023. The report's cover photo showed PTI supporters surrounding shipping containers as visible in the viral video. The photo was credited to Anjum Naveed of the Associated Press and its description read: "The car of former Prime Minister Imran Khan is surrounded by his supporters as he leaves the Judicial Complex in Islamabad on March 18, 2023." Per the report, a Pakistani court cancelled arrest warrants after Khan marked his appearance at the court in a corruption case. We also found a similar video shot from a different angle on Khan's official Twitter  shared on the same date. Both, the viral video and the one shared by Imran Khan, show the same set of people standing on the bonnet and roof of a car flanked by supporters. More videos of the motorcade accompanying Khan leaving the Islamabad court can be seen here  and here . Geolocation We also geolocated the place on Google Maps  and found several elements common between the viral video and the area visible in Street View. These included street lights and a red and white foot overbridge. Given below is a comparison. Thus, it's evident that an old video of Khan's motorcade was shared as scenes of his supporters welcoming him after securing bail. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: May 13, 2023 20:34 IST

title: Fact Check: AI-generated images shared as Putin collapsing after suffering heart attack
content:
The images are generated with the help of artificial intelligence.
Images showing purported videos of Russian President Vladimir Putin collapsing to the ground after suffering a heart attack have gone viral. Putin is seen falling over his hands and then finally collapsing.
A Twitter user, sharing the supposed screenshot of the newspaper "The Moscow Times", tweeted, "Putin suffers heart attack! South African ANC #BRICS."
The cover story in the screenshot is of Putin suffering a heart attack. The headline read: "President Putin suffers a heart attack."
Another user, sharing two images of Putin collapsing, wrote: "Putin fell down. During late-night meetings with exsoviet members he collapsed and was helped back to his feet by aids. #Putin #PresidentPutin #Trump2024."
India Today's investigation revealed that the images are not authentic and are generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI).
A close observation of the screenshot of the newspaper shows the date of publishing of the story to be May 12, 2023. We then went through the newspaper's website to verify whether such a news was indeed published. However, we couldn't find anything related to the viral news corresponding to May 12.
We then ran a reverse image search that led us to a Twitter user, Misha Petrov. Petrov shared the viral two images on March 22, 2023, and wrote in Russian: "Putin fell during a meeting in the Kremlin."
In the thread that follows the tweet , he clarified: "The pictures are generated by artificial intelligence if anything." The thread also had images that showed Putin collapsing to the ground.
In his later tweets, he said that the images were generated using Midjourney, an AI art generator application. Using the application, he created similar images of Putin being arrested .
As we checked for news reports of Putin suffering a heart attack, we couldn't find any. The AI-generated images of Putin are being falsely shared with the claim that he collapsed due to a heart attack.
Earlier as well, AI-generated photos of police arresting former US president Donald Trump went viral, with the claim that it was real. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: May 13, 2023 22:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Karnataka polls fallout? This video is old and not related to 2023 Assembly elections
content:
The video is at least a year old and has no relation to the Karnataka Assembly elections.
In Karnataka, the Bharatiya Janata Party lost its last bastion in the south on May 13. In its aftermath, a video of two women fighting in what looks like a BJP office has gone viral. Allegedly, it showed a young woman fighting with her parents for supporting the saffron party in the recently-held Karnataka Assembly elections.Â
A Twitter user sharing the video wrote , "An Eye opener video. A girl went against her own family which is supporting #BJP #KarnatakaElectionResults2023." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .Â
India Today's investigation found that the video is more than a year old and has nothing to do with the Karnataka elections.Â
A reverse image search of the viral video led us to older tweets from 2022. Twitter user Avishek Goyal , taking a jab at the BJP, tweeted the viral video on April 19, 2022. He wrote in Hindi, "While one should not poke into the domestic disputes of others, one must see this." Responding to a comment, Goyal said this video was from Delhi .Â
The same day, it was tweeted by filmmaker and journalist Vinod Kapri , who wrote in Hindi: "Such violence has taken place in the drawing rooms and WhatsApp groups of every house."Â
We also came across a news report by Jansatta  published on April 20, 2022. The report also attributed the video's origin to Goyal. However, it distinctly stated that the location of the incident and the reason behind the brawl couldn't be ascertained.Â
While we couldn't independently determine where the brawl between two women took place or even why it happened, it is clear that the video has been in circulation for a year and predates the Karnataka Assembly polls. Published By: Chhabi Kala Published On: May 16, 2023 19:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Kejriwal shares Congress-era 'power cut' data to showcase bright shining Punjab
content:
The survey is based on data from November 2019 to March 2020, when the Congress was in power in Punjab. Also, per the survey cited, Punjab did not rank second in terms of low power outage numbers.
One of the main poll planks of the Aam Aadmi Party in Punjab was free electricity. However, the Punjab government recently decided to raise the power tariff  from 25 to 89 paise per unit for different categories with effect from May 16. Naturally, it's facing flak for it and is now on the defensive. AAP supremo and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal tweeted an infographic  on May 16, claiming that the power outage rates in Delhi and Punjab were the lowest in the country, even as the party is providing "free 24x7 electricity". advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The infographic showed daily power outage numbers in various states alongside Kejriwal's photo. The text above the chart read: "Brilliant! Delhi has India's lowest power cuts!" The citation mentioned for this supposed fact was the India Residential Energy Survey by the CEEW. The graph showed that Delhi experienced the least hours of power cuts, followed by Punjab. Uttar Pradesh and Haryana were the worst in terms of load-shedding.
One of the main poll planks of the Aam Aadmi Party in Punjab was free electricity. However, the Punjab government recently decided to raise the power tariff  from 25 to 89 paise per unit for different categories with effect from May 16. Naturally, it's facing flak for it and is now on the defensive.Â
AAP supremo and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal tweeted an infographic  on May 16, claiming that the power outage rates in Delhi and Punjab were the lowest in the country, even as the party is providing "free 24x7 electricity".
The infographic showed daily power outage numbers in various states alongside Kejriwal's photo. The text above the chart read: "Brilliant! Delhi has India's lowest power cuts!"
The citation mentioned for this supposed fact was the India Residential Energy Survey by the CEEW. The graph showed that Delhi experienced the least hours of power cuts, followed by Punjab. Uttar Pradesh and Haryana were the worst in terms of load-shedding.
While sharing this, Kejriwal wrote, "Only Punjab and Delhi have free electricity in the whole country, and these two states have the least power cuts. Earlier, people used to say that power cuts would increase if free electricity is provided. On the contrary, now the power cuts have been reduced." पूरे देश में केवल पंजाब और दिल्ली में फ़्री बिजली है और इन्ही दोनों राज्यों में सबसे कम पॉवर कट हैं। पहले लोग कहते थे कि अगर फ्री बिजली देंगे तो बिजली कट बढ़ जाएँगे। उल्टे पॉवर कट कम हो गये। कैसे? क्योंकि इन दोनों राज्यों में साफ़ नीयत, ईमानदार और पढ़े लिखे लोगों की आम आदमी… pic.twitter.com/qOGh4qdsGj — Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) May 16, 2023 Following Kejriwal's tweet, many on Facebook and Twitter shared the same post. Archived versions of these posts can be seen here  and here .  पूरे देश में केवल पंजाब और दिल्ली में फ़्री बिजली है और इन्ही दोनों राज्यों में सबसे कम पॉवर कट हैं। पहले लोग कहते थे कि अगर फ्री बिजली देंगे तो बिजली कट बढ़ जाएँगे। उल्टे पॉवर कट कम हो गये। कैसे? क्योंकि इन दोनों राज्यों में साफ़ नीयत, ईमानदार और पढ़े लिखे लोगों की आम आदमी… pic.twitter.com/jqhxeTMooZ — टीम अरविंद केजरीवाल हरियाणा (@abpssharyana07) May 16, 2023 India Today Fact Check found that the graph shared by Kejriwal was not only manipulated but also three years old. The data is from a time when the Congress was in power in Punjab, not the AAP. Survey predates AAP rule in Punjab In Kejriwal's infographic, we noticed the source mentioned was the India Residential Energy Survey 2020. The AAP came to power in Punjab in April 2022.  We found the original report called "State of Electricity Access in India, Insights from the India Residential Energy Survey (IRES) 2020"  on the website of the Council on Energy, Environment and Water. The CEEW is a non-profit policy research institution that works on environmental change, use, reuse, and misuse of resources. On the very first page of this 76-page report, it was mentioned that it was published in October 2020. Further, on page 16, it was mentioned that the survey was designed, prepared and executed between March 2019 to April 2020. Notably, the data for the survey was collected between November 2019 and March 2020, when Captain Amarinder Singh of the Congress party was Punjab's Chief Minister.   The AAP had promised Punjab "free electricity" during the elections and according to a September 2022 Economic Times report , the party fulfilled this promise of providing 300 units of free electricity per month to 25 lakh domestic consumers. According to the state power minister, of the total 72 lakh domestic consumers, bills were sent to only 42 lakh. The remainder received zero electricity bills. Punjab still wasn't second-lowest According to the graph shared by Kejriwal, Delhi had the lowest amount of power outages in the country, followed by Punjab. The graph in the original report told a different tale altogether.  advertisement  In the original survey's graph, Kerala, Gujarat, and Tamil Nadu performed better than Punjab in terms of load-shedding. These three states were missing in the graph shared by Kejriwal. This suggested that even as per the 2019-2020 data, Punjab was not the second-lowest in terms of power outage rates. However, there were a few other differences between the two graphs as well. Unlike the graph Kejriwal shared, the worst-performing states listed in the original report's graph were Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Haryana, instead of just UP and Haryana. At the same time, Kejriwal's graph mentioned the "National Avg." In the report's graph, this was listed as "India." The values in both graphs, however, seemed to be the same. Additionally, the report stated, "An average Indian household receives 20.6 hours of power supply from the grid. The average daily supply in urban areas (22 hours) is longer by a couple of hours than in rural areas (20 hours). Delhi, Kerala, and Gujarat are the top states, maintaining slightly over 23 hours of average supply in both urban and rural areas. In contrast, households in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Haryana, Assam, and Bihar face the longest power outages, with rural households in these states facing six or more hours of daily outages."  ALSO READ | Fact Check: Bilawal Bhutto seen celebrating Imran Khan's arrest? No, this video is from 2022 Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: May 16, 2023 22:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Somalia floods FALSELY shared as Cyclone Mocha in Myanmar
content:
This video predates the Myanmar cyclone by at least two weeks and shows flash floods in Somalia.
Following the devastation caused by Cyclone Mocha in Myanmar, a video  of a man sitting what looks like a rickshaw, being carried away by floodwater gushing through the streets has gone viral. Allegedly, this video was from Myanmar and showed the cyclone's effect. A Twitter user shared this video and wrote, "Cyclone Mocha makes landfall, brings catastrophe." The archived version of this post can be seen here .Â
Reportedly, the death toll  in Myanmar rose to 60 on May 16. Although, hundreds are feared dead . Mocha made landfall on May 14.Â
India Today's investigation found that the viral video has nothing to do with Cyclone Mocha. In fact, it's not from Asia at all. It shows floods in Somalia. OUR PROBE
Using a keyword search, we found that a person quote-tweeted one of the viral posts claiming that it was from Somalia. Subsequent searches led us to an April 29 video news report  on Meteored, a YouTube channel focused on meteorology. In it, the viral video was credited to Action for Women & Children Concern , a non-profit organisation in Somalia. As per the report, the video was from Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. Clearly, this video predates the recent cyclone in Myanmar.
Flash floods across Somalia have affected over 450,000 people and displaced around 200,000, reported the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. The report  added that around 22 people were killed in 17 districts since mid-March.
We looked for videos of the recent flash flood in the country and found a collection of videos , allegedly from Somalia, shared on Facebook on May 1. They appeared similar to the viral video. One of these videos contained the watermark of the TikTok account "@craxmanyare8". We checked the TikTok account and found that it contained clearer versions of three videos from the same location, including the viral video. Â
We noticed two significant visual clues in these TikTok videos. First, the design and colour of the rickshaws. We compared the red-brown rickshaws seen in the viral video with the ones seen in a Switch TV news report  and noticed significant similarities.Â
Second, we also observed blue-white marks and numbers written on concrete pillars in the viral video. These appeared similar to pillars we noticed in a report on the flash floods by Universal Somali TV . We found these similarities in videos  posted by multiple vloggers . India Today reached out to Mohammed Nur, a former journalist based in Mogadishu who confirmed that this video was indeed from Somalia. While he couldn't tell us where exactly the video was shot, he said that it might have been somewhere in the Hodan neighbourhood of Mogadishu. India Today could not independently verify the exact date or location of this video. However, it is certain that the clip is from Somalia and is at least two weeks old. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: May 17, 2023 16:43 IST

title: Fact Check: This video shows AIMIM leader from Telangana - NOT Karnataka Congress MLA
content:
Neither is Jaffar Hussain Meraj a Congress member nor is he from Karnataka. He's an AIMIM MLA from Nampally, Telangana.
Following the Congress party's thumping victory in Karnataka, a video of an alleged Congress MLA threatening a policeman has been widely shared on social media. A Facebook user  who shared it claimed that Karnataka Congress MLA Jaffar Hussain Meraj of Nampally invited a police officer to his home in Jagtial and calmly explained that he would have to do as they said.
Another person  made the same claim, alongside comments like, "Trends have started changing even before the formation of a government in Karnataka," and, "The people of Karnataka will have to face the consequences of their deeds one day." Others on Facebook and Twitter  made similar claims.
India Today's investigation found that while Jaffar Hussain Meraj is indeed an MLA from Nampally, the constituency is located in Telangana and Meraj belongs to the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen, not Congress. Our Probe
A keyword search on the internet led us to an Indian Express report on the winners of the 2018 Assembly election in Telangana . Jaffar Hussain of the AIMIM was mentioned in it as a winner from Nampally, Telangana. The same information was also mentioned on the Election Commission of India's official website. Â
We found Meraj's official Facebook page , and his bio and cover image there mentioned the AIMIM and the Nampally Assembly constituency in Telangana.
We then looked for information about the viral clip and found a video news report by BBN News , a Hyderabad-based news outlet. In the report from May 11, the viral clip could be seen a little more than two minutes in.
Per the report, two women were allegedly manhandled and harassed on a bus by Jagtial Rural sub inspector called A Anil. Following that, the AIMIM MLA, along with other members of the party met both, the victim's family and the superintendent of police there. Jagtial is a city and the district headquarters of the Jagtial district of Telangana. The report added that the accused police officer was later suspended.
On May 11, the Deccan Chronicle also reported on this incident. The report contained a screenshot from the viral video. Telangana Today also published a news report about this on the same day.
We checked Meraj's Facebook page and found that on May 11, he too had shared photos  from his visit to the victim's family. The post said that "On the guidance of AIMIM President Barrister Asaduddin Owaisi sahab and AIMIM Floor Leader Akbaruddin Owaisi Sahab," Meraj reached Jagtial and met the victims' family and assured them that "we'll demand for immediate Suspension and strict action against the Sub-Inspector."
Thus, it is clear that the viral video has nothing to do with Karnataka at all.
(With inputs from M Sanjeeva Rao) Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: May 17, 2023 20:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Photo of cow slaughtered on BJP flag is NOT from Karnataka, it's from a 2022 Manipur incident
content:
This incident took place in Manipur in January 2022. It has nothing to do with the Karnataka Assembly polls.
In the aftermath of the Congress party securing a decisive victory in the Karnataka elections, a virulent campaign to demonise minority communities in the state has come to the fore. Two grisly photos of a slaughtered cow lying on a Bharatiya Janata Party have gone viral on social media.
Those sharing the photos linked them to Karnataka, alleging that Muslim supporters celebrated the Congress victory by slaughtering a cow on a BJP flag. A Twitter user while sharing the viral photos wrote : "Barbarians. I got a video saying it's from Karnataka and Izlamic fanatics cut the cow on the BJP flag to celebrate Khangres's victory. Twitter isn't allowing me to upload the video so posting the pics." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .
India Today's investigation found that the viral photos are from Manipur and are more than a year old. OUR PROBE
We noticed that in response to the viral post , one person said that the pictures were from a 2022 incident in Manipur. Subsequently, we searched on Twitter for more details about the incident.Â
We came across a tweet  from January 31, 2022, by a person called Nishant Azad who works for the Organiser, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's mouthpiece. It contained a video whose screenshots are now viral. The clip showed a few men examining the carcass of a cow in a field. Blood that had leaked from its slit throat could be seen splattered on a BJP flag on the ground.Â
The tweet read: "Manipur: Muzlims slaughtered a cow keeping on BJP flag. The goons also abused Chief Minister N Biren Singh and BJP Manipur president A Sarda Devi."Â
On February 1, 2022, Manipur Chief Minister N Biren Singh responded to the tweet  with the screenshot of an Imphal Free Press news report, which said that three people allegedly involved in the case had been arrested.Â
We found the news report in question , which stated that in Lilong, a cow was slaughtered on a BJP flag "as a mark of protest against the announcement of the BJP tickets for the Manipur Assembly polls" that year. It added that Nazbul Hussain, Abdur Rashid, and Md Arif Khan were booked under the Prevention of Cruelty To Animal Act 1960, and for allegedly inciting enmity among different groups.
We found news reports about this incident from other media outlets like The Hindu  and The Nagaland Post  and The Times of India .Â
Thus, it's clear that this incident has nothing to do with the Congress victory in the 2023 Karnataka Assembly polls. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: May 17, 2023 21:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Pak woman recounting police violence is from Imran Khan regime, NOT after his arrest
content:
Both clips are from a time when Imran Khan was the Prime Minister of Pakistan. Munir was not Army Chief at the time.
Earlier this month, Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan was arrested by authorities outside the Islamabad High Court. The country's apex court later ruled his arrest "illegal," and he was granted blanket bail in all cases for two weeks.Â
Amid the political chaos in the country, a video showing the plight of people in an allegedly "fascist" Pakistan has gone viral. Those sharing the video claimed that woman in the video was recounting the abuse she endured at the hands of the Pakistani police under the country's new Army Chief, Asim Munir.Â
The viral video consists of two clips. The first shows a woman being attacked by a police officer, while the second clip features a woman narrating her alleged abuse by the Pakistani police. The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today's investigation found that both clips in the video are from a time when Imran Khan was Prime Minister. Munir was not the Army Chief at the time.Â
Khan was ousted as PM on April 10, 2022, after losing the support of coalition allies. In a no-confidence motion that required 172 votes in the 342-seat Parliament, 174 members voted against Khan. General Qamar Javed Bajwa was the Army Chief of Pakistan at the time.Â
While Khan's party, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, claimed that the army played a part in his ouster, the army denied any involvement. General Asim Munir assumed charge as Pakistan's new Army Chief on November 29, 2022.
Now, let's examine when the viral clips were shot.
Video of cop manhandling womanÂ
The first clip in the viral video shows a police officer dragging a woman by her hair. Through a reverse search, we found screenshots from the same video in multiple media reports published in April 2021.Â
According to these reports , the video was from the Chunian area of the Kasur district in Pakistan's Punjab province. Reportedly , Kasur Police Sub-Inspector Jameel Khan entered a woman's house and tortured her based on a complaint filed by her husband, who alleged that she was illegally staying at his place. The reports added  that the police officer who attacked the woman was suspended by the Punjab police.
