title: Fact Check: This giant Pride rainbow on Paris monument is NOT real, it's 3D animation
content:
This is not a real installation. The rainbow structure was created by a visual artist using 3D animation tools.
June marks Pride Month in the US. Of course, this celebration of LGBTQIA+ people and culture has transcended American borders and now people across the world participate in it. Often during this month, in many parts of the world, rainbow Pride flags and buntings and banners are displayed publicly and prominently. One such purported display in France, however, seems to have caused some outrage online. Photos and videos of a rainbow installation wrapped around the Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile — the Triumphal Arch of the Star — in Paris, France, have been widely shared, and with some disdain. One person tweeted , "Arc de Triomphe, Paris, France This is how we respect the courage of the heroes who died in various wars." advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Others shared a short clip  showing this and wrote , "The Arc de Triomphe in Paris, the landmark, which holds the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, has been covered with a giant pride rainbow as well as a trans coloured square and a giant cloud with the words 'Marche Des Fiertes' which translates as Pride March." The archived versions of such tweets can be seen here , here , and here . The Arc de Triomphe is one of the most famous monuments in the world. It was commissioned by Napoleon Bonaparte in 1806, after his victory at the Battle of Austerlitz .  India Today's investigation found that the installation of the giant rainbow on the Arc de Triomphe was not real. It was CGI. Our Probe A keyword search on the internet led us to various news reports, where the viral video was called animated  or AI-generated . They also mentioned that it was created by an artist called Ian Padgham. A reverse search of keyframes of the viral video led us to the Instagram account of Padgham , a professional visual artist from California who lives in France. We found that he had shared the video  in question on June 1, 2023, on his Instagram. Its caption read: "Happy #pride2023 to everyone, everywhere Love is love, you are beautiful, and I am so proud to live in a world where we are fighting so that everyone can live their life exactly as they are #parisestfiere #marchedesfiertes #pridemonth." We also found many similar 3D animated artworks  on his Instagram .     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Ian Padgham (@origiful) We then reached out to Padgham to know more about the video. He said that he had made the video. The rainbow installation, he said, was created using 3D animation tools. He added, "It does not exist in real life." Thus, it is clear that the viral video is not real, but a work of 3D animation. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Jun 2, 2023 19:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Clip of overstuffed sleeper coach not filmed moments before Odisha train crash, it's a month old
content:
This video was shot on May 5, nearly a month before the devastating accident in Odisha that has killed more than 275 people.
The horrific accident involving the Bengaluru-Howrah Superfast Express, the Shalimar-Chennai Central Coromandel Express, and a goods train, in Balasore, Odisha, has so far claimed at least 275 lives and left over a thousand injured. As news — photos and videos of the accident, the dead, and the injured — continues to pour in, so does misinformation.Â
A viral video of a jam-packed sleeper coach of a train has emerged on social media. Those sharing the clip claimed that it was filmed by a passenger from one of the trains just before the tragic accident. One such tweet featuring the viral video read, "This video was captured shortly before the accident and was shared by the passenger with his friends." The archived versions of such posts can be seen here , here  and here .
India Today found that though the video was indeed from the Coromandel Express, it was shot on May 5, nearly a month prior to the devastating train accident in Odisha. Our Probe
With the help of a keyword search, we found that the same video was tweeted by a person named Sidhant Kumar Panda on May 5. According to his tweet , the video was shot inside a sleeper coach of the 12841 Coromandel Express. Sharing the video, Panda wrote, "This is the situation in 12841 Coromandel Express (Sleeper Coach). Please take the necessary action. Every one of us who has CNF seats are suffering a lot. My PNR 6318071331." Panda also tagged the Twitter accounts of the Ministry of Railways, its minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, as well as the Railway Protection Force.
On the same day, the Twitter accounts of Railway Seva and the Divisional Railway Manager for the Khurda Road Junction railway station in Odisha responded to Panda's tweet, saying the train ticket examiner on duty had been informed about the matter. The Twitter account of the Railway Protection Force in the Khurda Road Junction station also wrote in response  that some of the passengers who were on the waiting list were shifted to the general compartment when the train arrived at the station.Â
On June 4, responding to his tweet  from May 5, Panda said he was safe and that he had travelled in the train that was involved in the accident just a few days ago.Â
India Today reached out to Panda, who confirmed that the video was shot by him on May 5 on the Coromandel Express. He said that he was travelling from Bhubaneswar to Chennai Central.Â
"The train was extremely crowded that day, and I prefer not to recall how I spent that night. Many passengers with general tickets had occupied the reserved seats. Despite my tweet, I received no assistance from the railway officials. In fact, the train ticket examiner was unable to make his way through the crowd and seemed helpless as well," said Panda. He also mentioned that the train reached its destination safely that day.
According to survivors, the sleeper coaches of the Coromandel Express were crowded even on June 2, the day the accident occurred. A survivor from Kerala told the Indian Express , "Even the sleeper coach was crowded. Our tickets were not confirmed, so we had to vacate the seats for confirmed ticket holders after the train left Balasore station. The four of us were standing, carrying our bags when we heard a loud noise."
Regardless, it is clear that the video of the crowded train coach is not from moments before the accident at all. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 5, 2023 00:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Lalu Yadav's career as Rail Minister see zero accidents? No, here are the numbers
content:
Around 1,000 rail accidents were reported between 2004 and 2009 when Yadav was the Railway Minister.
The railway board has recommended a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the train accident in Balasore, Odisha, which has left at least 275 dead. Amid calls for the resignation of Union Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw on social media, there were also many posts comparing the management and performance of the Indian Railways under different ministers and governments.Â
One person, extolling former Bihar Chief Minister and former Railway Minister of India Lalu Prasad Yadav's contributions, wrote , "There was a railway minister Lalu Yadav, as long as he was the railway minister there was not a single train accident, railways was beneficial for the poor, they used to run Garib Rath Express to travel in AC at low fare."Â
Yadav held the rail portfolio from 2004 to 2009 during the UPA-I regime. The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .Â
India Today, however, found that the viral tweet's claim was false — the number of consequential accidents reported during Yadav's tenure as Railway Minister was much higher than in the last five years for which data was available.Â
According to the Ministry of Railways , 51 collisions, 550 derailments, 370 level-crossing accidents, 37 fire-related accidents, and 26 other miscellaneous accidents were reported between 2004 and 2009, bringing the total number of such accidents reported under Yadav's command to 1,034.Â
On the other hand, the total number of consequential accidents reported in the last five years for which data was available (from 2014-15 to 2018-19) was less than half of that — it stood at 478. The Railway Ministry classifies an accident as consequential when there is loss of life or injury or property damage or disruption to traffic.
Yadav, while presenting the Interim Railway Budget of 2009-2010 in the Lok Sabha, informed the house that the number of consequential accidents came down to 194 in 2007-2008 against 325 in 2003-2004.
In terms of casualties, 973 people died in the accidents when Yadav was at the helm of the ministry. In comparison, there were 1,080 deaths from 2014 to 2019.Â
Between 2014 and 2019, the Ministry was held by DV Sadananda Gowda (May 26, 2014, to November 9, 2014), Suresh Prabhu (November 9, 2014, to September 3, 2017), and Piyush Goyal (September 3, 2017, to July 7, 2021) respectively. Incumbent Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw took charge of the Railway Ministry in September 2021. The data for consequential accidents under Vaishnaw's tenure has not been public yet. The latest data released by the Railway Ministry is only till September 2019. Thus, the viral claim about Yadav's performance as the Railway Minister being unstained by any rail accident is patently false. Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Jun 5, 2023 10:12 IST

title: Fact Check: 2012 video of Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi FALSELY viral as jab at BJP after Odisha tragedy
content:
The viral video is more than a decade old and at the time, the UPA was at the Centre. It has nothing to do with the Odisha railway tragedy.
Following the devastating train accident in Balasore, Odisha, that has killed at least 275 and left more than a thousand people injured, a video of Bharatiya Janata Party leader Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi allegedly criticising the Centre over the mishap has been shared widely.
In the video , Naqvi could be heard saying, "The way train accidents are happening one after another — passengers are unsafe, there are no facilities. Without any facilities or safety, railway passengers are travelling. And this government that's ready to discuss everything is not ready to discuss the safety and convenience of railway passengers. Nor is it ready to implement them."
Sharing the video , one person tweeted, "At least one BJP leader dared to question his own government." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .
India Today's investigation found that the viral video is a decade old and has been shared out of context.
A keyword search led us to the full version of the viral video uploaded to the BJP's official YouTube channel on May 23, 2012. According to the video, Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi criticised the then-United Progressive Alliance or UPA government at the Centre and the Trinamool Congress' Mamata Banerjee over a railway accident in Andhra Pradesh.
Following the words that could be heard in the viral clip, Naqvi said: "Mamata Banerjee expressed concern over fare hike when the railway budget was presented and removed her minister for this reason. But she did not direct the new railway minister to look into passenger safety alongside fares. If passengers are not safe and accidents keep happening one after another, then that's a worrying matter and the government will be held accountable."
We looked for news reports on major railway accidents in India from around that time and found a BBC report from May 22, 2012. Per the report , the Bangalore-bound Hampi Express collided with a stationary goods train at the Penneconda station in Andhra Pradesh, killing 24 people and injuring almost as many.
Other news outlets also reported on this accident . Per the Ministry of Railways , Mukul Roy was the Railway Minister at that time.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video is a decade old and has nothing to do with the tragic accident at Balasore, Odisha. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 5, 2023 14:38 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Covid vaccine, these cows died after consuming poisonous plants
content:
The cattle in the photos died due to acute prussic acid poisoning on August 6, 2022. This acid comes from dhurrin, which is naturally present in young sorghum plants.
Covid-19 has ceased to be a global health emergency. Yet, anti-vaccine advocates are still dishing out conspiracy theories. A photo of dead cows  has been widely shared and allegedly, the animals died after the Italian government vaccinated them against Covid-19. One such tweet says, "Northern Italys Government came and vaccinated cattle against Covid-19. Look at the result all dead or dying the next day." Its archived version can be seen here . India Today found that the death of cows on such a large scale has nothing to do with Covid-19 vaccines. The massive cattle death in Italy was a result of acute prussic acid poisoning from plants. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story  Our Probe A reverse image of the viral pho led us to several news reports about cattle deaths in Italy. A report by Bangladesh's national news agency " Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha " that carried the viral photo attributed the cause of the cattle deaths to the drought in Italy. It was reported that around 50 cows died due to acute prussic acid poisoning on August 6, 2022. This acid, per the report, comes from dhurrin, which is naturally present in young sorghum plants — though not in the same high concentrations as those found in samples taken at the site. "We suspect that the drought caused this very large quantity of dhurrin within the sorghum plants," Stefano Giantin, a vet at the Istituto Zooprofilattico Sperimentale for northwest Italy, was quoted saying. The report said that because the drought stunted the growth of sorghum plants, dhurrin had concentrated inside them. The website of Corriere della Sera , Italy's oldest and most read newspaper, also carried a video report on the incident that occurred in Sommariva del Bosco, near Turin in northwest Italy. The news outlet attributed the cause to the drought as well. According to it, plants of the sorghum family secrete a compound called dhurrin , which releases hydrogen cyanide, commonly known as prussic acid when plants of this family are stressed by drought or frost. As per another report , upon ingestion of dhurrin, cattle can die in around 30–45 minutes. The chemical causes respiratory, nervous and muscular disorders. More than 900mg/kg of prussic acid  was found in the blood samples of the dead cattle. A dose of 700mg/kg of prussic acid is considered fatal for the animals. Death due to ingestion of sorghum plants containing higher concentrations of prussic acid, released under duress and stress is common . Such instances have been reported in many states in India  as well. Thus, it's clear that this has nothing to do with Covid-19 vaccines. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Jun 5, 2023 15:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Conspiracy theorists blame non-existent railway officer Mohammed Sharif for Odisha accident
content:
Bahanaga Bazar railway station was the closest to the accident site. The station master who was in charge at the time of the accident was SB Mohnty and he is not absconding.
On June 4, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told the press that the inquiry into the horrific railway accident that killed at least 275 in Balasore, Odisha, had been completed. He said that "as soon as the Commissioner of Railway Safety provides his report all the details will be known."
Vaishnaw added that the " root cause of the horrifying incident has been identified . I do not want to go into details. Let the report come out. I will just say that the root cause and the people responsible have been identified." But even as the details are awaited, many on social media have taken to sleuthing on their own. And this has led to conspiracy theories and misinformation. One such post alleged that the station master, a Muslim man named Mohammed Sharif, had been absconding ever since the tragedy occurred.Â
"Station Master Mohammed Sharif missing since the train crash. Threads are unravelling," read the post. The archived version of such posts can be seen here , here and here .
India Today found that the officer on duty at the station closest to the site of the accident was SB Mohnty. We found no Muslim senior officers listed working at the Bahanaga Bazar station.
The viral claim did not mention the name of the railway station where Sharif allegedly worked. We found that the Bahanaga Bazar railway station was the closest to the accident site. We could not find any credible news report about a station master by the name of Mohammed Sharif absconding from that station.Â
According to a report published by Odisha-based Kalinga TV, the assistant station master at the Bahanaga Bazar station was SB Mohanty .
India Today acquired the list of officers in the station's nominal roll. In this list, we couldn't find any employee by the name of Mohammed Sharif. According to that list, at the time of the accident, SK Pattnayak was the station manager. PK Panda, JK Nayak, and SB Mohnty were the superintendents. Â
Speaking to India Today, Pattnayak said that SB Mohnty was on duty at the time of the accident and he had been shifted to the Khurda Road Junction railway station after the accident for an inquiry. He also said everything would become clear after the inquiry and that Mohnty was not at fault for the accident.Â
Bahanaga Bazar station superintendent JK Nayak, speaking to India Today, said that no one called Mohammad Sharif handled station affairs. Nayak said, "No one is on the run. Everyone is cooperating in the inquiry. SB Mohnty, who was the station superintendent at the time of the accident, has been shunted to Khurda to join the investigation."
On June 4, the Odisha police tweeted warning those attempting to a communal spin to the train crash. "It has come to notice that some social media handles are mischievously giving communal colour to the tragic train accident at Balasore. This is highly unfortunate. Investigation by the GRP, Odisha into the cause and all other aspects of the accident is going on," the tweet said.
(With inputs from Rittick Mondal and Indrojit Kundu) Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Jun 5, 2023 17:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Cuttack hospital! DMK member shares 2022 pics of Gujarat hospital after Odisha train tragedy
content:
Both images are several months old and from Gujarat's Morbi civil hospital. They were shot before PM Modi visited the hospital to meet the survivors of the Morbi bridge collapse.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Odisha's Balasore on Saturday, June 3, a day after the train accident that claimed at least 275 lives and injured more than a thousand. The PM also met victims of the accident. The same day, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam IT wing's state deputy secretary Naveen N shared two photos showing repair work  being done inside a building, alleging that it showed a government hospital in Cuttack, Odisha, being renovated on account of the PM's planned visit there. On an account of PM's Arrival, renovation process in going on in a full swing at #Cuttack government hospital. Fate of the Nation 🙃 #OdishaTrainAccident #OdishaTrainAccident pic.twitter.com/GIu9NXRTuD — durgaiyan (@durgaiyandurga) June 3, 2023 He wrote, "On an account of PM's Arrival, renovation process in going on in a full swing at Cuttack government hospital. Fate of the Nation." This post was shared with the hashtag "Odisha Train Accident". Others shared the same photos and made the same allegation as well. Archived versions of those posts can be seen here  and here . India Today, however, found that the images making rounds are several months old and from Gujarat. Our Probe Upon reverse-searching the viral images, we found an India Today  report featuring both images published on November 1, 2022. Per the report, these images are from the Morbi civil hospital and were shot before PM Modi was set to visit there. Victims of the Morbi cable bridge tragedy were admitted there. On October 30, 2022, a suspension bridge over the Machchhu River in Morbi, Gujarat, collapsed , causing the deaths of at least 135 people and injuring more than 180. At the time, the Twitter accounts of the Aam Aadmi Party and the Congress shared these images and claimed that the hospital went through repairs to cover up its flaws before PM Modi paid a visit on November 1 to meet the injured. Morbi Civil Hospital में रातों रात रंग-पुताई की जा रही है ताकि कल PM Modi के Photoshoot में घटिया बिल्डिंग की पोल ना खुल जाए 141 लोग मर चुके हैं, सैकड़ों लोग लापता हैं, असली दोषियों पर कोई कार्रवाई नहीं हुई लेकिन भाजपाइयों को फोटोशूट करके लीपापोती की पड़ी है.. #BJPCheatsGujarat pic.twitter.com/KVDLdblD6C — AAP (@AamAadmiParty) October 31, 2022 त्रासदी का इवेंट कल PM मोदी मोरबी के सिविल अस्पताल जाएंगे। उससे पहले वहां रंगाई-पुताई का काम चल रहा है। चमचमाती टाइल्स लगाई जा रही हैं। PM मोदी की तस्वीर में कोई कमी न रहे, इसका सारा प्रबंध हो रहा है। इन्हें शर्म नहीं आती! इतने लोग मर गए और ये इवेंटबाजी में लगे हैं। pic.twitter.com/MHYAUsfaoC — Congress (@INCIndia) October 31, 2022 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The superintendent of Morbi civil hospital, Dr. Pradip Dudhrejiya, however, refuted these accusations  and said, "It is routine work and is taking place everywhere. The work is going on in every government setup." We also searched online to check if any similar repair or renovation work took place in any of Odisha's hospitals before the PM's visit, but found no credible news reports suggesting that. Thus, it is clear that months-old images from the Morbi civil hospital in Gujarat were shared in the context of the tragic Odisha train mishap. Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Jun 5, 2023 18:55 IST

title: Fact Check: 2021 video from Punjab becomes fodder for misinformation about police-army clash in Manipur
content:
This video is from a 2021 military training organised in Punjab's Pathankot, during which several soldiers collapsed because of extreme weather conditions.
While the internet continues to be suspended in Manipur, misinformation about the situation there appears to be plentiful. The northeastern state has been witnessing ethnic clashes between Meiteis and Kukis for a month now.Â
A new video, allegedly from the state, purports to show that clashes are now taking place between the military and the police there. It showed several uniformed men carrying a seemingly unconscious man towards a jeep. Other soldiers could be seen attempting to resuscitate two men. The whole scene seemed to unfold inside a cantonment.Â
"There has been a massive clash between Indian army soldiers (37 Assam Rifle Battalion) and Manipur police in which one Indian army soldier died while some others were severely injured," read a tweet containing the video. Archived versions of these tweets can be seen here  and here .
India Today, however, found that this video does not have any links to Manipur. It is from Pathankot in Punjab.
A keyword search about a standoff between the two forces fetched a news report from the Imphal Free Press. According to it, a confrontation reportedly took place at the Sugnu police station between the Sugnu police and the 37 Assam Rifles after the latter blocked the main entrance of the station on June 2.
We also found a video of the incident where officers could be seen arguing with each other as a huge military truck blocked the way. However, we could not find reports about a violent (even fatal) tussle between the two forces. Arguments erupted between the 37 Assam Rifles (37AR) and a team from the Manipur police outside Sugnu Police station. The incident unfolded at approximately 8:30 am in the morning on June 2 when the security forces were engaged in a heated exchange with each other. #Manipur … pic.twitter.com/bkwrvhqIUb — India Today NE (@IndiaTodayNE) June 2, 2023 Further searches led us to a tweet  from the Public Relations Officer for Kohima and Imphal in the Ministry of Defense. The tweet refuted the viral allegation. It said, "Indian Army & Assam Rifles rejects the fake video, that has emerged on social media, claiming casualties of a Assam Rifles in Manipur post scuffle with @manipur_police. The video depicts a training activity of army in Punjab in 2021." The official Twitter account of The Dimapur-based III Corps of the Indian Army (also known as Spear Corps) too tweeted the same information . #IndianArmy & #AssamRifles rejects the fake video, that has emerged on social media, claiming casualties of a Assam Rifles in Manipur post scuffle with @manipur_police . The video depicts a training activity of Army in Punjab in 2021. @SpokespersonMoD @PIBImphal @DiprManipur pic.twitter.com/IA66WnuQTN — PRO, Kohima & Imphal, Ministry of Defence (@prodefkohima) June 5, 2023 Using this clue, we found several tweets from August 2021 containing the video in question . According to these tweets, the video was shot during a Battle Physical Efficiency Test or BPET in Pathankot, Punjab. Allegedly, soldiers had collapsed following heat strokes and exhaustion. According to a news report by The Print , the training was organised in the area under the 9 Corps of the Indian Army at the Mamun military station. Nearly three dozen soldiers reportedly collapsed because of extreme weather conditions during a 10 km endurance run  as part of a recce troop competition. advertisement The Indian Army also issued a statement regarding this incident on August 21, 2021. According to it, the training was undertaken by "11 officers, 11 JCOs, and 12 other ranks" near Pathankot, Punjab. In an organized, supervised, and monitored training activity undertaken by 11 officers, 11 JCOs, and 120 other ranks near Pathankot in Punjab, due to severe weather conditions, there was one fatal casualty today: Indian Army (1/2) pic.twitter.com/phRHGVVNKj — ANI (@ANI) August 21, 2021 Thus, it is more than clear that an old video from Punjab is being peddled as a scuffle between Manipur police and the Indian Army. (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Jun 6, 2023 15:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Not a royal flush! AI pic viral as Chinese app-based mobile drone toilet
content:
This is not a real innovation but a concept design made using the AI tool Midjourney.
We live in the age of technological breakthroughs. So, to see social media gushing over weird new inventions is well within the ordinary. Of course, we should always be careful about what we believe on the internet.
"China has developed a mobile drone toilet that can be requested via an app remotely," claimed several tweets featuring a photo of a pristine white portable toilet fitted with propellers, sitting in the middle of what looks like a public park. The archived version of one such tweet can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the photo was not of a real invention — it was created by using an AI tool.
We looked for news reports about such an invention. Various searches in different languages yielded nothing. So, we reverse-searched the viral photo. This led us to a Facebook post featuring the same image by Jyo John Mulloor, who identified themselves as an "Artificial intelligence enthusiast."
Shared on May 15, 2023, this post featured several other designs of similar mobile drone toilets. In these posts , Mulloor made it clear that these designs were made using Midjourney, a generative artificial intelligence program that generates images from "prompts", similar to OpenAI's DALL-E and Stable Diffusion.Â
Mulloor named christened the drone toilet the "Shattle", whose logo could even be seen in the viral image, adding that it was just a concept design, making it evident that such drone toilets did not really exist.Â
On the same day, Mullor also shared several AI-generated photos of a conceptual drone sleeping pod that can "launch and take you on a journey to your chosen destination, where you can escape the hustle and bustle of everyday life and relax in the most beautiful and serene surroundings."Â
Therefore, it is clear that an AI-generated concept design was falsely shared as a futuristic Chinese innovation. Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Jun 6, 2023 17:23 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show June 6 blast at Ukraine's Nova Kakhovka dam, it's from 2022
content:
This video shows a November 2022 blast that happened on a road running across the Nova Kakhovka dam.
On June 6, the Nova Kakhovka dam in a Russian-controlled region of southern Ukraine was breached, creating fears of wide-scale flooding in the area. According to reports, around 22,000 people living across 14 settlements in Ukraine's Kherson region were at risk of flooding. Meanwhile, several videos, allegedly showing the damaged dam have been circulated on social media. Among them is CCTV footage  which purportedly shows the Nova Kakhovka dam blowing up. In the video, one can see a dam operating as normal. Suddenly there is a blast followed by a flash of light.  "The moment that the Nova Kakhovka dam was blown up," tweeted a person while sharing the video. The archived version of such posts can be seen here  and here .  India Today found that the video has been on the internet since as early as November 2022. As per the media reports from that time, it showed an explosion on a bridge that leads to the Nova Kakhovka dam and the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant. OUR PROBE Replying to the viral post, a Twitter account named War in Ukraine pointed out that they had shared the same video on November 12, 2022.  According to this account, the footage showed a blast at the bridge across the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant. #UkraineRussiaWar #Ukraine #Russia #UkraineWar 🚨 RV journalists confirmed the blowing up of the bridge across the #Kakhovskaya hydroelectric power station. This is first photo of the bridge this morning. The 3 bridge crossing the #Dnieper have now been destroyed by the russians pic.twitter.com/DE6m3wT8yr — 🛰️ War in Ukraine 🍉 (@EUFreeCitizen) November 12, 2022 With the help of a keyword search, we found the same video in reports by the BBC  and The Telegraph  that it was published on November 12, 2022. Per these reports as well, the video showed an explosion at a road that runs across the Nova Kakhovka dam. Per The Telegraph, the video was first uploaded on the website of the pro-war Russian newspaper Izvestia. According to the Izvestia report, Russian soldiers blew up the road running across the dam to slow the Ukrainian advance. The blast reportedly caused damage to sections of the Nova Kakhovka dam. The incident was also reported by The New York Times ( https://www.nytimes.com/2022/ 11/11/world/europe/kherson- bridge-russia-ukraine-war.html  ). The report noted that the blast happened after most Russian forces retreated and just before Ukraine's forces entered the city of Kherson. It is hence clear that the video in question is around seven months old and not related to the recent attack on the Nova Kakhovka dam. Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Jun 6, 2023 23:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Communal spin FALSELY added to 2022 Haldwani train incident after Balasore tragedy
content:
This incident is from 2022 and the man charged with endangering the lives of passengers was Hindu.
A video of a person pulling out the mangled remains of a gas cylinder from a train has been widely shared on social media. Allegedly, in Uttarakhand's Haldwani, a Muslim man threw a gas cylinder in front of a moving train . Those making the allegations linked it to the recent train accident in Balasore , Odisha, calling it a part of a larger conspiracy.
In the video, a person can be heard saying, "I have already informed the police and made a video of this incident. Let's make it viral. I fail to understand how he dared to do this?" The archived version of a tweet containing the video can be seen here .Â
India Today found that not only was the incident not recent, but the man charged for this was also Hindu. Our Probe
Using a keyword search, we found a tweet from the account "Railway Police Force North East Railways Izatnagar Division", responding to a viral tweet. This tweet stated that this incident took place on July 5, 2022, and the name of the person accused in this case was Gangaram, adding that a case had been registered against him. श्रीमान उक्त वीडियो के सम्बन्ध में रेसुब चैकी हल्द्वानी के उनि0 के द्वारा बताया गया कि उक्त वीडियो दिनांक-05.07.22 (पुराना वीडियो है) जिसमें मुअसं-131/22 अंतर्गत धारा/174, 153 रेल अधिनियम सरकार बनाम गंगाराम के विरुद्ध मामला पंजीकृत किया जा चुका है।
— @rpfnerizn (@rpfnerizn) June 5, 2023
श्रीमान उक्त वीडियो के सम्बन्ध में रेसुब चैकी हल्द्वानी के उनि0 के द्वारा बताया गया कि उक्त वीडियो दिनांक-05.07.22 (पुराना वीडियो है) जिसमें मुअसं-131/22 अंतर्गत धारा/174, 153 रेल अधिनियम सरकार बनाम गंगाराम के विरुद्ध मामला पंजीकृत किया जा चुका है।
— @rpfnerizn (@rpfnerizn) June 5, 2023
We also found that the Nainital police, too, had clarified on Facebook that this took place in 2022 and the accused in this case was arrested the same day.  Â
India Today accessed a railway police press release of the incident, which stated that the train was the Lucknow Kathgodam Express train, and the incident took place between Lalkuan and Haldwani in Uttarakhand. The note named the accused Gangaram, the son of Biharilal, a resident of the Pilibhit district of Uttar Pradesh.Â
The accused was presented before the court on July 5, 2022. The court sent him to judicial custody. A case was filed against him in the Resub Police Chowki of Haldwani. He was released on bail on September 1, 2022.Â
To ascertain the religious identity of the accused, India Today spoke to Pankaj Bhatt, the Senior Superintendent Of Police of Nainital. Bhatt said that the only accused in this case was Gangaram, and he was a Hindu. He further said that no Muslim person was involved in this incident.Â
Bhatt also clarified what had happened. He said: "When the accused Gangaram was arrested in this case, he told police that he was carrying his cylinder for refilling and was crossing the railway tracks when suddenly the train arrived. He dropped the cylinder in haste."
Rajendra Singh, the Public Relations Officer for the Izat Nagar Division in the North Eastern Railways, too, told India Today that the accused in this case was a man called Gangaram and that he was Hindu. Singh added that a case was immediately registered against him for endangering the lives of passengers.Â
It is noteworthy that following the tragic train accident in Odisha, there have been multiple attempts to add a false communal spin to it. The Odisha police too has appealed to people to refrain from sharing communally-coloured posts on social media. Â
To sum it up, a 2022 incident was shared in connection with the Balasore tragedy with a false communal spin.Â
(With input from Ankit Sharma) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 7, 2023 15:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Horrific video of millions of tyres burning is from Kuwait, but it's TWO YEARS old
content:
This video shows a 2021 arson incident at a 'tyre graveyard' in Kuwait.
As New York City became the most polluted city in the world on June 6, with massive clouds of haze seething from wildfires in Canada engulfing the city, a video of a sea of discarded tyres burning made the rounds on the internet.Â
"Look at this apocalyptic burn of 42 million tires in Kuwait, spewing toxic carcinogenic chemicals of benzene, xylene, ethylene, and acetone into the atmosphere. It could be seen on satellite from space," declared a tweet containing the video of uncountable tyres burning, with plumes of thick black smoke billowing from them. Its archived version can be seen here . advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story OUR PROBE Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found it in several media reports from August 2021. An India Today report  from August 2021 that contained a viral video reported that fire engulfed the world's largest "tyre graveyard" in Sulaibiya, Kuwait. The sheer scale of the fire, the report said, could be assessed from the fact that it was visible from space. We also came across several YouTube channels featuring the viral video from August 2021, which can be seen here and here . According to a France 24 report , satellite images captured a huge cloud of black smoke coming from a massive fire in the Salmi landfill in Kuwait's Jahra district. title: Fact Check: Heartwarming pic of child rescuing puppy is NOT related to recent Kakhovka dam attack in Ukraine
content:
This image is at least ten years old, and has been on the internet since as early as 2013.
Thousands of villagers in a Russian-controlled region of southern Ukraine are stuck  in a flood-like situation after the Nova Kakhovka dam was breached on June 6. Following that, several social media users shared a heartwarming photo of a child rescuing a puppy in a waterlogged area. While sharing this image , many claimed this was an outcome of the recent dam breach in southern Ukraine. "Young Ukrainian boy rescuing his dog from drowning after Russia destroyed the Kakhovka dam today," claimed several Facebook posts. The archived version of a similar post can be seen here . India Today Fact Check, however, has found that the image is at least ten years old and unrelated to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. Our Probe A reverse search of the viral image in Yandex took us to a YouTube video featuring the same picture in its thumbnail.  This video was uploaded to the verified channel of "People's Slavic Radio" on September 11, 2021, making it evident that the image in question could not be related to the recent incident. Another search with suitable keywords led us to a tweet posted by a person called Miguel Cunillera from May 20, 2014, that featured the same image. :( RT @Tech_HunterMX: Imagen de un niño Serbio, salvando a su perrito durante las inundaciones. pic.twitter.com/guIOfmJDqk — Miguel Cunillera (@MiguelCunillera) May 20, 2014 In Spanish, the tweet read, "Image of a Serbian boy, saving his puppy during the floods." With the help of this post, we found multiple blog posts , websites , and fundraising websites that contained the same image claiming that it was captured during the 2014 Serbia flood. In May 2014, a cyclone affected a large area of Southeastern and Central Europe, causing floods and landslides in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Reportedly, these two countries received the heaviest rainfall in 120 years resulting in massive floods that killed over 20 people. However, we also found a Croatian news report that debunked this image. It said that it was not shot during the aforementioned floods and that it had been on the internet since 2013 at least. Although we could not independently pinpoint the location or date of this photograph, it is certain that the image is not related to the dam breach in southern Ukraine.  Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jun 8, 2023 19:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Fake notice alert! No decision taken to consider B.Sc Nursing equivalent to MBBS
content:
The Nursing Council has said that it has not issued any such notice. The Health Ministry too, has called it fake.
Will B.Sc Nursing candidates now be considered equivalent to junior doctors with MBBS degrees? At least that's what some social media users are claiming .Â
Many shared a photo of what looked like a notification issued by the Indian Nursing Council. It said that all B.Sc nursing candidates would now be called "Nursing Officers" and the work of nursing candidates would be considered almost equal to that of MBBS candidates. The archived version of one such claim can be seen here. Â
India Today found that the viral notice was fake. The Indian Nursing Council did not issue any such notice. Fake notice
We found a Health Ministry tweet which called the viral notice fake and requested people to refrain from sharing it. #FakeNews This document is seen to be circulating on some social media platforms. This is a FAKE document. Please do not share it further. #MedicalEducation pic.twitter.com/owmND3w9lQ — Ministry of Health (@MoHFW_INDIA) June 8, 2023
#FakeNews This document is seen to be circulating on some social media platforms. This is a FAKE document. Please do not share it further. #MedicalEducation pic.twitter.com/owmND3w9lQ — Ministry of Health (@MoHFW_INDIA) June 8, 2023
We also scanned the official website of the Indian Nursing Council but did not find any such information.Â
On the contrary, we found a notice from June 8, calling the viral notification "fake and fabricated" . It said the document had "fake signatures" and that such a notification had "never been contemplated nor issued by the Council. All concerned are being advised to ignore the above fake and fabricated notification and desist from circulating or taking notice of the above fake notification in social media circles/ other platforms." The Indian Nursing Council added that it was contemplating taking steps to identify and punish the persons involved in circulating this fake notification. We also found that the Press Information Bureau, too, had rubbished the viral notice. Claim: A notification proposes equal status for https://t.co/gKIGXRFHYW . nursing candidates, considering them as nursing officers equivalent to MBBS and junior doctors #PIBFactCheck ▶️This Notification is #Fake . ▶️ Indian Nursing Council has not issued this Notification. pic.twitter.com/yADs6zLROP — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) June 8, 2023 Some nurses can still be called 'Nursing officers' The Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare issued a circular in 2017 that said all staff nurses should be called Nursing Officers and nursing sisters should be called Senior Nursing Officers. According to a report by Deccan Herald, the Karnataka government had also issued an order renaming nurses as nursing officers. Per the report, this change in nomenclature did not mean a change in grade or salary. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 8, 2023 22:21 IST

title: Fact Check: This helicopter DID NOT start wildfires in Canada, it's fighting fire with fire
content:
This is a process of extinguishing fire with fire called controlled burning or prescribed burning. A section of burnable forest is burnt beforehand to stop the wildfire from spreading.
US President Joe Biden spoke with his Canadian counterpart Justin Trudeau to offer to provide assistance to douse the "devastating and historic" wildfires burning in Canada. Biden offered to deploy federal assistance to suppress hundreds of blazes that have led to emergency situations and stress on Canada's firefighting resources.
Amid efforts to control the wildfires, a video making the rounds on social media shows a helicopter can be seen raining fire on, and setting ablaze a patch of forest. Sharing the video, many alleged that the wildfires in Canada were deliberately started using a helicopter.
One such tweet reads , "From British Columbia watching the fires get started with a helicopter." its archived version can be seen here .
India Today in its investigation found that the helicopter was part of the British Columbia Wildfire Service. It was fighting the wildfire by carrying out controlled burning, a process that prevents the further spread of wildfire.
We observed that the chopper in the video was yellow with blue and red and white lines running from the front to the rear end. It also featured a logo at the bottom right corner, which said, "British Columbia BC Wildfire Service".
Taking this clue, we performed keyword searches that led us to a recent video on the YouTube channel of Bloomberg Television. The video showed a helicopter over a large forest area engulfed in a fire, with a piece of equipment suspended beneath it. The equipment could be seen emitting flames and setting tree tops ablaze. The description of the video, however, provided no information as to what exercise this helicopter is conducting.
We found another video of a similar exercise by an identical helicopter on the Facebook page of the British Columbia Wildfire Service . The video uploaded on June 5 is captioned "Donnie Creek Wildfire-Planned Ignitions update June 4, 2023". The description stated that the BC Wildfire Service conducted a planned ignition on the Donnie Creek Wildfire that extends over 30 Kilometres.
It further detailed that planned ignitions were an essential wildfire management tactic, to contain a wildfire bringing its edge to establish containment lines and deter its further spread. Donnie Creek wildfire is currently the second-largest recorded wildfire the British Columbia's history . What is planned ignition?
Planned ignition, also known as controlled burning or backburning, is a technique that refers to controlled blazing under specified weather conditions. It is conducted by using either ground ignition or aerial ignition technique.
The aerial technique, also known as "helitorching", involves setting fire to a large area using aerial ignition devices , which generally hang from a helicopter. The devices use gasoline, or a mixture of gasoline and diesel, that has been thickened as an accelerant.Â
Planned ignition burns biomaterials including dead grass, fallen tree branches, dead trees, and thick undergrowth, consequently extinguishing the fuel available for a wildfire, and ultimately leading to its containment.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video doesn't show a helicopter starting wildfires in Canada. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 9, 2023 14:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of mother dog rescuing her puppies from floodwaters NOT related to Ukraine's dam collapse
content:
This video is more than seven years old; It has been on the internet since as early as December, 2015.
The collapse of the Nova Kakhovka dam in southern Ukraine on June 6 resulted in severe flooding and destruction of several villages.
Speaking to a US-based news site, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said dead bodies were found floating in the flooded areas. Per reports, as many as 300 animals at the Kazkova Dibrova Zoo also died in the flood.
Amidst this tragic event, a heartwarming video of a dog attempting to rescue her puppies from a waterlogged street started circulating on social media. In the video, a dog can be seen gently carrying the puppies in her mouth and swimming through the flooded waters. Those sharing the video claimed that the dog was trying to save her babies from the flood unleashed after the collapse of Nova Kakhovka dam. The archived version of such posts  can be seen here , and here .
India Today found that the video has been on the internet since as early as 2015. At that time, it was shared during the Chennai floods in Tamil Nadu.
A reverse search of the keyframes of the viral video led us to several media reports that featured the same clip and screenshots from it. According to a news report by Daily Mail published in December 2015, the video was from India . However, it made no mention of any particular place or state in this report.Â
On December 24, 2015, Yahoo News Australia also carried in its report , screenshots from the viral video. Per this report, the video was from the Chennai floods.Â
Around the same time, on December 22, 2015, the video was also uploaded on a YouTube channel named "Amazing Video's". The channel also stated that the clip was from the Chennai floods.
Several Facebook accounts as well shared the viral video in December 2015, claiming it was from the Chennai floods.Â
Chennai saw unprecedented flooding as a result of heavy rainfall between November and December, 2015. According to reports, it was the worst flood the city had experienced in a century.Â
We were not able to independently verify the location of the video. However, it is clear that the video is more than seven years old at least, and not related to the collapse of Ukraine's Nova Kakhovka dam. Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jun 10, 2023 20:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video from Bommai regime FASELY shared as Siddaramaiah insulting footballers
content:
This video is from March 2023, when the BJP's Basavaraj Bommai was the Chief Minister of Karnataka, not Siddaramaiah.
A video making the rounds on social media purports to show how new Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah kept the Santosh Trophy-winning football team waiting on the footpath outside his residence. In the video , a man questioned why the football team was kept waiting on the footpath for hours to meet the chief minister. He then criticised the Karnataka Football Association for not valuing the players.
On Facebook , one person shared the video and wrote, "The Karnataka state football team recently won the Santosh Trophy in Saudi Arabia, and the players were treated like this by the Chief Minister of Karnataka. Congress members have plenty of time for terrorists like Yasin Malik and Afzal Guru. Courts are opened at midnight to defend terrorists." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this incident is months-old. At the time, the Bharatiya Janata Party's Basavaraj Bommai was the Karnataka Chief Minister, not Siddaramaiah. Our Probe
According to a Times Of India report , the Karnataka football team won the Santosh Trophy on March 4, 2023, beating Meghalaya 3-2 in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh. Per the report, Karnataka last won the title 54 years ago.
Notably, when the Karnataka squad won the trophy, the Basavaraj Bommai-led BJP government was in power in Karnataka, not Congress. The results of the Karnataka assembly election were announced on May 13, and Siddaramaiah took oath as the Chief Minister on May 22.Â
We found news reports in the IB Times and Asianet featuring images of former Chief Minister Bommai with the football players confirming this meet-up. Â
The IB Times report, however, also criticised Bommai for making the players wait on the footpath and not even inviting them inside his residence. We compared screengrabs of the home seen in the viral video with images of Bommai's bungalow from news reports which confirmed that the players were indeed waiting outside the then CM's house.Â
The video, which has gone viral, was made by a YouTuber, Dhanraj Dhurve,  who makes videos on Indian football. We found the full video about this incident uploaded to his channel on June 8. It was titled, "Indian Football & players aren't for humiliation & disrespect. Why always us?".
So, while we could not independently find the person who recorded this video, it is more than clear that it dates from March 2023, when Basavaraj Bommai was the chief minister. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Jun 12, 2023 17:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Scary video of tall waves in Spain FALSELY viral as Cyclone Biparjoy in Gujarat
content:
This is an old video from Paseo Nuevo in San Sebastian, Spain.
Cyclone Biparjoy, which intensified into an extremely severe cyclonic storm on June 11, is likely to hit India's west coast and southern Pakistan later this week. The India Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for Mumbai and Thane and an orange alert for the Saurashtra and Kutch coasts of Gujarat. However, social media are already flooded with videos of high tides caused by the storm.
One such video showing high waves crashing on a shore was shared by a Pakistan-based Twitter account with over 61.3k followers. The tweet that this purported video of Biparjoy was from Madhavpur in Gujarat.Â
The tweet read, "Under the influence of very severe cyclonic storm 'Biparjoy' in Arabian sea which is passing nearby Gujarat coast, quite extreme sea-tides are being observed at Madhavpur (Gujarat)." The archived version of such posts can be seen here , here and here .
India Today, in its investigation, found that the video is old and is from San Sebastián, a resort town in the Bay of Biscay in northern Spain.Â
With the help of a reverse image search, we found multiple videos of high tide filmed from what appeared to be the same location. These videos were shared on Facebook and YouTube in 2021.Â
According to the posts, the videos were from northern Spain. "It's North of Spain, it happens roughly twice a year due to deep water sea wave that can reach up to 24m height. Force of nature," read the description of one such video.Â
We found a photograph of high tide from what looked like the same location on the stock image site Alamy . Per the website, the photo was shot at Paseo Nuevo in San Sebastián.Â
We found the Street View of Paseo Nuevo and were able to identify key similarities between that, the viral video, and the stock image. According to Google Maps and multiple other sites , the sculpture visible on the left side of the viral video is Construccion Vacia, designed by Spanish sculptor Jorge Oteiza. The island visible behind the sculpture is Santa Clara in San Sebastian , Spain.
It is, hence, clear that the video in question is from Spain and has nothing to do with Cyclone Biparjoy. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Jun 12, 2023 21:24 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this Hindu man did not kill his Muslim wife - photo of grisly suitcase corpse is not her
content:
The man and the woman in the photos are an interfaith couple from UP. Both are alive and well. The suitcase photo is from a 2022 Gurugram crime.
A disturbing set of photos being shared online allegedly shows how a young woman who married outside her faith was killed by her husband, stuffed inside a suitcase, and discarded. "The boy for whom she left her parents, left her religion, left her relatives, after fulfilling his lust, cut her and stuffed her in a suitcase," read a tweet containing these photos.
The insinuation here was that of the "Bhagwa Love Trap", a conspiracy theory like "Love Jihad", which purports that Hindu men seduce and entrap Muslim women to convert them to Hinduism. The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .
India Today's investigation found that the couple in the photo is from Uttar Pradesh and the woman was alive. The photo of the dead body in the suitcase is from Gurugram, Haryana. Our Probe
A reverse search of the photo of the dead body stuffed in a suitcase led us to several news reports from 2022. According to a news report   from October 19, 2022, the suitcase was discovered in Gurugram. A man called Rahul Kushwaha, per the report, confessed to the police that he killed his wife Priyanka.
Per the police, Rahul said that Priyanka would demand expensive appliances, which led to frequent fights. On the night of October 16, 2022, Priyanka allegedly slapped Rahul, which enraged him and he strangulated her. The following morning, Rahul allegedly bought a suitcase and stuffed her wife's naked body into it after peeling off the skin from her hand which had her name tattooed.
India Today had earlier fact-checked  posts claiming that the woman in the suitcase was a victim of "Love Jihad".
Other news reports related to this case contained no mention of the couple being interfaith or the woman having converted from Islam. So, we reversed-searched the photos of the couple. This led us to the Instagram account of the man in the photos.
Through Instagram, India Today was able to reach both Ravi Shrivastav and his wife Avni, the two people in the photos. India Today spoke to both via video call to confirm their identities.
Ravi, a resident of Moradabad in Uttar Pradesh, told India Today, "I am Hindu and [Avni] was Muslim. We married under the Special Marriage Act on May 8, 2023. She converted to Hinduism willingly after our marriage. I never forced her to convert. That's why we had a court marriage in Dehradun."
He said that he had shared their photos on Instagram and Facebook and people misused them to spread vicious rumours. "Because of all the fake claims, I removed all of her photos from social media. We love each other irrespective of all the barriers. Let us live," said Ravi.
Avni told India Today that she had converted to Hinduism of her own volition. "We fell in love and married according to the law. My name used to be Afreen, but it is now Avni. There is no disagreement between us. We have a happy marriage," she said.
Thus, it's clear that photos of an interfaith couple were shared on social media with misleading claims.
(With inputs from Vikas Bhadauria)
 Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 13, 2023 14:05 IST

title: Fact Check: Communal spin added to 2018 video of Colombian man getting electrocuted
content:
Victor Jose Arroyo Gonzalez was reportedly trying to die by suicide by jumping when he accidentally touched a live wire. This happened in Colombia in 2018.
WARNING: Graphic content A disturbing video of a man standing on top of a transmission tower and getting electrocuted has been shared on social media with some questionable claims. Allegedly, the man in the video was Muslim and he had climbed the tower to pray. The archived version of one such claim can be seen here. India Today found that this incident had happened in May 2018 in Colombia. The man, Victor Jose Arroyo Gonzalez, was not praying — he was trying to die by suicide. Our Probe Through reverse searches, we found the viral video's screengrabs in a Metro report from May 16, 2018, which stated that this happened in Barranquilla in northern Colombia's Atlantico department. Victor Jose Arroyo Gonzalez, a 20-year-old deaf man, reportedly climbed atop the pylon and threatened to jump off it. Per the report, he was suffering from depression and had threatened to die by suicide in the past as well. Reportedly, police officers and onlookers had managed to convince Gonzalez to not jump. Unfortunately, however, while he was trying to climb down, he accidentally touched a live wire and instantly died of electrocution. Many Spanish language websites had reported  this incident at the time. Geo-location According to a May 2018 news report  in the Spanish language news portal ZonaCero, this incident happened at the intersection of Calle 109 and Carrera 13B, in the Los Olivos neighbourhood of Barranquilla. Using Google Street View, we found a pylon at that intersection. We looked at other videos  of the incident , shot from different angles. In one of the videos , we noticed a white building adjacent to the tower, with two small and one large window and a slanting roof. There was also an electric pole near the building. We found the same markers on Street View. A comparison can be seen below. The religious angle India Today contacted Osvaldo Castilla Rojas, a Colombian journalist who had r eported this incident back in 2018. Rojas rubbished the claim that the man had climbed the tower to offer namaz. "He was a humble man with mental health issues who had climbed the same pylon earlier as well, with the intention to commit suicide. Unfortunately, that day he got electrocuted," she said. However, she couldn't confirm the man's religion. So, while we could not independently verify the man's religion, it's more than clear that a video of this tragic 2018 incident was shared with a communal spin. Published By: Sumana Nandy Published On: Jun 13, 2023 20:31 IST

title: Fact Check: No organ trafficking! Conspiracy theorists add false spin to video of young Syrian war victim
content:
The video was shot during the Syrian civil war in 2015. It shows healthcare workers treating a wounded child after Russian airstrikes in Idlib, Syria.
"In this disturbing footage, a young girl is seen being taken by traffickers. The girl is visibly panicked, her adrenaline surging as she is placed on a table with a tray positioned beneath her. It is believed that the traffickers intended to harvest either her adrenochrome or organs," read a viral tweet.
"In this video, we can also observe young children lying on harvesting tables and on the ground, seemingly discarded like refuse in bags," the tweet further read.
The video shared along with the tweet, was just as disturbing as the author claimed. In it, a child could be seen sobbing in a room that had dead bodies packed in polybags lying on the floor. The archived version of the viral tweet can be seen here .
Adrenochrome is a chemical compound produced by the oxidation of adrenaline. However, the belief that people harvest adrenochrome from the blood of children is part of new-age American conspiracy theories like QAnon and Pizzagate.Â
So, does the viral video have anything to do with harvesting organs and adrenochrome? Nope. India Today found that the video actually shows a child being treated for injuries received during Russian airstrikes in December 2015 in Idlib, Syria.
In the upper left corner of the video, the watermark of "SMART" could be seen. We found that it was a Syrian news agency . Using this as a clue, we reverse-searched keyframes of the viral video with keywords related to Syria. This led us to a Facebook post containing a news report that featured the viral clip.Â
The caption of this video shared by the Shaam News Network on May 14, 2017, said in Arabic, "Zainab is still alive... to refute the deception of the Assad media." In the video, the SNN journalist spoke to the child, Zainab, and her father. The video featured texts running throughout its length.
They read in Arabic: "Scenes from Muhalabiya, massacre in Idlib"; "Zainab six-year-old from Kafra Nabudah; "Loyalists of the Assad regime recirculated the massacre videos as organ trading operations"; and "Shaam Network met the little girl and her father".Â
What's more, this report also addressed the organ harvesting claims that had gone viral in the past as well.
Zainab's father told the journalist, "It's a big lie. I lost my sister and two kids in the Russian airstrikes. My daughter is in good health and the allegations that my daughter's organs were extracted and sold are utterly a lie. She's in good health."
Syria Charity , a partner of the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), also refuted the viral claim on its Facebook account.
The Facebook post made on May 15, 2017, and captioned, "This little girl wasn't eviscerated for organ trafficking", carried an interview of Zainab's father.
Calling all such viral claims of organ trafficking a hoax, he said, "Whatever the ruling dispensation claimed is fabricated." Pointing at her daughter, he said she was all fine.
On being asked how he felt as a father when such allegations were made, he said he was shocked. "The regime first bombed us then broadcasted lies. I, too, lost my leg and an eye in the airstrike. Now all this has worsened my sufferings," he said.
We also came across two fact-check reports about the organ harvesting claim from 2017, published by International Fact-Checking Network certified organisations.
The reports stated that the video was shot in a makeshift clinic in a Syrian village ravaged by war. The corpses lying on the floor were victims of bombings. They further noted that the girl wasn't crying out of fear that her organs were about to be extracted, but because she too had suffered injuries in the airstrikes.
Fact-checking organisation Teyit identified the healthcare staff belonging to the Al Sham Humanitarian Foundation by identifying the logo visible on the back of a person seen in the video. Al Sham Humanitarian Foundation  is a charity organisation that provides shelter, food, and water aid for the victims of the Syrian war. Besides, they also cater to health services in case of emergencies.
Thus, it's clear that an old video of a wounded Syrian child getting treated at a makeshift clinic went viral with dubious claims. Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Jun 13, 2023 22:51 IST

title: Fact Check: This is a sandstorm in Suez Canal - NOT Cyclone Biparjoy hitting the Pakistan coast
content:
This video shows a June 1 sandstorm in Egypt's Suez Canal.
India and Pakistan are on high alert over Cyclone Biparjoy, which is expected to hit both countries' Arabian Sea coasts on June 15. Meanwhile, a video  of a massive sandstorm sweeping across a water body is being shared on social media. Allegedly, this storm was approaching Pakistan's Karachi.
The archived versions of such posts that were also viral in Urdu  can be seen here  and here .
India Today found that the video shows a sandstorm that hit Egypt's Suez Canal on June 1. Our Probe
With the help of a reverse image search, we found several media reports that featured the same clip. According to a CNN repor t published on June 2, the video was from a sandstorm in Egypt's Suez Canal. The report also said while sandstorms are common in Egypt during the summer, this one was "unusually strong".
We also found the same video in a BBC report  from the same date. According to it, the sandstorm occurred on June 1. Apart from the Suez Canal, a massive cloud of sand was also seen moving across the road linking Cairo and Suez.
Reportedly, one person was killed and at least five were injured when a billboard collapsed as a result of the storm in Egypt's capital Cairo.
According to a Reuters report  on Cyclone Biparjoy, as India began evacuating people from coastal areas on June 13, four people drowned off Mumbai's coast. High waves and heavy rains in Gujarat's coastal areas also killed three people in the Kutch and Rajkot districts.
It is thus clear that the video in question was from a sandstorm in Egypt's Suez Canal, and not from anywhere near Pakistan's coast. Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Jun 14, 2023 14:46 IST

title: Fact Check: This quote is fake! Aussie keeper DID NOT admit Shubman Gill catch was unclean
content:
This is a made-up quote. About the controversial catch, Alex Carey said that "the right decision was made."
Australia vanquished India at the Oval in London in the 2023 ICC World Test Championship final, and in its aftermath, there has been much debate about Shubman Gill's dismissal in the second innings. Gill was batting on 18 when he edged Scott Boland low to the left of the gully, where Cameron Green dived to take the catch extremely close to the ground. The decision was referred to the third umpire, who determined it was an out. Of course, many fans have contended against this decision. Adding fuel to this fiery debate now is a purported quote from Australian wicketkeeper Alex Carey. "Greeny knew he didn't pick it up cleanly, he told me he might have picked it up from the ground but guess we got lucky with the TV ump [sic] there," Carey allegedly said according to posts widely shared on Facebook and Twitter. An archived version of such a post can be seen here . (Alex Carey on Shubman Gill's wicket ) Greeny knew he didn't pick it up cleanly, he told me he might have picked it up from the ground but guess we got lucky with the TV ump there. Shame on the 3rd umpire. #WTCFinal pic.twitter.com/O8fR0SP6J9 — Roshan Rai (@RoshanKrRaii) June 10, 2023 India Today, however, found that the quote was made-up. Carey never said this. In fact, he said something to the contrary. Our Probe Multiple searches with various keywords did not lead us to any reports about Carey making such a comment. However, we found an ANI report from June 11, the final day of the test match, quoting Carey saying that the TV umpire made the right decision. "Looked good to me. We were happy and the right decision was made," Carey reportedly said when asked about the catch. A report from Sportskeeda also said the same. We also found a tweet made by cricket expert Mufaddal Vohra, with the same quote from Carey from June 10, a day before the test match ended.  Alex Carey said, "Cameron Green's catch looked good from my end. The right decision was made". pic.twitter.com/bnN6ONbIul — Mufaddal Vohra (@mufaddal_vohra) June 10, 2023  Next, we looked for the visual evidence of Carey saying the same and came across it in the repeat telecast of the fourth day of the test match available on Hotstar. When asked what's his take on Cameron Green's catch after the play of day four, Carey said, "I thought he caught it fair in the square. It looked good from where I was. He was really happy with it. So, yeah, I think the right decision was made." Thus, it is clear that the quote in circulation is completely made up.  Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jun 14, 2023 17:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Horrifying video of car drowning is NEITHER from Karnataka NOR related to Cyclone Biparjoy
content:
The video is from Nicaragua in Central America and has nothing to do with Cyclone Biparjoy.
According to the India Meteorological Department, Cyclone Biparjoy is expected to make landfall in Gujarat's Saurashtra and Kutch regions and the adjoining Pakistani coasts on June 15. As a consequence of the cyclonic activities, other parts of India, including Karnataka, are also experiencing heavy rains.Â
Amid this, a terrifying video  of a car drifting off a waterlogged road into a nearby river has been widely shared. The video shows an SUV being pulled into the stream by the sheer force of the current and subsequently getting pummeled by muddy waters.Â
Allegedly, this video was from Dandeli, a town near the Hubli-Dharwad region of Karnataka. The video was shared with the hashtag "Cyclone Biparjoy". Its archived version can be seen here .
India Today, however, found that the video is from the Central American country Nicaragua.
A reverse search of frames from the video led us to a tweet from May 30 that contained the same video . The tweet said in Spanish, "Gentlemen, let's not put our lives in danger for an act of irresponsibility just because we drive a car that we think makes us stupid, we have a family, let's be prudent, thank God the driver survived and there was only material damage."
In response to another person asking where the video was from, the original poster said  Nicaragua. Another person, in the responses, shared a screenshot  of a Spanish-language news report from May 29 that contained grabs from the viral clip. Its headline said, "VIDEO: Strong current of water dragged a truck along with its driver; did not survive." pic.twitter.com/bs7oYetfh7 — Katherine Raudales (@knra25) May 30, 2023 Additional text in the screengrab added in Spanish, "The rainy season is already in force in Central America and in Nicaragua, the heavy downpours have already caused the death of a man this Monday after being swept away by a stream of water when he was driving his car." Subsequently, we found several news reports  about the incident on Spanish-language news sites . Reportedly , the incident took place in Veracruz, in the municipality of Nindirí in Nicaragua. The driver of the Toyota SUV seen drowning in the viral video was identified as Alberto Uriel Romero Martínez. The 48-year-old reportedly managed to jump out of the truck, which is visible in the viral video. However, he drowned in the waters. Firefighters and the National Police found his body in the Los Cocal region near the Managua International Airport. We also found the footage  of the incident on the official YouTube channel of "100% Noticias", a Nicaraguan broadcaster. The channel also contained a video of the same incident shot from another angle . So, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with India or Cyclone Biparjoy. Incidentally, this tragic incident wasn't just shared with misleading claims in India. In Sri Lanka, it went viral as an incident in the town of Haputale. This too was debunked  by fact-checkers. Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jun 14, 2023 20:32 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOESN'T show Cyclone Biparjoy in Gujarat, it's at least 4 years old!
content:
This video has been on the internet since as old as May 2019. At the time, it was widely shared as destruction caused by Cyclone Fani in Puri, Odisha.
Photos and videos of huge waves and tempestuous waters have been making the rounds on social media, with Cyclone Biparjoy all set to make landfall in India and Pakistan's Arabian Sea coasts. One such dramatic video shows an Indian Oil petrol pump caught up in a storm. The canopy of the petrol station was seen being ripped apart by strong winds.
Allegedly the video showed Dwarka, Gujarat, experiencing recent cyclonic weather, and those sharing the video used hashtags related to Biparjoy. Its archived version can be seen here .
India Today, however, found that the viral video is old and not related to stormy winds caused by Biparjoy. The video has been on the internet since as early as May 2019 when Cyclone Fani hit Odisha. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Daily Mail report from 2019 that featured what looked like a longer version of the same video. According to the report, a petrol station in India was wrecked by winds stronger than 200 km/h induced by Cyclone Fani. The report, however, did not add where in India the video was from.
We also found the video in question shared on Dailymotion , a video-sharing platform. The video titled "Dramatic moment Indian petrol station is engulfed in dust by cyclone winds" was shared by an account called Newsflare on May 3, 2019.Â
Further, we came across YouTube uploads of the viral video shared four years ago, which can be shared here  and here . Descriptions on YouTube said that the incident occurred in Puri, Odisha, but missed out on details.
We found the video also shared in a News18 report from May 5, 2019, two days after Fani made landfall in Odisha. The report, which was a curation of videos shared on social media, did not however independently verify if the video was from Puri as the tweet claimed.Â
Fani killed more tha 60 people in Odisha in 2019 and destroyed infrastructure and property all over the state. According to an India Today report  from May 2019, Puri suffered extensive damage.Â
While we couldn't establish the exact location or date of the incident with certainty, it is clear that it is at least four years older than Cyclone Biparjoy. Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Jun 15, 2023 15:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Two FAKE Biparjoy videos that hit social media even before the cyclone made landfall
content:
This CGI video has been on the internet since as early as 2018. It has nothing to do with Cyclone Biparjoy.
Cyclone Biparjoy is expected to make landfall on the Gujarat coast on the evening of June 15. In preparation, the Gujarat government has evacuated around 75,000 people from coastal and low-lying areas to safety. Several videos and photos purportedly showing the cyclone in action have already gone viral on social media. In this article, we will fact-check two such videos. Boat in stormy waters The first video  shows a boat navigating large waves and strong winds. Those sharing the video claimed it was recently recorded off the coast of Gujarat. The archived version of the post can be seen here . Gujrat cyclone biparjoy #Gujrat #cyclone #biparjoy pic.twitter.com/VH5rzKBUH8 — SANDIP KUMAR KANANI 🇮🇳 (@SANDIPKANANI19) June 13, 2023 Reverse-searching frames from the video, we found that the same clip was shared on the Facebook page of "RNLI Fraserburgh Lifeboat" on January 22, 2021. The accompanying text stated, "A short video taken by Larry Wood today as Fraserburgh ALB 'Willie and May Gall' opened up the harbour making ready for our run-in." On the same day, the page also shared another of a similar-looking boat. We noticed that both boats had the same registration number, proving that they were the same vessel.  The Royal National Lifeboat Institution or RNLI  is a non-profit organisation that offers search and rescue operations across the British Isles. We found that the page that uploaded these videos was not its official Facebook page. A representative from the organisation, however, told India Today that while their team may not have captured the video, the boat featured in the video did belong to the RNLI. So, it's clear that this video had nothing to do with Cyclone Biparjo, or even India for that matter. A tornado's formation The second video  of a tornado forming all of a sudden over a sea allegedly showed Cyclone Biparjoy hitting the Gujarat coast. "The dangerous encirclement of the storm coming towards Gujarat was caught on camera," wrote a Twitter user while sharing it. The archived version of the post can be seen here . The dangerous encirclement of the storm coming towards #Gujarat Was caught on camera.... 🌀🌀 #Kutch #Gujaratcyclone #GujaratWeather #CycloneBiporjoy #BiparjoyAlert #Biperjoy #BiparjoyUpdate #BiparjoyAlert #biporjoycyclone #NewsUpdate #cycloneBiperjoyupdate pic.twitter.com/UIkFPCWLL4 — ❢ ▬❤️ℜαhบl やαnchαℓ❤️▬ ❢ (@itz_silentking) June 15, 2023 Using a reverse search on the video's keyframes, we found the same clip on the YouTube channel "orphicframer", shared on December 22, 2018. According to the video's title, it was a computer-generated imagery or CGI simulation of a tornado in New Jersey. Its description further stated that it was created using Adobe After Effects and Cinema 4D. We also found that the channel was full of CGI videos. Thus, it's clear that this video as well had nothing to do with Cyclone Biparjoy. Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Jun 15, 2023 18:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Rain-dancing through Cyclone Biparjoy? Nope, this funny video of Indian 'jugaad' is from 2022!
content:
The video is neither recent nor related to Cyclone Biparjoy. This is a 2022 incident that took place in Indore, Madhya Pradesh.
Even before Cyclone Biparjoy could make landfall, a wave of videos and photographs claiming to show the severe cyclonic storm hit the internet.Â
Among them was an odd video of a wedding procession. It showed "baraatis" marching on and dancing to Daler Mehndi's iconic song "Bolo Tara Rara" despite the heavy downpour. And the revellers did so while carrying a giant yellow tarpaulin that shielded them from the rain.
One person, sharing the 47-second video, tweeted , "Cyclone Biporjoy cannot stop the wedding processions Indians are well prepared in Advance." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found the viral video is old and has nothing to do with Cyclone Biparjoy. This bemusing incident happened in Indore in 2022.Â
We ran a reverse image search on some of the keyframes from the viral video and came across a slew of media reports from July 2022. As per an India Today report published on July 6, 2022, this amusing incident took place in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. The report noted that the "baraat" or the procession was heading towards the wedding venue, covered by a huge tarpaulin amid heavy rainfall.Â
An Economic Times report stated that the weather was dry when the procession started. However, when it began raining all of a sudden, instead of stopping the procession, the "baraatis" improvised and ordered a large tarpaulin to cover themselves.
Several other reports testifying that the incident is a year old and from Indore can be seen here and here .
Thus, it is evident that an old video from Indore has been passed off as a recent visual of Cyclone Biparjoy's effects.
