title: Fact Check: Did US President Biden step on cat while giving speech?
content:
The video was edited to add the cat scream sound. Biden did not step on a cat, he stumbled on a floor wire.
A video of United States President Joe Biden  that's been widely shared on social media allegedly shows him stepping on a cat while delivering a speech. In the video , Biden, while speaking, was interrupted by the sound of a cat screaming. While the cat did not appear in the frame, Biden could be seen looking down and saying, "Whoops, stepping on him. But it's black. Anyway—." The archived version of the tweet can be seen here . India Today found that the video was edited. Biden did not step on a cat. Rather, he stumbled on a floor wire. Our Probe A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report  in the New York Post dated November 6, 2022. Per the report, Biden joined New York Governor Kathy Hochul in Yonkers, in the run-up to New York's 2022 gubernatorial election, where he nearly fell after stumbling on stage during the speech. Forbes shared a longer speech of Biden on its official YouTube channel on November 7, 2022. The viral clip appeared around the eight-minute mark. In it, while delivering a speech, Biden stumbled, looked down, and said, "It's black. Anyway". Then, he paused for a few seconds and started speaking again. In this video, however, there was no sound of a cat screaming. NBC News affiliate WGRZ-TV  also shared the same video on its official YouTube channel the same day. On November 6, 2022, the White House released the official transcript  of that event. Per the report, President Biden stumbled on a floor wire. The same was reported by American news network C-SPAN . We also found that Lead Stories debunked the viral claim on April 5, 2023. Thus, it is evident that Biden did not step on a cat while delivering a speech. - Ends Published By: Rajeev Singh Published On: Aug 2, 2023 21:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of K Annamalai dancing with Kala Master is not from BJP's padayatra in Tamil Nadu
content:
This video is from Annamalai's campaign in the run-up to the 2021 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections.
Tamil Nadu Bharatiya Janata Party president and former IPS officer K Annamalai is on a six-month-long statewide padayatra. The rally called En Mann En Makkal or My Land, My People  began at Rameswaram, in Ramanathapuram on July 28.Â
Now, a video of Annamalai dancing alongside a woman on top of a vehicle is making the rounds on social media. The woman was wearing a saffron scarf with the BJP symbol on it. In the background, the song "Kaavaalaa" from the upcoming Rajinikanth movie "Jailer" could be heard. Allegedly, this video was shot during his ongoing padayatra.Â
India Today found that the video is from a 2021 election campaign in Tamil Nadu. The song heard in the background was digitally added later. OUR PROBE
With the help of a keyword search, we found a longer version of the viral video shared on the Facebook page of Samayam Tamil, a news outlet that's part of the Times of India group  on April 4, 2021. According to the post, the video was shot during Annamalai's campaign in the runup to the Tamil Nadu Assembly polls. The woman dancing alongside him was identified as film choreographer Kala, professionally known as Kala Master.
In this version of the video, a pro-BJP election campaign song could be heard in the background. Kala Master could also later be seen exiting the vehicle and dancing with the crowd. The Indian Express Tamil  and Samayam Tamil  also published articles about Kala joining Annamalai's election campaign in April 2021.
The Indian Express Tamil  and Samayam Tamil  also published articles about Kala joining Annamalai's election campaign in April 2021.
According to reports, the video was captured on the last day of campaigning for the 2021 Assembly elections in Tamil Nadu. Annamalai was the BJP candidate  from the Aravakurichi Assembly constituency, and Kala Master joined him for campaigning.
The video was also shared by the choreographer on Twitter on April 4, 2021. Fantastic response - Undoubtedly the winner @narendramodi @BJYMinTN @annamalai_k @cibi_m @BJP4India @AmitShah @blsanthosh @JPNadda @khushsundar pic.twitter.com/L4BByr6P6q — Kala Master (@kala_master) April 4, 2021
Fantastic response - Undoubtedly the winner @narendramodi @BJYMinTN @annamalai_k @cibi_m @BJP4India @AmitShah @blsanthosh @JPNadda @khushsundar pic.twitter.com/L4BByr6P6q — Kala Master (@kala_master) April 4, 2021
In conclusion, it is clear that the video in question is from Annamalai's campaign during the 2021 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections and has no relation to his ongoing padayatra. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Aug 3, 2023 18:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Unrelated video of Muharram procession in Bengal falsely linked to Haryana violence
content:
The video is not related to ongoing Haryana violence. The video was captured in West Bengal's Murshidabad on the day of Muharram.
Amid the ongoing violence in Haryana, a video that's going viral  shows a group of young men and children marching and dancing with weapons and Islamic flags. One person shared the video on Twitter  and wrote: "What is the motto behind this level of radicalisation among children? The Mewat Terror Attack exposed the truth of the so-called Ganga-Jamuni Tehzeeb, which not only failed to achieve peace but also became the subject matter of atrocities against Hindus in their own homeland." He also used other hashtags related to the ongoing violence in the state.Â
Others shared it with hashtags related to the violence in Mewat (Nuh district). Archives of similar posts can be seen here , here , and here .
India Today found that the video is not related to ongoing violence in Haryana. It is from West Bengal's Murshidabad. Our Probe
In the viral video, we observed a statue in the background that featured people carrying a blue globe that had the Bangla letter "B" written on it. Statues featuring the emblem are all over West Bengal. This indicated that the video was likely shot in the eastern state.
After that, a reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the Facebook profile of Shaikh Aptaj Bharatiya, who shared this video  on July 29 and claimed it was from Dhuliyan, Murshidabad.Â
With the help of that clue, we found the actual place on Google Maps Street View.
The sculpture, the signboard, the blue railings, and the houses seen in the viral video matched with the Street View.
India Today also reached out to locals, who confirmed that the video was captured on Dakbangla and Dhuliyan State Highway, near Dhuliyan Municipality on July 29, the day of Muharram. The procession went towards Dakbangla from Dhuliyan Kanchan Tala High School in the afternoon.
Thus, it is safe to conclude that the video is not related to ongoing Haryana violence. The video was captured in West Bengal's Murshidabad on the day of Muharram. - Ends (With inputs from Gopal Thakur, Murshidabad) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Aug 4, 2023 16:34 IST

title: Fact Check: These women crying before Assam Rifles officials are Kuki, NOT Meitei
content:
The women seen crying before the Assam Rifles officials are Kuki, not Meitei.
A heart-wrenching video of a group of women crying before a uniformed officer has gone viral on social media. Allegedly, the women were Meitei Hindu women and they were begging army officials to not leave as they did not have faith in the state security forces. In the video, slogans like, "Assam Rifles, don't leave us," could be heard. An Instagram user  shared the video and wrote, "Save Meitei Hindus." Its archived version can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video shows Kuki women pleading with Assam Rifles officials not to leave the area. They were protesting against the Centre's plan to withdraw the Assam Rifles from the buffer zones in the Kangpokpi district. Our Probe
Using a keyword search, we found that the incident seen in the viral video was reported in detail by The Telegraph  on August 4, 2023. Per this report, the video shows Kuki-Zo women in the Kangpokpi district of Manipur requesting Assam Rifles troops not to leave a village located on the border of the Meitei-majority Imphal West because of the volatile situation in the buffer zone between the two districts. The buffer zone is a border between the Kuki and Meitei area, guarded by Central Security Forces.
Reportedly, the Kuki women staged a protest at Gamgiphai village after they came to know that the Assam Rifles personnel deployed in the peripheral area had been shifted to Churachandpur, over 110 km away, by the state government. They blocked the road so that the Assam Rifles personnel could not leave.
Lamminlun Singsit, secretary of the Kangpokpi-based Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU), told The Telegraph, "There is a fear that removing central forces without adequate replacement will expose the area to attack from well-equipped Meitei militants."
The Hindustan Times  and T imes Now also published reports about this incident. All the reports noted that the women seen crying in the video were Kuki. Clues in the video
Using a keyword search, we found a longer version of the video. At around the 3.35-minute mark in this video, the Assam Rifles official could be heard saying, "And if we have to go to CC Pur (Churachandpur) tomorrow, it is to keep your community safe, it is already ensured that the Meiteis don't attack. And to keep the Meitei community also safe."
It is likely that he meant Kuki when he said "your community" as referred to Meiteis separately next. Also, he said that it had been ensured that the Meiteis did not attack. Had the women seen in the viral video been Meiteis, he wouldn't have spoken about ensuring their safety from the group. Kuki leaders, journalists, security forces confirm
Ginza Vualzong, the official spokesperson of The Indigenous Tribal Leaders' Forum (ITLF) confirmed to India Today that the video shows Kuki women from the Kangpokpi district of Manipur. "Assam Rifle officials were leaving which made them feel insecure. They do not trust the local police. The local police are not capable enough to resist militant attacks," he said.
We also spoke to Haopu Gangte, the General Secretary of Kuki INPI, an organisation which describes itself as the apex body of Kuki Tribes. He said that the viral video shows Assam Rifles officials surrounded by Kuki women. "The video was recorded on the night of August 2 at around 2:00 am. The women were crying and pleading till dawn.
We spoke to two journalists from Manipur and they too said that the viral video shows Kuki women crying before the Assam Rifles officials. And finally, a spokesperson from the Assam Rifles also confirmed this to India Today.
As per a report by India Today North East , following the protests, the Centre halted plans of withdrawing Assam Rifles troops from the buffer zones.
Thus, it's abundantly clear that the viral video did not show Meitei women pleading with army officials. - Ends Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Aug 6, 2023 13:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Misleading video collage combines floods in China and Spain
content:
The first video in this collage is old and is related to floods in Spain.
China's capital, Beijing, recently experienced record-breaking rainfall due to Typhoon Doksuri, resulting in devastating floods and the loss of at least 21 lives. While the situation remains dire, a video collage purportedly showing flood in China has gone viral. The video collage comprises two parts: the first shows cars being swept away by floodwaters, with individuals clinging to the roofs for their lives. The second part shows cars floating in a massive water body. A Twitter user posted the video  and wrote, "Life & death moment in #China." An archived version of this post can be seen here . India Today found that while the second part of the video indeed shows the floods in China , however, the first part is not related to the current situation. Instead, it was filmed during the floods in Spain in early July 2023. Our Probe Several concerned social media users reacting to the viral post raised doubts about the video's authenticity , questioning whether it genuinely depicted the floods in China. We conducted a reverse search of the first part of the video's keyframes, and found it on YouTube  where users had shared it in the context of floods in Spain during early July. Where did this happen? On further examination with keyword searches, we came across media reports from July, 2023 , featuring the viral video . The reports explicitly mentioned that the visuals depicted the flash floods in Zaragoza, Spain. Several Spanish language media  outl ets also shared this video  in early July, adding to its widespread circulation. Some visuals of the recent floods in China can be seen here . Thus, it is clearly established that the video collage circulating on social media, while featuring genuine footage of the floods in China in its second part, also included an unrelated video of the flash floods in Spain from early July 2023. - Ends Published By: Rajeev Singh Published On: Aug 6, 2023 16:34 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of PTI protest in Pakistan FALSELY shared as recent after Imran Khan arrest
content:
This video is from November 4, 2022. This protest took place a day after Imran Khan was shot.
Political unrest in Pakistan reached a new peak after the fresh arrest of former Prime Minister Imran Khan on August 5. The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf chairman was sentenced to three years in prison in the Toshakhana case  by an Islamabad trial court. Since then, the country has witnessed a series of protests  by PTI supporters.Â
In its aftermath, a video of a protest  went viral on social media. Hundreds of protesters could be seen gathered both on top of and under a bridge. Many attributed these visuals to a protest in Pakistan's Faizabad after Khan's arrest.
"Visuals of protest after Imran Khan's arrest in Faizabad, Pakistan right now," read one such tweet. Its archived version can be seen here . Faizabad right now pic.twitter.com/vcIPjUBfVd — Sheikh Imtiaz Mehmood (@SheikhImtiazPK) August 5, 2023
Faizabad right now pic.twitter.com/vcIPjUBfVd — Sheikh Imtiaz Mehmood (@SheikhImtiazPK) August 5, 2023
India Today, however, found that the video is at least nine months old and unrelated to Imran Khan's recent arrest. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an Indonesian news report  from November 5, 2022, that featured a video of a similar protest.
As seen in the viral video, this video shows the same bridge with a mob. The report mentioned that this protest was held on November 4, 2022, in Rawalpindi, a day after Imran Khan was shot. Reportedly, protestors headed towards the capital city of Islamabad and pelted stones.
In a subsequent search, we stumbled upon a report in Al Arabiya  with the same bridge featured in it. The caption of the photo read, "File photo of a protest in Rawalpindi, Pakistan November 4, 2022." A Daily Mail report also carried photographs from the same protest site and mentioned that it took place in Rawalpindi.
A refined search with Urdu keywords helped us to find an older version of the viral clip shared on November 4, 2022. A Pakistani journalist named Khurram Iqbal tweeted this video  and wrote in Urdu, "Tehreek-e-Insaf workers and Islamabad Police, face to face in Faizabad."
Pakistan's Faizabad is located at the end of Rawalpindi city and works like a junction or connector between Rawalpindi and Islamabad. Additionally, we searched for English and Urdu keywords to determine whether a similar demonstration took place after Khan's arrest on August 5, but found nothing.
It is therefore safe to conclude that an old video of a PTI protest has been falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Aug 7, 2023 14:44 IST

title: Fact Check: No truth to Muslim refugee link in New York PlayStation 5 giveaway chaos
content:
The unrest was caused by the overwhelming number of attendees during a giveaway event organised by popular Twitch streamer Kai Cenat.
A video has surfaced depicting a scene of chaos and unrest at an undisclosed location. Those sharing it claimed that the turmoil was instigated by Muslim refugees, fuelling allegations of terror and rioting. The video shows individuals dressed in police uniforms seeking refuge behind a large plastic board or sheet while a barrage of projectiles, including bottles and other objects, were hurled at them.
A Twitter user sharing the viral video wrote, "US. Now the terror of refugee Muslims continues in New York as well." An archived version of the tweet can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video shows the chaos that ensued during a giveaway event hosted by Twitch streamer Kai Cenat in Manhattan when a huge crowd poured in hoping to receive promised PS5 gaming consoles. There was no involvement of Muslim refugees in causing the unrest. Our Probe
Upon conducting a keyword search of recent unrest in New York, we came across a deluge of reports from various sources about chaos and riots that broke out on August 4. Kai Cenat, a celebrity Twitch streamer, promised to give away free PlayStation 5 devices at Union Square Park. About 2,000 people gathered in anticipation of the giveaway.
Cenat promoted the giveaway on social media and people began to arrive at the park early in the morning. As the day went on, the crowd became increasingly restless, and some people began throwing objects at police officers. Police eventually declared the event an unlawful assembly and began to disperse the crowd. Cenat has not been charged with any crimes, but police said he could face charges of inciting a riot.
Taking this cue, we carried out a thorough search on social media platforms and found the exact video shot from the same frame of Kai Cenat's giveaway event. One Instagram user shared the viral video while describing it as "Mayhem during Twitch streamer Kai Cenat giveaway in Union Square."
We came across similar posts on Twitter linking the viral video with Cenat's event.
Moreover, we came across another video where police officials could be seen shielding themselves with a similar sheet as the one seen in the viral clip.
Carrying with our search further, we also came across similar footage showing people climbing an entrance to the Union Square subway station, in Manhattan, during the incident, as could be seen in the viral video.
Thus, it's evident that a video of recent unrest in New York during a giveaway event was misleadingly shared as a riot caused by Muslim refugees. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Aug 7, 2023 15:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Balasore tragedy video goes viral as recent train accident in Pakistan
content:
This video shows the site of the June 2023 train accident in Odisha's Balasore.
At least 30 people lost their lives and 100 were injured after the Hazara Express derailed in Southern Pakistan on August 6. In its aftermath, aerial footage allegedly showing this train accident has gone viral on social media. In the video, one can see derailed bogies and hundreds of people surrounding the train.Â
A Twitter user sharing the video wrote , "At least 30 were killed and over 80 injured after as many as 10 bogies of Havelian bound Hazara Express derailed today near Sahara railway station in Sindh's Nawabshah district, 275 kilometres away from Karachi." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the viral video is not from Pakistan at all — it shows the devastating June 2023 train accident in Odisha's Balasore. Our probe Â
We noticed that many people responding to the viral tweet claimed that it showed the train accident in Balasore, Odisha. We also observed the logo of "Odisha TV" in the top right corner of the video.Â
Using this clue, we found that Odisha TV shared this video on YouTube on June 3, 2023. Its description stated that it was an aerial view of the Balasore train tragedy site in Odisha.
Similar aerial visuals of the Odisha train accident were used in reports published by The Economic Times , ANI , and The Independent .Â
A triple train accident in Odisha's Balasore district on June 2 claimed more than 290 lives. According to the media reports, the Ministry of Railways later said that a signalling error caused this accident.
Actual visuals of the recent train accident in Pakistan can be seen here .
Thus, it's clear that the viral clip has nothing to do with the Pakistan train accident. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Aug 7, 2023 15:52 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this photograph DOES NOT show Elon Musk's childhood in apartheid South Africa
content:
This photo was captured in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1988 and features a mother, daughter and their maid. Musk was 17 in 1988, much older than the child in the photo.
Tech mogul and Twitter owner Elon Musk recently criticised South African political leader Julius Malema after the latter was seen chanting "Kill the Boer" at a stadium in Johannesburg. The words hark back to South Africa's apartheid era, characterised by race-based segregation under white minority rule, which ended in the early 1990s.Â
Musk accused Malema of promoting "genocide" of white people through the song, while Malema retorted by labelling Musk as "illiterate." Â
In its aftermath, a photo of a white woman and a white child sitting on an armchair and a black woman sitting on the floor next to them went viral. Allegedly this was the childhood photo of Musk, who was born in South Africa and left the country as a teenager. Sharing the photo on Facebook , a person wrote, "Elon Musk Life in South Africa, Pretoria whilst a Boy during Apartheid."Â
India Today found that the photo in question is not of Elon Musk at all. It was captured in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1988, when Musk was a lot older.Â
Using a reverse search on Google, we found a black-and-white version of the same photograph on the official website of the US National Gallery Of Art . According to information provided on this site, the photo was taken in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1988, and featured a mother and daughter and their maid.Â
We also found the same photograph at the Harvard Art Museums website with the same description. According to these sources, the photo was shot by American photographer Rosalind Solomon. The photograph was also featured in an interview with Rosalind Solomon by Vulture , published on October 28, 2021. None of these reports revealed the identity of the family seen in the photograph.Â
Musk was born on June 28 , 1971, in Pretoria, South Africa. In 1988, he would have been around 17. However, the child seen in the photo looks much younger.Â
Furthermore, we found a video on YouTube from September 25, 2020, showcasing Solomon's works. The video, titled "Rosalind Fox Solomon: The Trajectory of My Life and Work," features the same photo at around the 33-minute mark, highlighting Solomon's work in South Africa between 1988 and 1990.
An article by the Observer , published on January 18, 2020, showcased photos from various stages of Musk's life. One of these photos was taken on Musk's 18th birthday in 1989. This photo of Musk clearly differs from the child in the viral photograph.
It is hence clear that the photo in question is not a childhood photo of Elon Musk, but rather depicts an unnamed mother-daughter duo and their maid, shot in 1988 during apartheid in South Africa. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Aug 8, 2023 22:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Ravi Shastri NEVER hailed Babar Azam as 'best' compared to Virat Kohli
content:
This is a made-up quote. Shastri never said anything like this.
In cricket fandoms, the debate over who is the best batsman is an eternal one. Right now, the contenders include India's Virat Kohli and Pakistan's Babar Azam, two undeniably great sportsmen. But this debate seems to have now been settled by the cricketing great Ravi Shastri, at least if social media is to be believed.Â
An alleged quote by the commentator and former head coach of the India national cricket team began making rounds on social media. The quote  said: "Babar Azam is the best batsman of this era. Kohli is nowhere near to him." The archived version of a similar post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check has found that the alleged quote by Shastri is fictitious. Our ProbeÂ
Considering that Ravi Shastri was not only the former head coach of Team India but also the former captain of the Indian cricket team, it is only natural that such a comment would make headlines. Multiple rounds of searches, however, did not yield any relevant news reports.Â
Subsequently, we searched for Shastri's remarks on the two athletes. We found a Hindustan Times report  from August 25, 2022, which quoted Shastri saying, "Sometimes, it is important that when we talk about this rest and all that. Later on, you realise that when you are back in the media, you are doing all television, people come out with star. One stat that emerged during a Test match against England, which shocked me, really. It said that in the last three years, when you look at the top players in the world, that is [Kane] Williamson, David Warner, Babar Azam, Virat Kohli and Joe Root, Virat had played three times the number of games as everyone else across all cricket."
Before the 2022 Asia Cup, when Kohli was going through a rough patch, Shastri backed him and said that "mouths will be shut" if he managed to score a fifty  in the first match. He also vouched for Kohli ahead of the ICC World Test Championship Final  in June this year.Â
When we searched about Ravi Shastri's take on Babar Azam, we came across several news articles , none of which reported anything similar to the claim. Per an Amar Ujala report  from July 2022, Shastri called English batsman Joe Root "the Best" against spin bowling followed by Virat Kohli, Kane Williamson, and Steve Smith. Notably, he did not mention Babar Azam, which sparked a controversy.Â
India Today has mailed Ravi Shastri's office and this article will be updated once we receive a response. It is, however, clear that a fictitious quote was falsely attributed to Ravi Shastri. Â - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Aug 9, 2023 21:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video does NOT show Imran Khan in jail, it is old and edited
content:
This video predates Imran Khan's arrest and is edited.
A video of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan looking visibly distressed has been making the rounds on social media. Khan, in the video, could be seen sitting with his eyes closed. Allegedly, the video showed Khan's third night in prison. Khan was convicted in the Toshakhana case and sentenced to three years of imprisonment on August 5. He was arrested the same day.Â
Sharing the clip on Twitter , one person wrote, "Third night in jail, all because he dared to dream. He dared to stand up against the mafia that's the root cause for this country's devastation. Sucks." Archived versions of such posts can be found here  and here .
India Today found that this video is edited and it predates the arrest of Imran Khan. Our Probe
The viral clip contained the URL and logo of a Pakistan-based media outlet named "We News". We ran a keyword search on its YouTube channel  and found a video  similar to the one going viral.Â
In the clip, Khan could be heard talking about the Pakistan Democratic Movement or PDM , a coalition formed in 2020 by 11 political parties, including Pakistan's People's Party (PPP) and Pakistan Muslim League (PML), demanding the ouster of the then Prime Minister Imran Khan.Â
We then found a longer version of Khan's interview  shared by "We News" on August 1, which contained the visuals that are currently going viral. In the video, Khan talked about the then-ongoing Toshakhana trial.Â
India Today contacted a journalist working with We News, to get more information about the viral video. He told us that this video was shot by a We News correspondent on August 1 inside the premises of the Islamabad Session Court. He added that following Khan's arrest, no reporter had spoken to him.Â
It is worth noting that the video predates Khan's arrest. Further, in this video, Khan's eyes were not shut, suggesting that the viral clip was edited. A comparison between the viral video and the same shots in the original video can be seen below.
We then found that many YouTube channels shared the viral video  in a better resolution. These videos contained a logo of a TikTok account named "saad_hamdani_786". We found that this account shared the viral video  on August 7.Â
A new TikTok trend involves using an AR filter called "closed eyes" . When applied, it makes it look as though a person's eyes are shut even if they aren't. It is possible that this filter was applied to Khan's video. An example of such a video can be seen here .
Thus, it is more than clear that an old and edited video of Khan was shared with misleading claims. - Ends (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Aug 10, 2023 15:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Kyiv streets had water sprinklers for years, even before Russia-Ukraine war began
content:
This mist cooling system in Kyiv roads isn't new. This system has existed since 2019 in Kyiv.
Western military and financial assistance to Ukraine amid Russia's ongoing invasion of the country has been questioned time and again. This seems to be the core concern of a video, supposedly from the streets of Kyiv, that's been making rounds on social media.Â
This video shows water being sprayed from a pipe like a mist and pedestrians enjoying the sprinklers while cooling themselves. While sharing this video, people questioned the source of the funds for such an expenditure.Â
"Kyiv has a fancy new mister system throughout the city! I wonder who paid for that," said a tweet  that contained this video.
 Another tweet  said, "This is Kyiv with a new mister system throughout the city. At the same time, that's in middle of a war zone." The archived version of such a post can be seen here . This is Kyiv with a new mister system throughout the city. At the same time, that's in middle of a war zone. pic.twitter.com/ImExeT97WE — Joel Fischer 🇺🇸 (@realJoelFischer) August 9, 2023
This is Kyiv with a new mister system throughout the city. At the same time, that's in middle of a war zone. pic.twitter.com/ImExeT97WE — Joel Fischer 🇺🇸 (@realJoelFischer) August 9, 2023
India Today found this mist cooling system in Kyiv has existed for years and predates Russia's invasion.Â
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, the results led us to an Instagram image  from August 12, 2019, that captured similar-looking water sprinklers on a footpath. Although the post did not carry any details about the photograph, the location was listed as Khreshchatyk, the main street of Kyiv, Ukraine.
Subsequent searches with this keyword led us to a website where an image of the same cooling system  appeared on September 25, 2019. The caption of this photograph said, "New structures appeared on Khreshchatyk Street that spray water and are designed to cool pedestrians and water flowers at the same time. Summer." We also found news reports from August 2019  and 2020  that featured images of Kyiv's water sprinklers.
The 2019 report contained a photo gallery of what summers looked like in different parts of the world. The 2020 report was on the outbreak of Covid-19, where the photo was captioned, "People walk through a water sprinkler on a hot summer day in central Kyiv, Ukraine August 21, 2020."
A vlog video from July 2021, months before the Russian invasion, shows how these sprinklers helped keep the footpath comfortable for pedestrians in the middle of the summer heat.Â
With the help of an advanced keyword search, we came across a Russian news report  from August 2017. It contained a picture of a water dispenser cooling frame installed in a Kyiv park.Â
These misters or sprinklers appeared to be functional even after the invasion. Photos of them in the stock photo website Getty Images shot on June 21 this year  make that clear.
So, while we could not determine when the viral video was shot, it is evident that this mist cooling system was not installed during this ongoing conflict. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Aug 10, 2023 20:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of girl whose house was demolished in Delhi falsely linked to Nuh demolitions
content:
This video is from June 16, when the Delhi Urban Slum Improvement Board demolished makeshift homes in Priyanka Gandhi camp near Vasant Kunj, Delhi.
The Punjab and Haryana High Court on August 7 ordered a stay on the demolition drive in Haryana's Nuh district, which was launched following recent communal clashes in the area. The court questioned if the move was an "exercise of ethnic cleansing". Amid this, a video of a girl crying about her demolished home was widely shared.
In the video, the girl could be seen telling a reporter that her future was ruined and her books got buried in the rubble. One tweet containing the viral video  said, "A poor Muslim girl from Nuh, Haryana talking about her pain after her house was demolished by the authorities." Its archived version can be seen here
India Today, however, found that the viral video shows the victim of the demolition drive carried out by the Delhi Urban Slum Improvement Board in Priyanka Gandhi camp near Vasant Kunj, Delhi, in June. OUR PROBEÂ
We began our investigation by searching for the video on social media. We found the most viral tweet containing the video . In their responses, one person  shared the link to the extended version of the video and wrote in Hindi  that this was an old video from Vasant Kunj in Delhi.
The link directed us to a video posted by The Lallantop on its YouTube channel on June 19, 2023. The description provided with the video noted that several makeshift homes were demolished in the Priyanka Gandhi camp near Vasant Kunj on June 16, leading to the displacement of over 500 people living there for almost a decade. It further reported that after the demolition exercise by the Delhi Urban Slum Improvement Board, the land was allocated to the National Disaster Response Force.
In the extended video, the reporter also spoke to other affected residents, who also described their ordeal. Around the one-minute mark the reporter stated that the camp was located in Vasant Vihar, around four kilometres from Jawahar Lal Nehru University.Â
Indian Express, in its report  published on June 17, stated that the demolition by the DUSIB came two weeks after the Delhi High Court refused a stay on the exercise. The report that as bulldozers made their way into the area on the morning of June 16, residents and members of the CPI (ML), the All India Central Council of Trade Unions, and the All India Students Association were seen protesting.
Thus, it's clear that this video has no links to the demolition drive in Haryana's Nuh.Â

title: Fact Check: 2022 photo from Khargone in MP falsely shared as Nuh demolitions
content:
The photograph is from demolitions that followed the communal violence in Khargone, MP, in April 2022.
In the wake of recent communal violence in Nuh, Haryana, and the subsequent demolition drive, a viral photo has been circulating on social media, claiming to show a Muslim man gazing at his destroyed home. Sharing the viral image, a Twitter user wrote, "A helpless Muslim man from Nuh, Haryana, watching his home's demolition by the government." An archived version of one such tweet can be seen here .
Contrary to the claim, India Today found that the photo is not from Nuh, Haryana. Instead, it originates from demolitions in Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, when state authorities razed houses of people, citing their involvement in the communal clashes in April 2022. Our Probe
A reverse search of the image led us to a report by Scroll dated October 19, 2022. The report titled "Khargone violence: 12-year-old boy asked to pay Rs 2.9 lakh for allegedly damaging public property" contained the viral image. The caption accompanying the photo read: "A person's house in Khargone being demolished." The photo's source was listed as a "Special arrangement".
Additionally, we found a report in the Free Press Journal dated April 11, 2022. The report titled "Bhopal: Khargone rioters will not be spared: Chief Minister" also featured the same viral image. The image, however, was not credited to anyone.
We also found other instances of this photo being published in 2022. Bebaak Collective's December 2022 report "Social suffering in a world without support – Report on the mental health of Indian Muslims" contained the image, and here too it was linked to the demolition drive in Khargone. The photo  was credited to Scroll.Â
A Swarajya magazine report  from April 29, 2022, about the Khargone clashes too contained the image. The photo was captioned: "Stills from the demolition drive as posted by PRO Khargone from their official Twitter handle."Â
We searched for the photo on the official Twitter account of PRO Jansampark Khargone , under the Government of Madhya Pradesh. However, we were unable to find it there.Â
Regardless, the presence of the viral image on the internet since April 2022 confirms that it could not have been related to the demolition drive in the aftermath of the violence in Nuh, Haryana. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Aug 11, 2023 20:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of a tiger relaxing in a tub is not from Coorg — it's from the US
content:
This video is neither from Coorg nor from India. It is from the Carolina Tiger Rescue sanctuary in North Carolina, US, and dates back to June 2020.
A video of a Royal Bengal tiger relaxing in a tub of water in a wooded area has been making rounds on social media. According to those sharing it, this breathtaking scene was captured on a coffee plantation in Coorg, Karnataka.
One person wrote while sharing the video , "At a coffee plantation in Coorg in Southern India. A visitor inspects his bath and enjoys a lovely soak."Â
"This unique moment was captured at a coffee plantation in Coorg in Southern India," read another such post. This unique moment was captured at a coffee plantation in Coorg in Southern India. pic.twitter.com/3OWI7Fa2du — Anil Talwar🇮🇳 (@aniltalwar2) August 9, 2023
This unique moment was captured at a coffee plantation in Coorg in Southern India. pic.twitter.com/3OWI7Fa2du — Anil Talwar🇮🇳 (@aniltalwar2) August 9, 2023
India Today, however, found that the video is from somewhere other than Coorg or even India. It is from North Carolina in the US.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a similar video uploaded to a YouTube channel Carolina Tiger Rescue, a nonprofit wildlife sanctuary whose mission is saving and protecting wild cats.Â
Though this video uploaded on May 28, 2021, was filmed from a different angle, a Royal Bengal tiger could be seen soaking in a similar plastic tub.Â
The video was titled "Madonna Tiger gets her pool (2021)", and the description further added, "Last year, our video of Madonna Tiger receiving her first pool of the summer went viral on Facebook!! It's been viewed 5 million times and liked by nearly 150,000 people. So, we'd be remiss if we didn't share Madonna's first pool video from this year!"Â
Taking a clue from this, a subsequent search with keywords led us to the original video uploaded to the Facebook page of Carolina Tiger Rescue Sanctuary on June 11, 2020.Â
The video's description read: "We promised you Madonna Tiger in a pool, so here she is! We gave her her pool yesterday, and she immediately took advantage of the new water feature."
It further added, "Madonna is very vocal, and always has something to say to keepers and volunteers when they come to visit. She is also incredibly active and athletic for a tiger her age and never ceases to impress people with her stalking skills. Anytime she hears someone approach, she hides and stalks them! It can be very difficult to find her until she comes running up to the fence to say hello, but now that she has a pool, it may be a little easier to spot her!"
According to the website of Carolina Tiger Rescue, Madonna the tiger was rescued from Alabama, a southeastern region of the United States in September 2014. This indicates that a video from the Carolina Tiger Rescue sanctuary was misinterpreted as being from Coorg, Karnataka. It's noteworthy that In December 2020, Times Now too carried this video in a report and wrongly claimed this was from Coorg, Karnataka. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Aug 13, 2023 20:57 IST

title: Fact Check: These dramatic videos have nothing to do with the Hawaii wildfire
content:
The first video is from a 2022 fire incident in Ohio, US. The second video is at least two months old and possibly from Chile.
As you already know, a devastating wildfire swept through Lahaina, a town on Maui, one of Hawaii's islands, earlier this month claiming at least 93 lives till August 14. Social media is replete with videos and photos capturing this massive tragedy. However, there are also two videos being widely shared and passed off as from Hawaii. In reality, these videos are old and have no connection to Hawaii. Video of fire creeping along pavements
The first video  features fire along pavements amidst strong winds, as onlookers recorded the spectacle. Sharing the video , a Twitter user wrote, "BREAKING: Astonishing Hawaii Video - Fire Engulfs Street!" "BREAKING: Jaw-Dropping Hawaii Video - Fire Gets Blown Across the Street! #hawaiiwildfires #hawaii #hawaiifire #update #mauifires #hawaiifiresupdate #hawaiiwildfire #wildfireupdate #wildfires #mauifire #maui #mauifires #hawaiievacuation #news #prayingforhawaii #prayingformaui … pic.twitter.com/kHDUr8eBln — Empirical Eye (@Empirical_Eye) August 14, 2023
"BREAKING: Jaw-Dropping Hawaii Video - Fire Gets Blown Across the Street! #hawaiiwildfires #hawaii #hawaiifire #update #mauifires #hawaiifiresupdate #hawaiiwildfire #wildfireupdate #wildfires #mauifire #maui #mauifires #hawaiievacuation #news #prayingforhawaii #prayingformaui … pic.twitter.com/kHDUr8eBln — Empirical Eye (@Empirical_Eye) August 14, 2023
India Today, however, found that the video is not linked to Hawaiian wildfires. It's from a 2022 incident in Cleveland, Ohio, US.
A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to the same clip in a Fox8 report  from June 2022. The video originates from a Cleveland fire on June 18, 2022. According to the reports, fire investigators had found that a discarded cigarette accidentally ignited the fire in a mulch bed, carried by strong winds to other mulch beds. Mulch beds are generally made of dead leaves that are put around a plant to protect its base and its roots, to improve the quality of the soil. No one was injured in this fire.
Other media reports  documenting the same incident  used the same video and similar footage.
The video in question and other shots of the fire in the same area were shared on various platforms including Facebook , Twitter  and YouTube  in June 2022.Â
So, it is clear that old footage from Ohio, USA is being shared as Hawaii in the aftermath of the raging wildfire. Video of transformer explosion
The second video tries to tie the Hawaii fire to a conspiracy theory. It shows a 'light beam' striking a neighbourhood that starts a fire.Â
"Disturbing New FOOTAGE from Maui fires shows what allegedly happened," captioned some users  while sharing it.  🚨 Disturbing New FOOTAGE from Maui fires shows what allegedly happened #Hawaii #Hawaiifire #Maui #MauiFires #lahainafire pic.twitter.com/vBpux3ZHyo — Ivan (@Ivankalema01) August 13, 2023
🚨 Disturbing New FOOTAGE from Maui fires shows what allegedly happened #Hawaii #Hawaiifire #Maui #MauiFires #lahainafire pic.twitter.com/vBpux3ZHyo — Ivan (@Ivankalema01) August 13, 2023
India Today, however, found that the video in question is at least two months old and has nothing to do with the wildfire in Maui, Hawaii.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Telegram post  that featured a higher resolution of the same video that was shared on June 6.  We also found the same video on a YouTube channel, CHV News.
According to this news bulletin in the Spanish language, it was an explosion in the transformer due to strong winds. An optical effect made it appear as if a strange light from the sky caused this explosion.  Visuals of the damaged transformer also appeared in the bulletin.Â
This bulletin was uploaded on May 30, 2023. According to their Twitter handle , CHV news is based in Santiago, Chile. So possibly this video could also be from Chile but we could not independently verify that. However, it is sure that it has nothing to do with Hawaii. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Aug 14, 2023 20:38 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Muslims attacking railway gateman in UP's Hardoi
content:
This video shows a clash between two parties over an accident in Hardoi. The railway gateman was not involved at all.
A video of a mob assaulting a man allegedly on a railway line in Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh, was widely shared on social media. People in the video could be seen lashing belt blows at a man. "Hardoi, UP: Railway Gateman beaten by suspected Muslim Jihadis. They also proudly uploaded the attack video on social media," read one such tweet sharing the video.Â
India Today found that the video is from the Mahmudpur Saraiya village in Pihani Kotwali in Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh, and the violence was caused by villagers after an accident. The railway gateman was not involved in this. Our ProbeÂ
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to news reports  featuring screenshots from the viral video. According to a report published in UP Tak on August 13, the assault took place on the railway track in Hardoi's Pihani neighbourhood on August 11.Â
Per the report, Saba Haider, a resident of Mahmudpur, accidentally hit a woman named Parveen from the Saraiya village and fled the scene, abandoning his bike. However, when he arrived at his residence, Parveen's family was present there and assaulted him.Â
Individuals from both parties intervened. Saba Haider headed to his shop after some time. Parveen's relatives followed him and thrashed him again near the railway crossing 21D-2E. Someone recorded the brawl and shared it on social media. According to ASP Hardoi, Durgesh Singh, the clash was over an accident in the Pihani police station area. Six people have been charged in this matter by the police. In response to a tweet alleging that Muslims were beating the gateman, Hardoi police tweeted  that the allegation of attacking the gateman was baseless and false. The Divisional Railway Manager of Moradabad also tweeted from the official Twitter account and said that this was a personal matter and the railway gateman was not involved at all. "This incident happened yesterday at LC 21/D bet JKH-JBG, Major section RAC-SPC. Outsiders were quarrelling themselves and come to the railway track during their personal issues. There is no any involvement of gateman and the gateman performed his duty safely," tweeted DRM Moradabad NR. Thus, it's abundantly clear that the viral video did not show the Railway gateman being beaten up by Muslims. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Aug 15, 2023 14:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Dimmed by misinformation! Burj Khalifa displayed Pak flag on August 14, just not at midnight
content:
The Pakistani flag was indeed projected onto the Burj Khalifa. But the projection did not take place at midnight. Instead, it happened on the evening of August 14.
Both India and Pakistan celebrated their independence from British colonial rule this week. The iconic Burj Khalifa in Dubai has been known to illuminate  its facade with the colours of various countries' flags to honour  their respective Independence Days.Â
This year, however, several social media posts and even media reports  claimed that the Burj Khalifa did not display the Pakistani flag to mark its Independence Day on August 14
One person sharing a video of the Indian flag projected onto the tower, tweeted , "After disappointing Pakistan for not putting their flag on Burj Khalifa on Pakistan Independence Day it is lit with Tricolour. Same history same struggle but it's what INDIA chose to be post-1947 that made all the Difference." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today, however, found that both the Indian and Pakistani flags were projected onto the building on their respective Independence Days. The confusion arose due to a false alarm caused by Pakistani nationals gathering near the tower on August 14 at midnight, hoping to see their flag displayed. The flag was actually projected later, on the evening of August 14.
A keyword search revealed media reports claiming that the Pakistani flag was not projected on the building at midnight . These reports cited a tweet  featuring a video from an alleged Pakistani national expressing disappointment over the absence of Pakistani colours on the Burj Khalifa.
The woman recording the video could be heard saying, "The time is 12:01 am now and the Dubai officials have informed that Pakistan's national flag won't be displayed on Burj Khalifa."
Further searches, however, led to other media reports  showcasing the tower lit up in the Pakistani flag's colours .
The Burj Khalifa's official Instagram account also posted a video  the Pakistani flag projected onto the tower. The caption read, "Burj Khalifa lights up to celebrate The Islamic Republic of Pakistan's Independence Day. Wishing the people of Pakistan a day filled with pride, unity, and prosperity as you celebrate the rich heritage and achievements of your great nation. May the future hold even greater success and happiness for all Pakistanis. Happy Independence Day!"
However, The congratulatory message projected on the Burj Khalifa for Pakistan, stating "Happy 76th Independence Day of Pakistan", triggered doubts about the video's timing. Responding to an Instagram user's doubt, the Burj Khalifa account clarified that the Pakistani flag was displayed at 7:50 PM on August 14 this year. Pakistan and India celebrate their Independence Days on August 14 and August 15 respectively. In 2023, both countries observed their 77th Independence Days. Simply, it's a semantic choice to call it 77th or 76th. This year, it was the 77th Independence Day in both countries. However, in terms of anniversaries, it is the 76th. In previous years, the Pakistani flag projection on the Burj Khalifa has usually been carried out at midnight. The delay this year thus led to misinformation about the flag not being displayed there at all. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Aug 16, 2023 20:56 IST

title: Fact Check: This breathtaking space view of Earth was NOT captured by Chandrayaan-3
content:
The footage was captured from the International Space Station in September 2022, almost a year before the launch of Chandrayaan-3.
In what can be considered a momentous milestone, the Indian Space Research Organisation on August 17 successfully detached the Vikram lander from the propulsion module of the Chandrayaan-3 mission, bringing it another step closer to landing on the lunar surface. Throughout Chandrayaan-3's journey so far, many videos supposedly showing the spacecraft have made their way to social media. Many of them, however, had nothing to do with the Indian lunar mission
One such video showing a mesmerising view of Earth from space  was widely shared on social media as footage captured by Chandrayaan-3. The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today's investigation found that the footage was filmed aboard the International Space Station nearly a year prior to the Chandrayaan-3 launch. Our Probe
Upon careful examination of the viral video, we noticed that it was credited to the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit of NASA in its final frames. Additionally, the name "Som ET" also appeared in the credits.
Further search led us to the same video shared on Som ET's social media platforms on April 13. Som ET, as indicated in their bio, is a musician. The video's description on Instagram  said that the audio used in the video was taken from NASA's Van Allen Probes audio recordings, which explore Earth's radiation belts.Â
The post also clarified that the featured footage was from NASA's Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit. It even provided NASA's unique photo number for the images. The Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, per NASA , provides "operations and science team functions for handheld camera crew photography of Earth" from the International Space Station. It also "interacts with other ISS sensor teams and working groups, and coordinates ISS remote sensing response to natural disasters and other dynamic events through interaction with the United States Geological Survey."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Som ET (@som.et)
A post shared by Som ET (@som.et)
We also reached out to Som ET, who confirmed to India Today that the viral video was created by blending a modified version of the Van Allen Probes audio with NASA's video. Similar videos by Som ET are available on different platforms .
Furthermore, we traced the original video and the photos used to create it back to NASA's website . According to NASA, these photos were captured on September 11, 2022, using a Nikon D5 digital camera aboard the International Space Station by members of Expedition 67. The photos were then used to create the now-viral timelapse video. India's Chandrayaan-3, the third edition of the country's lunar mission, was launched  on July 14, nearly 10 months after the viral video's photos were captured.  It's worth noting that Chandrayaan-3 also captured remarkable images of the Moon and Earth  after the spacecraft entered the Moon's orbit on August 5. However, the video going viral has nothing to do with the lunar mission. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Aug 17, 2023 19:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video of plane stunt NOT from 2023 Indian Independence Day, it's from Italy
content:
The video actually shows an aerial performance by the Italian Air Force during centenary celebrations at the Mario de Bernardi military airport in Pomezia, Italy.
India marked its 77th Independence Day on August 15 with fervent celebrations across the nation. Amid the festivities, a video gained traction on social media, claiming to showcase an Indian Air Force performance on this year's Independence Day.
The viral video  shows a formation of jets soaring through the sky, leaving trails of coloured smoke that resembled the Indian flag – presumably saffron, white, and green. A Facebook user shared the video with the comment, "Wonderful performance by Indian Air Force pilots on Independence Day."Â
We conducted keyword searches and found the same video, filmed from the same perspective, on an Instagram account  under the username We_are_Italians. The caption for the June 24 post noted that it showed the centenary celebrations of the Italian Air Force. Another account, Italianexplorer_ , also shared the video on June 18, mentioning that it was filmed during the Italian Air Force's centenary celebrations at Mario De Bernardi military airport in Pratica di Mare.
India Today reached out to admins for both accounts, who turned out to be the same person. They confirmed the video's Italian origin, adding that the aircraft and flag formation seen in the viral video were indeed Italian. We also identified the background audio as " Turandot ", an opera piece composed by Italian composer Giacomo Puccini and sung by Luciano Pavarotti.
We also found news reports  that contained more photos of the performance of the Italian Frecce Tricolori aerobatic squad during a media preview of an airshow celebrating the centenary of the Italian Air Force in Pratica di Mare on June 16. Geolocation
We found the Mario De Bernardi military airport near Pomezia, Lazio, southwest of Rome. Using Google Earth, we found the three buildings near the airport that we observed in the viral video. A visual comparison of the viral video with Google Street View  showed the resemblance between the buildings and elements. No air shows
Contrary to the claim, India doesn't feature such spectacular aerial performances on Independence Day. Such displays generally take place during Republic Day celebrations on January 26. A press note issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs , Government of India, dated August 9, 2023, listed the events and ceremonies comprising the Independence Day celebrations.Â
The only event involving the Indian Air Force mentioned was the showering of flower petals from helicopters on Red Fort during the unfurling of the Tricolour, the video of which can be seen here .Â
Thus, it is evident that the viral video had nothing to do with the Independence Day celebrations in India.Â
(With inputs from Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Aug 17, 2023 23:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Burqa-clad man arrested for entering women's washroom in Kochi is neither Muslim nor BJP leader
content:
The individual in the video is not a Muslim; he belongs to the Hindu community. Moreover, he has no affiliations with any political parties.
On August 17, 2023, a male techie dressed in a burqa was apprehended for reportedly entering the women's washroom at Lulu Mall in Kochi. Accompanied by communal claims, the incident soon went viral on social media.
A user shared a screengrab from Aaj Tak  and wrote, "It's Very Shocking, In Kerala's Kochi, a burqa-clad Muslim youth entered the ladies' washroom and then secretly started making videos of women. As soon as the mall security staff caught sight of him, there was an uproar."
Another claim suggested that the male caught in a burqa was a BJP leader. A tweet featuring the viral video read, "BJP leader wearing burqa caught while planting a camera in the ladies' washroom of Lulu Mall in Kochi."Â
India Today found that the man arrested for entering a women's washroom wearing a burqa is neither Muslim nor affiliated with the BJP.
A keyword search led us to several media reports  and a Facebook post by Kochi city police  about the individual arrested at Lulu Mall.
According to an India Today report  dated August 17, Kochi police arrested Abhimanyu, a 23-year-old man who dressed as a woman in a burqa and recorded videos from the women's washroom. He is a B.Tech graduate employed at Infopark Kochi.
As per news reports, on August 16, Abhimanyu entered Lulu Mall in Kochi wearing a burqa. Allegedly, he entered the women's lavatory with a camera hidden inside a box, creating a hole in the box for the camera's lens. The police confiscated Abhimanyu's phone and burqa. We reached out to SHO of Kalamassery police station CI Vipindas for more details about the accused person's religion and political background. He informed India Today, "Abhimanyu is not a Muslim, and he is not affiliated with any political party. On the same day, he was arrested and charged under sections 354(C) (Voyeurism), 419 (Punishment for cheating by personation) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), and section 66(E) (Punishment for violation of privacy) of the Information Technology Act." Speaking on the current status of the case, he said that Abhimanyu was remanded in judicial custody for 14 days. For further insights, we contacted Saranya M Karivellur, a freelance journalist and Abhimanyu's neighbor in Karivellur. She stated, "People in this village are shocked to know about the incident. He was born and raised in Karivellur. He is from the Hindu community and has no affiliations with BJP or any political party. He was always a quiet person." advertisement Many individuals shared the incident's video on social media. content:

She then stepped out and placed a bottle of water in the middle of the road, presumably for the other women to drink from. This video will tell you why reservation is necessary. This video will tell you why reservation is necessary. Has this discrimination happened with any Brahmin Baniya Thakur person ? pic.twitter.com/9rXfbqR44o — The Dalit Voice (@ambedkariteIND) August 18, 2023
Sharing this clip , one person wrote on Twitter: "Reality of Hinduism. The Brahmin woman did not allow Dalit women to stand near her house and she also practiced untouchability. This is why Ambedkar burnt the Hindu book Manusmriti and left this cult along with more than 10 lakh people." Some of these posts are archived here  and here .
India Today found that the video did not show a real incident. It was staged by Bengaluru civic workers to raise awareness. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip shared on June 22, 2020, making it evident that it was not a recent incident. This tweet also alleged caste-based discrimination and mentioned that these sanitation workers were employed by the Bengaluru Municipal Corporation.
Since all the women featured in the video could be seen wearing masks, it is reasonable to speculate that the video was related to the Covid-19 pandemic. Following a subsequent search using relevant keywords, we came across a news report by Asianet Newsable which said that the video had been created solely to raise awareness.
We also found the clip uploaded to the YouTube channel of Asianet Newsable on June 24, 2022. The video's description noted that a few BBMP pourakarmikas or civic workers created this video. One of the pourakarmika women played the role of an arrogant house owner and refused to provide drinking water inside her home.
According to Asianet, the video went viral, with many, including officials, getting furious believing it to be true. The following day, they made another video to clarify that this was not a real incident and that they had made it as an awareness video, adding that all persons in the video were pourakarmikas from the Singasandra ward in Bengaluru. These reports quoted also Sarfaraz Khan, the Special Commissioner of Bengaluru Municipal Corporation, who lauded the effort of the workers and said this video would "bring some change in few who misbehave with pourakarmikas."
Thus, it is clear that a staged video went viral as an incident of caste-based discrimination. - Ends Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Aug 21, 2023 14:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Animated, AI-generated videos viral as visuals shot by Chandrayaan-3
content:
While the first video is an old 3D animation, the second one was created using AI.
The Indian Space Research Organisation recently released photos  of the far side of the moon taken by Chandrayaan-3. The images were captured on August 19 by the Lander Hazard Detection and Avoidance Camera. Reportedly, ISRO has already released  three videos of the Moon captured by Chandrayaan-3. One of them was taken by the Lander Position Detection Camera on August 15.
And even as many on social media shared these authentic Chandryaan-3 photos and videos, some shared CGI videos and AI-generated media as well, claiming that they were shot by the Indian lunar spacecraft. Let's debunk a few of these. Video 1Â
One such spectacular video  appears to show the surface of the moon with craters of various sizes and depths. The archived version of this post can be seen here .
Using reverse search, we found that a grab from this video, laterally inverted, was posted on the stock photo website i-Stock  on December 3, 2020.
"Textured surface of the moon close-up in motion. 3d illustration. Elements of this image furnished by NASA," read the photo's description there. It was credited to "Flash Movie" .Â
You can also find this video on the official website of Flash Movie , an online store which sells computer-generated videos and illustrations. The website's social media accounts mention the creator as Andrey Maslov, an animator and CG artist. Video 2
Another viral video  claimed to show what the Earth looked like from the Moon, as purportedly captured by Chandrayaan-3. The archived version of this post can be seen here .
We noticed that the viral video was taken from a tweet shared by a person called Mithlesh Keshari, as made clear by the account's name mentioned under the video. Keshari shared this video on August 20 and wrote, "Chandrayaan-3 Mission: Look how Earth looks from the Moon".Â
We noticed that in responses to his tweet, some pointed out that the video  appeared to be animated. To this, Keshari replied  that it was created using AI and was a small part of his documentary .Â
We could not independently verify the origin of this video. However, it certainly doesn't show the actual visuals of Earth from the Moon taken by Chandrayaan-3 as there is no information about it on the official website  or Twitter account  of ISRO.     - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Aug 21, 2023 16:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Not tropical storm Hilary's effect, these are film sets and rides at Universal Studios
content:
These videos are from Universal Studios Hollywood and don't portray the effects of the tropical storm at all.
Tropical storm Hilary unleashed furious flash floods east and west of Los Angeles in California, US, on August 20. In its aftermath, several videos circulating on social media claimed to show wreckage caused by the tropical storm.Â
In this story, we shall fact-check two such videos. Both videos are actually from different parts of Universal Studios Hollywood, a film studio and theme park in the San Fernando Valley area of California. They have nothing to do with the storm. Flooded subway
This video purportedly shows water gushing onto the platform of a metro station in Los Angeles. Sharing the video on Twitter, a person wrote, "BREAKING: The LA metro system is flooding," alongside hashtags for "Hurricane Hillary", "Los Angeles", and "California". The archived version of the post can be seen here .
We noticed people responding to one such tweet, pointing out that the footage was from a studio tour in Universal Studios Hollywood in California. Taking a cue from this, we searched on YouTube and found several videos resembling the viral one.
"Earthquake! Universal Studios Tour On-Ride Experience POV w/ Fire, Water and Disasters," read the title of one such video .
The video showed a train moving through an underground tunnel, with various disasters like fires, earthquakes, and floods taking place on the station platforms. At the floods section of the ride, we noticed several similarities with the viral clip.
 A visual comparison between the viral video and the YouTube video can be seen here.
According to a report by Inside Universal , the Earthquake segment of the Studio Tour is situated within Stage 50 of the studio.
The earthquake experience simulates an 8.3 magnitude earthquake occurring inside a San Francisco subway station.
The Earthquake attraction has made appearances in select films and TV shows , including "The Great Los Angeles Earthquake" (1990), "Beverly Hills Cop III" (1993), "Seaquest DSV" (1993), and "Bones" (2009).
Photographs taken within Stage 50 of the studio tour are also accessible on Google Maps.
 It is hence clear that the video in question is not related to the tropical storm. Plane crash
The second video shared on social media showed a plane's wreckage, several destroyed cars, and a wrecked home. Sharing the video on Twitter, people claimed tropical storm Hilary caused a plane crash in Long Beach.Â
"BREAKING: A plane has just crash landed in Long Beach, CA as a result of Hurricane Hilary and the 5.5 earthquake. Y'all stay safe out there," wrote a person on Twitter while sharing the video. The archived version of one such post can be seen here.Â
The video in question is one that India Today debunked earlier this yea r when it was falsely shared as a plane crash in Nepal.Â
The video shows the location of Steven Spielberg's movie "War of the Worlds", released in 2005. It is located at Universal Studios Hollywood in California. The official website of Universal Studios also lists this location of "War of the Worlds" as part of its studio tour. We also managed to geolocate the site on Google Maps .
It is adjacent to the iconic "Psycho House" featured in Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller "Psycho".
We also couldn't find any credible reports of a plane crash attributed to tropical storm Hilary in Long Beach, California. Regardless, it is clear that the video in question is from the sets of the Hollywood movie "War of the Worlds." It bears no relation to tropical storm Hilary. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Aug 21, 2023 20:21 IST

title: Fact Check: This old video of dolphin stampede has NOTHING to do with tropical storm Hilary
content:
This video is at least ten months old and has nothing to do with the tropical storm Hilary.
Tropical Storm Hilary battered the US state of California with heavy rainfall and floods. This was the first tropical storm to hit California in 84 years. Hilary weakened from a category 1 hurricane before making landfall over the northern Baja California Peninsula on August 20. In its aftermath, a startling video showing a huge group of dolphins swimming together in a synchronous way went viral on social media. Allegedly, this was a "Dolphin stampede" that was spotted along the California coast ahead of the tropical storm.Â
A Twitter user shared the video and wrote, "This dolphin stampede was spotted along the coast in California before #californiahurricane". The archived version of this can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this video dates back to October 2022 and thus has nothing to do with tropical storm Hilary. Our Probe
On reverse searching keyframes from the viral video, we found that many social media users had attributed it to an Instagram user called Taylor Parent and the Legacy Whale Watch , a boat tour agency that conducts whale watching tours in San Diego, US. Â
We found that both Taylor Parent and Legacy Whale Watch had shared this video in October 2022. Legacy Whale Watch mentioned in its post that the video was shot on October 6, 2022, by Parent, who as per her profile, is a photographer and shark safety diver.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Legacy Whale Watch (@legacywhalewatch) The San Luis Obispo Tribune , a Californian newspaper, carried this video in its November 2022 report. Per this report, the dolphins seen in the viral video were spotted at the Channel Islands National Park of California.  What is a dolphin stampede?
A post shared by Legacy Whale Watch (@legacywhalewatch)
The San Luis Obispo Tribune , a Californian newspaper, carried this video in its November 2022 report. Per this report, the dolphins seen in the viral video were spotted at the Channel Islands National Park of California. Â What is a dolphin stampede?
A dolphin stampede is the phenomenon of dolphins swimming in large groups. It is still unclear why large groups of dolphins do this. Experts believe it could be related to the need for safety in numbers, or because dolphins are chasing prey together, or both.
To sum it up, an old video of a dolphin stampede is being falsely linked to the recent tropical storm Hilary in the US. Â - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Aug 22, 2023 14:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Neither Ojai quake nor tropical storm Hilary, these lightning videos are old and unrelated
content:
While there was an earthquake in Ojai, these videos of lightning strikes predate the quake and tropical storm Hilary by months and years.
A seismic event with a preliminary magnitude of 5.1 rattled parts of Southern California on August 20 while residents in the area were preparing for Hilary, the first tropical storm to hit Southern California in 84 years. The earthquake's epicentre lay approximately six kilometres southeast of Ojai, California.
A video  featuring three separate clips now making the rounds on social media claims to show the earthquake that hit Ojai. Curiously, all three clips  showed lightning strikes and no earthquakes at all. The archived version of such posts can be seen here  and here .
India Today found that all three clips are old, and predate the earthquake and tropical storm by months, and in one case, even years. Let's look at the three clips individually. CLIP 1
This clip, seemingly shot from a building's balcony, showed a pink hue enveloping the atmosphere as lightning illuminated the sky.
Using reverse image search, we found the same video shared on Twitter on December 16, 2023. The video was tweeted by Matt Devitt , the chief meteorologist at WINK News, a Florida-based news outlet. According to the tweet, the video was shot at Madeira Beach in Florida, US. Devitt credited it to a person named Brittany Labonte. FLORIDA LIGHTNING! âš¡ Watch this close strike today on camera from Madeira Beach. When thunder roars, go indoors! Credit: Brittany Labonte @WINKNews @stormhour @spann pic.twitter.com/qLHUiiuYoa — Matt Devitt (@MattDevittWINK) December 15, 2022 Further searches led us to multiple media reports  featuring the same video . According to these reports, the footage was captured by a woman named Brittany Labonte who was present at Madeira Beach, near St. Petersburg, at the time of the lightning strike.Â
FLORIDA LIGHTNING! âš¡ Watch this close strike today on camera from Madeira Beach. When thunder roars, go indoors! Credit: Brittany Labonte @WINKNews @stormhour @spann pic.twitter.com/qLHUiiuYoa — Matt Devitt (@MattDevittWINK) December 15, 2022
Further searches led us to multiple media reports  featuring the same video . According to these reports, the footage was captured by a woman named Brittany Labonte who was present at Madeira Beach, near St. Petersburg, at the time of the lightning strike.Â
"So, I was just standing outside of my room just to get a look at the storm, and it really came out of nowhere," Labonte told FOX Weather . She also added that aside from feeling the building tremble, she did not experience any effects from her close encounter with nature.
Hence, it is evident that the video in question is over eight months old and originated in Florida, on the eastern coast of the US. CLIP 2
The second video, shot from a vehicle, captures lightning striking a car. The video contained the text, "Credit: Michaelle May Whalen via Storyful."
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the same video tweeted by the Washington Post  on July 8, 2022. According to the tweet, the video was captured by a person called Michaelle May Whalen near St. Petersburg, Florida. Whalen's name, Storyful, the date "July 1, 2022", and the location of Tampa were mentioned in the video. While driving home near St. Petersburg, Fla. on Friday, Michaelle May Whalen captured a video of lightning striking a truck on the highway. Meteorologists called the video capture the "most insane" and "most incredible" close-up lightning video ever. https://t.co/O3eFxB75EL pic.twitter.com/bczoj6J9QQ — The Washington Post (@washingtonpost) July 7, 2022
While driving home near St. Petersburg, Fla. on Friday, Michaelle May Whalen captured a video of lightning striking a truck on the highway. The same video  was also uploaded to the YouTube channel "Storyful News & Weather" on July 6, 2022. The channel's description of the video stated that it was filmed by Whalen in Tampa Bay, Florida, on July 1, 2022. Whalen informed Storyful that her husband and three children were in the vehicle ahead of her when it was struck by lightning.Â
She stated that although everyone in the vehicle remained unharmed, the lightning strike severely damaged the truck. "It started to storm and I thought the lightning was neat, so I was trying to snap a picture of the lightning and missed every time. So, my son-in-law suggested I record a slow-motion video, and that's when I captured the event on camera," she said.
Clearly, the footage is more than a year old and it is from Florida. CLIP 3
The third video shows lightning striking a tree adjacent to a house.
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the same video was shared on Twitter on September 2, 2017. According to this tweet, the footage was captured in Canada. Spectaculaire vidéo du foudroiement d'un arbre au #Canada (date non précisée). Vidéo Oliver via Supercelula https://t.co/i5W65XVvqf pic.twitter.com/iZFhqWHYzU — Keraunos (@KeraunosObs) September 2, 2017
