In this concluding part of the speech, the actor also reflected on the lessons his father, a freedom fighter, taught him about religions promoting harmony and the commonality between Ishwar and Allah. He said some individuals have distorted religions into forms of terrorism, and emphasised the moral duty of all religious believers to eradicate terrorism and choose life over death.
Nowhere in the video did he say that he was a Pakistani or that he was not a Hindustani. Thus, it's clear that the viral claim is absolutely baseless. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 9, 2023 17:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Old building collapse video falsely linked to recent Morocco quake
content:
The viral video is from August 2020 and is unrelated to the recent earthquake in Morocco.
A powerful earthquake of 6.8 magnitude struck Morocco's High Atlas mountains on September 8. Over 1,000 people lost their lives, more than 300 people sustained injuries , and numerous buildings were damaged. The epicentre was 75 km west of Marrakesh, Morocco's fourth-largest city.
The seismic event triggered a surge of videos and photos of the alleged effects of the quake, one of which shows a building collapsing in the dead of night.Â
A Twitter user sharing the viral video wrote, "Moment of building collapse after the strong earthquake hits in Marrakesh of Morocco." An archived version of the viral video can be seen here .
India Today found that this viral video is not related to the recent earthquake in Morocco. Instead, it is a three-year-old video, dating back to August 2020, when an old and dilapidated building collapsed in Casablanca, Morocco.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to several media reports from August 2020. A French news portal carried a report  containing the viral video. It stated that the incident took place on August 5, 2020, in the Sbata region, near Casablanca in Morocco. The report noted that one person died during the collapse.
Additionally, we found a viral tweet containing the same video from around the same time, further confirming that it pertained to the 2020 incident in Sbata, Casablanca.
According to reports, the building was already in a state of severe disrepair and had developed significant structural issues, eventually leading to its collapse. Authorities had previously inspected the building and advised residents to evacuate it. While some residents committed to vacating the building within a week, the collapse tragically occurred before they could do so.
Thus, the viral video showing a building collapse in the Moroccan city of Casablanca is being shared as a recent incident following a deadly earthquake in another part of the country. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Sep 9, 2023 20:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Rohit Sharma poster NOT displayed at Parliament or Bharat Mandapam
content:
The viral picture is from Chepauk Stadium in Chennai and is unrelated to the Indian Parliament or Bharat Mandapam.
Amid the gathering of world leaders at the 18th G20 Summit hosted at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi's Pragati Maidan, a viral poster featuring Indian cricket team skipper Rohit Sharma began making rounds on social media. According to a social media user, this poster adorned the walls of India's new Parliament and Bharat Mandapam, signifying the country's sporting achievements on a global stage.
The Twitter user who shared the viral picture wrote , "Rohit Sharma poster in India's new Parliament and G20 Summit representing the sports honours of our country. Captain Rohit representing sports in G20 has now become a proud moment for all our Indians #G20India #G20India2023."
India Today found that this picture has been edited, and was not displayed within either the new Parliament or Bharat Mandapam. Instead, the viral image of Rohit Sharma was displayed at the Chepauk Stadium Museum in Chennai. Our Probe
A reverse search of the viral image led us to several social media posts featuring it. A tweet from March 22, 2023, featured the viral picture of Rohit Sharma and specified that it was taken at Chepauk Stadium in Chennai.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Indian Parliament on May 28 and the Bharat Mandapam was inaugurated on July 26. These events evidently occurred months after the tweet was posted.
Another tweet from the same date displayed similar posters  of former Indian cricket team captains MS Dhoni, Kapil Dev, and Sunil Gavaskar, featuring a similar layout and aesthetic. This tweet indicated as well that the pictures were from Chepauk Stadium, also known as MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai.
We came across another picture from Chepauk Stadium shared by another Twitter user, which featured MS Dhoni and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin.
Furthermore, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) shared a tweet containing a video tour of Chepauk Stadium, showcasing the same posters. The video featured Indian fast bowler Jaydev Unadkat walking past these posters.
It's noteworthy that a new pavilion stand at Chepauk Stadium was inaugurated by the MK Stalin on March 17, 2023. This stand was named the "Kalaignar M. Karunanidhi Stand" in honour of the former Chief Minister of the state. A photo of the wall containing these posters was also tagged on Google Maps at the location of Chepauk Stadium.
Thus, it's clear that the viral poster of Rohit Sharma has no connection to either the new Indian Parliament or Bharat Mandapam. - Ends Published By: Arjita Mishra Published On: Sep 11, 2023 14:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Fistfight in Ukraine Parliament? Viral video is 13 years old
content:
This video is from 2010. Row over Russia's access to a key naval base led to a fistfight between parliamentarians.
A chaotic video of a scuffle  purportedly breaking out in the Ukrainian Parliament is being widely shared on social media. Allegedly, this video was recent and in it, lawmakers could be seen punching each other and throwing eggs at the speaker.Â
While sharing the video on social media, some people alleged that the Ukrainian Parliament was wasting financial aid provided by the United States to the war-hit country through such sessions. "Ukrainian Parliament.
That money is sure working. Protecting democracy one cheque at a time lol," wrote a Facebook user while sharing the video. The archived versions of similar posts can be seen here  and here.
India Today found that the video in question is over a decade old. A fight erupted between lawmakers over a deal to extend Russia's lease for a key naval base in Ukraine's Crimea. OUR PROBE
With the help of a keyword search we found similar videos  and images  used in media reports from 2010. According to a report by The Telegraph published on April 27, 2010, the video was from Ukraine's Parliament in Kiev.Â
Reportedly, parliamentarians were asked to vote on a controversial law allowing Russia to continue to use a Ukrainian port until 2042. As scuffles broke out, nationalist leaders unfurled the Ukrainian flag and began pelting then-Speaker Volodymyr Lytvyn with eggs.
According to NBC News , thousands of opposition demonstrators gathered outside the Parliament building as deputies from the newly elected pro-Russian President Viktor Yanukovich's coalition approved a 25-year extension to the Russian Black Sea Fleet's base in Crimea.
Smoke bombs filled the parliamentary chamber, and speaker Litvyn sought shelter under his umbrella as eggs were hurled at him.
Ukrainian nationalists, with former Prime Minister Yulia Tymoshenko and former President Viktor Yushchenko in the lead, reportedly considered the base extension a betrayal of Ukraine's national interests.
They aimed to eliminate it when the existing lease expired in 2017. Nevertheless, as reported by The Guardian , the Parliament ratified the lease extension with 236 votes, surpassing the minimum requirement by ten votes.Â
Yanukovich struck a deal on April 21, 2010, with Russian leader Dmitry Medvedev, agreeing to the navy base's continuation in exchange for a 30 per cent reduction in the price of Russian gas supplied to Ukraine.
It is hence clear that the video in question is over 13 years old and doesn't have anything to do with the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine, which began in February 2022. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Sep 11, 2023 20:53 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOESN'T show Aamir Khan praising 'Jawan'
content:
The clip is from 2015 and shows Aamir Khan reacting to Salman Khan's 'Bajrangi Bhaijaan'.
As Shah Rukh Khan's most recent blockbuster "Jawan" continues to make waves at the box office, a video featuring fellow actor Aamir Khan made the rounds on social media.
In it, Aamir allegedly praised "Jawan" , saying in Hindi and English, "Have you seen the movie? Great movie, very good movie. Best film and the best performance of his career. I am requesting everyone should watch this movie. Again and again, watch this movie."Â
Sharing the video, one person wrote on Facebook, "Amir Khan Jawan review." The archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today's investigation, however, found that the video is not related to "Jawan" at all. It is from 2015 and shows Aamir Khan's reaction to "Bajrangi Bhaijaan". OUR PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the video led us to the verified YouTube channel of IANS TV. There, we found a similar video  uploaded on July 20, 2015, titled: "Caught! Aamir Khan Crying after watching Bajrangi Bhaijaan."Â
At the 30-second mark, Aamir Khan made a similar statement. He said, "Have you seen the movie? Great movie, very good movie. Kabir Khan made a great film. Best film and the best performance of Salman Khan in his entire career.
I am requesting everyone should watch this movie. Again and again, watch this movie. I am very happy. Congratulations to the Writer, Director and the whole team. Even the child has done a fabulous job."Â
 This proved that the video being shared was not just old but edited out of context. It had nothing to do with "Jawan" at all.
IndiaTV , Eros Now , ABP News , The Indian Express , The Express Tribune  and the others media outlets also published reports about the same video at the time.
"Bajrangi Bhaijaan", starring Salman Khan, opened at the box office in July 2015. Has Aamir Khan reacted to SRK's 'Jawan' yet?
At the time of writing this report, there were no news reports about a public statement on "Jawan" by  Aamir Khan. Also, Aamir Khan is not on any social media platform.
It's noteworthy, however, that both Khans attended the "Gadar 2" success bash recently and were photographed with Sunny and Bobby Deol . - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Sep 12, 2023 20:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Old and CGI videos flood internet amid deadly Storm Daniel in Libya
content:
Neither video is related to Storm Daniel. One is years old and from Saudi Arabia. The other was created using CGI.
At least 2,000 people lost their lives as Storm Daniel unleashed deadly floods in Libya . While many shared photos and videos of the storm and its effects, there were also some who shared unrelated and even CGI clips. In this article, we will debunk two such videos. Tornado and Lightning
One video of a tornado visible behind a building was widely shared. Occasional lighting can also be seen in the video. Haring it on Twitter, one person wrote: "Huge tornado caught on camera in Libya's Benghazi as a result of Storm Daniel." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
Sky News Arabia also used this video in its collage related to Storm Daniel.Â
However, using a reverse image search, we found an uncropped version of this video on the stock images and footage website Shutterstock .
In this video, there was no tornado or lightning at all. However, a storm could still be seen taking place. The video was credited to " Cinematic Storm Footage" , a curation of hurricane, tornado, climate change, and storm videos shot professionally by filmmaker and storm chaser Gabriel Cox. But who added the tornado and lightning to this video? We found the viral video featuring the tornado and lightning on the YouTube channel   "rtsarovvideo" ,
But who added the tornado and lightning to this video? We found the viral video featuring the tornado and lightning on the YouTube channel   "rtsarovvideo" ,
shared on September 4, 2023. As per the "About" section of this channel, it shares real and edited videos of natural disasters.Â
It is noteworthy that CGI videos shared on this channel have been falsely shared as footage from natural disasters like Tropical Storm Hilary  and Cyclone Biparjoy earlier and have been debunked. An Incoming flood
Another video shows a massive stream  of water rushing towards and then and almost submerging a bridge. Vehicles could be seen moving away from the bridge as this happened.
This video was said to be from Libya and was shared with hashtags related to Storm Daniel. The archived versions of such posts can be seen here  and here .
Responding to a viral claim, a person wrote that this video was from a 2016 flash flood in Saudi Arabia's Al Farshah. Al Farshah is a locality in the Aseer province of Saudi Arabia.Â
We then found that the Saudi Arabian newspaper Azal had shared a longer version of this video on Facebook on April 8, 2016. The video's description clearly mentioned that it showed a flood in Al Farshah.
Similarly, Daralakhbar.com , another media outlet from Saudi Arabia also shared this video with the same details in 2016. Unusual rains and flooding killed 18 people in Saudi Arabia in April 2016, as per media reports.Â
Thus, it's clear that neither video shows Storm Daniel in Libya. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Sep 13, 2023 15:41 IST

title: India Today Fact Check on WhatsApp Channels: New way to counter fake news
content:
Meta, the parent company of WhatsApp, has launched Channels on the instant messaging application in India and over 150 countries, and India Today Fact Check is one of the first Indian organisations to be part of it. WhatsApp Channel is a one-way broadcast tool that delivers a private way to receive updates from people and organisations. Broadcasts can include text, photos, videos, stickers, and polls.
India Today Fact Check will use this new platform to publish regular stories debunking misinformation and disinformation trending on various social media platforms. You can follow India Today Fact Check's WhatsApp Channel here .Â
Channel broadcasts appear in a separate tab of the app, away from personal chats and calls under the Updates tab (formerly known as the Status tab). According to Meta, notifications for Channels are muted by default. To get notified about new updates, you can turn on notifications for each channel.Â
According to Meta, the goal of Channels is to build the most private broadcast service available that protects the personal information of both admins and followers. Following a Channel won't reveal your phone number to the admin or other followers.Â
India accounts for more than 490 million of WhatsApp's 2.7 billion monthly users globally. Essentially, WhatsApp is used by almost every Indian with a smartphone. Through Channels, India Today will tackle the unchecked sharing of misinformation and disinformation on the messaging app, whether about elections, health myths, or communally sensitive topics.
Meta first introduced Channels in WhatsApp in June 2023 in Singapore and Colombia, where users could follow various NGOs, medical research institutions, fact-checking bodies, and local authorities. The following month, it was launched in Egypt, Chile, Malaysia, Morocco, Ukraine, Kenya, and Peru. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Sep 13, 2023 19:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Morocco earthquake - these videos of destroyed buildings are old
content:
Both of these videos of destruction predate the recent earthquake in Morocco.
Days after the devastating September 8 earthquake in Morocco's Marrakesh-Safi region, photos and videos of its effects are still being widely shared on social media. Not all these videos, however, are related to the massive quake that has killed more than 2,400 people.Â
One such video showed a multi-story building crumbling to the ground. The other featured  a person standing atop a broken structure, seemingly singing prayers. The archived versions of these posts can be found here  and here.
India Today found that both videos predate the recent earthquake in Morocco. The apartment crumbling to the groundÂ
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post  dated February 12, 2023, featuring the video in question. This means that this incident took place around seven months ago, and thus, could not show the present condition of Morocco.
The caption in Turkish stated that the video showed an apartment collapsing in Cukurova, a district in the Adana Province in Turkey.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Adana Son Haber (@adanasonhaber)
A post shared by Adana Son Haber (@adanasonhaber)
Using keyword search, we then found several media reports  about this incident. Back in February , a series of earthquakes claimed more than 50,000 lives across Turkey and Syria.Â
We then found a report containing screenshots  of the viral video. According to it, the Kubilay Apartment in Adana's Cukurova district in Turkey was demolished in a controlled manner after it was destroyed by the earthquakes. At the time, many captured the moment when the building collapsed  on their mobile phones. In one of the tweets containing the viral video , a person quote tweeted  the video in question, stating that the same clip was shared back in 2017. The quote tweet , dated July 16, 2017, carried an extended version of the viral video.
The caption in Arabic stated that the video showed a person calling to prayer on the ruins of a mosque in Mosul, a city in Iraq. وهكذا يُرفع الأذان على أنقاض مسجدفي الموصل ارفع أذانك فالذي خلق الورى سيُريك يوماً في الأعادي أغبرا #العشماوي #الموصل pic.twitter.com/hQLuP9MFY0 — د.عبد الرحمن العشماوي (@Dr_Ashmawi) July 16, 2017

Further, we found that several people shared this video on social media back in 2017, including an Iraqi Radio station called "Radio Alghad" . However, some people shared the same video  claiming that this scene unfolded in a broken mosque in war-torn Syria. title: Fact Check: Rohit Sharma didn't give man of the match cheque to ground staff
content:
This image has been digitally altered. It was Virat Kohli, not Rohit Sharma who clinched the Man of the Match award. While both expressed their appreciation for the groundsmen, no such award was given.
Following India's victory against Pakistan in the Super Four round of Asia Cup 2023, a photo of the Indian skipper  Rohit Sharma with the ground staff began making the rounds on social media. This photo  c aptured Sharma handing his man of the match cheque to the ground staff.Â
"Rohit handed the man of the match award to the ground's staff. My captain," read one such tweet  containing the photo. Rohit handed the man of the match award to the ground's staff. My captain 💙 pic.twitter.com/jEGC9Ig8pW — Pr𝕏tham (@78thCenturyWhxn) September 12, 2023
Rohit handed the man of the match award to the ground's staff. My captain 💙 pic.twitter.com/jEGC9Ig8pW — Pr𝕏tham (@78thCenturyWhxn) September 12, 2023
"Rohit Sharma gave his winner of the match award money to all the ground staff. How can someone hate this man," wrote another Twitter user. The archived version of such a post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral image was digitally altered. Additionally, there was no official declaration from the Indian side about any award giveaway.Â
Upon conducting a reverse image search on the viral post, we found multiple news reports  highlighting the crucial role played by the groundsmen in ensuring an outcome in the India-Pakistan clash. This rain-affected match went into the reserve day as the Men in Blue registered a mammoth 228-run win in Colombo's R Premadas stadium.  Although these reports featured the same image that circulated in the viral post, it's worth noting that none of them depicted the groundsmen holding a replica of the man of the match award cheque in their hands. A screengrab from HotStar, the official broadcaster of the Asia Cup 2023, did feature it as well, indicating that the replica man of the match award cheque was digitally added. It's also noteworthy that Rohit Sharma was not the man of the match in this contest. It was former Indian Captain Virat Kohli . Had Indian Captain Rohit Sharma indeed presented the award to the groundsmen, it would likely have gained media attention. However, we found no news reports about such a gesture. However, both Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli acknowledged and lauded  the tireless efforts of the groundsmen during the post-match presentation. "We are happy to get some game time. A lot of guys did not have game time and that was great support from the groundsman as well. From the word go, they were right on the money. I know how difficult it was to come and do the job and do it the next day. We would like to thank them as a team," said Sharma. "A loud shout out to all the groundsmen for the work they have put in to make this game possible. They did a fantastic job," said Kohli while accepting his player of the match award. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Sep 13, 2023 20:53 IST

title: Fact check: Child rescue video of Syria falsely viral as that of Morocco quake
content:
The viral video is from February 2023 and shows a child in Aleppo, Syria, trapped under a broken building following an earthquake.
The recent earthquake in Morocco has claimed at least 2,900 lives, causing devastation in Marrakesh and the surrounding areas. Amid this tragic event, social media platforms have been flooded with videos and pictures claiming to be from the earthquake in the North African country. Â
One such video shows a child trapped under rubble being rescued. A Twitter user who shared the viral video wrote, "Our prayers and support go out to Morocco for their safety." An archived version of the viral video can be seen here . Â
India Today found that this viral video is from an earthquake that occurred in Syria earlier this year. Â
Reverse-searching frames from the video led us to a report published by Express on February 8, 2023, which contained an extended version of the clip. According to the report, the incident took place in Aleppo, Syria, when a powerful earthquake near the Turkey-Syria border devastated the region earlier this year. Â
The report further mentioned that the Syrian Civil Defence rescued the baby who was trapped under the rubble of her home. They discovered the girl pinned beneath a man who tragically lost his life under the broken concrete.  Â
A Turkish news portal  also shared the viral video, reporting that the baby was buried under the rubble in Aleppo. The child survived because she was shielded by the body of a dead man.  Â
Another Iraqi media organisation confirmed that the viral incident was indeed from the earthquake that struck Syria earlier this year. The report, however, noted that the child survived because she was buried under the body of her sister, who had died.Â
So, while it remains unclear whether it was a man or the child's sister under whose body the child was trapped, it's more than evident that the viral video has nothing to do with the earthquake in Morocco. Â - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 13, 2023 21:47 IST

title: Fact Check: 2017 video of Indian man in UK caught grooming minor viral as recent
content:
This incident is not recent. It occurred in July 2017, when Praju Prasad was catfished by a vigilante group. He was arrested and fined.
A video that's been widely shared on social media purports to show an Indian man begging for mercy at a UK metro station after being caught trying to groom a minor. Disgusting! Sanatani Brahmin "Praju Prasad," from india caught in a UK, Metro Station for trying to lure & have $exual relationship with a "12yo Girl" which he met online, caught there by ped0ph!le hunters. - @SitaMaa02 pic.twitter.com/ReVAjeUT38 — Susheel shinde (@susheelshinde98) September 12, 2023

Those sharing the video  claimed that the man, Praju Prasad, was caught trying to "have sex with a 12-year-old". Despite pleading for mercy, the man was escorted by the police in the video.
Allegedly, this video showed a recent incident. "Another Andh Bhakt 'Praju Prasad', from India, was caught at a UK metro station for trying to have sex with a '12-year-old girl, whom he had met online. Andh Bhakt are thinking that Rishi Sunak has become the Prime Minister of UK, which means the UK has also become a part of Akhand Bharat," read a tweet containing the video . The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
India Today found that the incident is more than six years old, and predates Sunak's Prime Ministership by half a decade. OUR PROBEÂ
A keyword search led us to a J uly 2017 report in the UK Metro that contained a screenshot from the viral video.
This report said that a vigilante group called "Guardians of the North" confronted 24-year-old Praju Prasad in North Sheilds, a town in England. This makes it clear that the incident is nearly six years old.Â
We then found a Daily Mail repor t dated July 14, 2017, that revealed that Prasad, a resident of North Shields, engaged in text conversations with someone he believed to be a 12-year-old girl on social media.
He was, however, being catfished. Prasad had actually been talking to members of the vigilante group pretending to be a 12-year-old.
This report also included screenshots of the conversations that occurred between Prasad and the members of the group, where Prasad suggested they "take a room" and "have some fun".
According to other reports from July 2017 , Prasad began pleading for mercy when confronted by the members of the vigilante group.
Subsequently, he was taken into custody by the police and ultimately received a nine-month prison sentence, along with a £140 fine. He was also ordered to sign the sex offenders register for five years.
It's worth mentioning that in July 2017, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom was Theresa May. Rishi Sunak assumed office as Prime Minister in October 2022.

title: Fact Check: These people sleeping out in open are not Morocco quake survivors
content:
This video is from a religious congregation that was held in Lisbon, Portugal, in August this year.
Morocco's deadly September 8 earthquake has killed about 3,000 people and rendered many more homeless. Those without shelter, and those concerned about aftershocks in the North African country reportedly slept outdoors or under makeshift canopies.Â
Now, a video depicting thousands of people sleeping on an open ground is being shared on social media. While sharing the video on Twitter , one person wrote, "Subhanallah this is really touching. Ta Allah! Protect the people of Morocco and forgive the dead ones. Ameen."
India Today found that the video is from a 2023 global Catholic youth festival held in Lisbon, Portugal. Our Probe
A reverse image search of the video's keyframes led us to the same clip , uploaded to a YouTube channel named "Solo Catecumenos" on August 6, 2023.
This confirms that the video predates the Morocco earthquake that occurred on September 8. According to this channel, the video was taken during the 2023 edition of World Youth Day (JMJ2023), an annual Catholic festival held in Lisbon, Portugal.
The same video was shared on Facebook by various people around the same time, who also claimed it was from the Lisbon festival.
According to media reports , more than 1.5 million people gathered at Tejo Park in Lisbon on August 5 to participate in World Youth Day, presided over by Pope Francis. The event spanned from August 1 to 6. Young Catholics from across the globe reportedly  arrived on August 5, equipped with backpacks and sleeping bags, prepared to spend the night until the final mass the following day, a Sunday.
Other YouTube channels also shared similar videos of attendees sleeping at Tejo Park in August. Additionally, several attendees uploaded photos and videos on Google Maps  that depict numerous people lying inside sleeping bags.
 It is hence clear that the video in circulation does not depict the aftermath of the Morocco earthquake. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Sep 14, 2023 23:01 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of bulldozer flood rescue is NOT from Libya but from China
content:
This video dates back to August 2023 and shows people stuck in floods in Beijing, China.
The calamitous Storm Daniel that caused massive floods in Libya has led to the deaths of over 11,000 people. And the death toll is expected to rise with at least 10,000 remaining missing in the days after. Of the videos purporting to show the horrid situation in the country being shared on social media, one was of a bulldozer rescuing people in a heavily flooded area.
A Twitter user  shared the video and wrote, "Libya: Successful rescue operation… Libya flooding disaster." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that this video is neither recent nor does it have anything to do with the floods in Libya. It's from China. OUR PROBE
We noticed that some people responded to the viral tweets and said that the video was from China.Â
A subsequent search with relevant keywords led us to the Chinese news outlet People's Daily China sharing a similar video on Twitter on August 1, 2023.
Per the outlet, the video showed a Chinese man using a bulldozer to rescue a family stuck during a flood in Beijing. A Chinese man used a bulldozer against the rushing current to rescue a family stuck on a roof during the flood in Beijing. title: Fact Check: Not under rubble in Morocco! Video shows baby found buried in Kanpur
content:
The video shows an incident that occurred recently in the city of Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh.
A shocking video of a man digging out a newborn baby buried in a field is circulating on social media . It's claimed that the baby was found under the debris after the recent Morocco earthquake, which claimed nearly 3,000 lives  on September 8.
A Twitter user posted this video  with the caption, "Here, a new-born baby is dug out of the debris after a magnitude 6.8 earthquake devastates Morocco."
The archived version of one such claim can be seen here .
India Today found that this video is not related to the recent earthquake in Morocco. Instead, it shows a child found buried in the fields of Kanpur Dehat district in Uttar Pradesh on September 9, 2023.
Several social media users were found responding to the viral video, affirming that the incident had taken place in Kanpur. Notably, many users tagged the Kanpur Police , seeking clarification on the matter.
Following this lead, we searched further and found a tweet by the Kanpur Dehat Police, shedding light on the incident. थाना मूसानगर क्षेत्रान्तर्गत खेत से मिले नवजात शिशु के सम्बन्ध में क्षेत्राधिकारी भोगनीपुर द्वारा दी गयी बाइट । pic.twitter.com/YBRRRAHzQ2 — Kanpur Dehat Police (@kanpurdehatpol) September 9, 2023 According to the details shared in this tweet, the infant seen in the video, was discovered in Pulandar village, Moosa Nagar of Kanpur Dehat, by a couple named Rajesh and Reshma. Additionally, Kanpur Dehat police had also posted another video  of the rescued infant. On searching further, we found a few media reports related to this incident. According to Aaj Tak's report , some residents of Pulandar village were drawn by the sound of a baby crying in a nearby field. Upon approaching, they made a startling discovery—a newborn baby buried under the soil. Immediately, they rushed the infant to the hospital and alerted the police. Thereafter, we came across a report in Dainik Bhaskar , which stated that the Kanpur Dehat police were searching for women who had then given birth to babies. For more information, we reached out to Ravikant Gond, the Circle Officer of Bhognipur. He confirmed that this incident did indeed take place in Kanpur Dehat, and they were conducting search operations to apprehend the individual responsible for burying the newborn in the field. India Today also spoke to a few journalists from Kanpur Dehat who corroborated our findings. To sum it up, the video showing the discovery of a baby buried in a field in Uttar Pradesh is being falsely shared in the backdrop of the Morocco earthquake. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Sep 16, 2023 20:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral brawl video not linked to current Italy migrant crisis
content:
This video is from a 2021 incident in Marotta di Mondolfo in Italy, and is unrelated to the recent migrant crisis in Lampedusa.
Recently, the Italian island of Lampedusa saw an unprecedented influx of migrants—7,000 people arrived within just two days. This sudden surge, which exceeds the island's resident population, has led local politicians to call for emergency aid. Lampedusa has been a primary entry point for those crossing from North Africa and is a longstanding hotspot in Europe's migration crisis.
Now a video showing a confrontation  between police and a group of young men is making rounds on social media. The video is being falsely attributed to recent clashes between police and migrants on the island.  Archived version of one such post can be seen here .
The video was shared on social media platform X, with the caption, "#BREAKING | Italy: Direct clashes between migrants and police began on the island of Lampedusa. Illegal immigrants throw stones at the carabinieri and demand that they be sent to Europe."
India Today's investigation found that the viral video dates back to a 2021 incident in Italy and has no relation to the recent migrant situation in Lampedusa, one of the Pelagie Islands in the southern Mediterranean Sea.
A reverse image search of the video's keyframes led to multiple media reports from August 2021. According to a report  published on August 7, 2021, the video was filmed in Marotta di Mondolfo in the Province of Pesaro e Urbino. The violent brawl involved dozens of young people exiting a music event at the Miu Club in Marotta. The altercation began between a young Albanian man and a Senegalese man and escalated into a large-scale fight that included stabbings. Some reports suggest the conflict originated from drug-related disputes.
Four individuals were identified and arrested  following the incident, including the Albanian who initiated the stabbing, another Albanian, a Colombian, and a Senegalese man. The incident drew condemnation from authorities, including the mayor of Marotta di Mondolfo and a member of the Justice and Anti-Mafia Commission.
The video was also circulated on social media in August 2021 . This clearly makes it over two years old and unrelated to the recent events in Lampedusa. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Sep 18, 2023 23:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Mexico's 'Alien Corpse' being cut like a cake? Here are the facts
content:
The video showcasing a knife cutting into an "alien corpse" is actually a cake created by a baker and has no connection to the alleged "alien corpses" in Mexico.
A recent social media frenzy was triggered by a video that seemingly showed a knife cutting into an "alien corpse," shortly after journalist Jaime Maussan presented  what he claimed were "mummified alien corpses" to the Mexican Congress. The video led some to believe that the Mexican government had staged the entire event. However, our investigation reveals that the viral video showcases a cake, skillfully crafted to resemble an alien, and has no connection to Maussan's presentation to the Mexican Congress.
Jaime Maussan, a Mexico-based journalist known for his interest in UFOs, claimed in a presentation before the Mexican Congress on September 13 that he had discovered two small "mummified alien corpses" in Peru in 2017. These figures had elongated heads and three fingers on each hand and were said to be around 1,000 years old.
Soon after Maussan's revelation, a video began circulating on social media that appeared to cut the "alien" like a cake. A Twitter user posted the video with a caption implying that the Mexican government was hand in gloves with the journalist to deceive the world in presenting the cake as a rare and mummified alien. An archived version of such posts can be seen here and here . Upon investigation, India Today found the viral video was actually a depiction of a cake designed to resemble an alien. Our Probe There were noticeable differences between the features of the supposed extraterrestrial beings Maussan presented and those of the cake. A reverse image search led to an Instagram page named " the_bakeking ," which featured the same video . The cake was created by Ben Cullen, a tattoo artist and baker from Birmingham . Cullen uploaded the video on September 15, two days after Maussan's presentation, making it clear that the two events were unrelated.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by The Bakeking - Ben Cullen (@the_bakeking) It's worth noting that Maussan made similar claims about mummified aliens  in Peru back in 2017. A report from Peru's prosecutor's office later found that these were fabricated figures, made from a mixture of paper and synthetic glue. The scientific community generally views the figures presented by Maussan as a debunked hoax .Â

title: Fact Check: Wasim Akram and Waqar Younis DIDN'T say Asia Cup final was 'fixed'
content:
Neither Wasim Akram nor Waqar Younis made any such comments.
Following Sri Lanka's abysmal performance against India in the Asia Cup final — the island nation managed to score only 50 runs — rumours of match-fixing have been spreading on social media. On Twitter and Facebook, people shared statements about the same, allegedly made by former Pakistani cricketers Wasim Akram and Waqar Younis.Â
A Twitter user wrote alongside Akram's photo , "Wasim Akram on Star Sports: 'The way SL turned up today it seems like some sort of arrangement was already made behind the scenes, to see a team that has reached the finals play in this manner raises quite a few ques, but maybe we should keep quiet and not upset the ICC & BCCI."Â
Others on Facebook attributed  this same statement to Younis. The archived version of these claims can be seen here  and here .Â
India Today found that neither Wasim Akram nor Waqar Younis made any such comments. Multiple sports journalists confirmed this to India Today.Â
Had popular former cricketers like Wasim Akram or Waqar Younis made such a controversial statement, it would have been covered by major news outlets. However, we did not find any such news report.Â
We then checked the social media profiles  of both former cricketers  but no such comments there.
To the contrary, we found a September 19 tweet by Akram urging people not to believe everything on the internet. He wrote, "People need to stop thinking everything on social media is true. The bad is always easier to believe than the good. Fake news, in our part of the world, ignites unnecessary controversies, sparks hate and toughens the rift between us something that both countries do not need any more of. Enough is enough!" People need to stop thinking everything on social media is true. The bad is always easier to believe than the good. Fake news, in our part of the world, ignites unnecessary controversies, sparks hate and toughens the rift between us something that both countries do not need any…
— Wasim Akram (@wasimakramlive) September 19, 2023 What do Pakistani journalists say? We sent the screenshots of the viral posts to Faizan Lakhani, a sports journalist at the Pakistan-based Geo News. Lakhani told India Today that neither Wasim Akram nor Waqar Younis made any such statement. Mirza Iqbal Baig, a sports analyst and anchor at Pakistan's Express News also called this statement baseless.  Match-fixing accusations According to media reports , a civil rights organisation called Citizen Power Against Bribery, Corruption and Wastage filed a complaint at the Police Headquarters in Colombo alleging that the final match between India and Sri Lanka was fixed. It is also noteworthy that following India's victory in the Asia Cup, Pakistani fans trended  "Well played Jay Shah" on social media, accusing the BCCI of match-fixing. However, it is certain that neither Wasim Akram nor Waqar Younis alleged match-fixing in the Asia Cup final. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Sep 19, 2023 21:30 IST

title: Fact Check: A robot isn't playing pickleball with humans in this video, it's CGI
content:
The robot in the video is CGI. The original video was of a match between human players at a Major League Pickleball competition held in Daytona Beach, Florida.
In what appears to be a stunning breakthrough in the field of robotics, a video of a doubles pickleball match featuring a robot player has been widely shared on social media. "Norway Robot Playing Pickleball with Humans." read the Instagram caption  of one such post.Â
India Today's investigation, however, found that the robot in the video was nothing more than CGI. Our Probe
We reverse-searched the viral video's keyframes and found an Instagram post containing the same video shared by US-based tech journalist Kim Komando . According to the September 15 post, the video was "great animation work", and the unaltered footage showed all human players: Andrea Koop, Maggie Brascia, Anna Leigh Waters, and Lea Jansen. The robot had been digitally inserted in place of Anna Leigh Waters.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Kim Komando (@kimkomando)
A post shared by Kim Komando (@kimkomando)
Further searches led us to a 16-minute-long version of the match between the four players. This video was uploaded to the YouTube channel  "House of Pickle" in March 2023. Near the three-minute mark in this video, we observed the segment used in the manipulated video.Â
Numerous other videos from the same match were also available on YouTube, offering additional context. A comparison between the original video's background  and the manipulated one can be seen below.
According to a Forbes report , the video was from a Major League Pickleball  competition held in Daytona Beach, Florida, in March. The Kitchen Pickleball , the largest online social media community dedicated to pickleball, shared a clip from this match on Instagram, dubbing it the "Most Viral Point in Pickleball History."
It is hence clear that the video in question was edited using CGI and does not actually show a robot engaging in the sport.
Incidentally, a similar video purportedly showing a robot defeating a human in table tennis went viral earlier this year. At the time, India Today's investigation  found that it was a standard match between two humans that was embellished using CGI. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Sep 19, 2023 22:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Rashtrapati Bhavan DIDN'T remove Sikh guards, baseless claims viral
content:
Both claims are baseless. A Defence Ministry spokesperson and the President of India's PA confirmed this to India Today.
Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's allegation of a potential link between the Indian government and the killing of the Sikh separatist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June has led to a series of diplomatic escalations, with each nation expelling the other's envoys . However, on social media, rumours of domestic repercussions against Sikhs are also spreading like wildfire.Â
Twitter users claimed that following Trudeau's explosive allegation, the Indian Army started denying leaves to Sikh soldiers. People also claimed that Sikh security personnel at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President of India's official residence, have also been replaced.
Several Pakistani Twitter users shared these allegations . The archived version of one such post can be seen here .Â
India Today found that neither has the Indian Army denied leaves of absence to Sikh soldiers nor have Sikh security personnel deployed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan been replaced. A Defence Ministry spokesperson confirmed this to India Today.Â
Had all Sikh security personnel been removed from the Rashtrapati Bhavan, it would have been reported all over the media. However, we couldn't find any such report.Â
Tweets making such allegations were posted on September 19, a day when there was a special session at the new Parliament building. Had there been any such development, there would have definitely been a buzz about this in political circles during the session. However, nothing of this sort was reported at all.Â
The Indian Army rubbished these allegations. The Additional Directorate General of Public Information wrote that such tweets were "fake messages" being spread on social media by "inimical agents about soldiers of the Indian Army, spreading rumours and hate-mongering". The tweet asked the public to safeguard itself against "such fake news". #FakeNewsAlert #Beware Fake messages are being spread on social media by inimical agents about soldiers of #IndianArmy , spreading rumours & hate-mongering. Safeguard yourselves against such fake news. #IndianArmy pic.twitter.com/7q1icOPXdm — ADG PI - INDIAN ARMY (@adgpi) September 19, 2023

The Press Information Bureau also clarified that no such decision has been taken. It noted that such baseless allegations were "shared with the intention to create disharmony". Claim: Following Sikh leader Hardeep Singh's assassination, Sikh security personnel at Rashtrapati Bhavan have been replaced & Army is denying leave to Sikh soldiers #PIBFactCheck This claim is Fake & shared with intention to create disharmony No such decisions have been taken pic.twitter.com/wF6bLOXrKK — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) September 19, 2023
Claim: Following Sikh leader Hardeep Singh's assassination, Sikh security personnel at Rashtrapati Bhavan have been replaced & Army is denying leave to Sikh soldiers #PIBFactCheck This claim is Fake & shared with intention to create disharmony No such decisions have been taken pic.twitter.com/wF6bLOXrKK — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) September 19, 2023
India Today also reached out to President Droupadi Murmu's PA Suraj Kumar Mahato. He too refuted these allegations, adding that currently there are several Sikh security personnel deployed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan.Â
Thus, it's clear that these claims have no basis in fact whatsoever. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Sep 19, 2023 23:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Photo of PM Modi hugging Justin Trudeau is NOT from 2023 G20 Summit
content:
This photo is more than five years old. It was taken during Trudeau's India visit in 2018.
Amid escalating diplomatic tensions between India and Canada regarding the killing of pro-Khalistan Sikh leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a photograph  featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Canadian counterpart Justin Trudeau, hugging surfaced on social media. Claims accompanying the photo suggest that it was shot during the recently concluded G20 Summit in New Delhi.
India Today found that the photograph is more than five years old. Most media reports note that while Modi and Trudeau behaved cordially during the G20 Summit, neither extended much warmth towards the other. OUR INVESTIGATION
A reverse search of the photograph led us to multiple media reports  from February 2018 that featured it with credits to Agence France-Presse. Further investigation brought us to the original image uploaded to the AFP website .Â
The photo was taken during a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi on February 23, 2018. Trudeau and his family were on an official week-long trip to India. PM Modi, as per reports , met Trudeau six days after his arrival and signed several agreements reaffirming Indo-Canadian ties.
This proves that the photo in question is not from the G20 Summit in New Delhi at all.Â
But, did Modi and Trudeau hug at the G20?
On September 9, PM Modi personally greeted every head of state and other top dignitaries at the G20 Summit. Modi received his guests in a designated area featuring a prominent Konark Wheel inside the newly constructed Bharat Mandapam.
According to a Times of India report , leaders like US President Joe Biden and British PM Rishi Sunak were welcomed with warm hugs and smiles. In contrast, leaders of two countries with whom India currently has difficult relationships, China and Canada, were greeted formally.Â
Several media reports  noted Modi's "reserved" reception of Canadian PM Trudeau and Chinese Premier Li Qiang, who received only handshakes and smiles at the Bharat Mandapam. A video of Modi welcoming Trudeau  at the Bharat Mandapam can be viewed below.
According to Reuters , Modi, who held bilateral meetings with many world leaders during the G20 Summit, did not hold one with Trudeau. However, on September 10, Modi tweeted  that he had a discussion on India-Canada ties with Trudeau "on the sidelines of the G20 Summit". According to Modi's website , he also conveyed strong concerns about "anti-India activities of extremist elements in Canada" during their meeting. Â
We were unable to locate any credible reports confirming Modi hugging his Canadian counterpart at the G20 Summit. Nonetheless, we were also unable to independently verify whether Modi extended any friendly gestures to the Canadian PM during the two-day event. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Sep 20, 2023 23:19 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral image of Siraj's physics-defying leap is photoshopped!
content:
The viral photo was digitally altered to dramatically increase the height of his jump.
In a spectacular display of bowling skills, Mohammed Siraj achieved a remarkable feat during the Asia Cup 2023 final in Colombo, Sri Lanka. He secured his career-best bowling figures, taking an astounding six wickets for just 21 runs, equalling the earlier records set by Sri Lanka's Chaminda Vaas and the US's Ali Khan.Â
Now, a photo of Mohammed Siraj has surfaced on social media , capturing the cricketer in ecstatic celebration. In the photo, he can be seen jumping to dramatic heights.Â
Sharing the viral picture, a Twitter user wrote with admiration, "What a lovely picture! Siraj was at a completely different level on the day of the final." An archived version of the viral post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral photo was digitally altered to fake his incredible jump.
Reverse searching the viral picture, we found the original photo on Siraj's official Instagram account . The Instagram post contained a carousel of pictures of him celebrating in joy. In the caption, Siraj expressed his honour in wearing the Indian blue jersey and his motivation to continue working hard.
A comparison between the viral image and the original one from his account revealed a notable contrast in the height of Siraj's jump, pointing to significant digital alterations in the former.
Further, upon close examination of the viral image, we observed that the crowd visible in the background of Siraj's jump was also digitally manipulated. The same group of spectators was duplicated multiple times, providing further evidence that the viral photo was digitally altered. You can see the duplications pointed out in the image below.
Thus, it's clear that the viral photo of Siraj was digitally manipulated to make his jump look much higher than it actually was. - Ends Published By: Vani Mehrotra Published On: Sep 21, 2023 16:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Hangry Pak cricketers during last Asia Cup meal? This video is old
content:
The viral video shows lawyers struggling to serve themselves during a dinner following a bar council election in Pakistan in 2020.
The Pakistani cricket team suffered its most crushing defeat in One Day Internationals against the Indian squad during the Asia Cup Super 4 clash in Sri Lanka. Now, a video that's being widely shared online claims to show the Pakistani team's demeanour before the match.Â
The video shows various people fighting over a buffet. Allegedly, among the people engaging in the food-related dispute before the fated match  was the Pakistani squad. Other posts claimed that this incident occurred during the team's last dinner  in Sri Lanka after their disqualification from the series.
One Twitter user, sharing the viral video , quipped, "Entire Pakistani cricket team and staff before the match today." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that contrary to claims, the viral video does not feature the Pakistani cricket team. The video has been circulating on the internet since October 2020 and shows lawyers struggling to serve themselves during a dinner following bar elections in Pakistan.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to multiple posts  dating back to October 2020. All the posts made during that year affirmed its connection to the Lahore Bar Council election dinner .Â
A Twitter user, whose bio states he's a lawyer, shared the video back in 2020 and wrote , "Lahore bar election gathering zindabad… let's slap each other to get first dibs on the meat - let's keep our facemasks off whilst we push and shove and let's show the next generation of lawyers what lies ahead for their time."Â
The dates on which the viral video surfaced on social media also coincide with the Punjab Bar Council election schedule, as can be seen below.Â
Notably, there was an absence of recognisable faces from the Pakistan cricket team in the video. Add to that, many people in the video appeared to be clad in white shirts and black coats and ties, an attire commonly associated with advocates.Â
So, while we were unable to independently verify whether the video was from the Lahore Bar elections, or from a different bar election in Pakistan, it's more than clear it has nothing to do with the recently concluded Asia Cup 2023. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Sep 21, 2023 20:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Unmasking KBC scam 2.0 - fraudsters now posing as cops to dupe people
content:
This video is manipulated. It's part of a scam that targets people who have already fallen for 'KBC scams' in the past.
Who in India hasn't dreamt of participating in "Kaun Banega Crorepati"? The opportunity to meet Amitabh Bachchan, the chance to become a millionaire, and the thrill of a great quiz contest, the show promises it all. But this dream has also become an easy target for fraudsters, who have time and again duped people under the guise of KBC organisers.Â
Hapless victims, of course, turn to the police for help. But now, in what can easily be called a scam inside a scam, fraudsters are also pretending to be law enforcement officers helping people who have been duped by such "KBC scams". Let's take a look at what's happening. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story How are they doing it? Take a look at the video below, which has been widely shared on various social media platforms and WhatsApp. It shows a police officer addressing victims of a KBC scam. In this video, the officer introduces himself as Kuldeep Singh, a Central Bureau of Investigation officer affiliated with "Kaun Banega Crorepati", and urges victims of the scam to contact him via WhatsApp and promises to help them recover their lost funds. Seems like a noble gesture, right? Well, appearances can be deceiving. A closer look at the video reveals a noticeable disparity between the officer's words and the movement of his lips, indicating that this too is a scam. So, who is this officer? A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a video posted on the YouTube page of the Punjab Police on April 23, 2022. In this Punjabi-language video, the officer identifies himself as Harshpreet Singh, the Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) in Ludhiana Rural. Ironically, in the original video, Singh was cautioning the public about the perils of cyber fraud. What does Harshpreet Singh say about this? India Today reached out to Harshpreet Singh, currently ACP Cantt at Jalandhar, Punjab. Singh confirmed that he is the person seen in this video. "I have shared this manipulated video with my technical team, and we are diligently working to trace its source. Once we identify the responsible party, appropriate legal action will follow," he said. Funnily enough, Singh said that he too has registered FIRs related to a KBC fraud. "It's truly baffling that fraudsters are now leveraging my video to orchestrate this scam," he added. How is the doctored video being used to scam people? Facebook posts containing this video  direct users to various WhatsApp numbers. The archived version of one such post can be seen here . One such number is "9126039054". This number's WhatsApp features a uniformed police officer seated in an office as its profile picture. In the photo, one can see a nameplate on the table, bearing the name "Varinder Kumar Sharma IPS." In the photo, we noticed that the reflection on the glass tabletop revealed a different name: "Akhilesh Kumar Chaurasia". This made it clear that the name Varinder Kumar Sharma was digitally added to the nameplate in the photo. We searched online and found that Akhilesh Kumar Chaurasia currently serves as the Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Varanasi Range in Uttar Pradesh. Another number, "8144498066", being promoted with such posts, also had Chaurasia's image as its WhatsApp display picture. Police officers or a 'paan shop' owner? A search for the number "9126039054" on Google Pay revealed that it was registered under the name "Ravi Paan Shop". Another WhatsApp number linked to the viral video was registered on GPay as "Umar Faruk." India Today reached out via WhatsApp to one of these numbers. The person, who identified themselves as CBI officer  Kuldeep Singh, asked us to provide the number that had been scammed. However, we received no response from them following that. Back in October 2021, India Today exposed a group of scammers posing as "KBC Officers", conning people with promises of wealth. - Ends (With Inputs from Ashish Kumar) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Sep 21, 2023 21:34 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT pregnant with nine babies! This lady with big belly had cancer
content:
The woman was not pregnant with nine babies. She was suffering from multiple diseases including ovarian cancer, that caused her belly to swell so much.
A video making the rounds on social media shows a woman with a giant belly with bulging veins. Those sharing the clip claimed that the lady was pregnant with nine babies. The video shows her first in the hospital and then a row of newborns, seemingly implying that she had given birth to the nine children.Â
One person shared the video on X, formerly Twitter, writing, "Living with 9 babies for 9 months! Mothers are the most magnificent creatures in the world. But it is not clear whether the dad is crying from joy or sadness." An archived version of this post can be found here .
India Today found that the video showed a Chinese woman suffering from multiple ailments including ovarian cancer that led to the condition of her stomach.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report  featuring screenshots from the video in question. According to it, the woman was Huang Guoxian, a mother of two from China, whose stomach had been expanding for two years due to an underlying medical condition. The woman was diagnosed with multiple diseases including ovarian cancer and liver cirrhosis.
We then found another report  about this woman from October 2020. It stated that the Chinese woman went through surgery. Huang Guoxian's abdomen reportedly ballooned by nearly 40 kilograms as it filled with fluid and tumours of different sizes in a span of two years. Huang, a resident of the Dazhi village of Songqi Town near Anshun, China, is a farmer who had two kids — a son and a daughter. Her belly, which was reportedly flat in 2018, swelled to an enormous size in two years. Huang then made a plea for help through local media following which donations poured in for her treatment in 2020. Huang reportedly received more than Rs 11 lakh in donations, and after the surgery, Huang said she would use the remaining amount to start a small business upon her recovery. We also found photos of Huang who went bald during the cancer treatment. While we could not find a source for the multiple shots of the newborns in the viral video, several news reports make it clear that the woman was not pregnant with nine babies. - Ends Written by Sanjana Saxena Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 22, 2023 20:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Zelensky was NOT greeted by 'Glory to Urine' billboard in US
content:
This video is old and has nothing to do with Zelensky's recent US visit.
Following Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's recent visit to the US, a video of a busy urban intersection  featuring a digital billboard with "Glory to Urine" written over the colours of the nation's flag went viral. Allegedly, this was displayed in New York City  to welcome Zelensky and the text "Urine" instead of "Ukraine" was a technical error. Â
The archived version of one such claim can be seen here .
India Today found that this video is old and has nothing to do with Zelensky's recent US visit.  Our Probe
Zelensky's US visit received worldwide coverage. Had such a message been displayed in New York City, it would definitely have been reported in the media. However, we didn't find any such report.Â
The viral video bears a "Fox News Digital" logo. However, a Fox News Digital spokesperson told India Today that they did not publish any such video. Clearly, the logo was digitally added to give the impression that this video was broadcast by the channel. Geolocating the placeÂ
Markian Kuzmowycz , a digital threat analyst based in the US, wrote on Twitter that this video was taken at the intersection of 42nd Street and 8th Avenue at Times Square, in Manhattan, NewYork. He also posted a recent picture from this location. Similarly, NBC News journalist Ben Collins, too, posted a video from the same spot. I just want to thank the absolute morons who got "Glory to Urine" trending. They were able to shine a light on a New York miracle: the construction and grand opening of an entire pizza restaurant in six hours. pic.twitter.com/qEnUiV6iys — Ben Collins (@oneunderscore__) September 21, 2023 On comparing them, we could say with certainty that this was indeed the location seen in the viral video. However, certain elements in the video posted by Collins appear to be different. For example, there was a McDonald's outlet in the place of a brown building and a narrow digital advertisement strip below the main advertisement. Using Google search, we found that the McDonald's outlet has existed at this location at least since April 2023 .  We found an image of the restaurant posted in February 2023  as well, but in this image, the logo at the top of the building was missing. There could be a possibility that this outlet was opened to the public between February and April. In a November 2022 YouTube video  of this location, we can see that the McDonald's outlet is not there and instead, it's the same brown building with black stripes as seen in the viral video. India Today contacted Big Outdoor , the company that manages the advertisements displayed on the signage at the spot seen in the viral video. Erin Watkins, General Counsel at Big Outdoor, said that the advertisement seen in the viral video was not run by them. Though many Twitter users have claimed that this video was manipulated , we could not independently verify its source. However, it is evident that an old video from New York's "Times Square" is being circulated in connection with Zelensky's recent US visit. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Sep 23, 2023 22:01 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Khalistan supporter threatening Gujarati is NOT from Canada
content:

India Today found that the video is not from Canada but from London and is unrelated to the ongoing crisis. OUR PROBE
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found a news report in "Desh Gujarat" . Published on March 2023, this report featured a screengrab from the viral video, and the headline mentioned that the incident took place in the United Kingdom.Â
Further refined searches led us to reports in Times Of India , OneIndia News , and Free Press Journal . title: Fact Check: Did India reject visa of 'maaro mujhe maaro' Pakistan influencer?
content:
Momin Saqib and Saad Ur Rehman (Ducky Bhai) explicitly stated on social media that they did not apply for an Indian visa.
After several dramatic episodes and significant delays, the Pakistani cricket team  finally received their visas to travel to India in preparation for the upcoming ODI World Cup. They were greeted in Hyderabad on September 27 with a warm welcome.Â
Meanwhile, several social media pages and individuals claimed that the visa  applications of Pakistani influencers Momin Shaqib and Saad Ur Rehman — popularly known as "Ducky Bhai" — were declined by Indian authorities.Â
Shaqib is a Pakistani cricket fan who went viral with his "Maaro mujhe maaro" interview after Pakistan's crushing defeat against India during the 2019 World Cup.
One person wrote on Twitter, "India Rejects Visas to Pakistan's Top YouTuber Ducky Bhai & TV Star Momin Saqib Ahead of the World Cup." The archived version of such a post can be seen here . India Rejects Visas to Pakistan's Top YouTuber Ducky Bhai & TV Star Momin Saqib Ahead of the World Cup. #pakistanrepublic #PakistanZindabad pic.twitter.com/gpGEAFu9N6 — Pakistan Republic (@republicdotpk) September 27, 2023
India Rejects Visas to Pakistan's Top YouTuber Ducky Bhai & TV Star Momin Saqib Ahead of the World Cup. #pakistanrepublic #PakistanZindabad pic.twitter.com/gpGEAFu9N6 — Pakistan Republic (@republicdotpk) September 27, 2023
We found no reliable media reports suggesting this had happened. Subsequently, we tried scanning the social media accounts of these influencers. The official Instagram account of Momin Shaqib  did not feature any photos or videos regarding this. However, Shaqib shared a story on his Instagram on September 26, which contained a screenshot of his tweet. This tweet read, "There's news circulating that my Indian visa got rejected. Just to clear the air, I haven't even applied yet! I'd also like to take this opportunity to emphasise on the importance of fact-checking & verifying news from authentic sources before spreading misinformation. Thank you." There's news circulating that my Indian visa got rejected. Just to clear the air, I haven't even applied yet! I'd also like to take this opportunity to emphasise on the importance of fact-checking & verifying news from authentic sources before spreading misinformation Thank you
— Momin Saqib (@mominsaqib) September 27, 2023 Saad Ur Rehman, also known as Ducky Bhai , shared a video on the same day, addressing the issue. He stated, "I came across some news articles this morning claiming that I had applied for an Indian visa to attend the World Cup, and it was denied... None of this is true. I haven't even applied. So, I decided to create this video to clarify that this is false information." This video can be seen below. India Today has reached out to the visa department of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad, Pakistan, for a statement. The article will be revised and updated once we receive a response. It is important to note that we cannot independently verify if anyone applies for a visa and if their application is subsequently rejected. However, both influencers have explicitly denied submitting visa applications, making the viral postcard misleading. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Sep 28, 2023 20:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Pak team not met with 'murdabad' chants in Hyderabad, viral clip edited
content:
The video is manipulated. The original footage shows a warm reception without any derogatory chants.
The Pakistan cricket team arrived at Hyderabad Airport for the ICC ODI World Cup amid heightened security. It received a spirited welcome from Indian cricket fans.Â
Amid this, a social media storm ensued after a video purportedly showing derogatory chants of "Pakistan Murdabad" by Indian fans went viral. Sharing the viral video, a Twitter user wrote , "Pakistan Murdabad chants were raised when Pakistan terrorist team arrived in Bharat. Based public. I bow down to them." An archive of the same can be seen here .
India Today found that the video was digitally manipulated to add the anti-Pakistan chants. Our Probe
Reverse searching the keyframes of the viral video led us to a video shared by the news agency ANI on September 27. The tweet read: " Telangana: Pakistan Cricket team arrives at Hyderabad airport, ahead of the World Cup scheduled to be held between October 5 to November 19, in India." In this video, fans could be heard chanting "Babar, Babar" in support of Pakistani skipper Babar Azam.
Further searches led us to several videos of this moment shot from different angles, corroborating the ANI video's authenticity and debunking any claims of "Pakistan Murdabad" chants.
India Today journalist Maruthi Acharya, who was present at the airport and covered the event, further affirmed that he heard no such anti-Pakistani slogans when the players arrived.Â
Contrary to the viral claims, the players' reception was overwhelmingly warm , prompting gratitude from Pakistani players and social media users.  Even Pakistan's Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari expressed his appreciation for the hearty welcome.
The Pakistan Cricket Board also shared glimpses of the warm reception on Twitter.Â
While we cannot independently verify if no anti-Pakistan slogans were raised by individuals there, it's evident that the viral video was digitally manipulated to make it look like there were. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Sep 28, 2023 20:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Kohli didn't announce party for Pakistan team, his parody account did
content:
The tweet originated from a parody account mimicking Kohli's official Twitter handle. The cricketer tweeted no such thing.
The Pakistan cricket contingent's arrival in India on September 27 has already been the subject of disinformation campaigns . Following a manipulated video  of people chanting anti-Pakistan slogans at the airport, now there are claims of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli allegedly  announcing a party at his residence for the Pakistani players, with special mention of Pakistan all-rounder and vice-captain Shadab Khan .
A Facebook user shared a poster of Kohli's alleged announcement, and wrote , "Pakistan Cricket Team receives a very warm welcome in last night which wins hearts, after 7 Years Pakistan Team landed in India. In a tweet Indian top batsman Virat Kohli welcomes the Pakistan Cricket team and said he is excited to host them to his residence, especially Shadab Khan. Pakistani Players looks confident after arrival to Hyderabad India. and they are very positive to brin the world cup to Pakistan." An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today's investigation found that Kohli made no such tweet about a party for his Pakistani counterparts. Our Probe
We checked all of Kohli's official social media accounts to see if he had indeed made such an announcement. Upon further probe, we found that the claim originated from a parody account mimicking Kohli's official Twitter account. The parody account's tweet went viral, amassing over a thousand retweets and 14K likes. I warmly Welcome Pakistan Cricket Team on their arrival in my country after a long time period of 7 years, I will host a party for my friends specially for Shadab at my house 🤗 Love you all, always spread love and joy❣️💕 #Hyderabad #PakistanCricketTeam #BabarAzam𓃵 #CWC23 pic.twitter.com/dLwQo17LOq — Virat Kohli (@amiVkohli) September 27, 2023
I warmly Welcome Pakistan Cricket Team on their arrival in my country after a long time period of 7 years, I will host a party for my friends specially for Shadab at my house 🤗 Love you all, always spread love and joy❣️💕 #Hyderabad #PakistanCricketTeam #BabarAzam𓃵 #CWC23 pic.twitter.com/dLwQo17LOq — Virat Kohli (@amiVkohli) September 27, 2023
The viral tweet from the parody account read, "I warmly welcome Pakistan Cricket Team on their arrival in my country after a long time period of 7 years, I will host a party for my friends, especially for Shadab, at my house. Love you all, always spread love and joy."Â
Many social media users and the news outlet Free Press Journal  fell for it, mistaking it for Kohli's official account. Notably, the parody account has only 785 followers on Twitter, whereas Kohli's real Twitter account boasts over 58 million followers.
The last tweet from Kohli's authentic Twitter account  was on September 27, featuring a photo of the Indian women's cricket team after winning a Gold Medal in a match against Sri Lanka at the Asian Games 2023.
In conclusion, it is evident that a tweet from Kohli's parody account was wrongly believed to be authentic. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Sep 29, 2023 16:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Old and CGI videos peddled as devastation caused by recent NY floods
content:
None of these clips show the present situation in New York. The clips of the submerged subway stations are old and that of the octopus attacking a car is CGI.
Emergency was declared across New York on September 29 after torrential downpours triggered flash floods in several areas. Amid this, a deluge of videos started making the rounds on social media, allegedly showing the devastation caused by the floods. Of these, two videos were prominently shared by many people. One contained  seven different clips of submerged subway stations  with water falling from the roofs on trains and gushing through the stations. Scary. The New York City subway looking like an end of times waterpark. #flashflood #flashflooding #flooding #flood #newyork #newyorkcity #nyc #brooklyn #rain #rainstorm #storm #downpour #streetflooding #sel #abd #usa #BREAKING #williamsburg #NewJersey #manhattan #queens #NYC pic.twitter.com/Ea2ejSjpKA — Usman Akram Goraya (@UsmanAkram82) September 29, 2023
