The other video featured a giant octopus  in a parking garage, climbing atop a car  with its tentacles, and then crushing it. Archived versions of these posts can be found here  and here . BREAKING: State of Emergency declared in New York City due to Mass flooding. Be careful where you park your car. pic.twitter.com/lhymSNal2l — Aldrich (@observer888888) September 29, 2023
BREAKING: State of Emergency declared in New York City due to Mass flooding. Be careful where you park your car. pic.twitter.com/lhymSNal2l — Aldrich (@observer888888) September 29, 2023
India Today, in its investigation, found that the clips of the submerged subway stations are old and that of the octopus attacking a car was made using CGI.
Clips of submerged subway stations
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a report in The Mirror dated September 2, 2021. According to it, tropical storm Ida battered America's northeast regions, leading to a state of emergency in New York. Â
Out of the seven clips, this report  carried a screenshot of the video of water falling from the roof on a train and longer versions  of two other videos of flood-hit subway stations . The report also stated that the clip of water cascading down the steps was from the Manhattan subway station, while that of a heavy pool of water hitting a train was from the Brooklyn station.
Further searches led us to an Instagram post  by Nieves Zuberbühler, a journalist based in New York , which featured all the seven clips in question. The post from September 2, 2021, credited an account named "subwaycreatures" for a few of them. This confirmed that these videos predate the ongoing floods in New York by at least two years.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by SubwayCreatures (@subwaycreatures) VIDEO OF GIANT OCTOPUS
A post shared by SubwayCreatures (@subwaycreatures)
We noticed that the viral video contained the watermark "@ghost3dee". Searching for this led us to a VFX YouTube channel of the same name . According to the channel's description, the Qatari artist Alex Z running the channel created a CGI octopus character called "Churro".
On this channel, apart from the viral video of "Churro" attacking a car , we found several other videos of the same CGI octopus loitering in the sand , taking a bath  and even changing its colours .
While sharing the viral video on Instagram  on September 25, 2023, Alex mentioned that he made the clip using Snap Renderfarm, a high-performance computer system built to render computer-generated images (CGI).Â
Thus, it is clear that a CGI video of an octopus and old videos of flooded subway stations were wrongly shared as scenes unfolding in flood-hit New York. - Ends (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Sep 30, 2023 18:53 IST

title: Fact Check: 2011 Assange statement on Afghanistan FALSELY attributed to Ukraine war
content:
The quote is old. Assange made the statement in 2011 in the context of the US-Afghanistan war, and the word "Afghanistan" was replaced with "Ukraine" in the viral quote.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, a prominent advocate for transparency, has on several occasions voiced opposition to wars. Now, a statement allegedly made by Assange on the Ukraine-Russia war is going viral  on social media.Â
The quote goes: " The goal is to use Ukraine to launder money from the United States and Europe through Ukraine and back into the hands of the transnational elite. The goal is an endless war, not a successful war." The archived version of one such post containing this alleged Assange quote can be seen here .
India Today found that while Julian Assange said something similar, it was in 2011, and it was about the US-Afghanistan war. Our Probe
Using a keyword search, we came across a tweet made by the official Wikileaks account in 2021 that contained a video featuring Assange. The tweet noted that Assange made this statement in 2011 and verbatim states his utterance as: "The goal is to use Afghanistan to wash money out of the tax bases of the US and Europe through Afghanistan and back into the hands of a transnational security elite. The goal is an endless war, not a successful war."
Even in the video, Assange can be seen saying Afghanistan and not Ukraine while making the statement.
We found the same video shared by TRT World , a leading Turkish media outlet, in 2021. Here too, Assange could be heard saying Afghanistan instead of Ukraine. The post here also notes that this statement was made by Assange in 2011, more than a decade before the current Ukraine-Russia conflict started.
We also found an extended version of Assange's video on YouTube , uploaded in 2012. The caption stated that Assange made the statement during an event called "Stop the War" on October 8, 2011.
Founded by British political activist, academic, and journalist John Rees, the Stop The War Coalition is a group in Britain campaigning against the wars. In 2011, Julian Assange attended a demonstration on the tenth anniversary of the Afghanistan War in Trafalgar Square, London.Â
We also found a p hoto of Assange on stock images website Alamy , titled, "Julian Assange joined the demonstration to stop the war and he gave a speech in Trafalgar Square," where he could be seen wearing the same clothes as in the video — further corroborating his presence at the event.
We also checked if Assange had made any statements on the Ukraine-Russia war. However, we couldn't find anything. Assange has been detained in the maximum security Belmarsh prison in London for over four years, where his visitation rights are restricted. Earlier this year, representatives of Reporters Without Borders were blocked from meeting him in prison.
Thus, it's clear that an old Assange quote about Afghanistan was modified to make it look like his opinion on the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Sep 30, 2023 21:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of flooded supermarket is NOT from flood-hit New York
content:
This video is from Auckland, New Zealand, and this incident happened in January 2023.
Heavy rainfall caused flash floods across New York City in late September. As the city drowned, many shared photos and videos of submerged locales. One such video , recorded inside a supermarket, showed flooding and customers inside the store wading through knee-high water and debris.Â
One tweet containing the video read: "USA, People grocery shopping in knee-high water during the apocalyptic flooding in New York City today." Archived versions of such posts can be seen here and here .Â
India Today found that the video is neither recent nor from the US. Our ProbeÂ
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across a news report in Yahoo News . Dated January 28, 2023, this article featured screenshots extracted from the widely shared video. According to this report, the video was shot at the Glenfield supermarket in Auckland, New Zealand.
Reportedly, Auckland witnessed floods after heavy torrential rains, which led to the loss of at least three lives. The city declared a state of emergency following an unprecedented 249mm of rainfall within 24 hours.
Subsequent searches with advanced keywords led us to a video report from The Chronicles Australia that mentioned a New Zealand supermarket in Wairau had been flooded as a state of emergency was declared across the city.
A News AU report on YouTube also featured this video. Another news report , which contained screengrabs from the video, mentioned that the store was called PackNSave and a TikTok user first shared this video.Â
Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with the New York City flash floods. - Ends Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Oct 2, 2023 15:07 IST

title: Fact Check: 2016 video of SRK pushing away fan falsely linked to 'Dunki'
content:
This video of the scuffle between SRK and a fan is from September 2016 and has no links to the upcoming movie "Dunki".
Shah Rukh Khan's upcoming movie "Dunki" is reportedly going to clash with Prabhas's "Salaar"  — both of which are slated to release on December 22 , prompting a fan war . Social media is now rife with speculations that "Dunki" is a remake of a Malayalam movie named "CIA (Comrade in America)".
Amid this, a video of SRK walking through a crowd  and angrily pushing someone away is making the rounds on social media. Those sharing the video , claimed that Shahrukh Khan slapped a fan in the crowd, who shouted that "Dunki" is a remake of a Malayalam movie.
One person shared the video on Twitter writing , "SRK was seen slapping a fan when someone from crowd shouted that Dunki is a remake of 2017 Malayalam movie CIA. No matter how much famous you get, never play with the emotions of fans. No respect to his fans." An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that this video dates back to September 2016, and has no links to "Dunki".
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an article  dated September 20, 2016, carrying an extended version of the video in question. According to it, this incident took place in Amsterdam, where SRK manhandled one of his fans, who tried coming too close to him. In the full video , Khan could be seen clicking photos with the other people in the crowd after the scuffle.Â
Using this clue, we found a YouTube video  containing the viral video in a better resolution, followed by another clip shot by the fan who was pushed away by the actor. This video was uploaded on September 19, 2016.
We also found several media reports about this incident from ABP news , India TV , DNA India , and India Today  published in September 2016. title: Fact Check: This massive landslide occurred in China, NOT Greece or India
content:
This incident occurred on September 27 in China's Sichuan province.
Elias, a powerful storm  that was the second one to hit Greece in the span of a month, has devastated central parts of the country. Floods and landslides have so far led to the death of at least 17 people . A video of a massive landslide, allegedly from Greece, is now being widely shared on social media.Â
However, while some claimed that the video was from Greece , others alleged that it was from India . The archived versions of two such claims can be seen here  and here . Â
India Today found that this video is neither from Greece nor from India. It shows a March landslide in the Sichuan province of China. OUR PROBE
In response to the viral tweets, we noticed that people pointed out  that this incident happened in China.Â
Subsequently, we ran a keyword search and found that the viral video was shared on Twitter by American meteorological news outlet AccuWeather  on September 30, 2023. Per the tweet, the incident took place on September 27 in China's Chongzhou city. The video has been attributed to "Newsflare via Reuters Connect". We found the longer version of the footage on the official YouTube channel of Newsflare.Â
As per Newsflare, this incident took place in Chongzhou, located in the Sichuan province on September 27. No casualties or vehicle damages were reported. Authorities reportedly quickly responded, enacting temporary traffic restrictions, and barring all vehicular traffic from the area.
This incident was also reported by multiple Chinese-language media outlets. Some such reports can be seen here , here , and here .Â
To sum it up, footage of a recent landslide in China was falsely shared as one in Greece and India. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Oct 3, 2023 19:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Old mass shooting video falsely linked to Bangkok mall shootout by teen
content:
The viral video is not of the recent Bangkok shooting by a 14-year-old. It is an old video from the 2020 Korat mass shooting in a different part of Thailand.
A 14-year-old boy shot and killed two people in a spree on October 3 at Bangkok's Siam Paragon shopping centre. The assailant used a modified pistol initially intended for firing blanks, turning it into a weapon that shot real bullets.
Following this, a video showing men taking cover behind wheelchairs and baby strollers in what appears to be a shopping mall while firing assault rifles has gone viral on social media. Allegedly, this video was of the mall shooting in Bangkok.
A Twitter user, while sharing the viral video, wrote, "In Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, a 14-year-old boy opened fire at the Siam Paragon shopping center with a pistol, killing 3 people and wounding 4 people. A conflict broke out between the 14-year-old boy and the security forces at the shopping center." An archived version of the viral video can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video is old and unrelated to the Bangkok mall shooting. It shows shootings that occurred between February 8 and 9, 2020, in another Thailand province, Nakhon Ratchasima.
Upon reverse searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across social media posts from 2020  that stated the clip was from the Korat shooting in Thailand.
Subsequent searches with relevant keywords led us to a February 2020 video on the YouTube channel of the British news network Sky News. This video contained a snippet of the viral video shot from another angle. In this video, several men, seemingly special forces, could be seen firing assault rifles. A blue baby stroller and several wheelchairs in the backdrop were also visible, consistent with the viral video.
Another Sky News video report  from the same time said that these videos were from inside the Terminal 21 mall in Korat, where soldiers had taken positions.
In February 2020, a soldier from the Thailand Royal Army went on a rampage , killing at least 29 people and wounding 57 in Nakhon Ratchasima. Most of the victims were at the city's Terminal 21 shopping centre, where the shooter laid an overnight siege with an assault rifle and ammunition stolen from his army base.
In conclusion, it's evident that an old video of soldiers taking positions to neutralise a gunman who had laid siege in a mall in another part of Thailand is being shared as a recent shooting inside a shopping centre by a teenager in Bangkok. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 5, 2023 15:44 IST

title: Fact Check: Violent robbery-gone-wrong video isn't from UK - it's from Brazil
content:
This video is from a 2022 incident in Brazil.
A video of a group of armed men brutally attacking a person is making the rounds on social media platforms. In the video , a person could be seen being robbed by two masked men. When he retaliates, a bunch of other people rush to the spot, beat up the victim, and stab him several times.Â
Those sharing the clip claimed that this was a recent incident that took place at the Sunderland Metro Station in Tyne and Wear, England. Blaming media outlets for not reporting the incident, one person shared the video, writing, "Metro in Sunderland. Not shown on any news channels. Covered up and censored because it's blacks with blades on a mugging spree. And it's gonna get worse cause your government is to blame for letting these scum in." The archived version of one such post can be found here.Â
India Today found that this video is not from the United Kingdom at all. It's an old incident from Brazil. Our Probe
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to a report  in O Globo, a Brazilian newspaper. In the report, we found the viral clip in higher resolution. According to the date stamp visible in the footage, the incident took place on February 20, 2022.Â
A subsequent keyword search led us to a Brazilian TV news report. SBT Rio's report stated that a man named Pablo Felipe Lima Bernardo was attacked at the Boiuna BRT station in Taquara, a municipality in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
The assailants were reportedly caught by locals and handed over to the police. Bernardo miraculously survived the attack and was interviewed by the Brazilian news channel. The report contained a video of the scene of the crime . In it, we observed a machine with "RioCard Mais" written on it — similar to the one in the viral video. RioCard is a smartcard system used in the transport system of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The report also showed clips of residents who reportedly caught the five men involved in the robbery and the police arresting them. We then found several reports  stating the same information about the incident. Vídeo mostra o momento em que homem é esfaqueado em estação do BRT. Crédito: Reprodução #ODia pic.twitter.com/yMwOGx8HNW — Jornal O Dia (@jornalodia) February 21, 2022 It's noteworthy that the video in question went viral earlier as well. At the time, people claimed it was from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It was debunked by the Malaysian police. - Ends (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Oct 5, 2023 19:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Kejriwal didn't mock ED hours before Sanjay Singh's arrest, clip is from May
content:
The viral video is from May 2023, when the ED included Singh's name in the charge sheet but later called it a mistake.
Aam Aadmi Party member and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate on October 4 in connection with a money laundering case linked to the ongoing investigation into Delhi's liquor policy. This was the third arrest of an AAP leader on similar charges after Satyendra Jain and Manish Sisodia. Opposition parties condemned the arrest as politically motivated.
Now, a video featuring Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has surfaced on social media, where he appears to be mocking the ED's involvement in implicating Singh in the alleged liquor policy scam. Those sharing the video claimed that this press conference occurred hours before Singh's arrest.
Speaking in Hindi during the press conference, Kejriwal remarked, "ED filed a chargesheet in the case, including Sanjay Singh's name. Following Singh's threat to file a case, they issued an apology, acknowledging the error in naming him. Despite the ED's prevalent nationwide notices instilling fear in people, this time Sanjay Singh served a notice to the ED and put them in distress. Consequently, ED was forced to admit in court a lack of evidence against him…"
A Twitter user, while sharing the viral video, wrote, "Sanjay Singh was arrested by ED today. Meanwhile, a few hours before he was arrested." An archive of the post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video of Kejriwal mocking the ED dates back to May 2023 and was not made hours before the federal law enforcement agency arrested Sanjay Singh. Our Probe
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a video uploaded on the Facebook page of Aam Aadmi Party Delhi. The press conference was convened by the Delhi chief minister to unveil details about a new scheme: an app-based air-conditioned bus service allowing seat reservations.
Following the scheme's presentation, questions were invited from reporters there. In response to a query about the investigation into the alleged liquor policy scam, the chief minister made the statement in question.
Media reports further corroborated the ED's apology to Sanjay Singh for erroneously including his name in the chargesheet filed in the Delhi excise policy case.
After Singh's arrest, the Aam Aadmi Party's UP wing shared the clipped version of the months-old press conference on Twitter. Subsequently, this gained traction and was picked up and shared by several social media users.
In conclusion, Kejriwal did not make the viral statement just before Singh's arrest by the ED. The video dates back to May 2023 when Singh's name was erroneously included in the chargesheet, leading to an apology from the investigating agency. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Oct 5, 2023 20:44 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 video from Austria goes viral as cloudburst in Sikkim
content:
This video was captured near Lake Millstatt in Austria in 2018.
A startling video purportedly showing a cloudburst in Sikkim has gone viral on social media. It shows what appears to be a thick column of rain rapidly moving from the mountains towards a water body. The sound of thunder can also be heard in the video.Â
At least 14 people were killed when a cloudburst over Lhonak Lake in North Sikkim resulted in flash floods in the Teesta River on October 4.Â
A Facebook user shared the video and wrote,"Cloud bursts. At North Sikkim chunthang". The archived version of two such posts can be seen here and here .Â
India Today found that this video is neither recent nor does it have anything to do with Sikkim. It shows a microburst over Lake Millstatt in Austria in 2018.
In the comments under one post containing the viral video, we noticed several claimed that it was old. We then took our search further and reverse-searched its keyframes. This led us to a 2020 YouTube video titled "Microburst at Lake Millstatt in Austria".
The video's description read: "It is situated at 588 metres above the Adriatic (1,929 ft), north of the Drava Valley within the Gurktal Alps (Nock Mountains) range of the Central Eastern Alps, near the town of Spittal an der Drau. With a surface area of 13.3 km2 (5.1 sq mi) Lake Millstatt is the second largest lake of Carinthia (after Lake Wörth), though with a depth of 142 m (466 ft) the most voluminous by far."
Subsequent searches led us to a longer version of the video shared on the YouTube channel of a person called Peter Maier on June 12, 2018. In the description of this video, Maier said that this timelapse video captured a microburst over Lake Millstatt in Austria.Â
An Insider report from June 2018 stated that mountaineer Peter Maier captured the video in question from his hotel terrace near Lake Millstatt, Austria. In 2018, when this video went viral, many questioned its authenticity. Maier quickly put an end to the speculations , writing on Facebook: "Here are a few original recordings with original sound clips, for all those who still believe that it is fake." DIFFERENCE BETWEEN CLOUDBURST & MICROBURSTÂ
According to the Indian Meteorological Department , a cloudburst is an extreme weather event characterised by the occurrence of a large amount of rainfall over a small area within a short span of time.Â
A microburst, on the other hand, is a small column of exceptionally intense and localised sinking air that results in a violent outrush of air at the ground, according to the US-based meteorological news network AccuWeather .Â
To sum up, an old video from Austria is being falsely shared as a recent cloudburst in Sikkim. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Oct 5, 2023 23:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Social media bombarded with old photos of devastation after drone attack in Syria
content:
This image dates back to February 2023 and shows a building that collapsed due to the devastating earthquakes in Syria and Turkey.
A drone strike on October 6 killed at least 89 people in Syria's Homs province. The Syrian government has blamed the attack on a military college during a graduation ceremony on "terrorist organisations supported by well-known international parties."Â
In its aftermath, two photos have been making the rounds on social media, both allegedly showing the effects of the strike. Neither photo, however, had anything to do with it. Let us talk about them one by one. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story PHOTO 1 The first photo showed a completely demolished building in what looks like a rural area. A Twitter user shared the photo and wrote: "People are dying and nobody cares #DroneAttack #Syria #SyriaDroneAttack".  Its archived version can be viewed here.  A quick reverse search of this image led us to a February 6 report published by The Moscow Times in an article about Russian aid being given to Turkey and Syria following devastating earthquakes . Thousands died and millions were displaced in two massive earthquakes that hit parts of Turkey and Syria in February 2023.Â
The first photo showed a completely demolished building in what looks like a rural area. A Twitter user shared the photo and wrote: "People are dying and nobody cares #DroneAttack #Syria #SyriaDroneAttack".  Its archived version can be viewed here. Â
A quick reverse search of this image led us to a February 6 report published by The Moscow Times in an article about Russian aid being given to Turkey and Syria following devastating earthquakes . Thousands died and millions were displaced in two massive earthquakes that hit parts of Turkey and Syria in February 2023.Â
As per the photo's caption, the image showed people searching through the wreckage of a collapsed building in Azmarin, a town in Syria's Idlib province. It was shot by Ghaith Alsayed of the Associated Press. The photo was also used in several other reports in February 2023 with the same description.Â
We also found the photo on Alsayed's Instagram page, where he had shared it on February 6 as part of a collection of photos from Syria in the aftermath of the quakes.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Ghaith Alsayed (@ghaith.alsayed)
A post shared by Ghaith Alsayed (@ghaith.alsayed)
Thus, it's clear that the photo in question has nothing to do with the drone strike. PHOTO 2
The second photo showed people, including a man carrying a child in his arms, running away from a fire. Smoke billowing out of a burning car could be seen in the backdrop. A Twitter user shared it and wrote, "#Syria Under Attack. about 100 innocent Civilians dead and several were injured after the #droneattack on the Army Academy. People rushed for help and shelter." Its archived version can be seen here . Using reverse image search, we found that this photo was used in a January 31, 2021, report by The Hindustan Times . As per the photo caption, it showed the aftermath of an explosion in the rebel-controlled northern countryside of Syria's Aleppo province. The image was attributed to the news agency Agence France-Presse. At least five people died in this January 31, 2021, incident involving a car bomb. Thus, it's clear that this photo, too, predates the October 6 drone strike in Syria. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 6, 2023 21:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Spat between Naidu and Pawan Kaylan supporters? No, both men are TDP members
content:
This is a 2016 incident involving two councillors of the Telugu Desam Party and is not related to recent events in Andhra Pradesh.
Actor-turned-politician and Jana Sena Party chief K Pawan Kalyan announced all-out support for jailed Telugu Desam Party supremo and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu on October 4. Following this, speculations about Pawan Kalyan leaving the National Democratic Alliance spread like wildfire.Â
Pawan Kalyan later clarified that he was not leaving the Bharatiya Janata Party-led alliance. And if social media is to be believed, a rift now appears to have formed between supporters of his party and those of Naidu.Â
A video of a violent altercation , allegedly between a TDP supporter and a JSP supporter in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, was widely shared. Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma also shared the video with a similar claim. The archived version of such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today found that the video in question is more than seven years old. Furthermore, according to reports from 2016, both men involved in the scuffle were councillors from the TDP.
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to an NDTV report from March 1, 2016, that contained a video of the same incident shot from various angles. According to the report, this incident took place during a municipal council meeting in the Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh, and both men were TDP councillors.Â
The two men were reportedly fighting over whose name should be entered first in the minutes of the meeting. Then-chief minister of Andhra Pradesh Chandrababu Naidu reportedly took disciplinary action against both men after the footage went viral on social media.Â
According to a Deccan Chronicle report from the same time, the incident happened at a council meeting in Tenali municipality, and the two councillors fighting were Gummadi Ramesh and Pasupulati Trimurtulu.
The dispute began when Ramesh insisted that every issue debated in the council should be documented in the minutes' book to ensure transparency, while Trimurtulu believed that trivial matters need not be recorded. The verbal argument escalated, and both men resorted to using unparliamentary language. As tempers flared, Ramesh physically attacked Trimurtulu, who responded in kind.
A video of the incident was also tweeted by ANI on February 29, 2016. Multiple other regional media organisations also reported the incident at the time. WATCH: Clash between 2 councillors of Telugu Desam Party(TDP) in Tenali municipality of Guntur Distt(Andhra Pradesh) https://t.co/Ax1fAQw5V1 — ANI (@ANI) February 29, 2016
WATCH: Clash between 2 councillors of Telugu Desam Party(TDP) in Tenali municipality of Guntur Distt(Andhra Pradesh) https://t.co/Ax1fAQw5V1 — ANI (@ANI) February 29, 2016
It is hence evident that the video in question is years old and does not show TDP and JSP members clashing with each other. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 6, 2023 22:01 IST

title: Fact Check: Gavaskar didn't criticise World Cup's management, viral quote false
content:
The viral tweet falsely attributes the viral remarks to Gavaskar. He was not part of the commentary team for that
 game.
The Cricket World Cup 2023 has ignited passion across India. However, the enthusiasm noticeably waned during the opening matches , especially the clash between England and New Zealand in Hyderabad. In response, organisers resorted to an immediate solution: selling tickets  at the stadium gates.
Against this backdrop, a fabricated quote attributed to Sunil Gavaskar emerged on social media . Alongside Gavaskar's photo, the claim suggests he's deeply upset with BCCI's handling of the World Cup, implying he's ashamed of his Indian identity.Â
After investigation, India Today's Fact Check found the narrative baseless. Upon reaching out to Gavaskar, he emphatically denied the allegations, asserting, "Those who know me understand that I would never be ashamed to be an Indian. I am and will always remain a proud Indian."
Among the first X users to spin this false narrative was a X user named "ASG." ASG's tweet, widely circulated with over 1500 shares at the time of filing this report, states, "Sunil Gavaskar on Star Sports: 'I am ashamed to call myself Indian. This is the worst Cricket World Cup. Empty stadiums, no scoreboard, pathetic management from BCCI. Gavaskar didn't hold back." The false narrative was then propagated by other users.
On investigation, India Today uncovered significant inconsistencies. Primarily, Gavaskar was not part of the commentary team for that match. Moreover, a thorough search of the mainstream media revealed no coverage of any such remarks by him.
Additionally, the user "ASG" has previously spread misleading information. In 2022, ASG wrongly attributed a fabricated statement  to English cricketer Nasser Hussain. Hussain promptly debunked this, labelling it false and urging its removal .
Further scrutiny indicated the misinformation wasn't merely a mistake. When another user pointed out Gavaskar wasn't commenting during that match, ASG defended the false claim, suggesting Gavaskar made a brief appearance to express his displeasure  and then departed. Some other users amplified the false claim asserting they had also heard Gavaskar's supposed comments.
Interestingly, many of these accounts  seem to originate from Pakistan and Dubai .
India Today has previously unearthed  sophisticated misinformation campaigns emanating from Pakistan. For instance, we debunked an incorrect statement assigned to Pakistani cricketers Wasim Akram and Waqar Younis . Disturbingly, these misinformation campaigns display similar patterns in their dissemination. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 7, 2023 22:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Some videos being shared as recent Israeli airstrikes are months old
content:
The viral videos show an older Israeli airstrike and are not related to the ongoing conflict.
In response to the recent infiltration by Palestinian militants from Gaza into southern Israel and the firing of thousands of rockets, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared , "We are at war." Following the escalation, social media platforms are flooded with pictures and videos documenting the ongoing conflict.
A viral video showing a high-rise being wiped out is going viral on social media. A user sharing it wrote : "Israel announces 'Operation Iron Swords,' drafts tens of thousands, launches first major retaliatory Airstrike on Hamas Interior Ministry building (planned terror attack)."
The second viral video , showing airstrikes demolishing a multi-story building, is claimed to show Israel's response to Hamas. Similar claims going viral can be seen here , here and here .
India Today found both videos to be old and unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Gaza Conflict.
A reverse search of keyframes from the first video led to the YouTube channel of Voice of America, where we found a similar video uploaded on May 13, 2023, titled "Israeli Strike Hits House in Northern Gaza." It reported that Islamic Jihad rebels had launched rockets towards southern Israel after the Israeli military bombed an apartment belonging to Islamic Jihad commander Mohammed Abu Al Atta. Guardian News  and AP Archive  also carried a similar video at that time with the same information.
Guardian News  and AP Archive  also carried a similar video at that time with the same information.
It is evident that the viral video showing an attack on Gaza by the Israeli military is not current but around four months old.
Similarly, a reverse search of keyframes from the second video led to a video uploaded on the video streaming website Daily Motion . The video was uploaded there two years ago.
Al Jazeera English , ABC News , and Middle East Eye  also carried the viral video uploaded on May 12, 2021, as an Israeli bombing in Gaza. Video shows the moment an Israeli airstrike hit and leveled the 14-story Al-Shorouk Tower in Gaza amid an escalating conflict between Israel and Hamas. https://t.co/Zwdwp29nE2 pic.twitter.com/O3xPEoCR20 — ABC News (@ABC) May 13, 2021
Video shows the moment an Israeli airstrike hit and leveled the 14-story Al-Shorouk Tower in Gaza amid an escalating conflict between Israel and Hamas. https://t.co/Zwdwp29nE2 pic.twitter.com/O3xPEoCR20 — ABC News (@ABC) May 13, 2021
According to several international media reports the Al-Shorouk Tower , a major media hub in one of Gaza's busiest neighbourhoods, collapsed after being hit by missiles during airstrikes carried out by Israel Defence Force (IDF) in May 2021.
In conclusion, the viral video shows an Israeli airstrike in Gaza that is old and not related to the ongoing war. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Oct 8, 2023 20:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of woman pelting stones goes viral amid Israel-Palestine war
content:
The video was shot during a clash between Israeli forces and Palestinians in May 2021.
Hundreds of Israelis and Palestinians have reportedly died in an escalating conflict between Israel and the militant organisation Hamas that launched an attack on Israel through land, sea, and air. As photos and videos of violence in the region flooded social media, one particular clip was widely shared.Â
It showed a burqa-clad woman pelting stones in the midst of an unrest. Those sharing the video alleged that she is a Palestinian woman resisting Israeli forces with stones amid the ongoing conflict. The video is being shared with hashtags like "AlAqsaflood", the name given to the operation that Hamas launched in Israel . Brave Palestinian women resisted Israeli forces with stones I stand with Palestine 🇵🇸 #Israel | #Hamas | #Ghaza | #savas #طوفان_الأقصى | #حماس | #FreePalestine #Mossad "From Pakistan" #AlAqsaFlood Egypt Qatar #IronDome #IronSwords #طوفان_القدس #فلسطین #حماس #PalestineUnderAttack pic.twitter.com/CmRenwheCR — Iqra Butt (@Iqra58287731) October 8, 2023
Brave Palestinian women resisted Israeli forces with stones I stand with Palestine 🇵🇸 #Israel | #Hamas | #Ghaza | #savas #طوفان_الأقصى | #حماس | #FreePalestine #Mossad "From Pakistan" #AlAqsaFlood Egypt Qatar #IronDome #IronSwords #طوفان_القدس #فلسطین #حماس #PalestineUnderAttack pic.twitter.com/CmRenwheCR — Iqra Butt (@Iqra58287731) October 8, 2023
The video, viral on both Facebook  and Twitter , was shared with captions like, "Brave Palestinian women resisted Israeli forces with stones. I stand with Palestine". The archive of one such post can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the video was shot during a clash between Israeli forces and Palestinians in May 2021. It's not from the ongoing conflict.Â
With the help of the InVid reverse search, we found that the viral video was uploaded by an Instagram user  on January 8, 2022. While the Instagram post did not contain information about the whereabouts of the video, it made it clear that the incident predated the ongoing conflict by more than a year at least.Â
Using keywords in Arabic, we found the video in a YouTube report by the Arabic media outlet "Alghad TV", uploaded on May 18, 2021. In the YouTube report, the viral video appears around the 25-second mark. According to the video's title, the Palestinian woman threw stones at Israeli forces in Nablus during a clash. The longer, uncropped version of the video shows the woman with several other people pelting stones. Palestinian flags can also be seen in the backdrop. An Associated Press report from the time  said that clashes took place between Palestinians and Israeli forces in Nablus on May 18, 2021, during which, protestors pelted stones and burned tires. Thus, it's clear that the viral video, while showing a Palestinian woman hurling stones at Israeli forces, is not from the ongoing conflict but predates it by more than two years. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 9, 2023 16:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Azerbaijan DID NOT display Israeli flag on tower amid conflict with Palestine
content:
This image is from 2015 when the Israeli flag was displayed on the Flame Towers alongside other countries' flags during the Baku Games in Azerbaijan.
The ongoing conflict between Israel and the Palestinian militant group Hamas has already resulted in over a thousand deaths , with casualties on both sides. Amid this turmoil, an image of the illuminated Flame Towers of Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, a Muslim-majority nation, was widely shared on social media.
This image showed three buildings of the Flame Towers lit up in the colours of the Israeli flag. Those who shared the photo claimed that Azerbaijan was doing this to show support to Israel. "The Azerbaijan government building projected Israeli flags in support of Israel. That is shocking from one of the middle-east countries," wrote a Facebook user while sharing it.Â
Another such post read, "The Israeli flag was projected onto skyscrapers in Baku, Capital of Azerbaijan. Azerbaijan thus declares support for its old ally, Israel." The archived version of such a post can be seen here. The Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 government building projected Israeli flags in support of Israel. That is shocking from one of the middle east countries. #Israel #Hamas #Palestine #Mossad #Jerusalem #IsraelUnderAttack #PalestineUnderAttack #TelAviv #Gaza #Iran #IStandWithIsrael … pic.twitter.com/n5OdMzb82X — GlobalIntellectHub (@hub_intellect) October 7, 2023

India Today found that the image is more than eight years old and unrelated to the recent Israel-Palestine conflict.Â

The tweet's text suggested the Israeli flag was displayed on the towers during the Baku Games in 2015, also known as the European Games. Israeli Flag displayed on Flame Towers in #Baku honoring part. of Team Israel at @BakuGames2015 in #Azerbaijan pic.twitter.com/24g8myymBG — Azerbaijan in L.A. title: Fact Check: This footballer waving the Palestinian flag is NOT Cristiano Ronaldo
content:
The video doesn't show Cristiano Ronaldo but Moroccan footballer Jawad El Yamiq. This happened after Morocco defeated Canada in the FIFA World Cup 2022.
Did Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo show his support for Palestine by waving its flag on the field amid the nation's ongoing conflict with Israel? Many alleged so while sharing a video of a football player in a white jersey waving the Palestinian flag.
One such viral tweet read: "Star footballer Christiano Ronaldo is supporting Palestine by raising their flag after victory". This video was shared by many on Twitter.  The archived version of one such viral post can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the man raising the Palestinian flag in the video is Moroccan footballer Jawad El Yamiq, and this video shows him waving the flag after Morocco defeated Canada in the FIFA World Cup 2022.
Using relevant keywords, we found that the media organisation Middle East Eye shared the viral video on YouTube  on December 2, 2022, saying that Moroccan player Jawad El Yamiq celebrated his team's victory over Canada with a Palestinian flag during the World Cup. WATCH: Moroccan player Jawad El Yamiq celebrates his team's win over Canada and advancing to the knockout stages of the World Cup with a Palestinian flag. pic.twitter.com/iZt2NtJo2m — Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) December 1, 2022 Qatar-based Doha News also shared the video on Facebook  with the same information. Reportedly, the incident took place in Doha's Al Thumama Football Stadium. Pictures of Jawad El Yamiq raising the Palestinian flag can also be seen on the stock image website Getty Images .
WATCH: Moroccan player Jawad El Yamiq celebrates his team's win over Canada and advancing to the knockout stages of the World Cup with a Palestinian flag. pic.twitter.com/iZt2NtJo2m — Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) December 1, 2022
Qatar-based Doha News also shared the video on Facebook  with the same information. Reportedly, the incident took place in Doha's Al Thumama Football Stadium.
Pictures of Jawad El Yamiq raising the Palestinian flag can also be seen on the stock image website Getty Images .
In fact, according to news reports, Moroccan footballers also waved a Palestinian flag again, while celebrating their historic World Cup win over Spain on December 6, 2022. Thus it's clear that the viral video does not show Ronaldo.
It is noteworthy that the North African country has on several occasions shown support for Palestine. According to an October 6 Morocco World News report, the chief of Moroccan diplomacy stated: "Morocco's position, as confirmed by King Mohammed VI, remains unchanged. The Palestinian issue is a fundamental and essential matter in Moroccan foreign policy."
This is also not the first time that Ronaldo's alleged support for Palestine has gone viral. In 2019, a digitally-edited image of Ronaldo went viral with the claim that he expressed solidarity with the people of Gaza by bandaging an eye. At the time, India Today fact-checked this claim. Again in 2022, it was falsely claimed that Ronaldo sold his "Golden Boot" award and donated the money to the children of Palestine. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 9, 2023 21:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Israeli soldiers being held by Hamas? No, this is from Turkey
content:
This video dates back to 2016 and shows Turkish military officials accused of attempting a coup.
A video allegedly showing Israeli soldiers being held hostage by Hamas has been widely shared on various social media sites. In the video, a bunch of bound men with visible injuries could be seen being interrogated on camera.Â
According to the Israeli military , a significant number of civilians and soldiers are being held hostage by the Palestinian militant group in the Gaza Strip.
A Twitter user shared the video and wrote, "People are asking me about captured Israeli soldiers, so here is the video which Hamas releases footage of captured Israeli army officers." The archived version of this post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video dates back to 2016 and shows Turkish military officials accused of organising a coup.Â
The first thing we noticed was that the video's subtitles suggested that the captured men were being questioned about a military coup. "Are you happy (now that you've failed the coup)?" read the closed captions in the video. An AI speech-to-text tool also revealed that the language spoken in the video was Turkish.
We then reverse-searched the keyframes of the viral video. This led us to a DailyMail report from July 18 , 2016. According to the report containing the video, it showed military officials accused of masterminding the failed coup in Turkey being paraded on camera with their hands bound. The footage was allegedly filmed at a police station in Ankara.Â
This incident was widely covered by Turkish news websites at that time . Around 6,000 people, including judges and military officials were arrested in connection with the attempted coup. Turkey's 2016 failed coup attemptÂ
On July 15, 2016, a section of Turkish military officials launched a coordinated military operation in several cities to topple the government headed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip ErdoÄŸan. Soldiers and tanks took to the streets and fighter jets dropped bombs on the Turkish Parliament.
However, as the news about the coup attempt spread via social media, thousands of ordinary citizens gathered on the streets to oppose it. With the help of loyalist soldiers and police forces, The coup attempt was thwarted.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video has no link to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 10, 2023 17:43 IST

title: Fact Check: This video does not show fake Hamas killings being staged by Israel
content:
The video shows behind-the-scenes moments from a short film titled "Empty Place."
As the conflict continues to escalate, both the Israeli defence forces and the militant group Hamas, have been accused of killing civilians — including children. A video now making the rounds purports to show how Israelis are manufacturing fake videos of Hamas killing children.Â
The video appears to show the filming of an injured child lying on the ground using professional camera equipment. Some men in the video could be seen directing the child to alter his posture. Sharing the video on Twitter, a person wrote, "Israeli media exposed. See how Israelis are making fake videos saying that Hamas killed children." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .Â

title: Fact Check: Putin didn't announce Russian support to Palestine
content:
This video was subtitled incorrectly. In the original video from 2022, Putin only spoke about the Russia-Ukraine war and not the Israel-Palestine issue.
Amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict, a video of Russian President Vladamir Putin  began making the rounds on social media. In the video, Putin can be seen speaking in Russian . The video's subtitles quote Putin saying : "America wants to destroy Israel. As we destroy Ukraine in past. I am warning America. Russia will help Palestine and America can do nothing."
Many shared the video on Twitter as " Breaking News ", sharing it with hashtags related to the Israel-Palestine war. The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video was subtitled incorrectly to mislead people. In the original video from 2022, Putin was speaking about the Russia-Ukraine war and not the Israel-Palestine issue. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an extended version of the clip shared on VKontakte , a Russian social networking service, back in 2022. The caption of the post stated that the video  was from a meeting between the Russian President and the country's Human Rights Council.Â
The post further listed select statements made by Putin during the meeting. These included Russia's capture of new territories, Western human rights organisations' treatment of Russia, and the threat of nuclear war among other statements — all broadly about the Russia-Ukraine war.
Further searches led us to the original version of this video, shared on the YouTube channel of USA Today . The subtitles here in English indicated that Putin was talking about the growing threat of nuclear escalation in the context of the Russia-Ukraine war, nowhere mentioning the Israel-Palestine issue. Per the description, Putin stated that Russia's nuclear arsenal was a "means of protection" which would be used as retaliation for an oncoming strike. The video of the meeting was also shared on the website of the Kremlin . According to it, this was from Putin's annual meeting with the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights on December 7, 2022. We also found several news reports  about this meeting from the time. According to them , Putin mostly spoke about Ukraine . The same was also corroborated by the transcripts of the meeting present on the Kremlin's website . It's noteworthy that Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov condemned violence against both Israelis and Palestinians on October 9. He, however, criticised the United States  for supporting Israel, claiming that it was a "destructive approach" which ignored the need for an independent Palestinian state. However, it is more than clear that the viral video of Putin was wrongly subtitled to mislead people. - Ends (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 10, 2023 18:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Iranian lawmakers didn't chant 'Death to America' amid Israel-Hamas war
content:
The video of Iranian parliamentarians chanting "Death to America" is from 2020. This happened after the killing of Iranian General Qasem Soleimani.
Following the Hamas attack on Israel, a video purportedly showing Iranian lawmakers chanting anti-America slogans in Parliament was widely shared. Social media users sharing the video containing the CNN logo claimed that legislators were chanting "Death to America". One Twitter user, sharing the video, wrote , "Happening now - Iran yelling 'Death to America!' I guess $6 BILLION WASN'T ENOUGH!"
India Today Fact Check found that the video of Iranian parliamentarians chanting "Death to America" dates back to 2020, following the killing of Iranian Major General Qasem Soleimani. Our Probe
Upon a keyword search, we found the viral video on CNN's YouTube channel , shared on January 5, 2020. The video was titled: "Lawmakers chant 'death to America' in Iranian parliament."
The video description stated that Hossein Dehghan, the military adviser to Iran Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei, said his country's response to the killing by the United States of one its most influential commanders will certainly be a military response "against military sites."Â
Additionally, we found a similar video shot from another angle on the YouTube channel of USA Today , also shared on January 5, 2020. The arrangement of legislators in this video mirrors that seen in the viral video and the one shared by CNN.
In January 2020, General Qasem Soleimani, Iran's most powerful military commander, was killed in a US airstrike , in Iraq. Soleimani, heading Iran's elite Quds Force, played a pivotal role in Iranian military operations in the Middle East. The strike ordered by former US President Donald Trump resulted in the death of Soleimani and other Iran-backed military figures at Baghdad airport.
It's worth noting that Iran has categorically rejected allegations of involvement in the Hamas assault on Israel. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nasser Kanani dismissed the claims as unfounded and politically motivated, asserting Iran's commitment to non-intervention in the decisions of other countries, including Palestine.
Thus, it's clear that the viral video is not recent and not related to the Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 10, 2023 23:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video from Syria FALSELY shared as Israel bombing Hamas
content:
The viral video has been on the internet since March 2019 and is likely from Syria.
Amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and the Palestinian militant group Hamas, a video of a group of armed individuals laughing on a moving car before getting bombed was widely shared. Sharing the video, a Twitter user wrote, "Hamas terrorists laughing on the way to attack Israel. Suddenly an Israeli bomb dropped and they met with 72 hours."
Several other tweets making similar claims can be seen here , here , and here. Even a Spanish news website called "Telediaro" ( published the video with the same claim. Its archive can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video has been on the internet since March 2019 and is likely from Syria. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led to the official Facebook page and the YouTube channel of the Syrian news outlet Orient, where we found the video uploaded on March 4, 2019.
Orient reported that a convoy of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's militia was passing through the desert near Deir Ez-Zor, Syria. While a soldier was capturing photographs of the convoy, an explosive device detonated in one of the convoy's vehicles. Other news outlets from Syria  and Saudi Arabia also published similar information their reports at that time.
In October 2019, the video also circulated widely, purporting to show Turkey's operation Peace Spring in Northern Syria. At that time, a Turkish website, "Gazeteduvar" debunked it. False claims surrounding the video were again debunked in 2020 during the escalation of tension between the United States and Iran.
While we couldn't independently confirm the location or the exact date of the video, it is safe to conclude that it predates the current Israel-Hamas conflict by at least four years. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Oct 11, 2023 00:05 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Hamas militant cutting, eating human heart
content:
This gruesome video shows a member of a Mexican drug cartel killing a person belonging to a rival gang.
An extremely gruesome video of a person slicing open the chest of another man, extracting an organ from inside, and eating it has been widely shared on social media in the context of the Israel-Hamas conflict. A Twitter user  shared the video and wrote, "Hamas Terrorist can be seen taking butchering an Israeli citizen, calving out his heart and then eating it. The victim was alive through his ordeal! Wake up! These are Monsters! This footage is haunting me but it's the reality of what Israel is dealing with!"Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from 2020 and shows a member of a Mexican drug cartel killing a rival gang member.Â
We noticed that several people responded to the viral post saying that this video was old and from Mexico. A subsequent keyword search in Spanish led us to an August 24, 2020, report by the Mexican newspaper "El Sol de La Laguna". Per the report, the video showed an alleged Jalisco New Generation Cartel member extracting and eating the heart of a drug trafficker who belonged to the Tepalcatepec Cartel. Reportedly, this incident occurred in a rural area of the state of Michoacan in Mexico.Â
Multiple Spanish-language news outlets reported  this incident  in August 2020 .Â
Mexican drug cartels  are leading suppliers of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, and other illicit narcotics to the United States. The Jalisco New Generation Cartel is among Mexico's fastest-growing cartels, with operations in more than two-thirds of the country.
Thus, it's more than clear that the viral video has no links to either Israel or Hamas. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 11, 2023 15:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Palestinian kids confronting Israeli soldiers viral as recent
content:
While the children are indeed Palestinian and the soldiers Israeli, this video dates back to 2012 and is unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.
Amid the Israel-Hamas conflict, a video of children angrily shouting at a group of soldiers has been shared by many on social media. One such post read, "Heartbreaking video surface online how Palestine kids are challenging Israel army to stop killing their people. Can Hamas soldiers listen to Israelite children like this? We want peace."
India Today found that while the children are indeed from Palestine and the soldiers from Israel, this video dates back to 2012 and is unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led to a news report in The Guardian, dated January 2, 2018 , containing the same video. In the report, one of the girls was identified as Ahed Tamimi , now a Palestinian activist. Per the news, in 2012 Israeli soldiers had arrested Ahed's older brother. This prompted her to raise her hand while yelling at the troops in protest.
Sky News , The Times Of Israel , the BBC  all published stories on Ahed Tamimi, mentioning the 2012's incident. Â
We also found photos from this 2012 incident on the stock photo website Getty Images. In these photos, Ahed Tamimi and other children can be seen more clearly, angrily shouting at Israeli soldiers in the West Bank village of Nabi Saleh, near Ramallah. Incidentally, back in February 2022, right after the Russian invasion of Ukraine began, this same video was widely shared. At the time, people sharing it alleged that it showed Ukrainian children confronting Russian soldiers. At the time, AajTak and other fact-checking websites  debunked it. Thus, it is safe to conclude that this video is unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Oct 11, 2023 21:18 IST

title: Fact Check: This video doesn't show Hamas militants burning kidnapped Israeli woman
content:
This video is from a 2015 incident in Guatemala, a Central American country. It has nothing to do with Noa Argamani or the Israel-Hamas conflict.
(Content warning: graphic violence)
Videos of Noa Argamani, a 25-year-old woman, being kidnapped  by what appeared to be Hamas militants were widely shared online in the aftermath of the group's surprise assault on Israel. Argamani, an attendee at a music festival near Gaza, was seen being driven away on a motorcycle by a group of men.Â
Now, a video surfaced on social media that purports to show the same woman being first assaulted and then burnt alive by a mob. Several posts  made the same claim while sharing either the video or screengrabs from it.Â
India Today Fact Check's investigation, however, found that this video is from a 2015 incident in Guatemala, a Central American country. It has nothing to do with Noa Argamani.
We reverse-searched the viral video's keyframes on Google and found media reports from 2015 featuring similar videos of the same girl. According to a CNN report from May 2015 , the video showed a 16-year-old girl being beaten and burned to death in the Guatemalan village of Rio Bravo.Â
Reportedly, the girl was killed for her alleged involvement in the killing of a taxi driver. This incident received extensive coverage in international media in May 2015.Â
According to the Daily Mail , the unnamed girl and two other men allegedly shot a 68-year-old taxi driver, robbed him, and fled. The girl took a wrong turn, was surrounded by a vigilante mob, and suffered the horrific fate captured in the video.Â
The video was widely circulated in Guatemala at that time and provoked an outcry on social media. According to the Guatemalan newspaper Prensa Libre , the taxi driver was killed for refusing to pay extortion money. The report also said that residents of Río Bravo received intimidating messages for having lynched the girl, who was allegedly the daughter of an incarcerated gangster.
A longer video of the incident was published by Al Jazeera on May 29 , 2015, on its YouTube Channel.Â
While many news outlets have reported unverified footage of a woman who looks similar to Noa Argamani seen drinking water in an alleged Hamas safehouse, at the time of writing this report, no concrete evidence of what happened to her after her kidnapping has been documented.Â
It is, however, clear that the video in question is over eight years old and has no connection to the Israel-Hamas war. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 11, 2023 22:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Woman posing next to a corpse is not an Israeli soldier
content:
This is an old photo from Iraq's Abu Ghraib prison. The woman in the photo is US soldier Sabrina Harman who was sentenced to six months in jail for abusing Iraqi prisoners.
Amid the Israel-Palestine conflict, a photo of a woman soldier posing with a corpse was widely shared on social media.  In the image, the woman is seen smiling and giving a thumbs-up pose next to the corpse.
Allegedly, the woman is an Israeli soldier and the corpse is that of a Hamas militant.
India Today's investigation found that the photo is nearly two decades old, and the woman in it is an American soldier. Our Probe
Through a reverse image search, we found the same photo in a 2008 report in The New Yorker . According to the report, the photo featured Specialist Sabrina Harman from Virginia, US. Part of the 372nd Military Police Company, Harman arrived with the company at Abu Ghraib, America's biggest military prison in Iraq, in October 2003.
According to the report, which contains interviews of Harman and her colleagues from the time, the soldier had taken numerous photos of corpses during her time in Abu Ghraib. In fact, she had said that taking pictures of dead bodies fascinated her. It featured multiple other photos of Harman posing in a similar fashion with corpses.
Additionally, we found several photos of Harman posing with detainees on the website of the International Center of Photography . In one such photo, she can be seen posing behind a pyramid of naked Iraqi prisoners, giving a thumbs-up in front of a corpse wrapped in plastic . Tattoos on both of Harman's hands were clearly visible in several of these images, including the one going viral.Â
Reportedly, the international publication of these photographs led to widespread condemnation of US practices in Iraq. According to a Guardian report, Harman was charged for her actions, which included ordering detainees to strip and then photographing and videotaping them. In 2005, she was found guilty of abusing Iraqi prisoners at Abu Ghraib and was sentenced to six months in jail by a military jury.
In 2018, the same photo was circulated with false assertions. At the time, it was alleged that the woman in the photo was the then-newly appointed CIA chief Gina Haspel.Â
It is, hence, clear that the photo in question is almost two decades old and does not show an Israeli soldier. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 12, 2023 22:25 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT beaten for 'Bharat Mata ki Jai', old video viral with communal spin
content:
The viral video is from Rajasthan, not Delhi, and has no communal angle. The people assaulting the man included Hindus and Muslims.
A video of an elderly man being assaulted by a mob was shared by many on social media with inflammatory claims. Allegedly, this incident occurred in Delhi and the elderly man was beaten up by Muslim men for saying "Bharat mata ki jai".
A Twitter user sharing the viral video wrote , "An old man was beaten by some Indian Muslims. As seen in the video, the old man was saying Bharat Mata ki Jai and those Indian Muslims was not happy because  of this slogan and beaten him very badly."Â
India Today Fact Check, however, found that neither did this incident take place in Delhi, nor was there a communal angle to it. The men accused of assaulting the man were local shopkeepers, both Hindu and Muslim. OUR PROBE
Running a reverse search of the keyframes of the viral video, we found an extended version of the video shared by Bharatiya Janata Party leader Manjinder Singh on his Facebook page in October 2019.Â
In this video, the elderly man could be seen using derogatory language against the BJP before chanting "Bharat Mata ki Jai". Soon, local people around him could be seen confronting and subsequently assaulting him.Â
Singh, in his post, said that the incident took place in Azad Chowk Market, Bhilwara, and called on the Rajasthan police to apprehend the accused for assaulting an elderly man. Singh had also tweeted details about the case, sharing what appeared to be a copy of an FIR in response to a now-deleted tweet.
Subsequently, with a keyword search, we came across another video of the incident shot from a different angle. In the video , a shop named "Lady Bag Shopee" could be seen. Taking this clue, we searched for it on Google Maps and located it at Azad Chowk Market in Bhilwara, Rajasthan.
We found that the video was also viral in 2019, with similar allegations that a Muslim youth had attacked a Sikh man for chanting "Bharat mata ki jai".Â
Several fact-checking organisations had debunked these claims at that time as well. The Bhilwara police had confirmed to Boom Live that the victim was Hotchand, a 55-year-old man belonging to the Sindhi community. He was assaulted by five individuals.Â
Following an investigation, all the accused were apprehended. Citing the Additional Superintendent of Police in Bhilwara, the report noted that the victim was struggling with mental health issues. Hotchand ran a stall in the same locality and had a history of disputes with neighbouring shopkeepers. He was known to frequently pick fights with shopkeepers and passersby.
In its fact-check report , Vishwas News carried a copy of the FIR that listed the names of the accused as Manoj, Hemant Nathani, Bhagwan Das, Majoor Sheikh, and Irfan. According to the FIR, there was no mention of any communal angle to the incident, and the accused were identified as being both Hindus and Muslims.
In conclusion, it's clear that the viral video does not show a man getting beaten up for saying "Bharat mata ki jai". - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Oct 12, 2023 22:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video falsely shared as Israel deploying white phosphorus on Gaza
content:
This video is at least seven months old, and according to reports from March this year, it shows thermite bombs being deployed by Russian forces in Ukraine.
Israel, since it began the siege of Gaza, has been accused of using white phosphorus munitions on the civilian population. A video now making the rounds on social media alleges to show the Israeli Air Force dropping phosphorus bombs on Gaza. The video shows a sky filled with bright, white flashes raining down on the streets.
White phosphorus  can ignite rapidly spreading fires on the ground, making it extremely challenging to extinguish. The substance poses a grave danger to civilians, causing deep tissue and bone burns, and it can reignite even after initial treatment. Because of its destructive effects, the use of white phosphorus munitions in war is tightly regulated under international law — and is illegal to be used near civilians. Our Probe
A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to media reports from March 2023  that contained the same footage. According to a report by The Sun , which included screenshots from the video, the footage depicts "thermite rain", an incendiary weapon used by Russian forces over the town of Vuhledar, a mining town north of Bakhmut in eastern Ukraine.
Thermite bombs, made of metal powder mixed with metal oxide, burn at temperatures exceeding 2,400°C. It is capable of searing through steel and causing deep tissue and bone burns, with the capacity to reignite even after initial treatment. These lethal devices are particularly dangerous because they burn instead of exploding.
A longer version of this video was also uploaded to The Telegraph's YouTube channel on March 13, 2023 . According to the Daily Express , Ukrainian MP Roman Hryshchuk also shared footage of the thermite rain on social media in March.
The Palestinian government, among others, has accused  the Israel Defense Forces of using white phosphorus munitions in its strikes against Gaza. This claim was made on October 10 in a social media post  by the Palestinian Foreign Ministry, attaching a video showing the aftermath of an alleged strike using the incendiary weapon.
So, while we could not independently verify whether Israel used white phosphorus in the recent conflict, it's nonetheless clear that this specific video does not show that. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 13, 2023 11:34 IST

title: Fact Check: This ISN'T a Hamas militant crashing into a high-voltage power line
content:
Conclusion: The viral video is not related to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. It is from South Korea.
Amid the Israel-Hamas conflict, a video  of a paraglider crashing into a high-voltage electric power line and bursting into flames has been shared by many on social media.Â
Sharing the video, a Twitter user wrote, "Hamas paraglider crashes into a high-voltage electric power line and bursts into flames." The archived version of this post can be seen here . Several other tweets making similar claims can also be seen here , here , and here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is not related to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. It is from South Korea.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led to a news report published on the Chinese news outlet CQ News , dated June 19, 2023, where we found a screenshot of the viral video. Per the report, initially, the video was being shared on social media with the claim that it was from Laibin, China.Â
However, the Cyberspace Affairs Office of the Laibin Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China confirmed that no such incident occurred there. Later, another Chinese media outlet, Jimu News, confirmed that the incident took place in South Korea on June 16, 2023.
A keyword search on the internet led us to a news report  published on the Korean news outlet Daum, dated June 16, 2023. Quoting the Jeju Fire and Safety Headquarters, the report stated that a 60-year-old man was caught in a high-voltage line and died while paragliding on a beach in Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo in South Korea that day. Other Korean news outlets  also reported  the same information  at the time. We compared the viral video with the photos in the news reports and found the colour of the parachute, the number of electric poles, and the structure of the bushes to be the same in both. A comparison can be seen below. Thus, it is safe to conclude that the viral video is not related to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Oct 13, 2023 11:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Syrian boy's tears become fodder for fake news amid Israel-Hamas conflict
content:
This video shows a victim of the 2014 Syrian air strikes in the city of Aleppo.
A heart-wrenching video of a small boy yelling and weeping for his sisters, who allegedly died during Israel's siege of Gaza, is making the rounds on social media. Those sharing the clip ( https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=1046931422968859 ) claimed that Israeli soldiers killed his sisters.Â
One post containing the video read , "A little boy in Gaza grieving for his sisters sees no distinction between an Israeli soldier and a Western journalist spewing Zionist propaganda. One murders with a rifle, while the other murders with a pen." An archived version of one such post can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that this is an old video from Syria and has nothing to do with the Israel-Palestine conflict. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared on a YouTube channel back in 2014. The description of the video stated that the video showed a Syrian child crying over the death of his sisters. That the video was shared almost a decade ago proves it has nothing to do with the present Israel-Hamas conflict.
We then found a longer version of the video in question shared by a Syrian media outlet called "Shaam News Network". In this clip, the young boy could be seen sitting with another boy and a man holding a toddler. The description in Arabic, loosely translated into English, read: "Aleppo, Hanano residences, children and civilians surviving the violent bombing 4/14/2014". Further searches led us to a CNN report about Syria's civil war  — a peaceful uprising against President Bashar al-Assad that turned into a full-scale civil war in 2011. This report carried photos of Syrian residents, some protesting in different regions, and others injured during the government's crackdown, across the years from 2011 to 2021.Â
Further searches led us to a CNN report about Syria's civil war  — a peaceful uprising against President Bashar al-Assad that turned into a full-scale civil war in 2011. This report carried photos of Syrian residents, some protesting in different regions, and others injured during the government's crackdown, across the years from 2011 to 2021.Â
In this report, we found a photo of the same boy who was seen weeping in the viral video. The description stated that these scenes unfolded on February 14, 2014, after an airstrike in Aleppo, Syria. Here, the photo was credited to Reuters. We then found this photo on the website of Reuters.
According to the description, this photo was shot by photojournalist Hosam Katan on February 14, 2014, in Aleppo.
It is thus clear that a 2014 video of a Syrian boy was falsely shared as a victim of Israel's attack on Gaza. - Ends (Written by Sanjana Saxena) Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Oct 13, 2023 15:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of man catching fire while burning Israeli flag is old, and from Iran
content:
This video shows a 2021 incident in which an Iranian man's clothes caught fire while burning an Israeli flag during a Jerusalem Day protest.
Amid Israel's ongoing siege of Gaza following the surprise attack by Palestinian group Hamas, protests — both, pro-Israel and pro-Palestine — have erupted across the world. Now, a video showing a protester's clothes accidentally catching fire while burning an Israeli flag is being widely shared on social media.Â
A Twitter user posted this video and wrote, "Palestine people were burning the Israel flag, but d Israeli flag burned the Palestine people." The archived version of this post can be seen here.
India Today found that the viral video is neither recent nor from Palestine. It shows a 2021 incident in which an Iranian man's clothes caught fire while burning an Israeli flag. Our Probe
A quick reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a May 9, 2021, tweet by the news outlet Al Arabia. As per the tweet, the incident seen in the video happened in Iran during an Al-Quds Day event. Watch: A man in Iran catches on fire while burning an Israeli flag during a Quds Day protest. https://t.co/qv4NUU1OEE pic.twitter.com/9q0Cv6W7zI — Al Arabiya English (@AlArabiya_Eng) May 9, 2021
Watch: A man in Iran catches on fire while burning an Israeli flag during a Quds Day protest. https://t.co/qv4NUU1OEE pic.twitter.com/9q0Cv6W7zI — Al Arabiya English (@AlArabiya_Eng) May 9, 2021
Iranian journalist and activist Masih Alinejad, too, shared this video at the time and wrote, "Authorities in the Islamic Republic attempted to burn the Israeli flag, as they usually do.
But this time, karma got them and they ended up burning themselves. Meanwhile, unlike the regime, ordinary Iranians increasingly refuse to burn or walk on Israeli and American flags." Authorities in the Islamic Republic attempted to burn the Israeli flag, as they usually do. But this time, karma got them and they ended up burning themselves. Meanwhile unlike the regime, ordinary Iranians increasingly refuse to burn or walk on Israeli and American flags. pic.twitter.com/flOKCA44wn — Masih Alinejad 🏳️ (@AlinejadMasih) May 9, 2021 Reports in the Jerusalem Post, the Times of Israel  and Iran International  also corroborate the fact that this incident happened in Iran. The Times of Israel mentioned in its report that the man whose clothes caught fire in this incident was Iranian. Thus, it's clear that this video is neither recent nor from Palestine. What is Al-Quds Day? Al-Quds Day protest , also known as Jerusalem Day was initiated by Iran in 1979. On this day, people in Iran express opposition to Zionism and Israel's occupation of the West Bank. Quds is the Arabic name for Jerusalem.   - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Oct 13, 2023 18:02 IST

title: Fact Check: 2021 video of Lebanese scaling Israel border shared as recent
content:
While it does show Lebanese citizens at the Israel border, the viral video is two years old and unrelated to the ongoing conflict.
