title: Fact Check: Qatar isn't threatening to halt gas supply amid Israel-Hamas conflict
content:
This video is at least six years old, and the claim is false. The Emir of Qatar did not make any such statement about halting gas supplies to the world.
A video of the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim Bin Hamad Al Thani , is being circulated on social media suggesting that it shows him threatening to shut off gas supply to the world. In his speech in Arabic, the Emir is purported to have said, "If the bombing of Gaza doesn't stop, we will stop gas supply to the world."
The Arabic text in the video reads , "Emir of Qatar: The refugee crisis is the result of regional conflicts, civil wars, and displacement operations based on racism."
India Today found that the Emir of Qatar has made no such statement. The video in circulation is old and mistranslated. OUR PROBE
If the Emir of Qatar, one of the world's major natural gas exporters, had made such a statement, it would have been widely reported. However, we could not find any credible reports about Qatar threatening to halt gas supplies.
The video being circulated is a seven-second clip of Al Thani saying, "The issue of Palestine is the issue of a people uprooted from their land and displaced from their homeland."
With the help of a keyword search, we found that the video is around six years old. We found a longer version of the video uploaded to the Y ouTube channel of Al Jazeera Mubasher on May 14, 2017.Â
According to the channel, the video was from Al Thani's speech at the 17th Doha Forum held in the Qatari capital under the slogan "Development, Stability, and Refugee Issues". In this extended video, Al Thani expressed his concern about the Israel-Palestine issue. However, at no point did he mention natural gas or any other energy commodity. Doha News, a Qatar-based online news site , reported on October 12 that the viral claim is false. According to this site, the disinformation initially appeared on a Twitter account called "@qattar_affairs," which has since been suspended. We also found other Twitter users  making the claim and citing @qattar_affairs as the source. Qatar's Stance on the Palestine Issue US Secretary of State Antony Blinken visited Qatar on October 13 to meet with Al Thani and Qatar's prime minister, primarily to discuss Israel's response to Hamas, and joint US-Qatari efforts to secure the release of Americans held hostage by Hamas. There was no mention of gas supplies in the news conference  from Qatar or in news coverage of the visit. Similarly, an October 11 Financial Times article covering the recent Israel-Hamas conflict only mentioned that Qatar has held talks with Israel and Hamas about reaching a deal to release hostages. It is hence clear that an old 2017 video of the Emir of Qatar is being circulated with false claims that the country has threatened to cease gas supply to the world. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Oct 14, 2023 17:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of 'Mossad' graffiti falsely linked to Hamas-Israel war
content:
India Today found that the viral video is at least four years old and unrelated to the recent conflict.
Following a call by former Hamas chief Khaled Meshaal for global protests on October 13 in solidarity with Palestinians, a video surfaced on social media that showed a woman graffitiing the word "Mossad", the name of the Israeli intelligence unit, leading to claims that Jewish shops in Moscow are being marked for a potential pogrom.
A Twitter user shared the video  and wrote, "In Moscow, Jewish shops are marked, in preparation for a possible pogrom tomorrow, and this, of course, reminds of other times. Hamas called to attack Jews and Jewish businesses all over the world tomorrow."
India Today found that the viral video is at least four years old and unrelated to the recent Hamas-Israeli conflict. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a four-year-old post  on the Russian social media platform VKontakte, with the caption "Israeli intelligence failure". The same video appeared in another post on the website from July 16, 2019  that suggested that an elderly lady had painted it on the walls in the neighbourhood. Uploads of the video  from the past were found across several websites .
We geolocated the video  and found that it was shot outside the B&BBurger outlet in Moscow.
Around the same time in July 2019 , the same woman on painted at least one more graffiti . We identified the place to be a wall of the State Public Historical Library of Russia in Moscow . Though the woman's intentions for the graffiti remain unclear, social media users suggested the proximity of the Jewish Agency for Israel's office and a synagogue might have influenced her actions. The fact that the location includes a public infrastructure dismisses viral claims that the woman was marking Jewish businesses for an impending attack. And regardless, this video being four years old makes it clear that it has nothing to do with the present Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 15, 2023 18:49 IST

content:

An Al Jazeera report containing the viral video stated that the violent battle in the region cut off the only route for sending supplies to the city of Aleppo. title: Fact Check: This photo of dead children is NOT from Israel-Hamas conflict
content:
This photo is from a 2013 incident in Syria. It is not related to the Israel-Palestine conflict.
A disturbing photo of dead children shrouded in white  is being circulated on social media. "CHILD GENOCIDE IN PALESTINE. 614 Palestinian children murdered by the Israeli IOF Forces," reads the photo's caption.Â
India Today found that the photo has no connection to the recent Israel-Hamas conflict. Instead, it is from a 2013 incident in Syria. According to Gaza's health ministry, however, at least 614 children have been killed in Gaza from Israeli strikes as of October 13. Our probe
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the same photo on the stock image site Alamy . According to this site, the photo was shot on August 22, 2013, on the outskirts of Damascus in Syria.
Syrian rebels reportedly claimed the children were killed on August 21, 2013, in a toxic gas attack by pro-government forces in eastern Ghouta. However, the Syrian government denied allegations of chemical weapon use. Other photos from the incident are also available on Alamy with credits to media site UPI.com .
On August 27, 2013, UPI.com  published the same photo in its report. The report detailed that United Nations weapons inspectors decided to postpone their visit to Syria due to ongoing safety concerns. According to the article, on August 26, 2013, these UN weapons inspectors were targeted by armed assailants as they attempted to access a suburb in Damascus for the purpose of investigating the alleged chemical weapon incident.
The same photo was also used by other websites including the National Geographic  and the Daily Mail  in 2013 in reports about Syria.Â
Meanwhile, according to The Guardian , Gaza's health ministry, on October 13 claimed that at least 1,900 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza from Israeli strikes, including 614 children and 370 women. A UN International Children's Emergency Fund spokesperson  on October 14 also reportedly said that as many as 700 children have been killed in the Gaza Strip since the start of the conflict.
It is hence clear that while the number of dead children mentioned in the social media post matches the reported figures, the image itself is over a decade old and unrelated to the recent conflict in Gaza. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 15, 2023 20:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of sea of Israelis protesting against Netanyahu is old
content:
The first part of this video is from a protest against judicial reforms in Israel in March. The second part, however, is from a recent protest demanding help to find the hostages taken by Hamas.
A video supposedly sourced from an ABC News report has been circulating on social media with claims that it shows thousands of Israelis protesting against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. In the first part of the video, a massive crowd can be seen at a junction.
Subsequently, another clip shows a journalist standing on a crowded road where people could be heard shouting "Bibi (Benjamin Netanyahu) is a murderer." The journalist says that the people were protesting against Netanyahu for his involvement in the war and for not providing adequate security to the people in southern Israel.
The caption of the video shared on Facebook reads, "In Tel Aviv, Israelis are chanting: Bibi (Benjamin Netanyahu) is a murderer. They are addressing the root cause of the problem, the right-wing Israeli government. When will Trudeau, Biden, Macron, and other world leaders learn."
India Today's investigation found that the video stitches together visuals from two different events. While the second part of the video indeed shows a recent protest in Tel Aviv, the first video is old and unrelated to the Israel-Hamas conflict.
We observed the logo of The Telegraph in the top right corner of the first part of the video depicting a large crowd. Using this lead, we conducted a reverse image search of the video's frames with relevant keywords and found a longer version of the video uploaded to The Telegraph's YouTube channel on March 12, 2023.
According to this report, the video showed a March 11 demonstration in Tel Aviv against the government's plan to overhaul the judiciary. Reportedly, half a million protesters participated in the demonstration. The report also mentioned that such protests had been a regular weekly event for more than two months in Israel.
A photo of a similar crowd in Tel Aviv was also published by the news website Iran International on March 11. As per the BBC, there have been significant protests in Israel throughout the year, with tens of thousands of people opposing the government's plans to change the way the judicial system operates.
Despite widespread opposition, the government, which has a strong parliamentary majority, passed a "reasonableness" bill in July that limits the Supreme Court's authority to cancel government decisions deemed "extremely unreasonable." Protesters have been demanding the scrapping of all planned reforms and the resignation of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. They have garnered support from political rivals, former top officials in the military and security services, former chief justices, legal experts, and business leaders. The ABC News report
The second part of the viral video with the ABC News logo, however, is recent. Through a keyword search, we located the original video uploaded to the ABC News YouTube channel on October 14. The video's description read, "ABC News' Matt Gutman is among dozens of protestors who are demanding Israel do more to find hostages."
According to this 10-minute-long report, an anti-government protest was organised in front of the IDF headquarters in Tel Aviv, seeking help to find the hostages taken by Hamas and demanding a prisoner exchange between Israel and Hamas. The now-viral clip can be seen close to the six-minute mark in this video.
It is, hence, clear that a video showing the protest against judicial reforms in Israel was merged with a recent news report to create the impression of a massive Israeli protest against the war with Hamas. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Oct 16, 2023 23:42 IST

title: Fact Check: News channel jumps the gun on Biden arriving in Israel, shares old video
content:
This video is old and shows Biden's maiden visit to Israel as President. Biden will travel to Israel on October 18.
US President Joe Biden will travel to Israel on October 18 amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and Hamas. Biden reportedly also plans to travel to Jordan thereafter to hold talks on the conflict with King Abdullah II, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi of Egypt and President Mahmoud Abbas of the Palestinian Authority.Â
However, on September 17, a day before his scheduled arrival, many, including a news organisation, shared a video of his arrival. Russian news network RT.com tweeted the video and wrote, "Biden arrived in Israel."
The video shows Biden being welcomed at an airport, standing on a red carpet, surrounded by dignitaries. An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the viral video is a year old, from Biden's maiden trip to Israel as US President.
Had Biden arrived there ahead of his schedule, it would have been widely reported by media outlets across the globe. In the absence of any credible reports, however, suggested that this was not the case.Â
We searched Biden's social media profiles and found a tweet from October 17 . In this tweet, he announced his planned visit to Israel the following day to express solidarity in response to Hamas' terrorist attack. Further, several media reports  confirmed Biden's scheduled visit to Israel on October 18.
We then performed a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video. We found a 50-minute video on the i24News English YouTube channel . The accompanying details indicated that it was a live-streamed video. It was titled, "President Biden lands in Israel for visit." Additional information specified that this marked his first visit to the Middle East as US President.
We found the viral video was excerpted from the extended video, around the 21-minute mark. Similarly, we found reports of his first visit to Israel as US President won the YouTube channels of several media platforms .Â
Hence, it's evident that a year-old video of Biden's first visit to Israel as president is being shared with the false claim that he has arrived in Israel a day in advance. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 18, 2023 03:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of anti-Muslim chants during Ind-Pak World Cup match is doctored
content:
This video is doctored. The audio is from a rally in Himachal Pradesh. In the original video, people were singing the AR Rahman classic "Maa Tujhe Salaam".
During the October 14 India-Pakistan World Cup match at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, Pakistani cricket player Muhammad Rizwan was taunted with "Jai Shri Ram" slogans while walking into the dressing room. This video quickly went viral on social media, leading to condemnation from politicians, including DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin and Trinamool Congress MP Saket Gokhale.
Now, a different video  is being widely shared on social media, in which "Jab mulle kate jayenge, Ram-Ram chillayenge", which translates to "When Muslims will be slaughtered, they will cry Ram-Ram", can be heard being chanted at the same stadium. Allegedly, this took place during the same match.Â
India Today found that the video in question is doctored. The anti-Muslim slogans used in the video were taken from an old rally held in Himachal Pradesh. Our Probe
Several people on social media expressed doubts about the video's authenticity, suggesting it was edited. A Twitter account "@Delhiite_"  shared the video alleging that the audio used in it was from a rally in Himachal Pradesh's Kullu. Â
With the help of a keyword search, we identified the video from which the anti-Muslim slogan was taken. This two-minute, 26-second video  shared on Twitter on June 26 showed a lengthy rally with people holding placards and saffron flags. The audio used in the viral video was extracted from the first few seconds of this clip. लोकेशन–कुल्लू, हिमाचल प्रदेश जब मुल्ले काटे जायेंगे राम राम चिल्लाएंगे हुनूद द्वारा आए दिन हिमाचल में मुसलमानों के खिलाफ रैली की जा रही है और कत्लेआम का आवाहन किया जा रहा है। इस्लामोफोबिया अपने चरम पर पहुंच गया है और हुनूद की घृणा प्रतिदिन बढ़ती जा रही है pic.twitter.com/CynG8dMeZk — The Muslim (@TheMuslim786) June 26, 2023 We also found footage of this protest in a report by the New Indian Express, uploaded to its YouTube channel on June 26 . According to the report, this demonstration was part of a series of protests organised across the state of Himachal Pradesh in response to the murder of a Dalit youth by a Muslim man.  The story behind the original video With a keyword search on YouTube, we found the original version of the stadium video in question . This 1-minute, 32-second video, uploaded on October 14 to the YouTube channel "Beyond the Boundary" featured the AR Rahman classic "Maa Tujhe Salaam | Vande Maataram" playing at the stadium, with the crowd singing along. The viral clip was extracted from two different segments of this video. According to the video's title, it captured fans singing the Rahman song after India's victory over Pakistan in the World Cup at the Narendra Modi Stadium. However, we could not independently verify the date of this video. The same clip also appeared in an 11-minute video of the match uploaded  by the  "Beyond the Boundary" channel on October 16. Comparisons between the viral video and the YouTube video can be seen below. It is, therefore, clear that the video in question is doctored and does not actually show anti-Muslim slogans being chanted during the India-Pakistan match at the Narendra Modi Stadium. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 18, 2023 15:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Not 'Jihadists' attacking cop car, this is BBC drama series shooting
content:
The video shows the filming of the BBC crime drama series 'Bloodlands' in Northern Ireland in 2020.
A video making rounds on social media  shows men attacking a police car with what appear to be Molotov cocktails. In the video, a burning man can be seen escaping the flaming police car. Those sharing the video  claimed that "Jihadists" attacked this police vehicle in the UK.
India Today Fact Check found that the video is behind-the-scenes footage from the BBC show being filmed in Northern Ireland in 2020. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led to a news report containing similar images published by Irish news outlets like Belfast Live on January 30, 2020 . The report titled, "Police car bursts into flames in Ballyclare ...but it's not what it seems," noted that the video was captured in Ballyclare, Northern Ireland in 2020, and it showed the BBC crime drama series "Bloodlands" being filmed.Â
The Irish Mirror also reported  that the video was from the shoot of the show "Bloodlands" starring actor James Nesbitt.
We compared the viral video with the photos in the news reports. The position of the burning police car is the same in both. We found the same "bomber" wearing a red jacket in both. And the wheel of a perambulator can be seen in those frames. The reverse search also led us to a video from January 2020 shared on the Facebook page "Love Bellyclare". The video titled "BBC Bloodlands drama shooting today in Ballyclare"  showed the same scene being filmed from a different angle. People can be seen watching the shoot in this clip. Its description reads, "Delighted to welcome James Nesbitt and the BBC to Ballyclare today. So excited to see behind the scenes of a top quality drama shoot." Finally, we found this very scene in the February 2021 official trailer  of the show on the BBC's YouTube channel. We can see this scene play out around the 15-second mark. The red-jacketed bomber could also be seen in the trailer. Thus, it is safe to conclude that the video does not show a real incident in the UK at all. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 18, 2023 17:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Anti-lockdown protests in Spain FALSELY shared as pro-Palestine riots
content:
This video has nothing to do with the recent Israel-Hamas conflict. This video dates back to 2020 when anti-lockdown protesters clashed with the police in Barcelona.
Protests broke out in many cities across the world  after a deadly air strike on the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital in central Gaza claimed hundreds of Palestinian lives. A video going viral  purports to show one such protest in Barcelona, Spain. It shows violent clashes between protesters and the police. Sharing the video , a Twitter user wrote, "Clashes between pro-Palestinian protesters and police in Barcelona, Spain". Other similar claims can be seen here . The archived version of such tweets can be seen here  and here . advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today found that the viral video has nothing to do with the Israel-Hamas conflict. This video dates back to 2020 when anti-lockdown protesters clashed with the police in Barcelona. Our Probe A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a tweet from November 5, 2020, containing the same clip. It read, "EU adopted refugees post Syrian unrest. France, and others warned of consequences, didn't pay heed. A grateful ISIS Pakistan Army & dreaded ISI-led Jihadis repaid the good gesture by killing innocents. Congress MLA incited mobs. Wake-up call Emmanuel Macron, Narendra Modi, Zero Tolerance?" This proved that the video predated the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict by at least three years. EU adopted refugees post Syrian unrest. France, others warned of consequences, didn't pay heed. A grateful ISIS #PakistanArmy & dreaded ISI led Jihadis repaid good gesture by killing innocents. #Congress MLA incited mobs. WAKEUP CALL @EmmanuelMacron @narendramodi Zero Tolerance? pic.twitter.com/qm8Ih7Y90b — Harinder S Sikka (@sikka_harinder) November 5, 2020 We searched on the internet to find out whether any clashes erupted around this time in Europe. In fact, Sanchez even called for an end  to what he dubbed "violent and irrational behaviour" against the government's decision to declare a six-month state of emergency in response to the pandemic. Barcelona,Spain : Clashes with police over lockdown restrictions results in officers injured . police used motorbikes to chase down rioters tonight with several arrests made as large crowds gathered in other places in the city to protest #worldnews #spain #Barcelona pic.twitter.com/5pUd2YY5us — Scarcity News (@ScarcityStudios) November 1, 2020 It's noteworthy that according to recent reports , hundreds of people marched through Barcelona to express their support for the Palestinian people affected during the ongoing conflict. To sum it up, an old video of anti-lockdown protesters clashing with the police in Barcelona was falsely shared in the context of the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 18, 2023 19:52 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT airstrike on Gaza's Al-Ahli hospital, this video is a year old
content:
This video is more than one year old and has no connection with the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.
Hundreds of people lost their lives following an air strike at the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital in Gaza on October 17. While the origin of the rocket remains to be determined — both Israeli and Palestinian authorities have pointed fingers at each other — a video allegedly showing the deadly attack  happening has surfaced online.Â
The video shows a fireball in the night sky boomeranging. Sharing it, one Twitter user wrote, "Stop with the propaganda. Israel did NOT attack any hospital. This was a heavy rocket that failed to launch and fell on the Gazans. 30 per cent of their launches are failed."
Another Twitter user  shared the video and wrote, "Failed rocket by Hamas hit a hospital." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the viral video has been on the internet since as early as August 2022.
We first noticed that many on Twitter responded to the viral video, calling it old. Upon reverse-searching its keyframes, we found that some social media accounts  had shared  it in August 2022 .
Several of these posts called the video a failed rocket launched by the militant group Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Avia.pro, a Russian military portal , on the other hand, called it a misfired anti-aircraft guided missile fired by Israel.Â
India Today could not independently verify the source of the video.Â
However, it is quite evident that the video in question has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict that began on October 7, 2023. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 18, 2023 21:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Israel UN envoy tearing human rights report is from 2021
content:
This video is from October 2021 and is unrelated to the current conflict.
A post circulating on social media purports to show that amidst the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict, the United Nations issued a 20-page notice to Israel for human rights violations. The post  also alleges that Israel's UN representative tore down this notice. The post is accompanied by a video showing a man tearing a piece of paper while standing at a podium.Â
"This report, and it should have no place in anybody concerned with human rights, security or peace. Its only place is in the dustbin of antisemitism, and that is exactly how we shall treat it," the man can be heard saying while tearing the document.Â
A tweet containing the video said, "BIG BREAKING: UN issued a 20-page notice to Israel, accusing them of human rights violations. Israeli representatives took the notice, tore it up, and threw it away, stating that terrorists have no human rights."
India Today found that this video is two years old and unrelated to the ongoing conflict between Israel and Hamas. Our Probe
With the help of a keyword search, we found multiple media reports about the incident from October 2021. According to the Palestine Post , Israeli Envoy to the UN, Erdan Gilad, tore up the UN Human Rights Council's annual report while at the UN General Assembly in October 2021. Reportedly, Gilad tore the report claiming it was biased against Israel.
As per the Jerusalem Post , while addressing the General Assembly, Gilad alleged that since the establishment of the Human Rights Council in 2006, it had issued a total of 142 condemnations against member states of the United Nations. Out of these condemnations, 95 were specifically directed at Israel, involving the passing of four resolutions against Israel.
Reportedly, Gilad also said the UN had a history of anti-Israel bias and referred to the 1975 General Assembly resolution that labelled Zionism as racism, a designation later revoked in 1991.
A one-minute 29-second video of his speech was shared by Gilad on Twitter on October 30, 2021. The now-viral clip can be seen around the one-minute mark. "Today, I addressed the @UN General Assembly and spoke out against the baseless, one-sided, and outright false accusations from the Human Rights Council's annual report," Gilad wrote while sharing the video. Today, I addressed the @UN General Assembly and spoke out against the baseless, one-sided, and outright false accusations from the Human Rights Council's annual report. 1/8 pic.twitter.com/b4YIv2jGaK — Ambassador Gilad Erdan גלעד ארדן (@giladerdan1) October 29, 2021
Today, I addressed the @UN General Assembly and spoke out against the baseless, one-sided, and outright false accusations from the Human Rights Council's annual report. 1/8 pic.twitter.com/b4YIv2jGaK — Ambassador Gilad Erdan גלעד ארדן (@giladerdan1) October 29, 2021
In the video, Gilad can be heard saying, "It was on this stage, at this very body, that the very right of the Jewish people to have a national home was itself declared to be racist. A decision that was justly overturned. A decision that Israel's ambassador at the time, Chaim Herzog, tore up before the United Nations."
He further added, "And this is exactly what should be done to this anti-Semitic, distorted, one-sided report. Just as that 1975 resolution equating Zionism with racism was itself a gross form of anti-Jewish racism, which has no place in this international body, so too, the Human Rights Council's obsessive anti-Israel bias, embodied once again by this report, should have no place in anybody concerned with human rights, security, or peace. Its only place is in the dustbin of anti-Semitism, and that is precisely how we shall treat it."
Thus, it is clear that the video in question is nearly two years old and predates the ongoing conflict. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Oct 18, 2023 23:56 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 video of rockets FALSELY shared as Hezbollah attacking Israel
content:
The video is almost six years old and has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Hamas skirmish.
Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and the Israeli military  have reportedly been exchanging artillery fire since the latest Israel-Hamas conflict began. Hezbollah also announced  the death of ten of their fighters in these clashes.Â
Now, a video making the rounds on social media purports to show Hezbollah rockets directed towards Israel being fired from a hilly region.
On X, a user shared the video and wrote, "Hezbollah (Lebanon), is going full-scale war against The State of Israel Hamas was just a puppet, Arab wanted to start war with Israel. Iran is very much keen to join the Israel-Hamas war. IT IS CLEAR NOW. IT IS A GREAT CONSPIRACY AGAINST ISRAEL."Â
The video was widely shared on Twitter  and Facebook  with similar claims. An archived version of one such post can be seen here . Â
India Today found the video is almost six years old and has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Hamas skirmish. Our Probe
With the help of the Invid tool, we reverse-searched keyframes from the video and found a Turkish news report  containing the viral video along with a compilation of other clips. The title of the report suggested that these clips showed the Turkish Armed Forces attacking Kurdish targets in Afrin, Syria.Â
Using relevant keywords, we found a January 2018 YouTube video shared by the Turkish news agency Ihlas featuring the same clip in the beginning followed by some other similar videos. The video's description stated that this was part of "Operation Olive Branch", launched by the Turkish Armed Forces on January 20, 2018, to "neutralise terrorists of Kurdish groups and Islamic state in Afrin." Turkish news outlet TRT Haber  also shared the same video on January 20, 2018, stating that Turkish forces hit targets in Afrin with multi-barrel rocket launchers. Other Turkish News channels like 24TV  also used the video in their reports alongside the same information. Russian state-controlled news outlet RT also tweeted a similar video showing multiple rockets being fired by "Turkish forces" in Afrin. Watch Turkey fire rockets on Kurdish-held targets in Afrin, Syria as Operation 'Olive Branch' gets underway READ MORE: https://t.co/9kt8ngb5Zm pic.twitter.com/n6CxGhd4xk — RT (@RT_com) January 23, 2018 An Al Jazeera report  from the time noted that Turkey launched the operation with Russia's backing. The national army of Syria was also reportedly part of this operation. Per a Reuters report , Turkey took full control of the Afrin region in March 2018. So, while we could not independently verify where the video was shot, it's more than clear that it has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 19, 2023 18:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Bahrain video misleadingly shared as attack on its Israeli embassy
content:
The video is at least a decade old and shows a different incident in Bahrain.
Israel, in the midst of its ongoing conflict with Hamas, has reportedly undertaken the evacuation of several of its embassies across the Middle East, including in Bahrain, Jordan, and Morocco. Now, a video allegedly showing a mob setting fire to the country's embassy in Bahrain's capital Manama has been widely shared. People of Bahrain tried to burn the Israeli embassy in Manama.🇵🇸 pic.twitter.com/A8H52DCsxM #طوفان_الأقصى #IsraelAttack #فلسطين_الان #PalestinianGenocide #PalestineGenocide 🇵🇰 #PAKvAUS — Babar Khan Niazi 🇵🇰 (@Akhanmevric) October 20, 2023
People of Bahrain tried to burn the Israeli embassy in Manama.🇵🇸 pic.twitter.com/A8H52DCsxM #طوفان_الأقصى #IsraelAttack #فلسطين_الان #PalestinianGenocide #PalestineGenocide 🇵🇰 #PAKvAUS — Babar Khan Niazi 🇵🇰 (@Akhanmevric) October 20, 2023
In the video, a mob could be seen carrying Molotov cocktails, running toward a building, and subsequently setting it on fire. One X user, while sharing the viral video , wrote, "People of Bahrain tried to burn the Israeli embassy in Manama." An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video is neither recent nor does it show an attack on the Israeli embassy in Bahrain. Our Probe
Had the Israeli embassy been set on fire in Bahrain, it would undoubtedly have made headlines in news reports. In the absence of any credible reports suggesting that, however, we reverse-searched the video's keyframes. This led us to a Facebook post from November 2012 . This post contained a screenshot of a similar building on fire, with a caption indicating it is from an incident of besieging and burning a police station on November 5, 2023.Â
Additionally, we found a longer video on YouTube  shared by a channel called The Revolution Media Centre in Bahrain in December 2012. This video contained the viral clip, making it clear that it had nothing to do with the ongoing conflict between Israel and Hamas.
According to the video's caption, it showed demonstrators attacking a police station on Sitra Island, south of the capital, Manama. It further suggested that the attack is believed to have taken place on November 3, 2012.
Bahrain witnessed unrest in 2011 , led by Shiite protesters, against the Sunni Al Khalifa family's rule, which has governed the island for about 250 years. A report by Al Mayadeen noted that dozens of individual s had attacked a police station in Sitra, Bahrain, using Molotov cocktails. Many of those responsible for the attack on the police station were arrested and subsequently tried by law enforcement agencies.
Thus, in conclusion, it's clear that this video does not show an attack on the Israeli embassy in Bahrain. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Oct 21, 2023 09:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Jewish protest in NYC shared as recent rally in support of Gaza
content:
The video is from March 2014 and unrelated to current events.
On October 19, hundreds of Jewish protesters were arrested for assembling on Capitol Hill, demanding the Biden administration's intervention in the siege of Gaza.
A video showing a large gathering of traditionally dressed Jews has now gone viral on social media. Those who shared it claim that it showed Orthodox Jews protesting Israel's Gaza offensive.Â
One X user shared the viral video , and wrote, "NEW YORK: thousands of Orthodox Jews came out against #Israel, declaring their support for #Palestine and asserting that #Zionism doesn't represent Jews." An archived version of this post can be seen here .
However, India Today found that the viral video does not show a recent Jewish protest in New York supporting Palestinians. It is an old video from March 2014, and the protest had no connection with the Palestinian cause.
Conducting a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video, we found a New York Times report from March 9, 2014, which featured a photograph of a large gathering of traditionally dressed Jews, similar to those seen in the viral video.
Various elements in the video, including a large vertical banner with "NYC" written on it, and the number and arrangement of police officers in front of the crowd, matched those in the picture from the report. According to the report, thousands of ultra-Orthodox Jews assembled in Lower Manhattan on March 9, 2014, to protest Israel's proposal to expand its military draft to include strictly religious citizens. Opponents of the legislation believed that compelling religious men to serve in the military would disrupt their religious education. Further, we also found a gallery of pictures from the 2014 protest on a Jewish community website . We found several pictures matching the keyframes from the viral video. A comparison between one of these pictures and the viral video can be seen below: In conclusion, an old video from an Orthodox Jewish protest is being falsely associated with the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Oct 22, 2023 22:41 IST

title: Fact Check: Artificial support! Pic of soccer fans with Palestine flag is AI-made
content:
This photo was made using Bing Image Creator. It does not show a real incident.
As the Israel-Palestine conflict rages on, a photo seemingly showing football fans holding a giant flag of Palestine during a match  has been making the rounds on social media. Those sharing the picture, claimed that these were Atletico Madrid fans, who showed their support to Palestine during a football match.Â
One person shared the photo  writing, "Atletico Madrid fans support Palestine." An archived version of one such post can be found here .
India Today Fact Check found that this photo was created using Artificial Intelligence and does not show a real incident. Our Probe
Upon looking closely at the viral photo, we noticed some distortion — a few fans seemed to be missing their hands. This suggested that the image might have been created digitally, using generative AI.Â
Further searches led us to an October 18 post on X containing the viral photo . It was shared by an account called "Atletico Universe". We went through the account's posts and found several photos shared by it that appeared to be AI-generated photos .
We then reached out to the person behind this account, who confirmed it to India Today over email that the viral photo was AI-generated. "I made this photo using the Bing Image Creator. It was meant to convey our support to the Palestine cause," they said.
We also searched for media reports about such incidents happening recently. Per a report by Al Jazeera , a Celtic Football Club fan group called "The Green Brigade" unfurled banners that read "Rree Palestine" and "Victory to the resistance"in a match on October 7 . The group also reportedly released a statement urging supporters to raise Palestine's flag in a match against Atletico Madrid on October 25. However, we could not find any photo or video of fans holding a massive Palestinian flag as seen in the viral photo. As always, Celtic fans show their support for Palestine pic.twitter.com/3IcxdF5nAc — Aida Celtic (@aida_celtic) October 7, 2023
As always, Celtic fans show their support for Palestine pic.twitter.com/3IcxdF5nAc — Aida Celtic (@aida_celtic) October 7, 2023
It is hence clear that the viral photo of football fans holding a massive Palestine flag in a stadium was created using AI. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Oct 23, 2023 00:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Stuffed toys thrown at soccer match was for Turkey quake, NOT Palestine
content:
This video is from February 2023, and was a part of a fundraiser for the victims of the Turkey and Syria earthquakes.
A video of fans showering stuffed toys during a football match  has surfaced on social media, with many claiming that this was done in support of Palestine amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. The Football Ground became a battlefield for the palestinians Thank you all for taking a stand in favor of Palestine. #ArmiesToAqsa #Lebanon #Gazabombing #GazaWar #Gaza #WestBank #Gaza_Genocide #CeasefireNOW #Israel #IsraelAttack #Israel_under_attack #FreeGaza #Gazabombing pic.twitter.com/Ev92as6Hu8 — Deepak Jangid (@itsDeepakJangid) October 23, 2023

Another person captioned the video on Facebook , "Only the woke society from the 'West' is capable of producing such third-rate morons: 'Battery-powered fighter jets', 'Biodegradable Missiles', 'Vegan Grenade'. #ProperEducationMatters."Â
India Today found that the clips's audio was edited and that it was initially shared as satire. SOURCE OF THE VIDEO
We observed "SATIRE" and "@snicklink" written at the bottom right corner of the video. Taking a cue from this, we searched for the handle "@snicklink" and found accounts on multiple social media platforms. All these accounts mentioned "Comedy" in the bios.
On October 20, @snicklink shared the now-viral video on X with the hashtag "satire." The post read: "Greta Thunberg on *Vegan Wars* #satire #israel." Greta Thunberg on "Vegan Wars" 🌱 #satire #israel pic.twitter.com/P2qjkm1rih — Snicklink (@snicklink) October 20, 2023 ORIGINAL VIDEO
Greta Thunberg on "Vegan Wars" 🌱 #satire #israel pic.twitter.com/P2qjkm1rih — Snicklink (@snicklink) October 20, 2023
The top left corner of the viral video displayed the BBC logo and the title "The One Show" at the 10-second mark. A relevant keyword search led us to a longer version of the video uploaded to the YouTube channel of the BBC on November 1, 2022. "Greta Thunberg on how to tackle climate anxiety," reads the title of the video.Â
In this video, one of the hosts asked Thunberg about her early activism and how she started making a difference before gaining global recognition.
She explained, "Certainly, as a child of eight, ten, or eleven, there are limited actions one can take to effect substantial change. So I began with small steps, like turning off the lights at home to conserve energy. This led to further initiatives, including giving up air travel, adopting a vegan lifestyle, and more. I even persuaded my parents to follow suit as they began to understand my concerns. These changes also emboldened me to commence school strikes."
The viral video was largely taken from this section. THUNBERG'S VIEWS ON GAZA
On October 20, Thunberg posted a message on her X account expressing solidarity with Palestine and Gaza. She urged the world to speak out, call for an immediate ceasefire, and seek justice and freedom for Palestinians and all affected civilians.
In response, the official X account of Israel made a comment , saying, "@GretaThunberg, Hamas doesn't use sustainable materials for their rockets, which have harmed innocent Israelis. The victims of the Hamas attacks could have been your friends. Speak up."
It is hence clear that the video in question has been edited, and in the original video, Greta Thunberg discussed how to address climate anxiety. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Oct 23, 2023 23:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Israel bomb Palestinian kids gathered to drink water? No, this is from Sudan
content:
This video is from the African nation of Sudan and has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Hamas war.
A video of a bomb being dropped on a group of people causing a huge explosion is going viral on social media with the claim that Israel bombed Palestinian children, gathered to drink water in Gaza. More than 1,800 children have reportedly succumbed to Israeli bombings  in Gaza so far.
The caption with the video reads, "The Israeli army dropped a bomb on Palestinian children who gathered to drink water. The Jews of Israel are the worst nation in the world. Countries that support Israel should be ashamed of themselves for standing with terrorism".  The video has been shared on both Facebook  and X with similar claims . The archived version of one such post can be seen here . Â
India Today found that the video is from the African nation of Sudan and has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Hamas war. Our Probe
With the help of the Invid tool, we found the viral video in a report  published by the Turkish media outlet "Haber7" on October 12, 2023. As per the report, the video showed a drone attack by the Sudanese army on the paramilitary force "Rapid Support Force" that caused severe damage.Â
The X account "Sudan News" also shared the video with the same information on October 12, 2023. It said that the Sudanese army attacked RSF soldiers when they were refuelling their motorcycles. مسيرة للجيش تستهدف مجموعة من مرتزقة مليشيا الدعم السريع، تجمعوا بغرض تزويد دراجاتهم النارية بالوقود. #السودان pic.twitter.com/KXOHm4GT0t — Sudan News (@Sudan_tweet) October 12, 2023
مسيرة للجيش تستهدف مجموعة من مرتزقة مليشيا الدعم السريع، تجمعوا بغرض تزويد دراجاتهم النارية بالوقود. #السودان pic.twitter.com/KXOHm4GT0t — Sudan News (@Sudan_tweet) October 12, 2023
Al Jazeera Sudan in a Facebook post  noted that the incident took place in Sudan's capital Khartoum. Apart from this, some X users claimed  that this happened near the Khartoum airport.Â
Using the above information, we geolocated the video  and found where the bomb was dropped — a jet fuel depot located near Khartoum airport.Â
The conflict between the Sudanese Army and RSF has been going on since April 2023. At least 5,000 civilians have been killed in the clashes triggered over the integration of the RSF into the army .Â
The tension began after the 2021 coup in Sudan when a disagreement arose between the army and RSF regarding how the integration would take place and which authority should oversee that process.Â
It can thus be concluded that the video of a drone attack in Sudan was falsely shared as a bombing in Gaza. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Oct 23, 2023 23:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Old pics from Gaza falsely shared as recent attacks on US bases in Syria
content:
Both these images are old and show Israeli attacks on Gaza.
US military bases in Iraq and Syria were recently attacked  and a group of Iran-backed militias  have claimed responsibility for the attack. US authorities have reportedly blamed Iran  for actively facilitating some of these attacks. Â
Amid these developments, two images supposedly showing the recent attack on US military bases in Syria have gone viral on social media. A Twitter user shared these images with the claim, "Consequences of attacks on the Al-Omar oil field in Syria, where US troops are stationed." The archived version of this claim can be seen here .Â
India Today found that these images are neither recent nor from Syria. Our Probe
Using reverse search, we found the first image on the stock photo website Alamy . As per the information on the website, this photo was taken on November 12, 2018, and shows an Israeli airstrike on the Hamas-run television station Al-Aqsa TV in Gaza City.
We found similar visuals related to this incident in a November 13, 2018, report by Turkish media outlet Haber 7 . This proved that this photo had nothing to do with the recent attack on a US base in Syria. What about the second image?
A quick reverse search of the second image led us to a February 2020 report published by The Guardian. According to this report, this image shows an Israeli airstrike at Rafah in the southern Gaza Strip. The photo was taken by photographer Said Khatib of the AFP.Â
We also found this image on the Stock photo website Getty Images where the date of its capture was stated as February 23, 2020.
Reportedly, the Israeli military carried out air strikes against the militant group Palestinian Islamic Jihad in Gaza and Syria in response to rockets allegedly fired by them at the time.Â
To sum up, old images from the Gaza Strip are being falsely shared with the backdrop of recent attacks on a US military base in Syria.  - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 25, 2023 16:45 IST

title: Fact Check: Kim Jong Un DIDN'T speak on Israel-Palestine, video is mistranslated
content:
This video of Kim Jong Un has been mistranslated. In the original speech, that he delivered back in 2020, Kim Jong Un did not speak on Israel-Palestine at all.
If some social media users  are to be believed, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un recently spoke about the Israel-Palestine conflict , blaming American President Joe Biden for the war, and adding that World War III could begin in the coming year.Â
The video subtitles  quoted him saying: "Under the Biden administration conflicts erupt yearly. This year a war begins between Israel and Palestine. Last year a war begins between Russia and Ukraine. And two years ago billions worth of military equipment was left to the Taliban. I'm afraid that if the Biden administration does not cease to exist in the next election World War 3 may begin. Who knows what next year's war will be. I support Donald Trump for President in 2024. Good luck to Mr Trump."
One person shared the video  writing, "Guess Who Made A Statement About Israel-Hamas. First time Kim Jong Un has come out to speak on global issues, this is serious." An archived version of a similar post can be found here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video was incorrectly translated. In the original video, Kim Jong Un did not speak about the Israel-Palestine conflict at all.
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to a report  carrying a video of the North Korean leader getting emotional while speaking at a military parade in Pyongyang on October 10, 2020. In this video, Kim Jong Un could be seen in the same outfit as the one in the viral clip. Per the report, this video was from the 75th anniversary of North Korea's ruling Party, the Workers' Party of Korea. During the speech, he apologised to North Koreans for their daily hardships as typhoons, floods, and the coronavirus pandemic battered their lives.Â
We then found several media reports about this speech. According to a report in The Guardian , Kim Jong Un shed tears while speaking at the military parade in the capital, which featured the expected unveiling of a new intercontinental ballistic missile  and other military hardware. He also thanked  the troops for their efforts amid the pandemic and natural disasters. He also warned in his speech that he would "fully mobilise" his nuclear force if threatened.
We also found the transcript of the full speech  on the website of the National Committee on North Korea, as published and translated by the Korean Central News Agency. Here, we could not find any mention of the Israel-Palestine conflict in the whole speech.
Further, we found the exact same part of the speech that could be heard in the viral video, shared by the YouTube channel "The Star", along with English subtitles. According to it, Kim Jong Un thanked the people of North Korea and appreciated the devotion of the service personnel who mitigated natural disasters and the pandemic.Â
Thus, it is clear that incorrect captions were added to an old speech of Kim Jong Un. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Oct 25, 2023 18:26 IST

title: Fact Check: No US warship attacked in Red Sea, clip of Saudi ship is years old
content:
This is a 2017 video that shows a Saudi warship attacked off the coast of Yemen.
A video  of a ship at sea bursting into flames has been widely shared on social media. Allegedly, this was the American warship USS Carney . "US Navy destroyer USS Carney allegedly attacked by drones in the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen. This would be another step closer towards WWIII," read one post containing the video.
These posts come at a time when the US has accused Iran of facilitating rocket and drone attacks by Iranian-backed proxy groups on its forces in Iraq and Syria. Such attacks have reportedly seen an uptick amid the Israel-Hamas war.
India Today found that the video in question is at least over six years old. According to reports from 2017, it shows a Saudi warship attacked off the coast of Yemen by Houthi militants. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of the video's keyframes led us to a similar video uploaded to the YouTube channel of Euronews  on January 31, 2017. According to the channel, the footage showed a Saudi warship attacked off the coast of Yemen. The video was reportedly released by al-Masirah television, which is run by the rebel Houthi movement.Â
Since 2015, the Houthi movement, which is backed by Iran and follows the Shiite branch of Islam, has taken control of significant portions of northern Yemen and has been engaging in warfare against a coalition led by Saudi Arabia. The Saudi state news agency SPA reported  that the warship was attacked by three suicide boats belonging to Houthi militants. Two crew members were reportedly killed, and three others were injured in the incident. The Houthis alleged that the warship was involved in aggression against coastal cities and Yemeni fishermen. They also claimed that the explosion was caused by a guided missile they fired.
The Saudi state news agency SPA reported  that the warship was attacked by three suicide boats belonging to Houthi militants. Two crew members were reportedly killed, and three others were injured in the incident. The Houthis alleged that the warship was involved in aggression against coastal cities and Yemeni fishermen. They also claimed that the explosion was caused by a guided missile they fired.
The viral video and screenshots from it were also used in reports about the same incident by other media organisations, including Sky News , Business Insider , and the Russian state-owned news agency Sputnik  in 2017.
Meanwhile, according to a CNN report  from October 19, 2023, the USS Carney, a US Navy warship, successfully intercepted three land attack missiles and multiple drones near the Yemeni coast. The Pentagon's press secretary, Brigadier General Pat Ryder, mentioned that these missiles were launched by Iranian-backed Houthi militants. There have been recent reports of similar attacks on US troops in the Middle East.
The United States has increased its military presence  in the Middle East since the start of the Israel-Hamas conflict in early October. This includes the deployment of the USS Gerald R Ford carrier strike group to the eastern Mediterranean. The USS Carney is part of this strike group.Â
Thus, it is clear that the video in question doesn't show a US warship. It is a years-old video and depicts the attack on a Saudi warship. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Oct 25, 2023 19:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Akshay Kumar clip manipulated to FALSELY portray support for Palestine
content:
The video has been manipulated. The original video from 2020 had no mention of Palestine.
Amidst the ongoing Israeli aggression in Gaza, many Hollywood celebrities have taken to social media to express their support for either Israel or Palestine. Even Bollywood stars, including Vishal Dadlani and Sonam Kapoor , have voiced their concerns .
Now, a video  featuring Bollywood actor Akshay Kumar has gone viral on social media, allegedly showing him express support for the Palestinian cause. In the video, Kumar can be heard saying in Hindi: "What's happening to the Palestinians is not right. It is wrong."
One user shared the viral video on X and wrote, "Breaking News: Akshay Kumar, Indian Bollywood Star, expresses his outrage against Israeli brutality in Palestine... Where are Muslim countries?" The archived version of the tweet can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video was. The original video is three years old, and his comments were made in a different context. Akshay Kumar has not made such a statement.Â
By conducting a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video, we came across a Telegraph report  dated October 3, 2020. The report, titled "Akshay Kumar breaks silence on Sushant Singh Rajput death, 'admits' drug problem in Bollywood: 'Not everyone is involved'," contained an X post from Akshay Kumar's official account. The video in it featured the actor dressed similarly and standing against a similar background as compared to the viral clip. Bahot dino se mann mein kuch baat thi lekin samajh nahi aa raha tha kya kahoon, kisse kahoon. Aaj socha aap logon se share kar loon, so here goes... #DirectDilSe 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/nelm9UFLof — Akshay Kumar (@akshaykumar) October 3, 2020  In this video, Akshay Kumar addressed the controversies following Sushant Singh Rajput's death in 2020. He acknowledged the existence of drug-related issues in Bollywood and urged people to not generalise and label every celebrity as part of the problem.
Bahot dino se mann mein kuch baat thi lekin samajh nahi aa raha tha kya kahoon, kisse kahoon. Aaj socha aap logon se share kar loon, so here goes... #DirectDilSe 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/nelm9UFLof — Akshay Kumar (@akshaykumar) October 3, 2020 Â
In this video, Akshay Kumar addressed the controversies following Sushant Singh Rajput's death in 2020. He acknowledged the existence of drug-related issues in Bollywood and urged people to not generalise and label every celebrity as part of the problem.
At around two minutes 40 seconds into the video, Kumar made similar gestures and used nearly the same words as those seen and heard in the viral video. However, in the original video, he never mentioned Palestine or Israel, nor was there any reference to the ongoing conflict.
Right before Kumar said, "Yeh sahi nahi hai. Yeh toh galat hai na?" or "This is not right. Isn't this wrong?" a new phrase in the voice of the actor was digitally introduced. This phrase was "Falasteeniyon ke saath jo ho raha hai" or "What's happening to the Palestinians".Â
Multiple media reports  confirmed the context of Kumar's video, in which he addressed  the controversies surrounding Sushant Singh Rajput's death.
Thus, it's clear that the viral video's audio was manipulated to mislead people into believing that Akshay Kumar spoke in favour of Palestinians. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Oct 25, 2023 21:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Yes, Macron got a faceful of yolk. Eggs-cept it didn't happen in Egypt
content:
This video dates back to March 2017 and took place in Paris during an agricultural event.
In the midst of the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict, French President Emmanuel Macron embarked on a diplomatic mission to the Middle East. During his visit to Egypt, he held talks with King Abdullah of Jordan before proceeding to Cairo.
Meanwhile, a video of the French President getting struck by an egg has gone viral on social media, with many claiming that the incident occurred during his Egypt visit. Macron is in Egypt 🇪🇬 French president Macron gets some "love" from the public 🥚😂 #France #egg #Egypt #PALESTINE #Macron pic.twitter.com/wE9rlwuBKJ — EdMar ☀️ (@d00m777) October 25, 2023
Macron is in Egypt 🇪🇬 French president Macron gets some "love" from the public 🥚😂 #France #egg #Egypt #PALESTINE #Macron pic.twitter.com/wE9rlwuBKJ — EdMar ☀️ (@d00m777) October 25, 2023
"An egg was thrown at Macron's head during his visit to Egypt," wrote one X user ( https://twitter.com/Heroiam_ Slava/status/ 1717236217220157906  ), adding, "Macron came to discuss the problems of Palestine. He promised to provide the Palestinians with a hospital ship to help the civilian population."Â
The archived version of a similar post can be found here. 🚨 #BreakingNews : Macron receives an egg in the face during a visit to Egypt. Good thing it's not a grenade. #Israel #Egypt #hamasattack #HamasislSIS #HamasNazis pic.twitter.com/1WKf102vCZ — Stay-With-Us (@DollarAndSense_) October 25, 2023
🚨 #BreakingNews : Macron receives an egg in the face during a visit to Egypt. Good thing it's not a grenade. #Israel #Egypt #hamasattack #HamasislSIS #HamasNazis pic.twitter.com/1WKf102vCZ — Stay-With-Us (@DollarAndSense_) October 25, 2023
India Today Fact Check found that the video dates back to 2017 and is not related to his recent Egypt visit.
Given the sensational nature of an egg-throwing incident involving President Macron, it is only likely that such a thing would be reported by international outlets. However, we found no such reports related to his Egypt visit. Instead, we came across two prior instances where Macron had encountered similar situations, one in 2017  and another in 2021.
In September 2021, Macron was struck by an egg in Lyon, France. Notably, at the time, he was wearing a mask amid the Covid-19 pandemic. But in the 2017 incident, he wasn't wearing a mask and an egg hit his forehead. Photos in news reports about this incident resembled the viral clip.
According to an Express UK report  dated March 1, 2017, a protester at an agricultural event in Paris lobbed an egg at the President. The egg struck him directly on the forehead during the incident. Among other news portals, this incident was also reported by ETV Telengana in March 2017.
We also found that the original was shared on the official Facebook Page of Le Petit Journal on March 1, 2017, with a French caption that translates to, "When Emmanuel Macron goes to the agricultural show."
Hence, it is evident that a 6-year-old video from Paris has been falsely shared as a recent incident in Egypt. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Oct 26, 2023 18:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral photo of 'Ceasefires are anti-Semitic' billboard is photoshopped!
content:
The billboard originally contained the message "Be human. Stand for Israel," and the text "Ceasefires are anti-Semitic" was digitally added later.
Times Square in New York is a globally renowned outdoor advertising hub. A photo of an ad there is now going viral. The billboard displayed, alongside the flag of Israel, messages in support of the nation . They were: "Be human. Stand for Israel," and "Ceasefire is anti-Semitic."
Many on social media expressed their disapproval of the second message. One X user questioned the advertisement, and wrote , "What the hell is actually going on right now; I can't believe we're just watching this happen." An archived version of the viral tweet can be seen here.
India Today found that while a Times Square billboard did carry a message calling for support for Israel, "Ceasefire is anti-Semitic" was digitally added to the photo. Our Probe
When we performed a reverse search on the viral image , we came across several social media posts that featured photos of the pro-Israel display at Times Square, New York.
We observed that the second billboard in the picture did not include the phrase "Ceasefire is anti-Semitic." Instead, both billboards displayed the same message "Be Human. Stand for Israel."
Further searches led to a tweet containing the viral picture that indicated  that it was a paid advertisement by the Israeli-American Council, an American nonprofit organisation.
We then found the viral image on the Israeli American Council's Facebook account . Importantly, the billboard seen in the Facebook post did not include the text "Ceasefires are anti-Semitic". This post contained various photos from the pro-Israel protest that occurred on October 20, showing other advertisements featuring the faces of hostages taken by Hamas and billboards displaying the Israeli flag. Moreover, several media organisations  and Israel Embassy in the United States had also shared the original photo of the viral advertisement on Facebook. Here too, the advertisement in question only contained the message "Be Human. Stand for Israel," and not the phrase "Ceasefires are anti-Semitic". We also found photos  and videos of the billboard shot from  other angles on Twitter , showing the grand billboard  featuring the viral message: "Be Human. Stand for Israel" #TONIGHT Billboards in Times Square show faces of hostages kidnapped by Hamas during "Bring Them Home Now" rally. Thousands gathered as screens lit up with images in support of Israel. Video by @yyeeaahhhboiii2 Desk@freedomnews.tv to license pic.twitter.com/QoBoS26WAW — Oliya Scootercaster 🛴 (@ScooterCasterNY) October 20, 2023 India Today contacted the Israeli-American Council to seek further clarification about the advertisement. The report will be updated once we receive a response. In conclusion, it's evident that an advertisement in Times Square calling for support for Israel was digitally altered to include a misleading message about ceasefires being anti-Semitic. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Oct 26, 2023 21:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral clip of reporter dying on camera does not show recent casualty in Gaza
content:
The video, while related to an Israel-Hamas conflict, is from 2014.
Disturbing and graphic videos and images of people getting bombed have flooded social media following Israel's siege of Gaza in the aftermath of a Hamas attack on October 7. One such video purports to show the final moments of a journalist and a medic in Gaza following an Israeli air strike.
In the video , two men can be seen attempting to escape a conflict-ridden area. The person holding the camera can heard discussing their options for evading the shelling. Suddenly, there's a loud noise and the camera falls to the ground. The lifeless hand of the cameraman can be seen as the recording continues. The on-screen text then reads, "Both Fouad Jaber and Khaled Hamad were killed by this missile. Khaled's camera continued to record after he died."Â
"In two weeks we have witnessed heartbreak after heartbreak, and this footage adds to another horror, killed in the line of duty," read one X post sharing the video. The archived version of such posts can be seen here  and here .Â
India Today, in its investigation, found that while the video is indeed related to the Israel-Palestine conflict, it's almost a decade old.
We noticed Al Jazeera's logo in the video's lower-left corner. With the help of a keyword search, we found the same footage in an Al Jazeera documentary that was uploaded to its YouTube channel  in July 2016. According to the channel, this footage was recorded in 2014, during Israel's Operation Protective Edge, which was initiated to halt alleged rocket fire from Gaza. The two individuals seen in the video, according to Al Jazeera, were video journalist Khaled Hamad and medic Fouad Jaber. This incident reportedly took place in Shuja'iyya, one of the Gaza Strip's most densely populated neighbourhoods. Israel had asserted that Shuja'iyya harboured Hamas "terror tunnels".  At that time, Hamad, 24, was employed by a local media company in Gaza City known as Continue Production Films.
This incident reportedly took place in Shuja'iyya, one of the Gaza Strip's most densely populated neighbourhoods. Israel had asserted that Shuja'iyya harboured Hamas "terror tunnels".  At that time, Hamad, 24, was employed by a local media company in Gaza City known as Continue Production Films.
According to a report by the Electronic Intifada , Hamad resided in the Jabaliya refugee camp in northern Gaza. On the day of his tragic death, July 20, 2014, he was travelling in an ambulance to the Shuja'iyya district of Gaza City. He was making a documentary, focusing on the work of paramedics during Israel's offensive against Gaza. This account was also confirmed by the company's owner, Alaa Alool, to the Committee to Protect Journalists , an independent nonprofit organisation dedicated to promoting press freedom.Â
As detailed by Alool, Hamad was accompanying an ambulance in Shijaiyah when it was hit by a shell fired by Israeli forces. A second shell struck, leading to the unfortunate deaths of Hamad and Jaber. Hamad's camera never ceased recording, even after he was struck, and it continued to roll long after he took his final breath.
On that fateful day, more than 60 Palestinians and 13 Israeli soldiers were reportedly killed in the clashes that unfolded between Israeli and Hamas forces in Shuja'iyya.
It is hence clear that the video in question is nearly a decade old and not related to the present conflict between Israel and Hamas that began on October 7, 2023. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Oct 27, 2023 00:12 IST

title: Fact Check: US troops landing in Israel? Nope, this 2022 video is from Romania
content:
This video shows the 101st Airborne Division of the United States Army arriving in Romania in 2022.
As the Israel-Hamas conflict rages on, US military forces on October 26 conducted " self-defence strikes " on two facilities in eastern Syria allegedly used by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a response to a series of attacks against US personnel in Iraq and Syria. The US has backed Israel's offensive in Gaza and has moved warships and aircraft to the region to provide Israel with support should the need arise.Â
Amid these geopolitical developments, a video of soldiers deboarding an aircraft  was shared by many on social media. People claimed that these were American troops  arriving in Israel.
One post containing the video read: "Wow, so first, the US advised other countries not to get into this conflict yet they send their troops to Israel, what kind of hypocrisy is this?"
India Today found that the video in question shows the 101st Airborne Division of the United States Army arriving in Romania in 2022.Â
A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to a longer version of the same video uploaded to a YouTube channel "Murphy " on June 30, 2022. According to this channel, the video featured the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault) Soldiers of the US Army arriving in Mihail Kogalniceanu, Romania on June 28, 2022.Â
"The 101st units are supporting V Corps' mission to reinforce NATO's eastern flank and engage in multinational exercises with partners across the European continent to reassure their Nation's Allies and deter further Russian aggression," read the video's description.Â
A comparison between the viral video and YouTube video can be seen below. Additionally, we found photos of the 101st division's arrival in Mihail Kogalniceanu on June 28, 2022, on Alamy, the stock image site . One of these photos, showing two officers from the 101st unloading bags, also aligns with the shots in the YouTube video. We also found multiple articles about different contingents  of the 101st Airborne Division arriving in Mihail Kogalniceanu in June 2022. The US Department of Defense's website  also posted about its soldiers' arrival in Mihail Kogalniceanu on June 28, 2022. It is, hence, clear that the video in question is over a year old and does not depict the arrival of the US Army in Israel. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 27, 2023 20:34 IST

title: Fact Check: This adorable father-daughter clip is not from Palestine!
content:
This is an old video from 2020, featuring a father-daughter duo from Syria.
Of the hundreds of heart-wrenching videos from Gaza that have flooded social media, one purports to show a Palestinian father and a daughter laughing every time there's the boom of an explosion is heard. Those sharing the clip claimed that this Palestinian father taught his daughter to laugh every time she heard the sound of an Israeli airstrike.Â
One person shared the clip on Facebook  writing, "A father tells his daughter to laugh every time she hears an Israeli airstrike so that she doesn't get scared. May Allah ease their pain." The archived version of a similar post can be found here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this is an old video of a Syrian father-daughter duo from 2020. Our Probe
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to an Instagram post  containing the viral video dated February 18, 2020. The caption in Turkish, loosely translated into English, read: "A Syrian father found a way to protect his daughter from bombs not only physically but also psychologically."Â
With the help of this, we found several media reports  from February 2020 about the video in question. According to The Guardian , this video featured Abdullah Mohammad and his daughter Salwa, laughing at the sound of shelling in Syria.Â
Mohammad, who moved his family from Idlib to the Sarmada district in Syria, told his daughter that the noise of bombs was part of a game to try and insulate her from trauma. A photo of the father-daughter duo  from Syria was also featured on Getty Images. We then found an interview of Mohammad on the YouTube channel of Agence France-Presse. In it, he explained that he told his three-year-old daughter that the sound of bombs, like fireworks, was harmless and just for fun. As per reports, Mohammad was living at a friend's house near the Syrian-Turkish border in Sarmada, after his family was forced to flee their house during the Syrian civil war. According to The Independent , this video was tweeted by Mohammad's friend and journalist Mehmet Algan  on February 17, 2020. When the video went viral on social media, the Turkish government helped Mohammad's family to cross the border on February 25 . As per an Al Jazeera report , dated March 6, 2020, the family went to live with a relative in Antakya, a municipality in Turkey's southern province of Hatay, after crossing the Bab al-Hawa-Cilvegozu border. title: Fact Check: Video doesn't show Muslim students demanding Hindu woman to wear burqa
content:
The saree-clad woman seen in the video, Asha Bhaskar, has refuted the viral claim. According to her, the argument was related to a bus stop issue and there was no mention of a burqa throughout the dispute.
A video of a verbal altercation between a group of burqa-clad women and another woman in a saree has gone viral on social media, accompanied by communal claims. Those sharing the video , like the RSS mouthpiece Panchjanya , claimed that it showed a group of Muslim women demanding a Hindu lady to wear a burqa if she wanted to travel on a public transport bus. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story One such post claimed, "Shocking video from Kerala - Muslim women force Hindu woman to cover her head (Sharia compliant), wear a burqa while travelling in a bus (public transport), video goes viral." A similar claim was also made by American far-right activist Amy Mek . The archived version of such posts can be seen here , here and here . India Today Fact Check found that the claim, along with the video, is false. Asha Bhaskar, the saree-clad woman in the video, confirmed that there was no communal angle to the matter. Our Investigation
A video of a verbal altercation between a group of burqa-clad women and another woman in a saree has gone viral on social media, accompanied by communal claims. Those sharing the video , like the RSS mouthpiece Panchjanya , claimed that it showed a group of Muslim women demanding a Hindu lady to wear a burqa if she wanted to travel on a public transport bus.
One such post claimed, "Shocking video from Kerala - Muslim women force Hindu woman to cover her head (Sharia compliant), wear a burqa while travelling in a bus (public transport), video goes viral."Â
A similar claim was also made by American far-right activist Amy Mek . The archived version of such posts can be seen here , here and here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the claim, along with the video, is false. Asha Bhaskar, the saree-clad woman in the video, confirmed that there was no communal angle to the matter. Our Investigation
In the video, the women were speaking in Malayalam. At no point in the exchange audible in the clip, however, was there any mention of religion.
Upon a close examination of the video, we identified a local inverter business's mobile number written on a poster inside the bus. Using this number, we managed to contact the conductor of the bus, Manoj, who was a witness to the incident. Manoj refuted the viral claims when speaking to India Today Fact Check. He clarified, "The incident occurred inside our bus, Sri Guruvayurappan, on October 20. The bus was travelling from Mulleria-Kumbla in the Kasaragod district of Kerala when a group of students from Khansa Women's College for Advanced Studies blocked it near the Narayana Mangalam area to board it."  He further explained, "There has been a longstanding demand for a bus stop in front of their college, but it has not been sanctioned yet. On that day, students were agitated because several buses did not stop in front of their college. The saree-clad woman you see in the video spoke in favour of the bus people, leading to the altercation between her and the students. The confrontation continued for some time." advertisement With the help of local journalists, we also contacted Asha Bhaskar, the saree-clad woman in the video. Asha, who works as an office assistant at Kumbla Academy, an educational institute in Kumbla, also refuted the communal claims circulating on social media. She clarified, "The students did not make any such communal statements as claimed in the social media posts. The students were already agitated because the vehicle did not stop at the bus stop in front of their college. While entering the bus, one of them accidentally stepped on my foot, which angered me. The altercation between me and the students began at this point. I also scolded them for blocking the bus. I travel this route every day, and this fight for a bus stop near Khansa has been ongoing for a while now." We also obtained more videos of the incident in which students and bus employees can be heard arguing over the bus stop issue. Anoob Kumar, the Station Head Officer of Kumbla Police Station, also confirmed to India Today that the viral claims were false. He stated, "I have spoken to the bus owners and the Principal of Khansa College. The college has been demanding sanction for a bus stop, but the Regional Transport Office (RTO) has not approved it yet. This was the basis of the entire altercation seen in the video. We have not received any complaints indicating that the students were pressuring the woman to wear a burqa." It is therefore evident that the video in question has been shared with false communal claims on social media. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Oct 28, 2023 23:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Israeli soldier playing with Palestinian kid is NOT from ongoing war
content:

Amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and Hamas, a video of a soldier playing football with a child went viral on social media. Many claimed that this video showed an Israeli soldier playing with a Palestinian child.
An X user who shared the viral video wrote , "It's Difficult to Watch this Israeli Soldier and Palestinian Kid Play Football Knowing We're At War. How did we get to where we are today?" An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video is not recent; it is at least a year old. Our Probe
While performing a reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video, we found it on the YouTube account of Hananya Naftali, a controversial Israeli influencer and aide to former Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He uploaded the video on YouTube on October 16, 2022, with a caption indicating that it showed an Israeli soldier playing soccer with a Palestinian child in Hebron, a Palestinian city in the West Bank.
It's noteworthy that Naftali on several occasions had shared content on social media related to Israeli soldiers playing and having fun with Palestinian children. Even amid the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza, he shared a similar video on his Instagram account.
We found the viral video on Naftali's X account as well, which was reshared by several social media users earlier this year.
While we couldn't pinpoint the original source, precise timing, or location of the video, it is more than evident that the video predates the current conflict between Hamas and Israel. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Oct 30, 2023 13:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Jewish people burning Israel flag is old, unrelated to ongoing conflict

title: Fact Check: Shocking video DOESN'T show Hamas militant getting shot in the head

title: Fact Check: Video of deadly road rage incident shared as man running over spouse
