According to it, this video showed a violent road rage attack in Elizabeth, New Jersey. The suspect, identified by the police as 56-year-old Vincent Jean was charged with first-degree attempted murder and third-degree assault by auto .
Using this clue, we found several media reports about the incident  from April 2022. According to reports, a man named Vincent Jean ran over 23-year-old Morgan Scott three times on April 12, 2022. This incident followed a minor collision between the two, during which Scott decided to take pictures of the license plate of Jean's vehicle, triggering the attack.
Notably, Scott miraculously survived the brutal attack with fractures, lacerations, and broken bones all over the body. Jean, on the other hand, had reportedly  claimed that he never saw the woman, denied being involved in the accident, and asserted that his car had slipped.
Quoting Scott's family, a report by Dailymail stated that the attack was not the result of any domestic dispute, adding that the man was a complete stranger to the victim. Scott's family had also set up a GoFundMe page  for her medical costs, where a video of Scott  recovering and getting better from her injuries was shared on September 7, 2022.
Thus, it is clear that the narrative passed off with the viral video of a horrific car attack is baseless. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 1, 2023 15:41 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Syrian army executing civilians falsely linked to Israel-Hamas conflict
content:
This video shows Syrian army soldiers executing civilians in Syria in 2013.
A distressing video showing the execution of handcuffed men by individuals in military uniforms and the disposal of bodies in a pit filled with tires is being widely shared on social media. The video is claimed to show Israelis killing Palestinian prisoners of war.
One Facebook post containing the video read: "This is what the Zionist Israelis are doing to their Palestinian prisoners of war. Please make viral and let the world know." An archived version of one of the posts can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the video in question is unrelated to Israel and the Israel-Hamas conflict; instead, it shows the Syrian army executing civilians in Syria. Our Probe
Reverse-searching the keyframes of the video with relevant keywords, we found several news reports regarding the incident. A DW report dated April 26, 2022, noted that the video shows a massacre that occurred on April 16, 2013. The report detailed how the Assad regime's security forces shot ten innocent civilians in less than seven minutes. The executioners placed blindfolded civilians into a grave dug in an abandoned alley in the city and then shot them without hesitation.
In a detailed report, The Guardian stated that the incident took place in Tadaman, a suburb of the Syrian capital, Damascus. The mass execution was carried out by the Pro-Assad forces on April 16, 2013, However, it only came to light after a former soldier of the regime leaked the video to two academics from the University of Amsterdam's Holocaust and Genocide Center.
The report identified the executioner as a Major in branch 227 of the Syrian military intelligence service, named Amjad Youssuf. The researchers spent years gathering information from families and witnesses on Facebook to identify and locate the perpetrators, with the aim of bringing them to justice.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video is not related to the Israel-Hamas conflict. It shows a 2013 incident in Syria. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 3, 2023 11:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral photo of Ramayana-themed metro station in Ayodhya is AI-generated
content:

The transformation of Ayodhya into a modern city alongside the construction of the grand Ram temple, which is set to open in January 2024, has been a topic of interest. Amid this, a photo resembling a Ramayana-themed metro station is making rounds on social media. Many users sharing it claimed that it's a blueprint for an upcoming metro station in Ayodhya.
India Today Fact Check found that the circulating photo is AI-generated and not an official blueprint of Ayodhya's metro station. Our Probe
Earlier this year, several media reports surfaced regarding the Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation's plans to introduce metro services in Ayodhya, Varanasi, and Mathura. However, neither the official website of the UP Metro Rail Corporation nor their social media accounts have published a similar-looking blueprint of Ayodhya's metro station.Â
Additionally, a senior official in Ayodhya confirmed to India Today that there is currently no proposal for a metro station in the city.
Furthermore, a reverse image search of the viral photo led us to a post from the Twitter account "@mp_index". On October 27, the account shared the same picture , claiming it as an ideal vision of the Ayodhya railway station as per the redevelopment project. title: Fact Check: Md Shami DID NOT slam Harbhajan Singh's bond with Shahid Afridi
content:
This is a fabricated quote. Shami did not say anything similar to this.
India's resounding triumph over Sri Lanka showcased remarkable performances by fast bowlers, particularly Mohammad Shami's exceptional spell of five wickets for 18 runs. The excellent spell earned him the second "Man of the Match" award in the World Cup.
Shami's unique celebration by rubbing the ball on his head garnered  widespread attention and sparked a quote attributed to him, which is now viral on social media. Many social media users claimed that the bowling sensation criticised former Indian spinner Harbhajan Singh for allegedly helping another Pakistani all-rounder Shahid Afridi collect donations.
"Shami in the post-match presentation, stated, 'I dedicated my 5-wicket haul to our bowling coach Paras Mhambrey, because he supported me during a low phase and enhanced my skills. I celebrated in that manner because he had no hair on his head. This celebration has nothing to do with Harbhajan bhajji. I could never dedicate my 5-wicket haul to someone who helped collect donations for Pakistani Shahid Afridi,'" read such posts . An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the quote is fabricated. Mohammad Shami did not make any statements regarding Harbhajan and Afridi, nor did he comment while celebrating.
Given the gravity of the alleged statement by Shami, there would have been several news reports about his purported comment. However, extensive searches using relevant keywords failed to produce any credible results.
Although, news outlets such as ESPN Cricinfo  and Times Now reported about Shami's post-match presentation  where he expressed his gratitude to the almighty and stated that there was 'no rocket science' behind his remarkable performance.
Shami was quoted saying, "Just a matter of rhythm, good food, keeping your mind uncluttered, and, most importantly, the love of the people." Notably, there was no mention of his celebration or to whom he dedicated his five-wicket haul.
A report from The Times of India  noted that the reason behind Shami's unique gesture of rubbing the ball on his head, was a tribute to their bald bowling coach, Paras Mhambrey, as explained by Shubman Gill during a post-match conversation with the broadcasters.
We thoroughly reviewed the post-match presentation and conversation on Hotstar , the official digital broadcaster of the World Cup, and found no indication that either Shami or Gill made any statements resembling the viral claim about Harbhajan.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral statement was mischievously attributed to Shami. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Nov 3, 2023 20:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of 2015 Swedish incident falsely tied to Israel-Palestine conflict
content:
This video is from a 2015 incident in Sweden and has no connection to the current Israel-Palestine conflict.
Misinformation surrounding the latest Israel-Hamas conflict is rife on social media platforms. Unrelated and miscontextualized videos, as well as outright falsehoods, are overshadowing genuine reporting on the ongoing conflict.
In this atmosphere, a video  showing a man in uniform strangling a child is gaining widespread attention on social media. In this disturbing video, a man in a neon green vest is seen pinning down a boy on the ground, while the boy resists.Â
Several social media users have shared this video, claiming it as footage of an Israeli police officer strangling a Palestinian child to death during a protest at the American embassy in Jerusalem. It is further alleged that the boy was reciting the Shahada, an Islamic prayer, before his death.
A person who shared the viral video on Facebook wrote, "An Israeli police officer choked a Palestinian child to death on Saturday during a protest at the American embassy in Jerusalem. The innocent boy even recited the Shahada before his death." An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
However, India Today found that the video actually shows a Swedish security guard assaulting a 9-year-old boy at the Malmo city train station in Sweden in 2015. Our Probe
A reverse image search of the keyframes from the viral video led us to a report by France 24 , which included a screenshot from the footage. The report, dated February 2015, highlighted that two private security guards were under police investigation after violently detaining a 9-year-old boy at the train station in the Swedish city of Malmo on February 6.
The report further detailed that a private security guard employed at the station forcibly pushed the boy to the ground, straddled him, and covered the boy's face and mouth with his hands. During this distressing incident, the boy was overheard reciting the Shahada, a Muslim prayer.
The report explains that the security guard detained the boy and his 12-year-old friend after they were caught travelling without tickets. Both boys had previously run away from a care home, and after this episode, they were returned to their care facility.
According to a report by The Independent , Swedish police initiated an investigation into the case after the video of the incident went viral, and received twelve complaints about the actions of the security guards.
In addition, another report from the same period stated that the security guard was suspended while a police investigation into the incident was underway. The report also mentioned a nationwide fundraising campaign aimed at covering the hospital expenses of the boy's father, who was living in Morocco and needed surgery.
Other reports confirming the true facts and context of the viral video can be seen here and here .
It is, hence, clear that the video in question is more than eight years old and is not connected with the Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 4, 2023 17:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of US Soldiers discarding medals NOT linked to recent Israel-Hamas conflict
content:
This video is from an anti-NATO protest held in Chicago in 2012.
A video has circulated on social media , claiming to show U.S. military veterans purportedly returning their service medals in response to the Israel-Hamas conflict. The accompanying post asserts that over 40,000 US soldiers resigned due to civilian casualties in Gaza. In the video, a group of men in military uniform address a large crowd, expressing solidarity with war-affected nations, including Palestine, Iran, and Afghanistan.
The text along with the video reads , "Seeing innocent people die in Gaza, over 40,000 US soldiers have left their army positions. Most had fought in countries like Iraq, Syria, Palestine, and Libya, with many returning their medals. NATO should be ashamed." An archived version of one such post can be seen here . #Gaza में मासूमों को मरता देख कर 40,000 US FORS के जवानों ने आर्मी की नोकरी छोड़ी, इनमे से ज्यादातर वो जवान थे जिन्होने #Iraq #Syria #Palestine #Libya जैसे देशों में जंग लड़ी है और बड़े मेडल भी प्राप्त किए हैं उन्हें लौटा दिया !! #NATO के लिए शर्म की बात है pic.twitter.com/6M8MjzAugZ — Noyan_bey_ 🦅 (@noyan_beey) November 2, 2023

India Today Fact Check found that the video of veterans discarding medals is over a decade old and unrelated to the recent Israel-Hamas conflict. Furthermore, there is no credible report about 40,000 American soldiers resigning in support of Gaza.
A reverse image search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a longer version of the same clip , uploaded on May 21, 2012, to a YouTube channel called "Democracy Now!" The video's title was "No NATO, No War: US Veterans of Iraq and Afghanistan Return War Medals at NATO Summit."
According to this channel, the video shows an anti-war protest organised by US veterans of the Iraq and Afghanistan wars, alongside members of Afghans For Peace. The event took place on May 20, 2012, near a venue where leaders of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) were convening for a summit with a specific focus on Afghanistan.
Multiple other media organisations, including Reuters, reported this anti-NATO rally. According to Reuters, nearly 50 US military veterans discarded their service medals onto the street during the protest to register their symbolic protest against US-led wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.
Thousands of people reportedly marched in the city as part of this protest. However, the situation escalated later, with some protesters clashing with riot police after disregarding orders to clear the streets.
The viral claim regarding the resignation of 40,000 American soldiers in solidarity with civilians in Gaza is also misleading; there are no credible sources to validate this claim.
In conclusion, the viral post is misleading, as the video from 2012 is falsely linked to the latest Israel-Hamas conflict that began on October 7. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 5, 2023 14:42 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video from Yemen falsely shared as Hamas terrorists forcing Gazans to fight!
content:

Amid the Israel Defence Forces' continued siege of Gaza, a video making rounds on the internet purports to show Hamas terrorists forcing Gazans to fight. The video shows a group of uniformed armed men storming into a house and dragging a man out.Â

It's quite possible that these children will never see their father again. Hamas must be stopped." The archived version of such claims can be seen here and here .Â

In the viral post, an X user wrote that the video was from Yemen and not related to the Israel-Hamas conflict. Taking a clue from this, we reverse-searched keyframes from the video, which led us to an X post from October 3, 2023, by Yemeni journalist Sameer Alnamri.Â
This Arabic post translates to, "As per the information, this video is from Mukalla, Hadhramaut, Yemen. Local security forces supported by the UAE stormed the homes of citizens, accusing them of being disruptive and not responding to the authorities. title: Fact Check: Debunking two 'Palestine' clips - One is old, other is from US
content:
This video is from a pro-Palestine demonstration held in Washington on November 4. The body bags were used to pay homage to the children who have died in Gaza.
In the month since Hamas' surprise attack on Israel on October 7 and Israel's subsequent siege of Gaza, social media has witnessed a deluge of disinformation and misinformation campaigns surrounding the conflict. In this report, we will examine and debunk two videos that have been widely shared.
The first is a video  that allegedly showed Israeli soldiers assaulting a Palestinian girl. In it, a number of armed and armoured guards can be seen subduing a woman in a crowded area. Those sharing it claimed that the incident occurred in Jerusalem on November 6.
The second video shows the bodies of children wrapped in white shrouds, placed on the roadside along with their photos. The clip was shared with the claim that these were the dead bodies of Palestinians in Gaza's streets because hospitals there had reached their maximum capacities.
India Today found that both of these videos are misleading. The video of the assault in Jerusalem is more than a year old. The second video features imitation body bags used during a pro-Palestine demonstration in Washington, not actual dead bodies of Gazan children. Israeli forces attacking Palestinian girl
Through a keyword search, we found the video on Al Jazeera's YouTube channel , shared on March 1, 2022. Per this report, the footage showed an 11-year-old hearing-impaired Palestinian girl who was hit in the face by a stun grenade fired by Israeli forces. She was part of a gathering in East Jerusalem on February 28, 2022, celebrating a Muslim holiday. We also found multiple media reports confirming the incident. According to the Times of Israel, the girl, identified as Manwar Burqan, was hospitalised after being struck in the head. She later provided an interview to Eye On Palestine.
We also found multiple media reports confirming the incident. According to the Times of Israel, the girl, identified as Manwar Burqan, was hospitalised after being struck in the head. She later provided an interview to Eye On Palestine.

A post shared by Eye On Palestine (@eye.on.palestine)
Approximately 25 Palestinians sustained injuries during the clashes, as reported by the Palestinian Red Crescent. Israeli Police reported that 20 Palestinians were arrested, and four officers were wounded.
The gathering in the Old City entryway celebrated al-Israa wa al-Miraj, the anniversary of Prophet Mohammed's journey to Al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem.
It is hence clear that while the video shows a Palestinian girl being attacked in Jerusalem, it's not recent at all. Palestinian children shrouded in whiteÂ
We noticed the watermark of the TikTok account "@maryannamustafa711" in the viral clip.
On this TikTok account, we found the same video and others from a demonstration, shared with like hashtags "protest" and "Washington." Although these videos were uploaded on November 6, one caption indicated that the demonstration took place on November 4. As per media reports , a pro-Palestine demonstration took place on November 4 in Washington DC's Freedom Plaza, where demonstrators called for a ceasefire in Gaza. Further searches led to multiple images from the protest that displayed the same body bags seen in the viral video. The description of an AFP photo from the demonstration clarified that these visuals represented imitation body bags placed as part of the protest at Freedom Plaza in Washington DC on November 4. These body bags symbolically paid homage to the children who had lost their lives during the Israel-Hamas conflict. A comparison between a screenshot of the viral video and the AFP photo can be seen below. title: Fact Check: Did Maxwell touch Sachin's feet? Viral pic is photoshopped
content:
The viral picture is photoshopped. Two different images were clubbed together to make it look like Maxwell touched Sachin's feet.
On November 7, the Australian Cricket team chased a target of 292 runs against Afghanistan at Mumbai's Wankhede stadium. Aussies lost seven wickets in quick succession but Glenn Maxwell's unbeaten double-century led the team to defeat Afghanistan by three wickets in the ongoing ICC World Cup.Â
Following Maxwell's heroic double century, a picture of him  bowing down in front of former Indian cricketer and batting legend Sachin Tendulkar was widely shared on social media.
Sharing this photo , a Facebook user wrote, "When Sachin Tendulkar came to congratulate Maxwell yesterday on the ground, the great Maxwell bowed down and touched the feet of the legend, Sachin Tendulkar and asked for blessings. One of the greatest moments in the history of cricket. Salute to these great cricketers."
India Today Fact Check found that this picture was photoshopped. Two different images were clubbed together to make it look like Maxwell touched Sachin's feet.
With the help of a keyword search, we found a photo of Sachin Tendulkar clicked with the Afghanistan cricket team at Wankhede Stadium a day before their match with the Aussies in Mumbai, India. In this photo, Sachin was in the same T-shirt that he was seen wearing in the viral picture.Â
We then found the original picture featuring only Sachin and not Maxwell at Getty Images . As per information on the website, on November 6, Sachin spoke to members of the Afghanistan cricket team prior to a training session. We compared both photos and found many similarities between them.
Further, according to journalists from SportsTak, Sachin Tendulkar was not present at the Wankhede Stadium during the Afghanistan versus Australia. However, he did  congratulate Maxwell after his double-century. We could not find the source of Maxwell's bowed-down photo.
In conclusion, the viral photo of Maxwell bowing down to touch Sachin Tendulkar's feet is photoshopped. Sachin was not present at the stadium during the match. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 9, 2023 22:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Clip DOES NOT show Saudi Imam being arrested for supporting Palestine
content:
This video is from 2018 and portrays security officers escorting out a mentally disabled man who attempted to deliver the Friday sermon at a mosque in Saudi's Yanbu al-Bahr.
A video allegedly showing the arrest of an Imam by the Saudi Arabian police from the pulpit of a mosque has gone viral on social media. Those sharing it allege that the Imam was detained for urging the Saudi government to declare war against Israel.
The text accompanying one of the videos read, "BREAKING: The Saudis arrested an Imam who called for a war with Israel. Saudi Arabia and Jordan are now protecting and helping Israel more than the US itself."
India Today found that the video in question is from 2018 and has nothing to do with the Israel-Hamas conflict.Â
A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to the same clip uploaded to a Facebook Page on March 3, 2018. According to the post, an Imam was arrested for criticising the modern policies of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Saudi Arabia.
A keyword search in Arabic and Urdu languages directed us to multiple media reports from March 2018 that featured screenshots from the same video. However, these reports presented a different perspective on the incident.
According to a report in "Akhbaar24", the footage showed security personnel attempting to prevent a mentally disabled person from delivering the Friday sermon while sitting in the preacher's chair. This incident reportedly occurred at the Jabriya Mosque in Saudi's Yanbu al-Bahr in March 2018.
The official spokesman for the Ministry of Islamic Affairs in the Medina region, Majid Al-Muhammadi, also issued a clarification, affirming that the man was not an Imam but a mentally disabled person. Following a medical examination, it was confirmed that he had a mental disability. As reported by the official spokesperson of the Medina Police, the man, who was in his 70s, was subsequently returned to his family.
Therefore, it is evident that the video in question is more than five years old and does not depict an Imam being arrested for advocating in favour of Palestine. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 10, 2023 01:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Not PM Modi dancing to Garba beats, this video shows his lookalike!
content:
The person seen dancing in this video is not PM Modi but his lookalike, actor Vikas Mahante.
On Navratri in 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared the music video of a Garba song called "Maadi" that he has penned. Now, a video allegedly showing the Prime Minister dancing to Garba beats has gone viral on social media.Â
In this video, a man resembling PM Modi can be seen dancing with some women. An Instagram user shared this video with the caption, "Wah Modi ji Wah." The archived version of this post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the person seen in this video is not PM Modi but his lookalike, an actor called Vikas Mahante. Our Probe
We did not find any news reports about PM Modi dancing at a garba event. Had this actually happened, it would have been reported by every media outlet in India. Then what is the story behind this video?
Reacting to the viral video, an X user wrote that the person in the video is Vikas Mahante , PM Modi's doppelganger, while sharing a screenshot of Mahante's Instagram story.Â
On Mahante's Instagram account , we found that he had shared a video on November 7 announcing that he was invited as a chief guest at a "Diwali Mela" in London. At one point in this video, he can be seen standing on the same Garba stage with women as seen in the viral video.  His outfit was also the same as the person seen dancing in the viral video. Mahante's photos and videos on his social media accounts make it abundantly clear that he bears a striking resemblance to PM Modi. He even dresses like the PM. To get to the bottom of it, we reached out to Mahante's PR team. A member of the team, Atul Pareek, told India Today that the video shows Vikas Mahante and was recorded in London. Vikas was in London on November 4 and 5. "Whoever is sharing Vikas's photos or videos as PM Modi is doing very wrong," he added. We also found a Facebook post related to the London Diwali Mela event in which Vikas Mahante was invited as a chief guest. In this post, it was stated that PM Modi's and Salman Khan's doppelgangers would participate in the "Diwali Shopping Bazar 2023". There are many news reports about Vikas Mahante , a businessman-turned-actor from Mumbai. He has even campaigned for the Bharatiya Janata Party during elections.    Thus, it's clear that the viral video does not show the prime minister dancing. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 10, 2023 20:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Is AIIMS selling magic bullets to hypertension patients? No, it's scam
content:
Neither is AIIMS Delhi selling any such medicine nor has India Today published a report on it.
A website impersonating India Today  is falsely claiming that AIIMS Delhi is manufacturing and selling a medicine called "Cardioton" which can cure hypertension.Â
The website is being promoted through Facebook posts  that feature a photo of India Today anchor Rajdeep Sardesai  and the channel's logo. Alongside the photo, it says, "Why are pharmacies silent about this? Hypertension will disappear once and for all, our best scientists have found and made a discovery!"
The archived version of one such post and an India Today impersonating website, "inecuruhi.shop", can be seen here  and here .Â
India Today contacted AIIMS media cell head Dr Rima Dada and asked her about the alleged hypertension drug Cardioton being manufactured and sold online by the institute. She rubbished this claim, calling it fake news. Stolen identityÂ
The article on the impersonating website "inecuruhi.shop" claims to be based on the interview of a 93-year-old Indian chemist called Ramchandra Bhargava Sapre. However, a quick reverse search of the alleged image of "Ramchandra Bhargava Sapre" led us to an NBT report  that said the photo was of Jagdish Gandhi, the founder of City Montessori School in Lucknow .  Ramchandra Bhargava Sapre on the other hand , was the first national chess champion of India, who died in 1999. The scam The article claims that AIIMS manufactures and sells a medicine named Cardioton that can cure hypertension almost completely. Per the article, to order this drug, one needs to spin a wheel on the website, filled with various discount offers. We spun this wheel thrice and each time it stopped at a 50 per cent discount. As soon as the wheel stops spinning, the message, "Congratulations, you can order Cardioton at a maximum discount of 50 per cent" appears. Next, if you click on "OK", you are asked for your name and phone number. You are then given a 10-minute deadline and a message below states: "If you do not fill out the form by the deadline, your reservation will be transferred to another person, because the product is running low." advertisement Once you enter these personal details (which you shouldn't), you'll see a message that says your order has been accepted. Fake websites often use these pressure tactics to scam people and harvest their data. Site created recently Using GoDaddy's WhoIs tool, we found that this website "inecuruhi.shop" was created in October 2023. Fraudsters often create fake websites for scamming people or harvesting their data and once their purpose is fulfilled, they deactivate the websites. According to GoDaddy, the website is registered in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. To sum it up, a fraudulent website is claiming that AIIMS is producing and selling a hypertension medicine Cardioton, which is totally false. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Nov 10, 2023 20:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of storm aftermath in Scotland FALSELY shared as Iceland quakes
content:
The video shows the aftermath of Storm Babet in Scotland.
An astounding 800 earthquakes shook Iceland in under 14 hours on November 10, following which a state of emergency was declared in the country. Amid this, a video  went viral on social media showing a patch of forest seemingly floating. Allegedly this was a consequence of the recent earthquakes in Iceland. The woods were moving like the sea this morning Is this another consequence of #earthquakes Filmed by David Nugent-Malone when he was walking his dog in #Mugdock #Grindavik #sismo #Iceland #Iceland #earthquakes #wxtwitter #evacuations #StateofEmergency #SOE #earthquake #Iceland pic.twitter.com/hSJdyBVozC — Arun Gangwar (@AG_Journalist) November 11, 2023
The woods were moving like the sea this morning Is this another consequence of #earthquakes Filmed by David Nugent-Malone when he was walking his dog in #Mugdock #Grindavik #sismo #Iceland #Iceland #earthquakes #wxtwitter #evacuations #StateofEmergency #SOE #earthquake #Iceland pic.twitter.com/hSJdyBVozC — Arun Gangwar (@AG_Journalist) November 11, 2023
An X user shared the video and wrote , "The woods were moving like the sea this morning. Is this another consequence of earthquakes? Filmed by David Nugent-Malone when he was walking his dog in Grindavik."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the viral video was unrelated to the earthquakes in Iceland. Our Probe
Reverse searching the keyframes of the viral video led us to The Telegraph's YouTube channel , where it was posted on October 21, 2023. The caption and description accompanying the video clarified that it showed a patch of a forest floor in Scotland appearing to breathe after Storm Babet winds lifted trees' roots.
The video description further explained the phenomenon, attributing it to a shallow root system meeting strong winds, creating the illusion of the earth breathing. It noted that David Nugent-Malone, a 38-year-old poet and short story writer from Strathblane in Stirlingshire, recorded the video while walking his dog, Jake, in Mugdock, Scotland.
The BBC and The Guardian  shared and reported the viral video on October 21, attributing it to the aftermath of Storm Babet. This intense extratropical cyclone affected large parts of northern and western Europe.
Thus, the video showing the aftermath of Storm Babet in Scotland is being falsely shared as footage of the aftermath of earthquakes in Iceland. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 14, 2023 14:45 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT Israel's phosphorus attack on Gaza's Al-Shifa Hospital
content:
This image is from September 2017 and shows a white phosphorus attack carried out by the US in Syria.
A photo of what appears to be a white phosphorus attack on a building has been widely shared on social media. Those sharing this image claimed  that Israel used white phosphorus on a Gaza hospital. "Israeli forces bombarded Al Shifa Hospital & ambulances. They dropped phosphorus bombs in the vicinity of the Hospital," claimed one such X post. Israeli forces bombarded Al Shifa Hospital & ambulances. They dropped phosphorus bombs in the vicinity of the Hospital. 🥲😐 #FreePalestine #Gaza_Geniocide #Terroristİsrael #Gaza pic.twitter.com/kq6qvJVKkv — Izhar (@Izharmhk32) November 10, 2023
Israeli forces bombarded Al Shifa Hospital & ambulances. They dropped phosphorus bombs in the vicinity of the Hospital. 🥲😐 #FreePalestine #Gaza_Geniocide #Terroristİsrael #Gaza pic.twitter.com/kq6qvJVKkv — Izhar (@Izharmhk32) November 10, 2023
On Facebook  and Instagram , people shared this image with captions like, "Recent reports reveal that Al Shifa Hospital went into complete darkness, as the hospital has run out of electricity due to the ongoing aggression by Israeli forces in the Gaza Strip. This comes as hundreds of patients are in ICU, and others are on life-saving devices and are left to meet their fate. The image below reveals the drops of phosphorus bombs by Israeli forces in the vicinity of Al Shifa Hospital." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the image is more than six years old and from Syria.Â
Upon conducting a reverse search with the viral image, we found a Russian news report  from September 27, 2017. This report featured the same image used in the viral posts. Per this report, an international coalition led by the United States carried out these strikes on a residential area in the Deir Ez-Zur province of Syria.Â
A subsequent search with keywords took us to a report in the "Viet Times"  featuring the same photo, among other images and videos of the phosphorus bomb strikes. This report also was about a US attack in Ar Raqqah, Syria, making it evident that the image in question is not related to the current Israel-Hamas war.Â
Syrian state-controlled news agency SANA also reported  this incident in September 2017 and noted that the attack led to the death of three civilians, with five others getting injured.Â
It is, however, noteworthy that the Palestinian health minister Mai Al Kaila has alleged  that the Israeli Defence Forces attacked Gaza's Al-Shifa Hospital with white phosphorus bombs, endangering the lives of at least 39 children.Â
Hence, it is evident that an old and unrelated image from Syria was falsely shared to assert an alleged incident in a Gaza hospital. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Nov 14, 2023 21:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Palestinian mom recovers kid's toy in Gaza? No, this is from Syria
content:
This picture was taken by Iranian photographer Hassan Ghaedi in Homs, Syria in 2016.
As the Israel-Hamas conflict continues, thousands of disturbing images and videos of destroyed houses, injured children, and more in Gaza have been shared online. Among them is a poignant photo , allegedly of a Palestinian mother retrieving her child's toy car from their destroyed house in Gaza.Â
The photograph shows a woman descending the staircase of a dilapidated structure, clutching a toy car in one hand. One such post shared on X by American political commentator Jackson Hinkle  reads, "You CANNOT BREAK the Palestinian spirit."
India Today found that the photo in question is old and not from Gaza. Our Probe
A reverse search of the viral image led us to the same photograph published on the website of the "Siena International Photo Awards," an annual photography competition held by the non-profit association Art Photo Travel .Â
According to its website, the photograph won the title of "Remarkable Artwork" in 2020 under the category "Documentary & Photojournalism". The description of the photograph titled "Mother" states that it was taken in Homs, Syria.
"Homs, Syria's third-largest city, had been involved in war for four years. A mother, who returned home after the end of the conflict, found her child's toy car in their destroyed house," read the description of the photo. As per the website, the photo was captured by Hassan Ghaedi, a freelance photographer from Iran. India Today reached out to Ghaedi, who confirmed that the photo was shot by him in Homs in 2016. We also found that Ghaedi shared the same photo on his Instagram account  in February 2020. The caption to the photo reads, "Life in war. The #mother, who returned home after the end of the conflict and has found her child' toys. #Homs #Syria. On June 2016." The photo was also featured in multiple reports  on the winners of 2020 Siena International Photo Awards . It is hence clear that the photograph in question is old and from Syria. It has no connection to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 14, 2023 22:53 IST

title: Fact Check: 2022 clip of Guatemalan volcano VIRAL as recent eruption in Italy
content:
This video is from August 2022 and shows the Guatemalan volcano Volcán de Fuego.
Over the past few days, there have been reports of volcanic activity in various parts of the European continent , with notable incidents occurring in Iceland and Italy. Meanwhile, a fantastic video of a volcanic eruption  was widely shared. The video showed red-hot magma being ejected into the sky with many people watching this sight. #WATCH 🔴 In #Sicily , Italy, the volcano #Etna has erupted. Eyewitnesses are sharing videos. The height of the gas and ash column reaches 4,500 meters above sea level. pic.twitter.com/IuHbYVFOZf — Voice of Europe 🌍 (@V_of_Europe) November 13, 2023
#WATCH 🔴 In #Sicily , Italy, the volcano #Etna has erupted. Eyewitnesses are sharing videos. The height of the gas and ash column reaches 4,500 meters above sea level. pic.twitter.com/IuHbYVFOZf — Voice of Europe 🌍 (@V_of_Europe) November 13, 2023
"In Sicily, Italy, the volcano Etna has erupted. Eyewitnesses are sharing videos. The height of the gas and ash column reaches 4,500 meters above sea level," read an X post containing the clip. At the same time, the official Facebook pages of both ET Now  and Kyiv Post also showcased this video, calling it Italy's Mount Etna. Archived versions of both posts can be seen here  and here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is nearly a year old and from Guatemala, not Mount Etna in Italy. GETTING TO THE CORE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post dated August 28, 2022, containing the same footage. The caption of this post indicated that the video was filmed at Volcan de Fuego, located in Guatemala in North America. The caption also added that to license the video, one could mail "licensing@viralhog.com".     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Rob Brown (@skiddinginbroadside)
A post shared by Rob Brown (@skiddinginbroadside)
Based on these clues, an advanced search with keywords took us to the video  uploaded to the verified channel of Viral Hog on September 9, 2022.Â
The description of this video mentioned that the eruption took place on August 26 that year, with a brief statement from the eyewitness of the rare occurrence, making it quite evident that the video in question has nothing to do with recent volcanic activity at Italy's Mount Etna.Â
We also came across several videos of Mount Etna's volcanic eruption uploaded to the YouTube channels of The Sun  and The Independent  on November 13 and 14.Â
Upon comparing screengrabs from the visuals of Mount Etna's eruption with the video of the Guatemalan volcano, it becomes clear that there are significant differences in the visuals of both events.
Thus, it's clear that an old video of a volcanic eruption in Guatemala was falsely shared as a recent incident in Italy's Mount Etna. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 15, 2023 22:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Israeli Parliament DIDN'T descend into a brawl, old clip from Jordan viral
content:
This video shows a scuffle that broke out in the Parliament of Jordan in 2021.
A video of a scuffle that allegedly broke out in the Israeli Parliament  has been shared widely on social media platforms. The clip shows a group of suited men slapping another man sitting in front of them, which is followed by a brawl.Â
Many shared the clip  claiming that an Israeli official was brutally beaten up in the Parliament. An archived version of one such post can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from the Parliament of Jordan, not Israel. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to several media reports about this incident. According to a report in The Tribune containing a screengrab from the viral clip, several deputies traded punches is a brawl in Jordan's Parliament on December 28, 2021. Reportedly, a verbal row escalated into a scuffle when the Assembly Speaker called on a deputy to leave. An extended version of the clip was shared by Reuters.
Per The Guardian , the incident unfolded during a session in Amman, the capital of Jordan, where lawmakers were discussing a proposed amendment  to the constitution--adding the female noun for a Jordanian citizen, to a chapter in the constitution that guaranteed equal rights to all citizens.Â
However, several MPs branded the amendment as "useless" during a heated debate in the House of Representatives. The punch-up began over the refusal of a member to apologise over unwarranted remarks during the session, all of which was broadcast live on a Jordanian news channel.
 Per reports, the debate  went out of hand when MP Suleiman Abu Yahya accused Speaker of the House Abdul Karim Dughmi of being unable to run the parliamentary meeting, following which a group of MPs engaged in verbal altercations and fisticuffs. Reportedly, no one was injured during the incident  and the parliamentary session was adjourned for 30 minutes . اشتباك بالأيدي بين نواب تحت قبة البرلمان #الأردن #التلفزيون_الأردني pic.twitter.com/ZmqtdUkr9Y — Jordan TV-التلفزيون الأردني (@JrtvMedia) December 28, 2021
