title: Fact Check: This is 2013 footage of Egypt massacre, NOT Gaza's Al-Shifa hospital
content:
The video is a decade-old footage from Egypt, shot during the August 2013 Rabaa massacre.
Israeli troops entered Gaza's largest Al-Shifa Hospital on November 15, prompting global concern for the hundreds of patients undergoing treatment. Israel called it a "precise and targeted operation against Hamas in a specified area"  within the medical complex.
Now, a video  that's been widely shared shows people inside a building attempting to flee amid sound of gunfire. An X user shared the video  and wrote, "BREAKING: FIRST FOOTAGE OF SHOOTING INSIDE THE AL SHIFA HOSPITAL. Does this prove Hamas was present inside the hospital, and clashing with the IDF as per this video?" An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today found that the video is decade-old footage from Egypt. OUR PROBE
An X user responded to one such viral post and claimed that it was an old video from Egypt. Using this clue, we performed a keyword search that led us to a better-quality version of the same video  on the YouTube channel of the Egyptian news organisation Rassd News Network (RNN), uploaded on August 16, 2013. The caption, written in Arabic, stated that it showed an intense shooting at detainees in Rabaa Hospital in Cairo.Â
Further searches led us to similar footage of destruction and chaos at a hospital in an Al Jazeera documentary on YouTube  titled "Massacre in Rabaa", uploaded on August 17, 2016.Â
The Rabaa massacre is considered to be one of the deadliest in Egypt. In 2013, large sit-in protests were organised demanding the reinstatement of the country's first democratically elected president, Mohamed Morsi .Â
Thousands had gathered in Rabaa al-Adawiya Square in Cairo to support Morsi, who was ousted in a coup led by the military leader and current president, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. Egyptian forces cracked down on protestors in "a scorched-earth assault"  using armoured vehicles, bulldozers, ground troops, and snipers, resulting in hundreds of deaths.
Human Rights Watch reported  817 deaths during the Rabaa dispersal alone, with the overall toll likely exceeding 1,000 when accounting for unidentified bodies and missing individuals.
Thus, it's evident that a decade-old footage from the Rabaa Massacre in Egypt was falsely attributed to the Al-Shifa hospital in Gaza. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 15, 2023 22:55 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of human sea is not pro-Palestine march, it is from Spain
content:
This video is from a demonstration against acting Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez in Madrid over the decision to grant amnesty to Catalan separatists.
A video of a city square filled with thousands of people has been shared by many as the bird's eye view of a pro-Palestine in Spain. "Human flood in Spain for Palestine," read one such post on X .Â
India Today found that the video is from an anti-government demonstration in Spain, not a pro-Palestine march. Our Probe
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the same video posted by multiple media outlets  on November 12 and 13. As per these posts , the video was from a protest against Spain's acting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's plans to grant amnesty to "Catalan separatists in order to stay in power." WATCH - Massive protest across Spain against prime minister Pedro Sanchez's plans to grant amnesty to Catalan separatists in order to stay in power pic.twitter.com/1kuKihkL9H — Insider Paper (@TheInsiderPaper) November 12, 2023 Â
WATCH - Massive protest across Spain against prime minister Pedro Sanchez's plans to grant amnesty to Catalan separatists in order to stay in power pic.twitter.com/1kuKihkL9H — Insider Paper (@TheInsiderPaper) November 12, 2023 Â
A different video from the same location was also posted by Reuters  on November 12. The text along with the video said, "Tens of thousands of people protested across Spain against acting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's plans to grant amnesty to Catalan separatists in exchange for support for another term in office." Reuters also reported that the video was from Madrid. Tens of thousands of people protested across Spain against acting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's plans to grant amnesty to Catalan separatists in exchange for support for another term in office https://t.co/k6ln3o3Ibx pic.twitter.com/bKXTI9Y3Fm — Reuters (@Reuters) November 12, 2023
Tens of thousands of people protested across Spain against acting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's plans to grant amnesty to Catalan separatists in exchange for support for another term in office https://t.co/k6ln3o3Ibx pic.twitter.com/bKXTI9Y3Fm — Reuters (@Reuters) November 12, 2023
Reportedly, Spain's caretaker government  reached an agreement with the Catalan separatist party Junts on November 9. This agreement involves the passage of a controversial law offering amnesty to those convicted in connection with Catalonia's bid for independence from Spain in 2017. The aim of this deal was to establish a new coalition minority government and secure another term in office following the inconclusive July election. Hundreds of people protested outside Spain's Socialist party headquarters in Madrid against ongoing negotiations for granting amnesty to people involved with Catalonia's failed 2017 independence bid pic.twitter.com/ucouFpKCP1 — Reuters (@Reuters) November 9, 2023
Hundreds of people protested outside Spain's Socialist party headquarters in Madrid against ongoing negotiations for granting amnesty to people involved with Catalonia's failed 2017 independence bid pic.twitter.com/ucouFpKCP1 — Reuters (@Reuters) November 9, 2023
However, this agreement sparked widespread concern across the country, with Sanchez's conservative opponents accusing him of jeopardising the rule of law for personal political advantages. Authorities reported a turnout of 80,000 people in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square, while the conservative opposition People's Party, which had called for protests nationwide, claimed the total was closer to one million.
According to a Politico report , in Barcelona, 6,000 people demonstrated, while numbers reached 30,000 in Granada, and 50,000 in Seville. Protests also took place in cities including Malaga, Palma, and Valencia.
Pro-Palestine marches have been taking in several cities across the world. Demonstrations in support of Palestine were held in Barcelona and Madrid, among other places, in October.Â
It is, however, clear that the video in question is from an anti-government protest in Spain and not related to the Israel-Hamas conflict. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Nov 17, 2023 14:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Ratan Tata's deep fake video is being used to lure people to betting app
content:
This video is AI-generated. Ratan Tata hasn't endorsed any such game
After Rashmika Mandanna, Katrina Kaif, Sara Tendulkar, and Kajol, now a "deep fake" of industrialist Ratan Tata is making the rounds on social media. In it, the renowned businessman can be seen endorsing an online betting coach. Â
In the video, Tata can be seen asking people to join the Telegram channel "@aviator_ultrawin" run by a man called Amir Khan, who he describes as a person who teaches others to play "Aviator", an online betting game. The archived version of this post  can be seen here .
It is noteworthy that the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology imposed a ban on 22 betting apps  in September this year. The highly talked about Mahadev App was too one of them.
So, let's look at what is going on here.Â
A quick reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a June 2015 video of Ratan Tata receiving an Honoris Causa degree at the HEC Paris Business School. At that time, many news outlets had reported this event. Â
Upon comparing the visuals of both videos, one can easily notice similarities between them. A comparison is given below. To understand what was going on, India Today contacted the person being endorsed in the viral video, who runs the Telegram channel "@aviator_ultrawin". He told us that his name was Amir and promised to help us earn a minimum of Rs 1 lakh every day. All we needed to do was play the "Aviator" betting game. He also shared some alleged testimonies from people praising him. He then asked us to register on the "Aviator" site. However, the link he provided led us to a different sports betting and casino platform called "1win". The page requested personal details like phone number and email ID, a common tactic used by scamsters to harvest data. Next, we asked Amir to explain how the game is played, and he shared the link to a Telegram channel called "VIP Training". This channel contained multiple videos explaining how to play "Aviator". advertisement Scamming Through Ads We noticed that the Facebook post that contained the Ratan Tata deep fake was actually an advertisement. It is not visible on the Facebook page as a regular post. However, we were able to find it in the Meta Ad Library . This deep fake video was posted as an advertisement on this page at least 5 times. We also found that people have complained about being duped at the a consumer complaints forum, by a person named "Amir Khan" running a Telegram channel related to the Aviator game. Are betting apps legal in India? Gaming laws in India are going through a transformation. As of now, there is no single law to govern online betting games in India. It differs from state to state. Supreme Court advocate Manish Pathak noted the same while talking to India Today. Last year, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued an advisory  about advertisements for betting. As per this advisory , since betting and gambling are regulated heavily in most part of India and pose a financial risk for the consumers, the promotion of online/offline betting is not advised in larger public interest. Cybersecurity expert and Supreme Court advocate Dr Pavan Duggal also told us that though there are no well-defined laws to regulate online betting games in India currently, ones which are based on skills, could be qualified as legal. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Nov 17, 2023 14:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Staged stunt video falsely shared as Israeli women knocking out Arab men
content:
The video is a staged performance by stunt artists from Campus Univers Cascades, a professional training centre in Paris.
The Israel-Hamas conflict has sparked an unprecedented surge in anti-Arab and anti-Muslim racism globally. A video making the rounds on social media now shows a street brawl involving three women and several men. Allegedly, this incident took place in Paris where three Israeli women overpowered 10 Arab men who accosted them.
One such post read , "Caught on CCTV - In a Paris underpass, three Israeli girls are accosted by 10 young Arab men. In about 10 seconds, the three girls prove that Arab boys are no match for Israeli girls." An archived version of this tweet can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video of the brawl is staged and claims about the individuals' ethnicity were fabricated to fuel animosity between Israelis and Arabs. Our Probe
Conducting a reverse image search on keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post dated November 2, 2023. The account "campus.univers.cascades" which posted the video , also contained several other videos of street fights, martial arts training, and combat stunts. This suggested that the viral video was likely staged.
Twelve people were tagged in the post containing the video. India Today reached out to all the people tagged to understand the context of the clip. Lucas Dollfus, one of the combatants seen in the video , confirmed that the video was part of a training exercise themed "street fight."Â
While aiming for maximum realism, he emphasised that it was merely a stunt for a movie. Dollfus clarified that the racial context being alleged was made up and that the fight was staged by stunt performers from Campus Univers Cascades, a professional training centre established in Paris in 2008 for stunt techniques in cinema and entertainment.
Another team member, Noa Potard, also confirmed that everything was meticulously prepared in advance and choreographed.
Thus, it's clear that a choreographed fight by stunt performers was shared with false racial claims. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Nov 17, 2023 18:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Fire in Iceland? This volcano video is not recent, it's from 2021
content:
This video shows Iceland's long-dormant Fagradalsfjall volcano spewing lava in March 2021.
Residents of Grindavik, an Icelandic town  that was evacuated after hundreds of earthquakes jolted the country, were allowed a brief visit home to collect pets and essential belongings on November 12 . The tremors have prompted fears of a possible eruption  in the country's southwestern Reykjanes Peninsula, as fissures formed on roads of the abandoned town .
Amid this, a video of a volcano spewing lava as people flee the area was shared widely on social media . Those sharing the clip claimed that volcanic eruptions have begun in Iceland . A person shared the clip on Facebook, writing, "Here we go, if the UK wasn't grey already it could possibly be covered in an ash cloud. Iceland - Volcano is starting to erupt. Mass evacuations are happening." An archived version of a similar post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is two years old and does not show a recent eruption in Iceland. Getting to the 'core'
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Reddit post  containing the same clip from March 30, 2021. This proved that the video did not show a recent incident. Further, we found several people sharing the same video  around the same time .Â
Many of these posts credited "Binni Smari" for the viral video . Using this, we found the viral video shared on March 21, 2021, by a Facebook account that goes by the same name. Per the caption, Smari went to see the volcano the same day and shared several photos from the spot.
We also found a news report about Iceland's long-dormant Fagradalsfjall volcano ejecting lava on March 21, 2021. The report carried a video similar to the one going viral, shared by Reykjavik resident Andri Magnason, who also headed out to see the rare eruption.
Further, we could not find any reports about any recent eruptions at the Fagradalsfjall volcano at the time of writing this report. Thus, it is more than clear, that an old video from 2021 was shared as a recent volcanic eruption in Iceland. - Ends Published By: Aishwarya Dakhore Published On: Nov 17, 2023 20:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Old clip of Kashmiri students celebrating falsely linked to Australia's World Cup win
content:
The video is two years old, and shows alleged celebrations by Kashmiri students following a Pakistan T20 World Cup win in 2021.
Australia clinched the ICC World Cup for the sixth time, breaking India's home-tournament dominance with a six-wicket victory. In its aftermath, a viral video of people celebrating jubilantly in what appears to be a hostel surfaced on social media.
Many alleged that this video showed students from the Sher-e-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences (SKIMS) in Srinagar celebrating Australia's victory over India in the 2023 World Cup. Kashmiri Students of SKIMS in Srinagar celebrating Australia's win over India #INDvsAUS pic.twitter.com/4muwCPKefk — Shabby (@Shabby_AI) November 19, 2023
Kashmiri Students of SKIMS in Srinagar celebrating Australia's win over India #INDvsAUS pic.twitter.com/4muwCPKefk — Shabby (@Shabby_AI) November 19, 2023
A user on X shared the viral video and wrote, "Kashmiri Students of SKIMS celebrating Australia's win over India." An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video is two years old and unrelated to the just-concluded ICC World Cup 2023.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led to a Mojo Story video report  shared on YouTube on October 26, 2021. The report contained the viral clip and highlighted that students faced charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act for allegedly celebrating Pakistan's victory against India in a T20 World Cup match. The description further noted that criminal cases had been filed against students from Government Medical College and SKIMS in Srinagar.
Another report by ABP News  from the same period confirmed the invocation of UAPA against SKIMS students for allegedly chanting pro-Pakistan slogans after Pakistan's victory in the T20 World Cup.
The Wire reported on October 26, 2021, that alongside students, college management and hostel wardens also faced charges made by the Jammu and Kashmir police after the video of the students went viral.
Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with the ICC World Cup 2023. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Nov 20, 2023 17:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of female Israeli soldier breaking down is more than a decade old
content:
This video dates back to November 15, 2012, and shows an Israeli soldier breaking down in Southern Israel.
A video allegedly showing a female Israel Defense Forces soldier howling and crying amid the noise of explosions has gone viral on social media. Those sharing the clip  claimed that the IDF soldier experienced a mental breakdown due to the fear of the Islamic Resistance Force, alias Hamas, in Gaza.Â
"FOOTAGE: IDF SOLDIER HAS MENTAL BREAKDOWN. OLD MAN WANT WAR | YOUNG PEOPLE HAVE TO FIGHT IT. Would the fighters, from both sides, go to war if it wasn't decided from above?" read one X post containing the clip. 🚨FOOTAGE: IDF SOLDIER HAS MENTAL BREAKDOWN OLD MAN WANT WAR | YOUNG PEOPLE HAVE TO FIGHT IT Would the fighters, from both sides, go to war if it wasn't decided from above? pic.twitter.com/mM8ZN1Fz4B — Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal) November 19, 2023
🚨FOOTAGE: IDF SOLDIER HAS MENTAL BREAKDOWN OLD MAN WANT WAR | YOUNG PEOPLE HAVE TO FIGHT IT Would the fighters, from both sides, go to war if it wasn't decided from above? pic.twitter.com/mM8ZN1Fz4B — Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal) November 19, 2023
The video was also shared on Facebook  with similar claims. Its archived version can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is 11 years old and unrelated to the ongoing war between Hamas and Israel.Â
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across its screenshot in an Arabic news report published on November 17, 2012.Â
The report said that the female Israeli soldier was screaming in response to a cacophony of sirens and the impact of rockets hitting the ground. This incident was similarly covered by other Arabic media outlets .
As the logo of Sky News Arabic was visible in the video, we searched using some advanced keywords and found the original video on its YouTube channel as well. Uploaded on November 15, 2012, the Arabic caption of this video translates to: "Qassam rockets cause panic in Israel". Qassam, or Al Qassam, is the military wing of Hamas.Â
As per the description of the video, these rocket attacks by Al Qassam brigades were in response to the killing of its deputy commander, Ahmed Al-Jaabari. Reportedly, the Hamas military chief was killed by an Israeli airstrike in the Gaza Strip on November 14, 2012.Â
Therefore, it leaves no doubt that the video was neither shot in Israeli-occupied Gaza nor does it show the ongoing war. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Nov 20, 2023 19:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Ponting didn't call BCCI 'cricket mafia', social media spins comment out of thin air
content:
India Today found no evidence of such a statement made by Ponting. The X account that made this claim has previously been found to share fake quotes.
Former Australian Captain Ricky Ponting made a subtle remark  suggesting India's alleged pitch manipulation may have backfired in the ICC World Cup 2023 finals. Following this, social media has been buzzing with claims  that the former Australian cricketer took a swipe at India's cricket establishment. Ricky Ponting on Fox Cricket: "This is a win of justice against cricket mafia. Your money and power are still not winning World Cups for you. How embarrassing." Ponting owned India and BCCI 😂 #INDvAUS #INDvsAUS pic.twitter.com/RiA5ii26Bb — Momina مومنہ🌻 (@IamMommynah) November 19, 2023
Ricky Ponting on Fox Cricket: "This is a win of justice against cricket mafia. Your money and power are still not winning World Cups for you. How embarrassing." Ponting owned India and BCCI 😂 #INDvAUS #INDvsAUS pic.twitter.com/RiA5ii26Bb — Momina مومنہ🌻 (@IamMommynah) November 19, 2023
Social media users claimed that Ponting criticised India's cricket board BCCI and said "This is a win of justice against cricket mafia . Your money and power is still not winning World Cups for you. How embarrassing." These claims suggest that he made this statement during an interview with Fox Cricket. An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found this claim to be baseless, as Ponting made no such comment against the BCCI. Our Probe
A thorough keyword search across the internet yielded no news reports about the alleged statement, not even on Fox Cricket. If Ponting had made such a remark, it would have been covered in the news.
We also scrutinised Ponting's social media handles but failed to find any such statement. We traced the viral claim to originate from the X account "@ahadfoooty" . This account has previously come under the spotlight for sharing false quotes attributed to cricket personalities.Â
Interestingly, many such accounts seem to emanate from Pakistan  and Dubai . India Today has previously debunked such misinformation campaigns from Pakistan.
In 2022, this account falsely attributed a fabricated statement to English cricketer Nasser Hussain , who promptly rebutted it, calling it false and urging its removal .
Similarly, India Today exposed incorrect statements attributed to Indian and Pakistani cricketers Sunil Gavaskar, Wasim Akram, and Waqar Younis . All these misinformation campaigns display similar patterns in their dissemination.
Regarding Indian pitches, the actual comment Ponting made was, "It was very, very sub-continental conditions today. A wicket preparation that has probably ended up backfiring on India to be totally fair."
So, to sum up, Ponting did not call the BCCI the "cricket mafia", and a false quote making this assertion has been widely shared. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 20, 2023 21:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Crowd chanted Hanuman Chalisa during World Cup Final? Nope, this is edited
content:
This video is edited. The clip originally showed Darshan Raval performing at the Narendra Modi Stadium during the India-Pakistan World Cup match on October 14.
Moments after Australia defeated India to lift the ICC World Cup trophy, spectators at the Narendra Modi stadium in Ahmedabad made headlines for leaving in disappointment as India drew closer to losing the final. Many condemned the crowd for lacking the proper spirit as Australia received their World Cup trophy in front of a near-empty stadium.Â
Now, a video purportedly from the finals is making the rounds. It allegedly shows a sea of people chanting the "Hanuman Chalisa" at the Ahmedabad stadium. One person wrote while sharing the clip : "It's IND vs AUS final and 1.5 lakh people singing Hanuman Chalisa."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip was edited. The video originally showed Darshan Raval performing at the Narendra Modi Stadium during the India vs Pakistan World Cup match in October. Revelry and Raval
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared on YouTube on October 16. It is noteworthy that this video did not feature the "Hanuman Chalisa" chants. Instead, Darshan Raval's hit song "Chogada" song could be heard playing in the background. The video's description read: "Darshan Raval at Narendra Modi Stadium", along with hashtags like "India vs Pakistan". This made it clear that the video had nothing to do with the World Cup finals. Watch the video
Per reports , prominent artists performed during the India-Pakistan match at the Narendra Modi Stadium on October 14. These artists included Shankar Mahadevan, Sukhwinder Singh, Arijit Singh, and Darshan Raval .
Using keywords, we found more videos of the performance, shot by spectators, — all shared in October . A comparison of the viral video with these proves that it's from the India-Pakistan match.
But where did the 'Chalisa' chants come from?
The YouTube channel that shared the viral video also shared the original version of the same video on October 16, in which Darshan's song could be heard playing in the background.Â
In YouTube Shorts, the source of audio is mentioned at the bottom of the video, similar to TikTok and Instagram Reels. In the viral video , we found the "Hanuman Chalisa" chants attributed to an event held in Jaipur .Â
This video from the Jaipur event was uploaded to YouTube on June 3.Â
Thus, it is more than clear that the video of spectators chanting Hanuman Chalisa in the Narendra Modi Stadium during the World Cup final was edited. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 21, 2023 12:51 IST

title: Fact Check: This clip of Aus players drinking from a shoe is NOT from WC23 final
content:
This video is not recent. It shows the Australian team celebrating its victory over New Zealand in the 2021 T20 World Cup.
A controversial photo of Australian all-rounder Mitchell Marsh sitting with his feet on the ICC World Cup trophy  has caused a storm online. Now, another alleged post-final celebration of the Australian team is making the rounds on social media.Â
The video  shows men donning Australian cricket team jerseys  pouring drinks into a shoe  and drinking it. One person shared the clip writing: "Australian team celebration after winning icc world cup 2023." An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video of the Australian cricket team is from 2021. WHAT OUR PROBE 'SHOE-D'?
With the help of a keyword search, we found an ANI report  from November 15, 2021, containing a screenshot from the viral video. According to it, the clip showed Australian players Matthew Wade and Marcus Stoinis celebrating their maiden T20 World Cup triumph by drinking from a shoe. This video was reportedly shot in Australia's dressing room and was shared by the International Cricket Council.
Further, we also found a tweet  from the official Twitter account of the International Cricket Council dated November 15, 2021. It is noteworthy that the original video had a logo of ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021 in the top-right corner. This logo was, however, blurred or hidden by emojis by those sharing the clip now as a recent celebration. How's your Monday going? 😅 #T20WorldCup pic.twitter.com/Fdaf0rxUiV — ICC (@ICC) November 15, 2021 Back in 2021, several media outlets  reported about this video, showing the Australian squad's unique celebration after defeating New Zealand  in the final, held at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. The act was termed "disgusting" by former Pakistan pacer Shoaib Akhtar  at the time. 'SHOEY': AN AUSSIE TRADITION
How's your Monday going? 😅 #T20WorldCup pic.twitter.com/Fdaf0rxUiV — ICC (@ICC) November 15, 2021
Back in 2021, several media outlets  reported about this video, showing the Australian squad's unique celebration after defeating New Zealand  in the final, held at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. The act was termed "disgusting" by former Pakistan pacer Shoaib Akhtar  at the time. 'SHOEY': AN AUSSIE TRADITION
Per reports, drinking from a shoe, called "the Shoey" is a popular way of celebrating in Australia. The act reportedly came to light after an Australian Formula One driver Daniel Ricciardo  drank champagne off of his racing boots  after finishing on the podium in the 2016 German Grand Prix. Since then, several sportspersons, television stars and even singers have done a Shoey .
Thus, it is more than clear that an old video of Australian cricketers drinking off of a shoe was falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 21, 2023 17:00 IST

title: Fact Check: World Cup retaliation? Nope, video of Shakib Al Hasan being manhandled is old
content:
The video is eight months old and shows an incident in Dubai during the inauguration of a jewellery showroom.
The ICC Cricket World Cup proved to be a challenging tournament for the Bangladeshi squad. Of the nine matches played, the team managed to win only two , drawing criticism for its catastrophic performance under the captainship of Shakib Al Hasan.
Now, a video going viral on social media shows a crowd surrounding Shakib, and seemingly dragging him. In the video , people can also be heard inciting harm towards the skipper. Those sharing the viral video claimed that upon the Bangladesh team's return home post their exit from the World Cup, cricket fans physically confronted Shakib.Â
A Facebook post user while sharing it, wrote , "Bangladeshi Fans beat Shakib al Hasan when he returned to Bangladesh after a poor World Cup campaign." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video is neither recent nor related to the World Cup.
Upon conducting a reverse search of keyframes from the video, we came across several media reports featuring Shakib in the same outfit. According to reports from March 16, 2023, Shakib was en route to inaugurate a jewellery showroom in Dubai when he was harassed by fans. This event had already stirred controversy due to the showroom's owner, Arav Khan, being a fugitive accused in a murder case involving a Bangladeshi police inspector.
Further, we found the video of the showroom opening on the YouTube channel of Bangladesh-based RTV News, containing the exact same frame of the viral video.
The caption noted that Shakib was harassed by expatriate Bangladeshis while inaugurating a jewellery showroom in Dubai. Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video has no connection to the recently concluded World Cup. It shows an eight-month-old incident when Shakib was mobbed while inaugurating a jewellery showroom in Dubai. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 21, 2023 18:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Old emotional videos of Rohit and Kohli go viral after India's World Cup defeat
content:
The Rohit Sharma video is from 2020 and the Virat Kohli one is from 2018. Neither has anything to do with the 2023 World Cup.
The stunning defeat against Australia at the ICC World Cup final has left Indians — fans and players alike — feeling down. Now, two videos are making rounds on social media that allegedly show Indian skipper Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli expressing their feelings about the match.Â
In one clip , Sharma could be heard saying, "Everyone thought we would do well. I know there were moments from the first match to the last match when it looked like we were going to win. We had eleven players in form, and everything was fine. But winning the World Cup by defeating different teams is not so easy. Winning the World Cup is a different kind of joy. We won a lot of bilateral series. But winning the World Cup doubles the confidence. Even if you lose, you go down that much. That is why we are so emotionally involved with the World Cup. The team has made some mistakes." Â
Sharing the video on Facebook, a user wrote , "Emotional Rohit Sharma Badly Crying on Live Video Call after India Loss World Cup Final vs Aus."
The second video shows Virat Kohli expressing his grief and extending apologies to his followers. Posting that video , another user wrote on Facebook, "Virat Kohli Say Sorry And Send Emotional Message For Indian Fans After Lost World Cup final Vs Aus."Â
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the Rohit Sharma video is three years old. The video of Virat Kohli was made after the Royal Challengers Bangalore's exit from 2018's Indian Premier League.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the Rohit Sharma video led us to a similar video posted on the X handle of Chennai Super Kings on May 14, 2020. The post read, "Hitman @ImRo45 and Chinna Thala @ImRaina pick a combined MI-CSK eleven where the water boys and assistant coaches are as legendary as it gets!" #Hitman @ImRo45 and #ChinnaThala @ImRaina pick a combined MI-CSK eleven where the water boys and assistant coaches are as legendary as it gets! #WhistlePodu VC: @mipaltan 🦁💛 pic.twitter.com/CUxJYWJQlB — Chennai Super Kings (@ChennaiIPL) May 14, 2020
#Hitman @ImRo45 and #ChinnaThala @ImRaina pick a combined MI-CSK eleven where the water boys and assistant coaches are as legendary as it gets! #WhistlePodu VC: @mipaltan 🦁💛 pic.twitter.com/CUxJYWJQlB — Chennai Super Kings (@ChennaiIPL) May 14, 2020
Using relevant keywords, we found another video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Sportskeeda Cricket on May 12, 2020, titled, "Rohit Sharma live Instagram chat with Raina." Around 22 minutes into this video, the viral clip can be seen.
Similarly, a reverse search of keyframes from the Kohli video led us to the official X handle of the cricketer , where we found the same video posted on May 24, 2018. The post read, "I really believe in the concept of, 'you either win or you learn'. We fought hard and gave it our all but one thing is for sure, next season we definitely will bounce back stronger than ever with our learnings from this season." I really believe in the concept of, "you either win or you learn". We fought hard and gave it our all but one thing is for sure, next season we definitely will bounce back stronger than ever with our learnings from this season. Take care. @RCBTweets #RCB #IPL2018 pic.twitter.com/b0QM9chRAN — Virat Kohli (@imVkohli) May 24, 2018
I really believe in the concept of, "you either win or you learn". We fought hard and gave it our all but one thing is for sure, next season we definitely will bounce back stronger than ever with our learnings from this season. Take care. @RCBTweets #RCB #IPL2018 pic.twitter.com/b0QM9chRAN — Virat Kohli (@imVkohli) May 24, 2018
A keyword search on the internet led us to a news report published by The Indian Express  at the time. According to it, after the Royal Challengers Bangalore's exit from 2018's IPL edition, Kohli apologised to fans who were disappointed by the team's performance of that season. News outlets like Scroll  and the Deccan Chronicle  also published news reports about the same.
Of course, it has been widely reported  that Rohit Sharma teared up after India's loss and Virat Kohli left the field with his head down. The duo, however, has yet to address the public about India's World Cup defeat.Â
So, it is more than clear that the videos are old and not related to India's defeat in the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023's final against Australia. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 21, 2023 20:32 IST

title: Fact Check: This isn't a 'Hamas tunnel' in Gaza, it's a World War bunker in UK
content:
This video shows a tunnel in London that was built during the Second World War.
A video of a man holding a flashlight allegedly traversing a Hamas tunnel is being widely shared on social media. The archived version of such posts can be seen here  and here .Â
An X user posted this video with the caption, "Part of a 7 min. clip of Hamas' tunnel system. Most would find it easy to get lost in. They placed these under schools, hospitals, daycares, civilisation's homes and wherever." Â
India Today found that this video is neither recent nor from Gaza. Instead, it shows a military bunker which was built in London during the Second World War. DIGGING INTO FACTS
In the viral clip, we noticed the watermark of a TikTok account "@urbexkev".
Accessing TikTok through the Tor browser, we found that the viral video was shared on October 31 with hashtags like bunker", "ww2", and "underground".
On November 8, @urbexkev shared another video  of a similar location, calling it a "WW2 HQ Bunker". Getting a clue from here, we ran a keyword search which led to a video  on a YouTube channel named "TheSecretVault". In this video, people can be seen going inside a similar-looking tunnel. The exact name of the tunnel or its location wasn't revealed in this video. However, its description contained the link to an article  on the website "Beyond the Point". Per this article, the tunnel in the video was the Reigate army bunker, a secret bunker located in Reigate, a town in England's Surrey county. It was reportedly built during the Second World War. The article contained several photos of the bunker, all of which bear a striking resemblance to the viral video.  LOCATING THE BUNKER ON GOOGLE MAPS At the beginning of the video posted on the "TheSecretVault" YouTube channel, one can see a wooden door, a brown building surrounded by a green fence and another brown building with "SES Water Tower" written on it. The building adjacent to it had the "The National Trust" written on a plaque outside it. A tall tower could also be seen. We found all of this on Google Street View. As the people in the video moved further past "The National Trust" building, they jumped over a small wooden gate and headed further into a forest area. Street View is not available for that area. However, it can be said with certainty that the Reigate army bunker is located in this vicinity. advertisement Others too have shared videos of their visit to the Reigate army bunker on YouTube. Some of these videos can be seen here , here , and here . HUNDREDS OF TUNNELS BUILT IN THE UK DURING WWII According to a report published in the Daily Mail , more than 600 secret bunkers were built in the UK during the Second World War. These bunkers served as military bases for soldiers and were furnished with basic facilities like wooden bunk beds, basic cooking equipment, and chemical toilets. A vast majority of these bunkers have now been identified but the locations of many others are still unknown. So, while many reports suggest that Hamas has built a labyrinth of tunnels in Gaza, and Israel has claimed to have found some of them , it's nevertheless clear that the viral video does not show one. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Nov 21, 2023 23:05 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT heavy floods in Palestine, this video is at least five years old
content:
This video has been present on the internet since as early as 2018. According to reports from the time, it shows flooding in Lebanon.
A video circulating on social media allegedly  shows a massive flood in the Palestinian city of Jericho in the West Bank. In it, a heavy stream of muddy floodwater can be seen surging past a residential area.
India Today found that the video is at least five years old. Back in 2018, it was widely shared as flash floods in Lebanon. Our Probe
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the same video shared by a Facebook page on June 15, 2018. As per this post, the video shows flash floods that hit the eastern coast of the Mediterranean, in Ras Baalbek, Lebanon on June 13, 2018. The Facebook page credited the video to "Lebanon Weather".
We then checked the Facebook page of "Lebanon Weather" and found the same video  shared by it on June 13, 2018. According to this post as well, the video was from Lebanon's Baalbek. The page has also posted other videos of flash floods, reportedly shot in Ras Baalbek.
The viral video and similar others were also shared by several Facebook users  on June 13 and 14, 2018 claiming to show floods in Ras Baalbek. We also found parts of this video used in a news report  from June 13, 2018 about the floods.
A screenshot from the video in question was also featured in an information note  on the June 2018 floods in Ras Baalbek, prepared by the Climate Change and Environment Program at Issam Fares Institute for Public Policy and International Affairs under the American University of Beirut. The flash flood of June 13 in Ras Baalbek is a natural phenomenon that has been occurring for years and is amplified by human activities. Check out the information note below done by the Climate Change and Environment program at IFI! #Bekaa #Lebanon #floods pic.twitter.com/P2yOC1lva2 — IFI at AUB (@ifi_aub) June 14, 2018
The flash flood of June 13 in Ras Baalbek is a natural phenomenon that has been occurring for years and is amplified by human activities. Check out the information note below done by the Climate Change and Environment program at IFI! #Bekaa #Lebanon #floods pic.twitter.com/P2yOC1lva2 — IFI at AUB (@ifi_aub) June 14, 2018
According to reports from the time, heavy rains led to flash floods in Ras Baalbek on June 13 and 14, 2018, causing flooding in houses and shops and submerging farmlands.
Reuters recently reported about the start of winter rains in Gaza and consequent fears about the possibility of flooding among homeless Palestinians living in makeshift tents following Israeli bombing. However, we couldn't find any reports of heavy floods in Jericho.
It is hence clear that the video in question is years old and not from Palestine. - Ends Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Nov 22, 2023 15:01 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Travis Head DID NOT dedicate Australia's WC23 victory to Palestine
content:
This post was made from a parody account of the Australian player. There are no reports about Head dedicating the victory to Palestinians.
Following Australia's smashing World Cup victory, many on social media are claiming that star cricketer Travis Head dedicated the championship trophy to Palestinians . According to some of these posts, Head also expressed gratitude to Pakistan captain Babar Azam, who gifted him the bat that contributed to his tournament-winning performance.
Many of these posts contained the screenshot of an X post purportedly made by Head . The post read: "I dedicate this victory to the innocent people of Palestine. May peace prevail all over the world. Special thanks to @babarazam258 for the bat, always proved lucky for me."
India Today found that the X post circulated in the name of Head was made by a parody account of the Australian player. There are no reports about Head dedicating Australia's victory to Palestinians. Our Probe
Had the Australian cricketer dedicated the World Cup trophy to Palestinians, it would have made headlines internationally. However, our search did not yield any credible reports supporting such a claim. Additionally, Instagram is the only social media platform where Travis Head has a verified account, and we found no posts related to dedicating the victory to Palestine there. Even an Instagram story by Head in solidarity with Palestine would likely have garnered media attention.
In the viral screenshot, the X username visible on the image was "@TravisHead_07". A search for this username on X led us to an account seemingly belonging to Travis Head . The bio of this account created in August 2023, however, states: "A proud husband and father. Parody Account." The now-viral screenshot is from a post made by this account on November 19, 2023. It's worth mentioning that this account has also made several pro-Palestine posts. Head parody used to be Kohli parody Further investigation revealed that this account previously used the handle "@amiVkohli" and parodied India's Virat Kohli. It used both Kohli's name and photo in the account. How did we find out? We observed multiple tweets from this account in October made in the name of Kohli. One of these was an edited photo of Kohli and Anushka Sharma with the flag of Palestine. The post read, "Me and Anushka Sharma Support Palestine. Do you? Retweet this if you also support Palestine." However, the original photo actually featured the Indian national flag and was originally shared by Sharma on Instagram as part of the "Har Ghar Tiranga" campaign on Independence Day 2022. advertisement We also observed individuals responding to some of these posts and tagging the account "@amiVkohli". When we searched for responses to this account on X, we found all posts leading to the Travis Head parody account. We also found that "@amiVkohli" does not exist on X anymore. On the Wayback Machine, we also found a bunch of posts made by "@amiVkohli" in October , all of which can also be found on the Travis Head parody account. Babar Azam's bat According to a Hindustan Times report from June 2023 , Babar Azam gifted Head with a bat during the Australian tour of Pakistan and the UAE in 2022. The report added that Babar and Head share the same bat manufacturer. However, we found no reports regarding the claim that Head used this very bat in the World Cup. Thus, it's clear that a parody account's post went viral as Travis Head's statement. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 23, 2023 20:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of angry cricket fans FALSELY shared as reaction to WC23 defeat
content:
The video is more than one year old and has nothing to do with India's recent defeat in the World Cup final.
Australia's victory against India in the ICC World Cup final broke the hearts of millions of Indians. But, are fans disappointed to such an extent that they are expressing their anger by bashing the posters of Indian players? This is what is being claimed by many who shared a video of people sloganeering against Team India and hitting a TV set with posters of players on it. Indians celebrating Australia's world cup win.😂 #INDvsAUSfinal #INDvsAUS #INDvAUS pic.twitter.com/r5wCUYnpa7 — 🐦‍⬛Temmi 🐦‍⬛ (@Akinloye702) November 20, 2023
Indians celebrating Australia's world cup win.😂 #INDvsAUSfinal #INDvsAUS #INDvAUS pic.twitter.com/r5wCUYnpa7 — 🐦‍⬛Temmi 🐦‍⬛ (@Akinloye702) November 20, 2023
An X user shared the video and wrote, "Indians celebrating Australia's World Cup win," along with hashtags related to the India-Australia final. The video has been shared by many on X  and Facebook  with the same caption. Pakistani news outlet "Bol News" also shared the same on its YouTube channel. An archived version of the viral post can be seen here .
India Today found that the video is more than one year old and has nothing to do with India's recent defeat in the World Cup final. Our probe
With the help of the InVid tool, we found that the video was shared by some Facebook users in November 2022 . A page named "Babar Azam Fan Club" posted the video  on November 12, 2022. Another Facebook user shared it on November 11 , 2022. However, none of these users mentioned the location of the video.Â
India lost to England by 10 wickets  in the semi-final of T20 world cup on November 10, 2022. Most likely, the backlash seen in the video is the fallout from this match.Â
We couldn't independently verify the location of the video, but it is clear that it is not related to the World Cup final because it is at least one year old.Â
It's noteworthy that as per a Dainik Bhaskar report , angry Indian fans broke a TV set in UP's Lakhimpur Kheri after India lost to Australia in World Cup final. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 23, 2023 22:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Iran passport found at Niagara Falls explosion site? Nope, it's a hoax!
content:
No such passport was reportedly recovered from the Niagara Falls explosion site. This image is fabricated.
On November 22, a speeding car crashed in flames on a bridge linking the US and Canada at Niagara Falls, killing two, and sending both countries' governments into high alert over a possible terrorist act. While America's domestic intelligence and security service, the FBI, later concluded that the crash was not related to terrorism, the panic had already led to disinformation on social media.
"BREAKING: Police have IDENTIFIED the driver of the Niagara Falls explosion from a passport found at the scene as 47-year-old Iranian-Canadian YouTuber by the name of Saman Heydari," read a viral post  that contained the photo of a document  with "Islamic Republic of Iran" written on it.
India Today found that no such passport was recovered from the site of the Niagara Falls incident. The document being shared is doctored. The actual image shows an Iranian visa issued in 2015. The photo of US comedian Sam Hyde was digitally added to it. Our Probe
A quick reverse search of the viral image led us to a post on a blog titled "aroundtheworldin800days.com" that contained a similar-looking photo. The blog post run by travellers Andy Smith and Emma Smart described the process of getting an Iranian visa. We compared the visas in the blog with the post and found that it was Emma Smart's Iran visa in the viral post, only with the photo changed, and some of the details redacted.
Reverse-searching the photograph on the visa, we found its GIF version on the GIF library Tenor . Its title was "Sam Hyde Get Well Soon GIF". Subsequently, we found the image in question shared on Hyde's Instagram account on August 20, 2023.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Sam Hyde (@snl)
A post shared by Sam Hyde (@snl)
According to The New York Times , Sam Hyde is a comedian whose name has surfaced in the context of mass shootings to the point that "Sam Hyde is the shooter" has become an identifiable meme.
The US comedian was earlier falsely labelled as the murderer of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and even as the Nashville mass shooter .
At the time of writing this report, the names of the victims of the Niagara Falls accident had not been revealed to the press. According to Robert Restaino, the mayor of Niagara Falls, the victims were a man and his wife from Grand Island, New York, both in their 50s. He, per the New York Times , declined to release their names because the family had not been officially notified.
Thus, it is clear that the photo of an Iranian visa allegedly found at the scene of the crash is a hoax. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 24, 2023 15:01 IST

title: Fact Check: No kidding! This video of Rohit Sharma's daughter talking to reporters has no links to WC23
content:
This video is not recent but shows Samaira giving health updates about Rohit Sharma when he was down with Covid-19 back in 2022.
A heart-warming video of Indian skipper Rohit Sharma's young daughter Samaira is making the rounds on social media. In the clip, Samaira can be seen giving updates about his father to the person shooting her video, as she is heading outside with two women. She can be heard saying that Sharma is in his room, he is "almost positive" and that within a month, "he will laugh". Many shared this video as a recent incident, shot after India's defeat in the World Cup 2023 final.
One person shared the video on Facebook  writing, "Rohit Sharma is still heartbroken," along with a hashtag related to the ICC Cricket World Cup where Australia bested India in the final. Some media outlets like the Navbharat Times and the Times of India also reported on this video , linking it to the World Cup .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from 2022 and shows Samaira giving health updates of her father after he tested positive for Covid-19. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a media report  from June 28, 2022, containing a screenshot of the viral clip. According to it, Rohit Sharma tested positive for Covid-19 ahead of a test match between India and England, that was scheduled to be held in England on July 1, 2022. The viral video of Samaira was shot by reporters who asked her about her father's health. Many people shared this video on social media at the time. #RohitSharma Daughter #samaira Today at #Leicester How cute she is 😍😍 MY FATHER IS TAKING REST IN THE ROOM GOT #covidpositive @ritssajdeh @ImRo45 #ENGvIND @ITGDsports pic.twitter.com/Tbpu0HSUIQ — Krish✊🇮🇳 (@Krishna19348905) June 27, 2022
#RohitSharma Daughter #samaira Today at #Leicester How cute she is 😍😍 MY FATHER IS TAKING REST IN THE ROOM GOT #covidpositive @ritssajdeh @ImRo45 #ENGvIND @ITGDsports pic.twitter.com/Tbpu0HSUIQ — Krish✊🇮🇳 (@Krishna19348905) June 27, 2022
We found several media reports about this incident. On June 26, 2022, the Board of Control for Cricket in India tweeted that the Indian skipper had tested positive for Covid-19 and was quarantined. Sharma reportedly contracted the disease amid India's four-day practice match against Leicestershire .
At the time, Samaira Sharma was reportedly asked about her father's health by reporters in the UK, while she was walking out of a hotel room in Leicester . UPDATE - #TeamIndia Captain Mr Rohit Sharma has tested positive for COVID-19 following a Rapid Antigen Test (RAT) conducted on Saturday. He is currently in isolation at the team hotel and is under the care of the BCCI Medical Team.
— BCCI (@BCCI) June 25, 2022
