It is noteworthy that, Rohit Sharma was indeed papped at the Mumbai Airport with his family post the World Cup on November 20 ( https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/etimes/bollywood/anushka-sharma-virat-kohli-return-to-mumbai-post-world-cup-final/videoshow/105359501.cms ) after India's World Cup final defeat. Along with him, Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma were also spotted at the time. However, neither the players nor their families spoke to reporters.
Hence, it is more than clear that an old video of Rohit Sharma's daughter was falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Nov 24, 2023 17:44 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral clip of animal dung dumped at McDonald's NOT related to Israel-Hamas conflict
content:
The video shows a protest by French farmers against fast food chains for importing foreign meat.
Fast-food giant McDonald's is facing international boycott calls following its Israeli franchise providing free meals to members of the Israeli military. Amid this, a video showing a truck unloading animal dung in front of a McDonald's outlet was widely shared on social media. Posts accompanying the video claimed that the global boycott campaign prompted hundreds of pro-Palestinian supporters in France to carry out this action.
An X post containing the video  read, "Protests have taken place in France by dumping animal dung in front of a McDonald's branch supporting Israel." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video is unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. It shows dissatisfied French farmers protesting against fast food giants, especially McDonald's and Burger King for not sourcing enough beef from local farmers. Our Probe
Conducting a keyword search, we found a report by Ouest-France, a French daily , dated November 24. The report, containing a still from the viral video, highlighted that 150 farmers from Haute-Saône in France dumped manure in front of McDonald's and Burger King outlets in Vesoul. The protest was organised to denounce fast-food giants for their inadequate sourcing of French meat.
It further said that the farmers, represented by the Departmental Federation of Farmers' Unions (FDSEA), criticised fast-food chains for extensively importing foreign meat — approximately 50 per cent — to produce their hamburgers.
We also found a press note released by FDSEA on Facebook . It emphasised that France has lost nearly one million cows in seven years, leading to an incessant decline in the number of animal farms. The post also featured images of disgruntled farmers lining up with their tractors to transport dung to the protest site, including a still of the red truck dumping manure outside a McDonald's as seen in the viral video.
Reports also noted that the farmers sought support and urged large fast-food chains to purchase the meat from local sources. Burger King responded with a press statement acknowledging that only half of the beef served in its outlets in France is currently of French origin. The company pledged to increase local sourcing of beef and chicken to 60 per cent by 2024.
Other reports corroborating the context of the viral video can be seen her e  and here .
Thus, the video showing a protest by angry French farmers was falsely shared as reaction to the fast food company supporting the Israeli army. Â - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Nov 26, 2023 21:45 IST

title: Fact Check: 5-year-old pic FALSELY shared as slain Indian army men in Rajouri
content:
This image dates back to December 2018, when the Indian army foiled Pakistan's Border Action Team's intrusion attempt.
On November 23, two Lashkar-e-Taiba members were killed in a gunfight in Rajouri's Kalakote in Jammu and Kashmir. Five Indian soldiers lost their lives in this operation, including two captains.Â
A disturbing photo  of two uniformed men lying motionless on the ground is now being shared, suggesting these two Indian army personnel were among those who lost their lives in the Rajouri encounter.
An X user shared the photo and wrote. "At least 11 commandos including a Major and a Captain from 9 Para SF Indian Army have been killed in the ongoing attack in Rajouri sector." The archived version of this post can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the image in question is related to a 2018 incident, during which the Indian army foiled an intrusion attempt by Pakistan.Â
Using reverse search, we found that the viral image was used in a WION News report from December 31, 2018, about how the Indian army had averted an infiltration bid by Pakistan's Border Action Team along the LoC in Kashmir's Naugam Sector on December 30, 2018. In this report, the viral image can be seen at the 16-second mark.Â
At this point in the video, it is stated: "From the bodies of these two who have been killed, the Indian army says that they are Pakistan's regular soldiers and they have been killed. Now they are making an offer to the Pakistan authorities to take these bodies back." Â
This image was also used in a Zee news article ( https://zeenews.india.com/india/indian-army-identifies-pakistani-soldier-among-intruders-killed-along-loc-2167000.html ) and video report ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gwEOE7uBAWc ).Â
ANI too had tweeted about this incident and said that Quadcopters were used to locate the dead bodies of suspected Pakistani soldiers in this incident. Â Quadcopters were used to locate the dead bodies of suspected Pakistani soldiers, who were gunned down by the Indian Army while foiling an attempt by Pakistani Border Action Team (BAT) to carry out an attack across the LoC (Pic source: Army) pic.twitter.com/pHLatVDtX7 — ANI (@ANI) December 31, 2018
Quadcopters were used to locate the dead bodies of suspected Pakistani soldiers, who were gunned down by the Indian Army while foiling an attempt by Pakistani Border Action Team (BAT) to carry out an attack across the LoC (Pic source: Army) pic.twitter.com/pHLatVDtX7 — ANI (@ANI) December 31, 2018
As per another report in India TV News at the time, the Indian army had accused Pakistan of providing support to the intruders.Â
Thus, it's clear that a five-year-old was falsely shared in the context of the recent encounter in Rajouri. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 26, 2023 21:59 IST

title: Fact Check: This young Palestinian girl was NOT imprisoned by Israel
content:
This video does not show a young prisoner but a girl who was separated from her mother during an Israeli attack in Gaza.
A group of 24 women and 15 teenage boys detained by Israel were released from prisons in exchange for a group of hostages held by Hamas on November 25. The bus that transported these detainees was welcomed by a sea of jubilant Palestinian supporters.Â
Following this, an emotional video of a reunion between a child and a mother went viral on social media. Those sharing the clip claimed that this was a Palestinian child who was imprisoned in Israel.Â
One person shared the video on Facebook writing, "Are you serious? That little one was in jail? It's hard to believe such a young child could face such harsh realities. Situations like these compel us to question the justice systems and their impacts on the most vulnerable," along with hashtags such as "free Palestine".
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows the reunion of a mother and her child in a hospital after they were separated during an Israeli attack.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a tweet containing an extended, black-and-white version of the viral clip. According to this tweet by Al Jazeera, this video showed a reunion between a mother and her daughter in the Nasser Hospital of Khan Yunis, a city in southern Gaza. The date stamp on the video read November 23. وجدتها حيّة في المستشفى.. مشهد مؤثر لأم فلسطينية تعانق ابنتها بحرارة في مستشفى ناصر بخان يونس #الجزيرة_مباشر #غزة #غزة_لحظة_بلحظة pic.twitter.com/p3JSjnj8MV — الجزيرة مباشر (@ajmubasher) November 24, 2023 We then found another video of the incident shared on the Facebook page of Al Hadath, a news outlet that's part of the international Arabic news television network Al-Arabiya TV. The caption, translated from Arabic to English, read: "A Palestinian mother eagerly hugs her daughter after she survived an Israeli raid near their home in Khan Younis." In the video, we could first see the viral portion of the mother hugging her child. This was followed by an interview of Muhammad Zuhdi Al-Dabiki, a resident of Khan Yunis.Â
وجدتها حيّة في المستشفى.. مشهد مؤثر لأم فلسطينية تعانق ابنتها بحرارة في مستشفى ناصر بخان يونس #الجزيرة_مباشر #غزة #غزة_لحظة_بلحظة pic.twitter.com/p3JSjnj8MV — الجزيرة مباشر (@ajmubasher) November 24, 2023
We then found another video of the incident shared on the Facebook page of Al Hadath, a news outlet that's part of the international Arabic news television network Al-Arabiya TV. The caption, translated from Arabic to English, read: "A Palestinian mother eagerly hugs her daughter after she survived an Israeli raid near their home in Khan Younis." In the video, we could first see the viral portion of the mother hugging her child. This was followed by an interview of Muhammad Zuhdi Al-Dabiki, a resident of Khan Yunis.Â
According to the subtitles, the resident recalled the moment bomb shells exploded in his neighbourhood, where this girl was separated from her mother. She was terrified but an ambulance helped her and then she found her mother at a hospital.Â
There are several videos of Palestinians reuniting with their families post their release by Israel. However, the young girl in the viral video is not one of those people. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Nov 26, 2023 23:46 IST

title: Fact Check: This video shows a 2021 brawl in Dublin, NOT recent riots in Irish capital
content:
The video is from 2021 and shows a brawl involving some men harassing a pregnant woman, unrelated to the recent rioting.
Riots erupted in Dublin's city centre after a knife attack left four people injured. Rumours about the perpetrator's nationality  fueled tensions online, consequently leading to far-right groups  causing a rampage in the city. Amid this unrest, a video went viral on social media, purportedly showing waiters in the Irish capital fighting "fascists" from the streets during the recent turmoil.
A Facebook user sharing the viral video , wrote, "You're watching Dublin waiters kicking fascists off the streets of our city. This is how we do it, comrades. Let's speak to the bastards in the language they understand." An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video is two years old and unrelated to the recent disturbances in Dublin. OUR PROBE
Running a reverse image search on keyframes of the video led us to media reports from June 2021. These reports  detailed a fight that occurred on South William Street between restaurant staff and four young men. The clash resulted in injuries to one of the waiters when one of the gang members swung a bottle, leading to the arrest of three men for rampaging in central Dublin.
A DublinLive , an anonymous source said that the fight ensued when a group pestered a pregnant woman, blowing cannabis smoke in her face.
The Irish Times reported that Ryan Dowling, a 20-year-old Dublin man with 16 previous convictions, received a 10-month prison sentence for his role in the brawl. The altercation began when a couple celebrating their anniversary was harassed by a group of men, including Dowling. The restaurant staff intervened, leading to the group throwing furniture and beer cans at them.
Thus, it's evident that an old video showing a brawl between unruly young men and restaurant staff, flared by harassment of a pregnant woman, is being falsely linked with the recent riots in the Irish capital. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 27, 2023 15:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Yemeni militants burnt Israeli ship? No, this 2021 video is from Sri Lanka
content:
This video is from May 2021 and shows MV X-Press Pearl, the Singapore-registered container ship that caught fire near the Sri Lankan coast.
Amid emerging reports detailing the seizure of a cargo ship in the Red Sea by Yemen's Houthi militants, a video of a burning cargo vessel has been shared by many on social media.
People sharing this video on Facebook asserted that the container ship named "Calandra" or "Kalandra", purportedly owned by the Israeli company ZIM, being set ablaze in the Indian Ocean by the Yemeni armed forces.Â
Similar posts were shared on Instagram and X as well. The archived version of such a post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from May 2021 and shows a cargo vessel carrying a consignment of chemicals near Sri Lanka that caught fire.Â
We conducted a keyword search to verify if Houthi militants from Yemen had been linked to any recent incidents of a cargo ship fire, but our search yielded no relevant results.
After conducting a reverse search on keyframes from the viral video, we found the same footage in a Russian news report dated May 25, 2021. The report indicated that the incident occurred near the port of Colombo, the capital of Sri Lanka. The report mentioned that on May 20, 2021, a fire was detected on a cargo ship carrying a consignment of chemicals. On May 25, an explosion occurred, leading to a massive blaze. Subsequent advanced keyword searches based on the report led us to a press release by the Indian Press Information Bureau stating that the Indian Government deployed three of its ships — Samudra Prahari, Vaibhav, and Vajrato — to combat the fire. The release also highlighted that MV X-Press Pearl was transporting 1,486 containers of nitric acid and other hazardous chemicals. We also found similar visuals of the accident on various other news reports and Instagram accounts from May 25, 2021.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Marine lords ⚓⚓ (@marine_lords) According to a Hindustan Times report dated May 30, 2021, no casualties were reported as the crew had already evacuated the vessel, and authorities successfully brought the fire under control in the meantime. The ship, however, sank a couple of days later during an attempt to tow the vessel to deeper waters. advertisement MV X-Press Pearl, the Singapore-registered container ship fiasco not only resulted in a monetary loss of millions but also caused long-term environmental damage to the Indian Ocean around the Sri Lankan coast. An editorial in the Maritime Executive highlighted that the fire was attributed to the leakage of nitric acid, which was inadequately or incorrectly packed or stowed. Nitric acid is known for its corrosive, toxic, and flammable substance, and the ship was carrying 25 tonnes of it. Therefore, it is clear that a two-year-old video was falsely linked to the capture of an Israeli cargo ship by Yemeni militants. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Nov 27, 2023 16:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Communal clash in Karnataka? Nope, this video is from Maharashtra
content:
This video is from a communal clash in Ahmednagar, Maharashtra. The clash was over disputed land housing both a temple and a dargah.
Ahead of the November 30 Telangana Assembly polls, a video of an alleged religious scuffle  has been widely shared online. In it, a loud argument can be seen taking place, before it escalates into a mob attacking men dressed in saffron. Per those sharing the video, it showed Muslim aggression against a Hindu gathering in Congress-ruled Karnataka.Â
"See how Hindus are being beaten to death in Karnataka for performing bhajan in front of the temple in the month of Kartika. If Congress comes to power in Telangana and not BJP, Hindus will be beaten to death by Muslims in the state," reads the Telugu text accompanying one such post  on Facebook.
India Today found that the video shows a land dispute between Hindus and Muslims in Maharashtra's Ahmednagar district. It is not related to Karnataka. Our Probe
Responding to the viral video on X, many pointed out that the people in the video were speaking in Marathi. Some also asserted that this incident happened in the Guha village of Ahmednagar in Maharashtra.
Taking a cue from this, we ran a keyword search in Marathi and found a report in News18 Lokmat . The report contained, aside from bits of the viral clip, footage shot from various angles. According to the report published on November 13, 2023, the video was from the Kanifnath Mandir in the Guha village of Ahmednagar. A screenshot from the viral video was also featured in a report in Dainik Bhaskar's Divya Marathi. As outlined in this report, contested land on which the Kanifnath temple and a dargah are situated in close proximity was at the centre of the conflict. Ownership claims over this land have been asserted by both Hindus and Muslims, and the matter is currently awaiting resolution in a local court.Â
A screenshot from the viral video was also featured in a report in Dainik Bhaskar's Divya Marathi. As outlined in this report, contested land on which the Kanifnath temple and a dargah are situated in close proximity was at the centre of the conflict. Ownership claims over this land have been asserted by both Hindus and Muslims, and the matter is currently awaiting resolution in a local court.Â
On November 13, on the occasion of Somvati Amavasya, a group of Hindus reportedly entered the Kanifnath Devasthan and conducted religious rituals. Their use of loudspeakers during these rituals drew objections from Muslims in the locality, resulting in a clash.
Reportedly, upon receiving information about the incident, Srirampur sub-divisional police officer Basavaraj Shivpuje and Rahuri police inspector Dhananjay Jadhav entered the incident site with a large contingent of police.
According to a Hindustan Times report , Rakesh Ola, Ahmednagar superintendent of police also confirmed the communal clash was over disputed land. Quoting Basavraj Shivpuje, the report also said an FIR had been registered against 124 people in the matter. Four people were injured in the incident.
It is hence clear that the video in question is from a communal clash in Maharashtra and not related to Karnataka. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Nov 27, 2023 21:45 IST

title: Fact Check: These AREN'T Black Friday shoppers! Looting video from George Floyd protests
content:
This 2020 video from Chicago shows looting during protests following the police killing of George Floyd.
Black Friday, the Friday after Thanksgiving in the United States that traditionally marks the start of the Christmas shopping season, has over the years witnessed violence between shoppers. A video has now emerged on social media that shows a group of black men and women looting a Nike store. Allegedly, it showed  shoppers ransacking a store on Black Friday, which fell on November 24 this year.
"This Black Friday discount must have been amazing. Look at all these satisfied customers," reads the text accompanying one such video  shared on X. This Black Friday discount must have been amazing. Look at all these satisfied customers! pic.twitter.com/9wpsw6FB5M — James Woods (@RealJamesWoods) November 27, 2023
This Black Friday discount must have been amazing. Look at all these satisfied customers! pic.twitter.com/9wpsw6FB5M — James Woods (@RealJamesWoods) November 27, 2023
India Today Fact Check found that the video in question is more than three years old. It is from protests surrounding the 2020 police killing of George Floyd in the US. Our Probe
With the help of a keyword search, we found the same video ( https://twitter.com/BenPopeCST/status/1266887022024757249?lang=en ) shared on X by a Chicago-based journalist Ben Pope on May 31, 2020. The accompanying text states, "Nike store on Michigan Ave smashed and completely looted." Nike store on Michigan Ave smashed and completely looted pic.twitter.com/IRZc4FuDBO — Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) May 31, 2020
Nike store on Michigan Ave smashed and completely looted pic.twitter.com/IRZc4FuDBO — Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) May 31, 2020
The video was also shared by Russian state media RT  on May 31, 2020. According to a report published by RT , on that very day, a flagship Nike store in Michigan Avenue, Chicago, was destroyed and looted during a protest surrounding the death of George Floyd.
Floyd, an African-American, was killed on May 25, 2020, by policemen who knelt on his neck for almost ten minutes while arresting him for allegedly using a counterfeit bill. Following his death, massive anti-police protests erupted all across the US.
Several other shops in downtown Chicago including  Zara, CVS, Walgreens, and Neiman Marcus were also reportedly  looted and ransacked during this protest. Then Chicago mayor Lori Lightfoot condemned the looting at the time, and said: "When you or anyone else behaves in this way, we all lose by giving the very same forces of oppression we are fighting against the false validation that they crave."
It is hence clear that the video in question is years old and does not show Black Friday shoppers looting a Nike store. - Ends Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Nov 28, 2023 14:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral NDTV poll predicting Congress victory in Telangana is FAKE
content:
The viral screenshot is photoshopped. NDTV has called it out on its social media.
With the Telangana Assembly elections just days away, social media has been inundated with myriad opinion polls projecting which party might rule the southern state. An NDTV chart , purportedly showing outcomes projected by multiple opinion polls, has gone viral.Â
The alleged opinion poll forecasts a landslide victory for the Congress party. Congress supporters and even party spokesperson Supriya Shinate  shared the figures projected in this infographic.
A Facebook user while sharing the NDTV chart, wrote , "BREAKING NOW - NDTV Poll of Polls gives Majority to Congress in TELANGANA ." An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral screenshot is fake. NDTV's Poll of Polls is actually an exit poll that is released once the voting concludes. OUR PROBE
A keyword search for NDTV's Poll of Polls for the Telangana assembly elections in 2023, yielded no results, raising suspicions about the chart's authenticity. A thorough advanced search on X using relevant keywords also failed to reveal any such an opinion poll. We also scrutinised NDTV's recent posts on X and found that the media organisation had explicitly debunked the viral screenshot, labelling it as "Fake."
In a tweet, NDTV clarified , "Fake News Alert | NDTV has not carried any poll of polls for Telangana 2023. Please don't spread fake news."
Contrary to its claims of being an opinion poll, Poll of Polls  is an exit poll, which is generally announced immediately after the conclusion of the last phase of voting. However, the alleged poll by NDTV went viral two days before Telangana is scheduled to vote — November 30 .
It's pertinent to note that the Election Commission from time to time issues notifications prohibiting the conduct and publication of exit polls from the commencement of polls until half an hour after it is over.
In conclusion, NDTV's alleged opinion poll did not project a sweeping victory for the Congress party in Telangana, as the viral graphic is fake. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 28, 2023 19:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of interracial brawl goes viral after Dublin riots
content:
This video dates back to September 2016 and shows a confrontation between two Nigerian tenants and Irish landlords.
A recent knife attack in Dublin sparked Ireland's worst anti-immigrant violence  in years, with rioters clashing with police, vandalising property, and looting across the Irish capital. Amid these tensions, a video of a clash between two black men and a group of white people was widely shared.Â
The video  was shared with captions, "In Dublin, cultural enrichers threaten native Irish with sticks. They're in charge now." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video dates back to September 2016 and is unrelated to the ongoing developments in Dublin.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report from Nigeria that featured a screenshot from the video. Published on May 19, 2017, the report noted that both black men seen in this video were from Nigeria.Â
According to the report, a brawl broke after the Nigerians were pushed out of their home by the white landlords in the United Kingdom, making it clear that the incident is unrelated to the recent riots in Dublin.Â
A subsequent search with relevant keywords, however, led us to a news report from the Irish Independent dated September 13, 2016. This report stated that the incident occurred in South Circular Road, Dublin. The owner allegedly paid a sum of money to the renters to reach a deal for them to leave. But when the owner arrived to vacate the house, the occupants refused to move out. Afterwards, a confrontation escalated into a violent physical clash between the parties, prompting the owner to call the police. The situation further intensified as a wheelie bin was set ablaze, necessitating the intervention of the fire brigade. Two individuals were hospitalised due to smoke inhalation. The police, however, made no arrests and warned both sides to keep the peace and the occupants agreed to leave the damaged house a couple of days later. An extended version of this video can be seen below. Therefore, it is evident that a seven-year-old incident was shared as a recent one against the backdrop of the recent riots in Dublin. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 29, 2023 00:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of rally against Nupur Sharma shared as NIT Srinagar protests
content:
This video shows 2022 protests against Nupur Sharma for making hurtful comments about Prophet Muhammad.
On November 28, protests reportedly erupted at the National Institute of Technology, Srinagar . Hundreds of students took to the streets of Srinagar over a non-local student allegedly making a social media post against Prophet Muhammad . The student in question has reportedly been sent home on leave. According to a police spokesperson, a case has been filed.Â
Now, a video making the rounds on social media  shows a number of people protesting, holding banners reading "Our Prophet, Our Honour", and chanting slogans. In the video, a man can be heard threatening people . Those saying the video claimed it showed the recent protests in Srinagar. The archived version of such a claim can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video has nothing to do with the recent NIT Srinagar protests. It dates back to 2022 when former Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Nupur Sharma made controversial remarks about Prophet Muhammad. Our ProbeÂ
In our investigation, we observed the watermark "Mufeed Hilal" in the clip. Using this, we searched for this person on X and found that his profile mentions that he is a journalist based in Kashmir . On his X account, we found a post from June 11, 2022, which contained photos that resembled the viral video. Banners as well as protestors in this post can also be seen in the video. Peaceful protest held in Downtown Area of District Srinagar over the derogatory remarks made by BJP spokesperson against Prophet Muhammad ï·º. Photos 📸 @Mufeed_hilal pic.twitter.com/q8a7qZEoKQ — Mufeed Hilal (@Mufeed_hilal) June 11, 2022
Peaceful protest held in Downtown Area of District Srinagar over the derogatory remarks made by BJP spokesperson against Prophet Muhammad ï·º. Photos 📸 @Mufeed_hilal pic.twitter.com/q8a7qZEoKQ — Mufeed Hilal (@Mufeed_hilal) June 11, 2022
We then searched for Mufeed's accounts on other social media platforms and found that on Instagram, he had shared the viral video on June 11, 2022 .
The video's caption said, "‎Peaceful protest held in Downtown Area of District Srinagar over the derogatory remarks made by BJP spokesperson against Prophet Muhammad". This makes it clear that it is more than a year old video and not from recent NIT protests.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Mufeed Hilal (@mufeed_hilal)
A post shared by Mufeed Hilal (@mufeed_hilal)
In 2022, Nupur Sharma irked Muslims after she made derogatory remarks against Prophet Muhammed during a TV debate , which drew a massive backlash in India, and from several Gulf countries as well.Â
Therefore, it is evident that an old video from protests against Nupur Sharma in Srinagar was falsely shared as the recent NIT Srinagar protests. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Nov 29, 2023 21:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Video shows Ganesh Chaturthi festival in Gujarat, NOT Congress rally
content:
This video is from Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations in Gujarat's Godhra.
A day before Telangana goes to polls, a video of a lively crowd dancing to a DJ on the road began making the rounds on social media. Allegedly, this was an election campaign organised by the Congress party in the state. The video's backdrop includes an election song for Telangana's Congress leader and Member of Parliament, Revanth Reddy.
"Rallies by Congress are better than major music performers performing live!!! #TelanganaElections2023," reads the text along with one such video .
The video was also shared by an unverified Instagram account  in the name of Revanth Reddy, which has more than 33,000 followers.Â
The archived version of such posts can be seen here  and here .
India Today found that the video in question is from a Ganesh Chaturthi celebration in Gujarat's Godhra. The audio in the clip was changed. Our Probe
Upon conducting a reverse search using the video's keyframes and relevant keywords, we found an identical video of better quality with a different song playing in the background, posted on an Instagram page named " DJ Hiiren " on September 19.
It was shared with hashtags like "Godhra City" and "Godhra Ganesh Festival". This date aligns with Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations observed between September 18 and 28 this year.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Dhamo Rajput (@mr_dhamu_9173) In this video, we observed "Guru Kripa" written in Gujarati on one of the shops. Additionally, in a different frame of the same video, a huge idol of Ganesha was also visible. This page also featured numerous other videos and photos from the same location. We then searched for "Guru Kripa'' in Godhra, a municipality in Gujarat, and found the Google Street View  of the same road. As per Google Maps, the street in the video is Panjarapole Road in Godhra, Gujarat. It is, thus, clear that the video does not show the Congress party's election campaign in Telangana. - Ends (With inputs from Manjeet Shah) Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Nov 29, 2023 23:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Old brawl video over luggage space FALSELY shared with communal angle
content:
The viral video is from April 2021 and shows a brawl that broke out over overhead luggage space on a Tunisia-bound flight.
A video of a vicious brawl in an aeroplane has gone viral. In it, a male passenger can be seen grabbing a woman's hair, pulling her backwards, and punching her. Many who shared the clip on social media claimed that the man attacked the woman for not wearing a hijab.Â
One Facebook user wrote while sharing the video , "Avoid Turkey and Turkish Airlines. An American female passenger who was travelling in a Turkish airliner was caught by Muslim men by her hair, and they started beating her because she was not wearing a hijab." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video has no communal angle. The brawl was caused by a disagreement over overhead luggage space. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post from April 12, 2021. In the post, the same video was shared with the caption, "Flight attendants try to break up a fight between passengers over the seat."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Passenger Shaming (@passengershaming)
A post shared by Passenger Shaming (@passengershaming)
Taking a clue from this, we searched about the incident using relevant keywords  and found many news reports that contained the viral video in them. According to reports, the video was filmed on Tunisair flight TU216 at Istanbul Airport, Turkey. Tunisair is the national airline of Tunisia.Â
Reportedly, a disagreement over overhead luggage space was the reason behind the altercation  onboard the Tunisia-bound flight. The incident reportedly delayed the flight by five hours. According to the Daily Mail , the shocking incident occurred on April 10. According to the Independent , some passengers had allegedly brought too much carry-on luggage and refused to pay extra to store it in the cabin. "An investigation has been opened," an airline spokesperson told reporters at the time, adding that the passengers who started the incident could be prosecuted. We also found the video on The Sun's YouTube channel  as well, uploaded more than two years ago. According to this video report, too, the brawl was caused by overhead luggage space. Thus, it is more than clear to say that a video of a two-year-old brawl was falsely shared with a communal spin. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Dec 1, 2023 22:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Man being pushed off building is ISIS execution in Iraq, NOT Hamas
content:
The video shows ISIS executions of men accused of homosexuality.
Amid the Israel-Hamas conflict, social media has become a cesspool of disinformation in the form of old or unrelated videos and photos with inaccurate claims. One such video making the rounds shows  a horrifying scene of a man being thrown off a building. Allegedly, the video shows Hamas executing its people.
A user, sharing the video on X, wrote , "This is who all you university and college students and others are supporting. Hamas executes people by throwing them off the roof of a building." An archived version of the post can be seen here .
However, India Today found that the video doesn't pertain to either Palestine or Hamas. Our Probe
Conducting a reverse search on the keyframes of the viral video led us to a slew of media reports from July 2015, featuring clearer stills from the gruesome footage. The Mirror reported on the video  and noted that it showed the execution of men accused of homosexuality by ISIS in Fallujah, Iraq.
The report further explained that the victims were tied up and blindfolded before being taken to the edge of a building. Four men were thrown to their deaths for their perceived sexual orientations.
The Daily Mail also reported it as an ISIS execution  of men accused of homosexuality in the Iraqi province of Fallujah.Â
More reports further substantiating the context of the video and confirming the identity of the executioners can be seen here  and here .
Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with either Palestine or Hamas. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Dec 3, 2023 16:40 IST

title: Fact Check: Russian train bombing? No, this is an old video of a gas pipeline blast
content:
This is an old video of a gas pipeline explosion that took place in Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia, back in March 2023.
A freight train carrying fuel reportedly caught fire on November 29, while travelling through the Severomuysky Tunnel on the Baikal Amur Mainline, in Buryatia, Russia. A second explosion hours later reportedly  hit another train carrying fuel while travelling  over the nearby Devil's Bridge.Â
According to Ukrainian media, the twin train bombing was a sabotage attack by the Security Service of Ukraine , aimed to disrupt a railroad line that serves as a key conduit for trade between Russia and China.
Now a video of a huge fire  allegedly from the train bombings in Russia has gone viral. The clip shows people witnessing the flames blazing at a distance. One person shared the video on Facebook writing , "Russia's main link to China 'paralysed' after tunnel 'sabotage' an explosion occurred in the Severomuysky railway tunnel in Bashkortostan during the passage of a fuel train, leading to the blockage of the tunnel and the suspension of over ten freight trains." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this is an old video of a gas pipeline explosion in Russia's Sverdlovsk Oblast back in March 2023.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a media report  containing a screenshot of the viral video. Per the report, there was an explosion at a gas pipeline in Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia.Â
Reportedly, part of the Yamburg-Yelets 1 gas pipeline caught fire during repairs in the district of Pelym. However, casualties or disruption to supplies were not reported. Another video of the incident , shot from a different angle, was shared by Daily Global on March 30.
We then found several news reports about this incident. According to Reuters , depressurisation of the Yamburg-Elets gas pipeline occurred near the village of Pelym on March 29. The gas pipeline section was then turned off for repairs, during which it caught fire.Â
The head of the local administration, Shahid Aliyev, confirmed to Russian media outlets  that there were no people at the scene and hence, no casualties. The reports also carried another video of the explosion that was shot by a witness . Explosion and fire at the gas pipeline in the north of Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia, town of Pelym. Commentary by the witness. pic.twitter.com/G7u2YHin1g — WarTranslated (Dmitri) (@wartranslated) March 29, 2023
Explosion and fire at the gas pipeline in the north of Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia, town of Pelym. Commentary by the witness. pic.twitter.com/G7u2YHin1g — WarTranslated (Dmitri) (@wartranslated) March 29, 2023
It is thus clear that this video shows an old explosion in a gas pipeline and has no links to the recent twin train bombing in Russia. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Dec 3, 2023 19:46 IST

title: Fact Check: Philippines earthquake was powerful, but this video is from Japan
content:
This video, dated February 14, 2021, was captured in Chiba City, Japan, during the occurrence of a 7.3-magnitude earthquake in Fukushima.
On the night of December 2, a powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake rocked the Philippines , claiming one life and causing numerous injuries. In the aftermath, images and videos from affected areas began circulating on social media.
In one such video , captured inside a bathroom in a high-rise building, foamy water splashes could be seen spilling out of a bathtub amid the intense tremors. While sharing this video on X, people asserted it was from the recent earthquakes in the Philippines. An earthquake with a magnitude of 7.6 occurred in the Philippines. A Tsunami warning was issued after the earthquake. Houses were destroyed in some cities. The country went into emergency #earthquakes #news #Philippines #Philippines #tsunami #earthquake #Philippinesearthquake pic.twitter.com/yQqSTCltx9 — DINESH SHARMA (@medineshsharma) December 2, 2023
An earthquake with a magnitude of 7.6 occurred in the Philippines. A Tsunami warning was issued after the earthquake. Houses were destroyed in some cities. The country went into emergency #earthquakes #news #Philippines #Philippines #tsunami #earthquake #Philippinesearthquake pic.twitter.com/yQqSTCltx9 — DINESH SHARMA (@medineshsharma) December 2, 2023
Others shared this clip on Facebook with captions like, "The Philippines was shaken near Bislig City, Surigao del Sur, Caraga, by an earthquake of magnitude 7.5. Power can be seen by water spilling out of the tub." The archived version of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is more than two years old and from Japan, unrelated to the Philippines earthquake.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Ukrainian news report dated February 15, 2021 , that featured similar screenshots. Â
According to the report, this incident occurred on February 13, 2021, when a 7.3-magnitude earthquake hit Japan's Fukushima and Miyagi regions. The report states that the quake was also felt in Tokyo, and a woman uploaded the viral video on TikTok.
A subsequent search using relevant keywords enabled us to locate one of the earliest versions of this video, uploaded to a YouTube channel on February 16, 2021. This made it clear that the video is unrelated to the recent earthquake in the Philippines.
On February 23, 2021, Weather.com showcased this video , clarifying its origin in Chiba City, Japan, and confirming that it was recorded during the Fukushima earthquake. Additionally, on February 14, 2021, the BBC reported that despite the intense tremors in Tokyo, the weather department refrained from issuing a tsunami warning.
Therefore, it is abundantly clear that an old and unrelated video from Japan was presented as a recent occurrence during the Philippines earthquake. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Dec 4, 2023 20:59 IST

title: Fact Check: This video doesn't show Palestinian influencer Mr FAFO abandoning Gaza for Qatar
content:
This video shows Al-Jafarawi's January 2023 Qatar trip via Egypt, months before the ongoing conflict began.
As the Israel-Gaza conflict continues to unfold, a video featuring Saleh Al-Jafarawi, a well-known Palestinian Instagram influencer and activist, known for documenting Israel siege of Gaza, has gone viral. Those sharing the viral video claimed that Al-Jafarawi, known as "Mr FAFO", is currently in Qatar, "living his best life".Â
Some alluded to his connections with Hamas. And some also accused Al-Jafarawi of being part of "Pallywood", a derogatory term referring to an alleged industry of staging or play-acting scenes of violence and repression of Palestinians to gain global sympathy.
An X user shared the video, stating, "He's done it again! Mr. Pallywood (aka #MrFAFO) has turned up in...Qatar. After posing in a dozen different jobs, adopting all the orphans in Gaza, dying and coming back to life more times than I can count, he is now living his best life in Qatar." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video shows Saleh Aljafarawi's January 2023 trip to Qatar via Eqypt — months before the current Israel-Gaza conflict that began on October 7.
Conducting a reverse image search, we found an extended version of the video , uploaded to Aljafarawi's YouTube channel on January 22, 2023.  The description accompanying the video reads in Arabic, "The action and the adventures begin. Today I am in Qatar for a very big reason for me." The video documents Jafarawi's trip to Qatar via Egypt. In a previous video , he explained the procedure he underwent to cross to the Egyptian side through the Rafah crossing.
 The description accompanying the video reads in Arabic, "The action and the adventures begin. Today I am in Qatar for a very big reason for me." The video documents Jafarawi's trip to Qatar via Egypt. In a previous video , he explained the procedure he underwent to cross to the Egyptian side through the Rafah crossing.
Notably, Al-Jafarawi has been continually documenting Israeli bombings and life in Gaza since the war's onset. His social media accounts affirm his presence in his home country.

content:

title: Fact Check: Old videos from Europe, Myanmar falsely shared as Cyclone Michaung
content:
Both these videos are unrelated to, and predate Cyclone Michaung, which hit south India's coastal areas.
Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh are on high alert with severe storms as Cyclone Michaung hit the southern India coast on December 5. Rains have caused at least 12 deaths  so far.
Many videos, allegedly showing the cyclone in action, have since been widely shared online. Not all of them, of course, are authentic. In this article, we shall examine two such videos. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story First Video This clip shows huge and powerful waves hitting the shores of a city. Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "These terrible waves are from Five Furlong Road, Velachery. Be alert. Be careful." The archived version of this post can be seen here . A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led to many news reports from November 2023 that contained the video or its screengrabs. According to reports, this video was from southern Russia  and showed hurricane winds and massive floods hitting Russia's Black Sea coast during a severe storm in November 2023. Around 500,000 residents in various parts of Crimea and 2,600 more in Sevastopol were reportedly left without electricity. Therefore, it is more than clear that a video from Europe was falsely shared as Cyclone Michaung. Second Video In this video , strong winds coupled with rainfall could be seen dangerously swaying trees and electricity poles. Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "After massive earthquake shook #Philippines, now warning of a cyclone is issued for southern states of India. Looks like nature's reckoning is onto something." An archived version of this can be seen here . We reverse-searched frames from the video along with relevant keywords and found the viral clip in a video report on CBS Mornings official's  X account. As per the report, this video showed Cyclone Mocha when it made landfall in Myanmar and Bangladesh in May 2023. We then found the same video on YouTube, shared by Global News. This video report noted that the viral clip was from Sittwe, Myanmar, and was shot on May 14, 2023. Thus it's clear that this video, as well, has nothing to do with Cyclone Michaung. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Dec 5, 2023 23:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Chennai soaking fun? No, this video is old not from Cyclone Michaung
content:
This video has no links to Cyclone Michaung. It is a 2021 video from flood-hit Kanyakumari.
At least 17 people have reportedly died in Chennai as Cyclone Michaung  ravaged the city and three neighbouring districts . Now, a video of people seemingly playing around in a waterlogged area  is making the round on social media.Â
In it, people can be seen doing push-ups and sliding on flooded streets. Those sharing the clip alleged that this was shot in Chennai during Cyclone Michaung . One person shared the video on Facebook , writing, "Peoples in social media: pray for Chennai.
Meanwhile, in Chennai people actually are #strangethings". The archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is neither recent nor is it from Chennai. It is an old video from Kanyakumari.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a YouTube video  from November 15, 2021, containing multiple clips of people enjoying themselves in waterlogged areas. The video featured people playing volleyball on a flooded ground, along with the video in question showing people doing pushups and sliding in a waterlogged street.
This proves that this clip predates the landfall of Cyclone Michaung in Chennai. Additionally, the description of the video stated that these clips were from Kanyakumari. We then found a report by News 18 , dated November 15, 2021, containing the viral video. According to it, multiple clips of youngsters turning the flooded streets of Kanyakumari into a water park surfaced on social media as heavy rainfall battered the state of Tamil Nadu. The report carried posts by the Facebook account that shared the visuals of people in Kanyakumari having fun amid the flood , including that of people sliding in the waterlogged streets . The caption stated the location was Anjugramam in the Kanyakumari district . Per reports, heavy rainfall hit different parts of Tamil Nadu , with 14 places in Kanyakumari recording rainfall of over 100mm within 24 hours  on November 13, 2021. Chief Minister MK Stalin also visited the rain-affected areas in Kanyakumari and took stock of the situation on November 16, 2021 . It is thus, clear that old videos from a 2021 flood in Kanyakumari were falsely shared as visuals from Chennai amid Cyclone Michaung. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Dec 6, 2023 20:18 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT brawl inside flight, this scripted video was created to train aviation students
content:
This is a scripted video created for training aviation students by an institute in Nagpur.
A video allegedly showing a heated argument between two inside an aeroplane has been widely shared on social media. In the video, a young girl repeatedly pushes her seat backwards. This annoys an old man seated behind her, who then questions her upbringing. This infuriates the girl's father, who warns the old man that he has no right to speak that way. A cabin crew member in the meanwhile tries to intervene.Â
An X user shared the clip and wrote, "Not giving good sanskar to child and then behave like a cultured man. Very bad behaviour with senior citizens. He should be punished." Another person wrote : "Indian airlines slowly becoming Indian railways." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this video was staged. It was created for educating aviation students by an institute in Nagpur. Our Probe
We noticed several people reacting to the viral post, saying that it was staged and that it showed a flight crew training video. We also noticed that the air hostess in the video wore an ID card with "Fly High Institute" written on its ribbon.Â
Getting a clue from here, we ran a keyword search and found the viral video on the YouTube channel of Fly High Institute. It was shared in a three-part-series .Â
The first part's description noted, "As discussed and witnessed in the previous videos, the handicapped, children (babies, toddlers, kids, and teens) and senior citizens need a watchful eye from the cabin crew. An understanding of basic psychology of kids and senior citizens is required," adding, "As seen in the video, rash behaviour of kids and short tempers of senior citizens can be really volatile, and the retaliation by the kid's father is adding fuel to the fire."
The second part contained the viral video. Its description ended with, "Stay tuned for the third part!" Generally, this style is used in the context of scripted videos.Â
As per the official website of the Fly High Institute , it is an institution located in Maharashtra's Nagpur which offers training in aviation, hospitality, travel, and tourism management.Â
Videos similar to the viral one can be seen on the social media accounts of the Fly High Institute .Â
To sum it up, a scripted video created for educating aviation students is being falsely interpreted by people as an actual brawl inside an aeroplane. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Dec 7, 2023 15:42 IST

title: Fact Check: 9-year-old photo from South Korea passed off as arms sent by the US to Israel
content:
This 2014 image shows bombs on display at Kunsan Air Base in the Republic of Korea.
Israel's Ministry of Defence recently revealed that it has received over 10,000 tonnes of US military equipment since the beginning of the ongoing war with Hamas. Now, an image of a pile of bombs has gone viral on social media.
Allegedly, these were the bombs sent by the US to Israel. One Facebook post containing the photo was captioned, "The third batch of American aid to the Palestinian children has arrived." The archived version of a similar post can be seen here .
India Today found that the image in question is neither recent nor related to the ongoing Israel-Hamas war. Instead, this 2014 image shows bombs displayed at the Kunsan Air Base in the Republic of Korea. OUR PROBE
A quick reverse search of the viral image led us to a similar picture on the stock photo website Alamy . As per the information there, this photo was taken on October 23,  2014. It shows Blu-109 and Mark-84 bombs displayed at the Wolf Pack Munitions Storage Area in the Kunsan Air Base in the Republic of Korea.
Upon comparing this image with the viral one, we found them to be the same. Business Insider and several Korean news outlets  also used this image in their reports with the same description.
Business Insider and several Korean news outlets  also used this image in their reports with the same description.
To sum it up, a nine-year-old image is being falsely shared in the context of the ongoing Israel-Hamas war. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Dec 10, 2023 19:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video from Andhra Pradesh, NOT bulldozers being sent from UP to Rajasthan
content:
This is an old video from Andhra Pradesh.
Following the Bharatiya Janata Party's victory in the Rajasthan Assembly elections, a video of a freight train carrying bulldozers has gone viral on social media. Text superimposed on the video reads, "Train from UP to Rajasthan."Â
An Instagram user shared this video with the caption, "Baba Balak Nath's bulldozer in Rajasthan." Mahant Balaknath is a BJP leader and MLA from Rajasthan. The archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that the video in question is at least two years old and was filmed near Andhra Pradesh's Tenali Junction railway station. Our Probe
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to its longer version on a YouTube channel called "GopiRailworld", shared on November 26, 2021. The viral clip's visuals can be seen around the three-minute mark.Â
According to the video's description, it was filmed at the Tenali Junction Railway Station of Andhra Pradesh.
We then looked at other videos filmed at Tenali Junction railway station. One such video uploaded to the "Only In India" YouTube channel shows a similar location as seen in the viral video. This place is also clearly visible in the Google Street View. Thus, it's clear that an old video from Andhra Pradesh showing a train transporting bulldozers is being falsely peddled in the backdrop of the recent Rajasthan Assembly elections. (With inputs from Abdul Basheer) - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 11, 2023 16:15 IST

title: Fact check: 2016 Ganesha Visarjan video peddled as T Raja fans celebrating his victory
content:
This 2016 video shows a Hyderabad resident waving a saffron flag on the occasion of Ganesh Visarjan.
A video allegedly showing supporters of Bharatiya Janata Party MLA T Raja Singh celebrating his election victory in Telangana's Goshamahal dancing and waving a huge saffron flag in the middle of a road has been widely shared on social media. An X user shared the video and wrote , "Mood in #Goshamahal .. after @TigerRajaSingh wins for the 3rd consecutive time." The archived version of this post can be seen here .
It is noteworthy that T Raja Singh recently won from the Goshamahal seat for the third consecutive time since he was elected as MLA in 2014.Â
India Today found that the viral video is from 2016 and shows Ganesh Visarjan celebrations in Hyderabad. Ritesh Modi, the person in the video, confirmed this to India Today. Our Probe
Upon reverse searching the keyframes of the viral video, we found that it was uploaded on the YouTube channel "Privateeye CCTV' on September 26, 2016. The description alongside this video noted the name of one Ritesh Modi and the festival "Ganesh Nimajjanam".Â
Ganesh Nimajjanam is the other name for Ganesh Visarjan , the ritual of devotees immersing an idol of Lord Ganesha in water. It also noted that the flag in the video was created using 10 metres of cloth and 20 feet of wood. Subsequent searches led us to the Instagram account of Ritesh Modi. There, we found similar videos  of Ritesh waving saffron flag . We also found such videos on his YouTube account . Â
Subsequent searches led us to the Instagram account of Ritesh Modi. There, we found similar videos  of Ritesh waving saffron flag . We also found such videos on his YouTube account . Â
Next, we contacted Ritesh to get more information about the viral video. He told India Today, "It was filmed near our colony in 2016 when Ganesh Nimajjanam was being celebrated. It has nothing to do with T Raja Singh's recent election victory." Geolocating the video
The video on Ritesh's YouTube channel is much clearer as compared to the viral video. Here, we observed a board for "Vamshi Diabetic Clinic". Another prominent marker was the building "Veerashaiva Vidhyavardak Hostel". We were able to locate both places on Google Maps.
This location can also be seen on Google Street View. Â
It's noteworthy that similar videos of people celebrating T Raja Singh's victory have surfaced. However, as evidenced, the viral video has nothing to do with it. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 11, 2023 23:21 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT a recent video of Israeli forces stopping ambulance from entering Gaza
content:
This video is from 2019 when Israeli forces stopped an ambulance during protests in the Beit Sira town of Ramallah.
A video of two uniformed men pointing a gun towards people sitting in an ambulance and yelling at them has gone viral on social media . Allegedly, these were Israeli soldiers stopping paramedics from entering Gaza. The English subtitles of the video read, "Hand over the keys, hand them over."Â
"Israeli forces detain paramedics at gunpoint preventing them from saving lives in Gaza," read posts on Facebook  and X alongside the video .Â
India Today found that this video is from 2019 when Israeli soldiers had stopped an ambulance during a protest in Ramallah.
Using reverse search, we found a photo very similar to the visuals in the viral clip, published in the state-run Turkish news agency Anadolu . Reportedly, Palestinians gathered near Beit Sira in Ramallah (which is in the West Bank) and held a demonstration. Israeli forces intervened in the demonstration and stopped an ambulance in the area. The image was credited to photographer Issam Rimawi.Â
We found that Rimawi had shared multiple images of the incident in question on Facebook on March 8, 2019. He wrote in Arabic, " The occupation soldiers detain a Red Crescent ambulance and its crew during their coverage of confrontations in Beit Sierra West, despite God." B'Tselem, a Jerusalem-based nonprofit that documents human rights violations in Palestinian territories, published a detailed report  about this incident on March 25, 2019. According to the report, on March 8, 2019, around 200 people were protesting in Beit Sira, Ramallah, against the killing of two Palestinians, Amir Dar Daraj and Yusef Anqawi. The demonstrators were demanding the Israeli army release their bodies. There were clashes between the Israeli forces and the protestors, following which ambulances were called. When the paramedics found themselves caught between protesters and soldiers, who continued to fire rubber-coated metal bullets and teargas canisters, the ambulance driver reportedly sought to drive away from that spot. However, as soon as the ambulance started moving, an officer ordered the driver at gunpoint to turn off the engine and hand over the keys. They were forced to wait there for about 15 minutes until the soldiers moved away. We also reached out to Anadolu photographer Issam Rimawi, who told India Today that this incident was indeed from 2019 and he was present when it happened. "The Palestinian Red Crescent ambulance was stopped for over 15 minutes. They (Israeli Forces) threatened the driver and searched the vehicle to look for certain injured Palestinians. They also asked us, the journalists, to leave," he added. advertisement Thus, it's clear that a 2019 video is being shared in the context of the ongoing Israel-Hamas war. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Dec 12, 2023 22:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Islamification of UK? Nope, viral pic of Arabic street signs is photoshopped
content:
The viral photo is photoshopped and not real.
A viral picture of a street sign , claiming to show English place names alongside their Arabic translations in Yorkshire, England, has sparked allegations of the "Islamification of the UK." An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today found that the photo is manipulated and not real. Our Probe
Using Google Translate, we found that the Arabic words don't correspond to the translated place names but instead include absurd phrases, like "As-Salaam-Alaikum", a common Arabic greeting that means "Peace be unto you", and "Refugees welcome you".
Further, a reverse search led us to a 2016 report by Metro.co.uk , which labelled it as a fake and the result of "cunning use of Photoshop." An earlier post by a Twitter user from the same period contained the authentic photo of the signboard without the purported Arabic translations, confirming it as photoshopped.
The Independent reported in 2016 that the manipulated photo first surfaced on the anti-refugee conservative website The New Observer , which later acknowledged being a victim of an "elaborate hoax" and removed the story, issuing a statement on its Facebook page.
We also examined the historical imagery on Google Street View to determine if the signboard had ever been altered to include Arabic translations. From 2012  to 2022 , the signboard maintained its original form, as supported by the available data. We did not find Street View images from 2013, 2014, 2021, and 2023.Â
The year-wise historical evolution of the location can be seen below.
Thus, it's clear that the viral image is a hoax. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 13, 2023 17:41 IST

title: Fact Check: This video does not show Americans discarding Zara clothes in support of Gaza
content:
This video is old and unrelated to Zara's ad campaign controversy.
Spanish fast fashion giant Zara recently issued an apology  after boycotts over an ad campaign whose images allegedly resembled photos of corpses in white shrouds in Gaza. As per a Reuters report , the Advertising Standards Authority, a  self-regulatory organisation of the advertising industry in the UK, received more than a hundred complaints.
Now, a video of clothes being dumped en masse in a commercial district has gone viral. Allegedly, several Americans threw their Zara clothes in front of the company building after the ad campaign was launched.Â
An X user shared this video alongside the Zara ad in question and wrote, "After Zara made an insulting advertisement about the Gaza War, the American people threw all Zara clothes in front of the company." The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that this video has nothing to do with Palestine and predates the recent Zara controversy.Â
We noticed that many people  reacting to the video pointed out that the was posted in November by a second-hand fashion company called Vestiaire Collective. In the viral video too, we observed Vestiaire Collective written on one of the display boards. Vestiaire Collective is a platform for buying and selling second-hand luxury fashion products. Getting a clue from here, we scanned the social media accounts of Vestiaire Collective, which led us to their November 16 Instagram post.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Vestiaire Collective (@vestiaireco) The caption alongside the video posted spoke about the brand's fast fashion ban campaign " Think First, Buy Second ". The brand announced banning 30 fast fashion brands like Zara, H&M, Gap, Mango, and Uniqlo from appearing on its site in November. Many media outlets including Vogue Business  and Harper's Bazaar  had reported about this at the time. "The decision to ban fast fashion was made to support Vestiaire Collective's long-time work to promote alternatives to the dominant model of fashion," said Dounia Wone, the chief impact officer of Vestiaire Collective. "Fast fashion brands contribute to excessive production and consumption, resulting in devastating social and environmental consequences in the Global South. It is our duty to act and lead the way for other industry players to join us in this movement, and together we can have an impact." To sum it up, an old video is being circulated in the context of the recent Zara ad campaign controversy. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Dec 14, 2023 18:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Don't fall for the barcode hoax - 729 doesn't mean a product was made in Israel
content:
The barcode prefix "729" does not determine the product's origin. It only shows that the barcode was issued in Israel.
Amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict, BDS (Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions), a movement promoting economic boycotts against Israel, has gained momentum again. In this context, some social media posts are now suggesting that barcodes starting with "729" denote products manufactured in Israel . An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that a barcode does not serve as a means to identify the country of origin or manufacture of a product. The digits "729" only indicate that the barcode number was allocated in Israel. Our Probe
A keyword search about the body responsible for assigning country codes and prescribing standards for barcodes globally led us to a website of a nonprofit, GS1 , which has member organisations in more than 100 countries  that work directly with governments to manage barcode standards. The website states that the first three digits of a barcode denote the corresponding GS1 organisation in that country.Â
The organisation notes that the first three digits of a barcode only determines which GS1 member organisation allocated them . It doesn't determine where an item was produced or distributed.Â
Misinformation about barcodes being an identifier of where a product has been manufactured have been known to surface amid geopolitical tensions . It was also rampant during the start of the Covid-19 pandemic, when there were calls for the boycott of Chinese-made products.
An AFP report about one such wave of misinformation about barcodes quoted senior director for public relations at GS1 US, Shannon Sullivan saying, "The company prefix does not determine the country in which a product was manufactured — it only indicates the country where the company prefix was obtained."
Barcodes that begin with "729" refer to GS1 Israel . But the products carrying these barcodes don't point to where they were manufactured. The country of manufacture is separately and conspicuously mentioned on the product packages or labels. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 14, 2023 20:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Decade-old video from Egypt FALSELY viral as Israel bulldozing patients in Gaza hospital
content:
Although the Gaza health ministry alleged a similar attack, this video is from Egypt and dates back to August 14, 2013.
A horrific video  of a bulldozer running over bodies draped in white has been widely shared by many online. Allegedly, this was an Israeli bulldozer targeting patients at the Kamal Adwan Hospital in Gaza. "Israeli bulldozers ran over displaced people and patients at Kamal Adwan Hospital. Share and expose their crime," read one such post on X.
On Facebook , one person wrote, "Horrific Video as an Israeli Bulldozer purposely running over immobile and seriously injured Palestinian patients in the grounds of Kamal Adwan Hospital. War Crimes by Israel."
The Free Press Journal, on its official YouTube channel, uploaded this video  and claimed it from the Gaza hospital. An archived version of this video and similar social media posts can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video is more than a decade old and from Egypt, not Gaza.
A search with relevant keywords led us to reports in Reuters  and France24 published on December 17. Both mentioned an alleged bulldozer attack by Israel on Kamal Adwan Hospital in Gaza City, as claimed by the Gazan Health Ministry.
Another report in Maktoob Media claimed that Israeli bulldozers deliberately destroyed tents used by Palestinians seeking refuge outside Kamal Adwan Hospital, crushing them. Notably, at the time of publishing this story, no international outlet featured photos or videos of this in their reports.
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found an extended version of the same clip uploaded to the YouTube channel of Al Jazeera. Uploaded on August 26, 2013, the Arabic caption of this video read: "A bulldozer sweeps away dozens of bodies of victims of the Rabaa massacre."
This made it abundantly clear that the video is in no way related to the Israel-Hamas war. The description of the original video further mentioned that the incident happened on August 14, 2013, during a sit-in protest when a bulldozer swept away dozens of bodies of victims of the Rabaa massacre. What is the Rabaa Massacre?
In August 2013, thousands in Egypt took to the streets demanding the reinstatement of the country's first democratically elected president, Mohamed Morsi, who was forced to resign as Egyptian Army Chief, General Abdel Fattah al-Sisi led a coalition to become president of Egypt.
During such protest on August 14, 2013, the Egyptian military mercilessly shot, bulldozed, and killed protestors. An investigation  by Human Rights Watch reported the deaths of at least 817. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Dec 18, 2023 15:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Mysuru SFI leader NOT arrested for Parliament breach! Here's what happened
content:
The photo doesn't show Manoranjan D. It shows Vijay Kumar, the SFI Mysore district president.
The Delhi Police charged six persons under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act after miscreants caused a ruckus inside and outside Parliament with coloured smoke canisters on the 22nd anniversary of the 2001 Parliament attack. Among those arrested was Manoranjan D, who was allegedly one of the two perpetrators who leapt from the visitors' gallery into the Lower House chamber.
Now social media is buzzing with claims  that Manoranjan D was a Students' Federation of India member from Mysuru. A post making the rounds right now shows a man talking on a mic, with an SFI banner in Kannada visible in the background.Â
A Facebook user sharing the viral photo wrote, "Manoranjan ???? He was also one of them who entered the parliament and was involved in the blasts... So do you see the 'SFI' banner behind him? I hope you have understood what I have posted." An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral picture is of Vijay Kumar, the SFI Mysore district president — not Manoranjan D. Our Probe
Keyword searches in Kannada led us to a Facebook post by SFI Karnataka State Committee , categorically refuting the claim that any SFI activist was involved in the Parliament breach incident.Â
Several posts on the page condemned the false linking and warned of legal action against those spreading misinformation .
A press release from the SFI state committee identified the person in the viral photo as Vijay Kumar, SFI Mysore district president. It rebuked those attempting to link him to the attack. The statement mentioned that responsible people will soon be brought to justice. We also found a copy of the complaint filed by Vijay Kumar at Mysore's Cybercrime police station seeking action against those misusing his photo for political purposes. The origin of the viral photo was traced to SFI Mysore's Facebook page , where it was shared under a post announcing the election of new office bearers at the second Mysore city conference held on September 8, 2022. Confirming the misuse of his image, Vijay Kumar told India Today that he had filed a complaint under the Information and Technology Act, and said that the picture going viral was two years old. He said that he planned to meet the Police Commissioner of Mysore to figure out a course of action against those spreading misinformation. A comparison of Vijay Kumar's social media photos with the reported picture of the actual accused Manoranjan D confirmed their distinct identities. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Dec 18, 2023 19:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Stage collapses in Pak during anti-Jew speech? Nope, this old clip is from a political rally
content:
A five-year-old video of a stage collapse in Pakistan was falsely shared with a communal twist.
In a video that's been shared by many on social media, a man can be seen delivering a sermon when all of a sudden the stage he and others were on collapses. Allegedly, this happened when the man, an Imam, spoke against Jews in Pakistan.
Sharing this video, a Facebook user wrote, "Imam in Pakistan preaches that he had a dream in which he said that all Jews must be exterminated. He goes on to say, 'If this is not true, may the ground sink beneath me, and look what happens."Â
India Today Fact Check found this video to be more than five years old. It shows a stage collapse during a political gathering in Pakistan. The man was not talking about Jews. Our Probe
A reverse image search of key frames from the video led us to a higher quality and larger version of the clip shared by journalist Aditya Raj Kaul on X on July 18, 2018. Per the post, the stage collapsed during a Jamaat-e-Islami rally in the Mohmand district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Pakistan. Among the people on the stage was Jamaat-e-Islami leader Siraj-ul-Haq.
Subsequent keyword searches led us to the video uploaded to the YouTube channel of "Public News" on the same date. The video was titled: "Stage collapses during Jamaat-e-Islami election campaign." This indicates that the viral video is not recent at all. We also found media reports about the incident , which relayed the same information. According to Geo TV, the stage collapsed due to overcrowding and that no one was gravely injured. Was it an anti-Semitic speech? We showed this video to an Urdu-language speaker, who confirmed to India Today.in that before the stage collapsed, the person was saying, "We welcome, Salar-e-Qafila (our leader), Quaid-e-Millat-e-Islamia (leader of the Muslim nation), Naib Sadar Muttahida Majlis-e-Amal (Deputy President Muttahida Majlis-e-Amal (a religious political party), Ameer Jamat-e-Islami Pakistan (Leader of Jamaat-e-Islami)." It was just an introduction for religious and political leaders. This shows that no anti-Semitic speech was made in the viral video. Thus, it is more than clear to say that a five-year-old video of a stage collapse in Pakistan was shared with a misleading claim. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 18, 2023 21:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Siddaramaiah admit Congress can't fulfil poll promises? Nope, viral clip cut out of context
content:
Viral video is clipped to distort the narrative. Siddaramaiah was criticising the former BJP government for their unfulfilled promises.
A viral video purportedly showing Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah admitting to his failure in fulfilling promises has sparked controversy on social media. In the video, he can be heard saying in Kanadda, "Where shall we get the money from? Where shall I get the money from? We might have said something before the elections. Can we follow up on whatever we said [then]? You say waive loans…"Â
Those sharing the video interpreted this statement as Siddaramaiah's admission that electoral promises were mere gimmicks.Â
An X user sharing the video suggested that Siddaramaiah conceded the impossibility of fulfilling his electoral promises. They wrote , "Sid Ram says, we will promise many things during elections, does it mean that we have to fulfil all? Also, where is the money, we are not printing money, he says. The court should not allow any party to make fake promises during elections. If they do, they will have to fulfil." Its archived version can be seen here .Â
Former Telangana minister and Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president KT Ramarao also shared the video   and wrote: "No money to deliver poll promises/guarantees says Karnataka CM! In the Assembly speech, Siddaramaiah also questioned the BJP's 2018 manifesto promise to waive loans up to Rs one lakh, pointing out their failure to deliver. Siddaramaiah substantiated his criticism by stating Yediyurappa's admission in 2009 about the insufficiency of funds to waive farm loans.
He said in Kannada: "This same Yeddyurappa, when was chief minister in December 2009, responding to a demand by [VS] Ugrappa in the Legislative Council to waive loans, said: 'Do we have a printing machine? Where shall we get the money from? Where shall I get the money from? We might have something before the elections. Can we follow up on whatever we said [then]?'" The CM responds
We also found that Siddaramaiah responded to the allegations on his official X account. While sharing the unedited video of his Assembly speech, he clarified that he was referring to Yediyurappa's statement from 2009. In a concerning turn of events, certain BJP leaders like Ashwath Narayan, CT Ravi, and others have engaged in spreading misleading information about me. The deceptive tactic involves circulating an edited video that distorts my statements, falsely implying an admission of the… pic.twitter.com/8HaeKdtwlU — Siddaramaiah (@siddaramaiah) December 17, 2023
