Siddaramaiah wrote, "...Contrary to the manipulated narrative, the unaltered video clearly reflects my remarks in the Assembly, holding the BJP accountable for failing to fulfil promises made in their 2018 manifesto, especially the loan waiver promise they had made. I cited the fact that Yediyurappa, in 2009, had stated that they didn't have a printing machine to print notes and lacked the funds to waive farm loans. Yediyurappa had acknowledged that it was not possible for the BJP to fulfil promises made during elections..."
In conclusion, the viral video was selectively clipped to change the meaning of Siddaramaiah's statement. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Dec 20, 2023 21:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Not 'Pallywood'! This video shows a short film being shot
content:
This video is from a film set. It was shared by a Moroccan actor and director Karim Doniazalle.
From the very beginning of Israel's siege of Gaza, accusations of Palestinian crisis actors overplaying the harm have made their way to social media. The term "Pallywood", referring to an alleged industry of staging scenes of violence against Palestinians to gain global sympathy, is often used along with these allegations.
In that context, a video of a patient being brought into a hospital has been widely shared on social media. In the video, a camera and sound crew can be seen recording a patient being brought in on a gurney . Once the scene is shot, the alleged patient sits up.Â
An X user wrote while sharing the video, "Trailer of the new Pallywood movie that's getting released on December 20th". Its archived version can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this video has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Hamas war. It's from a film set. Karim Doniazelle, an actor in the film confirmed this to India Today.Â
We noticed that several people reacting to the viral video claimed that the video was from a film set and that the man on the gurney was Moroccan actor Karim Doniazelle. We subsequently found the Instagram account of the Moroccan actor, Karim Doniazelle. Here, he shared the video in question on October 30 with hashtags like #hollywood, #bollywood, #cinema, and #aloulatv. Al Aoula is a state-controlled TV channel in Morocco.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Karim Doniazalle (@doniazalle) We contacted Karim to get more information about the video. He told India Today that this video showed the filming of a short film that he was part of. "It has nothing to do with Palestine," he added. Karim also sent India Today two more videos related to the short film. He did not, however, mention what the name of the film was.   Since the Israel-Hamas war began, multiple old and unrelated videos have surfaced under the "Pallywood" propaganda theory. Our fact checks of two such videos can be seen here . To sum it up, a video from a film set was falsely peddled as a recent video of Palestinians faking injuries.  - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Dec 21, 2023 16:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Dunking on 'Dunki'? Old and fake reviews of SRK film flood social media
content:
This screenshot is doctored. Taran Adarsh tweeted on December 21 morning that he is yet to watch 'Dunki'.
Shah Rukh Khan's third film in 2023, "Dunki", directed by Rajkumar Hirani, opened to mixed reviews on December 21. Even as social media has been filled with reviews and opinions about the film, some dubious ones have also surfaced. In this story, we will look at a few of these. Fake review 1
Claim : A screenshot  of film trade analyst Taran Adarsh's post on X, where he gave the film just one and a half stars and called it an "Epic Disappointment" was widely shared. The archived version of one such post can be seen here .Â
Fact : This screenshot is doctored. We found the same words (except for the film's and director's names and hashtags) in a Taran Adarsh post from June 16. This post was about the film " Adipurush ", which was released the very same day.Â
Moreover, Taran Adarsh recently underwent surgery  and as per his post  from December 21 morning, he was still under observation at a hospital and hadn't watched "Dunki" yet.  Good morning, extremely keen to watch #Dunki and #Salaar , both... Still under observation in hospital, have almost recovered after a major surgery... Thank you veryyy much for the wishes... Feeling blessed 🙏🙏🙏
— taran adarsh (@taran_adarsh) December 21, 2023

— taran adarsh (@taran_adarsh) December 21, 2023
Claim : Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, according to some online video reports, allegedly watched "Dunki" in a special screening and both gave it a standing ovation. They even praised Shah Rukh Khan, calling him the best actor in India. Archived versions of two such posts can be seen here and here .Â
Fact : At the time of writing this story, there were no reports of PM Modi or Arvind Kejriwal praising "Dunki".
The videos being shared with these claims were created using old videos featuring these leaders. The one showing SRK speaking in the presence of PM Modi, Rajkumar Hirani, and other Bollywood celebrities was from an October 2019 event  where the PM met several artists from the Indian film industry.Â
On the other hand, we found the video of Arvind Kejriwal talking to the media in his September 28 post on X . In it, he was taking a dig at a CBI inquiry of the alleged irregularities in the renovation of his residence.Â
Kejriwal was summoned by the ED for questioning in the excise policy-linked money laundering case on December 21. However, as per reports , he left for an undisclosed location for a ten-day Vipassana meditation session on December 20. Fake review 3
Claim : These videos show cinemagoers criticising "Dunki". In one such clip , a man wearing a pink shirt said that Shah Rukh had disappointed the people. In another clip , some youngsters said that the makers of this movie had fooled people by converting a world tour video into a Bollywood film. Another video showed an old man  saying that the movie practically did not have a plot. #DunkiReview - SRK PR Mafia is well known, every reviewer will come out & say it's a super etc . Movie has lag with a known slow story . It's loaded with cringe SRK overacting . It should be avoided. Don't waste money for a TV serial #Dunki pic.twitter.com/Zen9s8ygTO — Ravi @🔥🔥Prabhas Army 🔥🔥🦕 (@RaviPrabhas333) December 21, 2023

They were part of a compilation of public reviews of the SRK-starrer movie "Jab Harry Met Sejal", shared by the entertainment channel Viral Bollywood. Â
On the other hand, the video of the old man saying that the movie didn't have any story dates back to December 2018 and was part of another compilation of public reviews of the SRK film "Zero" by Viral Bollywood. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Dec 21, 2023 16:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of atrocities by Syrian militia shared as Israeli troops torturing Palestinians
content:
The viral video shows the brutal crimes of pro-Assad forces in Syria in 2013.
A horrifying video circulating on social media allegedly shows Israeli soldiers torturing Palestinians. In the viral video, one of the men seemed to have bled to death while the other was being stabbed, tortured, and eventually bludgeoned to death.
An X user sharing the brutal video, wrote , "The cowardly Israelis only bomb or stab in the back. Their army is a bunch of weak sadistic barbarians. This is video proof of why there is resistance. Palestinians are being killed. Ethnically cleansed by these vile creatures of darkness. They have no humanity and no mercy in their hearts. Anyone that supports Israel should be ashamed."Â
India Today traced the video to Syria, dating back to January 2, 2013. The video shows pro-Assad forces brutally executing Syrian civilians. OUR PROBE
Running a reverse image search of keyframes from the video, We found its extended version on a YouTube channel, uploaded on January 2, 2013. The video description in Arabic translates to: "The Shabiha force is slaughtering civilians with Knives."
Shabiha is an armed pro-government militia group loyal to Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. The viral segment can be seen at the 2:06-minute mark in the 5:50-minute video.
Al Arabiya also reported about the viral video and noted that it was sourced from a captured member of the Shabibha group. The report, however, couldn't verify either its location or the identity of the perpetrators and victims.
The video's presence on Russian social media site VK  and the use of its screenshot in another news portal's report further corroborate its Syrian origin.
So, while we couldn't independently verify the video's location, it is clear that the video dates back to as early as 2013, predating the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict by a decade. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Dec 21, 2023 20:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Kejriwal's alleged 2012 'tweet' on leaders skipping ED summons is fake
content:
The viral screenshot is fake. Arvind Kejriwal never made such a post.
The Enforcement Directorate issued its third summons to Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal  to appear before the agency on January 3, 2024, concerning the excise policy scam case. Kejriwal, who skipped the first two summons on November 2 and December 21, now faces increased scrutiny. Amid this, a screenshot of an alleged 2012 tweet by Kejriwal , criticising corrupt political leaders for evading ED and CBI summons, was widely shared on social media. Allegedly in 2012, Kejriwal condemned political leaders who refused to appear before enforcement agencies, yet remained in their posts with impunity. Several Bharatiya Janata Party leaders  among others shared the viral post , making cutting remarks at Kejriwal and the Aam Aadmi Party. Delhi BJP Chief Virendra Sachdeva also issued a statement to a news agency  based on the alleged post by Kejriwal. VIDEO | "(Delhi CM) Arvind Kejriwal is behaving like a criminal. A criminal always tries to avoid investigation. On November 24, 2012, he wrote on social media that politicians should resign once they get a summon from ED or CBI. However, to avoid the summon, he has gone for… pic.twitter.com/Xsz3JoxfZu — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) December 23, 2023 One such post read , "I agree fully with self-certified kattar honest Arvind Kejriwal ji, that it is shameful for corrupt leaders to avoid ED/CBI summons. Dear chameleon champion, please request Shri Arvind Kejriwal to appear before ED, visit Vipassana later." India Today found that the viral screenshot is fake. Kejriwal never made this post. Our Probe With the help of the date and keywords in the viral screenshot, we ran an advanced search on X to look for the alleged post on Arvind Kejriwal's official. However, the search did not produce the post in question. Here is a screengrab of all the posts that he made on November 24, 2012. Upon careful observation, we noticed that Kejriwal's alleged post contained 257 characters. Until November 2017 , the maximum character limit for a post was only 140. This hinted at the post being fake. On further searches, we came across a clarification posted on X by AAP Delhi's social media  head Amanpreet Singh Uppal, who called the viral screenshot fake. Fake Tweet और जुमला राजनीति के ऊपर भी कुछ सोच लिया करो भाजपाईयो pic.twitter.com/9wNAKe8F3O — Amanpreet Singh Uppal (@iAmanUppal) December 22, 2023 We also googled to search if any such post was made by Kejriwal then. Had he made the post, it would likely have been reported or discussed. But we found no credible news reports. Thus, it's clear that a fabricated screenshot is being shared with misleading narratives after ED summoned Kejriwal for the third time. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Dec 23, 2023 20:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Muslim man urinating in Dutch supermarket is staged prank
content:
This is a staged prank by Instagram user Danny Derix, who is neither Muslim, nor an immigrant.
A video allegedly showing a man urinating in a Dutch supermarket's pork section has gone viral on social media. Allegedly, the person seen in the video was a Muslim immigrant.Â
In the viral video, a man, facing away from the camera, can be seen leaning over the meat section, hands positioned as if he is urinating. The person behind the camera, speaking in Dutch, yells, "Bro, you're radical, just because you don't eat pork. Wow. We don't eat pork. We don't eat pork." Muslim immigrant in Holland urinates on the pork section of the supermarket as another films saying 'we don't eat pork' 😡 pic.twitter.com/in71rfapXP — Paul Golding (@GoldingBF) December 17, 2023
Muslim immigrant in Holland urinates on the pork section of the supermarket as another films saying 'we don't eat pork' 😡 pic.twitter.com/in71rfapXP — Paul Golding (@GoldingBF) December 17, 2023
A user sharing the video on X, wrote , "Muslim immigrant in Holland urinates on the pork section of the supermarket as another films saying 'we don't eat pork'."Â
India Today found that the video is a staged prank pulled by an Instagram user named Danny Derix.
Responding to the viral video, several people identified the man as Instagram user Danny Derix. While tagging him, they commented that he was a known prankster.
We searched for him on Instagram and found the viral video on his profile , also featuring other videos, where he dressed identically staged similar pranks of simulating urination in odd public places .     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Danny Derix (@buurtwachtt)
A post shared by Danny Derix (@buurtwachtt)
India Today reached out to Danny, who clarified that he is neither Muslim nor an immigrant and identified as a Christian of mixed ethnicity — half Indonesian and half Dutch. Danny clarified that his purpose in making such prank videos was to raise awareness about the ease of creating and disseminating misinformation online.
In a video uploaded to his YouTube channel , Danny disclosed that he didn't even use a bottle of water or any fluid to make it authentic. Instead, he used a urinating sound effect and juxtaposed it with the viral video for a realistic effect.Â
He also created a sample video mirroring the original act, demonstrating the process of searching for a urination sound on a metal sheet online and seamlessly integrating it into video.
Danny went on to explain, "The video gained widespread attention, to the extent that even Dutch far-right politician Geert Wilders reposted it with a misleading communal claim."Â
He further clarified that after shooting the video in Albert Heijn supermarket, it was posted to various social media platforms without any context, but people immediately assumed that this person must be a Muslim or an immigrant. He expressed astonishment at how people construct their narratives.
Expressing regret over the narrative created by those who shared the video, he revealed that several news organisations had contacted him to confirm the authenticity of the viral claims. Lamenting about the implications of such absurd claims, he alleged that Basic-Fit, a popular gym chain in Europe, cancelled his subscription and banned him from all their outlets.
Thus, it's clear that a viral prank video was circulated online with a communal spin. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Dec 24, 2023 18:14 IST

title: Fact Check: Is Elon Musk 2023's Time Person of the Year? Nope, it's Taylor Swift
content:
American singer Taylor Swift has been named Time magazine's Person of the Year for 2023, not Elon Musk. The Tesla CEO received the honour in 2021.
Has billionaire businessman Elon Musk been named Time Magazine's "Person of the Year"? If social media is to be believed, that is the case. Many on Facebook shared photos  that included what looked like a Time magazine cover featuring Musk and wrote: "Breaking: Elon Musk Is Time's Person Of The Year 2023."Â
India Today Fact Check found that American singer Taylor Swift has been named Person of the Year for 2023, not Elon Musk. The Tesla CEO received the honour in 2021. Our Probe
A keyword search on the internet led us to the official X account of Time magazine. There, it was announced that American singer Taylor Swift had been selected Time's Person of the Year for 2023. Taylor Swift ( @taylorswift13 ) is TIME's 2023 Person of the Year https://t.co/oyjR55azCZ pic.twitter.com/m2qbIbd5TX — TIME (@TIME) December 6, 2023
Taylor Swift ( @taylorswift13 ) is TIME's 2023 Person of the Year https://t.co/oyjR55azCZ pic.twitter.com/m2qbIbd5TX — TIME (@TIME) December 6, 2023
After that, we went through the official website of Time magazine  and found the same announcement . The cover and the other images of Swift can be seen there.
Subsequently, we ran a keyword search on the internet and found the list of people who were shortlisted for 2023 Time's Person of the Year . Aside from Taylor Swift, this list included Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, King Charles III, Chairman of the Federal Reserve Jerome Powell, and Open AI's Sam Altman.
Then a reverse image search of the viral magazine cover led us to the official website of Time magazine, and we found that the Tesla CEO was named Time Person of the Year in 2021. The same cover can be seen here .
A reverse search of the other image led us to the stock image website Getty Images. Per the photo's description , Musk appeared on the stage of the Time Person of the Year event with his son on December 13, 2021, in New York City.
Thus, it is clear that Musk was not named Person of the Year in 2023. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Dec 24, 2023 19:24 IST

title: Fact Check: This OLD video of Hardik Pandya mischievously edited with Rohit Sharma chants
content:
The video is three years old and was edited to add the Rohit Sharma chants.
The Mumbai Indians franchise courted controversy after trading Rohit Sharma for Hardik Pandya in the 2024 edition of the Indian Premier League, with Pandya replacing Sharma as captain.
Sharma successfully led the team to a record five victories in the T20 league since assuming leadership in 2013. This decision sparked an intense meltdown online, with fans urging the reinstatement of Sharma as the team captain.
Amidst this, a video going viral on social media shows Hardik Pandya getting down from his car at what appears to be an airport. In the background, chants of "Mumbai Cha Raja, Rohit Sharma" (Rohit Sharma is Mumbai's king) can be heard. Those sharing this video asserted that Rohit Sharma's fans were chanting this in front of Pandya.
One X user, sharing the video , wrote, "People are shouting 'Mumbai Cha Raja Rohit Sharma' in front of Hardik Pandya. Rohit Sharma is an emotion of India. SHAMELESS MUMBAI INDIANS." The Free Press Journal also reported on the viral video with a similar narrative.Â
India Today found that the viral video dates back to January 2020 and has been edited. The slogan was added later. OUR PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a photo set in paparazzo Viral Bhayani's Instagram account . This post from January 21, 2020, featured photos of Sara Ali Khan, Varun Dhawan, Janhvi Kapoor, Sanjay Dutt, Hardik Pandya, Shraddha Kapoor, and Shahid Kapoor. Pandya's photo seemed to match the viral clip. This hinted that the video was old.Â
A further search took us to a Lokmat Hindi report from the same period, featuring the viral video. No such slogans eulogising Rohit Sharma could be heard in the video in the report.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Bollywood Pap (@bollywoodpap)
A post shared by Bollywood Pap (@bollywoodpap)
Moreover, we traced the slogans heard in the viral video back to another YouTube video dated January 18, 2020, two days before the video of Hardik Pandya was shot at Mumbai's airport.
Thus, it's evident that an old video of Hardik Pandya was edited to add slogans extolling Rohit Sharma. - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Dec 24, 2023 19:46 IST

title: Fact Check: Kapil Sibal never said he would commit suicide before Ram Mandir's construction
content:
The viral post is fake. Kapil Sibal never made any such statement regarding Ram Mandir.
A screenshot of a post made by Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal on X has been widely shared on social media. The alleged post, dated July 29, 2020, reads: "I will stand by my word that I will commit suicide before the construction of Ram Temple".Â
Many shared the viral screenshot, sarcastically commenting that someone should remind Sibal about his old tweet with the inauguration date of the Ram Mandir fast approaching. The post was shared on X and Facebook as well.
India Today found that the viral post is fake. Kapil Sibal never made any such statement regarding the Ram Mandir.Â
We checked Sibal's official X account using time filters and did not find any such post since July 29, 2020. Had Sibal made such a statement, it would have been big news. But we couldn't find any credible news report about this either.
It's noteworthy that we found only one type of screenshot of this alleged post floating on social media. If Sibal had made this post, many social media users would have taken different screenshots of it and shared them on the internet. The screenshot also appeared digitally manipulated. The font sizes did not match X's format.
Finally, on Kapil Sibal's official account, we found a clarification that the post was fake. The following fake Twitter post is being circulated. This only shows the level to which our political discourse has been reduced to pic.twitter.com/Fsikh1XvFE — Kapil Sibal (@KapilSibal) December 24, 2023
The following fake Twitter post is being circulated. This only shows the level to which our political discourse has been reduced to pic.twitter.com/Fsikh1XvFE — Kapil Sibal (@KapilSibal) December 24, 2023
Thus, it's clear that a made-up statement was attributed to Sibal. AajTak Bangla earlier fact-checked this and you can read it here . - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Dec 25, 2023 18:46 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of clash during Sikh parade in US shared as Pakistanis thrashing pro-Khalistanis
content:
The video shows a clash between two Sikh groups during Nagar Kirtan in California and is unrelated to Pakistan.
A video of a clash between two groups has gone viral on social media. Allegedly, it shows Pakistanis assaulting pro-Khalistani Sikhs for asserting that Pakistan's Punjab is also a part of the independent Sikh state. One Facebook user  wrote, "Pakistanis were protesting with Khalistanis. One Khalistani said Pakistan's Punjab is also a part of Khalistan, and Pakistanis started beating the sh*t out of Sardars."Â
India Today found that the video shows a clash between two groups of Sikhs during a Nagar Kirtan ceremony in Yuba City, California. Our Probe
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to several media reports identifying the incident in Yuba City, California, in November 2023. Yuba City hosts one of the largest Sikh communities outside of India's Punjab. It attracts a massive crowd for the annual Sikh festival , Nagar Kirtan, which is held around the first weekend of November.
Reporting about the video, CNN-News18 highlighted it as a rift between two pro-Khalistan groups during Yuba City's Sikh Nagar Kirtan, sparked by a helicopter flying a banner reading "Delhi will be Khalistan." The report, however, also said that it could not independently ascertain these facts.Â
Chardikla Time TV North America also reported that this was a clash between two groups of Sikh men during Nagar Kirtan. The Times of India also described the event as a scuffle between two Sikh groups following heated arguments during a Nagar Kirtan in Yuba City. In an interview, an eyewitness recounted that during the last day of the Nagar Kirtan, two groups of unruly men had an altercation. As the fight escalated, some men bought sharp weapons from the festival stalls. He said the incident had nothing to do with Khalistan. The confrontation lasted about three minutes and the situation was brought to normal after the police intervened.

title: Fact Check: No, these images ARE NOT from recent bandit attack in Nigeria that killed more than 100
content:
These images are from June 5, 2022, and show the St Francis Catholic Church in Nigeria, where about 40 people were killed in an attack by unknown gunmen.
As the world celebrated Christmas Eve, Nigeria witnessed a tragedy on December 24. Armed bandits reportedly carried out a devastating attack in the state of Plateau , resulting in the loss of more than 100 lives. Some reports even indicate that the death toll has surpassed 160.
Meanwhile, two photos likely shot inside a church and one showing a floor stained with blood are making the rounds on social media. Allegedly, these were taken after the attack in Nigeria.
"Nigeria - New photos from within a church where at Christmas Christians were massacred in the name of Allah. Around 150 are confirmed dead so far, properties & farms were looted and burned. This is on par with what Hamas did, but the MSM & dancing Western Hamas fans ignore," claimed posts on Facebook and X. The archived version of such a post can be seen here.Â
India Today Fact Check found that these images are from June 2022 and are not related to the recent attack in Nigeria.Â
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, the results led us to an Al Jazeera report from June 6, 2022, that featured the shot of the ransacked church. According to the report, gunmen with explosives stormed St Francis Xavier Catholic Church in Owo, a town in Nigeria's Ondo State and opened fire, killing at least 50 people. We also found an ABC News report from the same day that also contained the same photo. The photo was credited to the Associated Press photographer Rahaman A Yusuf. A subsequent search with relevant keywords took us to the stock photo website Alamy where we found both photos. Both images were shot by Yusuf on June 5, 2022, inside the St Francis Catholic Church after gunmen opened fire and exploded detonators on a Sunday morning when worshippers gathered for weekly prayer. Additionally, we didn't find any credible reports of an attack on a church in Nigeria recently. Therefore, it is safe to conclude that the images linked to the recent attack in Nigeria date back to June 2022. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 27, 2023 19:24 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show UP police thrashing Muslims after Namaz ban
content:
The viral video shows a two-year-old incident from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh.
A video of police personnel lathi-charging  and dispersing a group of people was widely shared on social media. Allegedly, it showed Uttar Pradesh police thrashing Muslims offering Namaz on the road. These posts implied that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has brought a law in Uttar Pradesh to criminalise the offering of Namaz on the roads.
A Facebook user , claimed: "Such joy to see this. Yogi ji need of the hour to set straight religious fanatics. NEW RULES. Vote for BJP!" The archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that this was a two-year-old incident in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. The video shows police caning a gathering after some miscreants pelted stones during the Milad-Un-Nabi procession. Our Probe
We noticed that many responded to the viral post claiming that the incident was actually from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. In the video, we noticed that a shop's shutter had "S Deen Tailors" written on it. Using these clues, we found the shop in the Gohalpur area of Jabalpur.Â
With the help of some keywords, we found a Facebook post  on the "Mera Shehar Jabalpur" page, dated October 22, 2021. The post contained visuals similar to the viral video. The caption explained that these scenes unfolded during the Milad-un-nabi procession in Jabalpur, which prompted police intervention. Subsequently, we came across several media reports from October 2021. The Free Press Journal  reported that violence erupted in Dhar, Jabalpur, during the religious procession that was taken out on the occasion of Eid Milad-un-Nabi. The report noted that a ruckus ensued after participants of a procession decided to deviate from the permitted route.Â
Subsequently, we came across several media reports from October 2021. The Free Press Journal  reported that violence erupted in Dhar, Jabalpur, during the religious procession that was taken out on the occasion of Eid Milad-un-Nabi. The report noted that a ruckus ensued after participants of a procession decided to deviate from the permitted route.Â
The Indian Express  reported that at least four persons were arrested, five others were detained, and more than 100 people were booked for the violence.Â
Some other reports corroborating the facts of the incident can be seen here  and here .

title: Fact Check: Old Ramadan video FALSELY shared as Muslims praying at Times Square on Christmas
content:
This video shows Taraweeh prayers being offered during Ramadan in March 2023.
A video of a huge gathering of Muslims allegedly offering prayers at Times Square in New York on Christmas this year. A Facebook user wrote sharing the viral video, "Times Square - New York, Christmas Day, 2023."
The archived version of this post can be seen here . Times Square - New York, Christmas Day, 2023🕌🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/KSy0mKl6kS — 🇬🇧RonEnglish🇬🇧🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 (@RonEng1ish) December 26, 2023
Times Square - New York, Christmas Day, 2023🕌🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/KSy0mKl6kS — 🇬🇧RonEnglish🇬🇧🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 (@RonEng1ish) December 26, 2023
India Today found that while the viral video is from Times Square in New York, it is old and shows Taraweeh prayers during Ramadan. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes of the vial video, we came across reports with similar visuals , noting that these scenes show Iftar and Taraweeh prayers at Times Square in New York. Taraweeh is an Islamic prayer  that is performed only in the month of Ramadan.Â
With these clues, we performed a keyword search on YouTube and found the viral video uploaded to multiple accounts between March and April this year. These videos were described as Taraweeh prayers at Times Square on the first day of Ramadan.
The Muslim holy month of Ramadan in 2023 began on March 22 and ended on April 21.
Additionally, the news ticker in the video featured a report on violent clashes in France between police and demonstrators during an anti-reservoir protest. The clash took place on March 25, 2023, when protestors opposing the construction of a large water reservoir meant for farm irrigation in west France clashed with French police.
We also perused Christmas Day live vlogs from Times Square on YouTube and found the place was well-lit and decorated, and found nothing that resembled the scene in the viral clip.
All this evidence suggests that an old video of Ramadan prayers at Times Square was shared with a false communal spin. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Dec 28, 2023 20:05 IST

title: Fact Check: NYPD didn't water cannon Israel supporters at JFK airport, video is from Jerusalem
content:
This video dates back to July 2023 and shows Israeli police firing water cannons at people protesting Israel's judicial reforms.
On December 27, hundreds of pro-Palestine protestors gathered at two of America's busiest airports , Los Angeles International Airport and New York's John F Kennedy International Airport (JFK), blocking the entrances. Following the protests, a video of a police truck using a water cannon against demonstrators was widely shared.Â
The video  shows several people with Israeli flags in their hands hiding behind a wall as a water cannon blasted at them. People sharing this video alleged that the New York Police Department shot water at pro-Israel demonstrators after they took over the airport road. NYPD BRING OUT WATER CANNON AT #JFK AIRPORT AFTER DEEMING PROTESTERS A TERROR THREAT FOR TAKING OVER AIRPORT ROAD SITUATION ONGOING pic.twitter.com/gX7bvcZCzH — ⏰0HOUR⏰ (@__0HOUR1_) December 27, 2023
NYPD BRING OUT WATER CANNON AT #JFK AIRPORT AFTER DEEMING PROTESTERS A TERROR THREAT FOR TAKING OVER AIRPORT ROAD SITUATION ONGOING pic.twitter.com/gX7bvcZCzH — ⏰0HOUR⏰ (@__0HOUR1_) December 27, 2023
"Who would love to be pulling the trigger? NYPD Uses a Water Cannon at JFK Airport after deeming protesters a 'Terror Threat' for taking over Airport Road," read one such post. Its archived version can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is five months old and not from the United States at all.Â
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a five-month-old news report from the Independent  that featured the video in question, making it evident that the clip was unrelated to recent protests at America's airports. According to this report, the demonstration took place in the Israeli capital Jerusalem and central Tel Aviv and protestors were opposing controversial judicial overhaul plans in the country.
According to this report, the demonstration took place in the Israeli capital Jerusalem and central Tel Aviv and protestors were opposing controversial judicial overhaul plans in the country.
A subsequent search yielded several photographs of water cannons firing on protesters in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv, published by the Guardian  on July 25, 2023. Reportedly, protestors started demonstrating following a vote in the Israeli parliament on a contested bill that limited the power of the country's Supreme Court to void government decisions.
Israeli lawmakers approved a significant law on July 24 , as part of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's controversial justice reform plan. With the passing of this law, there were waves of mass demonstrations and accusations that Netanyahu was attempting to impose authoritarianism on the country.
The Times of Israel reported that at least 33 people were arrested and 20 were hospitalised during the protest due to alleged police brutality.
Thus, it's clear that an old-unrelated video from Jerusalem was falsely linked to recent protests in the United States. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Dec 28, 2023 21:30 IST
